dubai/jumeirah-village-circle.tutorsIntro: The profiles below reflect what Jumeirah Village Circle families ask for: Year 10 and 11 Mathematics and sciences, Diploma Higher Level subjects, and the occasional single session to work through an options decision properly. Each tutor teaches a named specification.

intro.heading: Four decisions decide the grade before any revision starts
paragraphs: There is a version of a tutoring enquiry that arrives with no crisis attached. The child is doing reasonably well, the school seems competent, nobody is panicking - and a form has come home asking which subjects to take next year. Jumeirah Village Circle produces a lot of these enquiries, because the community skews towards families with children in the primary and lower secondary years, which is exactly the window in which the decisions get made.

Four decisions do most of the work. The Year 9 option block, which fixes how many accredited subjects a student ends up with and whether the sciences are taken separately. The tier on each Cambridge entry, which caps the grade available. The choice between the Diploma and A-Levels at sixteen. And the three Higher Level subjects, which are what a university prerequisite actually tests. None of those is a tutoring question, and all four are more consequential than a term of lessons.

Underneath them sits the thing that matters at every stage, which is how much of each course the student is expected to carry alone. That proportion rises sharply at each transition. In Year 9, almost everything is set and marked by the school. By Diploma year two, a student is managing timed practice across six subjects, an internal assessment in each, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, with deadlines set by the school and no one checking the hours. A student who has never had to run their own work does not discover this gradually.

So the useful shape for a JVC family is not a weekly slot booked early and run for four years. It is: get the decisions right, build the independent habit before it is needed, and buy expert hours at the two or three points where a specific failure shows up in marked work. That is cheaper and it works better, and this page is written to make each of those three things possible.

On delivery: lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, so a tutor and a student work on the same script. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. In a community this dense that removes a real friction - no tutor parking, no arrival window, no dependence on who happens to live within a short drive of the circle - and it means a Higher Level subject is matched on who teaches the paper.

Nothing here promises a grade or an admission, and no figure on this page is an IB Gram price. The rates quoted are market rates with their source named, and the regulatory material is quoted from official publications. What follows is the sequence of decisions, what each one costs if it goes wrong, and where an hour of teaching is worth buying.

dubai/jumeirah-village-circle.programmesIntro: JVC families are usually choosing between routes rather than already committed to one, so each note below describes the decision the programme represents as well as the programme itself.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led courses examined at the end of Year 11, each syllabus carrying a code that determines the papers, the tiering and the formula sheet. The grades do two jobs: they decide sixth-form entry, and they supply the five accredited subjects the Ministry of Education counts for equivalency, from which Arabic and Islamic education are excluded.
programmes.countryNote: The JVC and Jumeirah Village Triangle schools and those immediately around them run both boards, so a parent cannot assume Cambridge. Ask the examinations officer for the code and, on Cambridge subjects, the tier - a Core entry caps the grade available and is recorded on the entry rather than in the report.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed work in each subject is marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The Diploma's defining feature for planning purposes is simultaneity: coursework in several subjects and timed practice for all six run in the same months.
programmes.countryNote: For a JVC family the Diploma decision usually comes down to breadth against depth. The Diploma keeps six subjects plus the core running; A-Levels narrow to three or four. Which suits a child is a question about how they work, and it is better answered from Year 11 evidence than from a prospectus.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted into a 1-7 grade, with no external papers until an optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11. The criterion breakdown is the useful part and is rarely shown to parents unless asked, which means a weak criterion can sit inside a respectable overall grade for two years.
programmes.countryNote: Where a JVC family is on the continuum rather than the IGCSE route, the Year 9 decision looks different: there is no option block in the same sense, and the question becomes which criteria are consistently weak. That is a six-week block of work, not a standing weekly slot.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with reporting against learning outcomes rather than marks. Reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina are what decide how Year 7 goes, and a prose report can hide all three. The Year 6 Exhibition is the first extended independent project, and the first real signal about whether a child can plan work unsupervised.
programmes.countryNote: JVC has a large primary population, and the most valuable thing to do at this stage is also the cheapest: establish a daily reading habit and secure number facts. The independent-study habit the Diploma assumes is far easier to build at nine than to install at seventeen.

dubai/jumeirah-village-circle.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones that appear most often in JVC option and level decisions. Each note says what the course assesses and, where it matters, what taking it or dropping it does to the options two years later.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier decision here is the one families most often miss. Extended keeps the full grade range and the sixth-form doors; Core caps both. Extended candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems that mix two topics and signpost no method, which is a practice deficit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: IGCSE Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A bridging course some schools offer alongside Extended Mathematics for students heading to Higher Level Mathematics or A-Level Maths. Where it is available and the student is coping, it reduces the step up considerably. Where it is not, that step has to be built another way.

subjects.name: IGCSE separate sciences
subjects.description: Three separate sciences keep more sixth-form and Diploma combinations available than the co-ordinated route. They also cost three option slots. For a student with any possibility of a science or engineering destination, that cost is usually worth paying in Year 9.

subjects.name: IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: All three sciences at reduced depth for two grades and two option slots. Entirely sound for students heading elsewhere, and it frees a slot for another accredited subject. The trade is that some sixth-form science courses expect the separate route, so check the intended sixth form first.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, proof and calculus. Commonly named in engineering, mathematics, physics and many computer science prerequisites, often at Higher Level. The exploration is marked against five lettered criteria for twenty marks, and is where whole grades move because students treat it as a write-up.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and substantial graphical-calculator work, with interpretation carrying marks students expect for the calculation. Suits business, social science and life science routes; less often accepted where a programme names calculus-heavy mathematics.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level Physics is a route subject for engineering as well as a demanding one. Marks are lost in algebra rather than physics - a sound argument abandoned when the rearrangement gets untidy - and the data-analysis component is the least-practised part of the course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Required for most medical, pharmacy and chemical engineering routes. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers, while the internally assessed investigation loses marks on uncertainty handling and on conclusions that go beyond the data.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume invites rereading, which achieves little. Grades turn on precision of terminology and on answering the command term actually used. Usually paired with Chemistry for medical routes, and it is the pairing rather than either subject that a prerequisite names.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Both reward application to unfamiliar material under timing. Economics marks sit in correctly labelled diagrams; Business Management marks sit in evaluating a decision rather than describing a company. Popular Higher Level choices in this community and often underestimated.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Compulsory in all Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, and excluded from the Ministry's five-subject equivalency count. First-language and additional-language routes are different courses needing different tutors, and neither should be folded into an academic slot.

regions.note: Dense mid-rise apartments and townhouse clusters around the circle, with a young family profile and a school inside the community. The internal road layout slows the final part of a school run more than the main-road distance suggests.

sections.heading: What the school carries at each stage, and what the student must add
paragraphs: A direct answer to the question JVC parents are actually asking: at Year 9 the school carries nearly all of it, at IGCSE the student carries perhaps a third, and by Diploma year two the student carries the majority. That shift is the real curriculum, and it is the one nobody publishes. A child who arrives at the Diploma having never run their own work has not become lazy; they have hit a structural change nobody warned them about.

It is worth being specific about what carrying means. It means deciding what to practise without being set it. It means attempting questions where no method is indicated, at a volume no teacher could mark. It means managing a coursework deadline across months. It means marking your own work honestly against a published scheme, which is harder than it sounds because a student recognises what they meant rather than what they wrote.

The table maps that progression stage by stage, with the decision that falls at each point. The pattern matters more than any individual row: every transition both raises the independent load and presents a choice, which is why families who handle the choice well and the habit badly still struggle. Getting the option block right and leaving the study habit to chance solves half the problem.

The practical implication for a JVC household with younger children is unusually cheerful. The most valuable thing available is free and early: a child who reads daily, knows their number facts cold and is used to attempting work without being told how will find each transition manageable. That is a habit built at nine and ten, not a service bought at seventeen, and it is why we will often tell a Year 7 family that tutoring is premature.

sections.heading: The Year 9 option block, and what each choice closes
paragraphs: The option form looks like a preference exercise and functions as a constraint on the next four years. Two decisions inside it do most of the damage when they go wrong. The first is how many accredited subjects the student ends up with, which matters because the Ministry of Education counts five for equivalency and excludes Arabic and Islamic education from that five. A thin block that relies on those two to make up the number has miscounted.

The second is the sciences. Three separate sciences keep more sixth-form and Diploma combinations open, at the cost of three option slots. Co-ordinated Sciences covers all three at reduced depth for two grades and two slots, freeing one for another accredited subject. Neither is wrong. The decision should be taken against where the student might go, with the understanding that reopening a science route after a co-ordinated entry is harder than keeping it open was.

The underrated third factor is which subjects a student will still be able to work at alone in Year 11 when nine subjects are all demanding attention. A subject chosen because it sounded interesting and then abandoned in the final term still occupies a grade slot. A subject the student can self-teach from a textbook and past papers is quietly worth more than its interest value, which is the opposite of how fourteen-year-olds choose.

The table sets out the common block structures and what each keeps open. Take it to the school rather than instead of the school: the options actually available depend on the timetable blocks that school runs, and a combination that looks sensible on paper may be impossible there. Ask which combinations are blocked against each other before building a plan around one.

sections.heading: Diploma or A-Levels: how to decide from evidence
paragraphs: This decision is usually made on atmosphere - the school's culture, what friends are doing, which prospectus was more persuasive. It can be made on evidence instead, and the evidence is already available by the middle of Year 11. The question is not which qualification is better. Both are widely accepted and both pass through the Ministry's recognition process. The question is which one suits how this particular student works.

The Diploma keeps six subjects running plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with internally assessed work in every subject. It rewards students who can run several things at once, meet deadlines without being chased, and write about their own thinking. A-Levels narrow to three or four subjects studied in more depth, with less coursework in most subjects. That rewards students who go deep on fewer things and who find simultaneity costly.

The Year 11 evidence that predicts this well is behavioural rather than academic. Does the student miss deadlines when several fall in the same week, or only when a single task is hard? Do their best marks come from sustained work or from last-minute intensity? Can they write a page about their own reasoning, or only about content? Those three answers point to one route or the other more reliably than their IGCSE grade profile does.

There is also a route consideration. Both qualifications satisfy UAE equivalency on their own terms - the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the IB, no points threshold appears in the Ministry clarification this page relies on, so verify any figure quoted elsewhere on moe.gov.ae before planning around it.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level: what the levels actually change
paragraphs: Every Diploma student takes three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and the choice is the most admissions-relevant decision in the whole programme. A prerequisite naming a subject at Higher Level is not satisfied by a strong grade at Standard Level. Families who choose Higher Level subjects on enjoyment and discover the constraint in Year 13 have lost options that were available eighteen months earlier.

The levels differ in more than difficulty. Higher Level carries additional content and more teaching time, sits additional or longer papers in most subjects, and asks for the same internally assessed component at greater depth. Both levels report on the same 1-7 scale, which creates a trap: a 6 at Standard Level and a 6 at Higher Level look identical on a transcript and are not treated identically by a prerequisite that specifies the level.

Choosing well means working backwards from two things. First, the published requirement of the destination, at programme level rather than institution level - these differ within the same university. Second, honest evidence from Year 11 about which subjects the student can sustain at depth. A student who found Extended Mathematics a struggle will find Higher Level Mathematics harder than the step from Core to Extended was, and that is a reason to plan support rather than to avoid the subject if the destination requires it.

The table compares the levels across the dimensions that matter for planning. Confirm the detail against your child's current subject guides, which the school can supply, because the IB revises them on a rolling cycle. The general shape holds, but the exact paper structure and internal assessment weighting for a given cohort is a question for the guide rather than for a web page.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: Parents in this community frequently discover, usually late, that their child's IGCSE is not the examination they assumed. Schools around Jumeirah Village choose boards subject by subject, so a single student can sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics. The subject name on the report is identical in both cases, and almost nothing else is.

The differences are practical. The papers are structured differently. Cambridge runs Core and Extended tiers on several subjects while Pearson generally runs a single tier. Formula sheets differ in what they supply. The syllabus codes differ - Cambridge codes are four digits, Pearson codes carry a letter prefix - and past papers bought or downloaded for the wrong board tell a student very little about where they stand.

The consequence for tutoring is direct. A tutor matched on subject name can teach competently for a whole term on the wrong specification, and the student will feel it only when a past paper looks unfamiliar. One question to the examinations officer prevents it: which board, which code, and which tier. Ask for it in writing, because reports and newsletters give the subject name alone.

The table sets out the codes that come up most often in this community. Treat it as a prompt for the question rather than as the answer: a school can change board between cohorts, and your child's entry is what counts. Confirm the code against the entry form, and use only past papers and mark schemes from the board's own site or through the school.

sections.heading: Who lives in JVC, and which schools the community feeds
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Circle is one of Dubai's densest mid-market communities, built around an internal road layout that makes a short distance take longer than it should. The household profile skews young: a high proportion of families with primary and lower secondary children, often in apartments rather than villas, often making their first set of school decisions in the UAE rather than their third.

That profile explains the enquiry pattern. Fewer crisis enquiries about Diploma year two, many more questions about which options to take, whether the local school is right, and whether a child in Year 7 should have a tutor at all. The answer to the last one is usually no, and saying so is more useful than taking the booking. What a Year 7 family should buy, if anything, is a diagnostic hour that tells them whether reading rate and number facts are secure.

School-wise, JVC children split in three directions: the schools inside the Jumeirah Village communities, the larger schools across Hessa Street in Al Barsha South, and the Motor City and Sports City cluster to the south. Those schools run both examination boards and both the British route and the IB continuum, which is why board and code questions matter more here than in a community served by a single anchor school.

For context on the market these decisions are made in: KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in Dubai in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Dubai is adding seven schools for 2026-27, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 places - so the option set in a community like this is still expanding rather than settled.

sections.heading: What support costs at each decision point
paragraphs: Spending on tutoring in this community tends to be lumpy rather than continuous, and that is the right shape. A single decision session before the option form. Nothing for a year. A block in Year 11 when a specific failure appears in mocks. Coursework supervision in Diploma year one. A short intensive before the final papers. Four or five purchases across five years, rather than a weekly slot from Year 9 to Year 13.

The rates below were read from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026. They are market rates and not an IB Gram price list; ask us for our figure before booking. The useful column is the last one, which says what each purchase should produce. A decision session should produce a written recommendation. A block should produce movement in marked work. An intensive should produce whole-paper scores. If a purchase cannot name its output, it is not a purchase, it is a subscription.

There is an obvious temptation in a community with this demography, which is to start early and keep going, on the theory that steady support prevents problems. The evidence in marked work rarely supports it. A student who has had a weekly tutor since Year 8 often has a weaker independent habit than one who has not, because the tutor has been doing the diagnosis and the planning that the student needed to learn to do. That is a real cost, and it is invisible until Diploma year one.

Where continuous support is genuinely justified, it is normally for a specific, persistent difficulty rather than for general reassurance. In that case the arrangement should still carry a review every six to eight weeks against marked work, with three legitimate outcomes: continue, change tutor, or stop. Stopping should be a normal result rather than a failure, and a provider who never proposes it is not measuring anything.

sections.heading: Coursework honesty, from the first option choice onwards
paragraphs: Coursework arrives earlier than most families expect. Several IGCSE subjects carry assessed components, the MYP has criteria-based tasks throughout and a Personal Project at the end, and the Diploma has internally assessed work in every subject plus the Extended Essay. Across those years a student accumulates habits about what help is acceptable, and the habits form long before anybody explains the rules.

The rules reduce to one principle: the work must be the student's, and every contribution from anywhere else must be acknowledged in the form the school requires. That covers quoted text, paraphrased arguments, data from a published source, diagrams, code and output from any tool. A student who understands why attribution exists will handle the Extended Essay safely at seventeen. A student who has spent four years receiving improved versions of their work will not.

The tutor's line is fixed and worth stating in the same words everywhere. A tutor teaches the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each. A tutor interrogates a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. A tutor questions method, data, sources and reasoning. A tutor responds to a draft with questions rather than corrections. A tutor does not supply text, restructure an argument on the student's behalf, or return a rewritten version to be retyped.

The test is practical. At the end, the student should be able to defend every decision in the work under questioning, without notes, because every decision was theirs. Providers in this market sell finished internal assessments at a fixed price; a student who submits one faces their school's academic honesty process and, under IB rules, a malpractice finding that can cost the diploma. The provider keeps the fee regardless.

sections.heading: Availability, scarcity and the permit a tutor should hold
paragraphs: Supply in this market is uneven in a predictable way. Higher Level Mathematics and Higher Level Physics tighten from February. Smaller Diploma options - Computer Science, Psychology, Global Politics - draw on a much shorter list than a headline subject grid implies. Arabic as a first language is thin all year. A platform claiming full coverage at all times has simply not disclosed its gaps, and the discovery usually happens after booking.

Our approach is to disclose before booking. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the fallback is a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online, with the tutor's base and the time difference stated before anything is confirmed. That is a different thing from routing a Dubai parent to a foreign number and leaving them to assume local delivery, which two providers in this market do.

On legality: private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the application with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted.

Two further conditions matter. The permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Separately, a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE centre, and claims no approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

process.title: Say which decision is live
process.description: Options, tier, Diploma or A-Levels, Higher Level subjects, or a subject that has gone wrong. Each needs a different response and only one of them needs a weekly slot. A clear answer here is what stops a decision question turning into a term of lessons it never needed.

process.title: Send the marked work and the entry details
process.description: The last two pieces of marked work, including the one that went badly, plus the syllabus code and tier from the entry form or the IB subject and level. Reports show neither the code nor the tier, and both change what the right support looks like.

process.title: Check the destination's published requirement
process.description: Where a route decision is live, we look up the published entry requirement for the specific programme rather than the institution's general international page. Those differ, and a prerequisite that names a subject at Higher Level is not met by a strong Standard Level grade.

process.title: One diagnostic hour, then an honest recommendation
process.description: For a subject problem the first session works on the script and a short set of unprompted questions rather than teaching. Sometimes the recommendation is a defined block. Sometimes it is a practice routine and no paid hours, and for a Year 7 or Year 8 family that is often the right answer.

process.title: Buy in blocks with a stated output
process.description: Where support is needed it runs as a defined block with a target, a session count and a review date, not as an open arrangement. A decision session should produce a written recommendation; a block should produce movement in marked scripts; an intensive should produce whole-paper scores.

process.title: Review on marks, then stop or continue
process.description: At six to eight weeks we compare against marked work and decide to continue, change tutor or finish. Finishing is a normal result. Continuous tutoring from Year 8 often leaves a weaker independent habit than none, because the tutor has been doing the planning the student needed to learn.

whyPoints.title: The decisions are treated as the main event
whyPoints.description: Options, tier, route and level decide more than a term of lessons does, and they are reversible only within a window. We set them out with what each one closes, against published requirements rather than general reassurance.

whyPoints.title: We will say when tutoring is premature
whyPoints.description: For a Year 7 or Year 8 family with no specific failure in the marked work, the honest recommendation is a reading and practice habit and no paid hours. A provider that never gives that answer is not diagnosing.

whyPoints.title: Board and code checked before matching
whyPoints.description: Schools around Jumeirah Village use both examination boards, sometimes within one student's subject set. A tutor matched on subject name alone can teach the wrong specification competently for a whole term.

whyPoints.title: Level-specific support, not subject-specific
whyPoints.description: Higher Level carries additional content, additional papers and greater depth in the same internally assessed component. Support matched to the subject but not the level misses the part the prerequisite cares about.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated to October 2026. Nothing on this page is our price, and you can hold our quote against the same bands.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The gain is a specialist pool defined by who teaches the paper rather than who can reach the circle.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE options should a Year 9 student in Jumeirah Village Circle take?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from two constraints. The Ministry of Education counts five accredited subjects at no lower than E or grade 3 for equivalency and excludes Arabic and Islamic education, so a block needs five other accredited subjects with a margin for one going wrong. Then decide the sciences: three separate sciences keep more sixth-form combinations open at the cost of three option slots, while Co-ordinated Sciences gives two grades for two slots. Take the proposed combination to the school before committing, because the timetable blocks that school runs may make a sensible-looking set impossible.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors into Jumeirah Village Circle homes?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, which is how a tutor and a student work on the same marked script. In a community as dense as JVC that also removes practical friction - no parking, no arrival window, no dependence on who happens to live nearby - and it means a Higher Level subject is matched on who teaches that paper rather than on driving distance from the circle.

faqs.question: Should my child do the IB Diploma or A-Levels after IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Decide on behavioural evidence from Year 11 rather than on atmosphere. The Diploma keeps six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS running at once, with internally assessed work in every subject; A-Levels narrow to three or four with less coursework in most. Ask three questions: does the student miss deadlines when several fall in one week, do their best marks come from sustained work or last-minute intensity, and can they write about their own reasoning. The answers point to a route more reliably than their grade profile does.

faqs.question: How many Diploma subjects are taken at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and the three Higher Level choices are the most admissions-relevant decision in the programme. A prerequisite that names a subject at Higher Level is not satisfied by a strong Standard Level grade in the same subject, however good the grade. Choose by working backwards from the published requirement of the specific programme the student might apply to, and then by honest evidence from Year 11 about which subjects they can sustain at depth. Those two filters usually leave one sensible combination.

faqs.question: What actually changes between Standard Level and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: More than difficulty. Higher Level carries additional content beyond the core syllabus, more guided teaching time, and additional or longer externally examined papers in most subjects, and the same internally assessed component is expected at greater depth. Both levels report on the same 1 to 7 scale, which is the trap: a 6 at each level looks identical on a transcript but is not read the same way by a prerequisite that specifies the level. Confirm the exact paper structure for your child's cohort in the current subject guide, which the school can supply.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether the school uses Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Yes, considerably, and schools around Jumeirah Village use both - sometimes within one student's subject set. The papers are structured differently, Cambridge runs Core and Extended tiers on several subjects while Pearson generally runs one tier, and the formula sheets differ in what they supply. Past papers downloaded for the wrong board tell a student almost nothing about where they stand. Ask the examinations officer in writing for the board, the syllabus code and the tier, because reports give only the subject name.

faqs.question: Which schools do Jumeirah Village Circle children attend?
faqs.answer: Three directions, in practice. Schools inside the Jumeirah Village communities themselves, the larger schools across Hessa Street in Al Barsha South, and the Motor City and Sports City cluster to the south. Those schools between them run both examination boards and both the British route to IGCSE and the IB continuum. That spread is why board and code questions matter more in JVC than in a community served by one anchor school, and why a tutor match here should start from the entry form.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9 and nothing is wrong. Is tutoring premature?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and we will say so. With no specific failure visible in marked work, a weekly slot tends to substitute for the habit the student needs to build - the tutor does the diagnosis and the planning, and the student arrives at Diploma year one having never done either. What is worth buying at this stage is a single decision session on the option block, and possibly a diagnostic hour to confirm that reading rate and number facts are secure. Beyond that, structured self-marked practice does more than paid hours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose subjects rather than teach one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many JVC families it is the most useful hour they buy. A decision session works from the student's own marked work and from the published entry requirements of wherever they might be heading, and produces a written recommendation on options, tier, route or Higher Level choices that you can take to the school. It involves no teaching and does not lead to a weekly commitment. The value is in the written output: a recommendation you can test against what the school proposes rather than a conversation you half remember.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to spend across Years 10 to 13?
faqs.answer: Less than a continuous weekly slot implies, if the spending is shaped properly. A realistic pattern is four or five purchases: a decision session before options, a block of eight to ten sessions in Year 11 on a diagnosed failure, a decision session before Higher Level choices, coursework supervision blocks in Diploma year one, and a short intensive before the final papers. At market rates of AED 150-300 an hour for a qualified tutor and AED 200-450 or more for a specialist, read in October 2026, that is a very different total from four years of weekly lessons.

faqs.question: Is three separate sciences better than Co-ordinated Sciences?
faqs.answer: Better for keeping doors open, not better in itself. Three separate sciences keep more sixth-form and Diploma science combinations available and cost three option slots; Co-ordinated Sciences covers all three at reduced depth for two grades and two slots, freeing one for another accredited subject. For a student with any realistic possibility of a science or engineering destination, the separate route is usually worth the slots, because reopening a science path after a co-ordinated entry is harder than keeping it open was. Check the intended sixth form's requirement before deciding.

faqs.question: What happens if my child picks the wrong Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: It depends how early it is noticed. Early in Diploma year one a school can often move a student between levels or subjects, subject to timetable and the IB's registration deadlines, so the first term is when to raise it. Later it becomes a question of whether the destination's prerequisite can be met another way, which sometimes it can and sometimes it cannot. This is precisely why the choice should be tested against published programme requirements before it is made, rather than against a general sense that a subject is well regarded.

faqs.question: When does independent study actually need to start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the point at which it becomes necessary. By Diploma year two a student is running timed practice across six subjects, an internal assessment in each, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, with nobody checking the hours. That is not a habit anyone installs in Year 13. The practical answer is Year 9: begin attempting work that has not been set, marking it strictly against a published scheme, and logging what was lost and why. In Years 7 and 8 the equivalent is a daily reading habit and secure number facts.

faqs.question: Should we ask a prospective JVC tutor whether they hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and asking is reasonable. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the application with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Ask an individual tutor directly whether they hold it - since it costs nothing, not holding it usually means the rules were never checked.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Within a fixed boundary, yes. A tutor can teach the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each, interrogate the research question until it is answerable in the word limit, question the method, data and sources, and respond to a draft with questions rather than corrections. What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure the argument on the student's behalf, or hand back a rewritten version to retype. The test is whether your child can defend every choice unaided. Purchased coursework exposes the student to a malpractice finding while the provider keeps the fee.

dubai/jumeirah-village-circle.closingHeading: Get the decisions right, then buy hours only where they change a mark
dubai/jumeirah-village-circle.closingBody: The pattern that works for a Jumeirah Village Circle family is lumpy rather than continuous: a decision session before the option form, nothing for a year, a defined block when a specific failure shows up in mocks, a second decision session before Higher Level choices, coursework supervision at the school's draft dates, and an intensive before the final papers. Tell us which decision is live, send the last marked work and the syllabus code or IB subject and level, and you will get a written recommendation, an honest answer about whether a slot is needed, the rate in AED and a review date. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/jumeirah-village-triangle.tutorsIntro: The profiles below cover what Jumeirah Village Triangle households book most often: IGCSE Mathematics and the sciences across Years 10 and 11, Diploma Higher Level subjects, and resit work for a student taking one subject again. Each tutor teaches a named specification.

intro.heading: One evening, three arrival times and a mock next week
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Triangle is a villa and townhouse community, which means households here are more often three and four children than one. That single demographic fact changes the whole tutoring problem. A household with one child needs a tutor and a slot. A household with three needs a timetable, and the timetable has to survive three different school runs, two different bus contracts and a fourth child's bedtime.

The arrival spread is the part that defeats most plans. A primary child from a school inside the Jumeirah Village communities may be home by half past two. A secondary sibling crossing Hessa Street or heading down the Al Khail corridor arrives an hour and a half later. A Diploma student at a school further west can be later still. Those three children cannot share a slot, cannot be taught in sequence by a visiting tutor without somebody waiting, and have genuinely different best hours for demanding work.

Which is the practical argument for online delivery in a community like this, and it has nothing to do with technology preference. When nothing has to travel, the primary child can take a short session at three, the Year 11 student can start at five and the Diploma student at seven, each with a different tutor who specialises in that stage. A visiting tutor cannot be in three places or teach three stages, so the household ends up compromising on at least two of the three.

The second thing that shapes enquiries from JVT is the resit question. In a community with several children, at least one is usually at a point where something has gone wrong in a public examination and the family has to decide whether to take it again, in which series, and what that does to the following year. That decision is made badly more often than it is made well, almost entirely because the calendar is not understood, and this page sets the calendar out properly.

On delivery: lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For a JVT household there is no tutor arrival window to manage, no gate access to arrange, and no need for a parent to be home at a particular minute to let somebody in - which in a four-person school run is a more significant gain than it sounds.

Nothing here promises a grade. No figure on this page is an IB Gram price; the rates quoted are market rates with the provider that published each one named. The examination dates are taken from Cambridge and Pearson's own published material, and IB session dates are deliberately absent, for reasons set out below.

dubai/jumeirah-village-triangle.programmesIntro: Most JVT households are running two or three programmes at once, which is why the notes below focus on what each one demands of a shared evening rather than on the programme in isolation.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led courses examined at the end of Year 11. The syllabus code decides the papers, the tiering and the formula sheet, and Cambridge runs Core and Extended routes on several subjects with different grade ceilings. Eight or nine subjects at once makes this the stage with the worst ratio of work required to hours available.
programmes.countryNote: In a JVT household the Year 11 child usually gets the protected slot, because that is where a public examination is imminent. The honest version of that decision is that the Year 10 sibling goes onto self-marked past-paper practice for a year, and that is almost always the right call rather than a compromise.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed components in each subject are marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. Coursework deadlines in several subjects cluster in the same weeks, which is the part a shared household timetable finds hardest to accommodate.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in JVT are typically the latest home of any child in the house, which pushes their session to the end of the evening. That is the worst hour for demanding work, so the usual answer is one longer weekend block for the Diploma student and a short weekday checkpoint rather than a full weekday lesson.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, with no external papers until optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11. Marks come from interim tasks, so a weak criterion can sit inside a respectable grade for a long time without anyone naming it.
programmes.countryNote: MYP work fits a shared evening better than any other stage, because it can be done in short blocks aimed at a single criterion. Six weeks on one criterion with a visible endpoint is the arrangement that fits a household already running a protected slot for an older sibling.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units and outcome-based reporting rather than marks. Reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina decide how Year 7 goes, and a prose report can hide all three. Thirty focused minutes beats a tired hour at this age, which makes primary children the easiest to slot into a busy evening.
programmes.countryNote: The primary child in a JVT household is home first and has the best capacity earliest, so a short session at three or half past three works well and leaves the evening clear. Scheduling the youngest last, which happens by default, is the commonest avoidable mistake in a multi-child plan.

dubai/jumeirah-village-triangle.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects JVT households ask for most. Each note says what the component assesses and, where relevant, how it behaves in a short session rather than a long one - which matters when an evening is being shared.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Responds better than any other subject to a weekly hour, because the failures are visible in the script. Extended candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems mixing two topics with no method signposted. Check the tier first: a Core entry caps the grade regardless of the revision.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the written practical paper carry most of the lost marks. The practical paper tests reading an unfamiliar method and finding its weakness, which responds to four or five focused sessions rather than a full term.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry decide the grade, and both reward drill in short bursts. Works well in a thirty-minute slot, which makes it a good candidate when an evening is being shared between children.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Marks turn on terminology precision and on answering the command term used rather than on content volume. A disciplined student can lift this subject substantially alone with past papers and the published mark scheme, which is useful when slots are scarce.

subjects.name: IGCSE Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: A separate qualification from International GCSE Mathematics, taken alongside it at some schools for students heading to Higher Level Mathematics or A-Level Maths. Tutor supply is thinner than for the main course, so book earlier than you would for Mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus are the Higher Level pressure points. The exploration moves whole grades because it is marked against five lettered criteria and students treat it as a write-up. Needs a long session rather than a short one, so it suits a weekend block.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and heavy graphical-calculator work, with interpretation carrying marks students expect for the calculation alone. Calculator technique is genuinely teachable and often neglected entirely.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers. The internally assessed investigation loses marks on uncertainty handling and on conclusions that outrun the data, both of which are fixable in a few checkpoints.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rewards reading a situation before reaching for an equation. The recurring loss is algebraic rather than conceptual, and the data-analysis component is barely practised outside the lessons spent setting up the investigation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tools are quick to learn; applying them to an unfamiliar case study under timing is not. Students describe a company when the question asked them to evaluate a decision, and skip the quantitative sections entirely.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Short, frequent sessions beat long infrequent ones in a language, which makes these a good fit for a thirty-minute weekday slot. Tutor supply for the less common languages is tighter, so give more notice than for a core subject.

sections.heading: What the JVT school run does to an evening with several children
paragraphs: The honest answer is that it creates an arrival spread of up to three hours, and that spread rather than the tutor's availability is what determines what is possible. A primary child from a school inside the Jumeirah Village communities can be home by half past two. A secondary sibling crossing Hessa Street arrives between four and half past. A Diploma student travelling further west may not be back until six. No single hour works for all three.

Families usually discover this the hard way, by booking one tutor for two children on the theory that an hour each side of five will work. It does not, because the younger child is at their best at three and exhausted by six, while the older child is not home at four. The result is two mediocre sessions instead of two good ones, and the usual conclusion drawn is that tutoring does not suit this household.

The table sets out the household shapes we see most often in JVT with the slot pattern that holds for each. The pattern that recurs is counter-intuitive: schedule the youngest first and earliest, give the protected slot to whichever child has the nearest public examination, and move the latest-arriving child to the weekend. Most households do the reverse, scheduling the eldest first because their work looks most urgent.

This is the specific thing online delivery makes possible, and it is worth being plain about why. A visiting tutor has to be somewhere, which means they can serve one slot in this household and they will offer the slot that fits their route between other families. Three sessions at three different times with three different stage specialists is not a scheduling preference; it is only available when nothing has to travel.

sections.heading: Staggering siblings through one evening without losing anything
paragraphs: A stagger is not just a sequence of bookings. It is a decision about which child gets the best hour of the evening, and in most households that decision is never consciously made - it goes to whoever shouted loudest or whose homework looked worst. Made deliberately, it goes to whichever child has a public examination closest, and everything else fits around that.

The second principle is that short sessions are not inferior sessions. A primary child's useful attention span for a demanding task is well under an hour, and thirty minutes aimed at one skill produces more than sixty minutes of mixed activity. For drill-shaped work - number facts, moles calculations, vocabulary, command terms - thirty minutes twice a week beats one long weekly session at any age. That makes a lot of a shared evening workable that otherwise would not be.

The third principle is to stop pursuing shared sessions between siblings unless the stages genuinely match. Two children in the same class on the same specification can share an hour profitably. Two children two years apart cannot: the tutor teaches one and occupies the other, and both families' time is wasted while feeling economical. Where a shared session is viable, it halves the cost per child and halves the slot count, which is the real prize in a four-person household.

The table gives the stagger patterns that work, with the failure mode each avoids. One practical addition: agree a single named fallback slot for the whole household rather than a fallback per child. In a house with three school runs something will collapse most weeks, and a single agreed catch-up time is far easier to protect than three floating rearrangements.

sections.heading: The mock fortnight: the two weeks that tell you everything
paragraphs: Mocks are treated by most families as a verdict and by most schools as a dress rehearsal. They are neither. They are the only diagnostic data available before the real papers, and the value is almost entirely in the scripts rather than in the marks. A parent who reads the mark and reacts has thrown away the useful part; a parent who reads the script knows what to do next.

What to look for is narrow. Go through each lost mark and assign it to one of four causes: the student did not know the content, knew it and misread the question, knew it and ran out of time, or knew it and wrote the wrong structure for the command term. Count the four. The distribution tells you what the next eight weeks should contain, and in most cases three of the four categories are nearly empty while one dominates.

The four causes need genuinely different responses. Content gaps need teaching. Misreading needs a procedure for the first thirty seconds of a question. Running out of time needs whole-paper practice under timing, not more content. Structure errors need command-term drill, which is mechanical and fast. A family that buys a general tutoring slot without doing this analysis is buying a response to an unidentified problem.

Mock timing also sets a practical boundary on the resit conversation. Cambridge takes final entries for its March 2027 series on 27 November 2026, so a school's autumn mock results arrive just as that window is closing. If a resit in the March series is under discussion, the conversation with the school has to happen within days of the mock results rather than at the end of term, and that is the single most common missed deadline in this market.

sections.heading: Resits and retakes: which series, and what it actually costs
paragraphs: Deciding whether to take a subject again looks like an academic question and is mostly a calendar question. Each board runs specific series with entry deadlines months in advance, results arriving weeks after the papers and certificates weeks after that. A family that decides in principle to resit and then starts looking for the window has usually already lost the nearest one.

Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June and a November series, with a March series for some centres and subjects. The March 2027 series is the clearest worked example: final entries due 27 November 2026, examinations 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May 2027 and certificates in late June. Note also that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official timetable is the only version to plan against.

For IB retakes this page states no dates. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. UAE schools sit the May session; for the retake window, the registration deadline and the results date, ask your child's IB coordinator and build the plan from what they confirm. That is not a hedge - it is the difference between a plan and a guess.

sections.heading: If the school will not enter a resit: the private candidate route
paragraphs: Schools decline resit entries for reasonable administrative reasons as well as unreasonable ones, and a family that wants a subject taken again sometimes has to arrange it independently. This is the private candidate route, and it is more involved than most parents expect, which is why it is worth understanding before it becomes urgent rather than during the week an entry closes.

In outline, a private candidate is entered through a centre that accepts external candidates rather than through the student's own school. The centre handles the entry, the timetabling and the administration, and the candidate sits the papers there. Because entries close months before the series, the centre has to be identified and the entry made well in advance. The student's own school is not involved in the process, which also means nobody else is tracking the deadline.

Several practical points follow. Subjects with assessed practical or coursework components are harder to arrange as a private candidate than written-only subjects, because the component has to be accommodated somehow. Forecast grades, where a series requires them, come from the centre rather than the school. And the certificate arrives through the centre, which matters later if documents are needed for attestation or admission.

The honest advice is to ask the school first and ask early. Many schools will enter a student for a resit if the request arrives before entries close and the case is reasonable. The private candidate route is a genuine option rather than a last resort, but it transfers all of the administration and all of the deadline risk to the family, and in a household already managing three school runs that is a real cost to weigh.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition with JVT travel priced in
paragraphs: Comparing formats on hourly rate alone hides the thing that matters in a villa community with several children. An in-home tutor bills travel whether or not the invoice itemises it, and a household needing three sessions at three different times cannot be served by one visiting tutor at all. A group class adds a journey to an evening that already contains three.

The rates below were read from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026. They describe the market rather than IB Gram's price list; ask for our figure before booking and hold it against the band. The last column is the one specific to this community: what each format actually involves for a JVT household rather than in the abstract.

The in-home row is included for honest comparison rather than as something we sell. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, because in-home tuition is a service offered only in India. If a parent's judgement is that a particular child needs an adult physically present, an in-home tutor is the right choice for that child and we will say so rather than argue. For most JVT households the binding constraint is the arrival spread, which in-home delivery makes worse rather than better.

The format worth looking at harder than most families do is the shared session between two children at genuinely the same point in the same subject. Done where the stages match, it roughly halves the cost per child and halves the number of slots the evening has to hold - and in a four-person household the slot saving is worth more than the money. Done where the stages do not match, it wastes both.

sections.heading: Which schools JVT children attend, and why the board question comes first
paragraphs: JVT children split between schools inside the two Jumeirah Village communities, the larger schools across Hessa Street in Al Barsha South, the Jumeirah Park schools to the west, and the Motor City and Sports City cluster to the south. In a household with three children it is common for two or three of those destinations to be in use at once, which is exactly why the arrival spread is wide.

The board spread matters more than the school list. Schools in this area choose examination boards subject by subject, so one student can sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics, and two siblings at different schools can be on different boards in the same subject. The subject name on both reports is identical. Nearly everything else - paper structure, tiering, formula sheet, syllabus code - is not.

The practical step is one question per child to each school's examinations officer: which board, which syllabus code, and on Cambridge subjects which tier. Ask in writing. Reports and newsletters give the subject name alone, and a tutor matched on subject name can teach the wrong specification competently for an entire term before anybody notices. In a multi-child household that question has to be asked two or three times, which is tedious and still worth it.

For market context: KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in Dubai in 2024-25 across seventeen different curricula, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. Dubai is adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 places. KHDA licenses and inspects those schools; it does not license private tutors, and IB Gram claims no approval from it or from any board.

sections.heading: What a tutor can do when the deadline is three days away
paragraphs: In a household with several children, coursework deadlines get noticed late. The request that follows - help, it is due Thursday - is the one where the boundary matters most, because it is where the temptation to cross it is strongest and the justification sounds most reasonable. So it is worth setting out exactly what is available at three days' notice and what is not.

What a tutor can do: read what exists, explain the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each, identify which criterion is currently scoring nothing, ask the questions that expose a weak method or an unjustified conclusion, and help the student plan which two hours of work will recover the most marks. That is a genuinely useful session and it can change a grade, because most late coursework is losing marks in one identifiable place rather than everywhere.

What a tutor cannot do, at any notice: supply text, restructure the argument on the student's behalf, rewrite a section, or hand back a marked-up document the student retypes. The test does not relax because the deadline is close. At the end the student must be able to defend every decision in the work under questioning, without notes, because every decision was theirs. A deadline is not a reason to put a student in front of an academic honesty panel.

There is a harder conversation that sometimes belongs here, which is that submitting incomplete work the student actually wrote is a better outcome than submitting complete work they did not. The first costs marks on one component. The second, under IB rules, risks a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma. Providers in this market sell finished internal assessments at a fixed price; the provider keeps the fee and the student carries the consequence.

sections.heading: Coverage, scarcity and the fallback when nobody is free
paragraphs: Specialist supply is uneven in predictable ways, and a household booking for three children will hit it sooner than a household booking for one. Higher Level Mathematics and Higher Level Physics tighten from February. The less common languages and smaller Diploma options draw on a short list. Pearson Further Pure Mathematics and Cambridge Additional Mathematics have thinner supply than the main mathematics courses. Resit requests concentrate in the weeks after results, which is when they are hardest to fill.

We disclose that before booking rather than after. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the fallback is a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online, with the base and the time difference stated before anything is confirmed. For a JVT household that detail matters practically as well as ethically: a tutor two and a half hours ahead cannot take a seven o'clock slot, and that has to be known while the stagger is being built rather than afterwards.

On legality, briefly, because it comes up: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted here.

Two conditions worth knowing. The permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. And a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, runs no UAE centre, and delivers lessons online.
