process.title: Send one line per child
process.description: For each child: school, usual arrival time, subject, and the syllabus code or IB level. That is what the stagger is built from. A household request without arrival times gets a generic evening offer, which is the usual reason a multi-child plan falls apart within a month.

process.title: Name which child has the nearest deadline
process.description: Whoever has the closest public examination or coursework deadline gets the protected slot and the best hour. That decision made deliberately beats the same decision made by default, which usually hands the best hour to the loudest child rather than the most pressed one.

process.title: One diagnostic hour per child who needs one
process.description: Each diagnostic works on that child's own marked scripts and a short set of unprompted questions rather than on teaching. For a mock script it assigns every lost mark to one of four causes. You receive the finding in writing, including whether a slot is needed at all.

process.title: Build the stagger, youngest first
process.description: Short early session for the youngest, protected slot for the exam-year child, weekend block for whoever arrives latest. One named household fallback time rather than three floating reschedules. Tutor bases and time zones are stated before you confirm anything.

process.title: Put the board deadlines on the same calendar
process.description: Cambridge and Pearson entry deadlines, mock windows and the school's coursework dates go on one household calendar. The Cambridge March entry deadline in late November lands days after autumn mocks, and that is the deadline families miss most often.

process.title: Review each child on marks, separately
process.description: At six to eight weeks each child's arrangement is reviewed against their own marked work, with three outcomes: continue, change tutor or stop. Stopping one child's slot while continuing another's is a normal result, and it is how a multi-child budget stays proportionate.

whyPoints.title: Three children, three times, three specialists
whyPoints.description: Because nothing has to travel, a primary child can take a short session at three and a Diploma sibling a block at the weekend, each with a tutor who specialises in that stage. One visiting tutor can serve one slot and one stage.

whyPoints.title: The stagger is designed, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Youngest first, protected hour to the nearest deadline, latest arrival to the weekend, one household fallback slot. That ordering is counter-intuitive and it is what keeps a multi-child plan alive past half term.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read properly
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is assigned to one of four causes - content, misreading, timing, or structure for the command term - because those need four different responses. Buying a general slot without that analysis is buying a response to an unidentified problem.

whyPoints.title: The resit calendar in one place
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson windows, entry deadlines and results dates are set out from the boards' own published material. IB dates are taken from your child's coordinator rather than restated here, because they could not be confirmed from the IB directly.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated to October 2026. Nothing on this page is presented as our price, and our quote can be held against the same bands.

whyPoints.title: A coursework line that holds at three days' notice
whyPoints.description: Criteria explained, the weakest one identified, a recovery plan agreed - but no text supplied and no section rewritten. Incomplete work the student wrote is a better outcome than complete work they did not.

faqs.question: What time can a session start for a Jumeirah Village Triangle family?
faqs.answer: It depends which child. A primary pupil at a school inside the Jumeirah Village communities can often start by three o'clock, which is their best hour anyway. A secondary sibling crossing Hessa Street usually arrives between four and half past, so half past four is a realistic start. A Diploma student travelling further west may not be home until six, which is why their work is better placed in a weekend block. Send one line per child with school and arrival time, and the stagger gets built from that rather than from an average.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to villas in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing. In a villa household with several children this is a practical gain rather than a compromise: there is no arrival window to manage, no gate access to arrange, and crucially three children can be taught at three different times by three tutors who each specialise in that stage, which no single visiting tutor can do.

faqs.question: How do we stagger three children through one evening?
faqs.answer: Youngest first, exam year gets the protected hour, latest arrival goes to the weekend. In practice that means a short twenty-five to thirty-five minute session for the primary child as soon as they are home, a fixed immovable slot for whichever child has the nearest public examination, and a ninety-minute weekend block for the Diploma student who gets back last. Agree one household fallback time rather than one per child. Most families do the reverse of this, scheduling the eldest first and the youngest last, which is why the youngest ends up being taught when they are exhausted.

faqs.question: Two children two years apart - can they share a tutor?
faqs.answer: Share a tutor across two slots, yes; share a session, almost never. Two years apart means different specifications, different papers and different skills, so a shared hour becomes the tutor teaching one child while the other waits politely. It feels economical and produces two half-sessions. Shared sessions work when two children are in the same class on the same specification at roughly the same point, in which case they genuinely halve the cost per child and halve the slot count. Review any shared arrangement after four sessions, because mismatch becomes obvious fast.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with the mock results?
faqs.answer: Read the scripts, not the marks. Go through every lost mark and assign it to one of four causes: did not know the content, knew it and misread the question, knew it and ran out of time, or knew it and wrote the wrong structure for the command term. Then count them. Usually one category dominates and three are nearly empty, and each needs a different response - teaching, a reading procedure, whole-paper timing practice, or command-term drill. Buying a general tutoring slot without this analysis is buying a response to an unidentified problem.

faqs.question: Should my child resit an IGCSE, and in which series?
faqs.answer: The academic question is whether the mark reflected a fixable gap or a bad day, and the script usually answers it. The harder question is calendar. Cambridge runs June and November series plus a March series for some centres and subjects: for March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026 for papers from 3 February to 4 March, with results on Direct 13 May. Pearson runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 timetable ending 19 November. Decide within days of mock results, not at the end of term, because the nearest entry window closes first.

faqs.question: Can my child sit a resit as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a centre that accepts external candidates rather than through their own school. The centre handles the entry, the timetabling and the administration, and the candidate sits the papers there. Entries close months before the series, so the centre has to be found early and nobody else is tracking the deadline for you. Subjects with assessed practical or coursework components are harder to arrange externally than written-only subjects. Ask your child's school about a resit entry first, because many will enter a student if the request arrives before entries close.

faqs.question: What does a resit cost in time rather than money?
faqs.answer: More than families expect, because a resit runs alongside the following year's course rather than instead of it. A student resitting in a November or March series is revising one subject while starting Diploma year one or A-Levels, and the revision has to be timed around new coursework. Realistically that is one weekly slot plus self-marked past papers for eight to twelve weeks. The decision should weigh that load against what the improved grade actually makes possible: if no destination requires the higher grade, the time is often better spent on the current course.

faqs.question: Which schools do Jumeirah Village Triangle children attend?
faqs.answer: Four directions in practice: schools inside the two Jumeirah Village communities, the larger schools across Hessa Street in Al Barsha South, the Jumeirah Park schools to the west, and the Motor City and Sports City cluster to the south. In a household with three children, two or three of those are often in use at once, which is why arrival spreads here are so wide. The schools choose examination boards subject by subject, so ask each school's examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code and the tier per child, in writing.

faqs.question: Is a group class in a nearby community better value than online one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Rarely, once the journey is counted. A group class is cheaper per hour and slower per hour, and for a JVT household it adds a fourth journey to an evening that already contains three school runs. Groups work reasonably for general revision where everyone needs the same content again; they work poorly for a specific diagnosed failure, because the tutor cannot stop and watch one student work while others wait. A shared session between two siblings at genuinely the same stage gives most of the cost saving without the journey.

faqs.question: The coursework deadline is in three days. How much can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: More than you would think, inside a line that does not move. A tutor can read what exists, explain the criteria by letter, identify which criterion is currently scoring nothing, question a weak method or an unjustified conclusion, and help the student plan which two hours of work recover the most marks. What a tutor cannot do at any notice is supply text, restructure the argument or rewrite a section. Submitting incomplete work your child actually wrote is a better outcome than submitting complete work they did not.

faqs.question: Do the November IGCSE series results arrive at a different time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the gap is substantial. For Pearson Edexcel, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - roughly two months after the papers. Cambridge's March 2027 series shows the same pattern: papers finish 4 March, results appear on Direct on 13 May and certificates are issued in late June. That lag matters when a grade is needed for an application, so check the results date before choosing a series rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my child do not get on?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the match, which is one of the reasons the review point exists at six to eight weeks rather than at the end of a term. A mismatch is usually visible within three or four sessions and shows up as the student having nothing to say about what was covered. In a multi-child household it is worth checking each arrangement separately, because one child's tutor working well says nothing about another's. Changing tutor is a normal outcome and does not mean restarting from zero: the diagnostic and the plan carry over.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help an IB student retake a single subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a well-defined piece of work: one subject, a known paper set, and a specific gap identified from the previous attempt. What this page will not do is state the retake session dates or deadlines, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. Ask your child's IB coordinator for the window, the registration deadline and the results date, and the support plan is built backwards from those. Expect one weekly slot plus independent timed practice.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to book from a community like JVT?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics first, then Higher Level Mathematics from February onwards. After those, Pearson Further Pure Mathematics and Cambridge Additional Mathematics have thinner supply than the main mathematics courses, and the less common languages - Spanish B, French B - draw on a short list. Resit requests in the weeks immediately after results are the tightest of all, because everyone wants the same thing at the same time. Where no UAE-based specialist is free you are told before booking, with the fallback tutor's base and the session time stated up front.

dubai/karama.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IGCSE on both boards, the IB Middle Years and Diploma programmes, and the Indian-curriculum stages most Karama students are on. Pick by subject and level, and tell us what the study space looks like, because that changes the session length more than anything else on this page.

intro.heading: The room, the device and the hour: planning tuition for a Karama flat
paragraphs: Karama is one of the few Dubai districts where travel is not the problem. The Oud Metha school belt is a short drive or, for some families, a walk. Children are frequently home before three. On paper that makes Karama the easiest place in the city to schedule a lesson, and tutoring pages written for the villa communities assume the rest follows. It does not, because the constraint here is spatial rather than temporal.

A typical Karama household lives in a one, two or three-bedroom apartment in a mid-rise block built when the district was laid out. Two or three children share a bedroom. The living room holds the television and the family. Somebody is cooking from five. Grandparents may be visiting for a month, or living there. The quiet corner that a tutoring page imagines, a desk in a room with a door, exists in some flats and not in most. If nobody plans for that, the first three sessions are spent with a tutor asking a student to repeat themselves.

The second Karama-specific constraint is the device. Many households run one laptop between everybody, with phones as the fallback. A phone works for a conversation and fails for mathematics, because the tutor cannot see working and the student cannot see a worked solution at a readable size. A tablet is workable with a stylus. A shared laptop is fine provided it is actually free at the booked hour, which is a scheduling question rather than a technical one.

Third, the boards. Karama's school belt serves Indian-curriculum schools and British-curriculum schools within the same square kilometre, so households on one staircase may be preparing for Grade 10 board examinations, Cambridge IGCSE papers and Pearson Edexcel papers in the same spring. The grade scales are different, the paper structures are different, and the thresholds schools use for progression are different. Several families here discover that only when a report card arrives with a number they cannot interpret.

Fourth, the household budget is real and it is shared. Many Karama families are paying school fees for two or three children from one income or a modest two. A tutoring decision here is a trade-off against something else in the month, and the respectful response is accuracy rather than a discount: the smallest intervention that moves a grade, a defined end point, and a straight answer when tutoring is not the right purchase at all.

So this page is written around those four things. It covers how to set up a usable lesson in a shared flat, how to schedule a week around one laptop, what the market charges and what the lower bands genuinely cover, how the two IGCSE grade scales compare, and what a tutor may and may not do with assessed work. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. All Karama lessons are one-to-one over live video, which means no additional person needs a seat in the flat for the hour and no bedroom becomes a classroom.

dubai/karama.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for almost all Karama enquiries. What follows is the part of each that families in this district actually come to us about.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers at sixteen on one of two boards. Cambridge examines in a June series and a November series and tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, which caps the grade available. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examines in May/June and November and reports on a 9-1 scale on most specifications. The paper structures differ enough that revision on the wrong code teaches the wrong habits.
programmes.countryNote: In Karama the first question is usually which scale the report card is using. A household with one child on A* to G and another on 9 to 1 cannot compare the two numbers directly, and schools in this belt set different progression thresholds for A Level and Diploma entry.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria with task-specific descriptors rather than percentage marks. The criteria reward reflection and evaluation explicitly, which students arriving from a marks-and-ranks culture have rarely been taught to produce in writing.
programmes.countryNote: Karama's Middle Years students are often the first in their family to be assessed without a percentage. Parents reasonably want to know what a 5 in criterion B means. The honest answer involves reading the descriptor, and a tutor who cannot do that with you is not going to help the child either.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed components carry real weight and are marked against published criteria, with school deadlines that land well before any board date. The workload is at its heaviest in the second half of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Karama usually travel out of the district to school, so their afternoons start later than their younger siblings'. In a shared flat that is an advantage: the younger child's session can finish before the older one arrives home, and the room is only contested once.

dubai/karama.subjectsIntro: Karama demand concentrates on mathematics and the sciences, with regular work on English language accuracy and on accounting and economics for students heading towards commerce.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in this district. Extended-tier algebra and trigonometry hold the marks that move a grade, and the fastest gain is almost always teaching a student to write each step down, because method marks cannot be awarded for reasoning that stayed in the head.

subjects.name: Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Same subject, different paper structure and a 9-1 scale. Students who revise from Cambridge papers for a Pearson examination meet question phrasings they have not practised, which costs marks that have nothing to do with their mathematics.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity, circuits and waves are where Karama students most often stall. The practical paper rewards a method described precisely enough to be repeated by someone else, so improvement comes from writing discipline as much as from understanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the quantitative paper separate the top grades. A student who memorised chemistry as facts rather than as calculation hits a wall in Year 11, and the recovery route runs through past papers on the correct code.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: The vocabulary subject. Paraphrase scores nothing where the mark scheme wants a specific term, and that single correction is often worth a grade. It is also one of the quickest subjects to improve in a short block before a series.

subjects.name: Accounting 0452
subjects.description: Widely taken in this part of Dubai and strict about presentation. The format of a statement carries marks independently of the arithmetic, so drilling layout against past papers produces visible gains fast.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the cheapest available improvement: axes, labels, curves and shifts earn marks that prose cannot replace. At Higher Level the quantitative questions and the policy paper reward precise real examples rather than general comment.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Accuracy, register and task fulfilment rather than literary analysis. Students from households where English is a second or third language often read well above their writing level, and targeted work on controlled writing moves the grade quickly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The Diploma route most Karama students take when they want mathematics without the proof-heavy demands of the analysis course. Statistics, modelling and calculator fluency carry it, and interpretation questions are where marks leak.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the expectations and language of instruction differ. Tutoring has to follow the school's stream or it produces work the school cannot credit.

sections.heading: What a Karama parent means by a tutor near me
paragraphs: The phrase "near me" carries a different meaning in Karama than it does in a villa community. In Arabian Ranches it means somebody who will drive in. In Karama, where the school is minutes away and the block is full of families in the same position, it usually means something more like "somebody who understands how we actually live". The underlying request is for a tutor who will not assume a study, a spare hour of silence or a dedicated laptop.

It also often means a tutor who understands the school. Karama's belt contains long-established schools with large cohorts, strong science uptake and particular habits: certain subjects set a lot of written homework, certain year groups sit frequent class tests, certain schools report in percentages and others in letters or numbers. A tutor who has worked with students from that belt will recognise a report format and know what a given mark usually signals.

The third meaning is cost sensitivity, stated honestly. Karama households are often paying school fees for two or three children from a single or a modest double income. A tutoring decision here is a real household trade-off, and the respectful response is not a discount but accuracy: the smallest intervention that moves the grade, a defined end point, and a straight answer when tutoring is not the right purchase.

What we do with all three is start smaller than most providers suggest. One subject, two short sessions a week, six weeks, then a review against the school's own next assessment. If the number has not moved and the tutor cannot explain why, that is information worth having after six weeks rather than after six months.

sections.heading: Where a child studies in a Karama apartment, and what each setup breaks
paragraphs: Almost every failed online tutoring arrangement we have seen in dense housing failed on setup rather than on teaching. The student sat somewhere the tutor could not see their working, or somewhere the household walked through, or used a device too small for the subject. None of those are expensive problems and all of them are invisible until somebody names them.

The first fix is audio. A pair of wired earphones with a microphone removes most of the difficulty, because it stops the room's noise reaching the tutor and stops the tutor's voice filling the room. It costs very little and it is the single highest-return change available. A headset is better than a faster connection in almost every Karama flat we have worked with.

The second is the working surface. Mathematics and the sciences require the tutor to see what the student has written as they write it. A phone propped against a water bottle, angled at the page, does this adequately. A tablet with a stylus does it well. A laptop camera pointed at a face and nothing else does not, and a tutor who does not ask to see the page is teaching blind.

The third is timing against the household. The quietest hour in a Karama block is usually mid-afternoon before cooking starts, or early on a weekend morning. The loudest is between six and eight. Booking around that is free, and it is the reason we recommend two short weekday sessions plus a weekend block rather than a long evening slot.

sections.heading: One laptop, three children: making the week work
paragraphs: Device scheduling sounds like a trivial domestic detail and it ends more tutoring arrangements in dense housing than price does. A family books three sessions across a week without checking that the laptop is free at those hours, and by week three two of the sessions have been taken on a phone in a corridor.

The approach that works is to treat the device as the scarce resource and build the week around it. Decide which two hours the laptop is reliably free, and place the subject that needs the most visual work, usually mathematics or a science, in those hours. Subjects that are largely spoken, language practice or Theory of Knowledge discussion, can take a phone slot without much loss.

Where there are two students, consecutive slots solve the problem outright. The younger child takes a shorter session first, finishes while still able to concentrate, and hands over the desk. One quiet window covers two lessons, and the parent supervises once rather than twice.

One more point specific to this district. Several Karama households have a parent working shifts or a parent who travels for work. Online delivery means a session does not need an adult at home to let somebody in, which is a genuine operational advantage over an in-home arrangement in a flat where the door cannot always be answered at four in the afternoon. It also means a session survives a month when the family is away, because the schedule follows the student rather than the address.

The last piece of device planning is the backup. Laptops fail, connections drop and a sibling occasionally refuses to hand over. Agreeing in advance what happens then saves a session: the student moves to a phone with earphones, the tutor switches that hour to spoken review and question practice rather than written mathematics, and the written work moves to the next slot. Ten minutes lost to a plan is better than fifty lost to improvisation.

sections.heading: The two IGCSE grade scales, side by side
paragraphs: A recurring Karama conversation starts with a report card and the question of whether a number is good. The confusion is reasonable: two boards operate in the same school belt, and they report differently. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G on most subjects. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1 on most specifications. A household with one child on each scale cannot compare the two figures directly, and the school's progression thresholds may be expressed in either.

What makes this consequential rather than academic is the progression decision. Schools commonly set entry conditions for A Level or Diploma courses in terms of specific grades in the subject concerned, so a result that looks respectable can still close a door the family assumed was open. The thresholds are set by the school and vary, which is why the only reliable source is the school's own published policy rather than a general rule.

The equivalency floor is a separate and firmer number. The published Ministry of Education requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five. That is a documented minimum rather than a progression threshold, and it sits far below what any Diploma or A Level course will ask for.

The practical move for a Karama family is to write both numbers down once: what the school requires for the next stage, and what the ministry requires for equivalency. Those two figures together are the planning frame, and almost no tutoring page in this market gives either of them.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the lower band genuinely covers
paragraphs: Cost sensitivity deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance. The market in Dubai has a real low end, and it does real work, but it does not do all work. Published figures put budget online tutoring from university students and generalists at roughly AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, with one platform advertising from about AED 33. That band buys explanation, homework support and accountability. It does not usually buy board-specific technique, criterion-level coursework feedback or Higher Level depth.

The middle band, qualified subject tutors working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, is where board-specific teaching starts. One agency publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The specialist band, quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above by several providers with one at AED 270 and a premium provider at AED 650, exists because of scarcity: Higher Level sciences, unusual languages and coursework supervision have small tutor pools.

In-home visits sit between those bands in quality and above them in price, because travel is inside the rate. Published figures run roughly AED 180 to AED 350 from one cost index and AED 200 to AED 500 among independent home tutors. For a Karama family that premium buys travel, and the travel is short, so the proportion of the fee going to the drive is higher here than in the outer suburbs.

The honest guidance is about sequencing rather than tier. One subject at the middle band, where a grade is closest to a boundary, moves more for a Karama household than three subjects at the budget band. If the budget supports only the lower band, spend it on the subject where the problem is practice volume rather than conceptual depth, because that is what the lower band does well.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor in a Karama flat against one-to-one online
paragraphs: In Karama this comparison has an extra dimension that does not appear in the villa communities. A visiting tutor in a two-bedroom apartment needs a room, and for the hour that room stops being a bedroom. For a family of five that is a real cost which never appears in the hourly rate, and it is why several Karama households who started with an in-home arrangement moved to online for reasons of space rather than money.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. We would rather state that plainly than imply a service we do not sell. The compensating advantage is the catalogue: a Karama family can work with a Pearson Edexcel mathematics specialist or a Higher Level chemistry tutor without either of them needing to be in Dubai at four in the afternoon.

In-home tutoring still has genuine strengths and it is worth naming them. An adult in the room sees written working without being asked, can annotate a page directly, and provides a social presence that some younger children respond to better than a screen. If those factors dominate for your child, an in-home arrangement from another provider may be the right choice, and we will say so.

What online wins on in a dense block: no room is surrendered, no door needs answering, a missed week can move to a weekend morning, two siblings can take consecutive slots at one desk, and the tutor is chosen on board and level rather than on willingness to drive to Karama.

sections.heading: Six weeks, and how to judge whether it worked
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements are judged on feeling, which is why so many of them continue for a year without moving a grade. The student says the sessions are helpful, the tutor is pleasant, the parent is reassured, and nothing measurable changes. A Karama household making a genuine financial trade-off deserves a harder test than that.

The test we use is the school's own next assessment. Before the first session we record the current position: the last marked script, the grade or percentage, and the specific thing the tutor says is wrong. At six weeks we compare against whatever the school has set since, and the tutor has to explain the result either way. An improvement that the tutor cannot attribute to anything specific is as uninformative as no improvement.

There are legitimate reasons a grade does not move in six weeks. The gap was structural rather than topical and six weeks was always going to be a start. The assessment covered content taught before the tutoring began. The student did not do the independent work between sessions, which is the most common explanation and the most useful to surface early. What is not legitimate is a vague report and a suggestion to continue.

At the review there are four honest outcomes: continue as is, change the format, change the subject, or stop. Stopping is a real option and we have recommended it. A student who needs a fortnight of structured independent practice rather than a tutor is better served by being told so, and a Karama parent who has been told so once will trust the next recommendation.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the boundary we will not cross
paragraphs: Karama families are as likely as any to be offered finished coursework, and in this market the offer is real: one provider in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The transaction looks like a shortcut and is an academic-integrity breach that the student declares and signs for. Board malpractice rules put the consequence on the candidate, not on the seller, and the sums involved are trivial against a diploma.

What a tutor may do is specific. Teach the content the assessment rests on. Explain each criterion and what its marks reward. Say whether a research question is viable before a student spends three weeks on it. Point out that a method will not generate usable data. Read a draft and name the criterion that is under-served. Ask the questions that make a student find their own gap. What a tutor may not do is supply text, rewrite sections, generate data, choose the question, or edit a draft into a finished state.

We also do not send out board syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and redistributing them is both a copyright problem and a signal about how a provider operates. We reference the official source, name where the school should have issued it from, and work with what the student legitimately has.

The practical version for a parent with no technical knowledge of the criteria: if a provider's offer would still work if your child were on holiday, it is the wrong offer. Everything legitimate requires the student to be present and doing the work.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work in a small Karama apartment with other people around?
faqs.answer: It works, provided the setup is planned rather than improvised. Wired earphones with a microphone solve most of the difficulty by keeping household noise out of the lesson and the lesson out of the room. A phone angled over the page lets the tutor see written working, which matters in mathematics and the sciences. Place sessions in the quietest window, usually mid-afternoon before cooking starts or a weekend morning, rather than between six and eight, which is the loudest hour in most blocks.

faqs.question: What is the best session length for a child studying in a shared bedroom?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes, twice a week, for most students. A ninety-minute block asks a shared flat for a long quiet period that rarely materialises, and the second half gets spent recovering the first. Two shorter sessions also create a gap for independent work, which is where most of the progress actually happens. Keep longer sessions for weekend mornings, when a full timed past paper can be sat without interruption. Younger children do better at thirty minutes than forty-five.

faqs.question: We only have one laptop for three children. Can tutoring still work?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the device is treated as the scarce resource and the week is built around it. Identify the two hours the laptop is reliably free and put the subjects that need visual work, mathematics and the sciences, into those hours. Spoken subjects such as language practice can take a phone slot without much loss. Where two children need sessions, consecutive slots at the same desk mean one quiet window covers both lessons and one parent supervises once.

faqs.question: My child's report shows a grade 5 and my nephew's shows a C. Which is better?
faqs.answer: They come from different boards and cannot be compared directly. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1 on most specifications; Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G. A grade 5 and a C are often described alongside each other, but the number that matters is the school's own entry condition for the next stage, which is set by the school and varies between them. Ask the school for its published progression thresholds in the subject concerned rather than relying on a general conversion.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful tutoring available to a Karama family?
faqs.answer: The budget online band, published at roughly AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and from about AED 33 on one platform, does genuine work: practice volume, homework structure and accountability. It does not reliably cover board-specific technique or coursework criteria. If the problem is that your child is not doing enough practice, that band fits. If the problem is that the practice is aimed at the wrong paper, or that a criterion is misunderstood, the middle band at AED 150 to AED 300 is the honest recommendation.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who visits our flat worth the extra cost in Karama?
faqs.answer: For some children, yes, and we will say so even though we do not provide it. An adult in the room sees written working without asking, can annotate a page, and gives younger children a presence a screen cannot. The costs are a bedroom becoming a classroom for an hour, an adult at home to admit the tutor, a higher rate because travel sits inside it, and a tutor chosen from whoever will drive here. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; our UAE lessons are over live video.

faqs.question: How do we know after six weeks whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By comparing the school's next assessment against a baseline recorded before the first session: the last marked grade, the assessment it came from, and the specific fault the tutor expected to find. At six weeks the tutor explains the result either way. Legitimate reasons for no movement include a structural gap, an assessment covering pre-tutoring content, or independent work not being done. A vague report plus a suggestion to continue is not one of them.

faqs.question: Which subjects do Karama students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics on both IGCSE codes is the highest volume, followed by chemistry and physics, then accounting and economics, then English language accuracy. The pattern follows the district's household mix: commerce and professional families, and homes where English is a second or third language. Accounting deserves a mention because marks there depend on the layout of a statement as much as the arithmetic inside it, so drilling presentation against past papers produces quick, visible gains.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child catch up if they are two years behind in mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not in six weeks, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling. A two-year gap in algebraic fluency is structural: the student is missing the foundations that current work assumes, so the work has to go backwards before it goes forwards. Expect two to three terms of consistent weekly work with independent practice between sessions. The grade may not move for the first half of that, which is why the baseline and the explanation at each review matter more than usual.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes for Karama students?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutoring service should. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and redistributing them is a copyright problem as well as a signal about how a provider operates. We reference the official source, tell you where the school should be issuing material from, and work with what your child legitimately has. A provider offering a downloadable library of board material has told you something useful about itself.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring two subjects at once, or one at a time?
faqs.answer: One at a time, almost always, for a household making a real financial trade-off. Pick the subject where the grade is closest to a boundary, run a defined block of six to eight weeks, review it against school data, and then move the slot to the next subject. Two simultaneous subjects double the cost and halve the independent practice the student can do for each. The exception is a Diploma student in a coursework term, where a short concentrated block alongside a weekly subject slot is reasonable.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a licence, and can we check it?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. You can ask to see it, and the application route is published on the MoHRE private tutor licensing service page.

faqs.question: Our afternoons are quiet but our evenings are not. Can sessions be early?
faqs.answer: In Karama, more often than anywhere else in Dubai, yes. Children attending the Oud Metha belt are frequently home before three, which makes a 3:30pm or 3:45pm start realistic rather than theoretical. That is also usually the quietest window in the flat, before cooking and before other family members return. Families travelling further, towards Al Quoz or along the Jumeirah road, should expect 4:30pm instead. We set the slot from last week's actual arrival time.

faqs.question: What happens at the first session, and is there anything to pay before it?
faqs.answer: The first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. The tutor works through the marked script with your child, tests where the marks are actually going, and writes you a short note afterwards naming the gap, the order to address it and a realistic timescale. Occasionally that note says a fortnight of structured independent practice would do more than a tutor, and we would rather write that. Send the script, the syllabus code and your preferred slot beforehand so the hour is not spent on discovery.

dubai/karama.closingHeading: Plan the room first, then the subject
dubai/karama.closingBody: Karama is the district where tutoring plans fail on setup rather than on teaching. Travel is short, the schools are close, and the scarce resources are a quiet corner and a free laptop. Decide where the lesson happens, put a pair of earphones on the desk, place two short sessions in the quietest hours the week offers, and keep the long timed papers for a weekend morning. Then pick the tutor on board and syllabus code, record a baseline, and judge the arrangement at six weeks against the school's own assessment rather than against how the sessions felt. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video, so no room is surrendered for the hour.

dubai/knowledge-park.tutorsIntro: Families here usually arrive with a destination in mind and a question about whether the current subject set supports it. The tutors below work on that: the Higher Level choices, the mathematics route, the grades a stated prerequisite actually requires, and the technique that converts understanding into those grades.

intro.heading: Working backwards from the degree, not forwards from the report
paragraphs: Dubai Knowledge Park is the emirate's free zone for learning and human-resource organisations, sitting in the Al Sufouh corridor between Internet City and the coast, with higher-education branch campuses and training institutes on site and Dubai International Academic City holding the larger share of university campuses further east. The households attached to this district are unusual in one specific way: a high proportion of the parents work in education, training or recruitment, and they ask about university entry long before the school's careers programme raises it.

That earlier question changes what useful tutoring looks like. A family that asks in Year 9 which subjects a particular degree expects is in a position to act. A family that asks in Diploma Year 2 is in a position to be told. The gap between those two conversations is usually two or three decisions: which mathematics route, which three Higher Level subjects, whether a science is needed, and whether the IGCSE option block left out something a course later requires.

Most of the published tutoring material for Dubai gets this backwards. It treats the current grade as the problem and the subject as the unit of work, so the answer is always more hours in the weakest subject. Sometimes that is right. Often the more valuable intervention is a single honest conversation about whether Higher Level Chemistry is needed at all for the course the student actually wants, because dropping a Higher Level subject the destination does not require frees enough time to lift the three that matter.

The second thing this district asks about more than most is paperwork, and specifically equivalency. The Ministry of Education's requirements for recognising a foreign secondary certificate are published and specific, and they are routinely misstated. One competitor page ranking for these queries says UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Families choosing an option block in Year 9 need the correct version, not the common one.

What follows is built for that sequence. Destination first, then the route at sixteen, then the mathematics decision, then equivalency, then the grades and the technique that produce them. There is also an honest section on what a KHDA permit for a training institute actually licenses, because in a district full of training organisations the phrase gets used loosely. Lessons are delivered online over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, which is a service offered only in India. Every AED figure below is a market rate attributed to the provider that published it in October 2026, and every entry requirement mentioned should be read on the institution's own published page in the year of application rather than taken from here.

dubai/knowledge-park.programmesIntro: At sixteen a Dubai student chooses between two very different structures, and the choice has consequences for university applications that are hard to reverse later. The notes below describe each programme in terms of what a destination institution actually sees.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45 with three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. Admissions offices see a breadth guarantee: mathematics, a science, a language and a humanity are all present. The cost of that breadth is that no subject can be dropped to protect another.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in the Al Sufouh corridor sit the May session. Predicted grades issued by the school in Diploma Year 2 are what most applications are assessed on, which makes the first year's results more consequential than students assume. No IB session or results date appears on this page; the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly for this project, so ask your coordinator.

programmes.name: A Level and AS Level after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, with no breadth requirement and no core. Depth suits a student with a clear direction and penalises one without, because a narrow set can close options that the Diploma would have kept open. For the UAE equivalency route, one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, is what the published guidance states.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run A Level after Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE, and the choice of three subjects at sixteen is where degree options are most quietly narrowed. Check the stated prerequisite for the courses on the list before the subject choice is made, because an added subject in Year 13 is rarely possible.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The qualification that carries the equivalency count and feeds both post-sixteen routes. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade available, so a tier placed in Year 10 can constrain an application made in Year 13. Pearson does not tier in the same way, and the two are separate qualifications with different codes and papers.
programmes.countryNote: The composition of the option block matters as much as the grades. Five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are required for the British-track equivalency count, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and some degree courses expect a specific IGCSE subject to have been taken at all. Both constraints bite in Year 9.

dubai/knowledge-park.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where a level decision has the longest reach, with the specific consequence rather than a general description. Where a university requirement is mentioned, it should be checked on that institution's own published page rather than taken from any tutoring site.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof, algebra and calculus route, with Higher Level Paper 3 asking for sustained reasoning through one extended problem. A number of engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and economics courses specify this route, frequently at Higher Level, so the decision has to be checked against stated prerequisites rather than assumed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. It suits social sciences, business and some life-science routes well. Taken by a student aiming at an engineering degree it can make an application harder than the grade suggests, which is why the route is a destination decision rather than a difficulty decision.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Required or strongly expected by many engineering and physical science courses. Marks leak in derivations and in uncertainty handling rather than in recall, and the scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, so a weak design caps a well-executed experiment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The subject most often taken at Higher Level without checking whether the destination requires it, and the one that costs the most time when it is not needed. Where it is needed, for medicine and many life sciences, the Higher Level extensions assume Standard Level material is automatic rather than recalled.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High content volume and the Diploma science most damaged by rereading notes rather than retrieving them. Several health-science routes expect it, sometimes alongside Chemistry, so the pairing should be checked before both are taken at Higher Level on the assumption that more is safer.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries a large share of the marks. For applications to economics degrees the mathematics route usually matters more than the economics grade, which surprises families: several courses expect Analysis and Approaches, and an Economics Higher Level grade does not substitute for it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case application rather than recall, with a Higher Level extension adding extended response. Useful and widely accepted, but it is not a mathematics substitute for quantitative business or finance courses, which is the most common misunderstanding attached to it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis under time pressure plus an individual oral tracing a global issue through two texts. It also carries weight as evidence of English proficiency in some admissions processes, which makes the grade relevant beyond the subject itself.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics and Double Award Science
subjects.description: The two option-block decisions that most often close a door. A Core mathematics tier caps the grade, and a single-award rather than double-award science can mean a sixth form will not accept a student onto two A Level sciences. Both are decided in Year 9.

sections.heading: Living beside the campuses, and what it changes about subject choice
paragraphs: There is a real advantage to this corridor that has nothing to do with schools. Higher-education campuses and training institutes operate inside Knowledge Park itself, and Dubai International Academic City further east holds most of the emirate's university branch campuses. Entry requirements here are visible things, published on institutional pages and discussed at open days a short drive away, rather than abstractions a school mentions in Year 12.

Families who use that tend to make better decisions, and the reason is sequencing. A destination has requirements. Those requirements dictate subjects and levels. Subjects and levels dictate which grades matter. Only then does the question of tutoring arise, and by that point it is a narrow question with a clear answer. Reversing the sequence produces the common Dubai pattern: hours bought in the weakest subject, with nobody having checked whether that subject is needed for anything the student wants.

The table below is a structure rather than a list of requirements, and that distinction matters. Course prerequisites change, differ between institutions, and differ between campuses of the same institution. Any specific requirement must be read on that university's own published page, in the year of application. What the table gives you is the shape of the decision and the point in school at which it has to be taken.

The point worth emphasising is the last column. Most of these decisions are taken in Year 9 or in the first term of Diploma Year 1, and most of them cannot be undone afterwards. A family in this district has the information available to get them right, which is a genuine advantage over a family three emirates away relying on a single careers evening in Year 12.

sections.heading: Maths AA or AI: the choice that closes doors quietly
paragraphs: This is the single most consequential decision in the Diploma and it is frequently taken for the wrong reason. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is the proof, algebra and calculus route. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Both are rigorous and both are respectable. They are not interchangeable in admissions.

The error is almost always the same. A student finds Analysis difficult in the first term, moves to Applications, improves, and everybody is relieved. Two years later the courses on their list specify Analysis, often at Higher Level, and the improved grade is in the wrong subject. The decision that felt like a sensible correction in November of Diploma Year 1 turns out to have been an application decision taken without reference to the application.

There is an opposite error, less damaging but still costly. A student who wants a social science or business degree stays in Analysis at Higher Level because it sounds stronger, loses time across all six subjects to a subject they do not need, and lowers three grades that mattered to protect one that did not. Admissions offices rarely reward Analysis over Applications where the course does not require it.

The right way to settle it is mechanical. List the destination courses. Read what each one states about mathematics, on its own page. If any of them specify Analysis, the decision is made for you. If none do, the choice is genuinely about fit, and then the honest test is a set of real past-paper questions from both routes to see which the student can actually work in. A tutor can run that test in two sessions; it is a far better use of money than a term of support in the wrong course.

sections.heading: Equivalency before admission: the step families leave too late
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that recognises a secondary certificate issued under a foreign curriculum. It is a regulatory step the family completes through the official channel. No tutoring provider performs it, accelerates it or guarantees it, and anybody suggesting otherwise should be treated with suspicion. What tutoring can affect is upstream: whether the subjects and grades the process requires were actually taken and achieved.

For the British track the Ministry publishes a specific and checkable list. The student must show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level graded no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and separately must pass five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education do not count towards those five, which is the detail families most often discover too late.

That exclusion is where families lose a year. A student taking Arabic and Islamic Education plus four other IGCSE subjects has four counting subjects, not six. One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced requirement is five, and composition matters more than the number. This is the detail to carry into a Year 9 option meeting, because by Year 11 the entry list is closed and the subject cannot be added.

On the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears on this page, because the sources consulted state none and nothing could be read on the Ministry's own site. A tutoring page publishing an unsourced IB equivalency figure is guessing with somebody's application, and one of them has already published the wrong IGCSE subject count.

sections.heading: IB Diploma or IGCSE then A Level: how the two routes differ at sixteen
paragraphs: In this corridor both routes are available within a few minutes of each other, so the choice is a genuine one rather than a consequence of where a family already is. It deserves a better treatment than the usual argument about rigour, which is unanswerable and beside the point. The useful comparison is structural: what each route guarantees, what it forecloses, and which kind of student each one punishes.

The Diploma guarantees breadth. Mathematics, a science, a language and a humanity are all present, and three subjects are studied at Higher Level. The consequence is that no subject can be dropped to protect the others, so a student with one genuinely weak area carries it for two years. The compensating benefit is that very few destinations are closed off, which suits a student who does not yet know what they want.

A Level guarantees depth. Three or four subjects, no core, and the capacity to spend far more time on each. The consequence is that the choice made at sixteen is close to final: a student who selects three humanities and later wants engineering has no route back. It suits a student with a clear direction and penalises an undecided one, which is the opposite of how the two routes are usually described.

Two practical points that rarely appear in this comparison. The Diploma's core, meaning Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, is a real time commitment and a real source of stress, worth three points of the 45 through the matrix. And predicted grades function differently: Diploma predictions come from a school's judgement across six subjects and the core, while A Level predictions rest on fewer subjects and therefore move more with a single bad mock. Both affect how an application is assessed.

sections.heading: The short commute, and what it buys you
paragraphs: Knowledge Park shares the Al Sufouh corridor's one real logistical advantage: journeys are short and some of them do not need a car. The tram runs along Al Sufouh Road, the metro is in the next free zone, and several of the schools this corridor uses are a brief ride away. For a secondary student that means a predictable arrival home without an adult leaving a desk, and a session that can realistically begin at a quarter past four.

Compare that with the Dubai average and the difference is substantial. In most of the emirate the earliest workable slot sits around a quarter to five, after a drive that cannot be guaranteed, and the slot moves whenever the traffic does. Here the arrival time is a known quantity, so the weekly arrangement holds through the year instead of quietly collapsing in November when somebody's commute got worse.

The practical consequence worth acting on is that the early slot is both better and easier to book. The most requested hour across the whole Dubai market sits between half past five and half past six, which is when the specialists fill first, particularly from January onwards as Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 demand peaks. A family that can genuinely use half past four has a wider choice of tutor at the same market rate.

In-home tutoring makes even less sense from this district than from most. Market in-home rates run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with the travel priced in, per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at 180-350 and home tutors quoted at 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Paying a travel premium so that a tutor can cross Sheikh Zayed Road in the evening peak, to reach a student who could have been at a desk forty minutes earlier, is difficult to justify. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai in any case.

sections.heading: What a KHDA permit actually licenses, in a district full of training institutes
paragraphs: This matters more here than elsewhere, because Knowledge Park contains a genuine concentration of licensed training organisations and the vocabulary gets borrowed loosely by businesses that hold nothing. A KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute is a specific licence issued to an organisation with premises in Dubai. Initial approval comes first, there is a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal must be requested at least thirty days before expiry.

What that licence is not is a badge for individual tutors. There is no KHDA inspection band and no KHDA approval that applies to a private tutor, and no online platform holds one for its tutors because the instrument does not exist in that form. A tutoring provider describing its tutors as carrying a regulator's approval is describing something that cannot be produced on request, and the phrase is the single most dangerous one available in this market.

The parallel instrument for individuals is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, approval or partnership, and does not operate a UAE office or centre. Saying that plainly is more useful to a family in this district than any claim could be, because the parents here can tell the difference and several of them hold the real licences in their own working lives.

sections.heading: What university-facing support costs in this market
paragraphs: Rates in the Dubai market are published inconsistently, so the table below prices by the kind of support rather than by the hour alone. Every AED figure is a market rate gathered in October 2026 and attributed to the provider that published it. None of them is an IB Gram price; our own figure follows a consultation and a trial session, because it depends on the subject, the level and the time remaining.

The bands for reference: a budget online tutor, generally a university student, runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist is AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

The important caution concerns a category this district encounters often. Admissions consultancy is a separate market with its own pricing, and it is worth keeping the two apart. A subject tutor raising a Higher Level grade is doing something measurable. A provider promising admission to a named institution is promising something no third party controls, and a claim that tutoring is required for admission, equivalency or school progression is a false-urgency claim about a regulatory and selective process.

One honest observation about value. The cheapest high-value intervention available to a family in this corridor is not an hourly package at all. It is two diagnostic sessions before a subject-choice decision, which can prevent two years of effort in a subject the destination never required. That is a small purchase with a large effect, and almost nobody sells it because it does not recur.
