sections.heading: Predicted grades, references and the Diploma timeline
paragraphs: Most university applications from a Dubai school are assessed on predicted grades rather than on final results, and families consistently underestimate how early those predictions are formed. For a Diploma student, the evidence a school uses accumulates across Diploma Year 1 and the first part of Diploma Year 2. A weak first-year report therefore has a longer reach than its position in the timetable suggests, because it becomes part of the evidence base for the number that goes on the application.

That changes when intervention is worth making. Support in Diploma Year 1 affects the prediction. Support in the final term affects the result, which matters for confirming an offer but not for receiving one. Families who understand that sequence tend to act a year earlier than families who do not, and they get more for the same money because the earlier work also has time to compound.

The second element is the reference, which rests on more than grades. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service all feed a teacher's sense of a student, and all of them are easy to neglect because none produces a weekly mark. A student who has engaged seriously with the Extended Essay gives a referee something specific to write about, and that is worth more than an additional point in a sixth subject.

The honesty boundary applies here with particular force. A tutor may teach, question, structure and give feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not write a personal statement, an admissions essay or any part of an application that is represented as the student's own. The same rule covers internal assessments, Extended Essays and Theory of Knowledge. Research for this project found a provider in this market selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750, which is academic malpractice under IB rules and lands on the candidate.

sections.heading: Academic honesty where the stakes are an application
paragraphs: The pressure to cross the line is highest at exactly the point where the consequences are worst. A student in the final months of Diploma Year 2, with an offer in view, an internal assessment unfinished and an application essay unwritten, is who the least reputable part of this market is built to serve. The transaction is quick, the student is desperate, and the risk transfers entirely to them.

Under IB rules, submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice. The investigation falls on the candidate, and the consequence can reach the whole Diploma rather than a single subject grade. For an application, an institution finding that an essay was not written by the applicant is a matter of admission being withdrawn. Neither of those outcomes falls on the provider who sold the document.

The legitimate alternative is not weaker, and it is worth being specific about what it contains. A tutor may explain what each published criterion rewards and the marks it carries. A tutor may interrogate a research question until it can generate usable data in the time remaining. A tutor may teach the structure of a reflection or an argument, and may read a draft the student has produced and say, in writing, where it falls short of a criterion. The student writes every word.

For parents in a district where many people work in education, the test is a familiar one. Ask what the student will be able to defend in a conversation with their teacher. A student who has done the work can discuss the method, the choices and the limitations. A student handed a finished document cannot, and schools in Dubai are alert to that gap because they encounter this market as often as parents do.

process.title: Start from the destination, not the grade
process.description: Tell us the courses or course types on the list, even loosely. Those stated prerequisites decide which subjects and levels matter, and that decides what tutoring is for. A family that gives us the destination gets a narrower and cheaper plan than one that gives us a subject and a worry.

process.title: Check the current subject set against them
process.description: We go through the proposed or current subjects and levels against what each destination publishes, and write down what is required and what is at risk. If a Higher Level subject is not needed anywhere on the list, that is worth knowing before another term is spent defending it.

process.title: Send the last marked paper for the target subject
process.description: Once the target subject is clear, the plan comes from a marked paper rather than a conversation. Every lost mark is classified as knowledge, technique or timing, and the proportions decide whether content, mark-scheme work or a watch on the desk is the priority.

process.title: Trial the tutor at the slot you will keep
process.description: The trial runs on a normal weekday at the time you intend to use, which from this corridor can genuinely be a quarter past four. You watch the named tutor work with your child before committing, and you find out whether the early slot suits them after the journey home.

process.title: Review against the next marked evidence
process.description: Progress is judged on the next marked assessment and against the named question types, not on how the sessions felt. If those have not moved, the plan or the tutor changes. For a Diploma student the review point should sit before predicted grades are formed, not after.

whyPoints.title: The plan runs backwards from the destination
whyPoints.description: Prerequisites decide subjects, subjects decide which grades matter, and only then does tutoring have a defined job. Reversing that sequence produces hours bought in the weakest subject without anyone checking whether the destination requires it at all.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency rules quoted, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: Five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count. A ranking competitor page says six. Getting that wrong changes a Year 9 option block and is discovered two years later.

whyPoints.title: We say what no figure is available for
whyPoints.description: No IB points threshold for Ministry equivalency appears on this page, because none could be read on the Ministry's own site. An unsourced number on a tutoring page is worse than a gap, because a family plans around it.

whyPoints.title: No claimed accreditation, in a district that would know
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval or partnership, and runs no UAE office. A KHDA Educational Services Permit licenses premises, not tutors, and we will not borrow the vocabulary.

whyPoints.title: A small purchase we will recommend over a large one
whyPoints.description: Two diagnostic sessions before a subject-choice decision can prevent two years spent on a subject the destination never required. It does not recur, which is why almost nobody sells it, and it is usually the best-value thing available.

whyPoints.title: We never write what has to be the student's own
whyPoints.description: Not an internal assessment, not an Extended Essay, not a personal statement. We teach criteria, question designs and give written feedback on drafts the student produced. A student who did the work can defend it; one who did not cannot.

faqs.question: Living beside the Knowledge Park campuses, how do we choose between Maths AA and AI?
faqs.answer: Settle it from the destination rather than from the current grade. Analysis and Approaches is the proof, algebra and calculus route; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with the calculator assumed throughout. Several engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and economics courses specify Analysis, often at Higher Level, so read each institution's own stated prerequisite first. If none specify it, the choice is genuinely about fit, and the honest test is real past-paper questions from both routes attempted cold across two diagnostic sessions.

faqs.question: My child wants to move from Analysis to Applications after a hard first term. Is that safe?
faqs.answer: It is safe academically and sometimes costly for applications, which is why it should be treated as an application decision rather than a relief. The common pattern is a student who struggles in the first term, switches, improves, and discovers two years later that the courses on their list specify Analysis. Before switching, read the stated mathematics requirement for every destination on the list. If none specify Analysis, switching is reasonable. If any do, the question becomes whether the difficulty is content, technique or timing.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold a KHDA licence or approval for its tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and nor can any online platform, because the instrument does not exist in that form. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to a training institute with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. There is no KHDA inspection band or approval covering individual private tutors. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation or partnership and operates no UAE office.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the Ministry of Education equivalency route count?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor page states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five, and composition matters more than the count. Take that into the Year 9 option meeting, because the entry list closes long before Year 11.

faqs.question: What IB score does the Ministry of Education require for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No figure appears on this page, deliberately. The sources consulted for the British and American tracks state no IB points threshold, and nothing could be read on the Ministry's own site, so publishing a number would mean inventing one. The British-track requirements are documented and quoted here; the American-track English and mathematics thresholds are too. For the IB, check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and treat any tutoring page quoting a specific IB figure without a citation as unreliable.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma or A Level the better route for university from a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: They suit different students rather than ranking against each other. The Diploma guarantees breadth across six subjects with three at Higher Level plus the core, so few destinations close, but a weak subject cannot be dropped and is carried for two years. A Level offers depth in three or four subjects with no core, which suits a student with a clear direction and penalises an undecided one, because the choice at sixteen is close to final. Check prerequisites before selecting either.

faqs.question: Does living near the Knowledge Park campuses actually help with applications?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and more than families use. Entry requirements become visible things rather than abstractions: higher-education campuses and training institutes operate in this corridor, and Dubai International Academic City further east holds most of the emirate's university branches. Visiting in Year 11 rather than Year 13 tends to settle subject arguments quickly, because a stated prerequisite read on an institution's own page is harder to argue with than a parental opinion. The decisions it informs are taken in Year 9 and early Diploma Year 1.

faqs.question: How early do predicted grades start forming for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Earlier than families expect. The evidence a school uses accumulates across Diploma Year 1 and the first part of Diploma Year 2, so a weak first-year report has a longer reach than its place in the timetable suggests. That changes when intervention pays: support in Diploma Year 1 affects the prediction that goes on an application, while support in the final term affects the result, which matters for confirming an offer rather than receiving one. Acting a year earlier buys more for the same money.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a university personal statement?
faqs.answer: Not by writing any part of it. A tutor may discuss what a statement is for, question whether a claim is evidenced, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write it, redraft it into final form, or supply text. The same applies to internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. An institution finding that an application essay was not written by the applicant treats it as grounds for withdrawing an offer, and that consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Is tutoring necessary to get equivalency or a university place in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No, and any page implying otherwise is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory and selective process. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education procedure completed through the official channel; admission is an institutional decision no third party controls. What tutoring can legitimately affect is whether the required subjects were taken and the required grades achieved. If a provider promises admission to a named institution, that promise is about something they do not control, and it should end the conversation.

faqs.question: What is the earliest session time that works from the Knowledge Park corridor?
faqs.answer: Around a quarter past four, which is earlier than most of Dubai manages. The tram along Al Sufouh Road and the metro in the next free zone put several schools within a short ride, so a secondary student's arrival home is a known quantity rather than a traffic guess. That has a practical benefit beyond convenience: the most requested slot across the market is between half past five and half past six, so a family that can genuinely use half past four has a wider choice of specialist at the same rate.

faqs.question: Which schools in this corridor offer both post-sixteen routes?
faqs.answer: The corridor contains both, which is why the comparison is a live decision here. Nearby options include Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Regent International School, Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, with the Al Barsha cluster adding Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Dubai American Academy, American School of Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. Ask each school directly which route it runs at sixteen and what its subject combinations allow. Those schools are named as context only.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons do. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and states a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website and e-services. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

faqs.question: Can a Knowledge Park student hold entries with two different exam boards at once?
faqs.answer: That is a question for the school's exams officer rather than a tutor, because entry arrangements sit with the centre. In practice Dubai schools generally run one board per subject and some run different boards across subjects, so a student can hold Cambridge entries in some subjects and Pearson in others. What matters for support is knowing which code applies to each subject, since Cambridge and Pearson differ in paper structure, tiering and timetable. Tutoring aimed at the wrong code wastes its first sessions.

faqs.question: What is the best-value thing to buy if our budget is limited?
faqs.answer: Two diagnostic sessions before a subject-choice decision, in Year 9 or early in Diploma Year 1. They establish whether the proposed subjects and levels support the destinations on the list, and whether a Higher Level choice is genuinely needed. That can prevent two years of effort in a subject nothing required, which no amount of weekly support later recovers. It does not recur, which is why it is rarely offered, and at market rates of AED 150-300 an hour it is a small purchase.

dubai/knowledge-park.closingHeading: Decide the destination, then let it set the subjects
dubai/knowledge-park.closingBody: Families in this corridor have an advantage most of Dubai does not: entry requirements are visible, published and close by. Use them in the right order. Name the destinations, read what each one states, check the current subjects and levels against that, and only then decide what tutoring is for. Send us the course list, the current subject set and the last marked paper in the subject that matters, and you will get a written note of what is required, what is at risk and a short plan with a review point before predicted grades form. Lessons run online over live video, one to one.

dubai/la-mer.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are the ones La Mer families ask for most: Diploma Mathematics and the sciences at Higher Level, and IGCSE Maths, Physics and Chemistry in Year 11. Each works to one syllabus code and to one school's own assessment calendar, not to a generic scheme of work bought off a shelf.

intro.heading: Why the school run, not the subject, decides your tutoring week
paragraphs: La Mer is a thin strip of Jumeirah 1 between Jumeirah Beach Road and the water. Port de La Mer, the beachfront residences and the low-rise blocks behind the boardwalk hold a few thousand residents, and almost none of them have a secondary school inside walking distance. Children here are driven: west along Jumeirah Beach Road towards Al Safa and Umm Suqeim, inland across Al Wasl, or up Sheikh Zayed Road towards Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. That drive, twice a day, is the single fact that shapes what a tutoring week can look like from this address.

Most parents start the search with a subject in mind. Chemistry at Higher Level is slipping, or Paper 2 in IGCSE Maths came back at a grade 5 when the predicted grade said 7. The subject is the easy part. The hard part is finding a slot that actually exists. A 3:10pm finish at a school in Al Safa becomes a 3:55pm arrival back at La Mer on a quiet Tuesday and a 4:30pm arrival in January, when Beach Road absorbs half of Jumeirah's traffic and the school buses stack at the Pearl Jumeira lights. Book a 4pm in-home session against that and you have paid a tutor to sit in your lobby.

Online lessons remove the problem rather than working around it. A La Mer student closes a laptop at 5:45pm and is at the dinner table a minute later. More usefully, the tutor pool stops being whoever can reach Jumeirah 1 by car in rush hour. If your child needs a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist who has marked the Paper 3 style question your school keeps setting, you are choosing from everyone available on live video rather than everyone within a twenty-minute drive of the beach.

The second thing La Mer parents run into is board confusion. The schools within reach of this address run at least three different assessment systems: Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and the IB continuum from the Primary Years Programme through to the Diploma. Two children on the same floor of the same building can sit different Maths papers with different formula booklets in the same June. Any tutoring that ignores which code is printed on the front of the paper spends its first three sessions finding out.

This page is written for that reality. It gives you the AED figures the Dubai market actually charges, with the source attached; a timetable of when a lesson can start from a La Mer address; the Cambridge and Pearson entry deadlines that fall months before the exam itself; what KHDA does and does not tell you in an inspection report; and the line a tutor must not cross on an Internal Assessment. Where a figure could not be verified against a primary source, it has been left off the page rather than guessed.

dubai/la-mer.programmesIntro: Three assessment systems account for nearly every secondary student living in Jumeirah 1. The notes below describe what each one demands in the Dubai context, and what a La Mer family should expect it to cost in evening hours between October and the exam window.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. There is no external exam unless the school enters students for eAssessment. What catches families is the move into MYP 4 and 5, where criterion C and D work stops rewarding effort and starts rewarding analysis against a command term.
programmes.countryNote: In Jumeirah 1 the MYP is run by the IB continuum schools in Al Safa and Umm Suqeim, and the pressure point is the jump into Diploma Year 1. A student who scored 6s on MYP criteria can land a 4 in a DP Higher Level subject because the mark scheme changed shape underneath them.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth 20 to 25 per cent of the grade, marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The Diploma total runs to 45 points, of which three come from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students living in La Mer sit the May session, which is what UAE schools use. IB session and results dates are not published on this page because ibo.org could not be confirmed directly; ask your school's IB coordinator for the dated version rather than trusting a figure from a tutoring site.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate qualifications that parents routinely treat as one. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C or 5. Pearson Edexcel does not tier in the same way and uses different paper structures and codes. Both run a June series; both also run a November series, which UAE schools use for resits.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a British-curriculum city by enrolment, so most La Mer teenagers will sit one of these two systems at 16 before choosing A Level or the Diploma. Five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are what the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency route asks for, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five.

dubai/la-mer.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects La Mer parents enquire about most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go missing. A tutor who cannot name the component weightings for your child's level is not working to the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with a Higher Level Paper 3 that asks for sustained reasoning over a single extended problem. Most marks are lost in Paper 3 and in the unseen proof questions, not in the routine calculus. HL students who were comfortable in MYP maths are the ones most often surprised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-driven work, with the graphic display calculator assumed in almost every question. Students lose marks by giving an answer without the modelling assumption, or by reporting a correlation without comment. The route matters for university entry, so check the prerequisite before switching off Analysis.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields carry the Higher Level load, and the scientific investigation is marked against criteria rather than against a right answer. Uncertainty treatment is where competent students shed marks: a correct result with an unquantified uncertainty scores less than a cruder result handled honestly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the usual trouble, and the Higher Level extension questions assume the Standard Level material is automatic rather than recalled. Data-based questions reward candidates who read the axes before the stem. Jumeirah 1 families ask for Chemistry Higher Level more than any other science.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Marks go missing where a command term is ignored: an outline answered as a description, an explain answered as a list. The scientific investigation needs a question narrow enough to generate real data, which is where most of the tutoring hours go.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks, and the Higher Level paper adds quantitative work that Standard Level candidates never see. The portfolio of commentaries is the other pressure point, because each one must be anchored to a real published article within a word limit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and the individual oral asks for a global issue traced through two texts. Students who read widely still lose marks by writing about content rather than about the writer's choices. Structured practice against the assessment criteria moves this faster than more reading.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier decision is the whole conversation. Cambridge Core caps the grade, so a borderline student moved to Core in Year 10 cannot reach the top grades in Year 11. Extended candidates lose marks on method rather than arithmetic, and on questions that span two topics at once.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics and Chemistry
subjects.description: Electricity in Physics and moles in Chemistry are the two topics that produce most of the enquiries from Jumeirah families. Both are fixable in a run of focused sessions because the marks sit in a small number of question types that repeat across papers and series.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application rather than recall. The Higher Level paper adds extended response under tighter time, and students lose marks by defining a term instead of applying it to the stimulus organisation. The internal assessment requires primary or secondary research planned early, not collected late.

dubai/la-mer.regionsTitle: Jumeirah 1 and the coast: where La Mer families sit
dubai/la-mer.regionsIntro: La Mer does not operate alone. The school run, the sibling drop-offs and the tutoring slot all depend on which neighbouring community a family actually crosses on a weekday. These are the areas that matter from this address.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: The district La Mer sits inside. Villa plots behind Jumeirah Beach Road feed the long-established British schools, and the 2 Street cut-through is the route most families use to avoid the beach traffic at 3pm.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: The reclaimed island immediately north, reached by a single causeway. Its traffic merges onto the same Beach Road junction as La Mer, which is why both communities see the same 4pm bottleneck on a school day.

regions.name: City Walk
regions.note: Inland across Al Wasl Road, five to ten minutes away off-peak. Apartment families here overlap heavily with La Mer on school choice, and the two communities tend to ask for the same Diploma subject specialists.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The corridor between Jumeirah and Sheikh Zayed Road. Crossing it is how a La Mer child reaches schools in Al Safa and Al Quoz, and it is the segment most likely to add fifteen minutes in the evening peak.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Further west along the coast, with several primary and secondary campuses inside them. Many La Mer families drive through these districts twice a day without living in them.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Home to IB continuum and British secondary campuses that take a share of Jumeirah 1 students. A 3:30pm finish here is a 4:15pm arrival at La Mer in term time.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: The nearest dense school cluster to La Mer, with British and IB schools within a few minutes of each other. Siblings in different systems at adjacent campuses is a common Jumeirah pattern.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Twenty to thirty-five minutes from La Mer along Beach Road or Sheikh Zayed Road. The selective British secondary schools here pull a steady number of Jumeirah 1 families each year.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah 1 and Al Safa
schoolClusters.note: The closest cluster to La Mer and the one that fills most of the morning run. British and IB schools sit within a few minutes of each other here, so two siblings can be on different assessment systems while leaving the same front door at the same time.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, twenty to thirty-five minutes from La Mer depending on the hour. Families usually accept the longer drive for a specific programme, which is also why their tutoring slot has to start later than the Al Safa families' slot.

dubai/la-mer.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request from Jumeirah 1. All of them are delivered over live video, because the drive that makes an in-home booking expensive in this area is the same drive that makes it late.

modes.description: A fixed slot, usually 4:45pm or later on a weekday, held with the same tutor across a term. The session works to your child's own school calendar: the unit test in two weeks, the mock in January, the paper in May. Screen sharing and an annotated whiteboard replace the exercise book being pushed across a table.

sections.heading: What time can a lesson actually start from La Mer?
paragraphs: Start with the bell, not with the tutor's diary. Dubai secondary schools generally finish somewhere between 2:45pm and 3:35pm, and the schools La Mer families use are spread across Jumeirah 1, Al Safa, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh. Add the return drive in the evening peak, add fifteen minutes for a snack and a change out of uniform, and the earliest honest slot from this address is around 4:45pm for most families and 4:15pm for the few whose school is inside Jumeirah 1 itself.

The table below is indicative and should be checked against your own school's timetable, which varies by year group and by day. Secondary year groups often finish later than primary on at least two afternoons a week for enrichment or sport, and Diploma Year 2 students in some schools have a study period that releases them earlier. What matters is that you set the tutoring slot from the real bell rather than from a convenient assumption.

This is also where the online delivery earns its place. An in-home tutor booked for 4pm has to leave their own location at roughly 3:15pm to clear Beach Road, which means they price the drive into the hour and still risk arriving as your child does. A live video session booked for 4:45pm starts at 4:45pm. Over a thirty-week school year that difference is several hours of teaching that otherwise evaporates into traffic.

One further point specific to this stretch of coast. Jumeirah Beach Road carries leisure traffic as well as school traffic, and La Mer itself is a destination, so Thursday and Friday evenings behave differently from Monday evenings. Families here tend to settle on a Monday-to-Wednesday pattern for the weekly slot and keep the weekend for longer intensive work.

sections.heading: The Beach Road hour, and what it does to an in-home booking
paragraphs: An in-home tutor is not selling you an hour of teaching. They are selling you an hour of teaching plus two drives, and in Jumeirah 1 those drives are not short. A tutor living in Al Barsha or Al Quoz who takes a 5pm booking at La Mer loses the best part of ninety minutes to the road on a weekday. That cost appears in the hourly rate, which is exactly why Dubai in-home rates sit well above online rates for the same qualification level.

There is a second cost that nobody prices. A tutor who has spent forty minutes in traffic arrives flat, and the first ten minutes of the session go on settling rather than teaching. A tutor who has to leave by 6pm to reach a second booking in Jumeirah 3 will stop teaching at 5:50pm regardless of what your child has just started to understand. Over a term, those edges eat a meaningful share of what you paid for.

The geography of La Mer makes this sharper than it is in a villa community with several road exits. Traffic from La Mer, Pearl Jumeira and the Jumeirah 1 blocks funnels onto the same Beach Road junctions, and the leisure traffic heading to the beachfront overlaps with the school run for part of the afternoon. A tutor's estimate of twenty minutes in October becomes thirty-five in January without anybody doing anything wrong.

IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; that is an India-only service, and this page will not pretend otherwise. What the online format gives a Jumeirah 1 family instead is a start time that holds, a tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than the postcode, and a rate that is not carrying somebody's fuel and parking.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Jumeirah: the AED bands, with sources
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai queries publish no price at all, and two of the remaining three quote in US dollars. The table below gives the Dubai market in AED, with the provider who published each figure named alongside it. These are market rates gathered in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list: our own figure comes from a consultation and a trial session, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks are left.

The pattern worth understanding is that the spread is driven by scarcity rather than by quality alone. A university student who can explain IGCSE algebra competently sits at the bottom of the range because there are many of them. A Higher Level Chemistry teacher who can diagnose a weak scientific investigation from a draft sits near the top because there are not. Paying mid-range money for a bottom-range tutor is the most common way a Jumeirah family wastes a term.

Monthly packages are quoted widely in this market and are worth reading carefully. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide before you compare: an eight-session package at AED 799 is about AED 100 an hour, which tells you something real about who is teaching it. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

One honest note about timing. Rates in this market firm up between January and April, when Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 demand peaks and the good specialists fill their evening slots. A La Mer family starting in October is buying from a wider pool at a calmer price than the same family starting in March.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for a Jumeirah 1 address
paragraphs: The question most La Mer parents actually want answered is whether a tutor in the room is better. For a seven-year-old who needs an adult to keep them at the table, often yes. For a Year 11 IGCSE candidate or a Diploma student, the evidence that matters is different: what decides the outcome is whether the tutor knows the paper, and the paper is the same whether they are sitting beside your child or sharing a screen with them.

Set the two formats side by side on the things that differ. Travel, cost, the size of the pool you are choosing from, and what happens when a session needs to move. On every one of those, a Jumeirah 1 address with a single main road out of it tilts towards the online format. The exception is genuinely practical rather than pedagogical: some families want another adult present for a younger child, and online cannot provide that.

There is also a scheduling argument that only becomes obvious after a term. An online slot can move by thirty minutes on a Tuesday because a school fixture overran. An in-home slot cannot move by thirty minutes, because the tutor has already left and has a second booking afterwards. Across a school year with sports days, exam weeks, half-terms and a Ramadan timetable, that flexibility is worth more than most families expect at the point of booking.

The honest limitation is bandwidth and discipline. A live video lesson needs a quiet room, a charged device and a child who is not also holding a phone. Jumeirah 1 apartments are not short of good connections, but they are short of quiet corners in a household with three children, and the families who get the most out of the format are the ones who solve that before the first session rather than during it.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost no competing page in this market names a single exam session, let alone an entry deadline. That is a strange gap, because the deadlines are where families lose options. An entry closes, a tier is locked, and a decision that felt reversible in November is final by February. The table below counts backwards from the papers rather than forwards from today, using dates published by Cambridge International and Pearson themselves.

The Cambridge March series is the clearest worked example of why this matters. Final entries for the March 2027 series were due on 27 November 2026, the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, and results reach centres through Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027 with certificates in late June. The entry closed more than two months before the first paper. A tier change after that date is not a conversation, it is an administrative impossibility.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in before you plan a revision schedule around a timetable found online. Pearson Edexcel publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live PDF is the only version worth planning against.

IB dates are deliberately absent from this table. The IB's own site could not be confirmed directly for this project, so no IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page. UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's IB coordinator holds the dated internal deadlines for the Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay, which in practice bind a Diploma student far more tightly than the exam window does.

sections.heading: KHDA, the six inspection bands, and what a report leaves out
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a rating on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. For a La Mer family comparing two schools in Al Safa, that report is the most useful public document available, and it is also widely misread.

The rating is a whole-school judgement. A school rated Very Good can contain a department that is struggling, and a school rated Good can have an outstanding sixth form. The inspection narrative, not the headline band, is where that detail sits. Read the sections on attainment and progress in your child's phase and subject group, and read the recommendations, which name what the inspectors told the school to fix. A school that has carried the same recommendation for three years is telling you something.

What a KHDA report does not do is tell you anything about private tutors. Inspection covers schools, not the tutor your child sees at 5pm. There is no KHDA rating for individual tutors, and any tutoring provider implying that it holds a KHDA inspection band or an approval for its tutors is describing something that does not exist in that form. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to a training institute with premises, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

Two pieces of Dubai context are worth having alongside the report. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. And the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More places in the IB sector is relevant if you are weighing a Diploma move for a child now in Year 9.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and most parents in Jumeirah have never been asked to think about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone providing private lessons without one is, in the ministry's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

The eligible categories are broader than people assume. The u.ae guidance names teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two conditions matter to a parent rather than to a tutor. First, the permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Hiring your child's own class teacher privately is the arrangement these rules exist to stop. Second, a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA permit for a training institute, not an individual tutor permit.

No fine amount appears on this page, and you should treat any page that quotes one with care. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. The useful action is simpler than a number: ask any individual tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and treat a vague answer as an answer.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment
paragraphs: This is the part of the market where real damage happens. One page found in the research for this project sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules and puts the student's whole Diploma at risk, not just one grade. A La Mer parent under pressure in March, with a deadline two weeks away and a child who has not started, is precisely the person those pages are built for.

The boundary is clear once it is stated. A tutor may teach the method: what the criteria reward, how a research question gets narrowed until it generates usable data, how uncertainty is handled, how a mathematical exploration is structured, what a global issue looks like in an English oral. A tutor may read a draft the student has produced and say where it falls short of a criterion. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, or provide a model answer intended to be handed in.

In practice the honest version is more useful to the student. The criteria are published, they are specific, and they are marked letter by letter with a stated allocation. A Diploma student who understands that a particular criterion carries a fixed share of the marks, and that their draft is currently losing most of it, has somewhere concrete to go. A student handed finished text learns nothing and carries the risk alone, because the IB's investigation lands on the candidate.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. If a tutoring provider offers to produce any of it for your child, that offer is the reason to walk away rather than the reason to buy. IB Gram's sessions on this work are teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own material, and that is stated here because the distinction is not visible from a price list.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the Dubai calendar around the tutoring slot
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for. KHDA's mandatory subject guidelines state the requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. For a La Mer family this means the timetable your child already carries is fuller than the IB or IGCSE subject list suggests, and the tutoring slot competes with homework in subjects nobody mentioned at the open day.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both Arab and non-Arab groups are strictly prohibited due to different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson.

One constraint matters for anyone offering tutoring in these subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach them. Any support in these subjects therefore works to the school's own material rather than to an imported scheme of work.

The academic calendar then shapes when real revision happens. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a different household rhythm, and families in Jumeirah routinely move the weekly slot to after Iftar for that period. The winter break lands in the middle of IGCSE and Diploma mock preparation, and the long summer sits immediately after results. A tutoring plan that ignores these is a plan that collapses twice a year.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what a Jumeirah 1 family should file
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university or employer can accept, and it is handled by the Ministry of Education rather than by a school or a tutoring company. The British-track requirements are published and specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

The detail that trips families up is what counts towards those five. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. If you are choosing an IGCSE option block in Year 9, that difference changes the decision, and it is worth checking against the Ministry's own guidance rather than against a tutoring site.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears on this page, because the source consulted for the British and American tracks states none and no figure could be read on the Ministry's own site. Anyone publishing an IB equivalency score without that citation is guessing.

Two cautions to carry into the process. Equivalency is a regulatory step the family completes through the official channel; it is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Where tutoring helps is upstream: making sure the five IGCSE subjects are passed at the needed grade, and that the A Level or Diploma route taken actually matches the course your child wants to apply for.

process.title: Tell us the school, the board and the bell
process.description: The first thing we ask is which school, which year group and what time the school day actually ends, because that decides the slot before anything else does. The second is which board: Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel or IB, and at what level. Those four facts narrow the tutor list more than a long description of the problem does.

process.title: Send the last piece of marked work
process.description: A marked mock, a returned unit test or a teacher comment on a draft tells us more in two minutes than a diagnostic call does in thirty. We want to see where the marks went, not where you think they went. If there is nothing marked yet, the first session doubles as the diagnostic and you get the written version afterwards.

process.title: Meet the tutor in a trial session
process.description: You see the specific tutor teaching your specific child before any commitment to a term. The trial runs at the slot you intend to keep, so you also find out whether 4:45pm on a Tuesday actually works for your household after the Beach Road return rather than in theory.

process.title: Fix the slot and the topic list
process.description: We agree a named list of topics and the assessment dates they are aimed at, in writing, before the weekly sessions start. For a Year 11 IGCSE candidate that means the January mock and the June paper. For a Diploma student it means the school's own internal deadlines, which bind harder than the exam window.

process.title: Review at the next piece of marked evidence
process.description: Progress gets judged against the next marked mock or unit test, not against a feeling after four weeks. If the marks have not moved in the topics we targeted, the right response is to change the approach or change the tutor, and we would rather say that than keep selling the same hour.

whyPoints.title: The slot holds because nobody is driving
whyPoints.description: A live video session booked for 4:45pm starts at 4:45pm. From a La Mer address, where every exit funnels onto the same Beach Road junctions, that is not a small thing: across a thirty-week school year it is the difference between buying teaching and buying somebody's commute.

whyPoints.title: The tutor is chosen for the syllabus, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Your child's Paper 3 does not care where the tutor lives. Removing the drive from the equation means the shortlist is everyone who can teach Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, rather than everyone who can teach it and reach Jumeirah 1 before five.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure on this page carries its source
whyPoints.description: The rate bands here are attributed to the provider that published them, with the month they were gathered. Three of the best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all. You should be able to check a number before you plan around it.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: Teaching the method, questioning the research design and giving feedback on the student's own draft is support. Supplying finished coursework is malpractice that lands on the candidate. We state which side of that line we work on, because a price list does not show it.

whyPoints.title: Dates come from the boards, not from a blog
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from the boards' own timetable pages. IB session dates are absent because the IB's own site could not be confirmed for this project, and an invented date on a tutoring page is how a family misses an entry deadline.

whyPoints.title: We say when we cannot cover something
whyPoints.description: Some subject and level combinations have a thin specialist pool, particularly minor languages and some Higher Level options. If there is nobody genuinely qualified free at your preferred slot, you get told that and offered the real alternatives rather than being handed a generalist.

faqs.question: Can we book an in-home tutor for a La Mer address?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. The honest comparison is on this page: the Dubai in-home market charges roughly AED 180-500 an hour with the tutor's drive priced in, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. For a Jumeirah 1 address with a single main road out of it, the online format also means a 4:45pm session starts at 4:45pm.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tutoring session can realistically start for a child in La Mer?
faqs.answer: Around 4:45pm for most families, and about 4:15pm for the few whose school sits inside Jumeirah 1. Work it out from the bell rather than from the tutor's diary: a 3:10pm finish in Al Safa becomes a 3:55pm arrival back at La Mer off-peak and closer to 4:30pm in January, once Beach Road is carrying both school and leisure traffic. Add fifteen minutes for a change out of uniform and something to eat. Secondary year groups often finish later on enrichment or sport afternoons, so check your own school's timetable by day.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor cost for a Jumeirah 1 family in 2026?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market in October 2026 runs roughly as follows. A budget online tutor, usually a university student, sits at AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are market figures from those providers, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in La Mer usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no secondary school inside La Mer itself, so families drive. The nearest cluster is Jumeirah 1 and Al Safa, which includes Jumeirah English Speaking School, Jumeirah College, Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, Horizon English School and Latifa School for Girls. The second ring, twenty to thirty-five minutes out, covers Emirates International School Jumeirah, Raffles World Academy, Dubai College and the Al Barsha campuses. Those schools are named as context for the school run, not as institutions IB Gram has any relationship with. Check each school's current KHDA inspection narrative rather than only its headline band.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring as effective for a La Mer student as having a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For a Year 11 IGCSE candidate or a Diploma student, what decides the outcome is whether the tutor knows the paper, and the paper is identical in either format. A shared screen with an annotated whiteboard does the same work as an exercise book pushed across a table, and the session can be revisited afterwards. For a young primary child who needs an adult keeping them at the table, a physical presence genuinely helps, and online cannot provide that. The practical requirement is a quiet room and a device, which is the thing worth solving before the first session.

faqs.question: Which exam board is my child in La Mer actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because parents routinely guess wrong. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are different qualifications with different paper structures and different codes, and Dubai schools use both. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capping the available grade; Pearson does not tier in the same way. The syllabus code on the front of a past paper is the fastest check: 0580 and 0625 are Cambridge Maths and Physics, 4MA1 and 4PH1 are the Pearson equivalents. Tutoring aimed at the wrong code wastes its first sessions.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge IGCSE entries close for a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Months before the exam, which is the part that surprises families. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge set final entries at 27 November 2026, with the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your school's exams officer for the zone and the internal deadline.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legally do with my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the method and give feedback on work the student has produced. That means explaining what each criterion rewards and the marks it carries, helping narrow a research question until it generates usable data, showing how uncertainty or a mathematical exploration should be structured, and reading a draft to say where it falls short. A tutor must not supply text for submission, rewrite a paragraph into final form or provide a model answer to hand in. One provider found in research for this page sells finished assessments outright; that is malpractice and the risk lands on your child.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with La Mer families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page states a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts with care.

faqs.question: Does KHDA inspect private tutors as well as schools?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA oversees private schools in Dubai and publishes an annual inspection rating on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. It does not rate individual private tutors, and there is no inspection band that applies to one. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is something different again: a licence issued to a training institute with premises, requiring initial approval first and renewal at least thirty days before expiry. Any tutoring provider implying it carries a KHDA approval for its tutors is describing something that does not exist in that form.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around an IB or IGCSE timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They sit alongside it. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a La Mer family this means the real homework load is heavier than the IB or IGCSE subject list suggests.

faqs.question: Can a La Mer family move the weekly slot to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Jumeirah families do exactly that. School days shorten during Ramadan and the household rhythm changes, so a 4:45pm slot that works in November is often wrong in the Ramadan weeks. Moving the weekly session to after Iftar keeps the continuity without fighting the timetable. This is one of the practical advantages of a live video format: a slot can be shifted by an hour for a few weeks and shifted back afterwards, which is not possible when a tutor has already left for a second booking elsewhere in Dubai.

faqs.question: After IGCSE in Jumeirah 1, what does Ministry of Education equivalency ask for?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor page states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. No IB points threshold appears here, because none could be read on the Ministry's own site. Equivalency is completed through the official channel, not by a tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Should my child take Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Start from the degree, not from the current grade. Analysis and Approaches is the proof, algebra and calculus route, with a Higher Level Paper 3 that demands sustained reasoning through one extended problem. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with the calculator assumed throughout. Several engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, so check the stated prerequisite for the universities on your list before switching. A tutor can test whether the Higher Level workload is realistic by running your child through genuine past-paper questions from both routes.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's subject in La Mer?
faqs.answer: You get told. Some combinations have a thin pool, particularly minor languages, a few Higher Level options and some Group 3 subjects, and demand across Dubai peaks between January and April when Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 families all arrive at once. If nobody genuinely qualified is free at your preferred slot, the options are a different time, a short wait for a named tutor, or a different structure such as a concentrated block closer to the papers. Being handed a generalist for a Higher Level subject is the outcome worth refusing.

dubai/la-mer.closingHeading: Start from the bell, then pick the tutor
dubai/la-mer.closingBody: If you live in La Mer, the first useful question is not which tutor but which slot. Take your child's actual finish time, add the Beach Road return, add fifteen minutes, and you have the earliest honest start. Then choose on the thing that decides the grade: a tutor who knows the syllabus code, the component weightings and where your child's marks are going. Tell us the school, the year group, the board and the last piece of marked work, and we will put a specific tutor in a trial session at the slot you intend to keep. Lessons run online over live video, so the slot holds.

dubai/living-legends.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB Diploma, MYP and IGCSE subjects to students in and around Living Legends. The brief we give them is narrow on purpose: find out what the student can and cannot do under exam conditions, then work on the second of those two lists.

intro.heading: The content was covered. The paper still goes wrong.
paragraphs: Living Legends sits as a single gated community off Emirates Road, a couple of thousand villas and apartments with no school of its own, which means every child here is bussed out to Sports City, Motor City, Barsha South or further. That matters less for this page than what happens when they get back. The schools families here use are mostly strong, well-inspected and properly staffed. Parents still ask for tutors, and the reason they give is almost always the same sentence: the teacher says the topic has been covered, and my child cannot answer the question.

Both statements are usually true at once. A Diploma or IGCSE scheme of work has to deliver a two-year syllabus inside roughly sixty teaching weeks, alongside coursework supervision, mock cycles and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons that KHDA requires of every Dubai private school whatever its licensed curriculum. There is time to teach each topic properly once. There is rarely time to teach it a second time in a different way for the four students in the set who did not get it the first time, and almost never time to mark thirty timed papers out loud.

That second pass is where marks live. A student who has read the chapter on electrolysis and a student who can answer an eight-mark electrolysis question under time are in different places, and the distance between them is made of specific, nameable skills: reading a command term accurately, laying out working that a marker can follow, choosing which part of the stem to use, knowing when a question wants description and when it wants evaluation. Those are teachable in a one-to-one hour and essentially untouchable in a class of twenty-four.

The other half of the gap is coursework. Internal Assessments carry a fifth to a quarter of most Diploma grades and are marked against named criteria, by letter, with published mark allocations. Students are given the criteria. Very few are taught to read them as a marker reads them, which is why a technically competent science investigation loses marks on research design and a well-written Extended Essay loses the twelve marks allocated to critical thinking. A tutor cannot and must not write any of it. A tutor can make a student read criterion C and see what it is actually asking.

This page is about that gap rather than about a neighbourhood. It sets out where marks go missing topic by topic, what the Internal Assessment criteria ask for and how many marks each carries, which parts of an assessment a school covers and which parts are left to the student, what an hour of genuine independent revision should contain, and what to do with a disappointing mock. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; nobody drives anywhere. Every figure is attributed, and there is no grade claim anywhere on the page.
bullets: Built around the second pass: timed practice, command terms, criterion reading
Internal Assessment and Extended Essay criteria named by letter with mark totals
One-to-one over live video, with the student's own marked script shared on screen
Official board documents cited and linked rather than reproduced or supplied
No grade promises, and no page on this site claims regulator accreditation

dubai/living-legends.programmesIntro: Living Legends families split across three routes, and each one leaves a different kind of work to the student. The notes below describe what is genuinely independent in each, because that is what a tutoring hour has to fill.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each judged out of eight against published band descriptors. Grades one to seven come from the total. The final year carries the Personal Project, supervised but independently produced. The independent work here is learning to write to a descriptor rather than to a task sheet, which is a genuinely new skill for most students.
programmes.countryNote: Students in this part of Dubai often arrive in MYP from a British Year 7 or from an Indian-curriculum primary, and the shift from mark-out-of-twenty to criterion bands is disorientating for a term or two. The commonest useful session for a Living Legends MYP student is one spent reading a returned task against the descriptor that produced the mark.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal Assessments are marked against criteria by letter. The written papers test command terms as hard as they test content, and Higher Level papers assume the student can select from the whole course rather than from the current unit. The independent load is heavy and front-loaded into DP1.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma students we work with around Sports City and Living Legends are usually fine until the first set of real Higher Level papers in DP1, which are the first assessments that draw on topics taught six months apart. That is the point at which a second pass stops being optional and the request for a tutor arrives.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects over two years, with Cambridge subjects tiered as Core or Extended and Pearson papers structured differently again. Codes matter: Cambridge 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610 against Pearson 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. Formula provision, practical assessment and tiering all differ, and a student sitting both boards in one year needs two sets of exam habits.
programmes.countryNote: Schools used by Living Legends families do not all use the same board, and some split boards between departments, so the first thing a tutor here should ask for is the syllabus code rather than the subject name. Getting that wrong wastes four sessions teaching the right content in the wrong format.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is a four-thousand-word independent piece scored out of thirty-four, with twelve of those marks on critical thinking alone. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and an essay on a prescribed title. Neither is taught as a conventional subject, and both are supervised rather than delivered.
programmes.countryNote: These two components generate more late-night panic in Dubai Diploma households than any single subject, because the deadlines are set internally by each school and therefore differ between the schools Living Legends families use. Knowing your own school's internal deadline, not the IB's, is the thing that governs the plan.

dubai/living-legends.subjectsIntro: The subject notes below are written around where the marks actually go, rather than around what each course contains. That is the information a parent needs before deciding which subject gets the hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and the graphic display calculator in every paper. Students who chose it to avoid proof often find statistical inference harder than algebra. Marks go on choosing the wrong test, and on reporting output without saying what it means for the context in the question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: At IGCSE, moles and electrolysis; at Diploma, energetics and organic mechanisms. The characteristic loss is answering an explain question with a description. That is a command-term problem, and fixing it tends to move several topics at once rather than one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Feels like memorisation until a six-mark explain question arrives. The gain comes from structuring extended answers against the mark scheme, and at Diploma level from the statistical handling the scientific investigation expects under criterion B.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall is necessary and not sufficient. Marks are decided by whether the named example answers the specific question asked, and by whether graphs and resource material in the paper are actually used rather than paraphrased.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work and essay argument, assessed separately. Students lose marks by narrating chronology instead of answering the question, and in source papers by describing a source rather than using its provenance to judge its value.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The research methods and ethics content underpins every answer, and students who skip it cannot evaluate a study properly. The Internal Assessment is an experimental replication with a tight structure, and most lost marks are in the design and analysis sections rather than the write-up.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis against a guiding question, Paper 2 a comparative essay, plus the Individual Oral. Reading more does less than learning to build a thesis and sustain it, which is the difference between a competent answer and a high one.

subjects.name: Spanish and French B
subjects.description: Productive skills decide the grade, and they are the ones hardest to practise alone. One-to-one over video is genuinely well suited here, because the whole hour can be spoken in the target language instead of three minutes of a classroom period.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case rewards structured early work. Students list tools instead of applying one properly, and Higher Level candidates lose marks by leaving the evaluation thin after a strong analysis section.

subjects.name: Design Technology and Computer Science
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0478 and 0979
subjects.description: Both are documentation-heavy. The artefact is usually fine; the marks go missing in the design cycle write-up and in the testing and evaluation sections, which students treat as paperwork rather than as assessed work.

dubai/living-legends.regionsIntro: Living Legends has no school inside it, so the relevant geography is the set of school clusters its families use and what each cluster leaves to the student. The notes below are about cohort and provision rather than about driving times.

regions.name: Living Legends
regions.note: A single gated community of villas and towers with no school on site. An IB tutor in Living Legends is therefore working with students from four or five different schools in the same week, which is useful: the same topic goes wrong in different ways depending on who taught it.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: The nearest cluster, with large year groups and broad subject offers. An IGCSE tutor in Dubai Sports City most often picks up students from sets that moved quickly through content and left a backlog of unmarked past papers.

regions.name: Dubai Studio City
regions.note: Mostly apartment households with a shorter run to the Sports City and Motor City schools. Requests here lean towards MYP and lower-secondary support, where criterion reading is the missing skill rather than content.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: A school inside the community and a settled cohort. An IB DP tutor in Motor City sees more Higher Level science and maths requests than anywhere else nearby, usually arriving after the first real DP1 paper.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Longer-established families, often with two or three children at different stages. Online delivery matters here because two siblings can be taught in the same evening at different levels without a second journey for anyone.

regions.name: Mudon and Remraam
regions.note: Larger, newer communities with students spread across many schools. IGCSE tuition in Mudon is commonly booked in the Year 10 spring, once the first mock papers have come back and the gap between coverage and performance is visible.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills
regions.note: A mixed cohort with a school on the edge of the community and a good deal of outward travel. The frequent request here is Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge process support, where the school's internal deadline is the binding constraint.

schoolClusters.city: Sports City, Studio City and Motor City
schoolClusters.note: The closest provision to Living Legends and the source of most of our students here. These schools run British and American routes with IGCSE or equivalent at sixteen, and the recurring pattern is strong content delivery with limited capacity for individually marked timed practice in the term before papers.

schoolClusters.note: Where most of the area's Diploma students actually sit, including the IB continuum schools. Coursework deadlines are set internally by each school, which is why two students living on the same street in Living Legends can be working to Extended Essay deadlines six weeks apart.
