dubai/living-legends.modesIntro: All three patterns below exist to do the same job, which is to put a second pass over material the class has already delivered once. They differ in how the week is shaped around it.

modes.title: Marked-work cycle
modes.description: The student sends a timed question or a draft before the lesson, the tutor marks it against the published criteria or mark scheme, and the lesson is spent on the marking rather than on fresh teaching. It is the most efficient use of an hour for a student who has the content and loses marks on technique, and it is the default we recommend from Year 10 upwards.
bullets: Work submitted at least a day ahead so marking happens before the lesson
Marked against the official wording, not against a general impression
Each lesson closes with one finishable task for the next cycle
A running record of which question types still cost marks

modes.title: Criterion clinic for coursework
modes.description: A short series of sessions attached to an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project, built around the criteria rather than the content. The student brings their own draft, the tutor reads it against each criterion letter, and the questions are returned to the student to answer. No text comes from the tutor at any point.
bullets: Criterion-by-criterion reading of the student's own draft
Topic feasibility challenged early, which is where most marks are won
Referencing and presentation checked against the component's own limits
A written note of what the student decided, kept for the school's process record

modes.title: Paired sibling evening
modes.description: Two children at different levels taught in the same evening, back to back, in a household where only one evening is genuinely free. Over live video this costs nothing extra in travel and lets a family cover a Year 9 and a DP1 in one sitting, which is the arrangement several Living Legends households settle on.
bullets: Consecutive slots in one evening rather than two separate journeys
Different tutors where the levels demand it, one booking either way
Shared written summary so a parent reads one note, not two
Easy to drop to a single slot during one child's exam term

sections.heading: What a school timetable can deliver, and what it cannot
paragraphs: A Diploma or IGCSE course has a fixed number of teaching periods, and every one of them is already allocated. The syllabus has to be covered, coursework has to be supervised, mocks have to be set and sat, and in Dubai the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies provision runs alongside the licensed curriculum for every student in every private school. KHDA calculates that provision in forty-minute lesson units and advises that no mandatory subject lesson falls below twenty-five minutes, which is a real claim on the week rather than a notional one.

What fits inside that is one careful pass through the content, with questions, with class discussion, with homework set and broadly checked. What does not fit is a second pass taught differently for the students who did not get the first one, or thirty individually marked timed papers with the student sitting next to the marker while it happens. Teachers know this. It is why the honest answer from a good teacher is often that the topic has been covered and the student needs to practise, which is accurate and not very actionable for a parent.

Naming the gap precisely is more useful than complaining about it. There are four distinct things a class cannot usually provide: individually marked timed practice, a second explanation in a different register, criterion-level reading of a coursework draft, and sustained spoken practice in a language. Every one of those is exactly what a one-to-one hour is good at. Deciding which of the four your child needs is the single most valuable thing you can do before booking anybody.
bullets: Individually marked timed practice, with the marking explained out loud
A second explanation in a different register for a topic that did not land
Criterion-level reading of the student's own coursework draft
Sustained spoken practice in a language, for a whole hour rather than three minutes

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: Parents often describe a subject as the problem when the problem is two or three topics inside it. A Year 11 who is losing eight marks a paper in Physics is rarely weak at Physics; they are usually losing them in electricity and in the practical-skills paper, and the rest of the subject is fine. Diagnosing that takes a marked script and twenty minutes, and it changes the plan completely, because four sessions on two topics will move a grade where four sessions of general revision will not.

The table below sets out the patterns we see most often across the schools this area uses. It is diagnostic rather than exhaustive, and the right version for your child is the one built from their own returned papers. What is worth noticing is how many of the entries are not content problems at all. Reading a command term, selecting from the whole course rather than the current unit, and laying out working a marker can follow are skills, and they transfer between topics in a way that memorising one more definition does not.

The practical consequence is the order of work. Content gaps are worth closing first if they are genuine holes, because technique cannot operate on knowledge that is absent. After that, almost all remaining gains are technical, and the sessions should look less like teaching and more like marking. A student who has seen every topic once and is still six marks short per paper does not need a fifth explanation of the topic. They need to sit the question, get it marked in front of them, and sit a similar one the following week.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment criteria, read the way a marker reads them
paragraphs: Internal Assessments are marked against named criteria with published mark allocations, and the allocations are not even. Knowing that twelve of the Extended Essay's thirty-four marks sit under critical thinking changes how a student spends their final fortnight, because polishing presentation can earn at most four. Students are given the criteria by their schools. Very few are shown how to read a band descriptor as a marker does, which is to look for the specific thing it names rather than for general quality.

The table below sets out the letters and the marks for the components that come up most in this area. It is reference information, with the official syllabus and subject guides as the source your child's teacher will use; those documents belong to the IB and are not reproduced or supplied here, only cited. Use the table to decide where effort goes, then read the actual descriptor your school issued, because the wording is what gets marked.

The pattern across all of them is the same. The highest-weighted criterion is almost always the one asking for reasoning, and the one students over-invest in is almost always presentation. A science investigation that is beautifully formatted but built on a research question too broad to answer with the data collected has lost marks under research design that no amount of formatting recovers. A tutor's job in a criterion clinic is to ask the awkward question about criterion A in week one, not in week nine.

sections.heading: What class covers, what homework covers, and what is left over
paragraphs: It helps to separate three different kinds of work that parents tend to merge. The first is content delivery, which happens in class and is the school's job. The second is consolidation homework, which is set, collected and broadly checked. The third is the preparation that nobody sets and nobody collects: the second attempt at a topic that did not land, the past paper sat under time and then actually marked, the coursework draft revised against a criterion, the vocabulary practised out loud. That third category is where most of the variance between students in the same set comes from.

The table maps the main assessment components against those three categories. The useful column is the fourth, because that is the honest list of what a sixteen-year-old is expected to organise for themselves alongside six subjects, two core components and whatever KHDA-mandated lessons their school timetables. Most students manage some of it. Almost none manage all of it without structure, and that is not a character flaw.

A tutor is one way of imposing structure on the fourth column, and not the only one. A disciplined student with a parent who marks past papers and a quiet room may not need one. What a tutor adds is subject-specific marking and the awkward questions a parent cannot ask about criterion A. What a tutor cannot add is the hours. If the independent work is not happening between sessions, a second lesson will not fix it and will mostly move the work from the student to the tutor.

sections.heading: What an hour of independent revision should actually contain
paragraphs: Most students, asked to revise for an hour, reread. It feels productive, it produces a sense of familiarity, and it converts into very little under exam conditions, because recognising material is a different cognitive act from retrieving it. The single most reliable change a Year 11 or Diploma student can make is to replace rereading with answering: close the notes, attempt the question, then check. The first few weeks of doing that are unpleasant precisely because it reveals how much was only recognised.

A usable structure for sixty minutes is five minutes recalling the previous session's topic from memory, twenty-five minutes on new or weak material with active questioning, five minutes off the screen, twenty minutes on a timed past-paper question, and five minutes marking it honestly against the mark scheme wording. The marking is the part students skip and the part that matters, because it is where the student finds out that the examiner wanted the reason as well as the observation.

Two further rules make the hour work in a household like this one. The phone leaves the room; a notification costs more than the minute it takes, because the retrieval that was in progress does not resume. And the session ends on a written note of what to do next, which removes the five minutes at the start of the following session spent deciding what to do. Those two habits are worth more than any revision app, and they are free.
bullets: Close the notes and answer from memory before checking anything
Twenty minutes of the hour under timed conditions, every time
Mark against the official wording, not against a general impression
Phone out of the room, without exception
Finish by writing the next task down, so the next hour starts immediately

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that quietly decides the grade
paragraphs: Every examined subject publishes a list of command terms, and every mark scheme is written against them. State wants a fact. Describe wants observable detail without reasons. Explain wants the reason. Deduce wants a conclusion reached from given information. Evaluate wants a judgement with both sides weighed. Compare wants similarities and differences in the same answer. Students who treat these as synonyms for write about lose marks steadily across every paper, and the loss is invisible in classwork because classroom questions are forgiving.

The symptom is a specific kind of frustration: a student who knows the material well, writes a lot, and gets six out of ten. Reading their script usually shows a description where an explanation was asked for, or an answer that lists three things when the question asked for a judgement between two. This is one of the cheapest things to fix and one of the least likely to be fixed in class, because it needs somebody to sit with the student's own script and point at the verb.

The exercise that works is deliberately repetitive. Take one topic and answer four questions on it with four different command terms, then compare what changed. After a dozen of those a student stops reading past the verb. In the Diploma sciences this single change frequently accounts for several marks a paper, and it transfers across every subject the student takes, which makes it the best return available on a single tutoring hour.
bullets: State, describe, explain, deduce, evaluate and compare are different instructions
The verb decides the answer's shape before any content is chosen
Practise one topic against four command terms and compare the answers
Mark schemes are written to the verb, which is why partial answers score low
The fix transfers to every subject at once

sections.heading: Mocks, predicted grades and what to do with a bad one
paragraphs: Mocks do two jobs, and parents usually only see the first. They give a grade, which causes the conversation at home, and they generate a marked script, which is the genuinely valuable output. A mock script shows the pattern of loss: whether the marks went on content, on command terms, on timing, or on working that could not be followed. That diagnosis is worth more than the grade attached to it, and it is the thing most likely to end up in a folder unexamined.

Predicted grades carry real weight because university applications use them, and in the Diploma they are issued by the school on the basis of work to date. A disappointing prediction is not a verdict, but it is a signal that the evidence base needs to change. The practical response is to find out what evidence the prediction was built on, do better work of that same kind, and make sure the teacher sees it. Vague improvement does not move a prediction; a better mock or a stronger piece of marked coursework can.

The timing question matters too. A weak mock in November of the final year leaves room to change the trajectory. The same result in March leaves room to change technique and triage subjects, which is a narrower but still real set of options. What does not work in either case is an immediate jump to three tutors across three subjects. Pick the subject where the marked script shows the most recoverable loss, fix that, and see what the next assessment says before expanding.
bullets: The marked script matters more than the grade printed on the front
Ask what evidence a predicted grade was built on, then produce better evidence of that kind
Triage by recoverable loss, not by which subject feels worst
One subject properly beats three subjects lightly, almost every time
Re-read the plan after the next real assessment rather than after a good week

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and what we will not hand you
paragraphs: Official past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them, cite them and teach from the student's own school-issued copies, and we do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads. That is a copyright position rather than a stylistic one, and for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure for the student. Any provider offering a library of mark schemes is making somebody else's copyright decision on your behalf.

The legitimate routes are better than parents expect. Schools hold centre access to official material and release it as part of teaching. Cambridge and Pearson publish specimen papers, syllabus documents and timetables openly on their own sites. The IB publishes subject briefs and assessment information. A student with their school's materials and the official specimens has more practice available than they will ever use, and the limiting factor is almost never supply.

The related boundary is coursework. A tutor can teach research skills, read a criterion out loud, question a draft, point out an unsupported conclusion and show how an argument of that shape is built elsewhere. A tutor must not supply text for an assessed piece. The student carries the consequence of malpractice, which can cost the subject or the whole Diploma, and the school is obliged to report it. We say this on every page because at least one page ranking for these searches sells finished assessed work outright.

sections.heading: What the first three sessions do for a Living Legends student
paragraphs: Session one is diagnostic and it needs material. A marked mock script is ideal, a returned coursework draft is nearly as good, and a recent report will do. The tutor works out what kind of loss is happening, which is a different question from which topics are weak, and ends by setting one finishable task. Nothing is taught in a vacuum in that first hour; the point is to stop guessing.

Session two acts on the diagnosis. If the loss is content, the weakest genuine gap gets a second explanation in a different register. If the loss is technique, the task set in session one comes back marked and the marking is the lesson. If the loss is coursework, the draft is read against one criterion letter and the student leaves with questions to answer rather than corrections to copy. The distinction matters: corrections make a better draft once, questions make a better writer.

Session three checks whether anything moved, using work done independently in between. If the task was not done, that is the conversation, because no arrangement survives the tutor being the only person working. If it was done and the same error recurs, the approach changes rather than repeats. By the end of the third hour a parent should be able to name the specific loss, the specific intervention and the next real assessment it will be measured against. If they cannot, the arrangement is not working yet and should be changed.

process.title: Send marked work, not a description
process.description: A mock script, a returned coursework draft or a report page tells a specialist in two minutes what a conversation takes twenty to approximate. It shows whether the loss is content, command terms, timing or presentation, and those four need four different first lessons.

process.title: Name the component, the board and the code
process.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are not interchangeable, and Higher Level is not Standard Level at speed. Confirming the exact syllabus version and tier before the first lesson prevents four sessions of correct content taught in the wrong format.

process.title: Agree what gets measured
process.description: Before the block starts, we write down the next real marker: the January mock, the March Internal Assessment deadline, the next returned paper. Progress is read against that, not against a sense that sessions are going well.

process.title: Run the marked-work cycle
process.description: Work goes in ahead of the lesson, comes back marked against the official wording, and the lesson is spent on the marking. Each session closes with one finishable task, and the next session opens by checking it.

process.title: Re-plan at the marker, not before
process.description: When the agreed assessment arrives, the plan either continues, changes or stops. If the marker has not moved, we change the approach or the tutor rather than adding a second subject and hoping.

whyPoints.title: Aimed at the second pass
whyPoints.description: The class delivers the syllabus once, properly. We work on what a single pass cannot provide: individually marked timed practice, a different explanation of a topic that did not land, and criterion-level reading of the student's own draft.

whyPoints.title: Criteria named, with their marks
whyPoints.description: Twelve of the Extended Essay's thirty-four marks are for critical thinking, and a science investigation carries six marks each across four criteria. Knowing where the marks sit changes where a student spends their last fortnight.

whyPoints.title: Marking is the lesson
whyPoints.description: The most productive hour for a student who has the content is one spent on their own marked script, with the examiner's wording in front of them. That is difficult to deliver in a class of twenty-four and straightforward one to one.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and give feedback. Text for an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project must originate with the candidate, because the candidate carries the malpractice risk and the seller does not.

whyPoints.title: Copyright respected, which helps you
whyPoints.description: We cite and link official board material rather than redistributing it. That keeps your child's position clean and pushes you towards the school's own centre access and the boards' open specimen papers, which are better sources anyway.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, holds no regulator accreditation, and operates no premises here. Where no specialist is free in your slot, we say so.

faqs.question: How much independent study does a Diploma student in Living Legends actually need each week?
faqs.answer: The IB Diploma is designed around substantial independent work, and most students in this part of Dubai find that between twelve and eighteen hours a week outside lessons is what the two years require once coursework is live. The number matters less than its composition. An hour spent rereading notes is worth very little; twenty minutes answering a question from memory and then marking it against the official wording is worth a great deal. If your child is putting in long hours and the marks are flat, the problem is almost always the method rather than the quantity.

faqs.question: What are the most common IB Internal Assessment mistakes UAE students make?
faqs.answer: Three, in order. A research question too broad to be answered by the data the student can realistically collect, which loses marks under research design before any writing happens. Evaluation written as a generic wish to repeat the experiment more times, rather than specific weaknesses in this investigation with realistic improvements. And leaving the criteria unread until the final fortnight, by which time the recoverable marks are the low-weighted presentation ones. A tutor cannot write any part of it, but asking the awkward question about the research question in week one is the single most valuable intervention available.

faqs.question: Can a tutor explain the Extended Essay criteria without writing any of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is exactly the work. The essay is scored out of thirty-four, with twelve marks for critical thinking, six each for focus and method, knowledge and understanding and engagement, and four for presentation. A tutor can read the student's own draft against each criterion letter, say where the argument stops being argued, point out that a conclusion overreaches the evidence, challenge a research question that cannot sustain four thousand words, and teach referencing. What a tutor must not do is supply text. The questions go back to the student; the answers have to be theirs.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students around Living Legends struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Physics and Chemistry generate the most requests, followed by Extended-tier Mathematics. The pattern in the marked scripts is consistent: in Physics the losses cluster in electricity and the practical-skills paper rather than across the subject; in Chemistry they cluster in moles and electrolysis, usually because multi-step calculations are written without working, so partial credit is unavailable; in Mathematics they appear late in the non-calculator paper as arithmetic slips and as method a marker cannot follow. All three are narrow, diagnosable problems, which is why four sessions on two topics often moves a grade where general revision does not.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child needs more teaching or more practice?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked script rather than asking the question in the abstract. If answers are blank or substantially wrong on topics the class has covered, there is a content gap and it needs teaching. If answers are long, broadly correct and still scoring six out of ten, it is almost never content: it is command terms, selection, timing or unreadable working. The two need opposite responses. Teaching a student who already knows the material produces a pleasant hour and no extra marks, and practising with a student who has a genuine hole in their knowledge simply rehearses the hole.

faqs.question: What should an hour of revision actually contain?
faqs.answer: Five minutes recalling last session's topic from memory with the notes closed. Twenty-five minutes on new or weak material, answering questions rather than reading. Five minutes away from the screen. Twenty minutes on a past-paper question under time. Five minutes marking it honestly against the mark scheme wording. The marking is the part students skip and the part that produces the gain, because it is where they discover the examiner wanted the reason and not only the observation. The phone leaves the room, and the hour ends by writing down the next task.

faqs.question: My child's mock grade dropped. What do we do with a disappointing predicted grade?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a statement about the evidence, not about your child. Predicted grades in the Diploma are issued by the school from work to date, so the useful question is which pieces of work they were built on. Then produce better work of that same kind and make sure the teacher sees it. A stronger mock or a better marked coursework piece can move a prediction; a general improvement in attitude usually cannot. Avoid the instinct to hire three tutors across three subjects at once. Pick the subject whose marked script shows the most recoverable loss and start there.

faqs.question: Do you give out past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Official past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and we cite and link them rather than redistributing them. For unreleased material, circulating it is also a malpractice exposure for the student. The legitimate routes are better anyway: your child's school holds centre access and releases material as part of teaching, and Cambridge, Pearson and the IB publish specimen papers, syllabus documents and timetables openly on their own sites. Supply is almost never the limiting factor; marking the papers that have already been sat usually is.

faqs.question: Which schools do Living Legends families usually send their children to?
faqs.answer: There is no school inside the community, so families use the Sports City, Studio City and Motor City cluster for primary and lower secondary, and travel further for the Diploma. The schools that come up most in our enquiries are GEMS United School Sports City, Victory Heights Primary School, Bradenton Preparatory Academy, GEMS Metropole School, GEMS FirstPoint School, The Aquila School, JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and GEMS International School Al Khail. They are named as local context only. IB Gram has no affiliation with, or endorsement from, any of them.

faqs.question: Are command terms really worth teaching separately from the content?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the cheapest gains available. Every examined subject publishes a command-term list and every mark scheme is written against it. State wants a fact, describe wants observable detail, explain wants the reason, deduce wants a conclusion from given information, evaluate wants a weighed judgement. A student who treats these as synonyms writes a great deal and scores six out of ten. The exercise that fixes it is answering four questions on one topic with four different command terms and comparing the results. It transfers to every subject at once.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring workable for a household with two children at different levels?
faqs.answer: It works better than the alternative, and several families in this community use it precisely for that reason. Because nobody is travelling, two consecutive slots in one evening cost nothing extra in logistics, and the levels can be genuinely different: a Year 9 followed by a DP1, with different tutors where the levels demand it. You get one booking and one written summary rather than two separate arrangements. If only one evening in the week is actually free, this is usually the only pattern that fits it without a car journey in the middle.

faqs.question: How long should the IB Maths exploration be?
faqs.answer: The exploration is a short independent piece, and the marks are not awarded for length. It is scored out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with the largest single allocation on the mathematics itself. The commonest failure is a Higher Level student writing at Standard Level depth, or presenting correct mathematics with no commentary explaining the choices. Your child's teacher will issue the current length guidance from the subject guide; we teach to that document rather than restating a figure here, because guidance is revised between syllabus versions.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor for Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Often not for the content, frequently for the structure. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and an essay on a prescribed title, and students who approach either as an opinion piece lose marks that a clear knowledge question and a properly worked counter-position would have secured. Two or three structural sessions tend to be enough: one to test whether the chosen objects or title can actually sustain an argument, one on building the knowledge question, one on the counter-position. Beyond that it is the student's own thinking, and it should be.

faqs.question: Is it better to tutor one subject properly or three subjects lightly?
faqs.answer: One subject properly, in almost every case. Three light arrangements produce three sets of homework, three relationships to manage and three hours out of the week, and they rarely generate enough independent practice in any single subject to move a grade. One subject with a weekly marked-work cycle and thirty minutes of independent practice between sessions moves measurably within a term, and the technique gains usually transfer. If three subjects genuinely need help, that is a signal to look at study method and timetable first rather than to buy three hours.

faqs.question: What does the first month look like for a Year 11 student in Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Four sessions. The first diagnoses from a marked script, names whether the loss is content, command terms, timing or presentation, and sets one finishable task. The second acts on that diagnosis, either closing a genuine content gap or marking the task out loud. The third measures whether anything moved using work done independently. The fourth either continues or changes approach. By the end a parent should be able to name the specific loss, the specific intervention and the next real assessment it will be measured against. If they cannot, the arrangement needs changing rather than extending.

dubai/living-legends.closingHeading: Bring the marked script, and we will work out what is actually missing
dubai/living-legends.closingBody: If your child's school says the topic has been covered and the paper still goes wrong, the useful next step is not more explanation. It is a marked script, read carefully by somebody who knows what that subject's examiners reward. Send a mock paper, a returned coursework draft or a recent report, tell us the board and the syllabus code, and we will match your child to a specialist who teaches that second pass one-to-one over live video. Nobody drives anywhere, the terms are written down before any block is booked, and the plan is measured against a real assessment rather than a feeling.

intro.heading: Who lives in Meydan, and what that does to tutoring
paragraphs: Meydan is two neighbourhoods wearing one name. On one side sit the towers and mid-rise blocks along Meydan Avenue and the Polo Residence, where the typical family has one or two secondary children, both parents working in Business Bay or DIFC, and no spare hour before seven in the evening. On the other side are the villa plots of District One, Millennium Estates, Grand Views and the gated clusters off the racecourse, where households are larger, children are spread across three or four key stages, and the school run itself eats ninety minutes of the afternoon. A tutoring plan that suits one of those households usually fails in the other, and that is the first thing worth saying on a page about IB and IGCSE tutors in Meydan.

The schools these families use sit mostly in Nad Al Sheba and across the water in Sobha Hartland rather than inside Meydan itself. North London Collegiate School Dubai, Repton School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Kent College Dubai take a large share of the secondary children here, with Hartland International School and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai picking up the rest. That matters because it fixes the boards: an IB continuum school means MYP eAssessment pressure in Year 11 and a full Diploma from Year 12, while a British-curriculum school means Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at sixteen and a choice between A Level and the Diploma after it. Two children in the same villa can be sitting different qualifications in the same month.

The academic pressure points follow from that mix, and they are predictable enough to plan around. Year 10 families are deciding IGCSE option blocks and tiers, and the Core-versus-Extended decision in Maths and the sciences is the one that quietly closes doors eighteen months later. DP1 families hit the six-subject load in October and discover that two Higher Levels plus an Internal Assessment schedule does not leave room for the third thing they were good at. MYP families arriving into the Diploma find the jump in written precision harder than the jump in content. Each of those is a different tutoring job with a different session pattern.

Lessons for Meydan families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature. A villa in District One that needs a Chemistry HL specialist is not well served by whoever is prepared to drive from Al Barsha at five in the afternoon, and an apartment family in Meydan Avenue that needs Maths AA HL on a Tuesday and Economics HL on a Thursday can have two different subject specialists in the same week rather than one generalist stretched across both.

What follows is the detail a Meydan parent actually needs before spending money: the market rate bands in AED with the source for each one, what an in-home hour costs once the drive is priced in, which schools in and around Meydan run which programmes, the Cambridge and Pearson deadlines that sit months before the exams themselves, the KHDA rules on Arabic and Islamic Education that occupy part of your child's timetable whatever the international curriculum says, and the line a tutor may not cross on an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay. None of it is hard to verify, and the sources are named.

dubai/meydan.programmesIntro: Meydan children sit four different programme shapes depending on which Nad Al Sheba or Hartland school they attend. The notes below say what each one demands of a student living here, and where a weekly online slot earns its place.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth 20 to 30 per cent of the final grade, set and marked internally against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The load is not the problem on its own; the collision of internal deadlines across six courses in the same fortnight is.
programmes.countryNote: North London Collegiate School Dubai and GEMS Modern Academy run the Diploma for a large share of Meydan's older teenagers. Those cohorts tend to arrive in DP1 from an MYP background, which means strong inquiry habits and weaker exam-technique habits. The common request from District One households is Maths AA HL and one science, taken as two separate weekly slots with different tutors.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight, with command terms that reward explanation over recall. Year 11 students may sit MYP eAssessment, an on-screen examination with its own question style. Grades are reported 1 to 7 per subject from criterion totals, which surprises parents used to percentages.
programmes.countryNote: MYP sits underneath the Diploma at the IB continuum schools in Nad Al Sheba, and the Meydan families who contact us about it are usually responding to a criterion grade that dropped without the content getting harder. The fix is almost always the command term and the structure of the written response, which is quick work in a one-to-one slot and very slow work in a class of twenty-four.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined at the end of Year 11, with Cambridge syllabuses such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics and Pearson equivalents such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge tiers several subjects as Core or Extended; Pearson offers Foundation and Higher in Maths. The tier chosen in Year 10 sets the grade ceiling, and changing it late is an administrative decision with a deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Repton School Dubai, Kent College Dubai and Hartland International School put Meydan's British-curriculum cohort through IGCSE. The question we field most from Meydan parents is which board their child's school actually entered, because the past papers are not interchangeable. The answer sits on the statement of entry, and it is worth checking before buying any tutoring at all.

programmes.name: A Level, after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four linear subjects, examined at the end of Year 13, with the content depth of a Higher Level IB course and none of the breadth requirement. Mathematics splits into pure, mechanics and statistics; the sciences carry separate practical endorsement. Universities quote offers in A Level grades, which makes the subject choice at sixteen a direct admissions decision.
programmes.countryNote: Kent College Dubai and Repton School Dubai both offer the A Level route, and Meydan families choosing between it and the Diploma usually want the same conversation: which one suits a child who is strong in three things and indifferent to the other three. A tutor cannot make that decision, but one session mapping subject content against intended degree subjects answers it faster than a term of worrying.

dubai/meydan.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Meydan households request most often, across both boards. Each note says what the assessment actually rewards and where marks leave the page, because that is what a weekly hour has to target.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the HL paper, and the Internal Assessment exploration is where most Meydan students lose ground. Paper 3 at HL rewards sustained reasoning across an unfamiliar context, which cannot be revised for by topic alone.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. Students who moved here from a CBSE or American background often find the graphical calculator requirement the hardest adjustment, not the mathematics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics absorb most of the tutoring time in this area. The HL extension topics are not conceptually harder so much as unforgiving on precision, and the IA demands a question narrow enough to generate real data.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward method over memory. Marks go missing in unit handling, significant figures and the explanation questions where a correct idea is written too loosely to score.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the issue, not difficulty. The command terms separate a 5 from a 7: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and students who write one shape for all four cap themselves.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation paragraph decide the grade. HL calculation papers are learnable in a few weeks; the commentary portfolio needs a tutor who will read a draft and ask harder questions than the student asked themselves.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are the two components Meydan students most often arrive underprepared for. Both respond quickly to structured practice with feedback.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.description: Tier choice sets the ceiling. Extended and Higher papers test algebraic manipulation, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and multi-step problem solving under time pressure.

subjects.name: IGCSE Combined and Separate Sciences
subjects.description: Separate sciences cover more content with more marks available for practical reasoning. The alternative-to-practical paper is the single most improvable component for a student who has never been taught how it is marked.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Graded separately from the international curriculum and taught in Standard Arabic for first-language students. Retention between weekly school lessons is the usual difficulty, which short frequent sessions address better than long ones.

sections.heading: What a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Meydan is usually really asking
paragraphs: A Meydan parent typing this phrase into Google is almost never shopping for tutoring in the abstract. In nine cases out of ten something specific has happened: a progress report came home with a grade 4 in a subject that was a 6 last term, a DP1 student admitted they have not started an Internal Assessment that is due in three weeks, or a Year 10 options form landed with a Core-or-Extended decision on it and nobody at home knows which way to tick. The search term is generic because the parent does not yet know the vocabulary for the problem.

That changes what a useful answer looks like. The question is not whether tutoring works in general. It is whether this particular gap, in this subject, at this point in the year, is the kind a weekly hour closes, and what that hour should cost in Dubai in 2026. Some gaps are closed faster by a single ninety-minute session that explains how a paper is marked than by a term of weekly lessons. Others need a tutor every week until June and will not respond to anything less.

The second thing the search is asking is logistical. Meydan addresses are a twenty to forty minute drive from most of Dubai's tutor supply depending on the hour, and an in-home tutor's earliest available slot is set by wherever they were before you. Online delivery removes that variable completely, which is the main reason a District One family can book a Chemistry HL specialist for 5pm on a Tuesday instead of accepting whoever can reach Nad Al Sheba by half past six.

So this page answers the parts a parent can act on: what the market charges and who publishes those figures, how an in-home hour compares with an online hour once travel is counted, which schools around Meydan run which programmes, when the board deadlines actually fall, what KHDA requires alongside the international curriculum, and the exact line a tutor may not cross on assessed work. Where a figure is quoted, the source is named. Where something is not verified, this page says so instead of guessing.

sections.heading: Four Meydan households, four different tutoring problems
paragraphs: The useful unit of analysis in Meydan is the household, not the student. A villa in Millennium Estates with children in Year 7, Year 10 and DP1 has three simultaneous academic timetables, three sets of internal deadlines and one evening in which to service all of them. An apartment on Meydan Avenue with a single Year 11 child has one problem and a much simpler calendar. The same tutoring product sold to both of them produces one satisfied family and one that cancels in February.

The table below sets out the four patterns we see most often from this postcode, with the school clusters each tends to use and the session shape that survives contact with a Dubai weekday. None of it is exotic. It is simply the arithmetic of how many hours exist between the end of the school run and the point at which a fourteen-year-old stops being able to concentrate.

The fourth row is worth singling out because it is specific to communities like District One. A meaningful number of families resident in Dubai have a child at boarding school in the United Kingdom or India sitting IGCSE or A Level there. Those students need support across a time-zone gap, usually at the weekend, and the tutoring is arranged by a parent in Meydan for a student who is not in Meydan. Online delivery is the only format in which that works at all.

The fifth row covers the Arabic stream, which cuts across every other category. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and those grades are reported separately from the IB or IGCSE result. Families who treat them as an afterthought until Year 10 generally find the catch-up expensive in hours.

sections.heading: What tutoring actually costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Meydan family transacts in. That silence is commercially convenient and useless to a parent trying to budget. The bands below are market rates in AED, collected from providers' own published pages and from a Dubai tutoring cost survey, with the source named for every row. They are not IB Gram's price list.

The pattern across the market is consistent: the hour itself costs roughly the same wherever it happens, and the difference between a budget rate and a specialist rate is the depth of subject knowledge rather than the delivery format. What moves the number most is travel. An in-home visit prices the drive into the hour, which is why the same qualified teacher costs more to have in a District One villa than to have on a screen.

Monthly packaging varies more than hourly pricing. Published examples in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A Dubai cost survey puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are the numbers to hold against any quote you receive.

One caution on reading any rate table, including this one. A figure published by a provider is what they advertise, not necessarily what a Meydan family pays after assessment fees, materials or a minimum booking. Ask for the all-in monthly figure, ask whether VAT is included, and ask what happens if the match does not work. Those three questions separate a real quote from a headline.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor in Meydan compared with one-to-one online
paragraphs: This is the comparison a Meydan parent is really making, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. In-home tutoring is a real service with real advantages, particularly for younger children who need an adult physically present to stay on task. Plenty of Dubai families use it and are right to. The question is what it costs you in tutor choice at a Nad Al Sheba address on a weekday afternoon.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. What we arrange for Meydan families is one-to-one tuition delivered live over video, which means the tutor is chosen from the whole roster by subject and level rather than from the subset willing to drive to Nad Al Sheba. For Chemistry HL, Physics HL and Maths AA HL, that subset is thin and gets thinner after five in the afternoon.

The travel arithmetic is the part most comparison pages skip. A tutor crossing Dubai for a 5pm start in District One commits roughly ninety minutes of unpaid time around a sixty-minute lesson, and that cost ends up in the hourly rate whether or not it is itemised. It also fixes the slot: the tutor's earliest Meydan availability depends on where their previous booking was, and the Ras Al Khor interchange between half past three and five o'clock is not a theoretical constraint.

The honest counterweight is that online lessons demand something from the student. A fourteen-year-old who will not open a book without someone in the room is harder to teach on a screen, and we say so rather than pretending otherwise. The format that works for that child is a shorter, more frequent session with a parent within earshot for the first fortnight, not a ninety-minute block on a Thursday night.

sections.heading: The schools around Meydan and what each one commits your child to
paragraphs: Meydan has no large secondary school inside its own boundary, so the catchment is effectively Nad Al Sheba plus the Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf side of Ras Al Khor Road. That gives families an unusual amount of choice within a ten-minute radius, and it also means two neighbours can be running entirely different academic calendars. Knowing which programme a school runs matters more than its reputation, because the programme sets the deadlines and the assessment style your child is actually judged on.

Dubai's private sector is the densest in the country. The emirate counted 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent, according to figures published by the Dubai Media Office in January 2025. Seven new private schools are opening for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places.

All of these schools are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. KHDA inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak and publishes the reports. If you want a school's current rating, read it on the KHDA site rather than on a tutoring page, including this one. Ratings change and a stale figure is worse than none.

The table lists the schools Meydan families most commonly use, with the community each sits in and what the school offers at sixteen and eighteen. Programme offerings change year to year, so treat the table as a starting point for a conversation with the school rather than as a current prospectus.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this market names a single exam session, registration deadline or results date. That is a strange omission, because the deadlines are the part of the year a parent can actually plan against, and several of them sit months before the exam itself. A Year 11 student whose tier is still undecided in late November has a problem that no amount of tutoring in February fixes.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with a March series as well. The March 2027 series is a clean worked example of how far ahead the administration runs: final entries are due 27 November 2026, the exam period is 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates follow in late June. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge is explicit that you must use the correct timetable version for your zone.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For reference on how long the results gap runs, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live PDF on the Pearson site rather than relying on any date restated elsewhere.

For the IB, this page does not publish a session or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a date that cannot be verified should not sit on a page a parent might plan around. Meydan families should confirm the May session window and the results date with their school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. What is safe to say is that the internal deadlines for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are set by the school, fall well before the IB's own upload dates, and are the deadlines that actually govern your child's autumn.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: This is the part of a Dubai timetable that almost no tutoring page mentions, and it occupies real hours of your child's week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements that schools were to implement from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The grades are reported separately from the IB or IGCSE result, and they do not disappear because a student is doing three Higher Levels.

KHDA is specific about how these subjects are organised. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Two further KHDA points are worth knowing before you buy any tutoring in these subjects. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai schools are required to hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential you can ask about. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which constrains what any tutor can legitimately introduce. Support in these subjects therefore means practice with the school's own material, not a parallel syllabus.

In practice, Meydan families use tutoring here in short, frequent sessions. Arabic retention between one school lesson and the next is the usual complaint, and twenty-five to thirty minutes twice a week does more for vocabulary and script fluency than a single long block. Islamic Education support tends to cluster before school assessments. Social Studies is rarely tutored at all, and is included here because it takes timetable hours that a parent planning an evening schedule needs to account for.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment
paragraphs: This matters more in the IB than in any other system a Meydan family is likely to meet, and the market around Dubai is not clean. At least one site ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum in AED. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the vendor. A Diploma candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own risks losing the award entirely.

The legitimate boundary is clear enough to state in a sentence. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, explain what a command term requires, help a student narrow a research question until it can generate usable data, teach the statistics or the laboratory technique the investigation needs, read a draft the student has written and ask questions about it, and point out where an argument is unsupported. Everything on that list is teaching.

What a tutor must not do is supply text, rewrite a passage into its final form, hand over a methodology the student has not understood, or take over the work in any way that makes the submitted piece not the student's own. IB Gram does not supply assessed work, does not edit a draft into a finished submission, and will not take on a request framed that way. Saying so plainly is useful in this market precisely because several competitors do the opposite.

There is a practical reason beyond the rules. An Internal Assessment is worth 20 to 30 per cent of a subject grade, and the skill it tests is the one the examination then tests again under time pressure. A student who did not do the thinking in October does not acquire it in May. The families who get the most out of IA support are the ones who book it early, bring a draft to each session, and treat the tutor as a demanding reader rather than a supplier.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a Meydan parent is entitled to ask about it before handing over money. The private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone telling you the permit costs money, or that it is optional, is wrong on a point of fact.

The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students may all hold the permit. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated two working day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount you see quoted online should be treated as unverified.

Two further points are worth knowing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor, and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not hold one and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because it holds no such approval. Any provider implying otherwise is making a claim you should ask them to evidence with a permit number.

The other point concerns school teachers. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Dubai families should not treat their child's own classroom teacher as an available private tutor, and a reputable provider will not arrange it.

process.title: Tell us the school and the exact problem
process.description: Which Nad Al Sheba or Hartland school, which year group, which subject, and what happened to trigger the search. A progress report, a mock paper or a returned Internal Assessment draft tells us more in two minutes than a general description does in twenty.

process.title: We confirm the board and the syllabus code
process.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are not the same course and do not share past papers. The statement of entry or the school's subject guide settles it. Getting this right before the first lesson is the single cheapest thing you can do for the outcome.

process.title: Pick the slot against the school run, not around it
process.description: We agree a weekday and time that survives a real Meydan afternoon, allowing for the Nad Al Sheba pick-up and the Ras Al Khor crossing. A slot that works in October and collapses in January is worse than a later one that holds all year.

process.title: Trial session with the matched specialist
process.description: The first session is diagnostic. The tutor works through the student's own recent paper or draft, identifies where the marks are actually going, and sets out what a term of weekly work would target. You decide after that, not before.

process.title: Weekly rhythm, with written output after each lesson
process.description: Worked solutions and a short summary are saved after every session so revision in April has something to work from. If the match is not right, say so in the first fortnight and we change the tutor rather than asking you to persevere.

whyPoints.title: The tutor is chosen by syllabus, not by distance
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run online, a District One family is not restricted to tutors willing to drive to Nad Al Sheba at five in the afternoon. For Chemistry HL, Physics HL and Maths AA HL, that difference is the whole difference.

whyPoints.title: Rates are published with their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are market figures with the provider or survey named for each one. You can check them. We do not publish a single national price and call it a quote, and we do not hide the number behind a contact form.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary on assessed work is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: An Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project stays the student's own work. We teach the criteria, question the plan and give feedback on the student's draft. We do not supply assessed work, and we decline requests framed that way.

whyPoints.title: No regulator or board approval is claimed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and says so. Those bodies are named on this page to explain what they do, never to borrow their authority.

whyPoints.title: Two children, two specialists, one week
whyPoints.description: Villa households in Meydan routinely need help at two different stages at once. Separate slots with separate subject specialists is a normal arrangement here, not an upgrade, and it is far easier to schedule when nobody has to drive between them.

whyPoints.title: The Arabic and Islamic Education stream is not ignored
whyPoints.description: KHDA requires these subjects in every Dubai private school and grades them separately. Support runs with the school's own material, in short frequent sessions, which is what the retention problem actually needs.

faqs.question: Can I get a home tutor who comes to our villa in Meydan?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Meydan families we arrange one-to-one tuition delivered live over video. Independent in-home tutors do operate in Dubai and the market rate is roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel priced in, according to a 2026 Dubai cost survey and tutors' own published rates. The trade-off is tutor choice: an in-home booking at a Nad Al Sheba address is limited to people willing to make that drive at that hour, which thins out sharply in specialist Higher Level subjects.

faqs.question: Which schools do Meydan children usually attend?
faqs.answer: Most secondary children in Meydan attend schools in Nad Al Sheba or across Ras Al Khor Road. North London Collegiate School Dubai, Repton School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Kent College Dubai take a large share, with Hartland International School in Sobha Hartland and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai in Al Jaddaf covering much of the rest. That mix means IB continuum, English National Curriculum and bilingual IB families all live in the same community. Check the programmes offered on the KHDA school listing rather than on a tutoring page, including this one, because offerings change by year group and by intake.

faqs.question: What is a realistic start time for a lesson in Meydan on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Five o'clock is realistic for most Meydan addresses, and 6.15pm is safer if the school run involves two pick-ups in Nad Al Sheba. The constraint is the Ras Al Khor and Al Ain Road crossing between roughly half past three and five, which is also what pushes an in-home tutor's earliest offer later than parents expect. Because online lessons start at the agreed minute rather than when someone arrives, the practical question is only when your child can sit down and concentrate, not when a car can get there.

faqs.question: How much should I budget per month for one subject in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A Dubai tutoring cost survey published in 2026 puts weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 for a mid-tier qualified tutor, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices. Ask any provider for the all-in monthly number, whether VAT is included, and what happens if the first tutor is not the right match.

faqs.question: My child is at an IB continuum school in Nad Al Sheba and the MYP grades dropped. Is that a content problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not. MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, and the command terms decide the shape of a good answer: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate each want something different. A student who writes the same shape for all four caps their own criterion score while understanding the material perfectly well. That is quick work in a one-to-one session, because the tutor can look at the actual marked task and show where the criterion was not addressed. It is very slow work in a class of twenty-four, which is why it tends to persist across a term.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE board does my child's Meydan-area school use, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal, and the answer is on the statement of entry rather than the school website. Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics; Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. The papers, the tiering and the question style differ, so past papers are not interchangeable and a tutor working from the wrong set is wasting your money politely. Confirm the board before the first session. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and is explicit that the correct zone timetable must be used.

faqs.question: When are the Cambridge entry deadlines, and why are they so early?
faqs.answer: Entries close months before the papers. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026, the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027 and results reach centres on Direct on 13 May 2027. The reason is administrative: tiers, zones and question-paper allocations have to be fixed before printing and distribution. For a parent, the practical consequence is that the Core-or-Extended decision is effectively locked in late November, which makes the autumn term the point at which tutoring changes an outcome.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to do Arabic and Islamic Education if they are in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and schools were to implement the current requirements from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The grades are reported separately from the Diploma. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for the first-language and Arab Islamic Education groups. These subjects take real timetable hours and are worth planning for rather than discovering in Year 10.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Chemistry Internal Assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that is easy to state. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, help narrow the research question until it will produce usable data, teach the laboratory technique and the data analysis the investigation needs, read a draft your daughter has written and ask hard questions about it. A tutor must not supply text, rewrite a passage into its final form or take over the work. IB Gram does not supply assessed work and declines requests framed that way, because submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: We have two children at different stages in the same villa. How does that work in one evening?
faqs.answer: Two separate slots with two different subject specialists, usually an hour apart, is the normal arrangement for villa households in District One and Millennium Estates. A Year 10 choosing IGCSE tiers and a DP1 student managing six subjects need entirely different sessions, and a single generalist stretched across both serves neither well. Because nobody is travelling, back-to-back scheduling is straightforward: 5pm and 6.15pm on the same weekday is a common pattern here, which also means one quiet household rule covers both lessons rather than two separate negotiations.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a poor substitute if my son will not concentrate without someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For some younger children it genuinely is harder, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. A twelve-year-old who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is a better fit for shorter, more frequent online sessions with a parent within earshot for the first fortnight than for a ninety-minute block on a weeknight. By Year 10 and above, most students work well on a screen with a shared document and saved worked solutions, and many prefer it. The practical test is the trial session: watch how the first forty minutes go before committing to a term.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE, free of charge, valid for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service via its app, website or e-services, with a stated two working day turnaround. Ask any individual tutor to show you the permit. Anyone operating without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: My son joined a Meydan-area school in January from a different curriculum. What should the first six weeks look like?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic against the new syllabus, not a general assessment, then a short concentrated block aimed at a named list of gaps. A student moving from an American or CBSE background into IGCSE or the Diploma mid-course has not met specific topics, and the fastest route is to list them and close them rather than to restart the course. Two sessions a week while the gap is open, dropping to one once it closes, is the usual shape. Ask for a written handover note at the end of the block so a term-long tutor can pick it up without starting again.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. During Ramadan, Dubai school hours shorten and many families move sessions to a post-Iftar slot; agreeing that shift a fortnight in advance is better than renegotiating weekly. Exam and mock weeks usually need a different pattern too, with one short session focused on the next paper rather than the usual sequence. The one thing worth protecting is the slot itself. Families who cancel through February and restart in April lose more than the hours, because the tutor loses the thread of what the student had stopped understanding.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject and slot we want?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist and hoping. Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Maths AA are the scarcest combinations, particularly in the hour between five and seven o'clock Gulf Standard Time, and the honest options are a different time, a short wait for a slot to open, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to the same syllabus at a time that suits both sides. All three are disclosed up front with any rate difference stated. What we will not do is put your child with someone who does not know the paper and leave you to discover it in week three.

intro.heading: Why a continuum student can look fine and then not be
paragraphs: Mirdif sits in Dubai's eastern suburbs, a villa and townhouse community between Al Rashidiya, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa, with Dubai Festival City and Silicon Oasis a short run away. Its school provision is unusual in one specific respect: alongside the British and Indian-curriculum schools that dominate this side of the city, it holds full International Baccalaureate continuum provision, which means a child can enter at Foundation Stage and leave with a Diploma without ever changing school.

That continuity is genuinely valuable and it produces a specific, recurring problem that families here recognise immediately. A student progresses through the Primary Years Programme and the Middle Years Programme with solid reports, grades of 5 and 6 against the MYP criteria, warm comments about inquiry and reflection, and then arrives in Diploma year one and visibly struggles. Nothing went wrong. The assessment changed.

MYP assesses against four published criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with the raw total converted to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. The Diploma assesses against papers with markschemes and an externally moderated Internal Assessment. A student who has learned to satisfy criterion descriptors has learned something real, but it is not the same skill as answering a Paper 1 question under time pressure for method marks. The gap between the two is the single most common reason a Mirdif family starts looking for a tutor.

So this page is built around the continuum rather than around a single stage. It names the four MYP criteria for each subject group, which no competing page in this market does. It sets out what the on-screen eAssessment and the Personal Project actually require. Then it maps the MYP to Diploma transition subject by subject, with the specific gap in each and a realistic estimate of how long it takes to close.

Delivery is online throughout. IB Gram arranges one-to-one tuition over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own work on screen. Tutors do not travel to UAE addresses; in-home visiting exists only in the India service. For a continuum family in Mirdif that matters practically, because a tutor who knows MYP criterion C in Sciences and a tutor who knows Diploma Higher Level Chemistry are often different people, and neither needs to live on this side of the city.

Where this page quotes a regulator, the regulator is named. Where it quotes a rate, the provider who published it is named. No IB examination or results date appears anywhere, because the IB's own site could not be verified for this project; confirm every IB deadline with your school's coordinator. Most of the dates that actually bind a continuum student are set by the school in any case, not by the IB: Personal Project milestones, Internal Assessment hand-in dates and Extended Essay drafts all sit on a calendar the coordinator writes, and that calendar is the one a tutoring plan has to fit around.
