dubai/mirdif.programmesIntro: In a continuum school these three are one journey rather than three products, and the handover points are where the work is. Each note below describes what changes at the join.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, with no external examination and reporting against learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning. Children finish the PYP with strong research habits, confident presentation and genuine curiosity. What a PYP report will not reliably tell you is whether number bonds are automatic or whether spelling and punctuation are secure.
programmes.countryNote: In Mirdif the PYP ends with the Exhibition in Year 6, which is the first time most children manage a long piece of independent work to a deadline. Families who use that experience as a diagnostic, rather than only as a celebration, usually enter the MYP better prepared.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, every criterion marked out of eight, giving a raw total of 32 that converts to a 1-7 grade through published subject boundaries. Assessment is continuous rather than terminal, with investigations, reflections and tasks through the year, culminating in the Personal Project in Year 11 and, in many schools, on-screen eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP's criterion structure is the most useful and least discussed thing about it. A Mirdif student losing marks in Sciences criterion B is failing to design an investigation, not failing at science. Naming the criterion turns a vague grade into a specific, fixable problem, and most students have never had it explained to them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment, teacher-marked and externally moderated, worth roughly a fifth to a third of the grade. UAE schools sit the May session. The assessment logic is markscheme-driven, which is the sharpest change from MYP criterion descriptors.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma's first term is where a continuum student's gaps become visible, and they are usually gaps in fluency and examination technique rather than in understanding. A Mirdif family that books a diagnostic in September of Year 12, rather than waiting for the January report, has a far cheaper problem to solve.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The alternative route at sixteen, examined terminally with syllabus codes that matter: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Pearson International GCSE Mathematics is 4MA1. Mirdif's British and Indian-curriculum schools run IGCSE, so a continuum family's neighbours are frequently on a completely different assessment model, which makes comparing notes misleading.
programmes.countryNote: Families sometimes move a child from MYP into an IGCSE school for Years 10 and 11, usually to secure externally examined grades. That transfer has a real content gap in Mathematics, where IGCSE students arrive with considerably more drilled algebraic fluency, and a smaller one in the sciences.

dubai/mirdif.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described at the point in the continuum where Mirdif families most often ask for help, with the criterion or component where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria: A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where most marks are lost, because it asks students to find and justify a general rule rather than to compute, and that is a specific skill nobody has taught them to practise.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B and C carry the investigation work, and students routinely lose marks in C by presenting data without evaluating the method's reliability, which the descriptor explicitly asks for.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria A analysing, B organising, C producing text, D using language. Marks are lost in A, where students summarise a text rather than analyse the writer's choices, and in B, where a strong argument is presented without a controlling structure the examiner can follow.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D separates the grades: students describe multiple perspectives without evaluating sources or recognising the limitations of their own evidence, which is precisely what the descriptor requires.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Criteria A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The commonest loss is in A, where students research the problem thinly and then produce a good solution to a badly defined brief, which caps the whole project regardless of execution.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Diploma's algebraic route, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Continuum students arriving from MYP typically understand the concepts and lack the manipulation speed, because MYP criterion C rewards clear communication rather than fluent execution. That gap is closeable in a term with daily short practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the calculator permitted throughout. MYP criterion D maps onto this course more naturally than onto Analysis, which is why continuum students often settle better here. The statistics still has to be learned properly: interpretation must name the variables, the test and the significance level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level difficulty, and the Internal Assessment is a single self-designed investigation. MYP Sciences criterion B and C prepare a student well for the design and evaluation, and barely at all for the content density of Higher Level.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward algebraic fluency, which is the exact skill a continuum student is most likely to be short of. Extended-response marks are lost to command-term confusion: describing a phenomenon where the question asked for an explanation using a named quantity.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most content-dense Diploma science and the biggest jump from MYP in sheer volume. Retrieval practice between sessions does most of the work, and command terms separate a 5 from a 7 more reliably than additional coverage does.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics Extended
subjects.description: Relevant to Mirdif families whose children sit IGCSE rather than MYP, and to those transferring in. Bounds, surds, algebraic fractions and graph transformations recur in every series and are the quickest marks to recover with targeted drilling.

subjects.name: IGCSE Separate Sciences
subjects.description: Three subjects, three entry codes and three sets of practical-skills technique. The practical paper is where marks are cheapest to recover, because candidates asked to criticise a method typically describe it instead.

sections.heading: What a full continuum changes about tutoring
paragraphs: A child who moves from a British primary school to a British secondary school and then sits IGCSEs has had the same kind of assessment applied to them throughout: marks against a markscheme, tending towards terminal examinations. A child who goes through the full IB continuum has not. Each stage assesses something different, and the thing it assesses changes more than the content does.

The Primary Years Programme assesses through inquiry, with no external examination. The Middle Years Programme assesses against four published criteria per subject, each out of eight, continuously through the year. The Diploma assesses against papers with markschemes plus an externally moderated Internal Assessment. Those are three different games. A student can be excellent at the first two and genuinely unprepared for the third, and nothing in their reports will have predicted it.

For a Mirdif family this is the central practical fact. The question is almost never whether the child is capable. It is whether they have the specific skills the next stage of assessment requires, and the honest answer is usually that they have some of them and not others. Naming which ones is what a diagnostic is for, and it is far cheaper to do that in September of Year 12 than in February.

There is also a positive side that gets understated. Continuum students arrive in the Diploma with research habits, presentation confidence and a tolerance for independent work that IGCSE students often lack, and those are exactly the qualities the Extended Essay and the Internal Assessments reward. The deficit is in fluency and examination technique, which are the two most drillable things in education.

sections.heading: The MYP criteria, named by letter
paragraphs: This is the most useful and least published information about the MYP. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of eight, giving a raw total of 32 which the school converts to a 1-7 grade using published subject boundaries. The criteria are not generic: they differ by subject group, and each has a descriptor that states exactly what a student must do to reach each band.

Across the pages competing for IB tutoring searches in this market, not one names a single criterion. That is a remarkable omission, because the criterion is the diagnosis. A student with a 4 in MYP Sciences has not failed at science; they have scored poorly against one or two of four specific descriptors, and which ones changes entirely what should be done about it.

The table below lists the four criteria for the subject groups Mirdif families most often ask about, with what each actually assesses and the commonest reason marks are lost. Read your child's marked task sheets against it. The criterion scores are usually written on the sheet, and the pattern across two or three tasks is normally obvious.

The practical move after that is to teach the student to read the descriptor themselves. An MYP student who understands that criterion B in Mathematics asks them to find and justify a general rule, and that computing an answer correctly scores nothing under that criterion, will change their behaviour without any further intervention. That single realisation is worth more than a term of content revision.

sections.heading: eAssessment and the Personal Project at the end of MYP
paragraphs: Many continuum schools end the MYP with formal external assessment, which surprises families who have been told the programme has no examinations. The on-screen eAssessment covers subject groups including Language and Literature, Sciences, Mathematics and Individuals and Societies, alongside an interdisciplinary component, with ePortfolios used in Language Acquisition, the Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education. The Personal Project is completed and moderated separately.

The eAssessment is a genuine examination with a genuine technique requirement, and it is the first time most MYP students have sat one. The format is on-screen, the tasks are set in unseen contexts, and students who have only ever been assessed on coursework-style tasks over weeks frequently underperform relative to their classroom grades. That is a technique problem, and it responds to timed practice rather than to more content.

The Personal Project is the other major component and the one where the honesty boundary matters most. It is the student's own extended independent project with a supervisor, assessed against published criteria, and the supervisor's job includes verifying that the work is the student's own. A tutor can help a student plan it, narrow its scope, understand the criteria and reflect usefully on the process. A tutor cannot produce any part of it.

The table sets out the components, who marks each, and where students lose marks. The last column is the one to act on, because in every case the loss is a predictable behaviour rather than a knowledge gap. Confirm all timings and arrangements with your school's MYP coordinator, since no IB date is published on this page.

sections.heading: MYP to Diploma, mapped subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the section a Mirdif continuum family actually needs, and nothing like it exists on any competing page. One competitor has a single subheading about the IGCSE to IB gap. Nobody has a structured, subject-by-subject account of what changes between MYP year five and Diploma year one, which is the transition most continuum students are making.

The pattern across subjects is consistent. What transfers well is conceptual understanding, research habit, independent working and the ability to produce extended written work. What does not transfer is procedural fluency, markscheme literacy and the ability to produce a correct answer quickly under time pressure. MYP criterion C in Mathematics rewards clear communication of a method; Diploma Paper 1 rewards getting it right in the time available without a calculator.

The table maps each major subject from its MYP endpoint to its Diploma entry point, states the specific gap, and gives a realistic estimate of how many weeks of support typically closes it. Those estimates assume work done between sessions; without homework they roughly double, which is worth saying to the student rather than only to the parent paying.

The timing matters as much as the content. A transition block that runs across the summer before Year 12 and the first weeks of term costs a fraction of remedial work in February, because it is fixing a fluency gap before it has had a chance to turn into a confidence problem. By the time a student has sat two Diploma tests badly, the work includes undoing their conclusion about themselves.

sections.heading: Mirdif and the eastern suburbs: who lives here and what they ask for
paragraphs: Mirdif's household mix is different from the coast and it changes the tutoring questions. This is villa and townhouse country with a large, settled, long-resident population: Arab families, substantial Indian and Pakistani communities, and a steady expatriate professional group, many of whom have been in Dubai for a decade or more rather than on a three-year posting.

That produces two distinctive patterns. The first is multi-curriculum households. It is entirely normal in Mirdif for one child to be on the MYP at a continuum school and a sibling on a national curriculum at an Indian-curriculum school a few minutes away, which means the household is managing two completely different assessment systems and two different sets of expectations. Comparing the two children's reports is actively misleading.

The second is the long view. Families who have been here ten years are frequently planning around UAE and regional university admission rather than only around a return to a home country, which makes Ministry of Education equivalency and attestation a live concern rather than an abstract one. On the British track, the Ministry requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E.

Practically, Mirdif has one real advantage over most of Dubai. Substantial school provision sits inside the community, so many children are home shortly after school rather than after a long bus run, and a 3.45pm or 4pm start is genuinely workable here. Families on the Silicon Oasis and Festival City routes are the exception and tend towards later weekday slots or weekend mornings.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs by continuum stage, in AED
paragraphs: Price varies by stage for structural reasons, and the structure is worth understanding before taking a quote. PYP support needs a strong generalist. MYP support needs someone who knows the criteria. Diploma Higher Level support needs a subject specialist who has taught the course to assessment, and that pool is small, which is what moves the rate.

The market bands in Dubai, as published, run as follows. EdFlik publishes online rates from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, which generally means a generalist or a university student. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table places in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors.

What that means stage by stage is set out below. The notable point is the MYP row, because MYP support is frequently bought at generalist rates and then does not work, for a precise reason: a generalist can explain content but cannot explain criterion B. Paying the qualified-tutor band for someone who knows the criteria is better value than paying the budget band twice.

None of these figures are IB Gram's price list, and none should be read as one. They are what the named providers publish, read in October 2026, and they are here because almost nobody in this market publishes anything at all in dirhams. Ask any provider which band their quote sits in and what the tutor has actually taught to assessment.

sections.heading: Honesty across the continuum: Personal Project, IA and Extended Essay
paragraphs: A continuum student produces three major pieces of independent assessed work across their school career: the PYP Exhibition, the Personal Project in MYP year five, and the Internal Assessments plus the Extended Essay in the Diploma. Each has a supervisor whose responsibilities include verifying that the work is genuinely the student's own.

That matters because there are providers in this market selling finished work. One advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price in dirhams. Measured per hour it looks cheap. It is the most expensive purchase available, because the IB's authenticity requirement places the consequence on the student: a malpractice finding can remove the award, and the seller carries nothing.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial, and at MYP it is arguably more valuable than at Diploma. Helping a student narrow a Personal Project from something unmanageable to something answerable is genuine teaching. So is explaining what the criteria ask for, teaching the discipline of a process journal kept as you go rather than reconstructed afterwards, teaching referencing properly before it matters, and reading the student's own draft and putting the criteria to them as questions.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of the work, including a rewritten section or an edit heavy enough that the words cease to be the student's. The practical protection is scheduling: review sessions placed early against the school's internal deadlines, so the boundary never comes under pressure in a panic week. Ask any prospective tutor directly what they will and will not do with a draft. The answer is diagnostic.

sections.heading: Starting at the right point in the continuum
paragraphs: The cheapest interventions in a continuum are the ones made at a handover rather than in the middle of a stage, and the handovers are predictable. There are four, and each has a characteristic failure mode a family can watch for.

PYP into MYP, at the start of Year 7, is where a child meets subject-specific criteria for the first time. The failure mode is a student who inquires beautifully and cannot structure a written answer to a descriptor. A small amount of explicit teaching about what the criteria want, early in Year 7, prevents two years of mild underperformance that nobody diagnoses.

MYP year three into year five, around Year 9 into Year 10, is where the criteria get genuinely demanding and the Personal Project appears on the horizon. The failure mode is drift: grades that sit at 4 and 5 without anybody being able to say why. This is the point at which reading the marked task sheets against the criterion table above pays for itself.

MYP into Diploma is the big one, and it is the one worth planning for in advance rather than reacting to. The failure mode is a capable student with a fluency gap who concludes after two poor tests that they are not good at the subject. A transition block over the summer and into the first weeks of Year 12 addresses the fluency before the conclusion forms. Diploma year one into year two is the fourth, and the failure mode there is coursework debt carried forward from a spring that got away. Each of these is a finite, diagnosable piece of work rather than an open-ended commitment.

sections.heading: What to send before the first session
paragraphs: A continuum family can make a tutor far more useful with three documents, all of which already exist and none of which cost anything. The difference between a first session spent diagnosing and a first session spent asking questions is usually just whether these arrived in advance.

The first is two or three marked MYP task sheets in the subject concerned, with the criterion scores visible. Those scores are the diagnosis. A pattern of low criterion B scores in Sciences across three tasks is a completely different problem from low criterion A scores, and the fix in each case is specific.

The second, for a Diploma student, is a marked paper rather than a report. The report gives a grade; the paper shows where the marks went. Five minutes with a script usually distinguishes a content gap from a technique gap, and those lead to different plans at different costs. Schools release scripts on request after internal assessments and mocks, and asking is routine.

The third is the school's internal deadline calendar, which the MYP or Diploma coordinator will normally provide. Personal Project, Internal Assessment and Extended Essay dates are set by the school, not the IB, and they are the dates a sensible plan is built around. With those three things in hand, a first session produces a named topic list and an honest session estimate instead of a conversation.

A fourth item helps for a Year 11 student: which Higher Level subjects they are heading towards, even provisionally. The transition gaps differ by subject, and the work worth doing in the summer before Year 12 is specific to the three subjects taken at Higher Level rather than spread across all six. A provisional answer is enough. It narrows an open-ended request into a finite block, which is both cheaper and considerably more likely to produce something visible by October.

process.title: Say which stage and which criterion
process.description: For an MYP student the useful detail is the subject and the criterion letters where marks are being lost, taken from marked task sheets. For a Diploma student it is the subject, the level and the next graded component. Stage and criterion together determine who should teach the hour.

process.title: Diagnostic from the student's own marked work
process.description: The first session reads the marked task sheets or script and watches the student attempt a comparable task. It ends with a named list of what to fix and a realistic number of sessions, which for a transition gap is usually a finite block rather than an open commitment.

process.title: Matched to the stage, not just the subject
process.description: A tutor fluent in MYP Sciences criteria and a tutor fluent in Diploma Higher Level Chemistry are frequently different people. Matching is done on stage and criterion as well as subject, and where a particular combination has no UAE-based tutor free you are told before booking.

process.title: Teach the student to read the descriptor
process.description: Part of every MYP session is spent on the criterion itself, so the student can eventually diagnose their own work. A student who understands that criterion B in Mathematics wants a justified general rule changes their behaviour without further intervention, which is the cheapest gain available.

process.title: Work placed against the school's deadlines
process.description: Personal Project, Internal Assessment and Extended Essay dates are set by the school rather than the IB, so sessions are scheduled from the coordinator's calendar. Early review sessions also keep the authorship boundary comfortable rather than tested in a panic week.

process.title: Review at the handover, then stop or continue
process.description: A transition block is finished when the fluency gap is closed, and finishing is the expected outcome rather than a lost sale. The plan is reviewed at the next graded component, with fewer hours treated as a legitimate recommendation.

whyPoints.title: The MYP criteria named, not alluded to
whyPoints.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, listed by letter for eight subject groups. Across the pages competing for IB tutoring searches in this market, not one names a single criterion, and the criterion is the diagnosis rather than a detail.

whyPoints.title: A real transition map
whyPoints.description: MYP to Diploma mapped subject by subject, with the specific gap and a realistic number of weeks to close it. One competitor has a single subheading on the IGCSE to IB gap; nobody has a structured version, and the transition is the commonest reason a continuum family searches.

whyPoints.title: eAssessment and Personal Project covered
whyPoints.description: The end of MYP involves genuine external assessment, which surprises families told the programme has no examinations. The components, who marks each and where marks are lost are set out, along with what a tutor may and may not do with a Personal Project.

whyPoints.title: Rates by stage with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure names the provider who published it and the month it was read, from EdFlik's AED 45 to 65 through to BartyED's AED 650. MYP support bought at generalist rates usually fails for a precise reason, and the table explains it.

whyPoints.title: Matched on stage as well as subject
whyPoints.description: Knowing MYP Sciences criterion C and knowing Diploma Higher Level Chemistry are different competences. Matching uses stage and criterion alongside subject, and coverage limits in scarce combinations are disclosed before a booking rather than afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Online, which widens the specialist pool
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video and nobody travels to a UAE address. For a continuum family that is the practical point: an MYP criteria specialist and a Higher Level subject specialist need not both happen to live in the eastern suburbs.

faqs.question: Why did my child's grades drop when they started the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually because the assessment changed rather than the child. The Middle Years Programme assesses against four published criteria per subject, each out of eight, continuously through the year. The Diploma assesses against papers with markschemes plus an externally moderated Internal Assessment. A student who has become good at satisfying criterion descriptors has a real skill, but it is not the same as producing a correct answer quickly under time pressure for method marks. The gap is in procedural fluency and markscheme literacy, both of which are highly drillable once named.

faqs.question: What are the four MYP assessment criteria and how are they marked?
faqs.answer: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each marked out of eight, giving a raw total of 32 that the school converts to a 1-7 grade using published subject boundaries. The criteria differ by subject group: in Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The criterion scores are usually written on the marked task sheet.

faqs.question: My child scores well in MYP Maths but badly on criterion B. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Criterion B in MYP Mathematics is investigating patterns, and it asks the student to find a general rule and justify it, not to compute an answer. A student can be entirely accurate and score poorly against B because they produced correct arithmetic where the task wanted a generalisation with reasoning attached. It is a specific, teachable skill, and it needs practice on pattern tasks rather than more content revision. It also matters for the Diploma, since justification is exactly what Analysis and Approaches rewards.

faqs.question: Does the MYP really have external exams at the end?
faqs.answer: In many continuum schools, yes, which surprises families told the programme has no examinations. On-screen eAssessment covers subject groups including Language and Literature, Sciences, Mathematics and Individuals and Societies plus an interdisciplinary component, with ePortfolios used in Language Acquisition, the Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education, and the Personal Project assessed separately. The on-screen papers are timed and set in unseen contexts, which is a genuine technique requirement for students assessed on coursework-style tasks until then. Confirm the arrangements with your school's MYP coordinator.

faqs.question: How long does it take to close the MYP to Diploma gap in Maths?
faqs.answer: Typically eight to twelve weeks of support with daily short practice between sessions, and roughly double that without the practice. The gap is fluency rather than understanding: continuum students generally grasp the concepts and lack the speed and accuracy that a non-calculator Paper 1 demands. Short daily algebraic drilling achieves far more than longer weekly sessions, because manipulation speed is built by repetition. Doing this over the summer before Year 12 costs a fraction of remedial work in February, when a confidence problem has usually been added to the fluency one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes, and at this stage it is genuinely valuable. A tutor can help the student narrow an unmanageable idea into something answerable, explain what the published criteria ask for, teach the discipline of keeping a process journal as the work happens rather than reconstructing it afterwards, teach referencing properly, and read the student's own draft and put the criteria to them as questions. What a tutor must not do is produce any part of it. The supervisor's responsibilities include verifying the work is the student's own.

faqs.question: Should we move our child from MYP to an IGCSE school for Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: Some Mirdif families do, usually to secure externally examined grades, and it is a legitimate choice rather than an obvious one. The real content gap is in Mathematics, where IGCSE students arrive in Year 10 with considerably more drilled algebraic fluency than an MYP cohort, and a smaller one in the sciences. Against that, a continuum student loses the familiarity with criteria that will help in the Diploma. If you are considering it, ask the receiving school what it expects of a student joining from MYP and plan a bridging block accordingly.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring cheaper than Diploma tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Somewhat, and the gap is smaller than families expect. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, which is roughly the shape of the market. MYP support sits in the qualified-subject-tutor band at AED 150 to 300 rather than the budget band, for a precise reason: a generalist can explain content but cannot explain criterion B. Buying MYP help at AED 45 to 65 an hour, which is where EdFlik's published range starts, usually means paying twice because the first attempt does not address the criteria.

faqs.question: Which schools in Mirdif offer the full IB continuum?
faqs.answer: Mirdif holds full International Baccalaureate continuum provision alongside British, American and Indian curriculum schools, with Uptown School in Mirdif the best known continuum option in the immediate area and Star International School, GEMS Royal Dubai School in Al Mizhar, Al Mizhar American Academy and Mirdif Private School all within a short run. Deira International School in Al Garhoud is the nearest continuum alternative to the west. These are named as context only, and each school's curriculum licence and current KHDA inspection band should be checked on the KHDA site.

faqs.question: My two children are on different curricula. Can I compare their reports?
faqs.answer: No, and trying to is actively misleading. An MYP grade is a 1-7 derived from four criteria each marked out of eight, assessed continuously. A national-curriculum or British-curriculum report carries a working grade against an examined standard. The two measure different things on different scales, and a child who looks stronger on paper may simply be on the more generous scale. Multi-curriculum households are the norm in Mirdif rather than the exception, so this comes up constantly. Judge each child against their own programme's expectations.

faqs.question: What time can lessons start for a Mirdif family?
faqs.answer: Earlier than in most of Dubai, which is a genuine local advantage. Substantial school provision sits inside Mirdif and Al Mizhar, so many children are home shortly after school rather than after a long bus run, and a 3.45pm or 4pm start is realistically workable. The exceptions are families on the Dubai Silicon Oasis, Academic City and Festival City routes, where the return leg is longer and less predictable, and those households tend towards a post-5pm weekday slot or a weekend morning instead.

faqs.question: Where do MYP Science students most often lose marks?
faqs.answer: In criteria B and C. Criterion B is inquiring and designing, and students lose marks by writing a method that is not genuinely reproducible or by failing to identify and control relevant variables. Criterion C is processing and evaluating, and the characteristic loss is presenting data accurately and then not evaluating the reliability of the method, which the descriptor explicitly requires. Both are behaviours rather than knowledge gaps, which makes them fast to fix once a student has read the descriptor and understood what it is asking for.

faqs.question: Does the IB Diploma or IGCSE route matter for UAE university admission?
faqs.answer: Both are recognised routes, and for long-resident Mirdif families the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements matter more than the choice between them. On the British track, the Ministry requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at E. No IB points threshold is published here because none could be verified on a Ministry source. Check the current requirements on the Ministry's own site.

faqs.question: What should I send a tutor before the first session?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free and all already in existence. Two or three marked MYP task sheets in the subject concerned, with the criterion scores visible, because the pattern of criterion scores is the diagnosis. For a Diploma student, a marked script rather than a report, since the report gives a grade and the script shows where the marks went. And the school's internal coursework deadline calendar from the coordinator. With those three, a first session produces a plan rather than a conversation.

faqs.question: Is it too late to help if my child is already halfway through Diploma year one?
faqs.answer: No, but the work changes shape. Early in Year 12 the job is closing a fluency gap before a confidence problem forms. By the middle of the year, two or three poor tests have usually happened, so the work includes undoing the student's conclusion about their own ability alongside the technique repair. That is slower but entirely doable. The priority order is usually the Higher Level subject causing most distress first, coursework debt second, and the remaining subjects after the next assessment round rather than all at once.

dubai/mirdif.closingHeading: Fix it at the handover, not in the middle
dubai/mirdif.closingBody: The continuum's great advantage is continuity and its characteristic risk is a student who looks fine right up to the point the assessment changes. The four handovers are predictable: into Year 7, into MYP year five, into Diploma year one and into year two. Each has a known failure mode and each is a finite piece of work if it is caught at the join. Read your child's marked task sheets against the criterion letters, get the coordinator's deadline calendar, and book a diagnostic before the report rather than after it. IB Gram arranges one-to-one lessons over live video, matched to the stage as well as the subject.

dubai/mohammed-bin-rashid-city.tutorsIntro: The tutors here are chosen for the specific gap a Mohammed Bin Rashid City student has, not for general subject coverage. That means someone who can teach the Paper 6 marking conventions, or the difference between criterion C and criterion D on a science investigation, rather than someone who re-explains the textbook.

intro.heading: What the school covers, and what your child is left to do alone
paragraphs: Parents in Mohammed Bin Rashid City rarely have a complaint about the teaching. The district's schools sit among the better-resourced in Dubai, the class sizes are manageable and the syllabus gets covered. The problem families bring to us is narrower and more specific: a student who understands the material in class is losing marks on paper, and nobody in the system has the time to work out why. That is a structural gap, not a teaching failure, and it is the honest subject of this page.

The arithmetic is straightforward once you write it down. A Higher Level Diploma subject gets four or five periods a week across two years, which is enough time to deliver content and almost no time to practise converting it into marks under exam conditions. An Internal Assessment worth a fifth of the final grade gets a handful of lessons on the criteria and then becomes the student's own project. The Extended Essay has a supervisor with a limited mandated contact time and four thousand words of independent work attached to it. Theory of Knowledge gets one or two periods a week and is treated as unexaminable until February.

On the IGCSE side the gap has a different shape. Extended-tier content is covered, but the papers that carry the marks are not all practised. Cambridge 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics and 0610 Biology each put twenty per cent of the grade on an alternative-to-practical or practical paper with its own marking conventions, and in a crowded scheme of work that paper is frequently never taught as a paper at all. A student can know the chemistry and still lose a grade on Paper 6 because nobody told them what the examiner is looking for.

This is the kind of gap a weekly one-to-one hour is genuinely good at closing, and it is worth being equally clear about the gaps it cannot close. A student who has not read the set texts does not acquire them in tutoring. A student two full terms behind in Maths Analysis and Approaches Higher Level needs a decision about the level, not an hour a week. The useful first step is a diagnostic against the student's own marked work, which tells you which category you are in before you spend anything.

Lessons for Mohammed Bin Rashid City families are one-to-one and delivered live over video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The reason that matters for a gap-closing brief in particular is that the person who can teach criterion D on a science investigation, or the Paper 6 conventions, is a subject specialist rather than whoever is available locally. Matching on specialism is the whole point when the problem is this specific.

dubai/mohammed-bin-rashid-city.programmesIntro: Mohammed Bin Rashid City covers Sobha Hartland, District One, District 11, Azizi Riviera and the Meydan edge, so the district contains every programme shape Dubai offers. Each one leaves a different amount of work to the student.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS alongside. Internal Assessments carry 20 to 30 per cent of each subject grade depending on the subject and level, marked internally against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The examined component rewards precision under time pressure, which is the part least practised in class.
programmes.countryNote: In Mohammed Bin Rashid City the Diploma gap is almost always the same two things: the Internal Assessment research question, chosen badly in week one and discovered in week eight, and timed paper practice, which gets postponed until the mocks expose it. Both are fixable, and both are cheaper to fix in October than in March.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight, with command terms that decide the shape of a good answer. Year 11 students may sit MYP eAssessment on screen. Criterion totals convert to a 1 to 7 subject grade, which rarely corresponds to a parent's intuition from a percentage system.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP gap in this district is the command term, not the content. A student who writes a description when the task said evaluate caps their own criterion score while understanding the topic perfectly. One session with the actual marked task in front of the tutor usually identifies it, and a term of weekly practice fixes it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined at the end of Year 11, using Cambridge syllabuses such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, or Pearson equivalents including 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge tiers several subjects Core or Extended; the tier fixes the grade ceiling and the decision is effectively locked at the entry deadline.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE gap here is paper-shaped. Extended content is taught, and the alternative-to-practical paper that carries a fifth of each science grade often is not, because it is a skills paper rather than a content one. A handful of sessions on marking conventions is the highest-return tutoring available at this level.

programmes.name: A Level, after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four linear subjects examined at the end of Year 13. Mathematics covers pure, mechanics and statistics; sciences carry a separate practical endorsement. Offers from universities are quoted in A Level grades, which makes the choice at sixteen a direct admissions decision rather than a matter of preference.
programmes.countryNote: The A Level gap in Mohammed Bin Rashid City is the jump in question length from IGCSE. Students who scored well at sixteen on short structured questions meet extended problems with no scaffolding and lose marks for stopping halfway. The fix is timed question sets with a mark-scheme walkthrough, which takes ninety minutes and does not fit in a school lesson.

dubai/mohammed-bin-rashid-city.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where the classroom-to-paper gap is widest in this district, with the specific component that tends to cause it. The point of naming the component is that it tells you what a session should actually be about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The gap is Paper 3 at Higher Level, which rewards sustained reasoning across an unfamiliar context and cannot be revised topic by topic. The Exploration is the second gap: criterion E asks for mathematics commensurate with the course, and most first drafts are below it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator fluency is the hidden gap. Students who can do the statistics by hand lose time and accuracy marks because they never learned the graphical calculator routes the paper assumes.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms are the content gap and the Scientific Investigation is the marks gap. Criterion D, evaluation, is where most students write generic limitations instead of naming the specific weakness in their own method.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Explanation questions are the gap. A student with the right physics in their head loses marks for writing it loosely, omitting units or giving an answer to the wrong number of significant figures. All three are coachable in weeks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume plus command terms. Outline, explain, discuss and evaluate each demand a different answer shape, and the difference between a 5 and a 7 is usually the shape rather than the knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation paragraph. The commentary portfolio is the other gap: a commentary that describes an article rather than applying a key concept to it loses marks the student did not know were available.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The unseen non-literary paper and the individual oral. Both are technique components, both are examined, and both get less class time than the set texts because the texts have to be covered.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.description: Method marks are the gap. Students who write an answer with no working forgo marks that were available even when the answer is wrong, and non-calculator arithmetic on the Extended paper is where multi-step questions unravel.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry, Physics and Biology
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper carries a fifth of the grade and its own conventions: apparatus naming, variable control, sources of error and how to read a results table. It is the single most improvable component at this level.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Directed writing and the unseen extract. The gap is the assessment objective split between content and language, which students are rarely shown explicitly and which determines where effort pays.

dubai/mohammed-bin-rashid-city.regionsTitle: The communities inside Mohammed Bin Rashid City
dubai/mohammed-bin-rashid-city.regionsIntro: MBR City is a district rather than a neighbourhood, running from the canal south to Nad Al Sheba and east toward Ras Al Khor. The communities inside it have different housing, different school patterns and different versions of the same academic gap.

regions.name: District One
regions.note: Large villa plots with households often running three or four school stages at once. The practical consequence is that the Diploma student's Internal Assessment deadline competes with a Year 10 options decision in the same month, and one of them loses.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Apartments and villas with two secondary schools inside the community, which means a short school run and an unusually early workable lesson slot. Families here can get a diagnostic session done in the afternoon rather than the evening.

regions.name: District 11 and Meydan Gated Community
regions.note: Newer villa clusters where a high proportion of families arrived in the last three years. Mid-course curriculum switches are common, and the gap is often a topic the previous board did not cover rather than a technique problem.

regions.name: Azizi Riviera
regions.note: High-density apartments along the canal, with many single-child households and a mix of curricula. Requests here skew towards one subject rather than a full package, which suits a short diagnostic plus a targeted block.

regions.name: Meydan and the racecourse edge
regions.note: Administratively adjacent and practically part of the same school catchment. Families here use the Nad Al Sheba schools, which puts them on a different exam calendar from the Hartland cohort a few minutes away.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: The school belt serving much of MBR City. Four secondary schools sit here covering the IB continuum and the English National Curriculum, which is why neighbouring households often sit entirely different qualifications.

regions.name: Ras Al Khor and Nad Al Hamar

sections.heading: What a teacher cannot fit into a week, component by component
paragraphs: The gap is easiest to see when it is laid out as a budget. Every assessed component in the IB and IGCSE systems has a class-time allocation and an independent-work requirement, and in several cases the independent requirement is the larger of the two. That is by design: both systems are explicitly testing a student's capacity to work alone. The failure mode is not that schools neglect this, but that students are expected to self-manage a workload that adults would find demanding.

The table below sets out where the budget runs out. Three rows deserve attention. The Internal Assessment line is the one families most often discover late, because the component looks like a project and behaves like an examination. The Extended Essay line matters because supervisor contact time is capped, and once the first draft is submitted the structured support largely ends. The exam-technique line is the one almost nobody plans for: students revise content, which feels productive, and never practise against a clock, which is what the paper tests.

Reading the table honestly also tells you where tutoring is not the answer. A student who has not covered the final two topics of a Higher Level syllabus because the class ran out of time needs those topics taught, which is a content job and takes a term. A student who knows the content and loses nine marks a paper on presentation needs four sessions. Those two situations attract the same parental worry and very different solutions.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually leave the page
paragraphs: Generic advice about working harder is useless at this level because the losses are specific and they are concentrated. The Cambridge science syllabuses sat across this district split the grade three ways: a multiple-choice paper worth thirty per cent, a structured theory paper worth fifty, and a practical or alternative-to-practical paper worth twenty. A student can be strong on content and still shed close to a grade through the twenty per cent nobody practised.

Mathematics loses marks differently. Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier is assessed across a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, each carrying half the grade, and the most common loss is method marks forfeited by writing an answer with no working. Pearson 4MA1 at Higher tier runs two equally weighted papers, and the characteristic loss there is the last two questions left blank because the pacing was wrong. Neither problem is about mathematics.

The table names the component, what it tests and where the marks go. The practical consequence for a parent is that you can ask your child one question that is more diagnostic than any report: which paper did you lose the most marks on, and why. A student who cannot answer that has not been shown their own mark breakdown, which is the first thing a diagnostic session fixes.

One caution on syllabus detail. Cambridge and Pearson both revise syllabuses on a cycle, and paper structures that held for one cohort can change for the next. The weightings in this table reflect the structures sat by current candidates in this district, and the authoritative version for your child is the syllabus document for their examination year, which the school holds and Cambridge publishes. sections.heading: The Internal Assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single Internal Assessment criterion, which is strange, because the criteria are published, they are the actual basis of the mark, and most students have never read them properly. A Diploma student who knows what criterion D rewards will write a different evaluation section from one who does not, and the difference is typically two to four marks on a component worth a fifth of the grade.

The science Internal Assessment in Biology, Chemistry and Physics is a single Scientific Investigation marked out of twenty-four across four criteria carrying six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The Mathematics Exploration in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with the last carrying six marks on its own.

The table sets out what each criterion rewards and the specific way students lose marks on it. Treat the mark totals as a guide and confirm them against the current subject guide for your child's cohort, since the IB revises subject guides on a cycle and a figure correct for one cohort can be wrong for the next. Your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative version, and asking for it is a reasonable request.

The reason this table changes behaviour is that criteria are not a marking formality; they are the instructions. A student who has read criterion D properly writes an evaluation section that names the specific weakness in their own method and proposes a realistic improvement, because that is what the criterion asks for. A student who has not read it writes a paragraph about human error and parallax, and loses three or four of the six marks available while believing the section is finished. The same applies to criterion B in the Mathematics Exploration, where undefined notation costs marks that no amount of additional mathematics recovers.

The useful move is to multiply the band by the number of sessions a gap actually takes, because that is the number a parent is deciding about. A technique gap is four to six sessions. A tier or level decision is one or two. A board-switch bridge after a mid-year move is eight to twelve. A full subject catch-up is a term. Written out this way, the technique gap turns out to be the cheapest intervention available and the one most families postpone.

Two cautions on reading any of these numbers. An advertised hourly rate is not what you end up paying if there are assessment fees, materials or a minimum booking, so ask for the all-in figure and whether value added tax is included. sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what your child must be able to show
paragraphs: Equivalency is absent from most tutoring pages in this market, and one competitor publishes the wrong subject count, which is worse than silence. For a Mohammed Bin Rashid City family planning a UAE university route, the rules matter early, because they constrain subject choice in Year 10 rather than at the point of application. The figures below are from a Gulf Today report of the Ministry's own clarification, published in July 2026.

On the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is the point most often got wrong. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB Diploma this page publishes no points threshold, because the source used here states none and a figure that has not been read on the Ministry's own site should not sit on a page a family might plan around. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not a requirement for any of it. What a tutor can legitimately do is make sure the subject and grade profile a student is on track for actually satisfies the rule, which is a one-session conversation in Year 10.

sections.heading: Why buying a finished Internal Assessment closes the gap in the wrong direction
paragraphs: There is a market in Dubai for completed coursework, and at least one site ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments for a four-figure AED sum. A Mohammed Bin Rashid City parent under pressure in February will see those offers, so this page states the position rather than leaving it implied. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, the investigation falls on the student rather than the vendor, and a Diploma candidate found to have done it risks losing the award.

The practical argument is almost as strong as the rules argument. The skill an Internal Assessment tests is the skill the examination then tests again under time pressure. A student who did not design the investigation does not learn to design one, and the deficit resurfaces in May on a paper nobody can sit for them. Buying the component does not close the gap this page is about; it moves the gap to a place where it cannot be fixed.

The legitimate boundary is wide enough to be genuinely useful. A tutor can teach the criteria and their mark allocations, explain what a command term requires, help narrow a research question until it will produce usable data, teach the statistics or laboratory technique the investigation needs, read a draft the student has written and ask harder questions about it than the student asked themselves, and point out an unsupported claim. A tutor must not supply text, rewrite a passage into final form, or take over in any way that makes the submission not the student's own. IB Gram does not supply assessed work and declines requests framed that way.

sections.heading: How to tell which gap you actually have before spending anything
paragraphs: Everything on this page reduces to one question a parent can answer cheaply: is this a content gap, a technique gap or a level problem. Those three have different costs, different timescales and different solutions, and the worry they generate feels identical from the outside. The evidence that distinguishes them is already in the house, in the form of a marked paper, a progress report or a returned coursework draft.

A technique gap looks like this: the student can explain the topic aloud, the marked paper shows marks lost on presentation, units, working or command terms, and the losses are spread evenly rather than concentrated in one topic. This is the cheapest gap to close, usually four to six sessions, and it is also the one that compounds if left, because the same losses recur on every paper for the rest of the course.

A content gap looks different: whole questions left blank, consistent losses in the same topics, and a student who cannot explain the material when asked. This needs the topics taught and takes a term. A level problem is the third case, where a student is two terms behind in a Higher Level subject and the honest advice is a conversation with the school about the level rather than more hours. A diagnostic session that reads the actual marked work tells you which of the three you are in, and it is worth doing before any commitment.

Content gap: whole questions blank and consistent losses in the same topics

faqs.question: My son understands the work in class but keeps losing marks. What is actually going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always a technique gap rather than a knowledge gap. The marked paper will show it: losses spread across questions on working not shown, units omitted, answers given to the wrong number of significant figures, or an explanation written too loosely to score. Those losses recur on every paper until someone addresses them, which is why they compound. The fix is usually four to six sessions working directly on his own marked papers against the mark scheme, not a term of general subject review. Ask to see his mark breakdown by question before buying anything.

faqs.question: How much of the IB science grade does the Internal Assessment carry, and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: The Scientific Investigation in Biology, Chemistry and Physics carries twenty per cent of the final grade and is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is assessed internally against the published criteria and moderated by the IB. Most lost marks sit in research design, where the question is too broad to answer, and evaluation, where students write about generic human error instead of naming the specific weakness in their own method. Confirm the current totals against your child's subject guide, since the IB revises guides on a cycle.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper, and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: It is the paper that replaces a live practical examination in the Cambridge sciences, and it carries roughly a fifth of the grade in Chemistry, Physics and Biology. It tests apparatus selection, variable control, reading and completing results tables, identifying sources of error and suggesting improvements. The reason it matters disproportionately is that it is a skills paper, and in a crowded scheme of work it is often never taught as a paper at all. A handful of sessions on its marking conventions is the highest-return tutoring available at IGCSE level.

faqs.question: Which criterion do Mathematics Exploration marks usually disappear on?
faqs.answer: Criterion E, use of mathematics, which carries six of the twenty available marks. The requirement is mathematics commensurate with the course, and a large share of first drafts sit below the level of the course because the student chose a topic they were already comfortable with. Criterion C, personal engagement, is the second common loss, where a textbook topic is reproduced with no independent contribution. Both are fixable at the planning stage and very difficult to fix once twelve pages are written, which is the argument for a session on the research question early rather than feedback late.

faqs.question: Is there any point hiring a tutor six weeks before the exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a technique gap, and much less so for a content gap. In six weeks a student can learn to show working, get units and significant figures right, handle command terms correctly and pace a paper, and those changes show up in marks immediately because the knowledge is already there. Six weeks will not teach two missing Higher Level topics properly. The honest answer depends on which situation you are in, and a diagnostic session on a recent mock paper answers that in an hour rather than after a month of lessons.

faqs.question: What does it cost to close a technique gap in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions at the market rate for a qualified subject tutor, which published figures put at roughly AED 150-300 an hour; Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. For an Internal Assessment method block, three or four sessions at specialist rates of AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and a 2026 Dubai cost survey listing 200-450 and upwards. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices. Ask any provider for the all-in number, whether value added tax is included, and what happens if the match is wrong.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the research design for my daughter's Chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most valuable place to use one. A tutor can explain what criterion A rewards, help narrow the question until it will actually generate usable data, discuss which variables need controlling and why, and teach the technique and uncertainty handling the method requires. What a tutor must not do is supply text, rewrite a section into final form, or take over the investigation. IB Gram does not supply assessed work and declines requests framed that way, because submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on your daughter.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Mohammed Bin Rashid City student need for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade, according to a Gulf Today report of the Ministry's own clarification published in July 2026. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. At least one ranking competitor states six subjects, which is the error to avoid inheriting. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before making subject decisions, and note that IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Why do I need a separate session for the Extended Essay if there is already a supervisor?
faqs.answer: Supervisor contact time is limited by design, and the structured part of it largely ends once the first draft is submitted. The components that cost marks afterwards are the argument's coherence, the use of sources and the reflections, and those are exactly what a reader outside the school can question usefully. A tutor reads the student's own draft and asks harder questions than the student asked themselves. The tutor does not research it, structure it on the student's behalf or write any of it, and the four thousand words have to be the student's own.

faqs.question: My child is at a Nad Al Sheba school and we live in District One. Does that change anything practically?
faqs.answer: It changes the slot rather than the tutoring. A District One address with a Nad Al Sheba school run realistically starts a lesson at five o'clock or later, because the drive runs into the worst of the afternoon. Families in Sobha Hartland, a few minutes away inside the same district, can usually start around quarter past four because their schools are inside the community. Since lessons run online there is no additional travel to account for, so the only question is when your child can sit down with a clear head.

faqs.question: Should we switch my son from Higher Level to Standard Level instead of getting a tutor?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and an honest provider will say so. If he is two full terms behind in a Higher Level subject, cannot explain the foundational material when asked, and is losing whole questions rather than marks within questions, extra hours are unlikely to recover it and the conversation belongs with the school. If he knows the content and is losing marks on presentation, timing and command terms, the level is not the problem. A diagnostic session on his marked papers distinguishes the two cases, and we will tell you which one the evidence shows.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do operate across Dubai at market rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel priced in, per a 2026 Dubai cost survey and tutors' own published pages. For the kind of work this page describes the trade-off is sharp: the person who can teach the alternative-to-practical conventions or a specific Internal Assessment criterion is a narrow specialist, and the subset willing to drive to District One for an afternoon start is narrower still.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's teacher before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Three questions. Which paper is losing the most marks, and roughly how many. Whether the loss is content the student has not grasped or technique they have not been shown. And what the internal deadline list looks like for coursework components this term. Those three answers turn a vague worry into a brief a tutor can act on, and they are information the school already holds. A teacher who can answer them has effectively written your diagnostic for you, which saves a session.

faqs.question: How early is too early to start Internal Assessment support?
faqs.answer: The expensive mistake is starting late, not early. The research question is chosen in roughly week one of the component and the consequences of choosing badly surface around week eight, by which point redesigning means losing the work already done. One session at the planning stage, spent narrowing the question until the data collection is realistic and checking it against the criteria, is worth more than three sessions on a finished draft. In practice that means September or October for most Diploma cohorts, timed against the school's own internal deadline list rather than a board date.

faqs.question: If the gap is technique, why would it take more than one session to fix?
faqs.answer: Because the losses are habits rather than facts. A student who has written answers without working for three years does not stop after being told once; the habit reasserts itself under exam pressure, which is exactly when it costs marks. Four to six sessions works because each one includes a timed attempt where the habit either holds or does not, with immediate feedback. One session identifies the problem and produces a list. The sessions after it are what make the change survive contact with a real paper in May.

Each tutor teaches a named specification, and an exam-run block is agreed with a fixed session count.

intro.heading: Plans built forwards from today usually run out of calendar
paragraphs: Most tutoring plans begin the same way. It is October, the mocks were disappointing, and a family decides to start an hour a week and see how it goes. That is a plan built forwards from today, and it has no relationship to the thing it is meant to prepare for. Examination boards do not work forwards. They work from fixed dates, several of which fall months before the paper, and a plan that ignores them is improvising with a deadline attached.

Built backwards, the same term looks entirely different. Twenty weeks out, there is room to teach content and fix a gap. Twelve weeks out, mixed practice should be taking over. Eight weeks out, content teaching should be finishing and whole papers under timing should be the main activity. Four weeks out, nothing new should be introduced at all. Each of those phases has a different session shape, and the sequence matters more than the total number of hours.

Motor City families bring a specific version of this because of where the community sits. The school cluster around Motor City and Dubai Sports City is largely self-contained, so the school run is shorter than for households further out in Dubailand - but Al Khail Road and the Hessa Street junctions still set the arrival time, and in exam term the evening also has to hold revision the student does alone. The slot is not the whole plan; it is the smaller part of it.

There is also a question families ask less often than they should, which is when to stop. Tutoring in the final week is usually counterproductive: it introduces new material at the point where consolidation matters, and it takes time from the student's own practice. A provider who never raises the question of stopping is not managing a plan, and this page says plainly where the endpoint belongs.

On delivery: lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, which is how a tutor and a student mark a paper together. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. In exam season that matters practically - a session can be rescheduled the same week rather than negotiated around a tutor's route, which is useful when a school adds an unexpected mock.

No figure on this page is an IB Gram price; the rates quoted are market rates with their source named. The Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the boards' own published material. IB session dates are deliberately absent, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. Nothing here promises a grade either, and the sequence below is the reason: what the remaining weeks contain is partly in a family's control, while what a particular paper asks is not.

The final stretch is therefore two problems at once: finishing coursework and building paper technique across six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: The sequencing question for a Diploma student in the final year is which comes first, and the answer is coursework. Internally assessed work has an immovable school deadline and a known mark allocation; paper practice can be compressed later, while a missed coursework deadline cannot be recovered at all.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight, with no external papers until optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11. For students taking eAssessment the final term looks more like an IGCSE run than most families expect, with timed on-screen tasks replacing the interim assessment pattern.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Motor City school enters students for MYP eAssessment, the final-term work is specifically about working to time on screen rather than about more content. Students who have only ever been assessed on interim tasks find the timing, not the material, is what costs them.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with reporting against outcomes rather than marks, and no public examinations. What matters here is building the habits the later stages assume: reading daily, knowing number facts cold, and attempting work that has not been set. None of that needs an exam-term plan.
programmes.countryNote: The useful thing for a Motor City primary family during an older sibling's exam term is simply to keep the younger child's routine intact. Households often suspend everything for the Year 11 child and then find the Year 5 child has lost a term of reading habit.

dubai/motor-city.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Motor City families most often want covered in the final stretch, with a note on what the last weeks in each should actually consist of. In several cases the answer is practice rather than teaching.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: In the final eight weeks this is whole papers under timing, not topic revision. Extended candidates lose marks on multi-step problems mixing two topics with no signposted method, and only full papers reproduce that condition. Check the tier before buying any practice material.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: The written practical paper is where late gains are easiest, because it tests reading an unfamiliar method and finding its weakness - a narrow, teachable skill almost nobody practises. Four or five sessions on it can move a grade more than ten sessions of content revision.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry reward drill right up to the paper. These are also the topics students avoid when revising alone, because they are uncomfortable, which is exactly why a tutored hour on them is good value late on.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Late marks come from command terms and terminology precision rather than from more content. A student who learns to answer the verb that was used can gain across every long question, and that is a fortnight of drill rather than a term of teaching.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level the final weeks belong to full papers and to the harder calculus and proof questions students have been skipping. If the exploration is still unfinished, it comes first: it has a fixed deadline and a known mark allocation, and papers can be compressed afterwards.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator technique is the late gain here and is genuinely teachable: students lose time and marks to clumsy use of the graphical calculator on questions they understand perfectly. Interpretation marks are the second gap, and both respond to paper practice.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers, and the final weeks are about working through them under timing. The internally assessed investigation, if still open, takes priority because its deadline will not move.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The data-analysis component is the least-practised part of the course and the easiest place to find late marks. Beyond that, the recurring loss is algebraic rather than conceptual, which paper practice exposes and topic revision hides.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume invites rereading, which is the least effective revision available. Retrieval against past questions, marked strictly against the scheme, is what moves the grade in the last ten weeks, and it is something a student can run alone once shown how.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Both are won in the final weeks on application under timing rather than on content. Economics marks live in correctly labelled diagrams; Business Management marks live in evaluating a decision. Both are fixable with past-paper case studies and strict marking.

modes.description: A fixed weekly hour used for actual teaching, appropriate while the papers are more than about ten weeks away. Content gaps get closed, methods get rebuilt, and the student practises between sessions. The session is driven by their own marked scripts rather than by syllabus order.
