sections.heading: What the remaining weeks should contain, phase by phase
paragraphs: The direct answer is that a revision term has four phases and they are not interchangeable. With more than twenty weeks left, teach. Between twelve and twenty, shift to mixed practice on taught material. Between eight and twelve, finish content and make whole papers the main activity. Inside eight weeks, teach nothing new and spend the time on timed papers, strict marking and the handful of technique faults that cost marks everywhere.

Families get this wrong in a predictable direction. They stay in the teaching phase far too long, because teaching feels productive and timed papers feel exposing. A student who is still being taught new material four weeks out has not had time to practise any of it under pressure, which means the new material will not be available to them in the paper. The teaching was real and the benefit was not.

The second common error is the opposite one, made by families who start late: going straight to whole papers with twenty weeks available and significant content gaps. A student who cannot do the topics will produce low scores on paper after paper, learn mostly that they are bad at the subject, and arrive at the exam demoralised. With twenty weeks there is time to fix the gaps first, and it should be used for that.

The table sets out the phases with what the session, the student and the schedule should be doing in each. Use the weeks-remaining column rather than the month, because the series matters: a student sitting the Cambridge March series is already inside the final phase in January, while a June candidate at the same school is still teaching. Both are in Year 11 and they should be doing different things.

sections.heading: Counted backwards: the board calendar that constrains the plan
paragraphs: Several of the dates that decide a student's options fall long before the examination, and families who meet them late lose a series rather than a week. Entries carry the syllabus code and, on Cambridge subjects, the tier, so the decision that caps a grade is taken months ahead of the paper being sat. A revision plan that does not have these dates on it is not a plan.

Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June and a November series, with a March series for some centres and subjects, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. For the March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026, the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results appear on Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates follow in late June. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning against.

IB dates are absent from this page on purpose. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session, registration or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. UAE schools sit the May session; for the exact window, the internal deadlines and the results date, ask your child's IB coordinator and build the backward plan from what they confirm in writing.

sections.heading: The last eight weeks: what to stop doing
paragraphs: Most advice about the final stretch is additive - do more of this, add that. The useful advice is subtractive, because the binding constraint is hours and every new activity displaces an existing one. Inside eight weeks there are four things that should stop, and stopping them is free.

Stop making notes. Note-making is a copying task that feels like studying and produces almost no retrievable memory. A student with a complete set of beautiful notes and no practice history is in a worse position than one with scrappy notes and a stack of marked papers. If notes are needed as a reference, they are already made; if they are not made by now, making them will not help.

Stop teaching new content, including content the student asks for. A topic learned four weeks before a paper will not have been practised under pressure, so it will not be available in the examination. The honest advice to a student who discovers a gap at this stage is that the gap is now a known cost, and the marks elsewhere that technique can recover are worth more than the ones the gap is taking.

Stop topic-by-topic practice with the book open, and stop generous marking. Both produce the feeling of competence without the substance. From eight weeks out the unit of work is a whole paper, under timing, notes closed, marked against the published scheme in a different colour, with every lost mark logged under one of four reasons. The log is what turns practice into a plan, and it is the single thing that most reliably separates a student who improves in the final stretch from one who does not.
bullets: Stop making notes; copying is not revision at this stage
Stop teaching new content, including topics the student requests
Stop open-book topic practice; the unit of work is a whole paper

sections.heading: The whole-paper routine that actually moves a grade
paragraphs: Whole papers under timing are the highest-yield revision activity available at any price, and they are free. The boards publish past papers and mark schemes and schools can supply them. What determines whether they work is entirely in the execution, and most students execute them in a way that removes the benefit.

The routine is narrow enough to write down. One whole paper, correct board and correct tier, in one sitting, under the real time limit, with notes closed and no calculator shortcuts the real paper would not allow. Then mark it against the published scheme in a different colour, to the scheme's wording rather than to whether the answer seemed reasonable. Then log each lost mark under one of four reasons: did not know it, misread the question, ran out of time, or wrote the wrong structure for the command term.

That log is the point of the exercise. After three papers a pattern appears, and it is usually lopsided: one reason accounts for most of the losses and the other three are nearly empty. A student losing marks mainly to misreading needs a procedure for the first thirty seconds of a question, which takes a fortnight. A student losing them mainly to timing needs more whole papers, not more content. Those are different plans, and the log is what tells you which you are in.

The table gives a workable volume by subject for the final ten weeks. Two cautions. First, use papers from the correct board and tier: Cambridge Core and Extended papers are different sets, and Pearson papers are structured differently again. Second, access the material through the school or the boards' own sites - past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and a tutor offering a downloadable pack of them is redistributing something that is not theirs to give.

sections.heading: When tutoring should stop
paragraphs: Almost nobody in this market will tell a family to stop, which is why it is worth saying clearly. An exam-run block should end before the final week, and in most cases a week to ten days before the first paper. The reason is not cost. It is that at that point the student's own consolidation is more valuable than anything a tutor can add, and a session in the last week displaces it.

There is a second reason, which is about the student rather than the schedule. A student still being taught days before a paper receives a message about their readiness, and it is not a helpful one. The final week should feel like the end of a process that was completed, not the continuation of a rescue. Ending the block on a planned date, after a session that reviews what was achieved, is a materially better last experience than tapering off.

There is a narrow exception. Where a student has a specific technique fault that is still costing marks - freezing in the first ten minutes, mismanaging the time split across sections, consistently misreading a particular command term - a single short session in the last week aimed only at that is justified, because it is consolidation rather than addition. That is a different thing from a scheduled lesson that continues because it was in the diary.

After the papers there is usually nothing to buy until results. The honest exception is a student who knows a resit is likely and wants to start before the decision is formal - and even then, the first useful step is the script review once results arrive rather than teaching in the gap. For a Motor City family the better use of that period is the younger sibling whose routine was suspended for a term.

sections.heading: What to buy in the final ten weeks, and what each purchase should produce
paragraphs: Budgets tighten exactly when the pressure peaks, which produces poor decisions. Families buy more subjects than the weeks can hold, or buy a premium rate for homework supervision, or buy a group revision course that repeats content the student already has. The way to avoid all three is to require each purchase to name its output before it is made.

The rates below were read from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026. They are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list; ask for our figure before booking and hold it against the band. The last column is the test: a purchase that cannot state what it should have produced by the first paper is not a purchase with a plan behind it.

Two specific judgements are worth making explicitly. A group revision course is usually poor value inside eight weeks, because it covers content at a pace set by the group while the student's actual losses are individual and diagnosable. And a premium specialist rate is good value for Higher Level work and paper technique, and poor value for supervising past papers the student could mark themselves once shown the method.

The cheapest high-value purchase in the whole of exam term is a single diagnostic hour spent reading three marked papers and building the loss log with the student. It costs one hour at a qualified rate, it produces the plan for the remaining weeks, and in a meaningful number of cases it shows that no further paid hours are needed - just the routine, run properly, by a student who now knows what they are looking for.

sections.heading: Which schools Motor City children attend, and when the bus gets back
paragraphs: Motor City is better served than most of the Dubailand belt, with schools inside the community and more immediately east in Dubai Sports City. A child at one of the local schools can be home by about half past three, which makes a four o'clock session realistic - a genuine advantage during exam term, when the useful hour is the one before fatigue rather than the one after dinner.

Older students more often travel, which changes the arithmetic. A Diploma student at a school across Al Khail Road or down towards the Ranches is typically home between five and six, which puts a weekday session at the wrong end of the evening for sustained work. For those students a weekend block of ninety minutes is worth more than two weekday hours, particularly for whole-paper practice that needs an uninterrupted stretch.

The board question matters here as everywhere. The schools in this cluster choose examination boards subject by subject, so a student can sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics, and past papers downloaded for the wrong board will be misleading in the one term where misleading practice is most expensive. Ask the examinations officer for the board, the code and the tier, in writing, before buying material or booking a tutor.

For market context: KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in Dubai in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. Dubai is adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 places. KHDA licenses and inspects schools and publishes inspection outcomes on a six-band scale; it does not license private tutors, and IB Gram claims no approval from it or from any board.

sections.heading: Coursework at the end of the course, and the line that does not move
paragraphs: In the final year, coursework and papers compete, and coursework should win. An internal assessment has a fixed school deadline and a known mark allocation, usually a meaningful share of the subject grade. Paper practice can be compressed into fewer weeks if it has to be; a missed coursework deadline cannot be recovered at all. Families who reverse this order lose marks that were available with certainty in exchange for marks that were not.

The pressure of that period is also where the honesty line gets tested hardest. Providers in this market sell finished internal assessments at a fixed price, and the offer looks most reasonable precisely when a deadline is close and a student is behind. The arithmetic is worth stating: a student who submits purchased work faces their school's academic honesty process and, under IB rules, a malpractice finding that can cost the entire diploma. The provider keeps the fee.

What a tutor can legitimately do in that window is substantial. Teach the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each. Identify which criterion is currently scoring nothing, which is usually one specific thing rather than the whole piece. Question the method, the data and the conclusion. Help the student decide which two hours of work recover the most marks. Respond to a draft with questions rather than corrections.

What a tutor must not do does not change with the deadline: no supplied text, no restructured argument, no rewritten section handed back to be retyped. The test is whether the student can defend every decision in the work under questioning, without notes. Submitting incomplete work the student wrote is a better outcome than submitting complete work they did not, and a tutor who will not say that out loud to a frightened family is not being helpful.
bullets: Coursework before papers: its deadline is fixed and its marks are certain
Criteria taught by letter, with the weakest one identified first
No supplied text and no rewritten sections, whatever the deadline
Incomplete work the student wrote beats complete work they did not

sections.heading: Availability in exam season, and the fallback when nobody is free
paragraphs: Exam season is when supply is tightest and demand is highest, which is a bad combination for a family deciding in February that help is needed for May. Higher Level Mathematics and Higher Level Physics are the first to go. Specialists in paper technique for a particular board are booked earlier than subject tutors generally. And the weeks immediately after results produce a resit rush that fills the same pool again.

The practical answer is to book the diagnostic early even if the block starts later. A diagnostic hour in November costs the same as one in February and produces a plan with fourteen more weeks in it. Where a family cannot book early, we say what is actually available rather than matching approximately: a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online with the base and time difference stated, or a waiting-list place with a date attached.

The time-difference point is not a formality in exam term. A tutor two and a half hours ahead cannot take a seven o'clock Dubai slot, and a student who needs their session at five because that is when they still have attention cannot take a tutor who is only free at nine. Those constraints have to be visible before booking, not discovered in week two when the schedule is already tight.

On the regulatory position, since parents ask: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted. IB Gram operates no UAE centre, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and delivers lessons online.

process.title: Tell us the series and the first paper date
process.description: Not the month, the series: Cambridge March, Cambridge June, Pearson November, the IB May session as confirmed by the coordinator. The whole plan is phased on weeks remaining, and two students in the same Year 11 class sitting different series should be doing different things this week.

process.title: Send three marked papers, including a bad one
process.description: The diagnostic works from scripts rather than from report grades. Three papers are enough for a pattern to appear, and the pattern is usually lopsided - one cause accounts for most losses. You get the loss log and the phased plan in writing before anything is booked.

process.title: Confirm the board, code and tier
process.description: Ask the examinations officer in writing for the board, the syllabus code and, on Cambridge subjects, the tier. In exam term practising the wrong board's papers is the most expensive mistake available, because there is no time left to correct the picture it gives.

process.title: Fix the phase, the slot and the session count
process.description: We agree which phase the student is in, how many sessions the block contains, and the weekly slot timed from their actual arrival home. For a student travelling across Al Khail Road that usually means a weekend block rather than a late weekday hour.

process.title: Put coursework first if it is still open
process.description: Where an internal assessment or Extended Essay is unfinished, checkpoints against the school's draft dates take priority over paper practice. Its deadline is fixed and its marks are certain; paper work can be compressed afterwards, and a missed coursework deadline cannot be recovered.

process.title: Set the end date at the start
process.description: The block ends a week to ten days before the first paper, on a date agreed when it begins, with a final session that reviews what was achieved. At that point the student's own consolidation is worth more than anything a session can add.

whyPoints.title: The plan is phased on weeks, not on months
whyPoints.description: Twenty weeks out, teach. Twelve out, mix. Eight out, whole papers only. Two out, technique alone. Most plans stay in the teaching phase far too long, because teaching feels productive and timed papers feel exposing.

whyPoints.title: Board deadlines are on the plan from the start
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's March entry deadline in late November, Pearson's November timetable ending on the nineteenth, the results lag of roughly two months - these change what is possible, and families meet them late more often than they miss anything academic.

whyPoints.title: The free routine is specified and checked
whyPoints.description: Whole paper, right board and tier, timed, closed notes, marked to the scheme in a different colour, every loss logged under one of four reasons. That routine does most of the work, and it stops the moment nobody is checking it.

whyPoints.title: We name the point at which to stop
whyPoints.description: The block ends a week to ten days before the first paper. Sessions in the final week displace consolidation and send a student an unhelpful message about their readiness. A provider who never proposes stopping is not managing a plan.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated to October 2026, and each purchase is required to name what it should produce by the first paper.

whyPoints.title: Coursework takes priority, and the line holds
whyPoints.description: Marks on an internal assessment are certain and its deadline is fixed, so it goes first. No text is supplied and no section rewritten, however close the deadline. Incomplete work the student wrote beats complete work they did not.

faqs.question: My child's exams are eight weeks away. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the right work is different from what it would have been in October. With eight weeks left the plan is whole papers under timing, strict marking against the published scheme, and the two or three technique faults that cost marks across every question. Content teaching should largely stop, because a topic learned now will not have been practised under pressure and so will not be available in the paper. Start with one diagnostic hour on three marked scripts: it produces the loss log that tells you where the recoverable marks actually are.

faqs.question: What time can a session start for a Motor City family in exam term?
faqs.answer: Earlier than in most of this part of Dubai, which is genuinely useful. A child at one of the schools inside Motor City or Dubai Sports City is often home by about half past three, making a four o'clock start realistic - and the hour before fatigue is worth considerably more than the hour after dinner for timed-paper work. Students travelling across Al Khail Road or down towards the Ranches are usually back between five and six, which is why a weekend block of ninety minutes suits them better than a late weekday hour.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to Motor City apartments or villas?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, which is how a tutor and a student mark a paper together on the same screen. In exam term there is a practical benefit: a session disrupted by an unexpected school mock can be moved within the same week rather than renegotiated around a tutor's driving route, and the tutor pool is defined by who knows the paper.

faqs.question: How many timed papers should a Year 11 student do each fortnight?
faqs.answer: In the final ten weeks, roughly two full Mathematics papers and one full paper plus one practical paper in each science per fortnight, with one reading and one writing task in English. That volume is only useful if the execution is right: one sitting, real time limit, notes closed, correct board and tier, then marked against the published scheme in a different colour with every lost mark logged by reason. Three papers is usually enough for the pattern to emerge, and the pattern is what the plan should respond to.

faqs.question: Should we add more subjects in the final term or fewer?
faqs.answer: Fewer, almost always. With eight weeks left, two subjects worked properly plus a marking routine the student runs across the rest beats four subjects half-covered and four ignored. The subjects to fund are the ones where the marked scripts show a specific, recoverable loss - a practical paper that is costing a grade, a calculator technique problem, a command-term fault. Spreading a fixed budget across every subject in the final term is the commonest way a family spends real money and sees no change in the results.

faqs.question: What should my child stop doing in the last eight weeks?
faqs.answer: Four things, and stopping them costs nothing. Stop making notes: copying is not revision and a complete set of notes with no practice history is worse than scrappy notes with a stack of marked papers. Stop learning new content, including topics the student asks for, because it will not have been practised under pressure. Stop open-book topic practice, since the unit of work is now a whole paper. And stop generous marking - mark to the scheme's wording rather than to what the answer appeared to mean.

faqs.question: Why does the entry deadline matter when the exam is months away?
faqs.answer: Because the entry carries the syllabus code and, on Cambridge subjects, the tier - so the decision that caps the available grade is taken months before the paper. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026 for examinations from 3 February to 4 March 2027. If a family wants a tier changed or a subject added, that conversation has to happen before the entry closes. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and using the wrong zone's timetable can cause a candidate to miss a paper.

faqs.question: Which schools do Motor City children attend?
faqs.answer: Many stay local: there are schools inside Motor City itself and more immediately east in Dubai Sports City, with Victory Heights Primary School alongside. Older students more often travel, across Al Khail Road to the Dubai Hills and Al Barsha South schools or south towards the Arabian Ranches cluster. Those schools choose examination boards subject by subject, so one student can sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics. Ask the examinations officer for the board, the code and the tier before buying practice material.

faqs.question: Can revision carry on through Ramadan if it falls before the exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the shape changed rather than the volume. School days shorten and the household rhythm shifts, so the productive window often moves later in the day. In exam term the sensible adjustment is shorter, more frequent sessions and timed sections rather than full papers during the day, with whole papers moved to whichever part of the day the student is actually sharp. What does not work is leaving a full schedule nominally in place and cancelling week by week, which costs the money and loses the continuity at the worst possible time.

faqs.question: When should tutoring actually stop?
faqs.answer: A week to ten days before the first paper, on a date agreed when the block began. At that point the student's own consolidation is worth more than anything a session can add, and a lesson in the final week displaces it. There is one narrow exception: a single short session aimed only at a specific technique fault, such as freezing in the first ten minutes or mismanaging the time split across sections, counts as consolidation rather than addition. Ending on a planned date after a review session is a better last experience than tapering off.

faqs.question: Is a holiday intensive course worth it before the papers?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what it contains. An intensive built around whole papers under timing, strict marking and individual loss analysis is good value, because it is concentrated practice with diagnosis. An intensive that re-covers content at a pace set by a group is usually poor value inside eight weeks, since the student's actual losses are individual and the content is already in their notes. Ask what proportion of the hours will be spent on timed papers and on marking. If the answer is less than half, it is a content course.

faqs.question: My child panics in the first ten minutes of a paper. Can that be fixed?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the fastest gains available late on, because it is procedural rather than academic. The fix is a written plan for the first five minutes: which page to read first, how long to spend scanning, which question to start with, what to do when the first question is unfamiliar. Then it is rehearsed under timing until it is automatic, which usually takes three or four papers. Students who freeze are generally not short of knowledge; they are short of a routine for the moment the paper lands.

faqs.question: How do we mark past papers at home without a tutor?
faqs.answer: Strictly, and to the scheme rather than to intent. Download the mark scheme for the exact paper, mark in a different colour, and award marks only where the scheme's wording is met - method marks only where the method is actually visible, no credit for a described answer to an explain question, units and uncertainties marked properly in the sciences. Then log every lost mark under one of four reasons: did not know it, misread, ran out of time, or wrong structure for the command term. Access papers through the school or the boards' own sites.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring between the last paper and results?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Nothing can be changed by then, and the useful work - reviewing the scripts, deciding on a resit, planning the next course - needs the results to exist first. The honest exception is a student who already knows they will be resitting a subject and wants a running start, and even there the first step is the script review once results arrive. For a Motor City household the better use of that period is often the younger sibling whose routine was suspended for a term.

faqs.question: What if the subject tutor we need is fully booked in exam season?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than matched approximately. Higher Level Mathematics and Higher Level Physics fill first, and board-specific paper-technique specialists go earlier than subject tutors generally. The options are a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online with the base and time difference stated up front, or a waiting-list place with a date attached. The time difference matters in exam term: a tutor several hours ahead cannot take a late Dubai slot, and that has to be known before the schedule is built.

dubai/motor-city.closingHeading: Count the weeks, then decide what the weeks should contain
dubai/motor-city.closingBody: Tell us the series and the date of the first paper, send three marked scripts including one that went badly, and confirm the board, code and tier from the entry form. You will get a loss log that assigns every lost mark to one of four causes, a plan phased by weeks remaining rather than by month, a named tutor who teaches that specification, the rate in AED, a fixed session count, and an end date a week to ten days before the first paper. If the scripts show the routine will do the job on its own, you will be told that too. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/mudon.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below cover the four curriculum tracks Mudon children are actually on, from Primary Years inquiry work to Higher Level Diploma subjects. Each is matched to a specification rather than to a subject label.

intro.heading: Three different Mudon households, three different requests
paragraphs: Mudon was built in phases on Al Qudra Road, and the phasing shows in its families. The original townhouse and villa clusters attracted younger households, many of whom arrived with pre-school or early-primary children and have been here long enough that those children are now in Years 5 to 8. Mudon Views added apartment stock, which draws a different profile: smaller households, more single-child families, and a higher proportion of teenagers because the move was often made for a school rather than for a garden. Then there is the constant third group, families arriving from the UK, India, Egypt, South Africa or elsewhere in the Gulf whose children have just changed school system entirely.

Those three groups generate three unrelated tutoring requests, and lumping them together is why most pages about this area are useless. The villa household with a nine-year-old wants to know whether their child's reading and number work is where it should be, because a Primary Years report card has no grades on it and gives them nothing to compare against. The apartment household with a Year 10 student wants someone who knows whether their child sits Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 and can work the right paper format. The new arrival wants to know what their child has missed by moving systems and how long it takes to close.

The third of those is the most urgent and the least served. A child moving from a CBSE Year 9 into an IGCSE Year 10 has strong procedural mathematics and little experience of extended written answers. A child moving from an American middle school into MYP 4 has done broad coverage and little depth. A child moving from a British Year 11 into Diploma Year 1 has never written an internal assessment and has no idea what a criterion is. None of those is a weak student; all of them will look weak on a first assessment, and the remedy is specific rather than general.

The fourth group worth naming is the one nobody plans for: the family whose child is doing well and whose Arabic grade is quietly failing. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed for, and they appear on the report card alongside Chemistry. Families focused on the examined subjects often discover the Arabic position late, when it is harder to fix.

IB Gram is a matching platform rather than a school or a centre. There is no IB Gram building in Dubai, and for UAE families every lesson is delivered one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India. What that means in Mudon is that the available pool is every specialist who teaches your child's actual specification, rather than the few who are willing to drive out past Arabian Ranches on a weekday evening.

dubai/mudon.programmesIntro: Mudon children are spread across four routes, and the parent question differs at each stage. These notes describe what each programme assesses and what it tends to ask of a family in this community.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry, no external examinations, and reporting written in descriptive rather than numerical terms, concluding with the Year 6 Exhibition. The programme develops research and communication early, which is a real strength later. Its weakness for parents is legibility: a report that says a child is a confident inquirer does not say whether they can read fluently or recall number bonds.
programmes.countryNote: This is the largest group in the villa phases of Mudon, and the most common enquiry is diagnostic rather than remedial. Parents want to know where their child sits against an external benchmark. The useful answer is short: check reading fluency aloud, check number fact recall under light time pressure, and check written stamina on a single extended piece. Two short sessions a week is the right dose at this stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0 to 8, converted to a 1 to 7 grade, with the optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 the only external component. The criteria reward inquiry, process and reflection as heavily as correctness, which rewards some students and disorients others.
programmes.countryNote: Mudon families reach the MYP mainly through Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City and Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park. The recurring decision is what happens at 14: continue to the Diploma or move to a British school for IGCSE. Families here weigh bus distance, sibling placement and the child's tolerance for extended independent research, which is the real difference between the two routes.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11 across short, structured papers with published mark schemes. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, and the Core tier caps the achievable grade at C. Pearson uses its own codes and paper structures for the same subjects, which is why the code matters more than the subject name.
programmes.countryNote: The apartment phases of Mudon skew towards this route, served by British-curriculum schools in Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Jumeirah Park and Al Barsha South. The practical risk here is tier placement set in Year 10 on Year 9 evidence. A Core-tier cap limits later options and interacts with the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency file, which counts five accredited subjects at grade E or grade 3 and above.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, scored out of 45 including three bonus points. Each subject carries an internal assessment written across months and worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade, which is the part of the course a school timetable cannot supervise closely.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Mudon travel to Greenfield International School, Fairgreen International School or Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches. A meaningful minority arrive in Diploma Year 1 from a British IGCSE background, and that group needs its first term on research method, criterion language and the habit of long-horizon work rather than on subject content they already have.

dubai/mudon.subjectsIntro: Requests from Mudon split along the lines described above: diagnostic primary work, IGCSE paper technique, and Diploma subjects where the internal assessment is the problem. The subject notes reflect that mix.

subjects.name: Primary English: reading and writing
subjects.description: The two checkable things are reading fluency aloud and written stamina across a single extended piece. A child who decodes accurately but slowly will struggle with every subsequent subject, and the fix is high-volume reading at the right level rather than comprehension worksheets.

subjects.name: Primary Mathematics: number fluency
subjects.description: Number bond and times-table recall under light time pressure predicts later algebra more reliably than any topic test. Children who calculate correctly but slowly run out of working memory on multi-step problems, which looks like a reasoning problem and is not.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion C and D work, investigating patterns and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, is where marks are lost by students who can compute perfectly. The skill is justifying a general rule and communicating a method, and it transfers directly into Diploma internal assessment work.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: The criteria reward inquiry design and reflection on method, not only correct results. Lab write-ups that describe what happened without evaluating the method cap in the middle bands, and this is the single most fixable thing at this stage.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The last third of each paper combines two topics, typically geometry inside algebra or algebra inside a problem-solving shell. Students abandon those questions rather than collecting the method marks available for a correct first line, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic, qualitative analysis results and electrolysis products are the reliable mark-losers. The qualitative tests are pure recall and can be drilled to automaticity in a handful of sessions, which is unusually good value early in Year 11.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Genetic crosses, transport in plants and homeostasis account for most lost marks. Crosses are procedural and highly scorable once the layout is fixed, and students lose marks mainly by omitting gamete rows or not stating the ratio the question asked for.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper do the damage. Circuit questions need the diagram read properly before any calculation starts, and the practical paper requires named apparatus and method held in memory.

subjects.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Many Mudon households are multilingual, and this is frequently the right entry rather than first language English. Marks turn on following the task instruction exactly, particularly in the directed writing question, where register and audience are explicitly assessed.

subjects.name: Diploma Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms dominate lost marks, and the internal assessment is where grades are quietly made. A well-chosen research question with a measurable variable is worth more than any amount of laboratory polish applied to a vague one.

subjects.name: Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 without a calculator exposes algebraic weakness that a graphing display had been covering. HL adds proof by induction and complex numbers. Most marks go missing on unjustified steps rather than on wrong answers, which makes marking the student's own script essential.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: KHDA mandatory stream, all year groups
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school alongside the licensed curriculum, and taught in separate classes for non-Arabs under KHDA rules. Support here means working through the school's own material, since additional or different content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

sections.heading: Who lives in Mudon, and why the request differs by phase
paragraphs: A search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Mudon comes from at least three different kinds of household, and the useful page separates them. The townhouse and villa phases hold longer-settled families whose children have moved up through a single school and are now somewhere between Years 5 and 9. The Mudon Views apartments hold smaller households with a higher proportion of teenagers, often because the move was made for school access rather than for space. And there is a steady stream of new arrivals whose children have changed curriculum within the last year.

The villa request is usually diagnostic. A Primary Years report card carries no grades, so a parent who wants to know whether their eight-year-old reads at the right rate cannot find out from the school's reporting. What they need is one hour of measurement against an external benchmark, not a term of weekly lessons. Providers who sell the term instead of the hour are answering a question that was not asked.

The apartment request is usually technical. A Year 10 or Year 11 student has a board, a syllabus code and possibly a tier, and the entire value of a tutor depends on matching those exactly. A family who books IGCSE Maths help without establishing whether the child sits Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher can spend a term practising the wrong paper structure while feeling productive.

The new-arrival request is the hardest and the most rewarding. It needs a gap audit before any teaching, because the gap is specific to the pair of systems involved and is rarely what the parent assumes. The table sets out the three household types against what they actually need.

sections.heading: Four curriculum tracks inside one community
paragraphs: Dubai licenses seventeen different curricula and 227 private schools served 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. Mudon reflects that spread in miniature. Two children in neighbouring houses can be in the same year group and sitting entirely different assessments, which is why generic year-group advice is worthless here.

The British track runs IGCSE at sixteen and then splits into A Level or the Diploma. It is the dominant route in this part of Dubailand because the schools the community's buses serve are mostly British-curriculum. The assessment is examination-heavy, the papers are patterned, and the single highest-return activity is timed past-paper practice with honest marking.

The IB continuum track runs Primary Years, Middle Years and then the Diploma without a change of system. It is available locally through Fairgreen International School and Greenfield International School. The assessment is criterion-referenced throughout and the Diploma hands a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade to independent research, which is a different skill from examination technique and needs teaching as one.

The Indian and American tracks sit alongside both, and families move between all four more often than school marketing admits. A child leaving CBSE Year 9 for IGCSE Year 10 brings strong procedure and little extended writing. A child leaving an American middle school for MYP 4 brings breadth and little depth. sections.heading: Primary in Mudon: what to check when the report has no grades
paragraphs: The most common first enquiry from the villa phases concerns a child between Years 2 and 6 whose report is positive, descriptive and completely uninformative about standard. This is not a failure of the school; inquiry-based primary reporting is designed to describe learning rather than rank it. But it leaves a parent with no way to answer the question they actually have, which is whether their child is where they should be.

Three things are worth checking, and all three are measurable in under an hour. Reading fluency, assessed by having the child read aloud from unfamiliar text at the appropriate level while someone times and notes errors. Number fact recall, assessed under light time pressure rather than untimed, because a child who computes correctly but slowly exhausts their working memory on multi-step problems. Written stamina, assessed on one extended piece rather than on short exercises, because stamina is the thing that collapses first in later years.

What parents usually fear is comprehension, and comprehension is usually fine. A child who decodes slowly appears to have a comprehension problem because the decoding consumes all the capacity. Fixing the fluency fixes the apparent comprehension, and the fix is volume of reading at the right level rather than worksheets about inference. This is one of the few places in tutoring where the honest advice reduces the amount of tutoring needed.

Dose matters at this age and almost every provider gets it wrong. Two sessions of twenty-five to forty-five minutes a week, placed before dinner rather than after, with one focus per session, is the pattern that works for a child off a Dubailand bus. Ninety minutes on a weekday evening does not work at nine years old regardless of how convenient it is for the adults.
bullets: Reading fluency, timed, aloud, from unfamiliar text
Number fact recall under light time pressure, not untimed

sections.heading: The decision at fourteen: continue the continuum or switch to IGCSE
paragraphs: Mudon families with a child in MYP 3 face a real decision, and the school's own advice is understandably partial. The choice is between continuing in the IB continuum to the Diploma, or moving to a British-curriculum school for IGCSE and then A Level or the Diploma elsewhere. Both are reasonable; they suit different children, and the deciding factor is rarely academic ability.

The continuum suits a student who tolerates long-horizon independent work. The Diploma's internal assessments are multi-month research tasks, the Extended Essay runs across two terms, and nothing about the structure rescues a student who cannot start something in October that is due in February. A child who has thrived on MYP criteria, who plans without being chased and who reads widely, is well placed.

The IGCSE route suits a student who performs better against frequent, short, closed assessments. Papers are patterned, mark schemes are public, and effort converts into marks fairly directly. For a student who works hard but needs structure imposed from outside, two years of IGCSE provides more scaffolding than two years of Middle Years criteria, and the examination habit transfers well into A Level.

The logistics then have their own weight. Moving school at fourteen means a new bus route, a new peer group and possibly a different corridor out of Mudon altogether. Sibling placement matters, because two schools means two runs. And a family planning a return to the UK or an application to a UK university should check how each route is read by their target institutions rather than assuming parity.

sections.heading: What a year of tutoring costs in this market, put in context
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search quote no price, and two of the larger ones quote in US dollars. The figures below are market rates in AED, taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026. They describe the market, not an IB Gram price list, and they are presented as an annual cost because that is the decision a parent is actually making.

The per-hour bands are consistent across providers. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to AED 500. Budget platforms advertise from AED 33 to AED 65, which generally buys a university student working from a textbook. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Context makes those numbers legible. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are therefore the fixed part of the education bill this year and tutoring is the variable part, which is an argument for deciding the tutoring budget deliberately rather than by accumulation.

The table models the realistic annual shapes. The point of it is that two sessions a week for a full year and a diagnostic hour plus an exam-run intensive differ by an order of magnitude, and the cheaper option is frequently the better one for a student whose problem is technique rather than content.

sections.heading: The equivalency file your child will need at eighteen
paragraphs: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency is the process that converts a school-leaving certificate into something a UAE university or employer will accept. It is a bureaucratic step, not an academic one, but the requirements reach backwards into subject choices made at fourteen. Almost none of the pages competing for this search mention it at all, and one of the ranking ones states the subject count incorrectly.

For the British track the sourced requirements are specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which means a student counting them towards the total is a subject short.

For the American track the requirements are different in kind. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. These are thresholds rather than subject counts, and they are checkable well in advance.

For the Diploma there is no figure worth publishing here. The sourced article that sets out the British and American requirements states no IB points threshold, so any IB equivalency number on a tutoring page is unsourced. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and tutoring is not required for it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty for parents who are new to the IB
paragraphs: A large share of Mudon families are in their first year of an IB programme, and the honesty rules are unfamiliar in a specific way. In many systems a parent helping with homework, or a tutor tightening a paragraph, is normal and harmless. In the Diploma and the Middle Years Programme, the internal assessments are formally assessed work and the student signs a declaration that the submission is their own. The rules are therefore not etiquette; they have consequences.

The permitted territory is wide. A tutor may teach research method, narrow a research question until it can be answered in the available word count, explain what each criterion is asking for in the criterion's own language, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is underserved, teach the statistics or referencing the task requires, and ask questions that make a student notice a flaw in their own argument. That is teaching, and a school coordinator expects to see it happening.

The prohibited territory is narrow and absolute. A tutor does not supply sentences for inclusion. Does not rewrite a draft. Does not provide data the student did not gather. Does not produce any part of a submitted document. The distinction is clean: feedback names the problem and leaves the solving to the student, while authorship solves it for them. One provider in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright, and a family buying one is buying an expulsion risk for their own child.

There is a materials rule too. Boards hold copyright in syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables. Those should be referenced and linked, not redistributed as downloads. A provider circulating board PDFs is creating a copyright problem, and for unreleased material a malpractice exposure as well.
bullets: The student signs the authenticity declaration and carries the consequence

Not permitted: supplied text, rewriting, supplied data, any part of the submission
Board materials get referenced and linked, never redistributed

sections.heading: Coverage, availability and the legal position on tutoring
paragraphs: Every provider has limits and almost none publish them. The honest position for Mudon is that common subjects at common levels are matched quickly and narrow combinations are not. IGCSE Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English and primary literacy and numeracy are deep pools. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics, Higher Level Psychology, Business Management, Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and second languages at Higher Level are thin pools everywhere, not only in Dubai.

Online delivery is what makes the thin pools workable at all. Because lessons run over live video rather than at an address, a Mudon family requesting Higher Level Chemistry is choosing among specialists who teach that specification, instead of among the few people prepared to drive out past Arabian Ranches on a Tuesday evening. When a specialist genuinely is not free for a requested slot, the useful answer is a different time with the right tutor, a short diagnostic block with a related-subject specialist, or a wait with a stated date.

On legality, the position is clear and worth knowing. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Those providing private tuition without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted to you is unverified. A separate and larger requirement, the KHDA Educational Services Permit, applies to tutoring operations with premises and staff in Dubai. IB Gram has no Dubai premises and holds no such permit; it matches tutors who then teach online.

process.title: Say which household you are
process.description: A primary benchmarking request, an IGCSE board-and-tier request and a curriculum-transition request need different first sessions. Tell us the year group, the school, the board and code if you have one, and whether your child has changed system in the last two years. That last question is the one that changes the plan most often.

process.title: Measure before teaching
process.description: The first session is diagnostic. For primary that means reading fluency, number fact recall and written stamina. For IGCSE and Diploma it means a marked unseen paper or school assessment against the official criteria. The report back is a plain statement of what was found, not a sales conversation.

process.title: Fix the dose to the age
process.description: Two sessions of twenty-five to forty-five minutes a week for primary, one or two sixty-minute sessions for IGCSE, and a ninety-minute block plus a weekend session for Diploma students. Sessions sit before dinner for younger children and after it for older ones, in Gulf Standard Time, in the same slot each week.

process.title: Build the plan backwards, including the Arabic slot
process.description: The term map runs backwards from the entry deadline and examination window, with the school's own assessment dates, the UAE breaks and Ramadan placed on it. Where the mandatory UAE subjects are a live problem, a slot for them goes on the map at the start rather than being added in a panic in May.

process.title: Review against marks, and stop when it is done
process.description: Every six to eight weeks the question is whether marks on comparable tasks have moved. Transition blocks and intensives have a defined endpoint and end there. A free trial session is available before any commitment, with the length and conditions stated at booking.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a specification, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 assess the same chemistry through different papers, and Cambridge Core caps the grade at C. The board, the code and the tier are confirmed before a tutor is assigned, because practising the wrong format feels like progress and is not.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson runs one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. For Mudon this widens the specialist pool rather than narrowing it.

whyPoints.title: The right dose for the age
whyPoints.description: Short, frequent sessions for primary children and longer blocks for Diploma students. Ninety minutes on a weekday evening does not work at nine years old however convenient it is to book, and we will say so rather than sell it.

whyPoints.title: Transition work with an endpoint
whyPoints.description: A child who has just changed curriculum needs a gap audit and six to ten targeted sessions, not an open-ended arrangement. Blocks of work are quoted with a finishing point and they finish there.

whyPoints.title: Figures in AED, attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Every market rate on this page names the provider publishing it and the month it was read. The annual cost table exists because the decision a parent makes is a yearly one, not an hourly one, and nobody else in this market models it.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency and honesty explained, not performed
whyPoints.description: The MoE equivalency requirements are set out with their source and a pointer to the official channel. We do not perform, guarantee or accelerate equivalency, and we do not supply any part of assessed work. Both of those are stated because the omissions elsewhere are the problem.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Mudon children attend?
faqs.answer: Mudon children split across two groups of schools. The British-curriculum destinations include GEMS Metropole School in Motor City, Victory Heights Primary School in Dubai Sports City, Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, Safa Community School, Dubai Heights Academy and South View School. The IB continuum options within reach are Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park and Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches. These names are local context only, to help you identify which board your child is actually on. IB Gram has no relationship with any school listed.

faqs.question: My child's primary report has no grades. How do I tell whether they are behind?
faqs.answer: Check three things, all measurable in under an hour. Reading fluency, by having them read aloud from unfamiliar text at the right level while someone times and notes errors. Number fact recall, under light time pressure rather than untimed. Written stamina, on one extended piece rather than short exercises. Parents usually worry about comprehension, and comprehension is usually fine: a child who decodes slowly uses all their capacity on decoding, which looks like a comprehension problem. Fixing fluency fixes the apparent comprehension, and the fix is reading volume rather than inference worksheets.

faqs.question: How long should a tutoring session be for a child in Year 3 or Year 4?
faqs.answer: Twenty-five to forty-five minutes, twice a week, placed before dinner. A child coming off a Dubailand bus has a short productive window that closes early, and ninety minutes on a weekday evening does not work at that age regardless of how convenient it is to schedule. One focus per session also matters: reading, or number, or writing, not all three. Providers who sell long sessions to young children are optimising for their own invoicing rather than for the child's attention span, and the difference is visible within a fortnight.

faqs.question: We have just moved to Mudon from another school system. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a gap audit rather than with lessons. The gap depends on which pair of systems is involved and is rarely what parents expect. A child leaving CBSE Year 9 for IGCSE Year 10 usually has strong procedural mathematics and little practice at extended written answers. A child leaving an American middle school for MYP 4 has breadth and needs depth. A child arriving in Diploma Year 1 from British IGCSEs has examination technique but has never written an internal assessment. Two sessions of auditing, then six to ten targeted ones, with a defined endpoint.

faqs.question: Should our child continue the IB continuum or move to IGCSE at fourteen?
faqs.answer: It depends on the child, not on the quality of either route. The continuum suits a student who tolerates long-horizon independent work, because Diploma internal assessments run for months and the Extended Essay spans two terms. The IGCSE route suits a student who performs better against frequent, short, patterned, closed assessments where effort converts into marks fairly directly. Then weigh the logistics: a school move at fourteen means a new bus route and possibly a second school run if there are siblings. Check how each route is read by the universities your family is actually targeting.

faqs.question: Does my child's Arabic grade matter if they are on a British or IB curriculum?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it surprises families every year. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA mandates separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Support means working through the school's own material, because additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: What does a full year of tutoring actually cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the pattern. Using Dubai market rates read in October 2026, a single diagnostic hour with a specialist is AED 200 to 450. One weekly session on one subject across a school year is roughly AED 6,800 to 15,300. Two weekly sessions in an exam year across two subjects reaches AED 13,600 to 30,600. A transition block of eight sessions is AED 1,600 to 3,600, and an eight-week exam-run intensive around AED 4,000 to 9,000. Those are market figures from published provider pages and Bestimate's 2026 table, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees rising this year, and how does that affect a tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That makes school fees the fixed part of this year's education bill and tutoring the variable part. The practical implication is to decide the tutoring budget deliberately, as an annual figure attached to a specific plan, rather than letting it accumulate session by session across a year.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require for equivalency on the British track?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is a regulatory process; no tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or speeds it up.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points threshold for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not one that can responsibly be published here. The sourced guidance that sets out the British and American track requirements states no IB points figure, which means any number you see on a tutoring page is unsourced. Check it directly on moe.gov.ae or with your school's university counsellor, who deals with the attestation process every year. Be wary of any provider that quotes a specific IB equivalency score without naming its source, because the same providers tend to be wrong about the IGCSE subject count as well.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Middle Years Personal Project or a Diploma internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes, and the limits are worth understanding before you start. A tutor may teach goal setting, research method and reflective writing, narrow a research question, explain each criterion in its own language, and give criterion-referenced feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a draft, provide data your child did not gather, or produce any part of the submission. Your child signs the authenticity declaration. A provider selling a finished assessment is selling your child an expulsion risk, whatever it is called.

faqs.question: Which Mudon requests are hardest to fill?
faqs.answer: Thin-pool Higher Level subjects: Physics, Economics, Psychology, Business Management, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and second languages at Higher Level. Those pools are small everywhere, not only in Dubai. IGCSE Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English and primary literacy and numeracy fill quickly. When a specialist is not free for a requested slot we say so and give the options: a different time with the right tutor, a short diagnostic block with a related-subject specialist, or a wait with a stated date. We do not substitute a generalist quietly.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a licence to teach my child in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, so nobody should tell you it carries a fee. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat quoted amounts as unverified.

faqs.question: How will we know whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By comparing marks on comparable tasks every six to eight weeks, not by asking whether the sessions feel useful. A narrow procedural weakness such as mole arithmetic or genetic-cross layout should move visibly within a month. Retrieval speed under time takes six to eight weeks of timed practice. Essay technique moves slowest, because the limiting factor is often unread text rather than unlearned skill. If marks have not moved on comparable work after two review points, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan or the tutor changes rather than continuing.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in the same Mudon household?
faqs.answer: Often, when the children are close in level and on the same board. Two IGCSE siblings a year apart can usually share a tutor working one plan with two branches, which also means one relationship for the parent to manage. Across a primary child and a Diploma student it does not work, because the skills and the assessment demands have almost nothing in common. Either way the sessions should be staggered rather than run in parallel, and each child needs a quiet space rather than a shared table.

dubai/mudon.closingHeading: Tell us which Mudon family you are
dubai/mudon.closingBody: The right first step depends on whether you need a benchmark, a board match or a transition audit. Send the year group, the school, the board and syllabus code if you have one, and whether your child has changed school system in the last two years. We will match a specialist who teaches that exact specification and run a diagnostic session over live video at a time that suits the age of the child. If the subject you need is one of the thin-pool Higher Level ones and nobody is free for your slot, we will tell you that and give you the alternatives.

dubai/muhaisnah.tutorsIntro: Tutors cover Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE and the IB Diploma at both levels. The match is made against the component a student is losing marks on, because the difference between a cheap hour and an expensive one is almost entirely what the tutor can diagnose rather than what they can explain.

intro.heading: Price first, because that is the real question
paragraphs: Three of the six strongest pages competing for tutoring searches in this city publish no price at all. One of them has a frequently asked question that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. The two that do give figures quote US dollars, which is not what a family in Muhaisnah pays rent in. That silence is not an accident: a page with no number cannot be compared with anything, which suits the seller and nobody else.

So this page starts with the money. Published market rates in Dubai run from around AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 at the named-examiner end, and the spread is explained almost entirely by two things: the format, and what the tutor can diagnose. Subject matters less than parents expect. Neighbourhood matters almost not at all, except that in-home rates rise with the drive.

Muhaisnah is a district where this matters more than in most. It runs from the villa and townhouse plots of Muhaisnah 2 through apartment blocks to the labour accommodation of Muhaisnah 4, and the household incomes along that stretch are not comparable. A page that quotes one rate as though it suits everyone is useless here. What a family needs is the whole ladder, an honest statement of what each rung buys, and a sensible order to spend in.

The order is the part nobody publishes. Given a fixed monthly figure, some purchases move a grade and some do not. A full marked past paper with a specialist walking through every lost mark changes a student's technique permanently and costs one or two hours. A term of general subject teaching for a student whose knowledge is already adequate changes almost nothing and costs twenty. Spending badly is more common in this market than spending too little.

There is also a legal question that the price conversation hides. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit, it is free, and it takes two working days to obtain. A tutor at the bottom of the rate ladder who has not bothered to get something that costs nothing has told you something useful about how carefully they work. The permit table further down sets out which categories of person may hold one and how a parent can check.

Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; the in-home service runs only in India. For a budget-conscious household that removes the single largest avoidable cost in this market, because the published in-home premium is substantially travel through the slowest hours of the Dubai afternoon. It also widens the pool, so a family paying a mid-market rate can still reach a tutor who has marked the paper their child sits, rather than choosing from whoever is willing to drive out to Muhaisnah at six in the evening.
