dubai/muhaisnah.programmesIntro: Three routes cover almost every student in this district, and each one has a different cost profile across the two years. The notes below give the spending shape rather than restating the programme.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects over two years, examined in terminal papers with practical or alternative-to-practical components in the sciences. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, and a Core entry caps the grade at C or 5. Pearson International GCSE runs single-tier papers in most subjects.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest effective IGCSE support is front-loaded and narrow: one subject, one weekly hour from the start of Year 10, stopped once the subject is stable. The most expensive pattern is the one most families end up with, which is three subjects bought in the February of Year 11 at crisis rates, when only technique is still movable.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment the student designs outside lesson time, plus the 4,000-word Extended Essay, the 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay and CAS, inside a total of 45 points.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma spending is cheapest when it is spent on scoping rather than rescue. Two sessions in the autumn of DP1 that test whether an internal assessment question can actually be answered cost a fraction of the block needed in the spring when the question has failed. This is the single clearest example of order mattering more than rate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and reported from 1 to 7. The programme rewards investigation and reflection and does not drill procedure, so fluency gaps can sit underneath respectable grades for years.
programmes.countryNote: For a household watching every dirham, MYP is usually the wrong place to spend. Criterion grades are not predictive of timed-paper performance, and a weak MYP report rarely justifies paid support on its own. One timed diagnostic will tell you whether there is a real fluency problem, and that is often the whole purchase.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth, examined in a June or November series, with little coursework in the sciences beyond a practical component. Fewer subjects means fewer places to spend, and a sharper consequence when one of them goes wrong.
programmes.countryNote: With only three or four subjects, a single weak one has a disproportionate effect on a university offer, which changes the spending logic. Concentrating a limited budget on the subject carrying the offer condition is almost always better than spreading it, and that is a decision best taken with the offer letter in front of you.

dubai/muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: The list below is ordered by how often families here ask, with a note on where the marks actually go, because that is what decides whether a cheap hour or an expensive one is the right purchase.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most requested subject at every price point. The highest-value cheap purchase in the whole market is a tier review in Year 10, because Core caps the grade at C or 5 while Extended reaches 9, and a mistimed entry decision cannot be undone close to the series.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, proof and notation discipline carry the grade, and marks go on unjustified steps. The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria with the largest allocation on use of mathematics, so scoping it properly early is cheaper than rescuing it late.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves dominate IGCSE losses; fields and thermodynamics at Diploma level. Method detail on the practical paper is the kind of thing a specialist fixes in two sessions and a generalist never notices, which is where the rate difference earns itself.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and qualitative analysis at IGCSE; energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms at HL. Observation answers need colour and state together. Unit and significant-figure errors cost about a mark a paper and are the cheapest thing on this list to repair.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A large content base rather than a difficult one, so frequency beats length and a shorter cheaper session can genuinely work. Command terms decide the marks: outline wants a list, explain wants a causal chain, and the fix is drilling rather than teaching.

subjects.name: English First Language and English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The best value on the whole list for a tight budget. Summary questions are mark-dense and routinely thrown away, and directed writing rewards register. Four marked sessions usually move both, after which the student can self-correct.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study marks go to candidates who use the figures inside their argument. At Diploma level, Economics needs three commentaries of 800 words built on news articles, and the article choice sets the ceiling, which makes early scoping the cheap intervention.

subjects.name: Accounting
subjects.description: Offered at several schools serving this part of Dubai. Marks go to layout discipline and consistent treatment rather than arithmetic, which makes it unusually responsive to short, cheap, repetitive practice with feedback.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode precision and system fundamentals carry the written papers. The solution development component needs a genuine client and documented consultation, and it is one of the thinnest components to staff, so it is rarely available at the cheap end at all.

dubai/muhaisnah.regionsIntro: These notes cover what each part of this area contributes to the school and tutoring picture, including the parts a brochure would leave out.

regions.note: Villa and townhouse plots, including the Lulu Village area, with settled family households and the most consistent demand for exam-year support in the district. Students here generally have a workable study space and can hold an early evening slot.

sections.heading: What a tutor costs in this market, with every figure attributed
paragraphs: Direct answer: market rates in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 at the premium named end, with a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those are market figures from the providers named in the table, not an IB Gram price list, and they were read from published pages rather than estimated.

The table matters more than the sentence, because the useful question is not what the market charges but what each band buys. At the bottom rung a tutor supervises homework and revises content from a textbook. That is a legitimate purchase for a Year 8 student who has stopped working, and a poor one for a Year 11 student losing marks to command terms. At the specialist rung a tutor reads a marked script and names the three repeated errors inside twenty minutes, which is a different service wearing the same word.

Format shifts the number more than seniority does at the lower end. Published in-home bands run from AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a comparable tutor online, and the difference is predominantly travel. A family in Muhaisnah paying the in-home premium for a tutor driving from Barsha or Mirdif through the late afternoon is paying for a car journey, and for the risk that the journey fails.

Monthly shapes are published too, and they are how a household should actually budget. Around AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions in this market. Four two-hour in-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Measure any quote, including ours, against those bands.

sections.heading: The order to spend in, which nobody publishes
paragraphs: Given a fixed monthly figure, the sequence of purchases matters more than the rate negotiated on any one of them. This is the part of the market with no published guidance at all, and it is where most money is wasted. The table below ranks interventions by what they move per dirham, based on what the mark scheme actually rewards rather than on what is easy to sell.

At the top of the ranking sits the cheapest thing on the list: a tier or entry review. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C or 5, and a student placed in Core in Year 10 after a weak start and never reviewed carries that ceiling into the final series however much they improve. One conversation with the department, prompted by one session of evidence, can be worth more than a term of teaching, and the deadline for changing an entry sits months before the paper.

Next is marked-script analysis, because it is diagnostic and cheap. Most students who are losing marks are not losing knowledge marks. They are losing command-term marks, precision marks and pacing marks, and all three are visible on one paper to someone who knows the scheme. Two sessions here routinely redirect a family away from a purchase they were about to make for the wrong reason.

At the bottom of the ranking sits the thing most often bought first: a long-running general subject arrangement with no defined endpoint, for a student whose content knowledge was never the problem. It is comfortable, it feels responsible, and it changes very little. A household in this district should buy it last if at all, and should expect any honest tutor to say so.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This question sits underneath every cheap quote in this market and almost nobody asks it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists a two-working-day completion time with the application made through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than parents assume. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. So a university student charging AED 60 an hour can be entirely lawful. The question is not whether their category is allowed but whether they actually hold the permit, and since it is free, failure to hold one is a choice rather than a cost.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which is why any page quoting a figure is guessing; a number circulating in this market could not be verified against a ministry source and is left out here deliberately. What is verifiable is the obligation.

A separate rule applies to anyone with premises. A tutoring operation with a centre and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a licence for premises, and nothing else. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and claims none, which is the correct position for an online matching service and one that several pages in this market obscure.

sections.heading: Group class, tuition centre, or one-to-one
paragraphs: For a household with a ceiling, this is the live decision and the answer depends on what is wrong rather than on what is cheapest per hour. A group class is genuinely good value when every student in the room is preparing for the same paper and the content is being revised rather than repaired. It is poor value the moment a student's problem is specific, because the pace belongs to the group and a specific gap cannot be addressed without holding everyone else up.

A tuition centre adds structure, which for some students is the actual product. A fixed time, a fixed place, other students working, and a parent who does not have to enforce anything. If a child's problem is that homework does not happen, that structure may be worth more than a better-matched tutor. It also adds a second journey to the day, which in this corridor is not free in time even when it is modest in money.

One-to-one costs most per hour and the least per unit of progress when the problem is diagnosable. The reason is simple: every minute is spent on this student's errors. Where a student is losing eight marks a paper to command terms, a specialist can fix that in a handful of sessions and nothing in a group class will touch it, because the class is not about that student.

The honest summary for Muhaisnah is a sequence rather than a choice. Start with two one-to-one diagnostic sessions to find out what is wrong. If the answer is broad content revision for a whole paper, a group class or a centre may serve well and cost less. If the answer is a specific recurring error or a coursework problem, the group option will not reach it at any price.

sections.heading: The extras that turn a quoted rate into a bigger number
paragraphs: A quoted hourly rate is not a price. Parents in this market are routinely surprised by four things after the first invoice, and all four are answerable before any money moves. Asking about them is not rude; a provider who will not answer them in writing has given you your answer.

The first is the unit. A rate quoted per hour and a rate quoted per lesson are different numbers if the lesson runs seventy-five or ninety minutes, and that distinction is frequently left vague. The second is minimum commitment: some providers quote per hour and then require a block of ten, which turns a trial into a purchase. The third is cancellation, specifically how much notice is needed and what happens when the school moves an event at two days' notice, which in Dubai it will.

The fourth is tax. Whether a quoted figure includes VAT should be stated on the quote. This page does not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and we are not publishing one. What a family can and should do is ask any provider whether the number they were given is inclusive, and ask for the answer in writing alongside a tax registration number if one is claimed.

There is a fifth item specific to materials. Nobody should be selling you syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to the examination boards and should be referenced and linked rather than supplied, and a provider offering a bundle of them is offering something they are not entitled to distribute. Official timetables and specifications are published free by Cambridge and Pearson, and that is where they should come from.
bullets: Ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, and how long the lesson is
Ask about minimum commitment before agreeing to a trial
Ask what happens when a school event moves a session at short notice
Ask in writing whether the quoted figure includes tax

sections.heading: How many sessions does a grade actually take?
paragraphs: No honest answer to this is a single number, and any provider offering one is guessing. What can be said is which kinds of problem are short and which are long, and that distinction is far more useful to a family with a ceiling than an average would be.

Technique problems are short. A student who knows the material and loses marks to command terms, precision or pacing is usually a four-to-six-session job, and the change tends to be visible on the next school assessment because nothing new had to be learned. This is the best value in the market and it is the purchase families are least likely to make unprompted, because it does not feel like enough.

Content gaps are medium. A fortnight missed, a topic taught badly, a module that never landed: these are defined blocks of specification, and a specialist can establish exactly which points are missing from the scheme of work and close them in two or three sessions each. The cost is predictable because the scope is.

Structural problems are long and sometimes are not tutoring problems at all. A student two years behind in algebraic fluency will not be fixed in a term, and a student who is not doing any independent work will not be fixed by adding an hour of supervised work. In the second case the honest recommendation is often a conversation with the school rather than a purchase, and a tutor who will not say that is not worth the rate.
bullets: Technique: four to six sessions, visible on the next school assessment
Content gap: two to three sessions per defined block of specification
Fluency rebuild: a term or more, and worth planning rather than buying monthly
Motivation or workload: often a school conversation, not a paid hour

sections.heading: Who lives in Muhaisnah, and how that shapes school choice
paragraphs: Muhaisnah covers a wide span. Muhaisnah 1 and 2 hold villa and townhouse plots with settled family households, including the Lulu Village area. Muhaisnah 3 is apartment-dominated with larger households. Muhaisnah 4 is predominantly labour accommodation rather than family housing. Treating this as one market would be misleading, and the schools families use reflect the span rather than a single catchment.

The nearest schools sit west in Al Qusais and north-east in Al Nahda, running British and Indian curricula with IGCSE at sixteen in the British stream. South along the main corridor, Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City hold British and IB provision at higher fee levels. South-east, Mirdif and Al Warqa add IB continuum options. A family's school choice here is usually a fee decision before it is a curriculum decision, and that has consequences for what is left over for tutoring.

Dubai's market context is worth knowing when weighing those choices. The emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the IB at 7. For 2026-27 KHDA confirmed no increase in private school fees, and seven new schools are opening, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

For a household that has stretched to pay fees at a Mirdif or Silicon Oasis school, the most useful thing this page can offer is permission to spend small and deliberately on tutoring rather than feeling obliged to match the school's price level. Two diagnostic sessions and a six-session technique block is a serious intervention. It is also a fraction of a term of open-ended support, and for most students it does more.

sections.heading: What the cheap end can do, and what it cannot
paragraphs: A low rate is not automatically poor value, and saying so is more honest than the usual pitch. At AED 45 to 150 an hour this market offers homework supervision, textbook revision and worked question practice, often from a capable university student. For a Year 8 or Year 9 student who has simply stopped doing the work, that is sufficient and buying more would be waste.

What the cheap end reliably cannot do is diagnose. Reading a marked script and identifying that a student is losing eight marks a paper because 'explain' is being answered as 'describe' requires knowing the mark scheme from the marking side. Judging whether an internal assessment research question will survive contact with a school laboratory requires having seen several fail. Those are the two services the specialist band is actually selling, and the gap between the bands is almost entirely this.

There is also a boundary question that becomes sharper at the cheap end, because the pressure to be helpful is higher. Anyone offering to produce coursework, to supply a finished internal assessment or to redraft an Extended Essay to completion is offering academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student: a withdrawn grade, potentially a withdrawn diploma, a problem on a university application. Operators in this market sell completed internal assessments at four-figure dirham prices. A parent should treat any offer in that direction as disqualifying regardless of price.

The practical rule is to match the rung to the problem. Supervision and revision at the bottom. Content teaching in the middle. Diagnosis, technique and coursework scoping at the top, bought in small quantities. A household that does this spends less and gets more than one that picks a rate and hopes it covers everything.
bullets: The cheap end genuinely covers supervision and content revision
Diagnosis and mark-scheme technique are what the specialist band sells

sections.heading: Starting small, and what we will tell you
paragraphs: The first purchase we would recommend to most households here is two sessions, not a term. Send the subject, the level, the board from the statement of entry and a marked script. The first session reads the script and the second tests whether the diagnosis holds. At the end you get a written statement of what is wrong and an estimate of how many sessions it takes, and a reasonable proportion of families stop there because the answer was narrower than they feared.

If the honest answer is that tutoring is not the right purchase, that is what should be said. A student not doing any independent work needs a different intervention, and an hour of paid supervision each week is an expensive way to postpone that conversation. We would rather lose the sale than take a monthly payment from a household in this district for something we do not think will work.

On availability, the limits are real. Evening hours between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf time are the most requested across the whole network and they run out in mock season. Computer Science solution development, Further Mathematics and Arabic as a first language at Diploma level are thin, and for those we give a dated alternative rather than a reassurance. No competing page in this market acknowledges a coverage limit at all, which is informative.

On price, our own figure depends on subject, level and frequency, and it comes after a trial session rather than before. What this page commits to is that every market figure on it is attributed and checkable, and that any quote you receive from us can be measured against the same bands. A provider who publishes the market honestly is harder to overcharge with, which is the point.

process.title: Send a marked script with the first message
process.description: Subject, level, the board code from the statement of entry, and one marked paper or report. Without evidence the only honest recommendation is a general one, and general recommendations are what cost families the most money in this market.

process.title: Buy two sessions, not a term
process.description: The first session reads the script with the student. The second tests whether the diagnosis holds against a fresh question set. At the end you have a written list of the repeated errors and an estimate of the work, and you decide from evidence instead of a sales conversation.

process.title: Check the entry and the tier
process.description: Before anything else is bought, we look at whether the student is entered in a tier that caps the grade below what they could reach. Changing a Cambridge Core entry to Extended in time is the cheapest grade movement available, and the deadline sits months before the paper.

process.title: Agree the endpoint in advance
process.description: Every arrangement gets a stopping condition: a school assessment result, a number of sessions, or a specific component completed. Tutoring without an endpoint becomes a subscription, and subscriptions are how a reasonable rate turns into an unreasonable total.

process.title: Review against the school's marks, then stop or switch
process.description: Progress is judged on the school's own assessments. If the subject holds, we say so and the hour stops rather than continuing out of habit. If it has not moved, the tutor changes or the scope narrows, and we say which we think it is.

whyPoints.title: The numbers are published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries the name of the provider or the research that published it. Three of the strongest pages competing for these searches publish no price at all, and one asks the price in its own FAQ and declines to answer. A figure you can check is worth more than a claim.

whyPoints.title: Spending is ranked, not bundled
whyPoints.description: A tier review, two diagnostic sessions and a technique block are cheap and move grades. Open-ended general tuition across several subjects is expensive and often moves little. We publish that ranking even though the second pattern is the more profitable one to sell.

whyPoints.title: The permit position is stated with its source
whyPoints.description: The private tuition work permit comes from Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is free, lasts two years and takes two working days. We publish who may hold one and how to verify it, and we state plainly that IB Gram holds no KHDA permit or accreditation.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the fee
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run above online rates for a comparable tutor, and the difference is substantially a car journey through the slowest hours of the Dubai afternoon. Online delivery removes that cost, which for a budget-conscious household is the largest avoidable item in the whole market.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you not to buy
whyPoints.description: Where the evidence says the problem is motivation, workload or a school issue rather than a teaching gap, the honest recommendation is a conversation with the school. Taking a monthly payment for something unlikely to work is the quickest way to deserve the reputation this market has.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment and Extended Essay work is content teaching, question scoping and written feedback on the student's own draft, documented so the school can see its scope. Operators here sell completed coursework at four-figure prices, and the penalty for that lands on the student.

faqs.question: How much should a family in Muhaisnah expect to pay for a tutor?
faqs.answer: The published market in Dubai runs from about AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 at the premium named end. EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 table puts the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the fee. Those are the providers' own figures, not an IB Gram price list, and any quote you receive should be measurable against them.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutor ever the right choice for a Muhaisnah household?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on the problem. At AED 45 to 150 an hour this market supplies homework supervision, textbook revision and worked question practice, often from a capable university student. For a Year 8 or Year 9 student who has simply stopped doing the work, that is sufficient and paying more is waste. What the cheap end reliably cannot do is read a marked script and name the three recurring errors costing marks, or judge whether an internal assessment question will survive. Match the rung to the problem rather than picking a rate and hoping it covers everything.

faqs.question: If we can only afford one thing, what should we buy first?
faqs.answer: A tier or entry review, if your child sits Cambridge subjects, followed by two sessions of marked-script diagnosis. The review costs almost nothing and can remove a grade ceiling entirely, since a Core entry caps the grade at C or 5 while Extended reaches 9. The diagnosis costs two hours and frequently redirects a family away from a purchase they were about to make for the wrong reason, because most students losing marks are losing command-term, precision and pacing marks rather than knowledge marks. Both are cheap, both are evidence-based, and most families buy neither.

faqs.question: Should a quoted tutoring rate in Muhaisnah include VAT, and how do we check?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and ask for the answer in writing, along with a tax registration number if one is claimed. This page does not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, because doing so responsibly needs a Federal Tax Authority citation and we are not publishing one. What you can insist on is clarity on the quote itself: whether the figure you were given is inclusive or exclusive. A provider who will not put that in writing before you commit has told you something about how the rest of the arrangement will run.

faqs.question: Is a tutoring rate in this market quoted per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Both are used, and the difference matters because a session may run sixty, seventy-five or ninety minutes. Ask which unit the number refers to and how long the session is, then convert to a per-hour figure yourself before comparing providers. Ask two further questions at the same time: whether there is a minimum commitment, because some providers quote per hour and then require a block of ten, and what notice is needed to move a session. Dubai school calendars shift events at short notice, so a rigid cancellation rule will cost you real money across a term.

faqs.question: How many sessions before we see a change in marks?
faqs.answer: It depends on the kind of problem, and any single number is a guess. Technique problems, where the student knows the material and loses marks to command terms, precision or pacing, are typically a four-to-six-session job and the change usually shows on the next school assessment because nothing new had to be learned. A defined content gap is two or three sessions per block of specification. A fluency rebuild, where a student is genuinely years behind, takes a term or more and should be planned rather than bought monthly. Motivation problems are often not tutoring problems at all.

faqs.question: Are group classes better value than one-to-one for us?
faqs.answer: They are when every student in the room is preparing for the same paper and the work is revision rather than repair. They are poor value the moment the problem is specific, because the pace belongs to the group and an individual gap cannot be addressed without holding everyone else up. A tuition centre adds structure, which for a student who will not self-start may be the actual product worth buying, at the cost of a second journey. The sensible sequence is two one-to-one diagnostic sessions first, then a group option if the answer turns out to be broad revision.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor is legally allowed to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time through its own app and e-services. Eligible holders include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it costs nothing, a tutor who has not obtained one has made a choice rather than a saving.

faqs.question: What extras catch Muhaisnah parents out after the first invoice?
faqs.answer: Four things, all answerable in advance. The unit, because a rate per lesson is not a rate per hour if the lesson runs ninety minutes. The minimum commitment, because some providers quote hourly and then require a block. The cancellation rule, which matters because Dubai schools move events at short notice. And tax, which should be stated on the quote. A fifth is materials: nobody should be selling you past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because those belong to the examination boards and are published free by Cambridge and Pearson.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Muhaisnah rise as the exam series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens sharply and that has the same effect as a price rise even where the published rate does not move. Evening hours between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf time are the most requested in the network, and in January and March they genuinely run out, so a family booking late is choosing from what is left rather than from what they wanted. The practical consequence is to book a mock-season block when the school publishes its mock dates rather than when the mocks arrive. The cheapest exam-year support is the support arranged before everybody else needs it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover three subjects to keep the cost down?
faqs.answer: For general homework supervision, sometimes. For anything mark-scheme specific, no, and the saving is false. A tutor who teaches Cambridge 0580 mathematics well is not the person who knows where marks go on 0620 Chemistry observation questions or what an Economics commentary needs from its article. The better way to control cost is to narrow the scope rather than widen the tutor: one subject taught properly with an endpoint, rather than three subjects covered thinly for the same money. Concentrating the spend reliably produces more than spreading it.

faqs.question: What happens if we decide to stop after the diagnostic sessions?
faqs.answer: Nothing, and for a sizeable share of families that is the right outcome. The point of a two-session diagnostic is to find out what is actually wrong before a term is committed, and sometimes the answer is that the student needs a specific habit changed rather than ongoing teaching. You should leave with a written statement of the repeated errors and an estimate of the work, which is useful to you whether or not you buy anything further. Any arrangement that makes stopping awkward was designed to make stopping awkward.

faqs.question: Which subjects cost the most to support, and why?
faqs.answer: Cost tracks scarcity rather than difficulty. Computer Science solution development, Further Mathematics, Arabic as a first language at Diploma level and Higher Level Economics commentaries during a shared deadline week are the thinnest to staff, so they sit at the top of the market and are rarely available at the cheap end at all. Mainstream IGCSE mathematics and the three sciences are the deepest pools and the most competitively priced. If your child needs a scarce component, book earlier rather than negotiating harder, because the constraint is people rather than price.

faqs.question: Can a university student or a school student legally tutor my child here?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they hold the permit. The private tuition work permit explicitly lists unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 among eligible applicants, alongside registered school teachers and government and private-sector employees. It is free and valid for two years. Legality and suitability are separate questions, though. A capable university student can supervise homework and revise content well. Judging whether an internal assessment research question will survive, or reading a marked script against the scheme, is a different skill, and that is what the higher bands in this market are actually selling.

dubai/muhaisnah.closingHeading: Buy two sessions and a diagnosis
dubai/muhaisnah.closingBody: Send the subject, the level, the board code from the statement of entry and one marked paper, and buy two sessions rather than a term. At the end you will have a written list of what is actually costing marks and an estimate of the work involved, and a fair number of families in this district stop there because the problem was narrower than they expected. If we think tutoring is the wrong purchase, we will say so. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, every market figure on this page is attributed, and our own quote comes after the trial rather than before it.

dubai/nad-al-hamar.tutorsIntro: Every profile below is tagged by board and code rather than by subject alone, because a Cambridge 0620 Chemistry teacher and a Pearson 4CH1 teacher are preparing students for different papers. Send the statement of entry and the shortlist takes about a day.

intro.heading: One neighbourhood, three examination systems
paragraphs: Nad Al Hamar runs along the eastern edge of Dubai between Ras Al Khor and Al Rashidiya, a mix of older villa plots, newer apartment blocks and the long approach roads towards Dubai Festival City and Mirdif. It is a settled, family-heavy part of the city rather than a tower district, and the households in it do not share a school. That is the fact a tutoring plan has to start from.

Walk one street and you will find a Year 10 student sitting Cambridge IGCSE at a British school in Mirdif, a Class 10 student on the CBSE route in Al Warqa or Al Qusais, a Year 11 student on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a Diploma student at an IB continuum school near Festival City. All four parents describe the same symptom — the marks have dipped, the homework takes too long — and all four need something different, because the examinations are different.

The mistake this community makes most often is buying a tutor by subject name. 'IGCSE Maths' is at least two qualifications: Cambridge 0580, where tiering into Core and Extended fixes the grade ceiling before a paper is sat, and Pearson 4MA1, with its own papers, its own formula provision and a modular structure in some subjects that Cambridge does not offer. A tutor fluent in one may never have marked the other. The same split runs through the sciences, and CBSE adds a third system with a different question style entirely.

Dubai's private-school statistics explain why this mix is normal rather than unusual. Dubai's media office reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curricula at 37% of enrolment, Indian curricula at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. In the eastern suburbs the Indian and British shares sit close together, which is exactly why one Nad Al Hamar street can hold three examination systems.

Because the format is online, one-to-one, over live video, the match is made on the board and code rather than on who will drive out to Nad Al Hamar at five in the afternoon. That matters here more than in a single-school community: the pool of teachers who know Pearson 4PH1 well is not the pool that lives within a twenty-minute drive of Ras Al Khor. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India.

The rest of this page is written around the board question. It sets out which codes sit behind which subject names, what the Core and Extended decision actually costs, how a modular Pearson route differs from a linear Cambridge one, where the real gap is for a student moving from CBSE into IGCSE, and what the market charges per hour with the source of each figure named.

dubai/nad-al-hamar.programmesIntro: Nad Al Hamar children sit across four routes, often with siblings on two of them at once. The notes below describe what each programme means for a household in this part of eastern Dubai rather than in general.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined at the end, with four-digit syllabus codes: 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English, 0450 Business Studies. Mathematics and the separate sciences are tiered, with Core papers capped at grade C or 5 and Extended papers reaching A* or 9. The structure is almost entirely linear, so a weak paper cannot be resat in isolation within the same series, and the grade reflects the whole set of papers taken together.
programmes.countryNote: The tier decision is the one Nad Al Hamar parents most often discover too late. Schools enter Core or Extended months before the exam, and a student parked on Core in Year 10 because of a shaky start can be capped at grade 5 even if they improve substantially by Year 11. If your child is on a Core entry and the mock marks have moved, that conversation with the school is worth having early, with the marked scripts in hand.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same age group and similar subject coverage, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4PH1 Physics and 4BI1 Biology. Several Pearson subjects use a modular structure in which units can be sat and, where the school allows it, resat in a later series; others are linear. Papers are available in May/June and November each year. Formula provision, question style and the balance between recall and application differ from Cambridge in ways that show up immediately in practice papers.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Nad Al Hamar moving between schools sometimes move board mid-course without realising it, because both schools called the subject IGCSE Physics. The transfer costs weeks unless it is planned: different past-paper bank, different mark-scheme conventions, sometimes a different tier logic. We ask which board the receiving school enters before the first session and we build the bridge around the gap rather than around the subject.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component marked against published criteria. Written papers sit in one window, so the qualification rewards consistency across components rather than a strong performance in one. The core alone absorbs a substantial share of a student's independent time in the second year, and it is usually what collides with university applications.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Nad Al Hamar typically travel towards Festival City or Academic City, which makes the weekday evening tight and the weekend slot valuable. The pattern that works here is a fixed 90-minute weekend session for timed paper work and marking, with a shorter weekday session when an internally assessed deadline is close. The autumn of the second year is the pressure point, and it is best planned backwards from the school's own deadlines.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum routes (CBSE and ICSE)
programmes.description: Board examinations at Class 10 and Class 12 with a syllabus set nationally, a heavier emphasis on worked procedure and numerical fluency, and question styles that reward completeness and standard method. Students are strong on computation and often less practised in the extended written justification that IGCSE and the Diploma reward. Many Dubai schools on these boards also prepare students for competitive entrance examinations alongside the board syllabus, which doubles the workload in Classes 11 and 12.
programmes.countryNote: Indian-curriculum schools serving Nad Al Hamar sit in Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Oud Metha, with long bus runs in both directions. The common request here is help with the step from Class 10 into either Class 11 or an international route, and the real gap is in writing: structuring an answer to a command term rather than reproducing a method. We teach that explicitly, with mark schemes open.

dubai/nad-al-hamar.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Nad Al Hamar households request most. Where the board changes what is assessed, the description says so, because that is the difference a tutor has to know about.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · Pearson Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The same mathematics, two different examinations. Cambridge 0580 Extended reaches grade 9 and Core is capped; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher tiers with its own paper structure. Method marks are where grades are made in both: a correct answer with no working loses marks that a wrong answer with sound method would have kept.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof and calculus route in the Diploma. Higher Level adds a demanding third paper. Students arriving from a procedural board often have strong computation and weak justification, and the exploration is where a wide topic becomes an unmanageable one. Marks go missing in skipped method lines rather than in final answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator-led work, with interpretation in context carrying real marks. The written explanation of what a model implies is the part students under-practise. Higher Level is substantial in its own right and is accepted for many engineering and business routes, so the choice deserves evidence rather than reputation.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 and 4PH1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves and thermal physics, with fields and quantum work at Higher Level. Formula provision differs between Cambridge and Pearson, which changes what must be memorised. The reliable losses are unit errors, graph axes read in a hurry, and experimental-design answers that give a method where a control variable was asked for.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 and 4CH1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics and organic chemistry. Mole arithmetic is the commonest source of lost marks at IGCSE and the commonest source of lost confidence at Higher Level. Mechanism questions ask for arrows and intermediates; a description of what happens earns very little. Practical-skills questions reward precise language about variables and uncertainty.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 and 4BI1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Cells, genetics, physiology and ecology, with a heavy command-term load. State, describe, explain and evaluate carry different tariffs and most students write the same kind of answer for all four. Data questions reward reading the axes and the units before the stem. Rereading notes produces a plateau; writing answers against mark schemes does not.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Business Management
subjects.description: Marketing, operations, finance and organisational structure, assessed largely through case studies. Marks come from applying a tool to the business in the stem, not from defining the tool. Ratio and break-even calculations must be shown line by line. At Diploma level the evaluation sentence at the end of a long answer is where grades separate.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Markets, macroeconomic objectives and the global economy. Diagram accuracy decides more marks than most students expect, and at Diploma level the internal assessment commentaries need news articles chosen for the economics they allow rather than for the topic's appeal. Higher Level quantitative work rewards short, regular practice.

subjects.name: English (0500, 0510 and Language A)
subjects.levels: IGCSE First Language and Second Language · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Reading response, directed writing and, in the Diploma, textual analysis and the individual oral. The commonest failure is retelling instead of analysing. Directed writing is marked on audience and register as much as content, which is one of the few areas where a handful of focused sessions reliably moves a grade.

subjects.name: Accounting and Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Two subjects Nad Al Hamar families ask about more than most. Accounting rewards format discipline: a correctly laid-out statement earns marks a correct figure alone does not. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a bridge into A Level or Diploma mathematics and is where students discover whether the algebra they have is secure enough.

sections.heading: Who actually lives in Nad Al Hamar, and what each household asks for
paragraphs: Four household types dominate here, and they want different things. The long-settled villa families, many of them South Asian, usually have children on an Indian board in Al Warqa or Al Qusais and ask about Class 10 and Class 12 board preparation alongside competitive entrance work. The newer apartment households, a mix of nationalities, are mostly on British-curriculum routes in Mirdif and ask about IGCSE grades. A smaller group sits on the IB continuum towards Festival City, and a further group has moved board at least once because of a school change.

The practical difference between them is not budget, it is which examination the child will actually sit and what that examination rewards. A Class 10 CBSE student who writes complete, procedural solutions can be under-prepared for an IGCSE extended-response question. A Cambridge Extended candidate who has practised structured answers for two years can be under-prepared for the volume of recall a different board expects. Both are fixable, but not by the same tutor doing the same thing.

The second difference is time. Indian-curriculum schools serving this area have the earliest bus departures and the longest runs, so those households have the latest workable lesson start. Families on the Mirdif run get home earlier. Families with a Diploma student at Festival City or Academic City have the tightest weekday evening of all, because the independent workload is heaviest in that programme.

Use the table as a sorting exercise. Find the row closest to your household, and the request that follows is usually the right place to start rather than the subject that happens to be worrying you most this month.

sections.heading: Three boards on one road, and why the subject name hides the difference
paragraphs: A parent comparing tutors by subject name is comparing the wrong thing. The qualification is identified by its code, and the code determines the papers, the formula provision, the tiering and the past-paper bank that practice should come from. Two children on the same Nad Al Hamar street can both be studying IGCSE Chemistry and be sitting genuinely different examinations in a few months' time.

Cambridge codes are four digits and widely recognised: 0580 Mathematics, 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0500 First Language English, 0450 Business Studies, 0455 Economics, 0478 Computer Science, 0452 Accounting. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look different and behave differently: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4BI1 Biology, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4PH1 Physics. The subject content overlaps heavily. The assessment design does not.

The differences that matter in a lesson are concrete. What is printed on the formula sheet changes what has to be memorised. The number and length of papers changes how timing is practised. Tiering logic differs. Mark-scheme phrasing differs enough that a student trained on one board's wording loses marks on the other's. And the availability of series differs: Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November, while Cambridge runs June and November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and a March series available to some centres.

Find the code before you buy anything. It is printed on the statement of entry, usually appears on the school's curriculum page, and the subject teacher will confirm it in one email. That five-minute check is the highest-return thing a Nad Al Hamar parent can do before spending a dirham on tutoring.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: For Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences, the school enters a student for either Core or Extended papers, and the two sets of papers reach different grades. Core is capped; Extended runs to the top of the scale. Parents are frequently unaware the decision has been made, because it is administrative rather than announced, and a student who improves across Year 11 may still be sitting papers that cannot express the improvement.

The decision is usually taken on Year 10 evidence, which is the weakest possible basis for it. A student who arrived from another system, or who lost a term to a school move, or who simply matured late, can look like a Core candidate in February of Year 10 and be an Extended candidate by the following November. Entries are confirmed months before the exam, so the window to change it is narrow and it closes quietly.

What a parent can do is specific. Ask the subject teacher, in writing, which tier your child is currently projected for and what evidence would change it. Collect the marked mock scripts rather than the percentages. Then have the conversation with the scripts in hand, because a teacher looking at a script showing sound method and careless arithmetic will read the situation differently from one looking at a percentage.

Tutoring has a clear role here and it is not the obvious one. The first job is not to teach more content; it is to produce evidence on paper that the student can hold the Extended material. That means timed Extended questions, marked honestly, in the weeks before the entry decision rather than after it.

sections.heading: Modular Pearson against linear Cambridge
paragraphs: Several Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are modular: the qualification is made of units that can be sat in different series, and, where a centre permits it, a unit can be resat with the better result carrying forward. Cambridge IGCSE is overwhelmingly linear: the papers are sat together at the end and the grade comes from that set. The difference changes how a two-year course should be planned.

On a modular route, a weak unit in the first series is a problem with a known remedy, and the planning question becomes which unit to sit when. Tutoring is best bought in short blocks timed to each unit rather than spread evenly across two years. On a linear route, there is no partial rescue, so the plan has to protect the whole set and the useful tutoring pattern is steady and long: build the content, then spend the last stretch on timed papers.

Parents who have moved between the two systems often carry the wrong instinct with them. A family used to modular resits can be complacent about a Cambridge mock, assuming a second chance exists. A family used to linear examinations can panic about a weak Pearson unit that is genuinely recoverable. Knowing which structure your child is on removes both errors.

Pearson publishes the series it offers and its timetables each year: International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so take the live official timetable from the board or your school rather than from any summary.

sections.heading: From an Indian board into IGCSE: where the gap actually is
paragraphs: The move from CBSE or ICSE into a Cambridge or Pearson route happens often in eastern Dubai, usually at the end of Class 9 or Class 10, and it almost never fails for the reason parents expect. The content is rarely the problem: students arriving from an Indian board are typically ahead on algebra, trigonometry and numerical fluency, and they are used to a heavier daily workload than the receiving school asks for.

The gap is in writing and in question interpretation. International boards ask for extended responses governed by command terms, where 'explain' requires a causal chain, 'describe' does not, and 'evaluate' requires a judgement with support. Students trained to present a complete and correct method sometimes write a correct answer that earns half the available marks because the required reasoning was never put on the page. Practical-skills questions are the other shock: naming a control variable, describing a source of uncertainty, criticising a method.

There is a smaller, more mechanical gap too. Different calculator conventions, different significant-figure expectations, different graph-drawing rules, and a mark scheme that awards marks for specific wording. None of these are difficult; all of them cost marks until someone names them. A bridging block of four to eight sessions per subject, with mark schemes open and real scripts marked, closes most of it.

The reverse move — from an international route into an Indian board, which also happens here — has the opposite shape. The student has to rebuild speed and procedural completeness and get used to a syllabus where coverage is wide and the paper rewards finishing. Both transitions are easier when they are treated as a specific project with an endpoint rather than as general tutoring.

In the eastern suburbs the practical range narrows. Households here tend to buy at the qualified-subject-tutor band rather than the premium band, and they tend to buy one subject rather than three. That is a sensible instinct: one subject taught properly for two terms moves a grade more reliably than three subjects covered thinly for six weeks, and it is easier to protect in a week with one usable evening.

Put the figures in context before deciding. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. Where school fees are flat, a household can plan a tutoring spend across a full year rather than a term, which is usually the cheaper way to buy the same number of hours.

Three questions separate a good quote from a bad one, whatever the number. Is the rate per hour or per session? Is marking of work set between sessions included, or billed? And does the rate change in the exam term, when demand peaks and some providers reprice?

sections.heading: A villa evening and an apartment evening are not the same evening
paragraphs: Nad Al Hamar has both, and the difference shows up in how a lesson actually goes. A villa household usually has a room that can be closed, which means a 90-minute session is physically possible and a camera can stay on without the rest of the family in frame. The constraint in a villa is competing activity: siblings, visitors, the household rhythm of a large family in the early evening.

An apartment household has the opposite profile. Quiet is harder to find and a shared table is often the study space, so sessions work better when they are shorter and earlier, before the flat fills up. A good compromise is a 45-minute session at a consistent time with headphones, plus a clear agreement about which surface is the study surface for that period.

Both benefit from one practical step that costs nothing: decide where the lesson happens and keep it there. A student who works in the same place every time settles in two minutes rather than ten. Over a term of weekly lessons that is more than an hour of recovered teaching, which is worth more than most changes of tutor.

Bandwidth is the other thing worth testing once rather than discovering mid-lesson. A screen-shared document with annotation needs very little, and a lesson can carry on with the student's camera off if the connection is weak. We would rather know in the trial than lose ten minutes of a paid session to it.
bullets: Villas can hold a 90-minute session; apartments usually do better with 45
Pick one study place and keep it, which saves settling time every week

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually leave the page
paragraphs: Ask a school why a grade is a 5 rather than a 7 and you often get a judgement about effort. Ask a mark scheme and you get a list. The list is short and it repeats across subjects and across both boards, which is why a marked script is the most useful document a parent can bring to a first session.

Method marks lost to missing working is the biggest single item in mathematics and the quantitative sciences. A student who writes only the final answer loses the marks a wrong answer with sound method would have kept. Command-term mismatch is the biggest item in the written subjects: an 'explain' answered as a 'describe', an 'evaluate' with no judgement. Both are technique failures, not knowledge failures, and both respond quickly to teaching.

After those come the mechanical losses: units omitted, significant figures ignored, graph axes mislabelled, formula misread from the sheet, answer written outside the space so a marker misses it. Then timing, which produces the pattern of a strong first half and an abandoned last question. And finally the genuine knowledge gaps, which are usually fewer than anyone expects and are concentrated in two or three topics.

The order matters because it tells you what to buy. A student losing marks to technique needs a tutor marking their scripts against the mark scheme, not a tutor reteaching the syllabus. A student with real topic gaps needs the opposite. The marked script tells you which, and it takes twenty minutes to read properly.
bullets: Missing working is the largest avoidable loss in quantitative subjects

Mechanical errors - units, significant figures, axes - come next
Genuine topic gaps are usually fewer and more concentrated than feared

sections.heading: Equivalency at eighteen, and the file your child will need
paragraphs: Students who finish school in the UAE and apply to a UAE university generally need their certificate recognised through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process. It is an administrative requirement, it has published criteria, and it is not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees. We describe it here because it changes which subjects should be protected in Year 11 and Year 13.

On the British track the requirements have been set out publicly: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, together with passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject rule for UAE candidates, which does not match the published five-subject requirement.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma we do not publish a points threshold on these pages, because no figure for it could be verified against a Ministry source, and an unsourced number here would be repeated across thousands of pages.

The practical consequence for a Nad Al Hamar family is a planning one. Count the five accredited subjects early, check that Arabic and Islamic Education are not among the ones being counted, and if a subject is being dropped in Year 11 make sure the remaining set still satisfies the requirement. Verify everything against the Ministry of Education's own channels before relying on it.

sections.heading: Starting from Nad Al Hamar, and the limits we will tell you about
paragraphs: Send three things and the first conversation is useful rather than exploratory: the board and syllabus code, the most recent marked script with the teacher's annotations still on it, and the two evenings that genuinely exist after the bus gets back. If there is an internally assessed task running, the task brief and the school's own deadline schedule help as well.

The trial session is taught, not pitched. The tutor sets a short diagnostic, works it through live, and writes afterwards naming the specific gaps found and what the first six weeks would target. Where the diagnosis is that tutoring is not the right purchase, we say so. A student who is sleeping five hours, or carrying a subject combination that cannot work, does not need an extra hour on a screen.

On availability we are straightforward. Weekday slots between half past four and six are the most requested in Dubai and the first to fill, and in this neighbourhood the Indian-curriculum households need the latest ones. For some niche Higher Level subjects the tutor who knows the paper may be based outside the UAE, teaching into a UAE evening; we tell you where a tutor is based when you ask. If the right person is not free, we say that rather than offering the nearest substitute.

What we will not do is sell a finished piece of assessed work, promise a grade, or describe ourselves as holding an approval we do not hold. KHDA inspects Dubai's private schools and sets the mandatory-subject rules; MoHRE issues the private tuition work permit. We explain what both do and link to their own pages, and we hold no accreditation from either.

process.title: Find the code, not the subject
process.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different examinations with the same name. The statement of entry, the school curriculum page or one email to the subject teacher settles it, and it prevents the commonest matching error families in this area make.

process.title: Bring a marked script
process.description: A script with the teacher's annotations shows where marks actually went. Twenty minutes reading it tells a tutor whether the problem is technique, mechanics, timing or genuine topic gaps, and those four problems need four different plans.

process.title: Name the two evenings that exist
process.description: Indian-curriculum routes from Nad Al Hamar have the earliest departures and the latest returns. Choose slots from the week you actually have rather than the week you would like, and leave a fifteen-minute buffer for the bus.

process.title: Check the tier before anything else
process.description: If your child is on a Cambridge Core entry and needs a top grade, the tier conversation comes before the tutoring. Ask the school in writing what evidence would change the entry, then produce that evidence on timed scripts.

process.title: Review at six weeks
process.description: The diagnostic is repeated and compared. If the gap has not moved we change the tutor, the method or the subject that gets the hour, and we say honestly when the problem is not one more hour of teaching.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the board, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Three examination systems run inside this neighbourhood. Matching on 0580 against 4MA1, or 0620 against 4CH1, is the difference between a tutor who knows the paper and one who knows the topic. The format is online precisely so that match is possible.

whyPoints.title: The tier question raised early
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended entries set a grade ceiling months before the exam and are rarely announced to parents. We ask which tier your child is entered for in the first conversation, and if it looks wrong we help produce the evidence that changes it.

whyPoints.title: Transfers treated as a project
whyPoints.description: A board change mid-course has a specific shape: audit both syllabuses, close gaps in order of paper weighting, teach the new mark-scheme conventions, finish with a timed paper from the new board. Four to eight sessions per subject, with an endpoint.

whyPoints.title: Market prices, attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is a market rate with the provider who published it named. None of them is presented as ours. We will tell you what sits inside our own hour, including whether marking between sessions is part of it, before you book.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Criteria taught by letter, research questions tested for scope, drafts the student has produced read and given feedback. No sentence in a submission originates with the tutor, and where a school limits external feedback to one draft, that limit applies.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: The late weekday slots this neighbourhood needs are the ones that fill first. If the subject and time you want are not free we say so, and we tell you where a tutor is based when you ask, including when the specialist is outside the UAE.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's school uses Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Three places give you the answer in minutes. The statement of entry, issued before an examination series, lists the board and the syllabus code for every subject. The school's curriculum page usually names the board for each key stage. And the subject teacher will confirm it in one email. Do this before buying any tutoring: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations with different papers, different formula provision and different past-paper banks, and a tutor fluent in one may never have marked the other.

faqs.question: My son is entered for Cambridge Core maths but we want a top grade. Can that be changed?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but the window is narrow and it closes before the exam. Core papers are capped in the middle of the grade scale, so improvement cannot show in the final grade once the entry is made. Ask the subject teacher in writing which tier your son is projected for and what evidence would change it. Then produce that evidence: timed Extended questions, marked honestly, before the entry deadline. A teacher looking at a script with sound method and careless arithmetic reads the case differently from one looking at a percentage.

faqs.question: Do tutors come out to Nad Al Hamar in the evenings?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver tutoring in the UAE as one-to-one lessons online, over live video, and we do not send anyone to a residential address anywhere in the Emirates; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Local agencies and independent tutors do offer visits, and published market rates for them run AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the figure. The trade we are offering instead is a tutor matched to the exact board your child sits, and a lesson whose full length survives a late school bus.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between a modular and a linear IGCSE course?
faqs.answer: On a modular route, used in several Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects, the qualification is built from units sat in different series, and where the centre permits it a unit can be resat. On a linear course, which covers almost all of Cambridge IGCSE, the papers are sat together at the end and the grade comes from that set. The difference changes the plan: modular rewards short tutoring blocks timed to each unit, linear rewards steady content building followed by a long stretch of timed paper practice.

faqs.question: My daughter is moving from CBSE into IGCSE next year. What will she find hardest?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not the content. Students arriving from an Indian board are usually ahead on algebra, trigonometry and numerical work. The gap is in extended written reasoning: command terms carry different tariffs, 'explain' requires a causal chain that 'describe' does not, and 'evaluate' requires a judgement with support. Practical-skills questions are the second shock, asking for control variables and sources of uncertainty. A bridging block of four to eight sessions per subject, with mark schemes open and real answers marked, closes most of it.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Nad Al Hamar household share one tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: For some of it, yes. Where two children are on the same board and close in year group, shared topic teaching works and reduces the number of evening slots a household has to protect. What does not share well is marked-script review, because the errors are individual and the whole value of the exercise is specificity. The usual arrangement is shared topic sessions plus a shorter individual slot each for script work. We review after six weeks in case the younger child is being carried or the older one held back.

faqs.question: Which subjects do families in this part of eastern Dubai ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a long distance, across every board. Then the separate sciences, with Chemistry and Physics ahead of Biology because mole arithmetic and formula handling cause visible trouble. After those come Accounting and Additional Mathematics, which are requested more here than in most Dubai neighbourhoods, and English for students whose extended writing has not kept pace with their reading. At Diploma level the requests concentrate on Higher Level mathematics and the internally assessed components of the sciences and economics.

faqs.question: How late can a lesson start for a child on the Al Warqa or Al Qusais school run?
faqs.answer: Those are the longest runs from Nad Al Hamar, with the earliest departures and returns often after four in the afternoon. Add thirty to forty-five minutes for food and decompression and the first workable slot is usually between half past five and six, with a later start on days carrying an after-school activity. Because lessons are online there is no second journey to accommodate, so a slot at half past six or seven is entirely workable and does not shorten the session when the bus is late.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking before A Level or the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For a student who is secure on Extended mathematics and heading for a quantitative route, usually yes. It covers calculus, trigonometry and algebra well beyond 0580 and it exposes whether the underlying algebra is genuinely secure before the stakes rise. For a student who is still losing method marks on 0580 Extended papers, it adds workload without fixing anything. The honest test is a timed 0580 Extended paper marked properly; if that script is clean, 0606 is a sensible investment of a year.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education's equivalency process need from a British-curriculum student?
faqs.answer: The published requirements are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Count the five early, and if a subject is being dropped in Year 11, check the remaining set still satisfies it. Verify current rules through the Ministry's own channels rather than any summary.

faqs.question: Does my tutor need a licence to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: A permit, yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to move one IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: There is no honest single number, and anyone who gives you one is guessing. What can be said is where the time goes. A student losing marks to technique — missing working, command-term mismatch, timing — often shows movement within six to eight sessions, because the fix is behavioural. A student with genuine topic gaps across a two-year syllabus needs a term or more, because content has to be taught and then practised. The marked script tells you which case you are in, which is why we ask for one first.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on my child's Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter, say honestly whether a proposed research question is narrow enough to produce usable data, read a draft your child has produced and comment on structure, reasoning and use of evidence, and teach the required skills using a different example. A tutor must not author text that appears in the submission or supply a model answer to your child's own question. Some Dubai schools also limit external feedback to a single draft, and the school's rule takes precedence.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we want is not available in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and then we give you the real options rather than the convenient one. Those are a different weekday or weekend slot with the same tutor, a different tutor with the same board and code experience, or waiting until a slot opens. For a few niche Higher Level subjects the person who knows the paper may be based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening; we say where a tutor is based whenever you ask. A term in the wrong slot with the wrong board experience is worse than four weeks of waiting.

faqs.question: Should a Nad Al Hamar family start IGCSE tutoring in Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the better purchase for most students in this neighbourhood, for a reason that has nothing to do with content. The Cambridge tier decision and most sixth-form conversations run off Year 10 evidence, so improvement that lands in Year 11 arrives after some doors have closed. Starting in Year 10 also means the technique work - working shown, command terms, timing - is in place before the content gets heavy. Year 11 tutoring still helps, but it is repair work and it buys less per hour.

dubai/nad-al-hamar.closingHeading: Find the code, then find the tutor
dubai/nad-al-hamar.closingBody: Nad Al Hamar holds three examination systems on the same street, and almost every tutoring mistake made here starts with buying a subject name instead of a syllabus code. Send us the board and the code, a marked script, and the two evenings that genuinely exist after the bus gets back. We will set a diagnostic in the trial, write to you about what we found, and tell you plainly if the right answer is a tier conversation with the school rather than an hour with us. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.
