dubai/palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Each programme loads independent work differently, and knowing which load falls where tells you when support is worth buying. These are the four we are asked about from Palm Jumeirah addresses.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at three Higher and three Standard Levels plus three core elements. Every subject carries internally assessed work marked against published criteria and moderated externally. The core adds the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and CAS. Roughly a fifth to a quarter of a typical subject grade sits in work the student produces outside taught lessons.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, so the crunch for a Palm Jumeirah student falls across the preceding November to February window when internal deadlines for coursework converge with mock examinations. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than taking a published date second-hand, because the IB is the only authoritative source for its own calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Nine or ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11, with some boards and subjects carrying coursework or practical components. The independent load is not coursework but revision: a Year 11 student has to manage a revision programme across nine subjects, which is a planning skill nobody assesses and few schools teach explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and states that the correct version of the timetable for the zone must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer for your centre's timetable rather than a generic one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. The MYP's own self-managed piece is the Personal Project in MYP 5, which asks a student to set a goal, keep a process journal and produce a report. For most students it is the first time they have been assessed on managing a project rather than on knowing content.
programmes.countryNote: For students heading into the Diploma, the Personal Project is the single best predictor of how the Extended Essay will go. A student who left the Personal Project to the last fortnight will do the same with the Extended Essay unless something changes, and that is a scheduling habit that can be taught.

programmes.name: A Level and AS Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth with no core requirement, which removes the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge load. The independent demand is different rather than absent: A Level depth assumes wide reading and self-directed problem practice well beyond what is set in lessons.
programmes.countryNote: On the UAE equivalency route for British-curriculum students, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, is required alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count. Check the current requirement on the authority's own page.

dubai/palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Palm Jumeirah families most often ask about, described by where the independent component sits rather than by syllabus content alone.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: The Diploma scientific investigation is where most Chemistry marks are lost outside the papers. Students pick research questions that cannot be controlled with school equipment, then write an evaluation that lists limitations without weighing them. Narrowing the question early is the intervention that matters.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Uncertainty handling and graph work carry disproportionate internal assessment marks, and both are teachable in two sessions. On the papers, explanation questions that want a mechanism rather than an equation are the reliable loss point at both levels.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The investigation needs a measurable dependent variable, which rules out a surprising number of appealing ideas. On examined papers, command terms decide the mark: outline, describe, explain and evaluate each want a different shape of answer regardless of how much biology the student knows.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is marked on presentation, communication, engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and students routinely produce an interesting topic containing no mathematics at the right level. Higher Level Paper 3 is a separate problem: an extended investigation most students meet without practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics dominate, and the exploration suits data the student can genuinely collect. Marks go on interpreting results in context, so an answer that produces a correct regression and no statement of what it means loses the communication marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of commentaries on published articles, each tightly limited in length and marked on diagrams, terminology, application, analysis and a key concept. Students lose marks by summarising the article instead of applying a model to it.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE First Language English
subjects.description: The Higher Level essay and the individual oral both reward a line of argument sustained through evidence. At IGCSE, directed writing marks turn on register and audience rather than vocabulary range, which is a skill that responds quickly to correction.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a research project at Higher Level and a shorter commentary at Standard Level, both requiring real organisational material. Application to the specific organisation, not general theory, is where the marks are.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title assessed holistically, plus an exhibition of three objects with a written commentary. Students who write about knowledge in general rather than about the specific title and their chosen objects underperform however well they write.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay assessed across five criteria, with critical thinking carrying the largest allocation. The usual failure is a research question too broad to answer in the word limit, which is fixable in the first two weeks and painful to fix later.

sections.heading: What a Palm Jumeirah search for a tutor is usually trying to solve
paragraphs: Parents on this island generally are not reporting a weak school. The campuses Palm Jumeirah feeds are among the most heavily subscribed in Dubai. The reported problem is narrower and more specific: a student who is clearly capable is losing marks, and the marks are being lost in the parts of the course the school explains once and then expects the student to manage.

Two structural facts make this sharper here than elsewhere. The first is the commute. No mainstream K-12 campus operates on Palm Jumeirah, so every student travels off the island and back along one trunk road, and the usable study window in the evening is genuinely shorter than in a community with a school inside it. The second is that this population is internationally mobile, so a meaningful share of students have changed curriculum at least once and carry gaps nobody diagnosed.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses at all; home visits are part of our India service. On the Palm that model has an obvious practical benefit, since no one has to drive the Trunk twice more in an evening, but the real argument is specialism. A student whose Chemistry internal assessment has a research question that cannot be controlled needs a Chemistry specialist who has supervised that component, not the nearest available graduate.

The sections that follow are therefore organised around the self-managed work rather than around the neighbourhood: what the school teaches versus what the student does alone, what the criteria actually reward, what the length limits are, and how the two-year calendar looks counted backwards from a May session.

sections.heading: What is taught in class, and what the student does unaided
paragraphs: It is worth laying out plainly which parts of a Diploma a teacher delivers and which parts a student runs. Schools do not hide this; it is in every programme handbook. But the handbook is read in September of Diploma Year 1, by parents who have not yet seen what four simultaneous self-managed deadlines look like in February of Year 13.

The examined papers are taught. A teacher works through the syllabus, sets practice, marks it and reports on it. The internal assessment in each subject is a different animal: the teacher explains the task, provides the criteria, gives a fixed amount of feedback that the IB's own rules limit, and sets internal deadlines. Between those points, the student designs the investigation, collects the data, analyses it and writes it up. The Extended Essay works the same way with a supervisor rather than a teacher.

The table sets this out component by component, with the failure mode for each. Read the final column as a diagnostic list: almost every student who underperforms on self-managed work does so for one of those reasons, and most of them are visible weeks before the deadline if anyone is looking.

One honest caveat on the figures in this section and the next two. Criterion structures and length limits are set by each subject guide and the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle. The allocations below are the published structures for the current guides at the time of writing, and your child's teacher or the subject guide itself is the authority. Ask the coordinator to confirm before building a plan on them.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single assessment criterion, which is strange, because the criteria are published and they are the actual marking instrument. A student who does not know that critical thinking carries the largest allocation in the Extended Essay will spend their effort on presentation. A student who does not know that the mathematics exploration awards marks for personal engagement and reflection will submit an accurate piece of mathematics that scores in the middle.

The practical use of knowing the letters is that feedback becomes specific. Instead of telling a student their investigation is weak, a tutor can say that criterion B is where the marks are going, because the data has been presented but not processed, and show what processing looks like at the top of that band. The student then does the processing. That is the whole of legitimate coursework support.

This is also where the boundary has to be stated. A tutor explains what a criterion rewards and reviews what the student has produced. A tutor does not supply content, rewrite a draft into finished prose, or provide a model for adaptation. If the tutor's words would appear in the submission, the line has been crossed, and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student as an academic-honesty investigation. Some providers in this market sell completed coursework; that is malpractice and no grade is worth it.
Confirm the current allocation with your child's teacher before planning around it. Subject guides are revised on a rolling cycle and the structure for a cohort is whatever that cohort's guide says.

sections.heading: Length limits by component, and why they are a design constraint
paragraphs: Word limits are published for most self-managed components and they are not advisory padding. They are the single most useful planning tool a student has, because they tell you how large a question can be. An Extended Essay question that would take a book to answer cannot be answered in 4,000 words, and the examiner does not mark the question, they mark the answer to it.

Running the arithmetic backwards is the trick that saves students most grief. Four thousand words across an introduction, a methodology or framework section, three or four substantive analytical sections and a conclusion leaves roughly six hundred to eight hundred words per analytical section. If the plan has eight sections, the essay will be a survey rather than an argument, and criterion C will suffer for it. Cutting the question in half in week two is far cheaper than cutting the essay in half in week twenty.

The same logic applies down the scale. An Economics commentary limited to a few hundred words has room for one diagram properly used and one line of analysis, not three. A Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary has space for the object, its real-world specificity and its link to the prompt, and nothing else. Students who write over the limit lose the surplus and the coherence of what remains.

The table below collects the published limits for the components students most often ask about. As with the criteria, these are set by subject guide and revised on a cycle, so confirm with the coordinator before planning. The right-hand column is the thing to act on: it says what the limit implies about the scope of the question.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma counted backwards from a May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, which fixes everything else. Working backwards from it is the single most useful planning exercise a Diploma family can do, and almost nobody does it, because the examination session feels far away during Diploma Year 1 and the internal deadlines are announced one at a time.

The important thing the backwards view reveals is that the self-managed work is not spread evenly. It compresses. Coursework internal deadlines for several subjects, the Extended Essay final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and mock examinations all land inside a window of a few months before the session. A student who has banked nothing by the autumn of Year 13 is then carrying six subjects of revision and four pieces of coursework simultaneously, and something gives.

The table below is a generic backwards calendar, not a set of dates. Precise IB dates must come from your child's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly; this page does not publish them, because the IB is the only authoritative source for its own calendar and second-hand dates circulate widely and wrongly. What the table gives you is the ordering and the lead times, which is the part that does not change.

For Cambridge and Pearson students the equivalent exercise uses published dates. Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, runs its exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades due 27 February 2027. That gap between entry deadline and exam is the point: the administrative decisions are made months before anyone sits a paper.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE students are left to themselves
paragraphs: The independent-work problem is usually framed as a Diploma issue, which lets IGCSE students down. A Year 11 student in a Palm Jumeirah household is being asked to run a revision programme across nine or ten subjects over roughly six months, with no training in how to do it, while also being told to maintain sport, music and sleep. That is a project-management task, and it is being handed to sixteen-year-olds.

Three specific skills are usually missing, and all three are teachable. The first is retrieval practice: closing the book and attempting to produce the content, rather than rereading it, which feels productive and is not. The second is mark-scheme reading: taking a question the student answered, putting the mark scheme beside it, and identifying exactly which marks were available and why they were not awarded. The third is timing, which means practising a paper at the real pace rather than at a comfortable one.

Practical arrangements also catch families out. Some subjects and boards carry coursework or practical components with their own internal deadlines, and students who study partly online or move schools mid-course can find the arrangements differ. The exams officer is the person who knows, and the question to ask is which components exist, when they are assessed and what the board requires.

On a pure time budget, the Palm Jumeirah commute matters here. A student losing ninety minutes a day to travel has lost roughly seven hours a week, which is more than a subject's worth of revision time. That is an argument for making the remaining hours efficient rather than longer, and efficiency in revision is almost entirely a matter of technique.
bullets: Retrieval practice rather than rereading, from the first week of a revision block
Mark schemes read against the student's own answers, not in the abstract
Timed practice at the real paper pace well before the session

sections.heading: Why the search says home tutor, and what online delivery changes
paragraphs: Parents here search for home tutors because that is the phrase this market uses, and the question deserves a real answer rather than redirection. In-home tutoring in Dubai is widely available and market rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside them, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The in-home premium buys presence, and presence is genuinely useful for younger children.

For the work this page is about, presence buys very little. Reviewing a draft internal assessment against four criteria, reading a mark scheme beside a mock script, or narrowing a research question are all screen-based activities. Shared screens make them easier, not harder: a mark scheme and a script can sit side by side, annotations persist, and the session leaves a written record. What matters is whether the tutor has supervised that component before.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are part of our India service only, and every country page on the site states the same. For Palm Jumeirah households there is a particular benefit: the island's single road means an in-home tutor's travel time is unusually unpredictable, and a tutor who has already spent fifty minutes getting to the Trunk will protect their schedule by serving fewer clients, which narrows your choice.

The setup that makes online work is unglamorous and worth getting right. A room with a door. A second screen or tablet so the student can write on paper while still seeing the tutor. A graphics tablet for any mathematical subject at Higher Level, which lets tutor and student write on the same page. And a protected weekly hour, because the first thing a busy household drops is an appointment that moves.

sections.heading: Getting started, with the limits stated up front
paragraphs: Begin by naming the component rather than the subject. Saying that a Diploma student needs Chemistry help is too broad to act on; saying that the scientific investigation has a research question the school has not yet approved, with an internal deadline in six weeks, produces a specific match and a specific plan. For examined work, the equivalent is a mock script and the mark scheme, because the script tells a specialist in ten minutes what a conversation will not.

The sequence is then a consultation, a trial with the named tutor who would take the slot, and a block or a weekly booking. For coursework the block is finite by design: four to eight sessions around a deadline, then finished. For examined components the booking is weekly with a review date, and when the student can do the thing unaided we say so and step down rather than continuing by default.

Three limits, stated before you ask. Specialist cover for the less commonly taught Diploma options and for narrow internal assessment specialisms is thinner than for mainstream subjects, and in those cases the right person may sit in another time zone, which changes which slots exist. We say so rather than placing a generalist. We do not publish a price list, because the rate depends on subject, level and tutor. And nobody here will offer a grade or a point total.

One last piece of due diligence applies to any tutor you engage in this market, including directly. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted as unverified.

process.title: Name the component and the deadline
process.description: The first conversation establishes which specific piece of work is in trouble, which criteria it is marked against, and when the school's internal deadline falls. For examined components it establishes the paper and the question type instead. This is what makes the match precise rather than approximate.

process.title: Read the real evidence
process.description: A mock script with its mark scheme, a draft internal assessment, or the teacher's written feedback. A specialist reading actual work identifies the losses in minutes. A placement test or a general conversation about how the subject is going does not, because students are poor witnesses to their own errors.

process.title: Trial with the specialist who would teach
process.description: One session with the named person, working on the student's own material rather than a demonstration topic. For coursework, the trial usually produces an immediate decision on whether the research question survives, which is worth having regardless of whether the booking continues.

process.title: Plan the block backwards
process.description: Sessions are scheduled from the deadline back, not from today forward. A six-week run before an internal deadline has a different shape to a term of weekly subject support, and conflating the two is why coursework help often arrives too late to change anything.

process.title: Close the block, or step down
process.description: Coursework blocks end when the component is submitted. Weekly bookings carry a review date against a named target, and when the student can do the thing unaided we say so and reduce or stop. An open-ended booking nobody reviews is the most common waste in this market.

whyPoints.title: Component-level matching
whyPoints.description: A request for help with a scientific investigation goes to someone who has supervised that component, not to a generalist in the subject. The difference shows up in the first session, because the specialist's first question is about the research question and the controllable variable rather than about the content.

whyPoints.title: Criteria quoted by letter
whyPoints.description: Feedback is specific to the criterion losing marks, with the published allocation named and the current subject guide treated as the authority. Telling a student their evaluation is weak changes nothing; showing them what the top band of criterion D requires changes the draft.

whyPoints.title: A boundary that protects the student
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria and review the student's own drafts. They do not supply content, rewrite drafts into finished prose or provide models for adaptation, and they do not distribute awarding-body material. Providers selling completed coursework put the student's whole Diploma at risk.

whyPoints.title: Calendars worked backwards
whyPoints.description: Coursework support scheduled from the school's internal deadline rather than from the examination session, because that is the deadline that actually binds. For Cambridge and Pearson students the published entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and plans are built on those.

whyPoints.title: Study technique treated as content
whyPoints.description: Retrieval practice, mark-scheme reading and timed papers are taught explicitly rather than assumed. For a Palm Jumeirah student losing around seven hours a week to a commute off the island, making the remaining hours efficient is worth more than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: No dates or figures we cannot source
whyPoints.description: IB session and results dates are not published on this page, because the IB is the only authoritative source for its own calendar and second-hand dates circulate incorrectly. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted with the series named, and criterion allocations are flagged as guide-dependent.

faqs.question: Is there a school on Palm Jumeirah, or does everyone commute off the island?
faqs.answer: Nurseries operate on the island, but there is no mainstream K-12 private campus on Palm Jumeirah. Every school-age child travels off, down the single trunk road, and returns the same way. The two main directions are west and south towards Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, for Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, the American School of Dubai and Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, or east along the coast towards Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah and Al Safa. The practical consequence for tutoring is a compressed evening, which makes efficient use of the remaining hours more valuable than extra hours.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma grade comes from work done outside lessons?
faqs.answer: A substantial share. Every one of the six subjects carries an internally assessed component marked against published criteria and moderated by the IB, and the core adds the Extended Essay at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and the CAS portfolio. None of these are taught the way a syllabus topic is taught: the task is explained, criteria are provided, feedback is limited by IB rules, and the student runs the rest. Students who lose points here usually do so through scheduling rather than ability.

faqs.question: Which Extended Essay criterion carries the most marks?
faqs.answer: Critical thinking, criterion C, is allocated twelve of the thirty-four marks in the published structure, which is more than focus and method or knowledge and understanding at six each, presentation at four and engagement at six. That matters because students instinctively invest in presentation and in demonstrating knowledge, both of which are capped relatively low. An essay that describes its topic thoroughly and analyses it thinly scores in the middle. Confirm the current allocation with your child's supervisor, since subject and core guides are revised on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: My child's Extended Essay question seems too big. How early can that be fixed?
faqs.answer: Week two is cheap; month six is expensive. The arithmetic is the argument: 4,000 words across an introduction, a framework section, three or four analytical sections and a conclusion leaves roughly six hundred to eight hundred words per analytical section. A question needing eight sections to answer becomes a survey, and the critical-thinking criterion punishes surveys. Narrowing means choosing one case, one period, one text or one variable instead of several. A single session early in the process, spent cutting the question in half, is usually the highest-value hour in the whole essay.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a scientific investigation without breaking academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can explain what each of the four criteria rewards, question whether the research design is controllable with school equipment, show what processing data properly looks like, and point out where an evaluation lists limitations without weighing their effect. The student then does the work. What a tutor must not do is supply content, rewrite a draft into finished prose, or hand over a model for adaptation. If the tutor's words would appear in the submission, the line has been crossed and the risk falls on the student.

faqs.question: Why does my child revise for hours and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the revision method produces familiarity rather than recall. Rereading notes and highlighting feel productive and leave very little behind. What works is retrieval: closing the book and attempting to produce the content, then checking. Alongside that, two specific habits move marks quickly. First, take a question the student has answered, put the mark scheme beside it, and identify precisely which marks were available and why each one was not awarded. Second, practise papers at the real pace rather than a comfortable one, because timing failures look identical to knowledge failures on a script.

faqs.question: What are the word limits on the main Diploma components?
faqs.answer: The published limits for the components students ask about most are 4,000 words for the Extended Essay, 1,600 for the Theory of Knowledge essay, 950 across three objects for the exhibition commentary, 3,000 for a sciences scientific investigation and 800 per Economics portfolio commentary. The mathematics exploration is guided by a recommended page range rather than a word count. Treat each limit as a design constraint on the size of the question rather than a target to reach. Confirm the current figure with your child's teacher, since guides are revised periodically.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student start the Extended Essay to avoid a pile-up?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's first deadline implies, because the pile-up is structural. Coursework internal deadlines across several subjects, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and mock examinations all land inside a window of a few months before the session. A student who has banked nothing by the autumn of the second year is then carrying six subjects of revision and four pieces of coursework at once. Having a research question settled and reading under way about eighteen months out is what prevents it. Ask the coordinator for the full internal deadline calendar.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge exam dates differ between schools in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, and this catches families out. Cambridge International allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct version of the timetable for the zone must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong timetable. So the dates your child sits are centre-specific, not generic. Cambridge also runs June and November series, with a March series in some regions, and entry deadlines sit months ahead: for the March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our villa on one of the fronds?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For the work most Palm Jumeirah families need, the online format is better suited anyway: reviewing a draft against criteria, reading a mark scheme beside a mock script and narrowing a research question are screen-based tasks where a shared screen helps. It also avoids the island's single-road travel time, which makes in-home scheduling unusually unpredictable here.

faqs.question: What equipment makes online sessions actually work?
faqs.answer: A quiet room with a door, rather than a shared living space. A second screen or a tablet, so the student can work on paper while still seeing the tutor and the shared material, which matters enormously in mathematics and the sciences. For any Higher Level mathematical subject, a graphics tablet is worth the cost because it lets tutor and student write on the same page in real time. And a protected hour at the same time each week, since a floating appointment is the first thing a busy household cancels.

faqs.question: Is the Theory of Knowledge essay worth paying for support on?
faqs.answer: It can be, because the failure mode is specific and correctable. Theory of Knowledge essays are assessed holistically against a single rubric, and the commonest weakness is writing about knowledge in general rather than answering the prescribed title that was chosen. A session spent turning a general discussion into a direct argument about the title, with two developed perspectives rather than four mentioned ones, changes the shape of the essay. What a tutor cannot do is provide the argument. The student has to own the thinking for the work to be theirs.

faqs.question: My child has changed curriculum twice. How do we find what is missing?
faqs.answer: With a diagnostic from real work rather than a conversation. Students who have moved between curricula carry sequencing gaps: every scheme of work orders topics differently, so a mobile student has missed whatever each new school taught before they arrived. Those gaps are invisible in reports because reports describe performance in the current class. The way to find them is to work through a past paper or a topic checklist with a specialist, who will usually identify three or four specific missing pieces rather than a general weakness. That is a short block, not a year of tutoring.

faqs.question: What does support for a mathematics exploration involve?
faqs.answer: Mostly getting the mathematics to the right level. The exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and the commonest shortfall is the last one: an interesting topic developed with mathematics below the standard of the course. A tutor can show what course-level mathematics applied to that topic looks like, check whether notation and terminology are being used correctly, and ask whether the reflection genuinely evaluates. The student chooses the topic, does the mathematics and writes the exploration.

faqs.question: Are IB exam and results dates published anywhere reliable?
faqs.answer: The IB itself is the only authority on its own calendar, and this page does not publish specific IB session or results dates because second-hand versions circulate widely and are often wrong. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator, who works from the IB's own schedule. UAE schools sit the May session, which is the fixed point you can plan around. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, published dates do exist: Pearson's International GCSE runs May or June and November series, and Cambridge publishes key dates per series with entry deadlines months ahead.

dubai/palm-jumeirah.closingHeading: Name the component, send the script
dubai/palm-jumeirah.closingBody: The fastest way to get useful help from a Palm Jumeirah address is to be specific. Which component is losing marks, which criteria it is assessed against, and when the school's internal deadline falls. Where a mock script and a mark scheme exist, send them, because a specialist reading real work finds the losses in minutes. From there it is a trial session with the named tutor, a block planned backwards from the deadline, and a review date rather than an open commitment. All lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/pearl-jumeira.tutorsIntro: Requests from Pearl Jumeira cluster around two moments: the MYP 5 student about to start a Diploma they have not seen the shape of, and the Year 10 student whose Core or Extended tier is about to be locked. The tutors below work on both transitions rather than on general revision.

intro.heading: An island with one road out, and two exam systems in range
paragraphs: Pearl Jumeira is a reclaimed island sitting just off Jumeirah 1, with villa plots, low-rise residences and a resort frontage. It has one causeway. Everything that leaves the island in the morning joins Jumeirah Beach Road at the same point, and everything that comes back in the afternoon does the same in reverse. For a family with two children at two different schools, that single access point is the hinge the whole week turns on.

Parents here rarely ask for tutoring in the abstract. They ask in one of two specific situations. The first is a child finishing MYP 5 who is about to begin Diploma Year 1 and has never met an external examination or a 20-point subject grade. The second is a Year 10 student whose school is about to decide between Cambridge Core and Extended, which quietly sets a ceiling on the grade they can reach eighteen months later. Both are transition problems, not revision problems, and they respond to different work.

What makes Pearl Jumeira unusual among Jumeirah communities is how mixed the school list is for such a small population. Within a twenty-five minute radius there are long-established British schools running Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel to 16, IB continuum schools running the Primary Years and Middle Years Programmes straight through to the Diploma, and selective British secondaries that run IGCSE then A Level. Siblings on this island regularly sit different systems, which means two parallel assessment calendars in one household.

The second thing worth saying early is about money, and specifically about context. Dubai families are used to seeing tutoring priced in isolation, as an hourly number with nothing around it. It is more useful to see the hour next to the school fee it supplements, next to the exam entry fee if a subject is sat privately, and next to what a two-year Diploma support plan actually totals. This page does that, with every AED figure attributed to the source that published it.

Pearl Jumeira is also small enough that word of mouth does most of the work, and that cuts both ways. A tutor who suited one neighbour may be entirely wrong for a child on a different board, and a rate quoted over coffee two years ago is no longer the market rate. Everything below is built for a Pearl Jumeira household rather than for Dubai in general. There is a timetable of what the causeway and Beach Road do to an afternoon; a transition map from MYP into the Diploma, subject by subject; the Core and Extended comparison that the Year 10 decision rests on; the rules on who may legally tutor your child; and the boundary a tutor must not cross on internal assessment work. Lessons are delivered online over live video, which is why none of the timings below include a tutor's drive, and every figure that could not be checked against a primary source has been left off rather than estimated.

dubai/pearl-jumeira.programmesIntro: The IB continuum is better represented in this part of Jumeirah than in most of Dubai, and families often move through two or three of its stages at the same school. The notes below describe what each stage assesses and the specific thing it tends to leave a Pearl Jumeira student unprepared for.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subject syllabuses, and finishing with the Exhibition in the final year. There is no external assessment. Reporting is against learner outcomes and approaches to learning, which is why a PYP report can look reassuring while a specific gap in number fluency or written structure goes unnamed.
programmes.countryNote: In Jumeirah the PYP is run by continuum schools whose students mostly stay for the Middle Years Programme, so a gap formed in Year 5 often travels. Pearl Jumeira parents who want a concrete read on where a child stands usually ask for a diagnostic against the national curriculum equivalents rather than against PYP outcomes alone.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four criteria marked out of 8, and the total converts to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries set by the school. Most MYP 5 students have never sat a three-hour unseen paper. Criterion-based marking also rewards process in a way that external examinations do not, which is the root of most Diploma Year 1 shocks.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for an island household is scheduling. MYP deadlines are spread across the year as criterion tasks rather than concentrated in exam weeks, so an MYP student and an IGCSE sibling need their tutoring slots arranged on two different rhythms, one steady and one spiky.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the grade, marked by the teacher and moderated externally. Three further points come from the matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge grade with the Extended Essay grade.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly for this project; your school's IB coordinator holds the dated internal deadlines, and for a Diploma student those internal dates bind far harder than the exam window does.

dubai/pearl-jumeira.subjectsIntro: Subject requests from Pearl Jumeira skew towards the two transition years: MYP 5 into Diploma Year 1, and Year 9 into the IGCSE option block. The notes below name the specific demand each subject makes at the point of transition.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier decision dominates. A Cambridge Core entry caps the available grade, so a student placed on Core in Year 10 cannot reach the top band in Year 11 regardless of later progress. Extended candidates lose marks on multi-topic questions and on method rather than on arithmetic.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty. Marks go missing where a command term is ignored and where a named example is expected but a generic one is given. The practical and data-handling questions reward students who have been taught to read the axes before the stem.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis question carry most of the risk. Strong readers routinely under-score by writing about what a text says rather than how it is built. Timed practice against the published criteria moves this faster than additional reading does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and sustained use of the graphic display calculator. Students lose marks by producing a correct figure with no stated assumption, or a correlation with no comment on its limits. Check university prerequisites before treating it as the lighter route; several courses specify the Analysis pathway.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and mechanics carry the Higher Level load, and the scientific investigation is marked against criteria rather than against the right answer. Uncertainty handling is the common leak: an unquantified uncertainty costs more marks than a slightly cruder result treated honestly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The Higher Level extensions assume Standard Level material is automatic rather than recalled, which is why organic mechanisms and energetics generate most enquiries. Students arriving from MYP science often meet quantitative reasoning at this density for the first time in Diploma Year 1.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks, and the Higher Level paper adds quantitative work Standard Level candidates never meet. The portfolio of commentaries is the other pressure point: each has to be anchored to a genuine published article inside a word limit.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Evaluation of studies, not recall of them, is what the mark scheme rewards. Students who can describe three studies and evaluate none sit in the middle band indefinitely. The internal assessment requires a replication handled to a specified structure, which is where the hours usefully go.

subjects.name: Spanish and French B
subjects.description: Productive skills under time pressure, with the individual oral and the written task carrying the weight. The specialist pool for Group 2 languages at Higher Level is thinner than for the sciences, so booking a named tutor early in the school year matters more here than elsewhere.

dubai/pearl-jumeira.regionsTitle: Pearl Jumeira and the mainland it connects to
dubai/pearl-jumeira.regionsIntro: What matters from this island is not distance but which junction you join and when. These are the neighbourhoods a Pearl Jumeira family actually crosses, with what each one adds to the afternoon.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: The district immediately across the causeway. Most Pearl Jumeira trips begin by joining Jumeirah Beach Road here, which is also where the beachfront leisure traffic merges with the school run on weekday afternoons.

regions.name: La Mer
regions.note: A few minutes along the same stretch of Beach Road. The two communities share a junction and therefore share a bottleneck, so a tutor's twenty-minute estimate in October behaves differently in January.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The inland corridor between Jumeirah and Sheikh Zayed Road. This is the route to the Al Safa school cluster and to Business Bay, and it is the segment that most often adds a quarter of an hour in the evening.

regions.name: City Walk
regions.note: Five to ten minutes inland off-peak. Families here share school choices with Pearl Jumeira, so sibling car pools between the two are common and so are shared tutoring arrangements that then run into timetable clashes.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: The nearest dense school cluster, with British and IB campuses minutes apart. Two children from one island household can sit entirely different assessment systems while leaving at the same time for schools on the same road.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Further west along the coast. Several primary and secondary campuses sit inside these districts, and the drive back along Beach Road at 3:30pm is slower than the same drive at 2:30pm by a noticeable margin.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Fifteen to thirty minutes out depending on the hour, holding IB continuum and British secondary campuses that take a steady share of Jumeirah 1 and Pearl Jumeira students each year.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah 1, Al Wasl and Al Safa
schoolClusters.note: The first ring across the causeway, and where most Pearl Jumeira children are enrolled. The cluster mixes long-established British schools with IB continuum campuses, which is why sibling households here run two assessment calendars at once.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, accepted when a family wants a particular programme. The longer drive is precisely why these households need a later tutoring slot than the Al Safa families on the same island.

dubai/pearl-jumeira.modesIntro: Three formats account for nearly every Pearl Jumeira booking, and all of them run over live video. The island's single access road is the reason: a format that depends on a tutor driving in is a format that depends on the causeway behaving.

modes.description: A concentrated run of sessions aimed at the step itself: MYP 5 into Diploma Year 1, or Year 9 into the IGCSE option block. The work is deliberately not revision of what has just finished. It covers the shape of the new assessment, the command terms, the first unit of the new syllabus and the study habits the previous programme never required.

modes.description: A fixed slot with the same tutor, aimed at the assessment dates in your child's own school calendar. For an island household with two children on different systems, the practical value is that both slots can sit in the same evening without anyone being driven anywhere, and either one can move by half an hour when a fixture overruns.

sections.heading: One causeway in: what Pearl Jumeira's geography does to a 4pm booking
paragraphs: Most Dubai communities have several ways out. Pearl Jumeira has one, and it joins Jumeirah Beach Road at a single point shared with the Jumeirah 1 traffic. In the morning that is manageable because departures spread over forty minutes. In the afternoon it is not, because every school bus, every parent collection and every delivery van arrives inside the same ninety-minute window, and the beachfront leisure traffic is building at the same time.

The practical effect is that an afternoon appointment on the island is really two appointments: the one you booked and the road you have to cross to keep it. Families who have tried in-home tutoring here describe the same pattern, which is a tutor who is fifteen minutes late in October, thirty minutes late in January, and who then has to leave on time for a second booking on the mainland. The teaching hour becomes forty minutes and the price does not.

The table below sets out how the afternoon actually behaves rather than how a map suggests it should. Treat the bands as indicative and check them against your own week, because the Beach Road pattern shifts with the school calendar and with events on the La Mer and Pearl Jumeira frontage. The point of the table is not the exact minutes; it is that a session fixed at 4:30pm from an island address is a session fixed on a hope.

An online slot removes the variable instead of planning around it. There is no causeway in the calculation, no second booking to leave for, and no fifteen minutes of settling after a drive. A session set for 5pm begins at 5pm, and the tutor shortlist becomes everyone who can teach your child's syllabus rather than everyone who can reach the island by car before dark.

sections.heading: MYP to Diploma: the step that catches Pearl Jumeira families
paragraphs: A student finishing MYP 5 with criterion scores of 6 and 7 looks ready. Many then take a 4 in a Higher Level subject in the first Diploma report, and the family concludes the child has suddenly stopped working. Almost always nothing has stopped. The mark scheme changed shape underneath them, and nobody said so in those terms.

Three specific things change. Assessment moves from criterion tasks spread across the year to unseen examinations concentrated at the end of it. Marking moves from rewarding visible process to rewarding a correct and complete answer against a command term. And the volume per subject roughly doubles at Higher Level, with a quantity of content that cannot be absorbed in the week before a test. A student who has never revised cumulatively has no method for any of this.

The transition work that actually helps is unglamorous. Unseen-paper timing, practised until a student stops running out of time. Command terms, taught as instructions rather than as vocabulary. Cumulative review scheduled weekly rather than before tests. And one honest conversation about Higher Level choices in the first term, while a change is still administratively possible, rather than in Diploma Year 2 when it is not.

The table below maps the step subject by subject, because the gap is different in each. It is written for the IB continuum schools in range of Pearl Jumeira, where a student may have been at the same campus since the Primary Years Programme and has therefore never seen another assessment system at all.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the Year 10 decision that sets a ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers several IGCSE subjects into Core and Extended. The difference is not only difficulty; it is the grade that becomes reachable. A Core entry carries a capped ceiling, which means a student placed on Core at the start of Year 10 cannot reach the top grades in Year 11 even if everything improves. Schools make this decision from Year 9 evidence, sometimes in a single meeting, and parents often learn about it afterwards.

Pearson Edexcel does not tier in the same way, which is one reason the two systems should never be discussed as if they were one qualification. If your child is at a Pearson school the tier conversation may not arise at all, and the equivalent decision is which subjects fill the option block. If your child is at a Cambridge school, the tier conversation is the single highest-stakes academic decision of Year 9.

What a parent can usefully do is ask three questions before the decision is made. Which Year 9 evidence is being used. Whether a Core placement can be reviewed, and by when. And what the student would need to demonstrate to be moved to Extended. A school with a clear answer to all three is making a considered judgement. A school with no answer to the second is making a permanent decision on temporary evidence.

Tutoring has a narrow and real role here. It is not to argue with the school. It is to establish, from genuine past-paper work in the weeks before the decision, whether the student can handle Extended material with support. That is a question with an answer, and it is far more useful to a Year 9 parent than a general sense that their child is bright.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Jumeirah 1 household
paragraphs: An hourly rate on its own tells a parent very little. What matters is the hour set against everything else a Dubai school year already costs, and against the specific thing the tutoring is meant to protect. The table below puts the figures side by side. Every AED number in it is either a market figure published by a named provider in October 2026, or a cost whose source is stated, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

The market bands are worth stating plainly. A budget online tutor, generally a university student, sits at AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session come to AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

One piece of Dubai context makes the arithmetic easier this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A household budgeting for the year is therefore working from a fee figure that is already known, which is a better position than usual for deciding what support is affordable.

The honest version of the cost conversation is that the cheapest route is rarely the lowest hourly rate. A term of AED 100-an-hour supervision that does not move the Paper 2 mark is more expensive than eight sessions with a specialist who identifies that the problem is method rather than content. Our own figure comes from a consultation and a trial session, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain.

sections.heading: Two children, two boards, one kitchen table
paragraphs: This is the most common practical problem in a Pearl Jumeira household and almost nobody writes about it. One child is in MYP 4 at a continuum school, the other is in Year 10 at a British school down the same road. The parents are now running two assessment systems with different vocabularies, different reporting cycles and different crisis points, and the advice that helps one child actively misleads the other.

The reporting cycles are the first thing to separate. MYP reports arrive with criterion scores out of 8 and a converted 1-7 grade, and they move gradually. IGCSE reporting is dominated by predicted grades and mock results, and it moves in steps at mock season. A parent reading both as if they were the same scale will conclude the MYP child is doing better than they are and the IGCSE child is doing worse, or the reverse, depending on the month.

The crisis points differ too. For the MYP child, pressure clusters around criterion task deadlines spread through the year, with the Personal Project in MYP 5 as a single large commitment. For the IGCSE child, pressure is concentrated in January mocks and the summer series, with the entry deadline months earlier. A single family revision timetable built on one of these rhythms will fail the other child twice a year.

The practical answer is to run two separate plans that share one calendar. Put both children's assessment dates in one place, mark the weeks where they collide, and set the tutoring slots so neither child is working on a deadline in the same week as the other if it can be avoided. Online sessions make this considerably easier, because two adjacent slots in one evening cost nothing in travel and either can be moved without losing the week.

sections.heading: Internal assessment: what each criterion rewards, and who may touch it
paragraphs: Internal assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most Diploma subjects, it is marked against published criteria by letter, and it is the part of the Diploma where good students most often underperform. The reason is rarely the subject knowledge. It is that the student has written a piece of work without ever reading what the criteria actually reward, which is a solvable problem and a fast one.

Take the mathematical exploration. The current Mathematics guide marks it against criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. A student who has produced a technically sound piece of mathematics with no genuine personal engagement and no reflection has already given away a meaningful share of the available marks, and no amount of additional mathematics recovers them. The sciences work the same way: the scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and a beautifully executed experiment with a weak design is capped by the design criterion. Confirm the exact criteria and mark allocations against the current subject guide through your school's coordinator, because guides are revised.

That is also where the honesty boundary sits. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, question a research question until it can generate usable data, explain how uncertainty or reflection should be handled, and read a draft the student has produced to say where it falls short. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final form, or hand over a model answer to be submitted. The research for this project found a provider selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750; that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the seller.

The useful consequence of the honest version is that it gives a student somewhere concrete to go. Published, specific criteria mean a draft can be diagnosed rather than merely praised or criticised. Pearl Jumeira parents who arrive two weeks before a deadline with nothing written are the hardest cases precisely because the method work has to happen first, and method cannot be bought at the last minute.

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA report when both schools are rated the same
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Within a short drive of Pearl Jumeira there are several schools sitting in the same band, which is exactly when the headline rating stops being useful.

The band is a whole-school judgement, so two schools rated identically can be very different for your child. The inspection narrative is where the difference shows. Read the attainment and progress judgements for your child's phase, not for the school overall, and read them by subject group. A school strong in English and weak in mathematics at secondary level reads as the same band as a school with the reverse profile, and only one of them is a problem for a student who needs maths support.

Then read the recommendations, which name what inspectors told the school to improve. Recommendations that repeat across years are the most informative line in the whole document. A school that has been told three times to improve the consistency of marking in secondary science is describing something a parent will encounter. None of this is hidden; it is simply longer than the band and therefore less read.

Two further Dubai facts are worth holding. The emirate's private sector covered 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and International Baccalaureate at 7. And the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after enrolment rose six per cent during 2025-26. More IB capacity matters if you are weighing a Diploma move for a child currently in MYP 3 or 4.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in Dubai
paragraphs: Very few Dubai parents have been asked to think about this, and the rules are more specific than the market suggests. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

Who may hold one is broader than most people assume. The u.ae guidance names teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, gives a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the official route, and it is worth knowing it exists before a tutor tells you it does not.

The condition that affects a parent most directly concerns your child's own teachers. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. The arrangement that feels most convenient, hiring the teacher who already teaches the class, is the one these rules exist to prevent. Treat that as press-reported for ADEK and verify against the current policy document if it matters to your decision.

No fine amount appears on this page. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and figures circulating online could not be verified. A separate point worth keeping straight: a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a licence for a centre, not a badge an individual tutor or an online platform can claim.

sections.heading: The November series, and when a resit is the right call
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. The November option is widely used by UAE schools and almost never discussed on tutoring pages, which is strange, because for a student who missed a grade in June it is the difference between a short recovery and a lost year.

The decision is mostly about arithmetic and time. A student two marks below a grade boundary in one subject is a different case from a student four grades below across three subjects. The first is a targeted eight-week piece of work on specific question types. The second usually needs the content rebuilt, and attempting it in a November window produces a second disappointing result rather than a recovery. An honest tutor should tell you which case you are in after looking at the marked paper, not before.

Entry deadlines are the practical trap. Cambridge sets final entries months ahead of the papers, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version to plan against. The November 2026 Pearson International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026.

Results timing is the other thing to factor in. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. If a sixth-form or university offer depends on a resit grade, that January date is the one that matters, and it is worth confirming with the institution before committing to the November route rather than after.
