process.title: Name the programme and the stage, not just the subject
process.description: MYP 4 is a different problem from Diploma Year 1, and Year 9 is a different problem from Year 11 even in the same subject. We ask which programme, which year, which board and which school, because on this island the answer is frequently different for each child in the household.

process.title: Send the last marked piece of work
process.description: A criterion-marked MYP task, a mock paper or a returned unit test tells us where marks were actually lost. For a Year 9 family facing a tier decision, a genuine timed Extended paper is the single most useful thing you can produce, because it answers a question the school is about to decide on.

process.title: Trial the tutor in the slot you intend to keep
process.description: The trial runs at the time you will actually use, after the causeway has cleared, so you learn whether 5pm on a Wednesday works for your household rather than whether it works in principle. You watch the specific tutor teach your specific child before committing to a term.

process.title: Agree the topic list and the dates it is aimed at
process.description: Before weekly sessions start we write down the named topics and the assessment dates they target: the January mock, a criterion task deadline, the school's internal coursework date. For households running two programmes, both children's dates go on one calendar so the collisions are visible.

process.title: Judge it at the next marked evidence, not on feel
process.description: Progress is assessed against the next marked mock, criterion task or unit test. If the marks have not moved in the topics we targeted, the honest options are a different approach or a different tutor, and we would rather raise that than keep billing the same hour.

whyPoints.title: No causeway in the calculation
whyPoints.description: Sessions run online over live video, so the island's single access road stops being a factor in whether a lesson starts on time. A 5pm slot begins at 5pm, and nobody has to leave early for a second booking on the mainland.

whyPoints.title: Transition work, not generic revision
whyPoints.description: The two moments that actually hurt here are MYP 5 into Diploma Year 1 and Year 9 into the IGCSE option block. Both need the shape of the new assessment taught, which is different work from covering more content.

whyPoints.title: Two children, two systems, one calendar
whyPoints.description: Households on this island commonly run an MYP child and an IGCSE child at once. We plan both against a single shared calendar so the collision weeks are visible, and adjacent online slots cost nothing in travel.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and its date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here name the provider that published them and the month they were gathered. Three of the strongest-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, which makes a checkable number unusual rather than ordinary.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: Teaching criteria, questioning a research design and giving feedback on the student's own draft is support. Supplying submittable text is malpractice that falls on the candidate. We state which of those we do, because a rate card does not.

whyPoints.title: We tell you when the pool is thin
whyPoints.description: Group 2 languages at Higher Level and a handful of option subjects have a genuinely limited specialist pool, and Dubai demand peaks from January to April. If nobody suitable is free at your slot, you hear that rather than meeting a generalist.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel onto Pearl Jumeira for home sessions?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. On an island with a single causeway, that is also the format that protects the lesson: the Dubai in-home market charges roughly AED 180-500 an hour with the tutor's drive priced in, and the drive is the part most likely to go wrong on a weekday afternoon between three and four o'clock.

faqs.question: What is the most reliable time of day to book a session from Pearl Jumeira?
faqs.answer: Between about 4:45pm and 7pm on a weekday. The afternoon collection window of roughly 3pm to 4pm puts every school bus, parent car and delivery van through the same causeway junction at once, and the 4pm to 4:45pm stretch is best used as buffer for a change out of uniform and something to eat. Older Diploma students often work well after 7pm; Year 9 and below usually do not. Check the pattern against your own week, because it shifts with the school calendar and frontage events.

faqs.question: Why did my child's grades drop moving from MYP 5 into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually because the mark scheme changed rather than the student. MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria marked out of 8, spread across the year, with visible process earning credit. Diploma subjects are assessed largely by unseen examination against command terms, with content volume roughly doubling at Higher Level. A student who has never revised cumulatively or sat a three-hour paper has no method for either. The fix is timed paper practice, command terms taught as instructions, and weekly cumulative review rather than more content coverage.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge Core or Extended decision mean for my child in Year 10?
faqs.answer: It sets a ceiling. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade that can be reached, so a student placed on Core at the start of Year 10 cannot reach the top band in Year 11 regardless of later progress, while Extended keeps the full range available. Core also covers reduced content and a different paper combination, so past-paper practice has to use the right component set. Ask the school which Year 9 evidence was used, whether the placement can be reviewed, and by what entry deadline.

faqs.question: Which schools do Pearl Jumeira families usually use?
faqs.answer: There is no school on the island itself, so every family crosses the causeway. The first ring covers Jumeirah 1, Al Wasl and Al Safa, including Jumeirah English Speaking School, Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, Jumeirah College, Horizon English School and Latifa School for Girls. The second ring, accepted for a particular programme, includes Emirates International School Jumeirah, Raffles World Academy, Dubai College and North London Collegiate School Dubai. Those schools are named as context for the school run; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: How do I manage one child on MYP and another on IGCSE in the same house?
faqs.answer: Run two plans on one calendar. MYP reporting arrives as criterion scores out of 8 converted to a 1-7 grade and moves gradually; IGCSE reporting is dominated by predicted grades and mocks and moves in steps. The crisis points differ too: criterion deadlines spread through the year against January mocks and a June series with an entry deadline months earlier. Put both children's dates in one place, mark the weeks they collide, and set the sessions so neither child is working two deadlines at once.

faqs.question: How much should a Pearl Jumeira family expect to pay for IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market in October 2026 runs from AED 45-150 an hour for a budget online tutor, usually a university student, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist is AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are market figures from those providers, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do on my child's mathematical exploration or scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria and respond to the student's own work. The mathematical exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics; the scientific investigation on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A tutor can explain what each rewards, push a research question until it generates usable data, and say where a draft falls short. A tutor must not supply submittable text or a model answer. Confirm the current criteria and allocations with your school's coordinator, because subject guides are revised.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth it, or should my child wait for the next June?
faqs.answer: It depends on the gap. A student two marks below a boundary in one subject is a targeted eight-week piece of work on specific question types, and November suits that well. A student several grades below across three subjects usually needs the content rebuilt, and a rushed November entry produces a second disappointing result. Ask for that judgement after the marked paper has been read, not before. Check the entry deadline early, because Cambridge closes entries months ahead of the papers.

faqs.question: Does a KHDA rating tell me enough to choose between two schools near Pearl Jumeira?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. The band is a whole-school judgement on a six-point scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and two schools in the same band can be very different for one child. Read the attainment and progress judgements for your child's phase and subject group rather than the headline, then read the recommendations, which name what inspectors told the school to fix. A recommendation repeating across years is the most informative line in the document and the least read.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold a KHDA permit or approval for its tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and nor does any other online tutoring platform, because the permit in question does not work that way. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to a training institute with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. There is no KHDA inspection band or approval that applies to individual private tutors. Treat any tutoring page claiming regulator approval for its tutors as describing something that does not exist in that form, and ask what document they actually hold.

faqs.question: Do the tutors working with Pearl Jumeira students hold a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: The UAE requirement applies to individuals giving private lessons in the country. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's service page stating a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any individual tutor directly, and do not accept a vague answer.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during the Personal Project or coursework crunch?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many island households that is the sensible pattern. An MYP 5 student deep in the Personal Project, or a Diploma student finishing an internal assessment, does not benefit from a weekly subject session competing for the same hours. Pausing for two or three weeks and returning with a revised topic list works better than pushing through. Online delivery makes this practical, because there is no travel commitment to protect and the slot can be held open rather than given away.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9 at a Pearson school. Does the tier question apply to us?
faqs.answer: Not in the same form. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE does not tier subjects into Core and Extended the way Cambridge does, so the capped-grade decision does not arise. The equivalent Year 9 decision is which subjects fill the option block, and that is where the attention belongs. It also means Cambridge and Pearson should never be discussed as one qualification: the paper structures, the codes and the entry arrangements differ, and tutoring aimed at the wrong code wastes its first sessions.

faqs.question: What if there is no specialist available for a Higher Level language?
faqs.answer: You get told before you book rather than afterwards. Group 2 languages at Higher Level, along with a handful of option subjects, have a genuinely thinner specialist pool than the sciences, and demand across Dubai peaks from January to April as Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 families arrive together. The realistic choices are a different slot, a short wait for a named tutor, or a concentrated block closer to the oral and written components. Accepting a generalist for a Higher Level language is the outcome worth declining.

dubai/pearl-jumeira.closingHeading: Plan around the causeway, then around the calendar
dubai/pearl-jumeira.closingBody: From Pearl Jumeira, two things decide whether tutoring works: a slot that survives the afternoon traffic, and a tutor who knows which assessment system your child is actually in. Settle the slot first, somewhere after 4:45pm, then match the tutor to the programme and the paper code rather than to a general subject. Send us the school, the year group, the programme and the last marked piece of work, and you will see a named tutor teaching your child in a trial session at the time you intend to keep. Sessions run online over live video, so nothing in that plan depends on the road.

dubai/remraam.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched to a syllabus code and a tier, and most Remraam bookings are single-subject rather than multi-subject. One subject taught properly beats four covered thinly, and the rate bands below explain why.

intro.heading: The least you can spend to move the grade
paragraphs: Remraam is apartment-only, sits on the Dubailand side of Al Qudra Road, and is priced below the townhouse communities around it. That shows up in the enquiries. Families here are rarely looking for a prestige tutor or a two-year arrangement. They have a Year 11 student with two or three weak subjects, a budget that is real rather than notional, and a reasonable suspicion that the tutoring market is not being straight with them about what is necessary.

That suspicion is well founded. Across the Dubai market the advertised hourly rate spans AED 33 to AED 650, a twentyfold range for something described in identical language at both ends. Three of the pages ranking for this kind of search publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. One competitor's own frequently-asked-questions section asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer. A parent in Remraam is being asked to buy a service whose price is deliberately obscured, which is exactly the condition under which people overpay.

The useful framing is marks gained per dirham spent, and it produces counterintuitive answers. The highest-return purchase in the whole market is a single diagnostic hour with a specialist who marks your child's real work against the real criteria, because it frequently collapses a four-subject worry into one subject plus a technique problem. The second highest is an eight-week block of timed-paper work before a series, for a student whose content is secure and whose technique is not. The lowest-return purchase is a weekly general session in a subject where the actual gap is reading or practice the student has not done, which no amount of contact replaces.

There is also a category of thing that should not be bought at all, because it is already available through the school. Past-paper access, mark schemes, subject guides, predicted-grade conversations and departmental revision sessions all sit with the school and its examinations officer. A provider charging for access to board material is charging for something they should not be distributing in the first place, and the material is not theirs to sell.

IB Gram is a matching platform, not a centre, and there is no IB Gram premises in Dubai. For UAE families every lesson is delivered one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. We do not send a tutor to any UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a budget-conscious Remraam household that matters directly: an in-home visit in this market carries AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel priced in, and this community is far enough out that travel is a large part of the number.

dubai/remraam.programmesIntro: Remraam's cohort is weighted towards the IGCSE years, with a smaller Diploma group and a steady primary population in the newer blocks. Each route has a different cost profile.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11 on short, patterned papers with published mark schemes. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, and Core caps the achievable grade at C. Pearson uses separate codes and paper structures for the same subjects. Of all the qualifications here this is the one where cheap, well-targeted intervention works best, because the assessment is predictable.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Remraam money goes, and usually in Year 11 rather than Year 10. The cost-efficient sequence is one diagnostic hour, then weekly work on the single diagnosed weakness, then a timed-paper block in the final two months. Starting in Year 10 is cheaper per mark than starting at Easter in Year 11, because there is time for the student's own practice to do the heavy lifting.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject's internal assessment is worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade and is written over months outside lesson time. The cost profile is different from IGCSE: fewer hours, but concentrated around deadlines rather than spread evenly.
programmes.countryNote: Remraam's Diploma students mostly travel to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park or Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City. For a budget-aware family the efficient pattern is not weekly tutoring across two years but short supervised blocks at the three internal assessment deadlines, plus an intensive before the May session.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked 0 to 8, converted to a 1 to 7 grade, with no external paper before the optional MYP 5 eAssessment. Marks are lost by students who can do the work but have not read what the criteria reward, which is the cheapest thing in the whole system to fix.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years enquiries from Remraam are usually about a specific criterion rather than a whole subject. Two or three sessions spent reading the criteria alongside the student's own marked tasks often produces more movement than a term of general subject work, and costs a fraction of it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with descriptive reporting and no external examinations before the Year 6 Exhibition. For a parent judging value, the honest position at this stage is that most children need no paid tutoring at all, and the ones who do need it briefly and specifically rather than continuously.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries from Remraam's newer blocks are usually about reading. The cheapest effective answer is volume of reading at the correct level, which costs nothing but needs the level identified properly. One session to establish that, followed by a library habit, outperforms a term of paid comprehension work for most children.

dubai/remraam.subjectsIntro: The subject notes below name the specific, drillable weakness in each case, because a narrow target is what makes a small number of paid hours worth buying.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The final third of each paper combines topics. Harvesting method marks from a correct opening line, instead of abandoning the question, is worth several marks a paper and takes about three sessions to establish as a habit.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Qualitative analysis results are pure recall and can be drilled to automaticity in two or three sessions. Moles arithmetic under time takes longer. Electrolysis products are a small, closed set worth memorising outright rather than reasoning out each time.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Circuit questions reward reading the diagram before calculating, and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper rewards knowing named apparatus and method. Both are closed-list items, which makes them unusually cheap to fix compared with conceptual topics.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Genetic crosses are procedural and highly scorable once the layout is fixed, usually within two sessions. Most marks go missing through omitted gamete rows or a ratio the question asked for and the student did not state.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics, Core tier
subjects.description: Worth treating separately because the tier caps the grade at C. If there is a case for moving to Extended it must be made with evidence early in Year 10, not argued in Year 11, and that case is itself a worthwhile reason to book a diagnostic hour.

subjects.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Often the right entry for multilingual households, and frequently cheaper to improve than first-language English because the assessment is more procedural. Marks turn on following the directed-writing instruction exactly, including register and audience.

subjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the named business in the insert is where the marks are. Definitions earn one each. This is a subject where a student can gain several grades from technique alone without learning any new content, which makes it a good target for limited hours.

subjects.name: IGCSE Accounting
subjects.description: Highly procedural: the layouts are fixed and the marks follow them. Students lose marks on presentation conventions rather than on understanding, and presentation conventions are the cheapest thing in the subject to teach.

subjects.name: Diploma Economics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is decided by diagram accuracy, which is a closed skill: labelled axes, a marked new equilibrium, shaded welfare areas. HL Paper 3 is arithmetically simple and interpretively hard. Targeted diagram work is a small number of hours with a visible return.

subjects.name: Diploma Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics and modelling carrying the weight. The recurring loss is interpretation: correct output, no statement of what it means in context. That is a writing habit, taught in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Diploma internal assessment supervision
subjects.description: Worth buying as a short block at each deadline rather than as weekly contact. The highest-value hours are spent on the research question before any writing starts, because a vague question cannot be rescued by effort later.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: KHDA mandatory stream, all year groups
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in every Dubai private school and taught in separate classes for non-Arabs. Support uses the school's own material, since different or additional content requires prior Ministry of Education permission.

regions.name: South View School
regions.note: Not a community but the school closest to Remraam, which gives some families here a genuinely short run while their neighbours in Town Square commute much further. A short run means earlier sessions and more of them available in a week.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: Townhouses and villas a short way along Al Qudra Road, with a younger average cohort and more primary-stage enquiries. Mudon Views apartments are the part of that community whose profile most resembles Remraam's.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: Dense townhouse stock with no secondary school inside it, so evening sessions there start later than in Remraam. Families in both communities often use the same schools in Motor City and Dubai Investments Park.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills 2
regions.note: Further out on the Al Qudra side with a longer bus run in most directions. Families there pay the largest travel premium of any community in this belt if they choose an in-home tutor, which is an argument for the online format.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Greenfield International School and Durham School Dubai sit here and take students from Remraam. Greenfield's IB continuum means a Remraam child can sit the Diploma without a long relocation at sixteen.

regions.name: Dubailand inner communities

regions.name: Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Schools within a short run of Remraam
schoolClusters.note: The nearest provision, and the reason some Remraam families have more usable evening time than their Dubailand neighbours. A shorter run means a 17:00 session is possible, which in turn means a cheaper weekday slot is available rather than a premium weekend one.

schoolClusters.city: The longer northern run from Remraam
schoolClusters.note: Schools in the Motor City, Dubai Sports City and Arabian Ranches belt, reached on routes that slow considerably at afternoon pickup. Families on these routes tend to concentrate paid sessions at weekends in exam years, which changes the shape of the budget.

dubai/remraam.modesIntro: The three formats below are the ones that make sense on a defined budget. All are delivered online over live video, which removes the travel component from the price entirely.

modes.title: The single diagnostic hour
modes.description: One session, bought on its own, in which a specialist marks a real piece of your child's work against the official criteria and tells you what they found. No teaching, no plan, no commitment. It is the highest-value purchase available in this market because it frequently establishes that two of the three subjects you were worried about share one fixable cause.

An unseen paper or a marked school assessment
A plain written statement of the diagnosis
Often reduces rather than increases what you need to buy

modes.title: Weekly single-subject work
modes.description: One sixty-minute session a week in one subject, on the exact syllabus code the school entered the child for. Between sessions the student does the practice and the tutor reads the marked outcome. This is the standard arrangement and it works, provided the subject chosen is the one where an hour moves the mark fastest rather than the one that worries the parent most.

Past-paper work from the correct series, marked live
Written task set after each session, checked at the next
Reviewed against marks every six to eight weeks

modes.title: The eight-week exam-run block
modes.description: Bought as a fixed block before a series, usually two sessions a week for eight weeks, entirely on timed papers marked live. It suits a student whose content is largely secure and whose technique is not, which is the most common profile in Year 11. It has a defined start, a defined end and a predictable total cost.

sections.heading: What a Remraam parent should pay for, and what is already theirs
paragraphs: Before comparing tutors it is worth separating the things that genuinely require paying someone from the things a family already has access to. The tutoring market blurs this deliberately, because a package sounds more substantial when it includes items that were never scarce. For a family searching for IB and IGCSE tutors in Remraam on a real budget, that separation is the most useful thing on this page.

Start with the school. Past-paper access, mark schemes, subject guides, the examinations officer's knowledge of entry codes and deadlines, predicted-grade conversations, departmental revision sessions and in many cases after-school clinics all sit inside the school and are included in fees already paid. The examinations officer is also the only reliable source for which syllabus code and tier your child is actually entered for, and that single piece of information determines whether any tutoring you buy is aimed at the right paper.

Then the student's own work. Timed practice, honest self-marking, an error log and reading the set text are not purchasable. A tutor can enforce them, structure them and check them, which is real value, but the hours themselves have to be done by the student and no fee substitutes. A provider promising progress without the student's independent work is selling a story.

What genuinely requires paying for is expertise the family does not have: someone who knows the specification well enough to diagnose precisely, who can mark against the real criteria rather than a parent's impression, and who can teach the specific technique that is costing marks. That is a narrow and valuable thing, and it is worth buying properly rather than diluting across four subjects.

sections.heading: What each AED band actually buys in this market
paragraphs: The advertised range across Dubai is AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, and the language used to describe the work is nearly identical at both ends. That is the central problem for a price-sensitive family: the market does not explain what the difference is. The bands below come from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, and the fourth column is the part nobody publishes.

At the bottom, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that price the tutor is typically a university student working from a textbook. For supervised homework or primary reading practice that can be adequate and honest value. For Higher Level Diploma content or IGCSE paper technique it is not, because the person does not know the mark scheme and cannot diagnose.

In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is the band for a qualified subject tutor working online. The important question at this level is not qualification but specification: a competent chemistry graduate who has never taught Cambridge 0620 will teach good chemistry aimed at the wrong paper. Ask which board and which code they have actually taught.

At the top, TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650, and in-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 with travel priced in. Above roughly AED 450 you are generally paying for scarcity or for a claimed examiner background, and examiner claims are worth verifying independently rather than accepting. Nobody should imply that examiner status gives access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because it does not.

sections.heading: One subject properly beats four subjects thinly
paragraphs: A family with a fixed budget faces a real allocation decision, and the instinct is to spread it. Four subjects at one session a fortnight each feels responsible and produces nothing measurable, because a fortnightly session has no continuity, sets no enforceable practice and cannot build a technique habit. The alternative, one subject weekly for a term, looks neglectful and is far more likely to move a grade.

The reason is that marks move through accumulated practice, not through contact hours. A weekly session works because it creates a seven-day cycle: task set, task done, task marked, next task set. Break that cycle to a fortnight and the student stops doing the task, because nothing is due. At that point the session becomes a conversation about the subject, which is pleasant and worthless.

Choosing which subject gets the slot should be done on marks-per-hour grounds rather than on anxiety. Subjects with narrow, drillable, closed-list weaknesses respond fastest: qualitative analysis results in Chemistry, genetic-cross layout in Biology, apparatus recall for the practical paper in Physics, diagram accuracy in Economics, layout conventions in Accounting, application to the named business in Business Studies. Each of those can be fixed in a small number of hours and each is worth several marks.

The subjects to deprioritise on a tight budget are the ones where the limiting factor is the student's own reading. If the set text for English Literature has not been read properly, no tutor can substitute for reading it, and paying someone to discuss a book the student has not read is the clearest waste available in this market. The honest advice there is to use the budget elsewhere and put the recovered hours into the text.
bullets: Weekly beats fortnightly because the seven-day task cycle is the mechanism
Prioritise closed-list, drillable weaknesses: they convert hours into marks fastest
Deprioritise subjects where the gap is unread text
If one cause is costing marks in several subjects, it is one purchase, not four

sections.heading: The resit and entry routes, and what they cost in time
paragraphs: A Year 11 family on a budget needs to understand the series structure before deciding how hard to push for a particular sitting, because a resit is sometimes the cheaper and calmer option and sometimes not available in the window they assume. The deadlines are also much earlier than parents expect, which turns a planning question into a closed door if it is left late.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. For the March 2027 series Cambridge publishes an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct from 13 May and certificates in late June. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, noting that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version worth planning around.

IB session dates are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing here is confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session; the exact window should come from the school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org, and a revision plan should not be fixed until it has.

sections.heading: What a mark actually converts to, and why that changes the plan
paragraphs: Parents reasonably assume that a few more marks produce a better grade, and sometimes that is true in a way that changes everything and sometimes it changes nothing. A student sitting two marks below a boundary and a student sitting fifteen marks below it are in completely different positions, and the sensible spend differs accordingly. This is the part of the calculation that nobody explains, because explaining it occasionally argues against buying tutoring.

The structural point is that grade boundaries are set per series after marking, so no boundary can be known in advance. What is knowable is roughly where a student currently sits on recent papers, how many marks separate them from the next band, and which questions in the paper are reliably available to them. Those three facts are obtainable from marking two past papers properly, which is an hour of a specialist's time rather than a term of it.

From there the plan follows arithmetic. A student a few marks short usually needs technique rather than content: method marks they are not collecting, command terms they are misreading, or a question type they are skipping. That is an eight-week block and the return is high. A student fifteen or twenty marks short needs content, which is a longer and more expensive proposition, and the honest conversation includes whether a later series or a tier change is the better use of the money.

Anyone quoting you a specific boundary, a predicted score or a guaranteed outcome is not working from available information. Boundaries vary by series, and no provider has access to them in advance. Treat a specific promise about a final grade as a signal about the provider.
bullets: Boundaries are set per series after marking; nobody knows them in advance
Two properly marked past papers tell you the gap in marks, which is the usable number
A small gap is usually technique: an eight-week block, high return
A large gap is content: consider a later series or a tier conversation before spending

sections.heading: The risk at the cheap end, and the permit question
paragraphs: Buying at the bottom of the market is a reasonable decision for some tasks and a bad one for others, and the risks are specific rather than vague. The first is specification mismatch: a tutor who does not know whether your child sits Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 will teach competent chemistry aimed at the wrong paper, and neither you nor the student will notice for weeks. The second is the internal assessment, where an inexperienced tutor can stray across the academic honesty line without intending to, and the consequence lands on the student.

The third risk is legal and easy to check. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so cost is not a reason for a tutor not to hold one. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Those providing private tuition without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted to you, including amounts circulating online, is unverified and should not influence your decision. A separate requirement applies to anyone operating a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai, who needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually with the request made at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram has no Dubai premises and holds no such permit.

On honesty, the line is worth stating plainly because one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A tutor may teach method, narrow a research question, explain criteria, and give criterion-referenced feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a draft, provide data the student did not gather, or produce any part of a submission. The student signs the authenticity declaration, and buying a finished piece buys them an expulsion risk.
bullets: Ask which board and code the tutor has actually taught, not what they studied
The MoHRE permit is free and valid two years; there is no cost reason to lack one
No published fine schedule exists, so ignore quoted amounts
Feedback on the student's own draft is permitted; supplied text never is

sections.heading: The regulator, the inspection report and what it is worth to you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a judgement on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Elsewhere the map differs: ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge covers that emirate, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

For a family weighing money rather than prestige, the inspection report has one practical use. It is free to read, and it contains subject and phase level judgements rather than only a headline band. A Remraam parent deciding whether a weak Physics position is the school's problem or their child's can look at the published judgement for that phase and subject and get a partial answer at no cost, which is more than most paid consultations provide.

What the band does not tell you is anything about your child. Schools rated Outstanding contain students who are failing and schools rated Good produce top grades. The inspection measures the institution. The only measure of your child is their own marked work, which is why a diagnostic hour is worth more than a school's reputation when deciding where to spend.

It also bears on claims. No tutoring provider should be described as approved by a regulator unless it holds the specific permit in question. The KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises, not to individual online tutors, and a provider implying regulator endorsement is making a claim worth checking before you pay them anything.

sections.heading: Spending the budget in the right order
paragraphs: The sequence matters as much as the total. Families who spend in the wrong order routinely pay more for less, because the first purchase determines whether the rest are aimed correctly. The order below is the one that produces the most marks per dirham for a Year 11 student in this community, and it starts with something very cheap.

First, confirm the board, syllabus code and tier with the school's examinations officer. This costs nothing and is the single most consequential piece of information in the process. Second, buy one diagnostic hour with a specialist in that exact specification, who marks a real piece of work against the real criteria. Third, read the diagnosis and decide which single subject gets the weekly slot. Fourth, run that weekly slot for a term with the student doing the between-session work.

Fifth, eight to ten weeks before the series, convert to timed-paper work. This is the point at which most of the measurable movement happens, and it is wasted if it starts too late or if content is still missing. Sixth, review against marks and stop when the goal is met. Blocks of work should have an endpoint and should end there rather than rolling into an open arrangement nobody has reassessed.

The thing not to do is start at step four with four subjects and no diagnosis, which is what most families are sold. It costs the most, aims at nothing in particular, and produces a term of activity that cannot be evaluated. A free trial session is available before any commitment, with its length and conditions stated at the time of booking, and it is a reasonable way to test whether a tutor can actually do step two.
bullets: Step one costs nothing: get the code and tier from the examinations officer
Step two is one diagnostic hour; it frequently reduces the total spend
Step five, the timed-paper block, is where most measurable movement happens
Every block has an endpoint and ends there unless there is evidence to continue

process.title: Get the code and tier before you spend anything
process.description: Ask the school's examinations officer which board, syllabus code and tier your child is entered for. It costs nothing, takes one email, and determines whether every dirham you spend afterwards is aimed at the right paper. Families who skip this step are the ones who discover in March that they practised the wrong paper format.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic hour, standalone
process.description: A specialist in that exact specification marks a real piece of your child's work against the official criteria and reports what they found. No package, no commitment. This often collapses a three-subject worry into one subject plus a shared technique problem, which reduces the total you need to spend rather than increasing it.

process.title: Allocate the slot on marks-per-hour grounds
process.description: Put the weekly session where a paid hour converts into marks fastest, which usually means a closed-list, drillable weakness rather than the subject that worries you most. We will say when a subject is a poor use of a scarce slot, including when the real gap is reading the student has not done.

process.title: Run it weekly, with the student doing the work
process.description: One sixty-minute session a week creates a seven-day cycle of task set, task done, task marked. Fortnightly breaks that cycle and the student stops doing the task. The tutor's job between sessions is to read the marked outcome, so the next lesson responds to evidence rather than to a scheme.

process.title: Convert to timed papers, then stop
process.description: Eight to ten weeks out, the work becomes timed papers marked live with an error log carried between sessions. The block has a defined end at the start of the series. Review against marks every six to eight weeks, and if they have not moved, change the diagnosis or the tutor rather than buying more of the same.

whyPoints.title: Prices published, with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider that publishes it and the month it was read, and the table says what each band does not give you. Three of the pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and one asks the question in its own FAQ and declines to answer it.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one to one over live video, so the AED 180 to AED 500 band for in-home visits does not apply. IB Gram does not operate home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. For a community this far out, removing travel removes a real part of the price.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis sold on its own
whyPoints.description: A single diagnostic hour can be bought standalone, without a package attached, because it is the purchase most likely to reduce what you need. A provider who will only sell it inside a term commitment is answering a different question from the one you asked.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a code and a tier
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different papers, and the Cambridge Core tier caps the grade at C. The board, the code and the tier are confirmed before anyone teaches anything, because the alternative is competent teaching aimed at the wrong assessment.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Transition work and exam-run intensives are quoted as a fixed number of sessions with a finishing point, and they finish there. Nothing rolls into an open arrangement that nobody has reassessed, which is how tutoring budgets quietly double.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what tutoring cannot do
whyPoints.description: No grade is promised, by us or by anyone working from available information, because boundaries are set per series after marking. We will also tell you when the cheapest effective answer is reading volume, school revision sessions or a later series rather than paid hours.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing that actually improves an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: One diagnostic hour with a specialist in your child's exact specification, who marks a real piece of work against the official criteria. It costs AED 200 to 450 at Dubai market rates and frequently collapses a three-subject worry into one subject plus a shared technique problem, which reduces the total you spend. After that, the cheapest effective purchases are closed-list fixes: qualitative analysis results in Chemistry, genetic-cross layout in Biology, apparatus recall for the practical paper, economics diagram accuracy. Each is a small number of hours and worth several marks.

faqs.question: Why is the Dubai tutoring rate range so wide?
faqs.answer: Because the market describes very different work in identical language. Published Dubai rates run from AED 33 an hour to AED 650, read in October 2026. At the bottom, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which typically buys a university student working from a textbook. In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor. At the top, TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. The deciding question is not qualification but which board and code the tutor has taught.

faqs.question: Should a Remraam family pay for past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Those sit with the school and the examinations officer, accessed through the boards' own portals, and they are covered by fees already paid. A provider charging for board material is charging for something they should not be distributing: boards hold copyright in syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and for unreleased material redistribution is a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. A tutor should reference and link official material, and spend your paid hours on diagnosis and technique instead.

faqs.question: Is one session a week in one subject better than a fortnightly session in four?
faqs.answer: Considerably better, and the reason is mechanical rather than philosophical. A weekly session creates a seven-day cycle: task set, task done, task marked, next task set. At fortnightly intervals the student stops doing the task because nothing is due soon, and the session degrades into a conversation about the subject. Spread across four subjects at that frequency it produces activity you cannot evaluate. Choose the subject where a paid hour converts into marks fastest and run it weekly for a term.

faqs.question: How much is an in-home tutor likely to cost out in this part of Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits appear in the market. Remraam is far enough out that travel is a substantial part of that number, and the tutor you can get is selected by willingness to drive rather than by subject. IB Gram's UAE lessons are online, so the premium does not apply.

faqs.question: My child is a few marks off a grade. Is tutoring worth it at that point?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and this is the best case in the whole market. A student a few marks short typically has a technique problem rather than a content one: method marks not being collected, command terms misread, or a question type being skipped. An eight-week block of timed papers marked live addresses exactly that and has a high return. A student fifteen or twenty marks short is a content case, which is longer and more expensive, and the honest conversation includes whether a later series or a tier change is better value.

faqs.question: Can anyone tell me the grade boundary in advance?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who offers to is not working from available information. Boundaries are set per series after marking has taken place, so they vary and cannot be known beforehand. What is knowable is where your child currently sits on recent papers, how many marks separate them from the next band, and which questions are reliably available to them. Marking two past papers properly produces those three facts, which is an hour of specialist time. Treat a specific promise about a final grade as information about the provider rather than about your child.

faqs.question: When do we have to decide about a November resit?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect, because entries go through the school months ahead of the papers. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the November sitting is the usual resit route, which means an intensive block falls in September and October. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November results reaching students in January, as on 22 January 2026. Ask the examinations officer for the entry deadline the moment results arrive.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge timetable really differ by zone?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it matters. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. For a family planning a revision schedule that means printing the zone-correct official timetable rather than the first one a search returns. The school's examinations officer knows which zone the centre sits in, and confirming it takes one message.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor a false economy for Diploma coursework?
faqs.answer: It carries a specific risk rather than merely being poor value. An inexperienced tutor can stray across the academic honesty line without intending to, by tidying a paragraph or suggesting a sentence, and the consequence lands on the student who signed the authenticity declaration. The permitted work is teaching method, narrowing the research question, explaining each criterion in its own language, and giving criterion-referenced feedback on a draft the student wrote. Supplied text, rewriting, supplied data and any part of the submission are not permitted at any price.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Dubai have to hold a permit, and would it raise their price?
faqs.answer: They need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years, so it is not a reason for a higher rate. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule.

faqs.question: Can the KHDA inspection report help us decide where to spend?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it is free to read, which makes it good value on its own terms. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes judgements across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, with subject and phase level detail underneath the headline. If your child's Physics position looks weak, the published judgement for that phase and subject gives you a partial answer about whether it is institutional or individual. What it cannot tell you is anything about your child specifically, which is what a diagnostic hour is for.

faqs.question: What if our budget only stretches to a handful of sessions?
faqs.answer: Then spend them in this order. Confirm the code and tier with the examinations officer at no cost. Buy one diagnostic hour. Use the remaining sessions on the single narrowest, most drillable weakness the diagnosis identified, as close to the series as is useful without being too late to practise. Four well-aimed hours on qualitative analysis, cross layout or diagram accuracy will outperform twelve unfocused ones. We will tell you if the honest answer is that your sessions are better spent in a different subject than the one you asked about.

faqs.question: Are the school's own revision sessions worth using before paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should be used first. Departmental revision sessions, after-school clinics, subject guides and the examinations officer's knowledge of codes and deadlines are all included in fees already paid. Use them, see what they leave uncovered, and buy only that. The specific things they usually cannot provide are one-to-one diagnosis against the criteria and sustained individual marking of your child's scripts, because a teacher with a full class cannot work at that resolution. That is the narrow gap worth paying to fill.

faqs.question: Is there a trial before we commit any money?
faqs.answer: Yes. A free trial session is available before any commitment, with its length and conditions stated at the time of booking rather than discovered later. The useful way to use it, particularly on a budget, is as the diagnostic step: ask the tutor to mark a real piece of your child's work against the official criteria and explain what they found. If they can do that convincingly, they know the specification. If they talk about motivation instead, you have learned something equally useful at no cost.

dubai/remraam.closingHeading: Start with the cheapest step, not the biggest one
dubai/remraam.closingBody: Email the school's examinations officer for your child's board, syllabus code and tier. It costs nothing and makes every later decision aimable. Then send us that code, the year group and the two or three topics where marks are going, and we will match a specialist in that exact specification for one diagnostic hour over live video. The diagnosis quite often reduces what you need to buy rather than increasing it. If the honest answer is that your money is better spent elsewhere, or that a later series is the sensible route, we will say so.

dubai/serena.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work in Gulf Standard Time and hold a fixed slot for a whole term, because a moving appointment is the first thing to collapse in a week this tight. Each is matched to the exact specification the student's school entered them for.

intro.heading: Count the hours before buying any of them
paragraphs: Serena is a townhouse community off Al Qudra Road, built in Mediterranean-style clusters, with no school inside it. Its secondary students travel out to Arabian Ranches, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Dubai Investments Park or The Sustainable City. Allowing for the collection circuit at both ends, a Year 12 student here spends somewhere between ninety minutes and two hours a day in transit. Over a five-day week that is between seven and ten hours gone before homework begins.

That is the number that should govern a tutoring decision, and almost nobody states it. Providers sell sessions as though the evening were empty. It is not. A Diploma Year 2 student has six subjects generating homework, a Theory of Knowledge essay, an Extended Essay, an internal assessment in each subject, a CAS portfolio and, in most households, at least one sporting or musical commitment that the family is not willing to drop. Adding two tutored hours to that week without removing anything produces a tired student and no measurable gain.

So the useful first exercise is arithmetic rather than shopping. Count the fixed hours: school, transit, sleep, meals, the commitments that are genuinely non-negotiable. What remains is the discretionary budget, and for a Serena Diploma student in the second year it is typically between twelve and eighteen hours a week. Every tutored session, every piece of homework and every hour of internal assessment work has to fit inside that, and the internal assessments alone can consume twenty to forty hours per subject across the course.

Once the budget is visible the decisions become straightforward and sometimes uncomfortable. Two tutored hours a week is roughly a sixth of the discretionary time, which is a serious allocation and has to be earning its place. A session that teaches content the student will then need four hours to consolidate is a six-hour commitment, not a one-hour one. A session that marks a timed paper and names three fixable errors is close to self-contained. The second kind is worth considerably more per hour out here than the first, and the difference between them is invisible on a provider's price list because both are sold as an hour of tutoring at the same rate.

IB Gram is a matching platform, not a centre, and there is no IB Gram premises in Dubai. For UAE families every lesson runs one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps, which means no part of the hour is spent on anyone travelling. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. In a week this tight, a format that adds no travel to either side is not a convenience but the condition for the arrangement working at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, scored out of 45 including three bonus points. The internal assessment in each subject is worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of that subject's grade and is produced over months outside lesson time, which is where the real time cost sits.

All three are long runs. The pattern that survives here is one ninety-minute midweek block plus a weekend session, because four short weekday appointments collide with CAS and collapse by week five.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11 on short, patterned papers with published mark schemes. The time cost is heavily back-loaded: Year 10 is comparatively light and Year 11 from January onwards demands volume of timed practice that has to come from somewhere in the week.

The arithmetic that matters: sixty to a hundred hours of past-paper practice across Year 11 is a realistic figure, which works out at around three hours a week from January. Families who have not reserved that time end up buying tutoring to replace practice, which does not work.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked 0 to 8, converted to a 1 to 7 grade, with the optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. Tasks are assessed as they are produced rather than saved for a final examination, which spreads the load evenly instead of concentrating it.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years load is kinder to a long-commute community because it is distributed. The thing worth protecting at this stage is the habit of starting a task the week it is set, which is the single most useful preparation for the Diploma's long-horizon work. A fortnightly session is often sufficient here, which frees hours for later.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units, descriptive reporting, no external examinations before the Year 6 Exhibition. The time cost to the family is low in work terms and high in transit terms, because the youngest children ride the same long route as their siblings with much less stamina at the end of it.
programmes.countryNote: For Serena primary families the binding constraint is attention, not availability. Two sessions of twenty-five to forty minutes placed before dinner work; a single long session after it does not, regardless of how neatly it fits the adult calendar. Reading aloud and number fluency are the two things worth the time at this stage.

dubai/serena.subjectsIntro: The subject notes name what a tutored hour actually buys in each case, because in a week this tight the question is not whether help would be nice but what an hour returns.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is calculator-free, which exposes algebraic weakness a graphing display was masking. An hour spent marking the student's own script line by line against the mark scheme returns more than an hour of teaching, because most losses are unjustified steps rather than wrong answers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics is usually secure; thermal physics, waves and the Higher Level option are not. The high-return hour is one spent reconstructing a derivation from first principles, because students who memorise the result collapse when the examiner changes the unknown.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks. Practising with the data booklet in hand is worth an hour on its own: students who have never used it under time waste minutes hunting values they are entitled to.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where marks sit in command terms. One session sorting past questions by verb, outline against explain against evaluate, returns marks across every paper and takes no consolidation time afterwards, which makes it efficient in a tight week.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is decided by diagram accuracy: labelled axes, a marked new equilibrium, shaded welfare areas. This is a closed skill with a short learning curve, so two or three focused hours produce visible movement without generating hours of follow-up work.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Worth three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay and routinely treated as unexaminable until the essay is due. The efficient intervention is two sessions unpacking the prescribed title and testing the knowledge claims, early, before the student has written in the wrong direction.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Roughly forty hours across two terms, and the hours are wasted if the research question is unworkable. The highest-value time is spent before any drafting, narrowing the question until it can be answered in four thousand words with evidence the student can actually obtain.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The final third of each paper combines topics. Teaching the student to harvest method marks from a correct opening line, rather than abandoning the question, is a habit established in about three sessions and worth several marks a paper.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Qualitative analysis results are a closed list and can be drilled to automaticity in two or three sessions. Electrolysis products are similarly finite. Both are good uses of scarce hours because they require no extended consolidation.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Circuit questions reward reading the diagram before calculating, and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper rewards named apparatus and method held in memory. Both are finite lists rather than open-ended understanding, which is what makes them efficient targets.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Genetic crosses are procedural and highly scorable once the layout is fixed, usually inside two sessions. Most losses come from omitted gamete rows or an unstated ratio, both of which are presentation faults rather than knowledge gaps.

subjects.name: IGCSE Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Breadth across three disciplines with less depth in each. Worth knowing which award the school entered, because the paper structures differ, and worth prioritising whichever discipline is weakest rather than revising all three evenly.

sections.heading: The Serena school run, and the hours it leaves behind
paragraphs: A search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Serena almost always starts with a grade and should start with a timetable. The community has no school inside it, so every secondary student travels out, and the routes are long: Arabian Ranches and Motor City to the north, Dubai Investments Park and The Sustainable City to the south. Add the collection circuit at both ends of the day and a Year 12 student is spending ninety minutes to two hours daily in transit.

Translate that into a week and the picture sharpens. Seven to ten hours gone to transit. Around thirty-five hours in school. Fifty-six hours of sleep if the student actually gets eight a night, which in a Diploma Year 2 household is optimistic. Meals, family time and the shower that follows sport take another ten to twelve. What is left, the discretionary budget inside which homework, internal assessment work, CAS, revision and any tutoring must all fit, is typically between twelve and eighteen hours.

Set the Diploma's own demands against that. Six subjects generating homework. An internal assessment per subject at twenty to forty hours each across the course. An Extended Essay at around forty hours across two terms. A Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition. A CAS portfolio with its own reflection requirements. The demands do not fit into the budget evenly; they arrive in clusters, and the clusters are predictable.

This is why a tutoring conversation that begins with how many sessions a week is the wrong conversation. The right one begins with which hours exist and what each one is being asked to do. The table below sets out a realistic weekday for a Serena secondary student, which is the document a family should have in front of them before buying anything.

sections.heading: What an hour of tutoring actually costs in week-time
paragraphs: A tutored hour is never only an hour. It carries follow-up work, and the amount varies enormously by what the session was for. In a week with twelve to eighteen discretionary hours, that difference decides whether tutoring helps or quietly crowds out the student's own practice, which is where most learning happens.

A content-teaching session is the most expensive. The tutor explains a topic the student has not secured, and the student then needs three or four hours of practice to make it retrievable. That is a four or five hour commitment from a one-hour purchase, and it is the right purchase when content genuinely is missing. It is the wrong purchase when the content is already there and the problem is something else.

A marking session is the cheapest. The student works a timed paper, the tutor marks it live, and the output is three named errors and the marks each one cost. Follow-up is limited to re-attempting the flagged items. For a student whose content is broadly secure and whose technique is not, which describes most Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 students by March, this is the highest-return hour in the market and it fits in a full week.

An internal assessment session sits in between and has an unusual property: time spent early is worth several times the same time spent late. An hour narrowing a research question before any writing saves ten hours of writing in the wrong direction. An hour of feedback on a nearly finished draft saves far less, because the structural decisions have already been made and unmaking them is expensive. The implication is to buy internal assessment supervision at the beginning of the task, not at the deadline.

sections.heading: Where the hours have to come from
paragraphs: If the budget is twelve to eighteen hours and the demands exceed it, something gives. The honest version of this conversation names what, because the alternative is that the student decides by default, at midnight, badly. In practice four things are candidates and they are not equally sensible.

Sleep is the one that gives first and should give last. A Diploma student running on six hours is slower at every task, which means every hour of work produces less, which creates the need for more hours. It is the one trade that makes the arithmetic worse rather than better, and it is the one families accept most readily because it is invisible until it is not.

CAS is the one families consider cutting and usually cannot, because it is a Diploma requirement rather than an extra. What can be adjusted is its distribution: front-loading CAS into the first year and the lighter months of the second is entirely legitimate and relieves pressure in the deadline clusters. That is a conversation with the CAS coordinator, worth having in September rather than February.

Sport and music are the ones that should usually survive, on the grounds that a sixteen-year-old without a physical outlet in a year this intense is a worse student, not a better one. The thing to reduce is more often the breadth of revision than the breadth of life: a student revising all six subjects evenly in April is wasting hours on the three that are already secure. Narrowing revision to the weakest papers is where most families find the hours they needed.

sections.heading: The year, month by month, for Years 11 to 13
paragraphs: The demands cluster, and the clusters are known in advance, which means a family can place tutoring where it is needed rather than spreading it evenly. This is the planning document nobody in this market publishes, and it is more useful than any list of subjects.

The shape of a Diploma second year is roughly this. September and October are deceptively light, which is exactly when internal assessment research questions should be settled. November and December are the first pile-up: internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay deadlines and mock preparation arriving together. January brings mock results and the first honest diagnosis of the year. February and March carry final internal assessment and Extended Essay submissions. April is revision, and by then anything not secured is unlikely to become so.

A Year 11 IGCSE year is differently shaped. The autumn term is genuinely light relative to what follows, the January mocks produce the diagnosis, and from February the work is volume of timed practice. The sixty to a hundred hours of past-paper work that an IGCSE year realistically needs mostly has to be done between January and the series, which is around three hours a week on top of everything else.

Entry deadlines sit outside this rhythm and ahead of it. Cambridge publishes final entries for the March 2027 series as due 27 November 2026, with the exam period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct from 13 May. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, noting it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November results reaching students in January. IB session dates are not confirmable here, because the IB's site blocks automated checking; UAE schools sit the May session and the window should come from the school's coordinator or ibo.org.

sections.heading: Why weekends do most of the work out here
paragraphs: In communities close to their schools, weekday evenings carry the tutoring and weekends are left alone. In Serena the arithmetic reverses, and families who recognise that early get more out of the year. A weekday evening after a two-hour round trip holds one useful session, and only in the 19:00 to 20:30 window. A weekend morning holds two, with a student who is rested and a tutor who is not working at the end of their own day.

That matters most for the tasks that need a long run. A full timed paper plus live marking is a two-hour operation and does not fit a weekday evening in this community. Internal assessment work needs continuity rather than fragments: ninety minutes on a research question is productive, three twenty-minute conversations about it are not. Extended Essay planning is the same. All three belong at the weekend here.

What should stay on a weekday is the short, self-contained session: a command-term sort, a marking hour on a paper section, a check on the week's homework. Those fit in ninety minutes between 19:00 and 20:30 and they generate almost no follow-up, which is exactly what a weekday in a long-commute household can absorb.

There is a scheduling discipline that goes with this. A weekend session is easier to move than a weekday one, because the day looks emptier, and a slot that moves twice stops existing. The rule worth writing down is the same one that applies to the weekday slot: a protected appointment at a slightly inconvenient time outperforms an ideal one that keeps being rescheduled, because the between-session work only happens when something is due.

sections.heading: Session length, rate and what you are actually buying
paragraphs: Because session length matters more in this community than in most, it is worth being clear about what the market charges and how length interacts with it. The figures below are Dubai market rates read in October 2026 from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They describe the market, not an IB Gram price list.

A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350. Budget platforms advertise from AED 33 to AED 65. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Length changes the value of the hour rather than its price. A sixty-minute session cannot contain a full timed paper plus marking; a ninety-minute one can, which is why ninety minutes is the right unit for the weekend slot and sixty for the weekday one. Two-hour sessions work for internal assessment and Extended Essay planning and are poor value for content teaching, because attention falls away and the last thirty minutes produce little.

For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Fees are the fixed part of this year's education cost; tutoring is the variable part, and in a week as tight as a Serena Diploma week the question is as much about hours as about dirhams.
