sections.heading: Internal assessment supervision bought at the right end of the task
paragraphs: The single most common mistake in Diploma tutoring is buying internal assessment help at the deadline. By then the research question is fixed, the data is collected, the structure is set, and feedback can only recommend expensive restructuring that the student has no hours left to do. The same money spent four months earlier would have prevented the problem rather than describing it.

The decisive hour is the one that interrogates the research question before any writing starts. Most weak internal assessments are not badly written; they answer a question that cannot be answered well in the format available. Too broad, no measurable variable, data the student cannot actually obtain, or a scope that requires more words than the task allows. An hour with someone who has read the criteria can spot all four and send the student off with a workable question instead.

The boundary on what a tutor may do is firm and worth stating because one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A tutor may teach research method, narrow the question, explain each criterion in its own language, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion is underserved, and teach the statistics or referencing the task requires. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a draft, provide data the student did not gather, or produce any part of a submission.

The student signs the authenticity declaration, which means the consequence of crossing that line falls on them and not on the seller. Buying a finished piece buys an expulsion risk. Boards also hold copyright in syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, so those should be referenced and linked rather than redistributed as downloads.
bullets: The highest-value hour is before drafting, not before the deadline
Most weak assessments answer an unanswerable question rather than answering badly
Permitted: method, criteria, questioning, feedback on the student's own draft
Not permitted: supplied text, rewriting, supplied data, any part of the submission

sections.heading: Availability, permits and the claims to be sceptical about
paragraphs: Coverage limits are real and almost never published. For Serena the honest position is that IGCSE Mathematics, the separate sciences, English and primary literacy and numeracy are deep pools matched quickly, while Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics, Higher Level Psychology, Business Management, Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and second languages at Higher Level are thin everywhere, not only in Dubai.

The online format is what makes the thin pools workable from a community this far out. A Serena family requesting Higher Level Physics is choosing among specialists who teach that specification rather than among the few willing to drive past Arabian Ranches on a weekday evening. When a specialist is not free for a requested slot, the useful options are a different time with the right tutor, a short diagnostic block with a related-subject specialist, or a wait with a stated date, and saying which applies is more use than filling the slot quietly.

On legality, individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified.

Three claims deserve scepticism in this market. Regulator endorsement: a KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and IB Gram has neither premises nor permit. Self-asserted ratings: one competitor publishes its own star rating in structured data, which is against Google's policy and worth nothing to you. And any promise about a final grade, since boundaries are set per series after marking and nobody knows them in advance.
bullets: Deep pools: IGCSE Maths, separate sciences, English, primary literacy and numeracy
Thin pools: HL Physics, HL Economics, HL Psychology, HL second languages

process.title: Write the week down before buying anything
process.description: List school hours, transit, sleep, meals and the commitments that genuinely cannot move. What remains is the budget every session has to fit inside. For a Serena Diploma Year 2 student it is usually twelve to eighteen hours a week, and seeing that number changes most families' first request.

process.title: Send the school, the code and the arrival time
process.description: Name the school, year group, board and syllabus code if you have it, the topics where marks are going, and when the bus actually reaches Serena. The arrival time is what makes a slot survive a term rather than being rearranged in the second fortnight.

process.title: Diagnose with a marking hour
process.description: The first session is a timed paper or paper section marked live, producing three named errors and the marks each one cost. It is the cheapest session in week-time because it generates almost no follow-up, and it usually narrows a multi-subject request to one cause.

process.title: Put the long tasks at the weekend
process.description: Full timed papers, internal assessment work and Extended Essay planning go in a protected weekend morning, because a weekday evening after this commute cannot hold them. Weekdays take the short self-contained session between 19:00 and 20:30.

process.title: Step the cadence with the calendar
process.description: Fortnightly in September and October while internal assessment questions are being settled, weekly from January once mocks have produced a diagnosis, and twice weekly in the final eight to ten weeks on timed papers. A free trial session is available first, with its length and conditions stated at booking.

whyPoints.title: The hour budget respected, not ignored
whyPoints.description: Sessions are planned against the time a Serena student actually has after a seven to ten hour weekly commute. We will tell you when an extra session would crowd out the student's own practice, which is where most of the learning happens.

whyPoints.title: No travel on either side
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson runs one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard and a recording kept. IB Gram does not operate home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. In a week this tight, a format that adds no travel is what makes the arrangement hold.

whyPoints.title: Marking hours, not just teaching hours
whyPoints.description: A timed paper marked live generates about thirty minutes of follow-up, while a content-teaching session generates three or four hours. We say which one your child needs rather than defaulting to the one that is easier to deliver.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment help at the right end
whyPoints.description: The decisive hour interrogates the research question before any writing starts, because most weak assessments answer an unanswerable question rather than answering badly. Late draft feedback costs hours the student does not have.

whyPoints.title: A month-by-month map, published
whyPoints.description: The deadline clusters in Years 11 to 13 are predictable, so the plan places sessions where the pressure actually is rather than spreading them evenly. No competing page in this market publishes a calendar of any kind.

whyPoints.title: Rates and claims both stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure names the provider publishing it and the month it was read. We hold no regulator endorsement and say so, we publish no self-asserted rating, and we make no promise about a final grade because boundaries are set per series after marking.

faqs.question: How much time does the Serena school run actually take out of a week?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student, seven to ten hours. The community has no school inside it, so children travel to Arabian Ranches, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Dubai Investments Park or The Sustainable City, and with the collection circuit at both ends a single day costs ninety minutes to two hours in transit. That is the number that should shape a tutoring decision, because it is subtracted before homework, internal assessment work, CAS and revision are even considered. Most providers sell sessions as though the evening were empty.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma Year 2 student in Serena actually have free?
faqs.answer: Typically twelve to eighteen, once school, transit, sleep, meals and non-negotiable commitments are removed. Into that have to fit homework from six subjects, an internal assessment per subject at twenty to forty hours each across the course, an Extended Essay at around forty hours, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and a CAS portfolio. Two tutored hours is roughly a sixth of that budget, which is a serious allocation. Writing the week down before buying anything is the most useful thing a family can do.

faqs.question: Which kind of tutoring session costs the least time overall?
faqs.answer: A timed paper marked live. The session runs sixty to ninety minutes and generates perhaps thirty to forty-five minutes of follow-up re-attempting the flagged items, so the total week-time cost is about two hours. A content-teaching session on a new topic costs four to five hours in total, because the student then needs three or four hours of practice to make the content retrievable. Both are legitimate purchases; they suit different diagnoses. In a full week, knowing which one you are buying matters as much as the rate.

faqs.question: Why should Serena families put tutoring at the weekend?
faqs.answer: Because the long tasks do not fit a weekday evening after a two-hour round trip. A full timed paper plus live marking is a two-hour operation. Internal assessment work and Extended Essay planning need continuity rather than fragments. A weekend morning holds those with a rested student. Weekdays should take the short self-contained session, best between 19:00 and 20:30, which generates almost no follow-up. The discipline is to protect the weekend slot, because an emptier-looking day is the easiest one to reschedule away.

faqs.question: When in the year should we buy internal assessment supervision?
faqs.answer: At the start of the task, not at the deadline. The decisive hour interrogates the research question before any writing: most weak assessments are not badly written but answer a question that cannot be answered well in the format available, because it is too broad, has no measurable variable, requires data the student cannot obtain, or needs more words than the task allows. An hour spent there saves ten. The same money spent on a nearly finished draft can only recommend restructuring the student has no hours left to do.

faqs.question: Can CAS be cut back if the academic load is too heavy?
faqs.answer: Not cut, because it is a Diploma requirement rather than an extra, but its distribution can be managed. Front-loading CAS into the first year and the lighter months of the second is legitimate and relieves pressure during the deadline clusters in November, February and March. That is a conversation with the CAS coordinator and it is worth having in September rather than in February. What usually should not give is sleep, because a student running short is slower at every task, which increases the hours needed.

faqs.question: Which months are hardest for a Diploma Year 2 student?
faqs.answer: November and December, then February and March. November and December bring internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay deadlines and mock preparation at the same time. February and March carry final internal assessment and Extended Essay submissions alongside the start of serious revision. September and October look light and are the right time to settle research questions, which is why using them well reduces the November pile-up. January delivers mock results and the first honest diagnosis of the year, which is the moment to reallocate the whole plan.

faqs.question: How much past-paper practice does an IGCSE year really need?
faqs.answer: Sixty to a hundred hours across Year 11 is a realistic figure, and most of it has to happen between January and the series because the syllabus is still being taught before that. That works out at around three hours a week on top of homework, which is why families who have not reserved the time end up trying to buy tutoring as a substitute for practice. It does not substitute. A tutor can enforce, structure and mark the practice, which is real value, but the hours have to be done by the student.

faqs.question: What session length is right for which task?
faqs.answer: Thirty to forty minutes for primary reading or number fluency and for single language skills. Sixty minutes for a paper section marked live, a command-term sort or a homework check. Ninety minutes for a full timed paper plus marking, or a Diploma teaching block. Two hours for internal assessment question-narrowing and Extended Essay planning, which need a long uninterrupted run. Two hours is poor value for new content teaching, because attention falls away and the last half hour produces little regardless of the tutor's quality.

faqs.question: What do Dubai tutors charge, and does session length change the rate?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Length generally prices pro rata, so what changes with length is the value of the hour rather than the rate. Those are market figures from published provider pages and Bestimate's 2026 table, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge entry deadline affect how we plan the year?
faqs.answer: Substantially, because it closes months before the papers. Cambridge publishes final entries for the March 2027 series as due 27 November 2026, with the exam period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct from 13 May. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, noting it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Confirm your centre's zone with the examinations officer.

faqs.question: Can you tell us the IB exam dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody writing a page like this honestly can. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date on this page has been confirmed from the IB itself. What is reliable is that UAE schools sit the May session. For the exact window, ask your school's IB coordinator or check ibo.org directly, and do not fix a revision plan against a date taken from a tutoring page. Cambridge and Pearson dates quoted here are from those boards' own published material.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to match from Serena?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics, Economics, Psychology, Business Management, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and second languages at Higher Level. Those pools are small everywhere rather than specifically in Dubai. IGCSE Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English and primary literacy and numeracy fill quickly. Because lessons are delivered online, the pool is not limited to tutors willing to drive past Arabian Ranches on a weekday evening. When nobody suitable is free for your slot we will say so and give the options rather than substituting a generalist.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts.

faqs.question: What claims should we be sceptical about when choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: Three in particular. Regulator endorsement: a KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and no online matching platform holds one, including this one. Self-asserted ratings: one competitor publishes its own star rating in structured data, which is against Google's policy and tells you nothing verifiable. And any promise about a final grade, since grade boundaries are set per series after marking and nobody has advance access to them. A provider making the third claim is describing their marketing rather than your child.

dubai/serena.closingHeading: Count the hours, then spend them
dubai/serena.closingBody: Write your child's week down first: school, transit, sleep, meals and the commitments that cannot move. The twelve to eighteen hours left is the budget, and it is the real constraint in a community with a commute like Serena's. Then send us the school, the year group, the board and syllabus code if you have it, and the time the bus reaches Serena. We will match a specialist in that exact specification and start with a marking hour, which is the cheapest session in week-time and the one most likely to tell you where the marks are actually going.

dubai/sobha-hartland.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here cover the subjects Sobha Hartland students most often need in a weekday slot: Maths AA and AI, the three sciences, Economics, Business Management and English. intro.heading: Why the clock, not the subject, is the first question in Sobha Hartland
paragraphs: Most tutoring conversations start with a subject. In Sobha Hartland the useful first question is the clock, because the answer here is genuinely different from the answer two communities over. Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai are both inside the development, which means the school run for a large share of families is a five to ten minute drive or in some cases a walk. A child who leaves school at ten past three can realistically be sitting down, fed and ready at quarter past four.

That hour matters more than it sounds. Across most of Dubai the earliest sensible weekday slot for a secondary student is five o'clock, and often half past, because the journey home from a school in another community runs straight into the worst of the afternoon. The practical consequence is that Hartland families have access to a slot that is both earlier and calmer, which is the single best predictor of whether a weekly session survives past February. Attention at quarter past four is not the same commodity as attention at half past seven.

The counterweight is the parent commute, not the child's. Sobha Hartland sits between Al Khail Road, Ras Al Khor Road and the Business Bay side of the canal, and a working parent heading home from DIFC or Business Bay at five o'clock is in traffic, not at home. Families who assume a parent needs to be present for the first few sessions should plan for the later slot and say so at the start. Families whose child can begin independently should take the earlier one, because that window is also where the scarcer Higher Level specialists still have availability.

Lessons for Sobha Hartland families are one-to-one and delivered live over video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. In a scheduling conversation that fact is the point rather than a caveat. An in-home tutor's earliest Hartland availability is set by wherever they were before you, so the quarter-past-four slot that the community's geography makes possible is only actually bookable if nobody has to drive to reach it.

The rest of this page is built around that single idea. It sets out the Hartland weekday hour by hour, what each session length can realistically achieve, what a travelling tutor's hour costs once the drive is priced in, how Ramadan and mock weeks change the pattern, which weeks of the year the schedule has to bend, and what happens when the specialist you need is not free in the slot you want. Every AED figure is attributed and every board date is taken from the board's own published schedule.

dubai/sobha-hartland.programmesIntro: Sobha Hartland's two schools cover the IB continuum and the English National Curriculum with an IB sixth form, so a single street can contain MYP, IGCSE, A Level and Diploma students. Each programme makes a different demand on the weekday evening.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment worth 20 to 30 per cent of the grade, marked internally against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The timetable problem is not the total workload but the collision of internal deadlines across six courses inside the same fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: Both Hartland schools feed Diploma cohorts, and the scheduling reality for a DP2 student here is that October and February are the two months in which an evening slot has to flex. A fixed weekday hour that moves to a different weekday during a deadline cluster works far better than a session cancelled and never recovered.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with command terms that reward explanation over recall. Year 11 may sit MYP eAssessment, an on-screen examination with its own question style. Criterion grades convert to a 1 to 7 subject grade, which rarely matches a parent's expectation from a percentage system.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Sobha Hartland are the group that benefits most from the early slot. Criterion work rewards a clear head: a forty-five minute session at quarter past four on a Tuesday produces more than ninety minutes at eight o'clock after a long day and a late dinner, and the difference shows within a month.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined at the end of Year 11 using syllabuses such as Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics or Pearson 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge tiers several subjects as Core or Extended, Pearson as Foundation or Higher in Maths, and the tier fixes the grade ceiling. Entries close months before the papers.
programmes.countryNote: Hartland's British-curriculum cohort sits IGCSE at sixteen, and the scheduling point specific to Year 11 is that January and February need two sessions a week rather than one. Building that increase into the plan in October is easier than negotiating it in the middle of mock results week.

programmes.name: A Level, after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four linear subjects examined at the end of Year 13, with Higher Level depth and no breadth requirement. Mathematics covers pure, mechanics and statistics; sciences carry a separate practical endorsement. University offers are quoted in A Level grades, which makes the choice at sixteen an admissions decision rather than a preference.
programmes.countryNote: A Level students in Sobha Hartland typically want a ninety-minute slot rather than sixty, because the useful unit of work at this level is a full past-paper question set followed by a mark-scheme walkthrough. That does not fit in an hour, and splitting it across two weeks loses most of the benefit.

dubai/sobha-hartland.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Sobha Hartland families book most, with a note on the session length each one tends to need. Length is not a detail here: the wrong format wastes the hour regardless of how good the tutor is.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Best in 90 minutes. HL rewards sustained reasoning across an unfamiliar context, which means working a full Paper 3 style question and then unpicking it. A sixty-minute slot ends halfway through the interesting part.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Works well in 60 minutes once calculator fluency is established. Statistics and modelling topics break cleanly into single-session units, which suits the earlier weekday slot and a younger student's attention span.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms need frequency more than length: two shorter sessions a week beat one long one, because the recall curve is the problem. Energetics and equilibrium are the opposite and want a full ninety minutes.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Method-heavy and well suited to the 4.15pm slot, when a student can still follow a multi-step derivation. Marks disappear in units, significant figures and explanation questions written too loosely to score.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High content volume, which makes short frequent retrieval practice more valuable than long sessions. The command terms separate a 5 from a 7, and that distinction is teachable in twenty minutes if it is taught at all.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation paragraph decide the grade. Commentary work needs a scheduled slot in the weeks before the school's internal deadline, not a general weekly session that happens to touch it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study analysis under time pressure is the examinable skill. A ninety-minute slot allows a full timed response followed by feedback, which is the only format that reliably moves a mark here.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the unseen non-literary paper are the two components students arrive least prepared for. Both improve quickly with structured practice, and both need a slot where the student can speak aloud without an audience.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.description: Tier sets the ceiling, so the first session is a tier conversation if Year 10 is still undecided. Extended and Higher papers test algebraic manipulation and multi-step problems against the clock.

subjects.name: IGCSE Sciences, separate and combined
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is the most improvable component for a student never taught how it is marked. Separate sciences carry more content and more practical reasoning marks than the combined award.

sections.heading: The Sobha Hartland weekday, hour by hour
paragraphs: A tutoring schedule that ignores the actual shape of the afternoon is the most common reason a weekly arrangement quietly dies in February. The grid below is the Sobha Hartland weekday as families here describe it, with an honest assessment of whether a lesson can run in each window and why. It assumes a secondary student at one of the two schools inside the community, because that is the majority case here.

Two windows do most of the work. The first runs from roughly quarter past four to half past five, which exists in Sobha Hartland precisely because the school run is short. The second runs from about half past six to eight, after a parent is home and dinner has happened. The gap between them is the awkward one: a lesson beginning at six collides with the end of the commute and the start of the evening meal in most households, and families who book it tend to move it within a month.

What falls outside the grid is just as useful to name. Nothing productive happens after half past eight for a student who started school at half past seven in the morning, and booking a nine o'clock session because it was the only slot available is a decision to pay for an hour that will not work. The weekend morning block is the better answer for anyone who cannot make a weekday window, and for the longer paper-practice format it is better in any case.

sections.heading: How long a session should be, and what each length can achieve
paragraphs: Session length is sold as a convenience choice and is actually an academic one. Sixty minutes, seventy-five minutes and ninety minutes do different jobs, and buying the wrong one produces a tutor who is competent and a student who is not improving. The table sets out what each format can realistically deliver, which window it belongs in, and the situation in which it fails.

The main error families make is buying length when they need frequency. A student forgetting organic chemistry mechanisms between lessons does not need a longer lesson; they need two shorter contacts in the same week, because the problem is the shape of the forgetting curve rather than the amount of explanation. The reverse error is equally common: buying sixty minutes for exam technique, which cannot be taught without a timed attempt first, and a timed attempt plus feedback does not compress into an hour.

There is also a floor. Sessions below forty-five minutes work for Arabic vocabulary, formula recall and a quick check on a specific misunderstanding, and they work poorly for anything requiring a student to build an argument. Families looking at a thirty-minute format for a DP2 Economics commentary are buying something that cannot do the job, however reasonable the hourly rate looks.

One further point on length applies specifically to Sobha Hartland. Because the early window exists here, families can run a ninety-minute block on a weekday afternoon rather than being pushed to a weekend. That matters most in the January to March stretch, when a Year 11 or DP2 student needs timed paper practice every week and a weekend slot is already carrying sport, family commitments and the other subject. Using the afternoon window for the long block and keeping a short midweek contact for retrieval is the pattern that survives an exam term here, and it is worth setting up in October rather than improvising it in February when everyone is already behind.

sections.heading: What the drive actually costs, and who pays for it
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real service and plenty of Dubai families use it sensibly. The honest version of the comparison is about the drive rather than the teaching. A tutor coming to a Sobha Hartland address for an afternoon session commits roughly sixty to ninety minutes of unpaid travel around a sixty-minute lesson, and that time ends up in the hourly rate whether or not it appears on the invoice.

It also fixes the slot, which is the point that matters most in this community. Sobha Hartland's short school run creates a quarter-past-four window that genuinely works, but that window is only bookable if nobody has to reach the address by then. A travelling tutor's earliest Hartland offer is set by their previous booking, and the Al Khail Road and Ras Al Khor approaches between four and six o'clock are not a theoretical obstacle. The community's main scheduling advantage is therefore only realisable online.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. The rate bands below are market figures from providers' own published pages and a Dubai cost survey, with the source named for each row, so that a Hartland family can see where the travel component sits. They are not IB Gram's price list, and no figure here is presented as a quote.

Two questions separate a real quote from a headline rate, and both are worth asking any provider in this market. The first is whether the advertised figure is the all-in monthly number or an hourly rate before assessment fees, materials and a minimum booking period. The second is whether value added tax is included in what is shown. A third question is worth adding for in-home arrangements: what happens if the tutor cannot reach the address on a given afternoon, because the answer determines whether you have bought a schedule or an intention.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened school day and the post-Iftar slot
paragraphs: Ramadan rearranges the weekday for every Dubai family, and a tutoring schedule that ignores it loses four to five weeks at exactly the wrong point in the academic year. School hours shorten, which moves the end of the school day earlier and in principle opens a longer afternoon. In practice the afternoon is the hardest part of a fasting day, and the useful window moves to the evening after Iftar.

The pattern that works for Sobha Hartland families is agreed a fortnight in advance rather than negotiated week by week. For students who are fasting, a post-Iftar slot roughly ninety minutes after sunset is realistic, and a shorter session than usual is better than the standard length. For students who are not fasting, the shortened school day genuinely does open an earlier slot, and families with children in both categories end up running two different schedules in the same household.

The thing worth protecting is continuity rather than volume. A family that reduces from ninety minutes to sixty for four weeks loses very little. A family that cancels through Ramadan and restarts afterwards loses considerably more than the hours, because the tutor loses the thread of what the student had stopped understanding and the first session back is spent rebuilding it. For Year 11 and DP2 students the timing is particularly unforgiving, since Ramadan in the current cycle falls close to the mock and final preparation window.

Sobha Hartland has one small practical advantage during this period. With both schools inside the development, the shortened school day does not get eaten by a long drive home, so a non-fasting younger student can genuinely use the earlier afternoon rather than losing it to traffic. For older fasting students the post-Iftar slot is the only realistic one, which means a household with children in both categories runs two schedules for a month. Agreeing both in advance, in writing, is considerably easier than resolving it on a Tuesday evening.

sections.heading: The weeks when the schedule has to change
paragraphs: A standing weekly slot is the right default for about thirty weeks of the year. The other weeks need something different, and knowing which ones in advance is the difference between a plan and a hope. The table lists the predictable disruption points in a Sobha Hartland academic year and what the session should become in each one.

Board administration is the part families underestimate. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers: for the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026 and the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May 2027. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who missed a paper after using the wrong version.

For the IB, this page does not publish a session or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than no date on a page a family might plan around. Confirm the May session window with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. What is safe to say is that the internal deadlines for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are set by the school, fall well before the IB's upload dates, and are the deadlines that actually govern a Hartland autumn.

sections.heading: Two schools inside one community, and what that commits a student to
paragraphs: Having both schools inside Sobha Hartland is a scheduling advantage and an academic decision. Hartland International School runs the English National Curriculum with an IB and A Level sixth form, which means IGCSE at sixteen and a choice after it. North London Collegiate School Dubai runs the IB continuum, which means MYP through the middle years and the Diploma from Year 12 with no IGCSE stage at all. Those are genuinely different student experiences, and they produce different tutoring needs from neighbours on the same street.

The practical consequence for a parent is the assessment calendar. An IGCSE route has a hard external examination at sixteen with entry deadlines months ahead and tier decisions in Year 10. A continuum route has criterion-based internal assessment through the middle years, possibly MYP eAssessment in Year 11, then the Diploma's internal deadline structure. A family moving a child between the two routes mid-course, which happens in both directions here, is changing the assessment system rather than just the uniform.

All Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 pupils across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25 according to figures published by the Dubai Media Office, and seven new schools are opening for 2026-27 creating 16,846 places. If you want a school's current inspection rating, read it on the KHDA site rather than on any tutoring page.

sections.heading: Coursework deadlines belong to the school, not the board
paragraphs: This is the single most useful scheduling fact for a Diploma family in Sobha Hartland, and it is rarely stated clearly. The deadlines that govern your child's autumn are set by their own school's IB coordinator, not by the IB. Internal deadlines for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge components sit well before the board's upload dates, because teachers need time to mark, standardise and moderate. A family planning around a date they found online is usually planning around the wrong one.

The practical approach is to get the school's internal deadline list in September and book coursework sessions backwards from it. Three or four scheduled sessions timed against a draft deadline achieve more than a standing weekly slot that happens to touch the IA occasionally. The pattern that works is: one session to narrow the research question until it will generate usable data, one on method, one responding to a first draft the student has written, and one on the criteria the student is still not addressing.

The boundary on that work is firm. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, explain what a command term requires, teach the technique or statistics an investigation needs, read a draft the student has written and ask questions about it, and point out an unsupported argument. A tutor must not supply text, rewrite a passage into its final form, or take over in any way that makes the submitted piece not the student's own. IB Gram does not supply assessed work and declines requests framed that way, because submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: When the specialist you want is not free in the slot you want
paragraphs: No tutoring provider has full coverage of every subject at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are the ones that substitute a generalist and hope you do not notice until week three. The honest version is a disclosure table. The scarcest combinations are Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Maths Analysis and Approaches in the hour between five and seven o'clock Gulf Standard Time, which is also the hour most families want.

Sobha Hartland has a structural advantage here that is worth using. Because the school run is short, families in this community can take the quarter-past-four slot, which is considerably less contested than the five-to-seven block. A Hartland family willing to start at 4.15pm has access to specialists that a family across town physically cannot reach at that hour. That is a real benefit of the geography rather than a sales line.

Where a slot still cannot be filled, there are three honest options and we name them rather than improvising. The first is a different time, usually earlier or at the weekend. The second is a short wait for a slot to open, with a date given. The third is a tutor based outside the UAE working to the same named syllabus at a time that suits both sides, disclosed up front with any rate difference stated. What we will not do is place a student with someone who does not know the paper.

It is worth saying what the third option does and does not mean, because other providers in this market conceal it. A tutor outside the UAE teaching Cambridge 0580 or IB Chemistry HL is teaching the same syllabus from the same published guide, and the lesson is identical in format to one taught from Dubai. What changes is the time zone, which has to suit a school night in Sobha Hartland rather than only the tutor. We state the tutor's location before the first session rather than routing you to a number and leaving you to work it out.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a lesson can realistically start for a Sobha Hartland family?
faqs.answer: Around quarter past four for most addresses, which is roughly an hour earlier than the practical floor across much of Dubai. The reason is specific to this community: Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai are both inside the development, so the journey home is five to ten minutes rather than forty. Allow an hour between the school gate and the lesson for food and decompression. Families using schools in Nad Al Sheba or Al Jaddaf instead are back on a five o'clock earliest start, because the drive rather than the child is the constraint.

faqs.question: Should I book 60 minutes or 90 minutes?
faqs.answer: It depends on the job, not the budget. Sixty minutes repairs one topic per session and suits Years 7 to 11 in the early afternoon slot. Ninety minutes is for a full timed question set followed by a mark-scheme walkthrough, which is the only reliable way to improve exam technique and does not compress into an hour. Where the problem is forgetting between lessons, as it often is with organic chemistry mechanisms or Arabic vocabulary, two thirty-minute contacts in the same week beat either. Ask the tutor which your child's situation needs after the diagnostic session.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to homes in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do work in Dubai, at market rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour according to a 2026 Dubai cost survey and tutors' own published pages, with travel priced into that figure. The scheduling point matters here more than most places: Sobha Hartland's short school run creates a genuinely workable quarter-past-four slot, and that slot is only bookable if nobody has to drive across the city to reach it.

faqs.question: My child has sport after school three days a week. Where does a lesson fit?
faqs.answer: Either the one free weekday in the early window, or a weekend morning. A student who finished training at half past five is not going to absorb a ninety-minute Physics session at seven, and booking it anyway is paying for an hour that will not work. The pattern that holds through the year for sporting students in Sobha Hartland is one weekend morning block of ninety minutes plus one short midweek contact of thirty minutes for retrieval practice. That combination covers more ground than a single weeknight session they are too tired to use.

faqs.question: How should the schedule change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Agree the change two weeks before Ramadan begins rather than renegotiating weekly. School hours shorten, which opens an earlier afternoon for students who are not fasting. For students who are fasting, the afternoon is the hardest part of the day and the usable window moves to roughly ninety minutes after Iftar, with a shorter session than usual. Reduce the length rather than cancelling, particularly in a Year 11 or DP2 year: a family that stops for four weeks loses the thread of what the student had stopped understanding, not just the hours.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the year do I need to plan extra sessions for?
faqs.answer: Four are predictable. Late November, because Cambridge final entries for the March 2027 series close on 27 November 2026 and the tier decision has to be settled. January, for school mocks, where the session should follow the order the papers are actually sat. The exam window itself, which for the Cambridge March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. And the school's own internal coursework deadlines, which the IB coordinator sets and which fall well before any board upload date. Plan all four in September rather than discovering them.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the two schools inside Sobha Hartland for tutoring purposes?
faqs.answer: A substantial one. Hartland International School runs the English National Curriculum with an IB and A Level sixth form, so students sit external IGCSE examinations at sixteen with board entry deadlines and Core or Extended tier decisions in Year 10. North London Collegiate School Dubai runs the IB continuum, so there is no IGCSE stage at all; assessment through the middle years is criterion-based, possibly including MYP eAssessment in Year 11, and the Diploma starts in Year 12. The diagnostic session asks completely different questions depending on which route your child is on.

faqs.question: Can a lesson run while I am still commuting home from Business Bay?
faqs.answer: For most secondary students, yes, and in Sobha Hartland that is the usual arrangement. The quarter-past-four window exists precisely because the child is home long before the parent is. Sessions run on a shared screen with worked solutions saved afterwards, so you can see what was covered without having been present. For younger children, and for any student in the first fortnight with a new tutor, it is worth being within earshot, which usually means choosing the half past six slot instead for those weeks.

faqs.question: Is a thirty-minute session ever worth booking?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a narrow set of jobs. Thirty minutes works for retrieval practice, formula recall, Arabic vocabulary and script fluency, and for checking one specific misunderstanding that has been identified. Two of those in a week is often better value than a single hour, because the problem being solved is the forgetting curve rather than a lack of explanation. It does not work for anything that requires building an extended argument, which rules it out for Economics commentary work, Extended Essay sessions and English written responses.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board my child's school entered?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry is the authority, not the school website. Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics; Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. The papers, the tiering and the question style differ, so past papers from the wrong board are not useful practice. Confirm the code before the first paid session. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, since it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong one.

faqs.question: My DP2 son has three Internal Assessments due in the same fortnight. What should we book?
faqs.answer: Deadline-timed sessions rather than the standing weekly slot. Get the school's internal deadline list from the IB coordinator, then book backwards: one session to narrow each research question until it will produce usable data, one on method, and one responding to a draft he has written. The tutor teaches the criteria and their mark allocations and asks hard questions about the draft. The tutor does not supply text or finish the work. IB Gram declines requests framed that way, because submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules.

faqs.question: What happens if the Higher Level tutor we want has no slot between five and seven?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you three real options rather than substituting a generalist. The first is the earlier window, which Sobha Hartland families can usually take and which is far less contested. The second is a dated wait for a slot to open. The third is a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same named syllabus at a time that suits both sides, disclosed up front with any rate difference stated. Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Maths Analysis and Approaches are the scarcest combinations in that hour, so this comes up regularly and is better handled openly.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a student who needs someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For some younger students it is genuinely harder, and saying otherwise would be dishonest. The format that works for a child who will not stay on task alone is a shorter session, more often, with a parent within earshot for the first few weeks, rather than a long block on a school night. From Year 10 upwards most students work well on a shared screen and many prefer having worked solutions saved to revisit. The test is the first session: watch the opening forty minutes before committing to a term.

faqs.question: How much should a Sobha Hartland family budget for one subject through an exam year?
faqs.answer: Published market figures give you the range. A 2026 Dubai cost survey puts weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 for a qualified subject tutor and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages seen in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Budget for the step up to twice weekly from January in a Year 11 or DP2 year, because that increase is predictable and most families do not plan for it.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover two subjects to save a slot?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and usually it is a false economy. A tutor genuinely strong in both Maths AA HL and Physics HL exists but is rare, and a generalist covering both tends to teach the easier one well and the harder one adequately. Because nobody is travelling between appointments, running two separate specialists in the same evening is straightforward: quarter past four and half past five on the same weekday is a common Sobha Hartland pattern. The slot is not the scarce resource here; the subject specialist in that slot is.

dubai/sobha-hartland.closingHeading: Settle the slot first, and the rest follows
dubai/sobha-hartland.closingBody: If your child is at one of the two schools inside Sobha Hartland, you have a scheduling option most Dubai families do not: a lesson that starts before the afternoon is gone. Tell us the school gate time, whether a parent needs to be home, and what has actually gone wrong in the subject. We confirm the board and syllabus code, recommend a session length against the job rather than the budget, and set a weekday slot with the predictable disruption weeks already planned in. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video, so the slot belongs to your child's day rather than to a tutor's route across the city.

intro.heading: The TECOM household: two offices, one bus, and an afternoon nobody is home for
paragraphs: TECOM, known on most maps as Barsha Heights, is a dense cluster of residential and commercial towers wedged between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, next door to Dubai Internet City, Dubai Media City and Knowledge Park. It has a Red Line metro station at its edge and almost no villa stock. What it has instead is a very particular household type: two working parents, apartment living, and children who travel out to school by bus because there is no campus inside the district.

That combination produces an afternoon that no tutoring advice written for a villa community addresses. The children arrive back in the early to mid afternoon, often before either parent finishes work. Supervision for those hours is frequently a nanny, a grandparent on a long visit, or an older sibling. The adult who will read the school report is not the adult present when the homework happens, and the gap between those two people is where academic problems grow quietly for a term.

The second feature of this district is time pressure of a different kind from the coastal communities. Evenings are not committed to swimming and tennis; they are committed to work that followed a parent home, to calls with other time zones, and to a commute that is short in distance and unpredictable in practice because Sheikh Zayed Road and the Al Barsha interchanges do what they do at 18:00. A 19:30 session is easy to hold here. A 17:00 one is not, because nobody is yet available to set it up.

The third is that TECOM parents buy tutoring the way they buy other professional services, and they have the right instincts about it. They want to know who the tutor works for, what happens if the tutor disappears, whether the person is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE, and what they will receive in writing. Almost nothing in this market answers those questions. Competitor pages compare themselves to an unnamed set of other platforms and publish no rates at all in three cases out of six.

So this page is built as a buyer's guide rather than a neighbourhood description. It compares the provider models that exist in Dubai, with AED bands attributed to whoever published them. It sets out the permit position under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and how a parent can check it. It lists the questions worth asking before paying anyone, with the answers that should worry you. And it explains how reporting works when the person paying was not in the room.

Delivery is one-to-one tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For an apartment household where the afternoon supervisor is not the decision-maker, online delivery has a specific practical benefit: the session is scheduled at the hour a parent chooses, it produces a written record, and nobody has to be let into the building.

dubai/tecom.programmesIntro: The programme a child is in determines how much of the week has to be supervised rather than simply scheduled, which is the relevant question in a household where both parents work.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Nine or ten examined subjects with a two-year run-up. Year 11 is where unsupervised afternoons show up in results, because the independent revision that decides IGCSE outcomes is invisible: a student can appear to be working for six months and produce almost nothing retainable without anyone noticing.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and states the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer at the Al Barsha or Al Sufouh school for the centre's own timetable rather than a generic one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with a substantial share of the grade sitting in work the student manages themselves across two years. For a household where nobody is home in the afternoon, the coursework calendar needs an external check rather than a parental one.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, so the pressure point runs from November to February when internal coursework deadlines collide with mock examinations. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator; the IB is the only authoritative source for its own calendar and second-hand dates circulate incorrectly.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, reported as a 1-7 grade. MYP students have a genuine workload and not yet the self-management to protect time for it, which makes them the group most dependent on an external appointment in a household with unsupervised afternoons.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 includes the Personal Project, an extended self-managed piece. In a working-parent household this is the component most likely to be discovered late, because the school's internal deadlines are communicated to the student and the student is the one managing them.

programmes.name: Key Stage 1-2 and the Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Reading fluency and number facts are the things that matter at this stage, and both are built by short daily practice rather than by teaching. The practical question in an apartment household is who does that practice with the child, and the answer is often someone who cannot assess whether it is working.
programmes.countryNote: TECOM primary children bus out to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh campuses and are typically home by early afternoon, which makes this the one age group here with a genuinely available late-afternoon slot. A 16:00 session with a nanny present to settle the child is often the most productive hour of the day.

dubai/tecom.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects TECOM households request most. Each note says what a parent who was not present should look for in the session record.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Progress is visible in the record: the notes should name topics and error types, not say that the student worked hard. Tier matters, since Core or Foundation caps the grade, so the first session should confirm which tier the school entered.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Expect notes about specific techniques and specific unseen-problem behaviour, because this course rewards fluency under unfamiliar conditions. Higher Level Paper 3 needs its own block of practice and should appear in the plan by name.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with marks for interpretation in context. The record should show whether the student is producing results and failing to interpret them, which is the usual loss pattern and a different fix from more content.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Loss points are specific and visible on paper: units, significant figures and explanation questions wanting a mechanism. A session note that names the question numbers from the student's own script is doing its job.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry decide the grade. For Diploma students the investigation needs its research question narrowed early, and an unsupervised household should expect that flagged in writing rather than mentioned verbally.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Content-heavy and therefore vulnerable to revision that feels productive and leaves nothing behind. The useful record here shows retrieval practice results over time, not topics covered.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE First Language English
subjects.description: Writing subjects need drafts produced between sessions, which is exactly what goes undone in an unsupervised afternoon. A good arrangement sets a specific piece of writing each week and the notes say whether it arrived.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Essay and case-study technique responds quickly to correction. Expect the record to show diagram accuracy and whether a judgement sentence is being written, since those two things carry the top band.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Popular in this district, with a developed-solution internal assessment at Diploma level that demands sustained project work. The documentation, not the coding, is where most marks are lost, and it needs scheduling.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs. For non-Arab families nobody at home can check the homework, which is why these subjects drift in a working household.

sections.heading: Who supervises what, when both parents are at a desk
paragraphs: The practical question in this district is not when a child could theoretically study. It is who is with them, and what that person can realistically do. A nanny can make sure a child sits down and does not watch television; a nanny usually cannot tell whether twenty minutes of mathematics produced anything, and should not be asked to. An older sibling is worse than nothing for this purpose, because the arrangement generates conflict rather than work.

The result is a supervision gap that runs from early afternoon until a parent gets home, which in TECOM is frequently 18:30 or later once the Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Barsha interchange traffic has done its work. During that gap a child either has a structured externally scheduled activity, or has unstructured time that produces very little. For younger children the gap is the best hours of their day, which is why it is worth filling deliberately.

The table below sets out the hours and what each can carry. The useful distinction is the final column: which activities genuinely need a parent and which only need an adult in the building. Most tutoring needs the latter, provided the session produces a written record afterwards, which is the mechanism that replaces the parent's presence.

One habit worth adopting in a household like this: ask the school to copy both parents into every communication, and ask the tutor to send the session note to both rather than to the one who booked. A surprising share of academic problems in two-office households persist because the information reached one parent during a working day and did not survive the evening.

sections.heading: Provider models in Dubai, compared without a straw man
paragraphs: Every competitor page in this market compares itself to an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a buyer nothing. A more useful comparison is between the models that actually exist, because each has a genuine structural advantage and a genuine structural weakness, and the right choice depends on what a household needs rather than on which brand is loudest.

The rates below are market bands with their publishers named. Market pricing in Dubai runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits including travel; AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270; and AED 500 to 650 or more for premium named tutors, with BartyED at AED 650.

Three structural points are worth more than the prices. First, who employs the tutor determines what happens when things go wrong: an independent freelance arrangement has no substitution path, while a matched or agency arrangement should. Second, in-home rates include travel, so a comparison that ignores the journey is not a comparison. Third, group rates look cheaper per billed hour and add the parent's own two journeys per session, which in a two-office household is the scarcest resource there is.

IB Gram's position in that table is specific and worth stating plainly: a tutor-matching platform delivering one-to-one online lessons, with no in-home service anywhere in the UAE, no published fixed price list because the rate depends on subject and level, and a free trial session before any commitment. Home visits exist only through our India service.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question a TECOM parent asks and almost nothing in this market answers. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated completion time of two working days.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. That matters because a fee is one of the things people invent about this process; there is not one, and any provider quoting a permit cost should be asked where the figure comes from. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

The enforcement position is also published, within limits. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published. A figure circulating in press coverage could not be verified against an official source, so this page quotes no amount, and you should discount any page that does.

One further distinction is important. An individual tutor and a tutoring operation with premises and staff are different legal animals. A training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, renewed annually with the request made at least thirty days before expiry. That permit applies to premises-based institutes. IB Gram does not hold it, does not operate premises in the UAE, and nobody should describe themselves as endorsed by KHDA on the strength of anything else.

sections.heading: What to ask before you pay, and the answers that should worry you
paragraphs: Parents in this district are generally good at due diligence in their working lives and oddly reluctant to apply it here, partly because the market trades on reassurance. The questions below take ten minutes and eliminate most of the bad outcomes. None of them is about qualifications, because qualifications are the one thing every provider will volunteer.

The most revealing question is about replacement. If the tutor is unwell for a fortnight, leaves the country, or simply stops answering, what happens? An answer involving a named process and handed-over session notes is a working arrangement. An answer that amounts to hoping it does not happen is a single point of failure, and in a two-office household that failure arrives as three weeks of nothing before anyone notices.

The second is about the academic-honesty boundary, and the answer should be immediate and specific. A tutor who says they will help with the internal assessment should be asked what exactly they will do and what the student will do. Any version that involves producing, completing or writing the work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. One provider ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price. That is what the question is screening for.

The third is about evidence. Ask what you will receive after each session and ask to see an example. A note that says the student worked well on quadratics is decoration. A note that names the question numbers attempted, the error types corrected and the specific work set for the week is a document a parent who was not in the room can act on.

sections.heading: Reporting to a parent who was not in the room
paragraphs: In a villa household where a parent is present, the session report is partly ambient: you hear what happened. In a tower household where both parents are at work, the written record is the only information that exists, and its quality determines whether the arrangement can be managed at all. This is the single most under-specified part of buying tutoring, and it is worth being demanding about.

A useful session note has four parts. What was worked on, named specifically enough to be checked against the school's scheme of work. What the student got wrong, by error type rather than by sentiment. What was set for the week, in a form the student and the afternoon supervisor can both read. And what the tutor would like the parent to know, which is where a drifting coursework deadline or a tier problem should appear in writing rather than being mentioned and forgotten.

What that enables is the thing busy parents actually want: ten minutes a week of real oversight instead of an hour of vague worry. Reading four notes in a month tells you whether the same error type keeps reappearing, whether the set work is being done, and whether the arrangement is converging on something. If three consecutive notes say the same thing, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan needs changing rather than extending.

It also protects the student. When a parent can see that the independent work is not happening, the conversation becomes about scheduling rather than about effort, which is both more accurate and considerably less damaging. In this district the independent work is the part most likely to be missing, because the hours it should occupy are unsupervised by anyone who can tell.
bullets: Topics named specifically enough to check against the school's scheme of work
Errors described by type, not by how hard the student tried
Set work written down for both the student and the afternoon supervisor
Anything a parent must decide flagged in writing, not mentioned in passing

sections.heading: Short-notice life: exam terms, business travel and the handover
paragraphs: Two-office households run on short notice, and the tutoring arrangement has to survive it. A parent travels for a week with a different time zone and the usual oversight disappears. An exam term arrives and three extra sessions are needed quickly. A nanny goes on leave for a month and the afternoon structure collapses. None of these is unusual; all of them break arrangements that assumed stability.

Online delivery handles the first two straightforwardly. A session can move to a different evening without anyone losing a journey, and extra sessions can be added at hours an in-home tutor's route could not absorb. For a travelling parent the written notes continue arriving regardless of where they are, which is more useful than a phone call that gets missed across time zones.

The third needs planning rather than flexibility. When afternoon supervision changes, the structured parts of the week should be moved into hours when someone reliable is present, even if those hours are less academically ideal. A 19:30 session with a parent home is better than a 16:00 session nobody starts. For primary children, where the good hours are the unsupervised ones, this sometimes means accepting a shorter weekend-morning arrangement for the month.

The one thing worth resisting is the exam-term reflex to add sessions sharply in the final fortnight. At that point the student needs timed past papers, technique and sleep, and extra hours of teaching buy reassurance rather than marks. If more support is genuinely needed, the right time to add it was January.

sections.heading: What the Al Barsha bus run does to the usable hours
paragraphs: TECOM has no school campus, so every child here travels. The two directions are inland to Al Barsha and Al Barsha South, where the American School of Dubai, GEMS Dubai American Academy, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Kings' School Al Barsha, Repton Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai sit, or coastward to Al Sufouh for Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School. Some families go further inland to Regent International School in The Greens or across Al Khail to the Emirates Hills and Meadows campuses.

The journeys themselves are short. What is not short is the bus route, which collects across several towers and interchanges, so a child leaving campus at 15:10 can be home closer to 16:15. That is still early by Dubai standards and it is why this district genuinely has usable late-afternoon hours for primary children, unlike the villa communities further out where the bus arrives at 16:45 and an activity follows.

The afternoon constraint here is not the child's availability but the adult's. Both parents are typically at desks until 17:30 or 18:00, and the Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Barsha interchange traffic adds thirty to forty minutes to a journey that is nominally ten. The practical consequence is a two-tier schedule: primary children use the early hours with a nanny present, and secondary students use the post-19:00 hours when a parent is home.

Metro access changes the picture for older students specifically. A Year 11 or Diploma student who can use the Red Line from Dubai Internet City station has independent mobility that a villa-community peer does not, which is worth remembering when planning anything that needs the student to be somewhere. For online sessions it is irrelevant, which is part of the appeal.

sections.heading: Getting started from TECOM, with the limits stated
paragraphs: Start with four things: the examination board and syllabus code for each subject, the most recent mock mark with its mark scheme if the school released one, the school's internal coursework deadlines, and an honest account of who is home in the afternoon. The last one is the item most families leave out and the one that determines whether the plan survives a term.

Then a trial session with the named tutor who would hold the slot, at the hour the slot would actually run, with whoever supervises the afternoon briefed to settle the student at the start. The trial exists to test the working relationship and the setup, not the subject knowledge. If the fit is wrong we rematch rather than persuading anyone to continue.

The limits, said in advance. Specialist cover is not uniform: mainstream subjects are matched quickly, while a niche Diploma option or a narrow internal assessment specialism may take longer, and the right person may sit in a time zone that makes a particular Dubai hour awkward. We disclose that rather than placing a generalist. We publish no fixed price list, because the rate depends on subject, level and tutor. And we are not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring provider in this market holds a regulator's endorsement of its teaching.

Finally, one thing we will state as a boundary rather than a feature. Tutors explain assessment criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not produce content for an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project, and they do not distribute awarding-body syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. Those are referenced and linked to the official source. The reason is that the consequence of crossing that line falls on the student.
