process.title: Establish the subject facts and the household facts
process.description: Board and syllabus code for each subject, the last mock mark with its mark scheme, the school's internal coursework deadlines, and who is actually home in the afternoon. The household half of that list is the part most families omit and the part that decides whether a schedule holds.

process.title: Choose the tier of the week deliberately
process.description: Primary and lower-secondary sessions go in the early afternoon while a nanny or grandparent is present to settle the student. Secondary and Diploma sessions go after 19:00 when a parent is home and the student can start independently. Mixing those two up is the commonest scheduling error here.

process.title: Trial at the real hour, with the real supervisor
process.description: One session with the named tutor at the time the slot would run, with whoever looks after the afternoon briefed to be present for the first and last two minutes. This tests the setup, the room and the working relationship rather than the credentials.

process.title: Agree what arrives in writing
process.description: Session notes after every lesson, naming what was covered, the error types corrected, the work set for the week and anything a parent needs to decide. Both parents are copied by default, because in a two-office household information that reaches one person during the working day often does not survive the evening.

process.title: Review on a date, not on a feeling
process.description: Each block carries a named target and a fixed review date. If three consecutive session notes report the same error type, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes rather than extending. When the student can do the thing unaided, the booking steps down or closes.

whyPoints.title: Written records designed for an absent parent
whyPoints.description: Every session produces notes naming the topics, the error types corrected and the work set, sent to both parents. In a household where nobody was in the room, the record is the only information that exists, and its quality decides whether the arrangement can be managed at all.

whyPoints.title: A comparison table rather than a straw man
whyPoints.description: This page sets out the provider models that exist in Dubai with AED bands attributed to whoever published them, including where our own model sits and what it does not offer. Competitor pages compare themselves to unnamed other platforms, and three of six publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: The permit position, sourced and unspun
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit comes from Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is free for two years, and covers specific eligible categories. Those tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule. We publish no fine figure because none is official.

whyPoints.title: A replacement path that exists before it is needed
whyPoints.description: If a tutor becomes unavailable, a specialist from the same area is matched and the session notes are handed over so the new tutor starts where the last one stopped. An independent arrangement has no substitution path, and in a two-office household its absence shows up as weeks of nothing.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that follows the adults, not the ideal
whyPoints.description: The best academic hours for a primary child in TECOM are the ones no parent is home for, and the best hours for a Diploma student are after 19:00. We build around that two-tier reality rather than recommending a single time that suits nobody here.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on coursework, written down
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not produce content for an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project, and they do not distribute awarding-body material. A provider in this market sells completed coursework; the risk of that falls on the student.

faqs.question: Which schools do TECOM and Barsha Heights children usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no school campus inside TECOM, so children travel in one of two directions. Inland to Al Barsha and Al Barsha South for the American School of Dubai, GEMS Dubai American Academy, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Kings' School Al Barsha, Repton Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. Or coastward to Al Sufouh for Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School. Some families go to Regent International School in The Greens or across Al Khail to the Emirates Hills and Meadows campuses. The journeys are short; the bus routes are not.

faqs.question: Both of us work until 18:00. Can tutoring happen without a parent present?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for primary children it generally should, because the best concentration hours in this district fall in the early afternoon when no parent is home. What replaces the parent is a written record: notes after every session naming what was covered, the error types corrected and the work set. An adult in the building helps for the first and last two minutes of a younger child's session, to settle them and hand over, but they do not need to understand the subject and should not be asked to assess the work.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and is there a fee?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and there is no fee. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Anyone quoting a permit cost should be asked for their source.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for tutoring without a permit in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published by the ministry, and a figure circulating in press coverage could not be verified against an official source, so this page quotes no amount. Treat any website that publishes a specific figure with scepticism and check the official channel instead. The relevant point for a parent is simpler: ask whether the tutor holds the permit, and ask to see it.

faqs.question: How do an agency, a marketplace and a freelance tutor actually differ?
faqs.answer: They differ in who the tutor answers to, which decides what happens when something goes wrong. An agency vets and places tutors and should supply a replacement from its roster. A marketplace lists sellers and leaves you to search again if a tutor stops. An independent freelance tutor answers to themselves and has no substitution path, so a fortnight's absence is usually a fortnight of nothing. Rates also differ: market bands run roughly AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor and AED 180 to 500 in-home with travel included.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre better value for a working household?
faqs.answer: Per billed hour it looks cheaper, with two to four students sharing the time. Per hour of a working parent's time it rarely is, because it adds two journeys per session into Al Barsha or Al Quoz traffic and fixes the timing to the centre's timetable. Group teaching also cannot work from your child's own marked script, which is where the specific losses are visible. For core content at a modest level it can be reasonable; for diagnosing why a Year 11 student loses marks on a particular paper, it is the wrong instrument.

faqs.question: What should a session note actually contain?
faqs.answer: Four things. The topics covered, named specifically enough to check against the school's scheme of work rather than described generally. The errors corrected, described by type instead of by how hard the student tried. The work set for the week, written so both the student and the afternoon supervisor can read it. And anything the parent needs to decide, such as a drifting coursework deadline or a tier problem, flagged in writing rather than mentioned in passing. Ask to see a sample note before you pay anyone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our apartment in Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. In a tower household the practical benefits are specific: nobody has to be let into the building, the session happens at the hour you choose rather than the hour a tutor's route allows, and a written record arrives afterwards for the parent who was at work.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor stops being available halfway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: A replacement is matched from the same specialism and the session notes are handed over, so the new tutor starts from where the previous one stopped rather than from the beginning. This is worth asking about before you book, because it is the scenario most likely to cost a term. An independent arrangement typically has no answer to it: there is rarely a like-for-like substitute who is also free at your hour, and in a household where nobody is home in the afternoon, several weeks can pass before the gap is noticed.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by KHDA or the IB?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutoring provider in this market holds a regulator's or awarding body's endorsement of its teaching. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that operate premises with staff; that is a specific permit for a specific kind of business, and we do not hold it or operate premises in the UAE. We explain what each body does and link to it. Any provider describing its tutors as approved by a regulator or board is making a claim worth checking.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do on an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Explain what each criterion rewards and in what language, question whether a research question can be investigated with the time and equipment available, review a draft the student has written and say where the evidence does not support the claim, and point out where a paragraph asserts rather than demonstrates. The student then rewrites it. What a tutor must never do is produce content, rewrite a draft into finished prose or hand over a model for adaptation. If the tutor's words would appear in the submission, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: We travel for work regularly. Does the arrangement survive that?
faqs.answer: It should, and online delivery is why. A session can move to a different evening without anyone losing a journey, extra sessions can be added at hours a travelling tutor's route could not absorb, and the written notes keep arriving wherever the parent is, which works better across time zones than a phone call that gets missed. What needs planning rather than flexibility is a change in afternoon supervision: when a nanny is on leave, move the structured work into hours when a reliable adult is present, even if they are less ideal academically.

faqs.question: Should we add extra sessions in the last two weeks before exams?
faqs.answer: Usually not. At that point a student needs timed past papers, component technique and sleep, and extra hours of teaching buy reassurance rather than marks. New content taught in the final fortnight rarely survives into the examination hall. If more support is genuinely needed, the time to add it was January, when mock results were available and there was still room to absorb corrections. Light maintenance, one session a week on technique, plus a protected sleep schedule, outperforms an intensive sprint for almost every student.

faqs.question: Our nanny supervises homework. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a limitation rather than a problem, and it is worth being clear about which. A nanny can ensure a child sits down, keeps to a start time and does not drift to a screen, and that is genuinely valuable. What a nanny cannot do is judge whether twenty minutes of mathematics produced anything retainable, and asking them to do so is unfair to everyone. The fix is to make the set work explicit in writing so it can be followed exactly, and to have the assessment done by the tutor in the session.

faqs.question: How do we know when to stop paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Set the exit at the start. Every block should carry a named target, which might be a component, a tier decision or a specific skill, and a fixed review date. The test at that date is simple: can the student do, unaided, the thing they could not do at the beginning. If yes, the booking should close or drop to monthly maintenance. If three consecutive session notes report the same error type, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan needs changing rather than extending. Open-ended weekly bookings nobody reviews are the biggest waste in this market.

dubai/tecom.closingHeading: Buy it the way you buy anything else
dubai/tecom.closingBody: If you are hiring from a TECOM address, treat it as a procurement decision rather than a leap of faith. Ask which syllabus code the tutor will teach and how they will confirm it. Ask what happens if they are unavailable for a fortnight. Ask exactly what they will do on coursework and what your child will do. Ask to see a sample session note. Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit. Those five questions take ten minutes and eliminate most bad outcomes. Lessons here run online, one-to-one, over live video, with a written record after each one.

dubai/the-greens.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here cover both IGCSE boards and the IB Diploma at the levels The Greens asks for. A match is made against a syllabus code and a component, not against a subject name, because 0625 Paper 6 and 4PH1 Paper 2 are not the same lesson.

intro.heading: Who lives in The Greens, and what a flat does to the study week
paragraphs: The Greens is apartments. Al Arta, Al Dhafra, Al Ghozlan, Al Jaz, Al Nakheel, Al Samar, Al Sidir and Al Thayyal are low-rise clusters of one, two and three-bedroom units around shared pools and lawns. That architecture changes the tutoring conversation in a way nobody writing about Dubai neighbourhoods seems to notice. A three-bedroom villa has a spare room; a two-bedroom flat with two children has a dining table, and the dining table is also where dinner happens at seven.

The people here are mostly professionals working a short drive away in Barsha Heights, Dubai Internet City, Media City or along Sheikh Zayed Road. Commutes are short by Dubai standards, which means a parent is often home by six and able to supervise an evening session in a way a parent driving back from Jebel Ali is not. It also means households are smaller - one or two children is typical rather than three - so the family is usually buying one or two matches, not three.

Schooling is the unusual part. Regent International School sits inside The Greens, which is rare: most Dubai communities have no school at all. Families with a child there have a five-minute walk and a British route through Cambridge IGCSE. Everyone else drives, mainly to Emirates International School Meadows for the IB continuum, Dubai British School Emirates Hills, or across into Al Barsha for GEMS Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha and the American School of Dubai.

Having a school inside the community produces a specific and underrated problem: the social default. When most children in a cluster attend the same school, parents compare notes constantly, and tutoring recommendations circulate on a building WhatsApp group. That works beautifully for a shared syllabus and fails completely the moment a family's child is on a different board. A tutor who is genuinely strong on Cambridge 0580 Extended is not automatically useful for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher, and the WhatsApp group has no way of knowing that.

The last constraint is noise and space, and it is the one that makes online delivery practical rather than merely cheaper. A session delivered over live video needs a laptop, headphones and a corner - not a quiet room for a visitor, a parking space, and an hour of somebody else's travel. Two children in a two-bedroom flat can take sessions at 4.15pm and 5.30pm from the same table with headphones on, and the household loses no space at all. A tutor physically in the flat makes that impossible. Visitor parking in these clusters is contested at precisely the hours tuition happens, between four and seven in the afternoon, which is a small detail that quietly decides whether a weekly arrangement survives past October.

Put those four facts together and the shape of the useful week becomes obvious. Short sessions rather than long ones below Year 9, because the table is shared and attention is the limit. A board-specific match rather than a well-reviewed generalist, because the building holds two boards. A later slot than a villa community would use, because the parent is home early and the child is home late. And a plan that counts backwards from an entry deadline, because in a community this well connected the information that circulates is reputation rather than dates.

dubai/the-greens.programmesIntro: Four routes run through The Greens, and the boundary that matters is not IB against British - it is which examining board sets the paper. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both award an International GCSE and they assess differently enough that the preparation is not interchangeable.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, and the tier caps the attainable grade. Mathematics 0580 runs Papers 1 and 3 at Core or Papers 2 and 4 at Extended. Sciences carry a practical component: Physics 0625 offers either a practical test paper or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and schools choose. Exams run in a June series and a November series, with some centres also entering candidates for a March series.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the organisation states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A Greens parent should take the timetable from their own school rather than from a friend at a different school, because the zone may differ.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson runs a single tier in most subjects, with Mathematics A offered at Foundation and Higher. Codes are different again: 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology, 4EA1 for English Language A. Science practical skills are assessed within the written papers rather than by a separate practical test. Some subjects allow modular entry, which lets a candidate bank a unit before the final series.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live PDF is the only version worth planning against.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the extended essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Higher Level adds a further written paper and additional syllabus depth. Dubai schools sit the May session, and the internal deadlines a school sets for coursework fall months earlier.
programmes.countryNote: The Greens sends Diploma students mainly to Emirates International School Meadows and across to GEMS Dubai American Academy. Apartment households find the extended essay the hardest component to support at home, because 4,000 words of independent research needs a desk and a routine, and neither is automatic in a flat where the table is shared.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria lettered A to D with achievement levels from 1 to 8. No external examination is required until the optional MYP 5 eAssessment. Reports show criterion achievement rather than percentages, and students are credited for investigation, communication and reflection as much as for the right answer. A pupil who can solve a problem but cannot document the method loses marks that are fully recoverable.
programmes.countryNote: Parents in The Greens who have an older child on the Cambridge route and a younger one in the Middle Years Programme get two reports written in two different languages. A criterion C level 5 is not 62%, and treating it as a percentage is the most common misreading in this community. Learning to read the descriptors is usually the first job a tutor does.

dubai/the-greens.subjectsIntro: Requests out of The Greens lean towards the IGCSE core - maths, the three sciences and English - with Business Management, Computer Science and the languages close behind. What follows is what each paper actually demands.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry and statistics. Cambridge Extended runs Papers 2 and 4; Pearson Higher runs Papers 1H and 2H with a different balance of structured questions. Marks go missing in method not shown, premature rounding, and bearings and transformations - three topics almost every Year 11 can be taught to secure in a fortnight.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics, magnetism and radioactivity. Cambridge adds a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper; Pearson examines practical skills inside the theory papers. The recurring failure is unit handling and the refusal to draw the diagram the question implies.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, rates, electrolysis and organic chemistry. Moles work carries disproportionate marks and is where a weak Year 10 becomes a struggling Year 11. Equation balancing and state symbols are low-hanging marks that students drop through habit rather than misunderstanding.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Cells, transport, nutrition, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. The subject looks like recall and is marked on precision: a question asking students to explain and receiving a description earns part marks. Graph and data questions on unfamiliar experiments reward practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, directed writing and composition, with a separate coursework option at some centres. Students lose marks by paraphrasing rather than analysing, and by writing to a length instead of to a purpose. The directed-writing task is the most coachable component on the paper.

subjects.name: Business Management and IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Organisational structure, finance, marketing, operations and human resources. Case-study papers reward students who treat the pre-released material as a dataset rather than as reading. Calculation questions - break-even, ratios, cash flow - are the reliable marks and the ones most often rushed.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithms, data representation, hardware, networks and programming, with an internally assessed solution at Diploma level. Students who can code often lose marks on written theory, particularly on trace tables and on explaining complexity in words. Pseudocode conventions differ by board and must be learned from the right specification.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Markets, macroeconomic objectives, international trade and development, with diagrams carrying marks independently. The internally assessed commentaries ask for a named theory applied to a published article; summarising the article is the standard error. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a policy paper.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Reading, listening, writing and two oral components, assessed across five themes. Progress here is a function of contact time rather than cleverness, and short frequent sessions beat long infrequent ones. The individual oral needs a stimulus discussed in the target language, which is practice rather than content.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools for non-Arab students in a scaffolded form. Support is ordinary language teaching - vocabulary, script, listening and spoken practice - and is best booked as weekly conversational and written work rather than as exam coaching, because the subject is assessed continuously in most schools.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word supervised research essay plus a Theory of Knowledge exhibition and prescribed-title essay. Support is process coaching: narrowing a question, testing whether sources exist, building a timeline against the school's internal deadlines. The written work stays entirely the student's own throughout.

dubai/the-greens.regionsTitle: The Greens and the rest of New Dubai
dubai/the-greens.regionsIntro: The Greens is ringed by communities with quite different school patterns, and a family's carpool usually crosses two or three of them. The notes below are about how each one changes a tutoring timetable rather than about property.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Immediately adjacent, taller buildings, and overlooking Emirates Golf Club. Shares Regent International School as a walk-to option, so the two communities often share carpools and therefore share the problem of a 3.30pm pickup.

regions.name: Barsha Heights
regions.note: Minutes away and where many Greens parents work. The short commute is why evening sessions here can start at 6.30pm with a parent present, which is unusual in Dubai and worth using.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: The main secondary destination: GEMS Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha and the American School of Dubai. The drive back at 3.15pm is the reason a 4.00pm slot often fails.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Villas across Sheikh Zayed Road, holding Emirates International School Meadows and its full IB continuum. Most Diploma enquiries from The Greens concern that school's internal assessment calendar.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: Townhouses with a younger demographic and a heavy British-curriculum flow into Dubai British School Emirates Hills. Primary and lower-secondary requests dominate there.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: A longer drive but a shared social circle, and a community that runs later evenings. Several Greens families hold weekend blocks alongside Marina friends because the timing suits both.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lake Towers
regions.note: Office towers and apartments on the other side of Sheikh Zayed Road. Families crossing in both directions for school and work make the interchange the single biggest variable in an afternoon.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School sit here. Greens families with a child at either are commuting past Mall of the Emirates twice a day, which removes the early slot from the week entirely.

schoolClusters.city: Inside The Greens and The Views
schoolClusters.note: The walk-to option, and the reason this community compares notes so efficiently. A British route through Cambridge IGCSE into A Level, with a large share of the cluster's children in the same year groups at the same time.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, five to twelve minutes outside peak. Between them these schools cover the IB continuum and the British route, which is why two Greens neighbours can be sitting different boards in the same subject in the same term.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Barsha Heights and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: The secondary ring, and where most Greens children in Years 10 to 13 are enrolled. The commute is 20 to 35 minutes at school-run time, which pushes the earliest workable session to around 5.00pm on a school night.

dubai/the-greens.modesIntro: Three formats are used from The Greens, and the choice follows the apartment rather than the subject: how much space there is, who is home, and how late the evening can run.

modes.title: Short twice-weekly sessions
modes.description: Two 45-minute sessions a week rather than one long one, which suits younger students and suits a shared dining table. Shorter sessions also fit the gap between the school run and dinner without displacing either, and they produce more frequent contact, which matters more than session length for languages and for number fluency. Work is set between the two and marked before the next.

A Cambridge 0620 candidate and a Pearson 4CH1 candidate get different tutors and different plans. The slot is held through the year, including mock fortnight, because a marked mock script is the best teaching material a tutor ever gets.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: why the same subject is two different exams
paragraphs: A Greens parent will eventually be told, on a building WhatsApp group, that a particular tutor is excellent for IGCSE Physics. The question that should follow is: which Physics? Cambridge 0625 and Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 cover similar content and assess it through different papers, in different structures, against different mark schemes. A tutor fluent in one is not automatically fluent in the other, and the first thing a family should establish is which one their child's school entered them for.

The differences are concrete. Cambridge tiers Mathematics 0580 into Core and Extended, and the tier sets a ceiling on the grade available; Pearson's Mathematics A 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher. Cambridge sciences carry a practical component that is either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, decided by the centre; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the theory papers. Some Pearson subjects permit modular entry, so a unit can be banked before the final series, which Cambridge generally does not offer at this level.

Series timing differs too. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and some centres entering candidates for a March series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. That means two children in the same apartment cluster can have exam windows weeks apart, which has a direct effect on when revision has to start for each.

None of this is obscure information - it is printed on the specification and on the exam entry sheet. It is simply information that no competing page for this search puts in front of a parent, which is why families discover it in Year 11 instead of Year 10. Checking the board and the code takes five minutes and changes which tutor is the right one.

sections.heading: Where a child in a two-bedroom apartment actually works
paragraphs: This is the practical question The Greens turns on, and it never appears on a tutoring page. A villa has a study. A two-bedroom flat with two children has a bedroom each at best, usually shared, and a dining table that doubles as everything. The study environment is not a nice-to-have in exam years: it determines whether four hours of revision happen or whether two hours happen badly.

The arrangement that works in these clusters is a fixed station rather than a fixed room. One end of the dining table, a laptop, a headset, a document camera or just a phone on a stand for showing written working, and a drawer that holds the past papers so setup takes 90 seconds rather than ten minutes. Setup friction is the reason most home revision timetables collapse by the third week, and it is entirely solvable.

Headphones are the other piece. A live-video session with headphones is private even in a shared room, which means a sibling can read on the sofa while a lesson runs. A tutor physically present needs the room cleared, the family displaced and a parking space found. Families who have tried both usually describe the online version as the one that disrupted the household less, which is the opposite of what they expected.

There is a scheduling dividend too. Because the Barsha Heights and Internet City commutes are short, a Greens parent is often home by six, and a 6.30pm session with an adult in the apartment is genuinely available here in a way it is not in communities an hour from the office. Younger students benefit from that proximity far more than from the tutor being in the room.
bullets: Build a fixed station, not a dedicated room - setup under two minutes
Headphones make a shared space private; a visitor makes it unavailable
Keep past papers in one drawer so a session never starts with a search
Use the short local commute: 6.30pm slots with a parent present

sections.heading: What tuition costs a Greens family, priced by session length
paragraphs: Three of the six pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Below are Dubai market rates in dirhams, attributed to the providers who published them and to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They are the market, not IB Gram's list, and the reason to lay them out by session length is that this is where families in apartment communities are most often caught.

A quote that sounds hourly and delivers 45 minutes is roughly a third more expensive per contact hour than it appears. Two 45-minute sessions a week at a quoted hourly rate cost the same as 90 minutes but deliver 90 minutes of teaching across two contacts, which for a Year 7 or a language learner is better value even at the same total. The comparison a parent needs is cost per contact hour and contacts per week, not the headline number.

On the market bands themselves: EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, which buys homework supervision rather than a named-paper specialist. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED's published premium rate is AED 650. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Two questions to ask before paying anything. Is the price per hour or per lesson? And is VAT included in the figure quoted? IB Gram publishes no price list on these pages; a rate is quoted after a free consultation and a trial session, against the actual subject, level and session length, so that what is quoted is what applies.

sections.heading: A tutor in the flat against a specialist on screen
paragraphs: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is worth saying before the comparison rather than after it, because the comparison is still worth running and a family deserves to know who is making it.

The honest case for a visiting tutor is a young child who needs an adult beside them, a student who disengages from a screen, or a household with unreliable connectivity. For a Year 3 pupil doing fifteen minutes of reading aloud, presence beats expertise. The case weakens sharply from about Year 9 onwards, when the binding constraint becomes whether the tutor has taught that specific paper repeatedly, not whether they can be in the building.

In The Greens the space argument runs the other way from the usual assumption. A visiting tutor needs a cleared room for an hour in an apartment that does not have a spare one, plus a parking space in a cluster where visitor parking is contested at exactly the hours tuition happens. An online session needs a corner and a headset. The household that chose the online format is usually the one whose evening was disrupted less.

The pool argument is the decisive one for Years 10 to 13. Cambridge 0625 with the alternative-to-practical paper, Pearson 4MA1 Higher, IB Chemistry HL with an internal assessment due in February: these are specific jobs. The number of people within a 20-minute drive of The Greens who do each of them fluently is small. Over video, the drive is irrelevant and the pool is the whole set of people who teach that paper.

sections.heading: The exam year counted backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: Nobody in this search publishes a calendar. Every competing page talks about exam preparation and none of them names a session, an entry deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because the dates are the reason a plan either works or arrives late, and the entry deadline is always months before the paper.

The clearest worked example comes from Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries are due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027, with results released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. A family that starts thinking about entries in January has already missed the entry deadline by six weeks. The deadline, not the exam, is the first fixed point in the year.

Pearson's pattern is similar in shape. International GCSE exams run in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live PDF on its site is the only version worth planning against.

For the IB, treat dates differently. Dubai schools sit the May session, and the school's own internal deadlines for coursework fall months before it. Specific IB session and results dates should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one. What a family can plan against without any uncertainty is the school's internal calendar, which is published and which is what actually governs the DP1 and DP2 workload.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Only one competing page in this search touches licensing at all, in a single subheading, and it appears to rank partly on that alone. The position is not complicated and a parent is entitled to ask about it directly. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 regarding the introduction of private tuition work permits.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service via the smart app, website and e-services system, and the service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. There is no reason for a tutor not to hold one.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which matters because figures circulate online that cannot be verified; treat any specific amount you are quoted with scepticism. The absence of a published figure is not the absence of a penalty.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal category and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit because it operates no centre, office or branch in the UAE, and it is not approved, accredited or endorsed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any examining board. Any page claiming otherwise should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for a Greens school leaver
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step families meet last and should meet first. A UAE school leaver who wants to use a British or American qualification for a UAE university place needs the Ministry of Education's equivalency, and the published requirements are specific enough that a Year 10 subject choice can affect them.

For the British track, a student must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One page currently ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold is published in the source that sets out the British and American tracks, so no IB equivalency figure should be taken from a tutoring page. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a Ministry process - IB Gram does not perform it, expedite it or guarantee it, and no tutoring provider can. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; anyone implying it is has turned a regulatory process into a sales argument. What tutoring can do is help a student reach the grades the rule asks for, which is a different and more honest claim.

sections.heading: What to ask before you pay for a first session
paragraphs: The Greens runs on recommendations, and a recommendation is a starting point rather than a match. Five questions turn a name into a decision, and all five can be answered in a single short call. They are the questions this community's WhatsApp groups do not generally get around to.

Which syllabus code have you taught, and how recently? A tutor who last taught Cambridge 0580 four specifications ago is not current. Which component is the problem, and what did the last marked script say? A tutor who wants to see marked work before quoting is a better sign than one who does not. Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and does it include VAT? And finally: what happens if the match does not work after two sessions?

There is a sixth question specific to the Diploma: what will you do with coursework, and what will you not do? The right answer names a boundary. A tutor may teach content, explain criteria, test whether a research question is answerable, confirm a method will yield usable data, and give feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite work to a finished state, or provide an analysis for a student to adapt. One page in this search sells finished internal assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice exposure for the student, not a service.

The process from here is short. A consultation establishes the board, the code, the tier and the window. A trial session with a matched tutor follows, usually including a short piece of timed work marked against the real scheme. Then a written plan with the school's own deadlines on it, reviewed fortnightly against marked evidence. Where no specialist is free for a scarce Higher Level subject, you get a date rather than a substitute.

process.title: Establish the board before anything else
process.description: The first call settles which examining board set the paper, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies, and the school's own internal deadlines. In a community where two neighbours sit different boards in the same subject, this single step prevents the commonest mismatch.

process.title: Match the component, not the subject
process.description: A tutor is proposed who has taught that specific code and component recently - 0625 with the alternative-to-practical paper, or 4MA1 Higher, or IB Chemistry HL coursework supervision. Each child in a household is matched separately.

process.title: Trial session with timed work
process.description: The first session typically includes a short timed task marked against the published scheme, so the topic list comes from evidence rather than from the order of the specification. The student decides afterwards whether the match works.

process.title: Set the slot around the real commute
process.description: Sessions are placed after the longest school run in the household, or in the 6.30pm to 8.30pm window the short Barsha Heights commute makes available. Two children get staggered slots from the same table, with headphones.

process.title: Plan written against the entry deadline
process.description: The written plan counts backwards from the entry deadline and the mock window rather than forwards from today, because the entry deadline sits months before the paper and is the date families discover last.

process.title: Fortnightly review on marked evidence
process.description: Every two weeks the plan is checked against something marked. Closed topics come off, new ones go on. The review uses scripts and scores rather than impressions of how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific from the first session
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are treated as different exams because they are: different codes, different paper structures, different practical arrangements and different series. The match is made against the code on the entry sheet, not against the subject name.

whyPoints.title: Built for an apartment, not a villa
whyPoints.description: A session needs a corner and a headset rather than a cleared room and a visitor parking space. Two children can take staggered sessions from the same table without the household losing its living space for two hours.

whyPoints.title: Dates published, not implied
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, mock windows and results dates are laid out with the examining board named, taken from Cambridge and Pearson's own published key dates. No competing page in this search names a single session or deadline.

whyPoints.title: Rates with a publisher and a date attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is a market rate with the provider who published it named and the month stated. IB Gram quotes its own rate after a free trial against the actual subject, level and session length rather than from a page.

whyPoints.title: A stated coursework boundary
whyPoints.description: Diploma coursework is supported as supervision: criteria explained, feasibility tested, the student's own draft read and fed back. No text is supplied for submission in any component, which is the line that separates teaching from malpractice.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit position is set out in full, including that it is free for two years, who is eligible, and that no fine schedule has been published. Parents are told to ask to see the permit rather than to take anyone's word.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit apartments in The Greens, or are lessons online?
faqs.answer: Lessons for families in The Greens are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. In an apartment community the online format tends to disrupt the household less rather than more: a session needs a corner of a table and a headset instead of a cleared room for an hour and a visitor parking space in a cluster where parking is contested at exactly the hours tuition happens.

faqs.question: How does a parent in The Greens confirm which IGCSE board their school enters?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the exam entry sheet the school issues, and it appears in the school's assessment policy. The syllabus code is the fastest tell: Cambridge uses four digits such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry, while Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. Ask the subject teacher or the examinations officer if you cannot find it. The answer changes which tutor is the right one, so it is worth five minutes before booking anything.

faqs.question: Is there a school inside The Greens itself?
faqs.answer: Yes. Regent International School sits within the community and runs a British route through Cambridge IGCSE, which makes it a walk-to option for a share of families here. That is unusual in Dubai, where most communities have no school at all. Everyone else drives, mainly to Emirates International School Meadows for the IB continuum, Dubai British School Emirates Hills, or across into Al Barsha for GEMS Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha and the American School of Dubai.

faqs.question: Where should a child study in a two-bedroom flat during exam term?
faqs.answer: Build a fixed station rather than looking for a spare room. One end of the dining table, a laptop, a headset, a phone on a stand for showing written working, and a single drawer holding the past papers so setup takes under two minutes. Setup friction is why most home revision timetables collapse by the third week. Headphones make a shared space private, so a sibling can read on the sofa while a live session runs - something that is impossible if a tutor is physically in the room.

faqs.question: Are two short sessions a week better than one long one?
faqs.answer: For younger students and for languages, yes. Two 45-minute sessions produce two contacts, two sets of homework and two corrections, and attention rather than content is the limiting factor below about Year 9. For Year 11 and DP2 the reverse usually applies, because a timed past paper needs an uninterrupted hour. Check how the rate is expressed before comparing: a quote that sounds hourly but delivers 45 minutes is around a third more expensive per contact hour than it looks.

faqs.question: What is the earliest realistic session time for a child at school in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Around 5.00pm on a school night. The drive back to The Greens from Al Barsha is short in distance and long at 3.15pm, and a child who walks in at 4.20pm needs food before they need algebra. Families whose children attend Regent International School inside the community can start considerably earlier because there is no drive. The useful second window is 6.30pm to 8.30pm, which the short Barsha Heights and Internet City commutes make genuinely available here.

faqs.question: When is the entry deadline for an IGCSE series, as opposed to the exam itself?
faqs.answer: Months earlier, and this is the date families discover last. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Always plan against the live PDF on the board's own site.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge zone timetable matter if we are in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. The practical rule for a parent is simple: take the timetable from your own child's school rather than from a friend at a different school, because the two centres may be in different zones with different paper times.

faqs.question: Does my tutor need a MoHRE permit, and is there a fee?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and there is no fee. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking for these searches states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: My child codes well but loses marks in Computer Science theory. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and quickly, because it is a writing problem rather than a subject problem. Students who can produce working code often lose marks on trace tables, on describing an algorithm in prose, and on explaining why one data structure suits a problem better than another. The fix is practising written answers against the mark scheme for the specific board, since pseudocode conventions and expected terminology differ between specifications. Six to eight focused sessions on written theory typically move more marks than any amount of further programming practice.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children if they are in different year groups?
faqs.answer: It is possible and rarely the best choice. A Year 8 student and a Year 11 Cambridge candidate need different things: one needs patient consolidation, the other needs mark-scheme discipline on a named paper. Stretching one tutor across both usually means the older child gets the better hour. The arrangement that works in these clusters is two separate matches at staggered times - say 4.30pm and 5.45pm - taken from the same table with headphones, which costs no more than a single tutor travelling between two subjects would.

faqs.question: What should a tutor refuse to do with an extended essay?
faqs.answer: Supply text. A tutor may help narrow a research question, confirm that sources exist and are accessible, check that a method will produce usable material, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not provide wording for submission, restructure the argument into their own prose, or hand over an analysis to adapt. The test is whether the student can explain, unprompted, why every paragraph is there. The school's supervisor also signs an authenticity declaration.

faqs.question: Is online tuition as effective for a student who says they prefer a person in the room?
faqs.answer: For most students above about Year 9, yes, provided the format is used properly. A shared screen lets a past paper be annotated live, a mark scheme sat beside the student's own answer, and the session replayed afterwards - none of which works across a kitchen table. The genuine exceptions are younger children who need an adult physically beside them and students with specific needs that require it. The honest version of the trade is expertise in a named paper against physical presence, and above Year 9 expertise usually wins.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue over the summer and during school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the holiday pattern is different from the term one. Summer is the only block of time in the year long enough to close a real content gap rather than patch a topic, so families often use July and August for the subject that has been a problem all year, at two or three sessions a week. Because delivery is over live video, a family travelling out of Dubai keeps the same tutor and the same slot in whatever time zone they are in, which is harder to arrange with a visiting tutor.

dubai/the-greens.closingHeading: Bring the entry sheet, not just the subject name
dubai/the-greens.closingBody: A match from The Greens takes about a day once three things are known: the examining board, the syllabus code and what the last marked piece of work said. With those, a tutor who has taught that exact component recently can be proposed, and the first session can open with a short timed task marked against the real scheme. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, from a corner of your own table, at a slot built around the school run or the 6.30pm window. Where a specialist is genuinely unavailable, you will be given a date rather than a substitute.

dubai/the-lakes.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and both IGCSE boards at the levels The Lakes families ask for most. Each one is matched to a named subject and level rather than to a postcode, which is the whole point of teaching over video.

intro.heading: Who lives in The Lakes, and what that does to a tutoring timetable
paragraphs: The Lakes is a villa community, not an apartment one. Deema, Forat, Ghadeer, Hattan, Maeen and Zulal are family clusters with three to five bedrooms, a garden and, in most cases, children who have been in the same school since Foundation Stage. That tenure matters more than it sounds. Families who move every two years treat tutoring as crisis management; families who have been in Emirates Living for eight years tend to ask a different question, which is why a child who was comfortable in Year 7 is suddenly adrift in DP1. The answer is almost never ability. It is that the IB Diploma asks for independent work on a scale no earlier year group demanded.

The second thing that shapes the week here is that The Lakes has no secondary school inside it. Children leave the community every morning. Emirates International School Meadows is a five-minute drive and runs the full IB continuum. Dubai British School Emirates Hills takes the British route through IGCSE into A Level. Regent International School sits over in The Greens. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is an IB school on the other side of Sheikh Zayed Road, and a good number of Lakes children cross Al Barsha for Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia or Kings' School Al Barsha. Six families on one street can be sitting four different boards.

That spread is why a tutor who lives nearby is the wrong unit of selection. A villa in Hattan and a villa in Zulal might both need Chemistry help, but one child is sitting IB Chemistry HL with an internal assessment due in February and the other is sitting Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 with an alternative-to-practical paper. Those are not the same job. A specialist on live video who has taught that exact paper repeatedly is worth more than a generalist who can be at the door in fifteen minutes, which is the trade The Lakes families are actually making.

The third pressure point is the sibling problem. Villa households here commonly have two or three school-age children, and the useful window between the school run and dinner is roughly 90 minutes. Two children cannot both have the undivided 4.30pm slot. Online delivery is what makes the arithmetic work: one child takes 4.00pm, the other 5.15pm, neither tutor has to drive between the two, and nobody loses half an hour to Emirates Hills traffic. A single in-home tutor covering both subjects sounds cheaper until you notice that the same person is teaching Year 9 English and DP2 Physics.

Finally, there is what parents in this community reliably underestimate: how early the Diploma's deadlines land. The internal assessment, extended essay and Theory of Knowledge essay are set by the school months before the written papers, and a DP2 student in The Lakes is usually juggling all three alongside mock exams and university applications. Families who start support in February of DP2 are managing damage. Families who start in the first term of DP1 are building a timetable. The cost is similar; the outcome is not comparable.

dubai/the-lakes.programmesIntro: Children in The Lakes sit one of four routes, and each one changes what tutoring has to do. The Diploma needs coursework supervision as much as content. The Middle Years Programme needs criterion literacy. IGCSE needs mark-scheme discipline. Primary needs the opposite of all three: slow, unhurried number and reading work.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the three core components: Theory of Knowledge, the extended essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the final grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The written papers sit in the May session that Dubai schools use. HL subjects add a third paper and extra syllabus depth, which is where most of the grade pressure appears.
programmes.countryNote: The Lakes students generally take the Diploma at Emirates International School Meadows or Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, both a short drive from the community. Dubai's IB cohort is comparatively small - the IB accounts for 7% of private enrolment in the emirate against 37% for UK curricula - so a Lakes parent looking for an HL specialist in a minority subject has a genuinely thin local pool to draw on.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, lettered A to D, with achievement levels from 1 to 8 rather than percentages. There is no public examination until the optional MYP 5 eAssessment, which means a parent reading an MYP report sees criterion scores and not a grade they recognise. The programme rewards process: investigation, communication, reflection and transfer between subjects. Students who are strong at recall and weak at explaining their method lose marks they could keep.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single biggest source of confusion among Lakes families whose older child did IGCSE. A criterion B score of 5 is not a B grade, and it does not convert to one. Tutoring at MYP level here is mostly about teaching a child to read the criterion descriptors their teacher is marking against, which is work almost no family does at home because the vocabulary is unfamiliar.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses in eight to ten subjects, examined by terminal written papers with syllabus codes that matter: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654; Pearson Edexcel equivalents are numbered differently again, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, which caps the available grade. Pearson Edexcel runs a single tier in most subjects but allows modular entry in some.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School both run the British route, and families in The Lakes are often surprised to learn their two children sit different boards because they attend different schools. Checking the syllabus code on the exam entry sheet before booking a tutor is five minutes that saves a wasted term, because the papers, the practical arrangements and the mark schemes differ.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around units rather than subjects, with a personal exhibition project in the final year. Assessment is continuous and descriptive, so there is no percentage for a parent to track. Mathematics and English are taught inside units of inquiry, which suits children who ask questions and can leave a child with shaky number fluency carrying a gap that only becomes visible in MYP, when algebra arrives and the foundations are expected to be automatic.
programmes.countryNote: Several Lakes families use PYP years for quiet remediation rather than acceleration: twenty minutes of number bonds, times tables and reading aloud, twice a week, with nothing that resembles a test. It is the cheapest tutoring a family will ever buy and the only kind that reliably prevents the Year 9 maths emergency.

dubai/the-lakes.subjectsIntro: The requests that come out of Emirates Living cluster tightly around maths and the sciences at Higher Level, with English A and Economics close behind. Below is what each one assesses and where marks actually go, rather than a list of subject names.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, assessed across two papers at SL and three at HL, with Paper 3 at HL carrying extended problem-solving. The mathematical exploration is internally assessed. Marks are lost most often in reasoning that is correct but unjustified, and in students who can execute a method but cannot say why it applies.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and the graphic display calculator, with technology use assumed throughout. Many Lakes students choose this route after IGCSE and then discover the statistics content is heavier than expected. The exploration here rewards a real dataset and a genuine question; invented data is visible to a moderator within a page.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, and organic mechanisms, with HL adding depth in each. The internally assessed investigation is the student's own. Students lose marks on significant figures, on uncertainty propagation, and on explaining a mechanism in words rather than arrows when the question asks for the mechanism.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields and energy production, with HL extending into more demanding algebra. The commonest failure here is not conceptual: it is unit handling and the habit of skipping the diagram. Dubai students who come from an IGCSE background often arrive strong at recall and weak at multi-step derivation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology, genetics, ecology, physiology and the HL extensions, with heavy demand on precise command-term response. A question that says 'explain' and receives a description earns part marks at best. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments reward students who have practised reading a graph they have never seen.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with diagrams carrying marks in their own right. The internal assessment asks for commentaries on published news articles, and the usual error is a commentary that summarises the article instead of applying a named theory to it. HL adds quantitative work and a policy paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a case study released in advance for one paper. Students who treat the pre-released case as reading rather than as a dataset to be analysed lose the easiest marks on the paper. HL adds a research project on a real organisation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary works, assessed by two written papers, an individual oral and, at HL, an essay. The individual oral is where Lakes students most often need help, because it asks for a global issue argued through two extracts and most students arrive with a theme rather than an issue.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Higher and Foundation
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry and statistics across two or three papers depending on the board and tier. The Core tier caps the top grade, so a Year 10 sitting Core who wants to take the Diploma later needs that decision revisited early rather than in Year 11.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay
subjects.description: The extended essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece supervised by a school teacher; Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Support here is process coaching - narrowing a question, testing an argument, planning a timeline - and the written work remains entirely the student's own.

dubai/the-lakes.regionsTitle: Emirates Living and the communities next door
dubai/the-lakes.regionsIntro: The Lakes rarely operates alone. School runs, carpools and sibling timetables tie it to the rest of Emirates Living and across to New Dubai, and the tutoring pattern in each neighbouring community is slightly different.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Directly adjacent, and home to Emirates International School Meadows, which runs the IB continuum. The majority of DP enquiries from The Lakes concern this school's deadlines, so sessions are often timetabled around its internal assessment calendar.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: Townhouses rather than villas, with a younger average age and a heavier concentration of primary and lower-secondary requests. Dubai British School Emirates Hills draws a large share of the children here into the IGCSE route.

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: Apartments on the other side of Sheikh Zayed Road, with Regent International School inside the community. Study-space constraints shape sessions there in a way they do not in a Lakes villa.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Mid-rise towers overlooking Emirates Golf Club, mostly families with one or two children and a heavy DP presence. Requests from The Views skew towards the Diploma core rather than content catch-up.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large villas immediately north, with Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills nearby. Enquiries here are often for minority Higher Level subjects where no local specialist exists at all.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Fifteen minutes towards the coast, holding Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School. Lakes families with older children frequently commute here, which pushes the earliest workable session to 5.00pm.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Apartment living with a different rhythm - later dinners, later sessions, and a strong preference for weekend blocks. Several Lakes carpools end in Marina, so pickup timing matters to both.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Home to Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Kings' School Al Barsha. The drive from The Lakes is short in theory and long at 3.15pm, which is the single most common reason a 4.00pm slot does not work.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The schools most Lakes children attend, all within a short drive of the community. Between them they cover the full IB continuum and the British route from Foundation Stage to A Level, which is why one street can contain four different assessment calendars.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, reached across Sheikh Zayed Road or Umm Suqeim Street. Families here are driving 20 to 35 minutes each way at school-run time, which removes the early-evening slot from the week and pushes tuition to 5.30pm or later.

schoolClusters.city: Motor City, Sports City and the Dubailand belt
schoolClusters.note: A smaller flow, usually families who moved out of Emirates Living but kept the school, or who chose a school for a specific programme. The commute is long enough that online lessons are the only realistic way to fit tuition into a school night.

dubai/the-lakes.modesIntro: Three formats work for The Lakes, and they are chosen by what the week looks like rather than by preference. All three are delivered over live video, one tutor to one student unless a family specifically asks otherwise.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, same slot every week
modes.description: The default and the format that suits villa households with more than one child. A fixed weekly hour per subject, booked at a time that survives the school run, with the tutor holding the slot through the year. Consistency matters more than volume: one well-prepared hour a week beats three improvised ones, and a fixed slot is what lets a household run two or three separate matches without collisions.
bullets: One subject, one tutor, one recurring slot per child
Sibling slots staggered so the same hour is not contested
Work set between sessions and marked before the next one
Slot held through mock weeks rather than cancelled

modes.title: Coursework supervision blocks
modes.description: For the Diploma core and the internally assessed components, where the calendar rather than the content is the problem. These are shorter, denser sessions clustered around a school's own deadlines: narrowing a research question, checking a method is feasible, reading a draft the student has written and giving feedback against the published criteria. The written work is the student's own throughout, and the tutor's notes stay as feedback rather than text.

Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft

No text supplied for a student to submit, in any component

modes.title: Intensive pre-session revision
modes.description: A compressed run of sessions in the eight to twelve weeks before written papers, usually two or three a week on the weakest two subjects. Built around past-paper work under timed conditions, mark-scheme reading and the specific topics a diagnostic has flagged. This is the format Lakes families ask for in February and March, and it works best when the diagnostic happened in November rather than the week it starts.

Topic list driven by the diagnostic, not by the syllabus order

sections.heading: Where The Lakes children actually go to school, and why that decides the tutor
paragraphs: The Lakes contains no school. Every child leaves the community each morning, and the destination determines the board, the calendar and the paper they sit. Emirates International School Meadows runs the IB continuum from primary through the Diploma. Dubai British School Emirates Hills takes the British route: IGCSE at 16, then A Level. Regent International School in The Greens is British. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is an IB school. Across Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia and Kings' School Al Barsha add American and British options again.

The practical consequence is that a parent asking a neighbour for a tutor recommendation is asking someone whose child sits a different examination. A recommendation that was excellent for Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 is close to useless for IB Physics HL, because the first is a terminal written paper with an alternative-to-practical component and the second carries an internally assessed investigation worth a fifth of the grade and a Paper 3 that most IGCSE teachers have never read.

The first thing worth checking, before any tutor conversation, is the exam entry sheet or the school's assessment policy. It names the board, the syllabus code and the tier. With those three facts a match takes a day. Without them, the first two sessions are spent working out what the child is actually sitting, which is time a family has paid for and learned nothing from.

This is also why the online model is not a compromise here. A Lakes family needs a specialist in one named paper of one named board. The pool of people within a 20-minute drive who have taught that exact paper repeatedly is small; the pool who can teach it over video is not. The constraint being removed is geography, and in Emirates Living geography is the binding one.
bullets: Find the board and syllabus code on the exam entry sheet before booking
Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel and IB mark the same subject differently
A neighbour's recommendation is only useful for the same board and level
Tier matters: Cambridge Core caps the available grade
