sections.heading: The pressure points a villa household in Emirates Living hits, year by year
paragraphs: Tutoring requests from The Lakes arrive in a predictable pattern, and the pattern follows year group rather than subject. In Year 6 and Year 7 the trigger is transition: a child who was fluent in primary number work meets algebra and formal written response, and the gap shows within a term. Support at this point is cheap, short and preventative, and almost nobody buys it, because nothing has gone wrong yet.

Year 9 and Year 10 bring the option-choice problem. A child picks three sciences and then discovers that Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences and three separate sciences are different workloads, or chooses Core tier maths without realising it caps the grade. These are reversible decisions for a few weeks and then they are not. A single diagnostic session in the first term of Year 10 is often the highest-value hour a family buys in five years.

Year 11 is mark-scheme year. The content is largely taught; the marks are lost in how answers are written. Command terms, working shown, units, significant figures and the discipline of answering the question asked rather than the question revised for. This is coachable and it moves grades without new content, which is why intensive revision blocks in the months before papers are the commonest request from this community.

DP1 and DP2 are a different animal entirely. The Diploma runs six subjects, three internally assessed components of real weight, a 4,000-word extended essay, Theory of Knowledge and university applications, all inside two years. The failure mode in The Lakes is not a weak student; it is a capable student with no timeline. Families who map the DP core deadlines in the first term of DP1 spend less and worry less than those who discover them in January of DP2.
bullets: Year 6-7: transition to algebra and extended written response
Year 9-10: option and tier decisions that cap or open later routes
Year 11: mark-scheme literacy, command terms and timed practice
DP1: map the core deadlines before content support begins
DP2: triage - two weakest subjects, timed papers, nothing else

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tuition costs around Emirates Living, and who charges it
paragraphs: Most competing pages for this search publish no price at all. Two publish rates in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. The table below is the market, in dirhams, drawn from rates those providers publish themselves and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. These are not IB Gram's prices; they are what a parent in Emirates Living should expect to be quoted if they ring round.

The spread is wide and it is not arbitrary. At the bottom, AED 45 to 150 an hour buys an online session with a university student or a generalist - EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. The middle band, AED 150 to 300, is a qualified subject teacher online; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that, AED 200 to 450 buys a specialist in a named IB or IGCSE paper, and TutorChase publishes AED 270 for its tier. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED's published rate shows.

An in-home visit in a villa community carries a travel premium whether or not it is itemised. Bestimate's survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors in Dubai at AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen across the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. The arithmetic is visible once it is written down: the home visit costs more per contact hour and buys a smaller pool of specialists.

Two practical points before anyone quotes you. Ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, because a 45-minute lesson quoted at an hourly-sounding number is a 33% increase. And ask whether VAT is included. IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages; the honest route is a free consultation and a trial session, after which a rate is quoted against the actual subject, level and session length.

sections.heading: A tutor in the villa or a specialist on screen: the Emirates Living arithmetic
paragraphs: This is the decision The Lakes families actually agonise over, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - so there is no pretending otherwise. What follows is the comparison a parent should run before choosing either option.

The case for a tutor in the room is real and worth stating. A younger child who needs a presence beside them, a student who will not engage with a screen, a family with unreliable connectivity: these are genuine reasons. For a Year 4 child doing twenty minutes of number work, physical presence can matter more than subject expertise. Nobody should pretend that is not true.

Above roughly Year 9, the balance shifts, and it shifts for a reason that has nothing to do with technology. The binding constraint becomes expertise in one named paper of one named board. In Emirates Living, a 20-minute radius covers Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Emirates Hills, Springs, Meadows and Marina - a large area with a small number of people who have taught IB Chemistry HL internal assessments or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 Paper 2 enough times to be fast at it. Over video, that radius stops mattering.

Then there is the week itself. A 4.30pm home visit in The Lakes depends on Al Khail Road and the Umm Suqeim Street interchange behaving, and in term time they often do not. A missed 20 minutes of a paid hour is a 33% loss. Screen sharing also changes what a session can do: a past paper annotated live, a mark scheme opened beside the student's answer, and a recording the student can replay before the next session. None of that is possible across a kitchen table.

sections.heading: Two children, one evening: how a Lakes household actually schedules tuition
paragraphs: The practical problem in a villa community with three bedrooms full of children is not money and it is not motivation. It is that there is one usable window between the school run and dinner and more than one child who needs it. Families solve this badly by default: one tutor, two subjects, both children half-served.

The workable pattern is staggered slots with separate specialists. A Year 9 MYP student takes 4.00pm to 5.00pm while the DP2 student finishes a past paper in another room; the DP2 student takes 5.15pm to 6.15pm while the younger one has dinner. Two different tutors, neither of whom has to be anywhere, and a household that is not organising its evening around a car arriving.

A second pattern suits exam years: one child on a weekly slot through the year, the other on an intensive block in the run-up to papers. This spreads cost across the calendar rather than stacking it, and it recognises that a Year 7 and a DP2 student do not need the same intensity at the same time. The Year 7 needs 40 weeks of unhurried consistency; the DP2 student needs ten weeks of pressure.

The third thing families underestimate is the value of holding the slot through mock weeks. The instinct is to cancel tuition during mocks because the child is busy. The mock fortnight is the single most informative two weeks of the year: it produces real marked papers against real schemes. Cancelling then throws away the diagnostic and keeps the problem. A session during mock week spent reading the marked script is worth three sessions of new content.
bullets: Stagger slots rather than sharing one tutor across two children
Match each child to a subject specialist, not the household to one person
Pair a year-long slot for the younger child with an intensive block for the exam-year one
Keep sessions running through mock weeks and read the marked scripts
Build the week around the longest commute in the household, not the shortest

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA inspection report before you read a tutor profile
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a report on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Every school a Lakes child attends has one, it is free to read, and most parents have not opened it.

The reason to read it before hiring a tutor is that the report separates attainment from progress, and those two words answer different questions. Attainment is how the cohort performs against a standard. Progress is how far they have moved from where they started. A school with high attainment and weaker progress is often selecting well rather than teaching exceptionally, which has a direct implication: a bright child may be coasting, and the intervention needed is extension rather than remediation.

The report is also broken down by phase and by subject. A school rated Very Good overall can carry a weaker judgement in secondary mathematics or in a specific science. That paragraph is more useful to a parent choosing tutoring than the headline band, because it tells you where the school's own capacity is thinnest and therefore where a child is most likely to need outside support.

The context worth knowing is scale. KHDA counted 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai for 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curricula at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the IB at 7%. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For a family budgeting a tutoring year, a frozen fee line is the one fixed point in the calculation.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an internal assessment
paragraphs: Every internally assessed component in the Diploma must be the student's own work. That is not a preference; it is an IB academic-honesty requirement, and a breach is a malpractice finding against the student, with consequences up to loss of the Diploma. One of the pages competing for this search sells finished internal assessments at a published price. A Lakes family should treat that as a reason to walk away, not a service.

The boundary is clear once stated. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, check that a proposed method will produce usable data, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is underserved, and model the analysis of a different dataset entirely. All of that is teaching, and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor may not do is supply text, restructure a student's argument into their own words, correct a draft to a finished state, or hand over an analysis for a student to adapt. The test a parent can apply is simple: could the student explain, unprompted, why every sentence is there and where every number came from? If not, the work is no longer theirs. The school's own supervisor also signs an authenticity declaration, and experienced moderators spot a mismatch between a student's written register and their oral fluency quickly.

There is a second practical reason to respect the line. The internal assessment is where a student learns the method that the written papers test. A student handed a finished piece has lost both the marks they did not earn and the preparation they needed. The families in Emirates Living who get the most out of coursework support are the ones who book it early and treat it as supervision rather than rescue.
bullets: Permitted: content teaching, criterion explanation, feasibility checks, feedback on the student's own draft
Not permitted: supplying text, rewriting to a finished state, providing an analysis to adapt
The parent's test: can the student explain every sentence and number unprompted?
Past papers and mark schemes are referenced from official sites, never reproduced as downloads

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside an IB or British route
paragraphs: This is the part almost no competing page mentions, and it affects every child in The Lakes regardless of curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for. KHDA's published requirements had to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

KHDA is specific about how these subjects run. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students runs in Arabic; non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

There are two further constraints a parent should know. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises no mandatory-subject lesson should run under 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA permission to teach those subjects. Separately, for the mandatory UAE subjects, use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited.

What that last line means for tutoring is worth being plain about. Support for Arabic as an additional language is ordinary language teaching and entirely normal. Support in Islamic Education or UAE Social Studies must stay inside the school's prescribed material rather than importing a different course, because the content itself is regulated. A Lakes family whose child is struggling with Arabic B is usually best served by weekly conversational and written practice, which is a different request from exam coaching and should be booked as one.

sections.heading: Getting started from The Lakes, including what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The honest version of the process is four steps and one disclosure. First, a consultation: what school, what board, what syllabus code, what the last marked piece of work said, and what the household's realistic weekly window is. Second, a trial session with a matched tutor, which exists so the student can decide whether the match works rather than so we can describe one. Third, a short written plan naming the topics, the deadlines and the number of sessions before the next review. Fourth, a fortnightly check that the plan is still the right one.

The disclosure is about availability. Some requests are easy: IGCSE Mathematics, IB Chemistry SL, English A at either level. Some are hard: Higher Level minority subjects, specific language B combinations, or a Theory of Knowledge specialist in the fortnight before a school deadline. Where no tutor with the right specialism is free, we say so and give a date rather than putting a generalist in the slot. A parent in Emirates Living who was promised a specialist and given a generalist has paid for something they did not get.

It is also worth knowing the regulatory position on the people doing the teaching, because parents ask and most pages do not answer. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram has no centre, office or branch in the UAE, and no regulator has approved, accredited or endorsed it. What we are is a matching platform delivering one-to-one lessons over live video, and anyone claiming regulator endorsement on a page like this should be asked to show the permit number.

process.title: Consultation about the actual paper
process.description: A short call that establishes the school, the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component causing trouble. We ask for the most recent marked work, because a marked script tells us more in two minutes than a description does in twenty.

process.title: Match on the paper, not the postcode
process.description: A tutor is proposed who has taught that specific syllabus and component repeatedly. For Lakes households with more than one child, each child is matched separately rather than one tutor being stretched across two year groups and two boards.

process.title: Trial session and a timed diagnostic
process.description: The first session usually includes a short piece of timed work marked against the real scheme. That produces a topic list driven by evidence rather than by the syllabus order, and it gives the student a say in whether the match is right.

process.title: A written plan with the school's dates on it
process.description: Topics, session count, and the school's own internal assessment and mock deadlines, written down. In The Lakes this plan is usually built backwards from the Diploma core deadlines, because those are the dates families discover last.

process.title: Fortnightly review against marked work
process.description: Every two weeks the plan is checked against something that has been marked. If a topic has closed, it comes off. If a new one opens, it goes on. Reviews happen on marked evidence rather than on how the sessions felt.

process.title: Exam-session triage
process.description: In the final ten weeks the plan narrows to the two weakest subjects and to timed papers. Sessions continue through mock weeks so the marked scripts can be read with the tutor rather than filed.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest person
whyPoints.description: Emirates Living is well served by roads and poorly served by paper specialists. Teaching over video removes the 20-minute radius as a constraint, so a Lakes child gets someone who has taught their exact component instead of the best-qualified person who happens to live nearby.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown with their source
whyPoints.description: The AED figures on this page are market rates with the publisher named and the month stated. No competitor page in this search publishes a sourced dirham rate at all. IB Gram's own rate is quoted after a trial, against the real subject and session length.

whyPoints.title: A schedule that survives the school run
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set around the longest commute in the household, not the shortest. Nothing depends on a car arriving, so a slow afternoon on Al Khail Road costs the family nothing and a 4.00pm slot is actually a 4.00pm slot.

whyPoints.title: Coursework supervision with a visible line
whyPoints.description: The Diploma core is supported as supervision: criteria explained, feasibility checked, the student's own draft read and fed back against the published criteria. No text is supplied for submission, in any component, which is a line two pages in this search do not hold.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated rather than implied
whyPoints.description: Where no tutor with the right specialism is free, you are told so and given a date. Minority Higher Level subjects and some language combinations are genuinely scarce, and a family that knows that can plan around it.

whyPoints.title: One platform, several children, separate plans
whyPoints.description: A villa household with three school-age children gets three matches, three plans and three staggered slots rather than one tutor spread thin. Each plan tracks its own school's deadlines, which in The Lakes are frequently three different calendars.

faqs.question: Can we get an IB or IGCSE tutor in The Lakes who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons for families in The Lakes are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; home visits are a service we run only in India. The market rate for a visiting tutor in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour according to Bestimate's 2026 survey and published home-tutor rates, with travel priced in. The reason we deliver online is availability rather than cost: a Lakes family needs a specialist in one named board and paper, and the number of such people inside a 20-minute drive of Emirates Living is small.

faqs.question: Which schools do most children in The Lakes attend?
faqs.answer: There is no school inside The Lakes, so every child commutes. The nearest options are Emirates International School Meadows, which runs the full IB continuum, and Dubai British School Emirates Hills on the British route. Regent International School sits in The Greens and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is a short drive north. Across Sheikh Zayed Road, families use GEMS Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Kings' School Al Barsha, while older students often travel to Dubai College or GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh.

faqs.question: How much should a Lakes family expect to pay per hour for IB tuition?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates for IB tuition sit in four broad bands. Budget online sessions run AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject teacher online is AED 150 to 300, and Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. A specialist in a named IB paper is AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED's rate shows. These are other providers' published figures, not ours. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, against the actual subject, level and session length.

faqs.question: My two children are in different schools on different boards. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost always yes, and it is cheaper than it sounds. A Year 9 Middle Years Programme student and a Year 11 Cambridge IGCSE candidate are assessed against entirely different things: criterion descriptors lettered A to D in one case, terminal written papers and mark schemes in the other. One tutor stretched across both does neither well. The practical pattern in a villa household is staggered slots - one child at 4.00pm, the other at 5.15pm - with separate specialists. Nobody is driving between the two, so the second slot costs no more than the first.

faqs.question: When is the right time to start tutoring for a child in Year 10 at a British school?
faqs.answer: The first term of Year 10, and for a reason that has nothing to do with grades. That is the window in which option and tier decisions are still reversible. A child entered for Cambridge Core tier maths has a capped maximum grade, which matters if they later want the IB Diploma or A Level mathematics. A single diagnostic session early in Year 10 that checks the tier, the subject combination and the workload against the child's intended route is frequently the highest-value hour a family buys across five years of schooling.

faqs.question: What does the KHDA inspection report tell me that the school's own newsletter does not?
faqs.answer: It separates attainment from progress, and it reports both by phase and by subject. Attainment is performance against a standard; progress is movement from a starting point. A school with strong attainment and weaker progress may be selecting well rather than teaching exceptionally, which means a capable child could be coasting. The subject-level paragraphs are more useful than the headline band, because a school rated Very Good overall can carry a weaker judgement in secondary mathematics. That paragraph tells you where outside support is most likely to be needed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IB internal assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, confirm a method will produce usable data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a draft to a finished state, or hand over an analysis to adapt. The test a parent can apply: could the student explain, unprompted, why every sentence is there and where every number came from? If not, it is no longer their work.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still apply if my child is in the IB at a school near The Lakes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also mandates separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in their school's licensed-curriculum language rather than in Arabic.

faqs.question: Is it worth keeping tuition running during mock exam fortnight?
faqs.answer: It is the most valuable fortnight of the year to keep it. Mocks produce real scripts marked against real schemes, which is the only hard evidence a family gets before the written papers. The instinct is to cancel because the child is busy; the result is that the diagnostic is thrown away and the same mistakes repeat. A session during mock week spent reading the marked script with a tutor - command terms missed, working not shown, units dropped - typically moves more marks than three sessions of new content.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how do I check one?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, and you can simply ask to see the permit.

faqs.question: How do staggered sessions work when both my children need the same hour?
faqs.answer: They are booked as two separate recurring slots with two different specialists, usually about 75 minutes apart. One child takes the earlier slot while the other finishes a past paper or eats; then they swap. Because nothing depends on a tutor arriving at the villa, the second slot carries no travel gap and no risk from traffic on Al Khail Road. Households in The Lakes with three school-age children typically run three slots across two evenings rather than trying to compress everything into the window before dinner.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for a Higher Level subject we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date, rather than given a generalist. Mainstream requests - IGCSE Mathematics, IB Chemistry SL, English A - are usually matched within a day or two. Minority Higher Level subjects, specific language B combinations and Theory of Knowledge supervision close to a school deadline are genuinely scarce, and pretending otherwise just wastes a family's term. Where a specialist is unavailable in the UAE we will say where the available tutor is based and what the rate is, so the choice stays with you.

faqs.question: Does a Lakes child doing IGCSE need to worry about UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: It is worth understanding early rather than in the final year. For the British track, the Ministry's published requirements are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects are needed, which is wrong. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry, not by any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a later slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families in Emirates Living ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon but makes the late afternoon unproductive for fasting students, so sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar time. Because delivery is over live video there is nobody travelling, which makes a 9.00pm slot as practical as a 4.00pm one. Families usually keep the same tutor and the same weekly rhythm and simply shift the clock for the month, then return to the term-time slot afterwards.

faqs.question: Is a 45-minute lesson or a 60-minute lesson better value for a Year 7 student?
faqs.answer: For most Year 7 students, two 45-minute sessions beat one 60-minute session, because attention rather than content is the limiting factor at that age. The thing to check is how the rate is expressed. A quote that sounds hourly but delivers 45 minutes is effectively a third more expensive per contact hour, and that is the commonest hidden extra in the Dubai market. Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and whether VAT is included, before comparing two providers' headline numbers.

dubai/the-lakes.closingHeading: Start with the paper your child is actually sitting
dubai/the-lakes.closingBody: Bring three things to a first conversation: the board, the syllabus code and the most recent marked piece of work. With those, a Lakes family can be matched to a specialist in that exact component within a day or two, and the first session can begin with a timed diagnostic rather than with introductions. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, at a slot built around the Emirates Living school run, with a written plan that carries the school's own deadlines on it. If no specialist is free for the subject you need, you will be given a date instead of a substitute.

dubai/the-meadows.tutorsIntro: Tutors here are chosen for the unsupervised part of a course rather than the taught part: an exploration that has no deadline until it suddenly has one, a Paper 2 technique that classroom time never reaches, or the three weeks of study leave before an IGCSE series when nobody is teaching at all.

intro.heading: The part of the grade that nobody is timetabled to teach
paragraphs: The Meadows is nine numbered sub-communities of detached villas inside Emirates Living, bounded by Sheikh Zayed Road on one side and Al Khail Road on the other, with Emirates International School Meadows on its edge and The Springs and The Lakes as immediate neighbours. Plots are larger here than in The Springs, which means most households have a room that can be closed. That solves the physical problem of studying at home and leaves the harder problem untouched, which is that nobody in the house knows what the student is supposed to be doing in that room.

Here is the arithmetic that brings Meadows parents to a page like this one. In the IB sciences and in both mathematics courses, the internal assessment is 20% of the final grade. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together carry up to three points on the Diploma matrix. Past-paper practice, which is the single highest-return activity in the final six months, appears on no timetable at all. Add those up and a substantial fraction of a Diploma grade is produced in the student's own time, against criteria the student has usually read once, with a teacher who has thirty other students doing the same thing.

IGCSE has a sharper version of the same problem. Teaching finishes, study leave starts, and a Year 11 student in a Meadows villa is handed two or three weeks that will move their grades more than the preceding two terms. Most use them badly, not through laziness but because nobody has ever taught them how to run a revision week. They re-read notes, which feels productive and measurably is not, instead of working timed questions against a mark scheme and keeping a log of what the marks were actually lost for.

A school cannot fix this at scale, and it is unfair to expect it to. A subject teacher with a full timetable can set an internal deadline, give a lesson on criteria, read one draft and return it with comments. What they cannot do is sit with one student while they work out why their evaluation section keeps scoring in the middle band, or check on a Tuesday evening in February whether the exploration has moved since Sunday. That is a one-to-one job and it is the job this page is about.

What follows is the map. Which components are taught and which are not, what the published criteria letters actually reward on a mathematics exploration, every word and page limit a Diploma student has to respect in one table, what to do with IGCSE study leave, the command terms the mark scheme uses, the honest comparison between an in-home tutor in Emirates Living and an online specialist, and the line a tutor must not cross on assessed work.

dubai/the-meadows.programmesIntro: Meadows children sit three systems between them, and the share of the grade that falls outside lessons is different in each. That share, rather than the content, is what decides whether tutoring is worth buying.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of eight and converted to a grade from 1 to 7. The criteria are the whole system: a student who understands the content but never practises the investigating or communicating strands sits permanently in the middle bands. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, which is supervised, self-directed and assessed on process as much as outcome, and which is the first genuinely unmanaged piece of work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: In The Meadows the Middle Years cohort is concentrated in one nearby school, so the Personal Project arrives at the same time for most of the street. Families who plan for it in the summer before MYP 5 rather than in the term it is due consistently report a calmer year, because the project's failure mode is schedule rather than ability.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three Higher and three Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS alongside. Forty-two points come from subjects and up to three from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Internal assessment carries 20% in the sciences and both mathematics courses and 30% at Standard Level in economics. Higher Level mathematics adds a third paper worth 20%, which rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall.
programmes.countryNote: The practical point for a Meadows household is that the school sets the internal deadlines, not the IB. Those dates sit months ahead of the formal submission and they are the only calendar that matters day to day. Get the school's internal deadline sheet, put it on the fridge, and plan backwards from the earliest date on it.

programmes.name: IGCSE at Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Cambridge splits most subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C; Pearson Edexcel tiers mathematics as Foundation and Higher with a grade 9 ceiling. Paper structures diverge: Cambridge physics 0625 runs multiple choice, theory and either a practical test or a written alternative, while Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 uses two papers with practical skills assessed inside them. The board on the entry decides which past papers are useful.
programmes.countryNote: The decisive feature of IGCSE for Meadows families is study leave. Teaching stops, two or three unstructured weeks follow, and those weeks move grades more than either preceding term. A plan written before study leave starts is worth more than any amount of extra teaching during it.

programmes.name: A Level, where the cluster offers it
programmes.description: Several British schools around Emirates Living run A Levels rather than the Diploma after IGCSE, with three or four linear subjects and no core. The independent-study load is different rather than lighter: fewer components but far deeper content per subject, and in most subjects the entire grade rests on terminal written papers. A student who coasted through IGCSE on recall meets a genuine wall in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: The choice between A Level and the Diploma is usually made in Year 11 and is driven as much by breadth tolerance as by ability. A student who wants to stop writing essays should not be pushed into the Diploma core; a student who has no idea what they want at eighteen is generally better served by the Diploma's breadth.

dubai/the-meadows.subjectsIntro: These notes name the unsupervised part of each subject, because that is what a Meadows household is usually buying help with. The taught content is rarely the problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is 20% of the grade and is marked against five criteria worth twenty marks in total. At Higher Level the third paper is a long investigation worth another 20%, and almost nobody practises it until a mock goes badly. Both are unsupervised work by default, and both reward a style of sustained reasoning that routine homework never asks for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The calculator is assumed throughout, which catches students arriving from a non-calculator IGCSE paper. The exploration is the pressure point: a weak or borrowed dataset caps the marks available under use of mathematics and under personal engagement, and the topic decision is usually made in a rush because nobody scheduled it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers plus one scientific investigation worth 20% at both levels. The investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and the evaluation band is where Meadows students most often sit mid-range: limitations get listed rather than weighed for direction and size of effect on the result.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate Higher from Standard Level. The investigation carries 20% and has a 3,000 word ceiling, which is a planning constraint rather than a target. Students who write up as they go score better than those who collect data for three weeks and write for one weekend.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-dense course decided by command terms. Outline, describe, explain and evaluate carry different expectations and different marks, and a student who answers everything as describe caps well below their understanding. Statistical treatment inside the investigation is the second recurring gap, particularly for students who came through double award science.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries built on published news articles, each with its own word allowance, worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher. It is the first extended analytical writing many Diploma students produce, and marks live in diagram accuracy, axis labelling and explicit links back to the article rather than in general economic commentary.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a timed guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, which rewards a repeatable method rather than wide reading. The Higher Level essay has a 1,200 to 1,500 word range and is written on a text studied in class, which makes it one of the few components where early planning is almost entirely within the student's control.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation runs to 2,200 words and is graded in three sections, with the evaluation of sources routinely the weakest. Paper answers are decided by comparative argument and by using named evidence rather than narrating a period. Students who revise content without practising argument structure plateau around the middle of the mark range.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study command and calculation accuracy decide this subject. The Higher Level research project is built on a real organisation and has a 1,800 word limit, so the choice of organisation and the availability of data matter more than the writing. Answers lose marks for listing advantages and disadvantages where a justified recommendation was asked for.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition built on three objects with a 950 word commentary, plus a 1,600 word essay on a prescribed title. Both are assessed and both contribute to the matrix points. TOK is the component students most often leave until the term it is due, and it is the one where a few structured hours of coaching change the grade most reliably.

dubai/the-meadows.regionsIntro: The Meadows sits inside Emirates Living and shares its schools, buses and sports fixtures with the communities around it. These notes are about what each neighbour means for a study timetable rather than for a property search.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: Immediately adjacent, with smaller townhouses and the same bus routes. Springs households usually run sequential evening slots because there is one workable table; Meadows households can often run parallel sessions in two rooms, which changes what is schedulable.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Lower-density villas with later pickups and the same school calendar. Lakes and Meadows students frequently share internal deadline dates, which makes a joint push on an exploration or a Personal Project in the same fortnight genuinely workable.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large villas, with Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Dubai British School Emirates Hills inside the same perimeter. This is the nearest point of comparison for Higher Level subject choices, because the Diploma cohorts overlap socially.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Apartment communities on the Sheikh Zayed Road side, home to Regent International School. Higher tenancy turnover means more mid-year arrivals, and a mid-year arrival into Year 10 is the hardest catch-up case in this cluster.

regions.name: Al Barsha South
regions.note: Where several larger campuses sit, including Nord Anglia International School Dubai. The Al Khail Road run is quick before eight and unreliable after five, which is why evening sessions for children at these schools start after six.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: A fifteen-minute drive at a quiet hour and far longer at the wrong one. Meadows families with older children at sixth form in this direction generally abandon weekday in-person arrangements entirely by the second term.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park
regions.note: Villa community across Sheikh Zayed Road with its own British provision. Families who move between here and The Meadows keep the same online slot, because a weekly video lesson survives a house move in a way a local arrangement does not.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The campuses closest to The Meadows. One runs the IB continuum through to the Diploma and the others are British-curriculum routes through IGCSE, which means neighbours in the same street are working to different internal deadline calendars.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Al Safa
schoolClusters.note: The second ring of campuses reached by bus along Al Khail Road or Sheikh Zayed Road. These set the earliest realistic weekday session time for the Meadows households that use them, usually somewhere after a quarter past four.

modes.title: Component supervision
modes.description: A weekly slot attached to one unsupervised component: an exploration, a scientific investigation, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. The session is a checkpoint with a deliverable attached, so progress is visible between the school's own internal deadlines rather than only at them. It ends when the component is submitted.

sections.heading: Counting the Diploma hours nobody is timetabled to supervise
paragraphs: Ask a Meadows parent how many hours a week their child is taught and they will know. Ask how many hours of assessed work happen outside those lessons and almost nobody can answer, which is the gap this section closes. The table below separates the Diploma into components and asks two questions of each: is it taught in timetabled lessons, and who checks progress between the school's internal deadlines. The pattern is consistent. The components with the highest ratio of independent work to supervision are the ones where grades drift.

The internal assessment is the clearest case. It carries 20% of the grade in both mathematics courses and in each of the sciences, it runs over months rather than weeks, and the school's realistic involvement is a lesson or two on the criteria, one set of written comments on one draft, and a signature confirming authenticity at the end. None of that is negligence; it is what thirty students per class allows. But the consequence is that a student who is drifting in October is often not visibly drifting until February, by which point the dataset is thin and the evaluation is being written in a hurry.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay behave the same way with an extra complication: neither sits in a subject a student identifies with, so both lose every scheduling contest against a mathematics deadline. Past-paper practice is the sharpest example of all, because it appears nowhere on any timetable and yet it is the activity with the highest return in the final six months of any course. A Meadows household that treats these four things as timetabled commitments, with a named hour in the week, is doing the single most useful thing available to it.

sections.heading: The exploration is a project with no project manager
paragraphs: Of all the unsupervised components, the mathematics exploration is the one Meadows families ask about most, partly because it arrives in DP1 when nothing else is urgent and partly because the marks are so legible once you see the criteria. It is worth 20% of the grade. It is marked against five published criteria worth twenty marks between them, and the weighting is lopsided in a way that surprises students: presentation and mathematical communication are worth four marks each, personal engagement and reflection three each, and the mathematics itself six.

Read that distribution again, because it explains most mid-range explorations. Fourteen of the twenty marks are awarded for how the work is framed, communicated, reflected on and personally owned. A student who picks a difficult topic and executes it coldly can score well on the mathematics and still land in the middle overall. A student who picks a modest topic they genuinely care about, writes clearly, uses correct notation throughout and reflects meaningfully on what the result means can score higher with less advanced content. That is not a loophole. It is what the criteria say, and almost nobody reads them before choosing a topic.

The supervision problem is scheduling. An exploration has a submission deadline set by the school and no intermediate structure, so it competes with everything that has a weekly deadline and loses. The fix is a short series of checkpoints with a deliverable at each: topic shortlist, dataset or model secured, a complete first pass with notation checked, a reflection section drafted. A tutor working this way is supervising rather than teaching, and the student still produces every word, which is the only arrangement IB academic honesty rules permit.

sections.heading: Every Diploma word and page limit in one table
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes this, and it is one of the most useful things a Diploma parent can have on the fridge. Each assessed written component has a ceiling, the ceilings differ by subject, and exceeding them costs marks or results in work not being read beyond the limit. The table below collects the limits for the components Meadows students most often sit. It is a planning tool rather than a target list: a 4,000 word ceiling on the Extended Essay is not an instruction to write 3,980.

The limits shape the work in ways students do not anticipate. A 3,000 word ceiling on a scientific investigation means the method cannot be narrated step by step, so the write-up has to be designed before the data is collected. A 950 word commentary across three objects in the Theory of Knowledge exhibition is roughly three hundred words per object, which rules out any attempt to say everything. A 1,600 word Theory of Knowledge essay on a prescribed title has room for two developed arguments and a counter-position, and no more. Students who discover this at the editing stage lose their best material to the word count.

Two practical notes. First, confirm each limit against the current subject guide through your school, because guides are revised and this page is a summary rather than the source. Second, build the limit into the plan at the start: allocate words to sections before writing, then write to the allocation. Students who do that submit on time and in range; students who write freely and then cut spend a weekend deleting their own analysis to make room for an introduction they should have shortened in the first place.

sections.heading: IGCSE study leave: the three weeks that move the grade most
paragraphs: For a Year 11 student in The Meadows the decisive period is not a term, it is the stretch between the last taught lesson and the first paper. Schools call it study leave, it typically runs two to three weeks, and it will shift results more than either of the preceding terms. It is also completely unsupervised. The student is at home in a quiet villa with a timetable they wrote themselves, if they wrote one, and a pile of revision guides that feel useful and mostly are not.

The failure is specific and predictable. Left alone, almost every sixteen-year-old re-reads notes and highlights them, because that feels like studying and produces no measurable gain. What moves marks is working timed questions from the correct board, marking them against the published mark scheme, and recording in one place what each lost mark was lost for. After a week of that a student has a list of perhaps a dozen recurring errors, and almost all of them are fixable in an hour each: a unit never carried through, a command term consistently misread, a graph axis never labelled, a rearrangement always done the long way.

A plan written before study leave starts is worth more than any teaching during it. Build the days around papers rather than topics, two or three papers a day at most with marking time attached, and keep subjects separated rather than blended. Protect one full rest day a week, because a Meadows student who works thirteen days straight will spend the fourteenth doing nothing useful anyway. And get the right series and the right timetable: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and the board states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone version was used.

sections.heading: Command terms are the vocabulary the mark scheme is written in
paragraphs: A persistent pattern in Meadows students who read well and score averagely is that they answer every question in the same register. Asked to state, they explain at length and run out of time. Asked to evaluate, they describe and score in the lower band. The command term is not decoration at the front of a question; it is the instruction that tells the marker what to look for, and the mark allocation is calibrated to it. A two-mark state question has no reward available for a paragraph of context.

The table below sets out the terms that appear most often across IB and Cambridge papers, what each one actually requires, and the answer type that loses marks. It is worth printing. The highest-value hour a tutor can spend with a student who is already competent is often not on content at all: it is taking a past paper the student has already done, covering the answers, and rewriting four responses to match their command terms exactly. The gain shows up immediately in the next mock.

There is a second-order benefit for internal assessments. Criteria descriptors use the same vocabulary, so a student who has learned to distinguish describe from evaluate in a written paper is better equipped to read what criterion D on an investigation is asking for. Students who treat command terms as a single skill shared across papers and coursework make faster progress than those who treat the exam and the coursework as separate projects, which is how most schools' timetables implicitly present them.

sections.heading: The home-tutor question from a Meadows villa, answered honestly
paragraphs: Meadows households have the space that makes an in-home tutor attractive. There is a study or a dining room with a door, so the objection that applies in a smaller townhouse does not apply here. The appeal is real: a person in the room who takes the phone away, keeps the student on the page, and gives a parent something visible to point at. Any page that dismisses that as old-fashioned is selling rather than answering.

The accounting is still what it is. Published Dubai market rates for an in-home visit run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 200 to 450 for an online subject specialist, and the difference is travel time priced into the fee rather than better teaching. Available people are those willing to drive into Emirates Living in the evening, which in practice skews towards generalists rather than Higher Level subject specialists. The start time is set by the tutor's previous booking. And the components this page is about, explorations, Extended Essays, Theory of Knowledge essays, timed paper practice, do not benefit from physical presence in any measurable way; they benefit from a specialist who has supervised twenty of them.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody will be sent to a Meadows address. Lessons here are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing for drafts and a document camera for working. The table below compares the two models on the questions a Meadows parent actually asks rather than on the ones a marketing page prefers.

sections.heading: Supervision without authorship: the line on assessed work
paragraphs: Everything above describes a tutor supervising work that must be entirely the student's own, so the boundary deserves stating precisely rather than implied. Under IB academic honesty rules an internal assessment, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by a school supervisor and declared by the school. A malpractice finding falls on the student, not on whoever was paid. At least one page competing for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments outright, and a Meadows parent should recognise that for what it is.

What supervision legitimately includes is a long list. Teaching what the published criteria reward, and reading them with the student line by line. Reading a draft the student produced and returning written comments and questions on it. Asking the question that exposes a method the student cannot yet explain. Checking notation, units and labelling. Planning a timeline backwards from the school's internal deadline and holding the student to intermediate checkpoints. Teaching the statistical treatment a dataset needs. None of that puts a tutor's sentence into a submission.

What it excludes is simple to state: no part of a submitted assessment should exist unless the student made it. No sentence, no calculation, no diagram, no restructured paragraph typed by somebody else. We also do not pass on board materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the correct behaviour is to cite and link the official source rather than hand a family a copy. If a provider offers your child finished coursework, that is an integrity problem with an invoice attached.
bullets: Legitimate: reading the criteria together, commenting on the student's draft
Legitimate: checkpoints planned backwards from the school's internal deadline
Never: authoring any sentence, calculation or diagram in a submission
Never: supplying syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as files

sections.heading: Starting from The Meadows, with the limits stated up front
paragraphs: The useful first message is short and factual: the school, the board, the syllabus code on the entry, the level, which component is at risk and when the next internal deadline falls. If the concern is an exploration or an Extended Essay, say what stage it is at honestly, including if the answer is that nothing has been written. We then name the tutor who would supervise it, where they are based, and what they have taught at that exact level, before anything is paid. A trial session follows at a time set around the school bus.

The limits are worth stating now. Coverage is uneven in narrow Higher Level subjects, in less common languages and in uncommon Pearson Edexcel options, and the honest response is one of three things rather than a hopeful match: a different hour where the right specialist is free, an adjacent level or board where the overlap is genuine and the gap can be named, or a plain statement that we cannot cover it. Component supervision also has a timing limit. An exploration with ten days left is a damage-limitation exercise, and we will say so rather than imply otherwise.

On money and data: the rate is agreed before the first paid session, no figure on this page is a quote, and there is no outcome-linked refund scheme because an honest one is difficult to write and easy to misuse. Forms on this site ask for a parent's contact details and the child's year, board and subject, which is what matching needs. A photograph, a grade history and a teacher's name are not required to arrange a trial. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs the handling of that data, and the privacy link explains how to have it removed.

process.title: Name the component, not just the subject
process.description: Tutoring for an exploration, an Extended Essay or a study-leave block is a different job from weekly subject teaching, and the plan differs accordingly. Tell us which component is at risk, what stage it is at, and the date of the school's next internal deadline. Those three facts shape everything that follows.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and the level
process.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher are both called IGCSE Maths and are different examinations with different papers and calculator rules. The code on the school's entry confirmation removes the guesswork, and for Diploma students the Higher or Standard Level split decides which papers matter.

process.title: We name the tutor before any payment
process.description: You are told who would teach, where they are based, which board and level they cover and what they have supervised at that level. If nobody suitable is free at the hour you need, you hear that rather than being matched to a generalist who will work hard against the wrong specification.

process.title: A checkpoint plan after the first session
process.description: For component work you get a short written plan with dated checkpoints running back from the school's internal deadline, each with a deliverable the student produces. For weekly subject teaching you get the list of components at risk and the order they will be worked on. Either way the student owns the deliverables.

process.title: Review at the school's reporting points
process.description: Progress conversations happen when the school issues a report, so independent evidence is in the room rather than only our own session notes. At each review there is a decision rather than a drift: continue, change the component focus, change the tutor, or stop because the job is done.

whyPoints.title: We work on the part nobody supervises
whyPoints.description: Explorations, investigations, Extended Essays, Theory of Knowledge and timed paper practice are where the unsupervised share of a grade lives. A tutor who only re-teaches content is duplicating the school at a price. The useful work is almost always on the components that appear on no timetable.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and limits, read properly
whyPoints.description: Fourteen of the twenty marks on a mathematics exploration are awarded for framing, communication, engagement and reflection rather than for advanced content. Most students never read that distribution. Sessions here start with the published criteria and the word limit, because those decide the ceiling before any work begins.

whyPoints.title: One board, one level, one named tutor
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches one named syllabus rather than a subject in general, which is why we ask for the code rather than the subject name. It is also the reason an online match beats a local one: the right Higher Level specialist is unlikely to live within a short drive of Meadows 4.

whyPoints.title: A line on assessed work that does not move
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, read drafts the student wrote and give written feedback. Nobody authors any part of a submission, and we do not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. The official source is where those belong, and we link it rather than copy it.

whyPoints.title: Stated coverage limits, including the timing ones
whyPoints.description: Some Higher Level subjects and uncommon options are thinly covered, and some component work starts too late to rescue. You get the real position in the first reply, including a plain no, rather than a match that looks like coverage and an exploration that was never going to be finished properly.

faqs.question: How much of an IB Diploma grade is earned outside timetabled lessons?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter. The internal assessment carries 20% of the grade in both mathematics courses and in each of the sciences, and 30% at Standard Level in economics. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute up to three points on the Diploma matrix, and both are largely self-directed. Timed past-paper practice, the highest-return activity in the final six months, appears on no timetable at all. A school can set deadlines, teach the criteria once and comment on one draft; what it cannot do is check on a Tuesday evening whether the work has moved since Sunday.

faqs.question: My child's exploration has not started and the deadline is in six weeks. Is that recoverable?
faqs.answer: Usually, but the shape of the work changes. With six weeks the sensible route is a modest topic the student genuinely owns, a dataset or model that is already accessible, and a write-up designed before any analysis begins. That protects the criteria that carry most of the marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement and reflection are worth fourteen of the twenty marks between them. With ten days left it becomes damage limitation and we will say so. Nothing in this arrangement involves anyone other than the student producing the work.

faqs.question: What are the word limits on IB coursework?
faqs.answer: They differ by component. The Extended Essay has a 4,000 word ceiling; the Theory of Knowledge essay 1,600 words and the exhibition commentary 950 words across three objects; the scientific investigation in biology, chemistry and physics 3,000 words; the history historical investigation 2,200 words; the English A Higher Level essay a 1,200 to 1,500 word range; the Business Management Higher Level research project 1,800 words. The mathematics exploration is guided by a recommended 12 to 20 pages rather than a word count. Confirm each against the current subject guide through your school, because guides are revised periodically.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge worth paying for help with?
faqs.answer: It is one of the better-value components to support, for an unintuitive reason: it is assessed, it contributes to the matrix points, and it is thinly timetabled, so a few structured hours move it further than the same hours in a subject that is taught five times a week. The exhibition needs three objects that can each be justified in roughly three hundred words, and the essay needs two developed arguments plus a counter-position inside 1,600 words. Students who leave both until the term they are due consistently score below their ability, not through weakness but through compression.

faqs.question: How should a Year 11 student use the study-leave weeks before IGCSEs?
faqs.answer: With a plan written before study leave starts, built around papers rather than topics. Two or three timed papers a day at most, each marked against the published mark scheme for the correct board, with every lost mark logged and categorised. After a week the log usually shows about a dozen recurring errors, most fixable in an hour each: a unit never carried through, a command term consistently misread, an unlabelled axis. Keep subjects separated rather than blended, and protect one full rest day a week, because thirteen days straight produces a wasted fourteenth.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in class and badly in exams?
faqs.answer: The most common cause we see is command terms. A student answers every question in the same register: asked to state, they explain at length and lose time; asked to evaluate, they describe and sit in the lower band. The mark allocation is calibrated to the command term, so a two-mark state question has no reward available for a paragraph. The fastest fix is to take a paper the student has already done, cover the answers and rewrite four responses to match their command terms exactly. The gain usually shows in the next mock.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our villa in Meadows 6 instead of teaching online?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Tuition for Meadows families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing for drafts and a document camera for written working. For context, the published Dubai market rate for an in-home visit runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 200 to 450 for an online subject specialist, and the difference is travel priced into the hour. The components this page covers gain nothing measurable from physical presence.

faqs.question: What does Diploma coursework support cost per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands, surveyed October 2026, put an IB or IGCSE subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more per hour and a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300. Generalist and university-student tutors are quoted from AED 45 to 150, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the fee, and named or examiner-branded tutors at AED 500 to 650 and above. Those figures come from published platform and agency rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They are market rates, not our price list.

faqs.question: Does the school not supervise the Extended Essay already?
faqs.answer: It does, at set meeting points, and that supervision is a genuine requirement rather than a formality: the supervisor authenticates the work and the school declares it. What the structure does not provide is anything between those meetings. A student with 4,000 words to produce over several months, competing against weekly deadlines in six subjects, will deprioritise it unless something external creates intermediate pressure. Supervision support fills that gap with dated checkpoints and a deliverable at each, while the student writes every word themselves.

faqs.question: Is A Level a lighter independent-study load than the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Different rather than lighter. A Level removes the core, so there is no Extended Essay, no Theory of Knowledge and usually no equivalent of the internal assessment in several subjects, which cuts the number of unsupervised components. In exchange the content per subject is deeper and in most subjects the entire grade rests on terminal written papers, which places the whole weight on timed practice that no timetable covers. A student who coasted through IGCSE on recall meets that wall in the first term either way.

faqs.question: Should both my children have the same tutor if they study different boards?
faqs.answer: Only where the two demands are the same skill at different depths. A Year 11 Cambridge 0580 Extended student and a Year 8 student both need algebraic fluency, so one tutor can plan across both. A Diploma Higher Level chemist and a Year 10 Pearson Edexcel student do not, because Higher Level organic depth sits far above the IGCSE specification. A Middle Years student needing Personal Project supervision and a Diploma student needing timed unseen analysis are different jobs. Where boards differ we use two specialists on one shared calendar rather than one compromise.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a UAE permit to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE operates under a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website or e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit faces fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so distrust any specific figure.

faqs.question: Can lessons keep running while we travel over the long summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the summer is often the best window for component work. Because lessons are delivered online over live video, the same tutor and usually the same slot continue from wherever the family is, with an allowance for the time difference. Summer is when an exploration topic can be settled without six other subjects competing, when a Middle Years student can prepare for the Personal Project, and when a student moving into the Diploma can close the quantitative gaps in mathematics and the sciences. During Ramadan sessions generally move to a post-Iftar slot, agreed in advance.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is available for a subject like Higher Level Philosophy?
faqs.answer: You get told plainly. Coverage in narrow Higher Level subjects, less common languages and uncommon Pearson Edexcel options is genuinely uneven, and the standard industry response is to seat a generalist in front of the student and hope. We will give whichever of three answers is true: a different hour of the week where the right specialist is free, an adjacent level or board where the content overlap is real and the gap can be named, or a clear statement that we cannot cover it with a suggestion of where to look. A match that only looks like coverage costs a Diploma student a term.

dubai/the-meadows.closingHeading: Start with the component, not the subject
dubai/the-meadows.closingBody: If something in your house has a deadline and no supervision, that is the thing to tell us about. Send the school, the board, the syllabus code, the component and the next internal deadline, and you will get back the name of the person who could supervise it and the hours they have free. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video. If the honest answer is that the deadline is too close for the work to be done properly, you will hear that in the first reply rather than after four paid sessions, and you can spend the time on the papers instead.

Each teaches one named syllabus.

intro.heading: Who actually lives in The Springs, and what that does to tutoring
paragraphs: The Springs sits inside Emirates Living, between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, and is made up of fifteen numbered sub-communities of two- and three-bedroom townhouses laid out around artificial lakes. Springs 1 through 15 were built in the early 2000s, which makes this one of the older family communities in what Dubai still calls New Dubai. The Springs Souk anchors the middle of it. Units are small by Dubai villa standards: a compact ground floor with an open-plan living and dining space, two or three bedrooms upstairs, and a garden measured in square metres rather than in trees. That footprint matters more to tutoring than any other single fact about the neighbourhood.

Two household types dominate. The first is the long-tenure family, five to twelve years in the same unit, with children spread across primary, Year 10 and the Diploma at the same time. These parents are not shopping for a tutor; they are solving a specific, named problem they have already watched develop over two school reports. The second is the family that moved out of an apartment in the Greens or the Views to get a garden and a bus stop, usually with children in Foundation Stage to Year 6, who are suddenly inside a British-curriculum pathway that leads to IGCSE at sixteen and a decision at eighteen they have not thought about yet.

School routes out of The Springs split in a way that confuses everybody's recommendations. Emirates International School Meadows sits a few minutes away and runs the full IB continuum, PYP through MYP to the Diploma. Almost everything else in the surrounding cluster is British: Regent International School in The Greens, Dubai British School Emirates Hills, GEMS Wellington International in Al Sufouh, Nord Anglia International School Dubai in Al Barsha South, Jumeirah College in Al Safa. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is the other IB option nearby. The practical consequence is that in one Springs cul-de-sac you will find a Middle Years student graded on criteria out of eight, a Year 11 student sitting Cambridge papers, a Year 11 student sitting Pearson Edexcel papers, and a Diploma student working on an exploration, all in the same week.

That is why the neighbour's recommendation travels so badly here. A tutor who is genuinely good with a Regent Year 10 Edexcel maths class is not automatically the right person for an Emirates International School Meadows MYP 4 student, because one is teaching towards a tiered written paper and the other is teaching towards four criteria with published descriptors. The second constraint is the townhouse itself. There is usually one table that works, it is in earshot of everything, and a younger sibling is at it. Any plan that ignores the geometry of a three-bedroom Springs unit falls apart in week three.

So this page does the things a Springs parent actually needs. It sets out how to plan a week when two children sit different boards, what the gap between MYP 5 and DP1 really contains, what the Dubai market charges in AED per hour and who published those numbers, why families here search for a home tutor and what IB Gram does instead, how the mandatory UAE subjects work inside a British or IB school, and how to count backwards from the exam series your child is actually entered for.
