dubai/the-springs.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover nearly every child in The Springs. Which one your family is inside decides what a tutor should be doing week to week, because the assessment machinery behind each is genuinely different rather than differently named.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than subject textbooks, and it reports against learner attributes and approaches to learning rather than percentages. Parents moving in from a British primary often read a PYP report and cannot tell whether their child is behind. Tutoring at this stage is almost never about the inquiry units. It is about securing number fluency, reading stamina and written sentence control, because those are the things that a Year 7 setting decision will quietly test later.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows is the PYP route that most Springs families consider, and it feeds its own MYP directly. Families who choose a British primary in the cluster instead should know that a move into the Middle Years Programme later is a change of assessment language, not just a change of uniform, and that it is easier at the start of MYP 1 than halfway through MYP 4.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, converted to a programme grade from 1 to 7. The published criteria are specific: in mathematics they cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student can be numerically strong and still sit on a 4 because the investigating and communicating criteria are never practised. MYP 5 also carries the Personal Project, which is supervised, reflective and assessed on process as much as product.
programmes.countryNote: In The Springs the MYP cohort is concentrated in one school, which means a Springs parent comparing notes with a neighbour is usually comparing against a different system entirely. If your child is in MYP 4 or 5 and the Diploma is the plan, the subjects to protect are mathematics and the sciences, because those are where the DP assumes the most unstated prior content.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Forty-two points come from the six subjects and up to three more from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Each subject carries an internal assessment: 20% in the sciences and in both mathematics courses, 30% at Standard Level in economics. Higher Level mathematics adds a third written paper worth 20% of the grade, which is where HL students most often lose ground.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in The Springs are split between Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, with a handful travelling further. Exam entries, internal deadlines and the Extended Essay timetable are set by the school, not by the IB, so the first job of any Diploma tutoring plan here is to get the school's own internal deadline sheet in front of the tutor.

programmes.name: IGCSE at Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Two boards dominate Dubai, and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge splits most subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended running A* to E; Pearson Edexcel tiers mathematics as Foundation and Higher instead, with Higher reaching grade 9. Paper counts, calculator rules and practical arrangements differ subject by subject. A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers is doing accurate teaching against the wrong specification.
programmes.countryNote: Springs children sit IGCSEs at several different schools, so the household question is always which board and which tier, not which subject. Ask the school for the syllabus code on the entry, not the subject name: Cambridge 0580 Extended mathematics and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher are both called IGCSE Maths in conversation and look nothing alike on the day.

dubai/the-springs.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Springs households ask about most often, in the form the request usually arrives. Each note says what the component actually assesses and where the marks tend to go missing, because that is the part a school report rarely spells out.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry this course. At Higher Level the third paper is a long extended-response investigation worth 20% of the grade, and it rewards a style of sustained mathematical reasoning that neither Paper 1 nor Paper 2 practises. Most HL marks lost here are lost to abandoned part-questions rather than to wrong methods.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work. The graphical display calculator is assumed throughout, including in Paper 1, which surprises students coming from a non-calculator IGCSE paper. The exploration is where AI students gain or lose most ground, because a weak dataset limits the marks available under the mathematical communication and use of mathematics criteria.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The current course assesses through two written papers and a single scientific investigation worth 20% at both levels. Mechanics and fields reward algebraic confidence; the data-based questions reward reading a graph for gradient and intercept meaning rather than for shape. Students who were strong at IGCSE physics often stall at the point where uncertainty and error propagation first count for marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where Higher Level separates from Standard Level. The investigation is 20% of the grade at both levels and is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The single most common loss is an evaluation section that lists limitations without explaining their direction or size of effect on the result.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where command terms decide marks. Outline, describe, explain and evaluate carry different expectations and different mark allocations, and a student who answers every question as describe will cap out well below their understanding. Statistical treatment in the investigation is the other recurring gap for students arriving from IGCSE double award science.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries built on published news articles, worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level, and it is usually the first piece of extended analytical writing a Diploma student produces. Diagram accuracy, correct axis labelling and explicit links back to the article are where the marks sit. Higher Level adds quantitative work and policy evaluation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text under time pressure, which rewards a repeatable approach to structure, audience and effect rather than wide reading. The individual oral and the HL essay are both internally prepared and both have strict parameters. Students who read widely but never practise a timed opening paragraph tend to underperform their ability here.

subjects.name: English as a second language and English B
subjects.description: Cambridge 0510 and 0511 assess reading, writing and listening against a different specification from first-language English, and schools sometimes enter a bilingual student in the wrong one. At Diploma level English B tests receptive and productive skills with a prescribed text-type range. The decision about which route a Springs student should take is better made in Year 9 than in Year 11.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Non-Arab students in a Dubai private school take Arabic as an additional language as a KHDA mandatory subject, and some also sit Cambridge 0544 Arabic as a foreign language. The mandatory stream and the examined qualification are not the same thing, and progress in one does not automatically show up in the other. Support here is mostly about vocabulary retention and script fluency.

subjects.name: Business Management and Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study command and calculation accuracy decide these subjects, not business opinion. At Diploma level the Higher Level course carries extra content on strategy and finance plus a research project built on a real organisation. At IGCSE, Cambridge 0450 answers lose marks for giving advantages and disadvantages where the question asked for a justified recommendation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Cambridge 0478 splits theory from practical problem-solving, and the programming paper is where students who have only used block-based environments struggle. At Diploma level the internal assessment is a developed solution with documentation, and the documentation carries a large share of the marks. Planning the solution on paper before any code is written is the single highest-value habit here.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Both are source-and-structure subjects. IGCSE geography loses marks on case-study specificity, where a named place and a named figure beat a general description every time. Diploma history is built on comparative argument and a historical investigation with a strict word limit, and the investigation's evaluation of sources is routinely the weakest section when it arrives unplanned.

dubai/the-springs.regionsIntro: The Springs is one piece of Emirates Living, and families here move between its neighbours constantly for school, sport and swimming. These notes are about what each adjacent community means for a school run and an evening study slot, not about property.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Directly adjacent, larger villas, and the community that shares the Emirates International School Meadows campus. A Meadows and Springs household can run the same bus route, which makes a shared evening tutoring slot workable across two families on the same board.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Lower density and slightly later bus pickups, with children spread across the same Emirates Living and Al Sufouh schools. Lakes families often sit on the same internal deadline calendar as Springs families, which is useful when planning an exploration or coursework block.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Apartments overlooking the Emirates Golf Club, with a younger average child age and a high turnover of tenancies. Mid-year arrivals are common here, and a mid-year arrival into Year 10 is the single hardest IGCSE catch-up case in this cluster.

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: The apartment counterpart to The Springs and the location of Regent International School. A short hop by car, but the evening exit onto Sheikh Zayed Road is slow enough that a 5pm in-home appointment here regularly becomes a 5:25pm start.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large villas, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Dubai British School within the same perimeter. Diploma students from The Springs frequently study alongside Emirates Hills students, which makes it the nearest comparison point for Higher Level subject choices.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: Villa communities on the far side of Sheikh Zayed Road with their own British school provision. Families who moved here from The Springs usually keep the same tutor and the same slot, because an online lesson survives a house move in a way an in-home arrangement does not.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Where several of the cluster's larger campuses sit, including Nord Anglia International School Dubai. The Al Khail Road run between here and The Springs is quick at 7am and unreliable at 5pm, which is the main reason evening slots get pushed past 6pm.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living schools
schoolClusters.note: The schools inside or on the edge of the Emirates Living district, which take most Springs children. One runs the IB continuum and the others are British-curriculum, so a single street can contain MYP, Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel students at the same stage.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Al Safa campuses
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, reached along Al Khail Road or Sheikh Zayed Road. These campuses pull Springs children for sixth form and for specific subject provision, and their bus routes set the earliest realistic weekday lesson time for the households that use them.

dubai/the-springs.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Springs request. All of them run online over live video with one named tutor, and the choice between them is about the shape of the problem rather than about budget alone.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one by subject
modes.description: One tutor, one subject, one board, at a fixed weekly time that survives the school term. This is the format that works for a student who is coping but underperforming, and it is the only format that builds the kind of cumulative record a parent can read against a school report. The slot is set after the bus, not before it.

modes.title: Sibling split timetable
modes.description: Two children on different boards, planned as one household rather than two accounts. Usually that means back-to-back slots on the same evening so the table is only occupied once, with the exam-year child taking the earlier and better hour. Different tutors, one shared calendar, one conversation about priorities.

modes.description: A fixed number of sessions run tight against a known exam series, built entirely around timed questions, mark-scheme reading and the student's own error log. This is not revision teaching; it assumes the content is broadly there and the marks are being lost in execution. It is the right format in the final six to eight weeks and the wrong one in September.

sections.heading: The Springs townhouse is the scheduling problem, not the tutor
paragraphs: A Springs unit is a compact plan. The ground floor is one open space, the kitchen opens onto it, and there is almost never a door between the dining table and the television. Upstairs there are two or three bedrooms, one of them small enough that the desk faces a wall at the end of a bed. This is a good house to raise a family in and a difficult house to run two simultaneous evening study sessions in, which is exactly what households here end up needing by the time a first child reaches Year 10.

The practical consequence is that the first conversation about tutoring should be about where the lesson happens before it is about who teaches it. The best Springs setups we see are not the grandest. They are a bedroom desk with a wired connection or a 5 GHz band, a cheap pair of over-ear headphones with a boom microphone so the student can be heard without shouting over a sibling, and a tablet or second phone propped as a document camera so the tutor can see the working rather than the face. That last item changes maths and physics lessons more than any platform feature.

It also decides the timetable. In a two- or three-bedroom unit, two children cannot study in different rooms if one of those rooms is where somebody sleeps at eight o'clock. So the realistic pattern here is sequential rather than parallel: one child at 5:15pm and the other at 6:15pm, both at the same table, with the room handed over cleanly. That is unremarkable planning, but it is the difference between a tutoring arrangement that lasts a term and one that quietly collapses in week four when the novelty of the first slot wears off.
bullets: Wired or 5 GHz connection beats a stronger laptop every time
A second device as a document camera shows working, not faces

Headphones with a boom microphone end the shouting problem

sections.heading: Two children, two boards, one week: planning a sibling split
paragraphs: The defining feature of tutoring in The Springs is that the second child is rarely on the same system as the first. A long-tenure household might have a Diploma student at one school and a Middle Years student at another, or an older child who sat Cambridge papers and a younger one entered for Pearson Edexcel because the family changed schools in between. Parents reasonably assume one tutor can cover both, and sometimes one person technically can, but the two jobs are not the same job and pretending otherwise costs the younger child.

The table below sets out the sibling pairs we see most often in Emirates Living and what each child actually needs. Read the last column first. It is the honest answer to the question every Springs parent asks at some point, which is whether one good maths tutor can take both children and halve the cost. Where the two demands are the same skill at different depths, one tutor is sensible. Where one child needs criterion-based project supervision and the other needs timed paper technique, splitting them is not an upsell, it is the only arrangement that works.

Sequencing matters as much as matching. In an exam year, the child sitting papers takes the better hour, which in this neighbourhood means the first slot after the bus and before dinner rather than the 7:30pm slot when nobody is sharp. The younger child takes the later slot and a shorter session, usually forty-five minutes rather than sixty, because attention rather than content is the limiting factor at that age. And one review conversation covering both children, once a term, replaces two separate progress calls that tell a parent the same thing twice.

sections.heading: From MYP 5 into DP1: the bridge nobody puts in the diary
paragraphs: Continuum students have an advantage that gets talked about and a specific disadvantage that does not. The advantage is familiarity: the same school, the same teachers, the same vocabulary of inquiry and reflection. The disadvantage is that the Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria with published descriptors, while the Diploma assesses against grade boundaries on written papers, and nothing in MYP 5 trains a student to work under a clock against a mark scheme they will never see. A student who finished MYP 5 on a 6 can land a 4 in their first DP1 mock without anything having gone wrong.

The second half of the problem is unstated content. Diploma courses assume a baseline that the Middle Years Programme does not promise, because MYP is deliberately not a syllabus-coverage system. In mathematics the gap is usually algebraic manipulation speed and trigonometric identities. In the sciences it is quantitative handling: moles, uncertainties, rearranging equations under time pressure. In economics and psychology, which most students meet for the first time at DP1, there is no prior content at all, only the question of whether the student can write a structured analytical paragraph.

The sensible intervention is short, specific and happens in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 rather than in October when the first assessment has already gone badly. Six to ten sessions per subject, targeted at the gaps in the table below, changes the shape of DP1. It is also the cheapest tutoring a Springs family will ever buy, because it is preventative rather than remedial, and because a Diploma student who starts DP1 behind in two subjects usually ends up buying support in both of them for two years.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Emirates Living, in AED and with sources
paragraphs: Most providers in this market will not publish a number. Of the ranking pages reviewed for this project in October 2026, several quote no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The bands in the table below are market figures taken from published rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are what the Dubai market charges, not an IB Gram price list, and they are published here so a Springs parent can tell whether a quote they have been given is normal.

Two things are worth noticing in the table. The in-home band is higher than the online specialist band, and that difference is travel time being priced into the hour rather than better teaching being paid for. And the top band is scarcity pricing on a named individual rather than a different product. Published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with package offers seen at around AED 799 per month online for eight sessions.

For context on the household budget: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the emirate valued at AED 1.5 billion. That makes 2026-27 an unusual year in which the fee line is flat and the tutoring line is the variable one. Ask any provider, including us, three questions before committing: is the quoted figure per hour or per session, does it include VAT, and what happens to money already paid if you stop after one lesson. Get all three answers in writing.

sections.heading: Why a Springs family searches for a home tutor, and what happens instead
paragraphs: The search phrase that brings most families to this page includes the words home tutor, and the reason is sensible rather than sentimental. A parent who has watched a child slump at a laptop for two years of school assessments wants somebody physically present who will take the phone away and sit there until the question is finished. In a community of three-bedroom townhouses where the dining table is also the study, having a stranger at that table for an hour is also a visible, auditable thing. Those are real arguments and they deserve a real answer rather than a sales line.

Here is the honest accounting. Market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the tutor's travel is inside the fee. The pool of available people is whoever is willing to drive to Emirates Living at five in the evening, which in practice means generalists rather than Higher Level specialists, and it means the start time is set by the tutor's previous booking rather than by your bus. Al Khail Road between Interchange 4 and the Al Barsha exits does not cooperate at that hour. Families who try it usually report that the teaching was fine and the logistics were what failed.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and no tutor will be sent to a Springs address. Lessons here run online, one-to-one, over live video, with one named tutor per subject and the session time set around the school bus. The trade is deliberate: a Springs family gets a Chemistry Higher Level specialist or a Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher specialist instead of whoever happened to be free within a twenty-minute drive, and the hour that would have been travel stays in the lesson.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies inside a British or IB school
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver. This is not a school policy that varies between Emirates Living campuses; it follows a federal rule that private schools must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations on Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and KHDA's own mandatory-subject guidelines set out how it is implemented, with requirements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Most Springs parents first think about it in Year 9, when it starts affecting an option block.

The detail that catches families out is the class organisation rule. KHDA requires schools to run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies it is the school's licensed-curriculum language. Instructional time is planned on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

There is a hard limit on what any tutor can do here. For the mandatory UAE subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so legitimate support means working on the school's own material, vocabulary retention, script fluency and the mechanics of writing in Arabic rather than importing a parallel course. Schools are also required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a reasonable thing for a parent to ask about. One more wrinkle for British-curriculum families: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five subjects required for Ministry of Education equivalency.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the series your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what decides whether tutoring starts early enough to matter. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, with a March series as well, plus Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year. The table below uses Cambridge's own published key dates for the March 2027 series as a worked example of how far ahead the real deadlines sit.

Read the first row again. Final entries for a series that begins in February 2027 were due on 27 November 2026, which means the board, the tier and the option codes are locked more than two months before the first paper. A family that decides in January to move a child from Core to Extended has usually missed the decision. There is one further trap specific to this region: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the school which zone it sits in.

For Pearson Edexcel, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is always the document to work from rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. For the IB Diploma this page deliberately publishes no dates at all: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every Diploma deadline with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on internal assessments and coursework
paragraphs: This is the part of the market that needs saying plainly, because at least one page ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments. Under IB academic honesty rules an internal assessment, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by a supervisor at the school and declared by the school. A student who submits anything else risks a malpractice finding, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever took the money. No tutoring arrangement is worth that risk.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial, and it is worth spelling out so a Springs parent knows what they are buying. A tutor can teach the skills an assessment needs: how an exploration is structured, what the published criteria reward, how to read a dataset, how an evaluation section should discuss the direction and size of an effect rather than list limitations. A tutor can read a draft the student has produced and give feedback on it, in writing, as comments and questions the student then acts on. A tutor can ask the awkward question that reveals the student does not yet understand their own method. A tutor can help plan a timeline against the school's internal deadlines.

What a tutor must never do is become the author. No sentence, paragraph, calculation or diagram should reach a submitted assessment unless the student made it. We also do not supply board materials: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the right behaviour is to point a family at the official source and link it rather than hand over a copy. If a provider offers your child a finished exploration or an essay, that is not a premium service, it is an academic integrity problem with a price tag.
bullets: Legitimate: teaching the criteria, reading a student draft, giving written feedback

sections.heading: Starting from The Springs, and the limits we will tell you about
paragraphs: The first conversation is short and it is about facts rather than aspirations. Which school, which board, which syllabus code on the entry, which tier, which internal deadline is next, and what the last two school reports actually said. If you can send a photo of the subject page from the most recent report, that saves a week. Then we name the tutor who would teach it, including where they are based and what they have taught at that exact level, before any money changes hands. A trial session follows, at a time set around the bus rather than around our calendar.

There are limits and we would rather state them now than discover them with you in week two. Some combinations are thin: a Higher Level subject with a small global cohort, a less common language, or a very specific Pearson Edexcel option can mean no specialist is free at the hour a Springs household needs. In that case there are three honest answers and we will give you whichever is true: a different hour with the right specialist, a nearby alternative with the same board where the content genuinely overlaps, or a clear statement that we cannot cover it and a suggestion of where to look next. Nobody is served by a generalist being presented as a specialist.

On money and data: prices are agreed before the first paid session, we do not run outcome-linked refund schemes, and no figure on this page is a quote. Lead forms on this site collect a parent's contact details and the child's year group, board and subject, because that is what matching needs. We do not need a child's photograph, their grades history or the name of their teacher to arrange a trial. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs how that information is handled, and the privacy link on this page sets out how to have it deleted.

process.title: Send the board, the level and the syllabus code
process.description: Not the subject name. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher are both called IGCSE Maths in conversation and are different examinations. The entry code, the tier and the next internal deadline tell us more in one line than a paragraph of description, and they are all on the school's entry confirmation or the report.

process.title: We name the tutor before you pay
process.description: You get the tutor's name, where they are based, which board and level they teach, and what they have covered at that exact level. If the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free at the hour you need, you hear that instead of being matched to a generalist who will do their best with the wrong specification.

process.title: One trial session, set around the bus
process.description: The trial is a real lesson on real material, not a diagnostic quiz, and it is scheduled after the Springs Souk bus window rather than in a slot that suits us. Any condition attached to a trial is stated before you book it. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than the time.

process.title: A written plan after the second session
process.description: Two sessions is enough to see where marks are actually going missing. You get a short written plan naming the components at risk, what will be practised in what order, and what the student is expected to do between sessions. A plan that depends entirely on the tutor doing the work is a plan that fails in exam conditions.

process.title: Reviews on the school's reporting cycle
process.description: Progress conversations happen when the school issues a report, so there is independent evidence in the room rather than only our own notes. For a Springs household with two children, that is one conversation covering both, once a term, with a clear decision at the end of it about whether to continue, change subject or stop.

whyPoints.title: One board, one level, one tutor
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches one named syllabus rather than a subject in general. That is why we ask for the code rather than the subject name, and it is the main reason an online match beats a local one in this cluster: the right Chemistry Higher Level specialist is unlikely to live within a twenty-minute drive of Springs 9.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around Emirates Living bus times
whyPoints.description: The slot is set after the bus arrives, and it moves by message when a fixture, a trip or a sibling's fixture collides with it. Households with two children get back-to-back slots so the one workable table in a three-bedroom unit is occupied once rather than twice in an evening.

whyPoints.title: Money discussed in AED, openly
whyPoints.description: Market bands are published on this page with their sources so you can judge any quote, ours included. We state whether a figure is per hour or per session, whether VAT is included, and what happens to a prepaid balance if you stop. There is no outcome-linked refund scheme, because an honest one is hard to write and easy to misuse.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the criteria, read drafts the student wrote and give feedback on them. Nobody authors any part of a submission. We also do not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, because those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB and the official source is the right place to get them.

whyPoints.title: We say when we cannot cover something
whyPoints.description: Coverage in niche Higher Level subjects and uncommon Pearson Edexcel options is genuinely uneven. You get the real position, including a plain no where that is the answer, rather than a match that looks like coverage. That disclosure is the single thing none of the competing pages in this market will give you.

faqs.question: Which schools do most children in The Springs go to?
faqs.answer: The nearest option is Emirates International School Meadows, which runs the full IB continuum from PYP through MYP to the Diploma. Most other Springs children travel to British-curriculum schools: Regent International School in The Greens, Dubai British School Emirates Hills, GEMS Wellington International in Al Sufouh, Nord Anglia International School Dubai in Al Barsha South and Jumeirah College in Al Safa. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is the other nearby IB route. That split is why advice passed between neighbours often does not transfer: one family's child is graded on criteria out of eight and the next family's child is sitting tiered written papers.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our townhouse in Springs 7?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Tuition for Springs families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with one named tutor per subject. The market rate for an in-home visit in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the tutor's travel sits inside the fee, and the pool of people willing to drive to Emirates Living at 5pm is mostly generalists. Online, you are choosing from specialists in the exact board and level rather than from a twenty-minute radius.

faqs.question: We have one child in MYP and one sitting IGCSE. Can the same tutor take both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on whether the two demands are the same skill at different depths. A Year 11 Cambridge 0580 Extended student and a Year 7 student both need number and algebra fluency, so one tutor planning backwards can serve both well. A Diploma Higher Level chemist and a Year 10 Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 student do not, because Higher Level organic depth sits far above the 4CH1 specification. A Middle Years student needing Personal Project supervision and a Diploma student needing timed unseen analysis are different jobs entirely. We will tell you which case you are in before you book.

faqs.question: When should a Springs student start bridging from MYP 5 into DP1?
faqs.answer: In the summer between the two, not in October. The Middle Years Programme assesses against published criteria, while the Diploma assesses against boundaries on timed written papers, and nothing in MYP 5 trains a student to work to a mark scheme under a clock. Six to ten sessions per subject during the break closes the specific gaps: algebraic speed and trigonometric identities for mathematics, moles and uncertainties for chemistry, graph interpretation for physics, structured analytical paragraphs for a new subject like economics. It is the cheapest support a family buys, because it is preventative rather than two years of remedial work.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour for a family in Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands, surveyed in October 2026, run from AED 45 to 150 for a generalist or university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the fee, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. Named or examiner-branded tutors are quoted at AED 500 to 650 and above. Those come from published platform and agency rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They are market figures, not an IB Gram price list; ask us for a quote.

faqs.question: Our townhouse has no spare room. Does online tutoring still work here?
faqs.answer: It works if the setup is planned once rather than improvised weekly. The three things that matter in a three-bedroom Springs unit are a wired or 5 GHz connection, over-ear headphones with a boom microphone so the student can be heard without competing with the room, and a second phone or tablet propped as a document camera so the tutor sees the working rather than the face. That last item changes maths and physics lessons more than anything else. Then run slots sequentially, one child at 5:15pm and the next at 6:15pm, so the single workable table is handed over cleanly.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 Extended harder than Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher?
faqs.answer: They are differently shaped rather than simply harder or easier, and the honest answer depends on the student. Cambridge 0580 splits Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C, and the Extended route includes a non-calculator paper. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 tiers as Foundation and Higher, with Higher reaching grade 9, and allows a calculator in both papers. A student with weak mental arithmetic but strong structured problem solving often reads better on 4MA1. Your school has already chosen, so the practical step is to confirm the code on the entry and have the tutor work from that board's papers only.

faqs.question: Does my child need support in Arabic if we are not an Arabic-speaking family?
faqs.answer: Your child will be taught Arabic as an additional language regardless, because Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever international curriculum it is licensed to teach. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups and prohibits combined ones, and instructional time is planned on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support is worth it if written script and vocabulary retention are holding your child back. It has to work from the school's own material: using different or additional content for a mandatory UAE subject without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed.

faqs.question: Why does this page not print IB Diploma exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them from the IB itself. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and publishing a date that later moves is worse than publishing none. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are different: both boards publish key dates openly and those figures are quoted from their own documents. For your child's Diploma deadlines, including internal coursework dates which the school sets rather than the IB, ask the school's IB coordinator and check ibo.org directly.

faqs.question: Does the person tutoring my child in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you see with caution.

faqs.question: Our neighbour teaches at my child's school. Can she tutor our child privately?
faqs.answer: Treat that as a question for the school before it is a question about money. The permit that allows private tutoring carries a code of conduct, which press reporting indicates bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's ADEK has set professional-ethics rules prohibiting private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Those positions are reported rather than quoted here from the current policy documents, so verify with the school directly. A tutor with no connection to the school avoids the conflict entirely, which is one quiet advantage of matching outside the neighbourhood.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions does a Springs household usually start with?
faqs.answer: One subject, one hour a week, is the normal honest starting point, and two for a Diploma student in an exam year where two components are genuinely at risk. Families who start with four subjects almost always stop within a term, because the student loses every free evening and resents all of it. Published monthly estimates for a single weekly hour in Dubai run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, so the cost of starting narrow and widening later is small compared with the cost of starting wide.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for something like Higher Level Economics?
faqs.answer: You get told. Coverage in narrow Higher Level subjects and uncommon Pearson Edexcel options is genuinely uneven, and the usual industry response is to put a generalist in front of the student and hope. We will offer one of three honest answers: a different hour of the week where the right specialist is free, an adjacent subject or level where the content genuinely overlaps and the gap can be named, or a plain statement that we cannot cover it with a suggestion of where to look next. A match that only looks like coverage costs a Diploma student a term.

faqs.question: How do Springs families handle lessons during Ramadan and over the summer?
faqs.answer: Both are planning questions rather than pauses. During Ramadan school hours shorten and concentration moves later in the day, so sessions generally shift to a post-Iftar slot and sometimes shorten to forty-five minutes; that is agreed in advance rather than rearranged weekly. Over the summer many Springs families travel for several weeks, and because lessons run online the same tutor and the same slot can usually continue from wherever the family is, allowing for the time difference. The summer is also the best window for MYP 5 to DP1 bridging or for closing a gap before Year 11 starts.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE grades count towards UAE equivalency for a British-curriculum child?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement, as reported in July 2026, is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees, so verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

dubai/the-springs.closingHeading: A short first conversation beats a long search
dubai/the-springs.closingBody: If you are in Springs 1 or Springs 15, the useful next step is the same: send the school, the board, the syllabus code and the next internal deadline, and we will tell you who could teach it and when they are free. If two children need support, say so in the same message so the evening can be planned once rather than twice. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video. If the honest answer is that we cannot cover a subject at the hour you need, you will hear that in the first reply rather than in week three, and you will keep the hour you were going to spend searching.

intro.heading: A community on one curriculum, and the part of it that happens after school
paragraphs: The Sustainable City is a net-zero community of around five hundred villas on Al Qudra Road, built in clusters around biodome greenhouses, with an IB continuum school inside it. That last fact makes this community unusual in Dubai. Most neighbourhoods scatter their children across four or five curricula; here a large share of families are on one programme family, from the Primary Years Programme through the Middle Years Programme and into the Diploma, often with the same school for a decade.

A single curriculum simplifies the conversation between neighbours and sharpens one particular problem. The IB is built on work the student does alone. A Diploma subject carries an internal assessment the teacher supervises but cannot write. The Extended Essay is four thousand words produced over roughly a year with a supervisor who is allowed three formal meetings in many schools' own policies. Theory of Knowledge demands a written essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of objects. The Personal Project at the end of MYP 5 is assessed on a process journal the student keeps themselves.

None of that is a teaching failure. It is how the programme is designed, and it is the reason a strong student with excellent reports can still arrive at February of DP2 with three unfinished components. The school has delivered the taught content. What it cannot deliver is the twenty or thirty hours of independent judgement each component needs, spread across months, in the gaps between every other deadline.

There is a second consequence of a one-curriculum community that parents notice late. Because so many neighbours are in the same programme, information travels fast and arrives slightly wrong. A family hears that the Extended Essay is marked out of thirty-four, or that a particular subject is an easy seven, or that six IGCSE subjects are needed for Ministry equivalency, and the claim gets repeated until it is treated as settled. Two of those three examples are wrong, and the third depends on the subject. Anything that will shape a subject choice or a deadline is worth checking against the school's own documents or the authority's own page rather than against the street.

That gap is what this page is about. It sets out which components sit outside taught lessons, what the MYP criteria actually reward, how to choose an investigation question when your own neighbourhood is full of measurable environmental data, where a tutor must stop on work that has to be the student's own, what supervision costs in the Dubai market, and what an IB leaver has to show the Ministry of Education for equivalency. Every lesson described runs online. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and for draft work a shared screen is better than a shared table anyway.

dubai/the-sustainable-city.programmesIntro: Three stages run inside this community at once, and each one hands the student a different kind of independent work. The notes below describe what each stage leaves unsupervised rather than what it teaches.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no grades on most reports and an exhibition in the final year. Parents often cannot tell from a PYP report whether a child is behind in arithmetic or reading, because the reporting language describes dispositions rather than attainment. The exhibition at the end is the first piece of extended independent work most children produce.
programmes.countryNote: Families here usually meet standardised testing for the first time around Year 4, when Dubai schools administer cognitive and attainment tests. A PYP report plus a test percentile is a far more useful pairing than either alone, and reading the two together is often the only diagnostic a Sustainable City primary family actually needs.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, marked out of eight, and converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. A student can revise content thoroughly and see no movement, because the task was weighted to a criterion they never practised. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, assessed on planning, action and reflection recorded in a process journal.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools also run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies for every pupil regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. For an MYP student here that is real timetable time on subjects outside the four criteria, which is why the independent workload lands in evenings.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus three core components. Each subject carries internal assessment marked against criteria named by letter; Theory of Knowledge requires an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition; the Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words. Higher Level adds an extra paper in most sciences and considerably more content depth in mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm every IB session, upload and results date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. This page does not publish IB dates, because they could not be verified from the IB directly for this project, and the school's internal deadlines sit weeks earlier than the board's in any case.

dubai/the-sustainable-city.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested from this community, described by the independent work each one demands rather than by its syllabus headings.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The internal assessment needs a measurable variable, a repeatable method and statistical treatment of the results. Most lost marks sit in the analysis and evaluation criteria rather than the biology. A student who collects data before defining the hypothesis has usually lost those marks before the writing starts.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that rewards systems thinking and penalises description. The internal assessment is an individual investigation with a strong preference for primary data, which students in a community built around measurable resource use are unusually well placed to collect.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, kinetics and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level difficulty. The internal assessment fails most often on scope: a question broad enough to be interesting is usually too broad to measure in the time and equipment available.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The shift from recall to derivation catches strong IGCSE students in the first Diploma term. Uncertainty propagation and error analysis are examinable and almost never practised deliberately, which is where the investigation marks are quietly lost.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks are awarded for reasoning, so an unjustified correct answer scores a fraction of what is available. The exploration needs genuine mathematics rather than an application of a formula, and choosing a topic that allows real manipulation is most of the work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology. Students lose marks presenting a test without stating the hypothesis, the assumptions or a conclusion in context, and the exploration often repeats a textbook procedure instead of interpreting a result.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper one is unseen guided analysis, which cannot be revised by rereading set texts. The individual oral needs a global issue and two prepared extracts, and Higher Level adds an essay that must build an argument rather than summarise a text.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision decides grades, and an unlabelled axis costs marks the prose cannot recover. The commentaries require real published articles within a stated word limit, and the common error is choosing an article that will not support the required analysis.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on one of the prescribed titles plus an exhibition of three objects with a written commentary. Students treat it as unteachable; in fact the marks go to precise claim and counterclaim structure, which is coachable in a handful of sessions if started early enough.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and the school's curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Non-Arab students joining late need script and vocabulary work at a pace the timetable cannot provide.

sections.heading: Which components the timetable cannot cover
paragraphs: Start by separating the course into what a teacher delivers and what the student produces. Taught content is the school's job and most schools here do it well. Everything in the second column is supervised rather than taught: the teacher may advise, read a limited number of drafts, and sign the work off as authentic, but the thinking, the data and the writing have to be the student's own.

Add the hours up and the scale becomes clear. A Diploma student with six subjects has six internal assessments, each needing somewhere between fifteen and thirty hours of independent work. On top of that sit a four-thousand-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and the CAS record. None of those appears on a weekly homework sheet, and all of them have school deadlines that cluster in the same two terms.

This is where most Sustainable City enquiries come from, and it explains a pattern that confuses parents: a child with good lesson reports and poor component progress. The reports describe the taught half. The missing half is invisible until a deadline is two weeks away. The honest diagnosis is almost never that the student is weak, and almost always that nobody has scheduled the independent hours.

There is a practical way to see the problem before a deadline arrives. Ask your child to list every assessed component they owe, with the school's internal deadline next to each, in one place, on one page. Most students cannot do it from memory, and the act of writing it out usually reveals two components nobody had started and one that was quietly finished weeks ago. That list is also the only document a supervision plan needs, because it converts a vague sense of pressure into a sequence of dated tasks that can be worked through in order.

sections.heading: The three handovers inside an IB continuum, and where each one leaks
paragraphs: Families who stay in one continuum school from Primary Years to Diploma assume the transitions are smooth, because the programmes share a philosophy. The philosophy is shared; the assessment is not. Each handover changes what a mark means, and a child who was praised consistently for years can suddenly be told they are at a 4.

The first handover is PYP to MYP. A child moves from reports describing dispositions to subject grades built from four criteria with published descriptors. Parents see numbers for the first time and frequently misread them, because an MYP 5 is a sound performance and looks like a failure to anyone used to percentages.

The second is MYP into the Diploma, and it is the steepest. The MYP rewards process, reflection and communication; the Diploma rewards precision against command terms and tight analytical writing under time pressure. Students who learned to write expansively in MYP write too much and too loosely in DP1. The third handover is DP1 into DP2, where the independent components stop being future problems and all arrive at once. Each of these is predictable, which means each is preparable, and none of them is usually prepared for.

A fourth transition exists that nobody names, and it is the one out of the Diploma into a university application. Predicted grades are issued during DP2 on the basis of work completed by that point, which means the components left unfinished in DP1 affect an offer long before the final examinations. Families who understand that stop treating internal assessments as end-of-course paperwork and start treating them as the evidence behind a prediction. That reframing does more for a Diploma result than any amount of revision in the final term, and it costs nothing but a conversation in the first year.

sections.heading: MYP criteria, named by letter, and why effort sometimes moves nothing
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, each marked out of eight against published strands. The letters mean different things in different subject groups, which is the first thing parents need to know: criterion C in a science is not criterion C in a language. What is constant is that a task is designed to assess some criteria and not others.

That design is why revision can produce no change. A student who spends a fortnight memorising content walks into a task weighted towards analysis or communication and scores what they scored before. The fix is not more effort; it is reading the task sheet, which almost always names the criteria being assessed, and preparing against those strands.

The second thing worth knowing is how criterion marks become a grade. The four marks are added to a figure out of thirty-two and converted to a 1 to 7 grade using boundaries published for each subject group. A student sitting at the bottom of a grade band may need two marks across two criteria to move a whole grade, which is a specific and achievable target. A student at the top of a band may gain six marks and move nothing. Asking the teacher which criterion is closest to a boundary turns a vague worry into a piece of work.

One more thing is worth asking the school for. Many MYP departments publish the task-specific clarifications they use when marking, which translate the general strand descriptors into the language of that particular task. Those clarifications are what the teacher marks against, and a student who has read them before starting writes to a different standard than one working from the generic criterion. Requesting them is reasonable and routine, and a tutor can use them in a single session to show a student exactly which sentence in their own work would earn a mark and which would not.

sections.heading: Choosing an investigation question when your own neighbourhood is the dataset
paragraphs: Students here have an advantage most Dubai candidates do not. A community engineered around measurable resource use produces primary data that is genuinely accessible: irrigation and greywater reuse, photovoltaic output against time of day and season, shaded against unshaded surface temperature, growth rates under different conditions in a greenhouse, waste separation rates, the effect of car-free streets on recorded movement. Primary data is what the analysis criteria reward, and it is the hardest thing for most candidates to get.

The discipline is narrowing. A question like whether the community is sustainable cannot be assessed; a question about how shading affects recorded surface temperature across three surface types at fixed times of day can be. The test is whether the student can name the independent variable, the dependent variable, the controlled variables and the number of repeats before they collect anything. If any of those four is missing, the data will not support the analysis the criteria ask for.

The second discipline is permission and honesty. Data collected from a neighbour's property, a school facility or a community system needs consent, and the method section has to say how the measurements were taken rather than implying a precision the instruments did not have. A tutor can interrogate all of this, suggest how comparable published investigations were structured, and check the plan against the criteria. The student designs it, collects it, analyses it and writes it. That division is not a formality; it is what makes the work submissible.

sections.heading: Where a tutor has to stop, and what the IB asks the school to confirm
paragraphs: Internally assessed work carries an authentication step. The supervisor confirms the work is the student's own, and a student whose submission is not faces a malpractice process rather than a low mark. The outcome lands on the child, not on whoever was paid to help, which is why the boundary belongs in the first session rather than in small print.

The Dubai market contains operators selling the thing that breaks this. The research behind these pages found one advertising completed internal assessments at a fixed price. That is not tutoring; it is an integrity breach with a diploma attached. A provider willing to sell it is telling you what their other claims are worth.

The legitimate scope is wide enough to be genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the content, explain criteria strand by strand, question a research design until it is measurable, point to published work as a structural example, read one draft the student wrote and reply with questions, and check length and formatting against the current subject guide. A tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion, supply data, or hand over anything the student could submit. We also keep a record of what was discussed in a supervision session, and will release it if the school asks.

Parents sometimes ask where the line sits when a student is genuinely stuck rather than looking for shortcuts. The answer is that the tutor changes the question rather than supplies the answer. A student who cannot analyse their results is asked what the pattern would look like if the hypothesis were true, and what it looks like instead. A student whose essay has no argument is asked to say in one sentence what they are claiming. That kind of questioning moves work forward without any of the tutor's words entering the submission, and it is also how the thinking actually improves.

sections.heading: What component supervision costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Supervision is priced differently from weekly teaching, and most of the market does not explain the difference. A weekly subject slot is an ongoing arrangement at an hourly rate. Component supervision is a small number of longer sessions at specific points: question design, method review, draft response, final checks. Four well-timed hours across three months usually beats twelve hours bought in a panic in the last fortnight.

The figures below are Dubai market rates published in October 2026, attributed to whoever published them. They are not an IB Gram price list, and they exist here because three of the six agency pages ranking for these searches publish no figure at all. Compare any quote you receive against the band rather than against a feeling.

Set the number against your existing bill. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under an economic incentives package worth AED 1.5 billion. Tuition is therefore the part of the education budget that can be shaped this year, and the shape that works for an IB household is a small number of supervision hours placed early rather than a large block placed late.

Ask one question of any provider before you pay: is the quoted figure per sixty-minute hour or per session, and what is included. A ninety-minute supervision session quoted at an hourly rate is a different number, and marked feedback, a written session note and access to the tutor between sessions are either inside the price or they are not. Several providers in this market publish a headline rate and then add a registration fee, a materials charge or a minimum block of sessions. Getting the total for a component in writing beforehand prevents the most common billing dispute in this sector.

sections.heading: Why a draft supervises better on a screen than across a table
paragraphs: This is the one comparison where online delivery is not a compromise. Component supervision is document work. The criteria, the draft, the data file and the subject guide all need to be visible to two people at once, with one of them pointing at a specific strand and the other scrolling to a specific paragraph. On a shared screen that is natural. Across a dining table it means one laptop turned sideways and a printed copy nobody is annotating.

The second reason is the pool. Supervision requires someone who knows the criteria for that subject at that level, which is a narrower requirement than being able to teach the content. Filtering those people by whether they will drive to Al Qudra Road at five in the afternoon removes most of them. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so the filter never applies, and the specialist is chosen on the component rather than the postcode.

The third is record-keeping. An online session leaves a written note of what was discussed and what the student agreed to do next, which is exactly what a school wants to see if a question is ever raised about authenticity. A conversation in a kitchen leaves nothing. For work that has to be defensible as the student's own, that paper trail is worth having.

The last argument is about scheduling, which decides whether supervision happens at all. Component work needs a session at the moment the student is ready for it, which is rarely a fixed weekly slot: the draft-response hour has to come after the draft exists. An online arrangement can be moved to the Thursday the draft is finished. A visiting arrangement is built around a driving route and a fixed evening, and when the draft slips by four days the session happens anyway, too early to be useful. Flexibility is not a comfort here; it is what makes the hour worth buying.

sections.heading: What an IB leaver has to show the Ministry of Education
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a school-leaving certificate for use here, including for university admission and some employment. It is worth understanding in DP1 rather than discovering in July of DP2, because the requirements are about which subjects were taken and passed, and by then nothing can be changed.

The British-track rules are published and specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competitor ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong, and parents repeat it. The American track sets separate tests: English through IELTS at 5, TOEFL iBT at 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB there is a point worth stating plainly: no points threshold is published in the source used for the figures above, so this page does not give one. Check the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on anything you have been told, including by a school. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it. What we can do is make sure a student knows in DP1 which documents and which subjects the process will ask about.
