sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: the component nobody revises
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge contributes points to the Diploma total and receives, in most households, no preparation at all. Students who score sevens in three Higher Level subjects routinely underperform on it, and the reason is consistent: the course is not assessed on knowing things. It is assessed on the quality of an argument about how knowledge is produced and justified, which is a skill nobody has practised because no other component asks for it.

The essay is written on a title prescribed by the IB, and the first mistake is answering the title as a general question rather than as a knowledge question. A title about certainty in the natural sciences is not an invitation to describe the scientific method. It asks the student to make a claim, support it with a specific real example from a named area of knowledge, then raise a counterclaim that genuinely threatens the claim and deal with it. Students who write two paragraphs of agreement and one of disagreement have not argued.

The exhibition is more mechanical and therefore more coachable. Three objects, each linked to one of the IB's prompts, each with a commentary that establishes what the object is, why it links to the prompt, and what that link shows about knowledge. The commonest failure is choosing an object because it is available rather than because it illustrates something, which produces a commentary that describes the object at length and establishes nothing.

Four to six sessions is usually enough to change the outcome here, and they are best spent in DP1 rather than the week before a deadline. The sequence that works: read two titles and turn each into an arguable claim, write one paragraph of claim plus example, then write the counterclaim that most threatens it. Doing that twice teaches the shape of the whole essay, and the shape is what the marks are for.
bullets: The essay is marked on argument about knowledge, not on subject content
A claim needs a specific real example from a named area of knowledge
A counterclaim that does not threaten the claim earns nothing
Choose exhibition objects that illustrate a prompt, not ones that are to hand
Four to six sessions in DP1 beats a fortnight of panic in DP2

sections.heading: The independent half of IGCSE: papers, command terms and mark schemes
paragraphs: At IGCSE there is no internally assessed essay to supervise in most subjects, and families therefore assume the independent work is just revision. It is not. The content is taught in class; the marks are lost in execution, and execution is practised on past papers with the mark scheme open afterwards. That cycle is the independent half of IGCSE and it is almost never run systematically at home.

Command terms are the clearest example. A question that says state wants a fact; describe wants what happens; explain wants why; compare wants both sides addressed against the same criteria; evaluate wants a judgement supported by evidence. Students lose marks in every science and humanity by giving a description where an explanation was asked for, and they lose them repeatedly, because nothing in the normal pattern of homework tells them they are doing it.

The mechanical marks are the other half. Units omitted. Working not shown on a multi-step calculation, so a slip costs all the marks instead of one. Premature rounding. Significant figures. Graph axes unlabelled. These are each worth a handful of marks across a paper, and together they often account for a grade boundary. None of them requires new learning; all of them require somebody to point out the pattern in a marked script.

The cycle that works is one paper a week from October, sat under timed conditions, marked against the published scheme, with the following session spent only on the lost marks. Twelve weeks of that covers the question types twice. The reason it rarely happens without a tutor is not discipline; it is that marking your own child's paper against a mark scheme is tedious, contentious and slow, and most households give up by week three.
bullets: One timed paper a week from October covers the question types twice by February
Mark the paper against the published scheme, then teach only the lost marks
Command-term discipline is worth more than another pass through the textbook
Units, working shown and significant figures often add up to a grade boundary
Reference past papers from the board's own site rather than redistributing them

sections.heading: What supervision costs, and how it is priced against weekly tuition
paragraphs: Coursework supervision is bought differently from weekly tuition and should be priced differently too. It is concentrated rather than continuous: four sessions clustered before a checkpoint, then nothing for six weeks, then three more. A family budgeting for a weekly hour across forty weeks is budgeting for the wrong pattern and usually over-buying.

The market bands are the same ones that apply to any specialist tuition in Dubai. Bestimate's 2026 survey puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 for budget online sessions and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. BartyED's published premium rate is AED 650. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions.

What those figures do not show is the shape of the spend, which is the useful part. A full extended essay supervision across DP1 and DP2 is typically eight to twelve sessions spread over eighteen months. A single internal assessment is three to five. A Theory of Knowledge clinic is four to six. A twelve-week past-paper cycle is twelve. Laid out that way, a family can see what a Diploma year costs in total rather than guessing from an hourly rate.

IB Gram publishes no price list on these pages. A rate is quoted after a free consultation and a trial session, against the actual component and session length, and the honest reason is that a Theory of Knowledge clinic and a Physics Higher Level past-paper cycle are different jobs priced differently. Ask any provider whether the quote is per hour or per lesson, and whether VAT is included, before comparing.

sections.heading: Why independent work supervises better on a screen than across a table
paragraphs: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That matters less for this kind of work than it would for a younger child, and the reason is worth setting out, because supervising a draft is the one job where a screen is straightforwardly better than a visitor.

A shared screen puts the student's own document, the assessment criteria and the tutor's cursor in the same place. A criterion descriptor can be read aloud while the paragraph that fails it is highlighted. A past paper can be annotated live and the file kept. The session can be recorded, so a student revising in March can rewatch the February explanation of why their evaluation criterion was weak. None of that exists across a kitchen table with a paper copy.

The pool argument is sharper here than for content teaching. Supervising a Theory of Knowledge prescribed title, or a Geography fieldwork report, or a Higher Level History investigation, requires someone who has supervised that specific component repeatedly. The number of people within a 20-minute drive of The Views who have supervised a Theory of Knowledge essay more than a handful of times is very small. Over video the drive is irrelevant.

There is also a scheduling reason. Coursework supervision is bursty: four sessions in a fortnight before a checkpoint, then nothing. A visiting tutor needs a standing slot to make the travel worthwhile, which pushes families towards continuous weekly tuition they do not need. Online, a burst of four and then a six-week gap costs nothing extra and matches how the work actually arrives.

sections.heading: Starting with a diagnostic rather than with a syllabus
paragraphs: The wrong first session works through the syllabus from the beginning. The right one produces evidence. For an IGCSE or A Level student that means a timed past paper marked against the published scheme; for a Diploma student with coursework in progress it means reading the current draft against the criteria and naming which criterion is weakest. Either way the topic list comes out of the marking, not out of the specification order.

What that evidence usually reveals is narrower than the family expected. A student described as bad at Chemistry turns out to be fluent in bonding and organic mechanisms and lost on moles and uncertainty. A student described as weak at English scores well on analysis and poorly on focus, because the individual oral was built on a theme and not on a global issue. Narrow problems are cheap to fix; broad descriptions are expensive to act on.

The written plan that follows a diagnostic carries three things: the component, the lost-mark pattern, and the school's own deadline for whatever is next. It is reviewed every fortnight against something marked, so closed topics come off and new ones go on. Reviews on marked evidence rather than on impressions are the difference between a plan and a subscription.

One honest limit. Supervision of a scarce component close to a deadline is the hardest thing to staff: a Theory of Knowledge specialist in the fortnight before a school checkpoint, or a Higher Level minority subject investigation. Where no suitable tutor is free, the answer is a date rather than a substitute, because a generalist supervising a component they have not marked before is worse than nothing. Families who book core supervision in DP1 never meet this problem.
bullets: First session produces marked evidence, not a tour of the syllabus
Topic list comes from the lost-mark pattern, not the specification order
The plan carries the school's next internal deadline on its face
Fortnightly review against something that has been marked
Book core supervision in DP1 and scarcity stops being your problem

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: The first conversation establishes which component is in trouble: an exploration, a scientific investigation, a prescribed-title essay, a Paper 3. Supervision of a named component is a different job from teaching a subject, and the match is made accordingly.

process.title: Collect the school's internal calendar
process.description: We ask for the school's published internal assessment and mock dates before planning anything. Those dates, not the exam session, govern the workload across DP1 and DP2, and most families have never been shown them in one place.

process.title: Diagnostic on marked evidence
process.description: A timed past paper marked against the published scheme, or the current coursework draft read against the criteria. The output is a lost-mark pattern and a weakest-criterion judgement, both written down rather than described.

process.title: Scope before writing
process.description: For any coursework component, scope is settled first: is this question answerable in the word limit, will this method yield usable data, do accessible sources exist? One session here prevents the rewrite that otherwise arrives six weeks later.

process.title: Bursts timed to checkpoints
process.description: Sessions are clustered in the fortnight before each school checkpoint and paused between them, which matches how the work actually arrives and avoids paying for a weekly slot during a quiet term.

process.title: Fortnightly review, marked evidence only
process.description: Every two weeks the plan is tested against a marked script or a fed-back draft. Topics that have closed come off. The review does not run on how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a component, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: A Theory of Knowledge prescribed-title essay, a Geography fieldwork report and an English A individual oral are three different jobs. Tutors are matched to the component they have supervised repeatedly, which is the whole reason a screen beats a 20-minute radius.

whyPoints.title: Criteria read before the work begins
whyPoints.description: Every supervision block starts with the top-band descriptor for each criterion and one sentence per criterion on how the work will satisfy it. It takes twenty minutes, it almost never happens, and it is the highest-return habit in Diploma coursework.

whyPoints.title: Plans built from the school's dates
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines are set and published by the school, and they govern DP1 and DP2 far more than the exam session does. Plans here count backwards from those checkpoints rather than forwards from the first session.

whyPoints.title: Sessions clustered, not subscribed
whyPoints.description: Coursework support is bursty by nature. Four sessions before a checkpoint and nothing for six weeks costs nothing extra online, which means families buy what the work needs instead of a standing weekly slot.

whyPoints.title: The boundary stated before the first session
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches content, explains criteria, tests scope and feasibility, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. No wording is supplied for submission in any component. One page in this search sells finished internal assessments; that is a malpractice exposure for the student.

whyPoints.title: Limits and marks shown with a place to check them
whyPoints.description: Criteria, mark totals and word limits appear here with the instruction to confirm them in the school's current subject guide, because the IB revises them between cycles. No competing page names a single criterion at all.

faqs.question: My child's school in The Views is strong, so why would tutoring help?
faqs.answer: Because a good school and a supervised internal assessment are different things. A Higher Level subject gets four or five periods a week for a class of twenty, which is enough to teach a syllabus and not enough to work through one student's coursework line by line against five criteria, or mark eight full past papers for one candidate. That work is independent by design. Tutoring in this community is mostly supervision of the independent half rather than re-teaching content the school has already covered competently.

faqs.question: How many hours of help does an extended essay actually need?
faqs.answer: Typically eight to twelve sessions spread across DP1 and DP2, not a block in one term. The sequence matters more than the volume: subject chosen by about November of DP1, research question narrowed by January, sources confirmed accessible before research begins, then drafting against the school's own checkpoints. A student who starts in the first term has eighteen months and needs little intervention; one who starts in June of DP1 needs more sessions to achieve less, which is the pattern worth avoiding.

faqs.question: What are the assessment criteria for the IB mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Five criteria totalling 20 marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The largest single allocation sits on use of mathematics, which is why a question that is too easy caps the mark however well the write-up reads. Personal engagement and reflection together carry a substantial share and are the two most often treated as decoration rather than as marks with descriptors. Confirm the current allocations in your school's mathematics subject guide, because the IB revises them between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: Where do students lose marks on the IB sciences investigation?
faqs.answer: Evaluation, more often than anywhere else. The investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation in equal weight, and evaluation asks the student to identify what limited the method and what a better design would have done. Reporting what happened is easier and earns less. A student who writes an honest evaluation of a flawed experiment generally outscores one who writes a confident account of the same experiment, which surprises families and is consistent with the descriptors.

faqs.question: Does the extended essay have to be exactly 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: 4,000 words is the stated upper limit, and the practical consequence is that the research question must be narrowed before research begins rather than after a draft runs long. A student who writes 6,000 words and cuts to 4,000 produces a weaker essay than one who planned for 4,000, because the cutting removes evidence instead of padding. Confirm the current limit and how it is applied with your school's extended essay coordinator, since the IB revises requirements between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: Why do strong students underperform in Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Because the course is not assessed on knowing things. The essay is marked on the quality of an argument about how knowledge is produced and justified, which is a skill no other Diploma component asks for and therefore one nobody has practised. The commonest failure is answering a prescribed title as a general question instead of making a claim, supporting it with a specific real example from a named area of knowledge, and then raising a counterclaim that genuinely threatens the claim. Four to six sessions usually changes the outcome.

faqs.question: How should a Year 11 student use past papers properly?
faqs.answer: One paper a week from October, sat under timed conditions, marked against the published scheme, with the next session spent only on the lost marks. Twelve cycles of that covers the question types roughly twice by February. The reason it rarely happens at home is not discipline but tedium: marking a child's paper against a mark scheme is slow and contentious, and most households stop by week three. Reference the papers from the examining board's own site rather than redistributing copies.

faqs.question: What is a command term and why does it cost marks?
faqs.answer: A command term is the instruction word that sets what an answer must do. State wants a fact; describe wants what happens; explain wants why; compare wants both sides against the same criteria; evaluate wants a judgement supported by evidence. Students lose marks across every science and humanity by giving a description where an explanation was required, and they lose them repeatedly because nothing in ordinary homework flags the pattern. Spotting it in a marked script takes one session and changes every paper afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supervise coursework without crossing the IB's honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may teach content, explain what each criterion rewards, test whether a research question is answerable within the limit, confirm a method will produce usable data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply wording for submission, restructure the argument into their own prose, or hand over an analysis to adapt. The school's supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and a mismatch between a student's written register and their spoken fluency is noticed quickly.

faqs.question: Where do I find my child's internal assessment deadlines?
faqs.answer: From the school's Diploma coordinator, who publishes an internal assessment calendar. Ask for it in the first term of DP1 rather than in DP2. It shows when the extended essay question must be registered, when the first draft is due, when each subject collects its internal assessment, and when mocks run. Those dates govern the workload far more than the May session does, and families who have the calendar in front of them find the rest of the planning straightforward. The school sets these dates, so they are reliable.

faqs.question: Is supervision of a draft better online or in the room?
faqs.answer: Online, for this specific job. A shared screen puts the student's document, the criterion descriptors and the tutor's cursor in one place, so a descriptor can be read aloud while the paragraph failing it is highlighted. The session can be recorded, which means a student revising months later can rewatch why a criterion was weak. Paper copies across a table offer none of that. The honest exception is a younger child who needs an adult physically beside them, which is not what coursework supervision involves.

faqs.question: How much does coursework supervision cost across a Diploma year?
faqs.answer: It is easier to budget by block than by hour. A full extended essay supervision is typically eight to twelve sessions across eighteen months; one subject internal assessment is three to five; a Theory of Knowledge clinic is four to six; a twelve-week past-paper cycle is twelve. Dubai market rates for specialist IB support run AED 200 to 450 an hour per Bestimate's 2026 survey, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB Gram quotes after a free trial against the actual component.

faqs.question: Should my child take A Level or the IB Diploma after IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether a direction is settled. A Level gives three or four subjects in depth with no core components and generally more content per subject; the Diploma gives six subjects plus the extended essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, which rewards breadth and independent management. A student certain about engineering or medicine often does better with depth. A student still deciding usually does better with breadth. Both Regent International School and Dubai College take students through the British route, and The Views sends children to each.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for a Theory of Knowledge deadline next week?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date, rather than given someone who has not supervised the component before. Scarce supervision close to a deadline is the hardest thing to staff, and a generalist reading a prescribed-title essay they have never marked is worse than no help at all. Mainstream requests - IGCSE maths, IB Chemistry, English A - are usually matched within a day or two. Families who book core supervision early in DP1 rather than in DP2 never encounter this constraint.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause between coursework checkpoints?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. Coursework supervision is bursty: four sessions in the fortnight before a school checkpoint, then nothing for six weeks, then three more before the next one. Because nobody is travelling, a gap costs nothing and the tutor holds the relationship rather than the slot. A visiting tutor needs a standing weekly booking to make the journey worthwhile, which pushes families into buying continuous tuition during terms when the work does not require it.

dubai/the-views.closingHeading: Start with the draft, or with a marked paper
dubai/the-views.closingBody: The most useful thing a family in The Views can bring to a first conversation is evidence: a current coursework draft, or the last paper somebody marked. From either, a tutor can name the weakest criterion or the lost-mark pattern in one session, and the plan writes itself from there with the school's own deadlines on its face. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, clustered around the school's checkpoints rather than spread across a term you do not need them in. Where a component is genuinely hard to staff at short notice, you will get a date instead of a substitute.

dubai/tilal-al-ghaf.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and both IGCSE boards at the levels Tilal Al Ghaf students actually sit. Each one teaches a named syllabus rather than a subject in general, which matters more here than in older districts.

intro.heading: A villa community whose children are spread across a dozen schools
paragraphs: Tilal Al Ghaf is a Majid Al Futtaim master community built around a recreational lagoon off the Hessa Street extension, between Dubai Sports City and Dubai Studio City. The housing is almost entirely villas and townhouses: Harmony, Elan, Aura, Alaya, Serenity. There are no apartment towers, which changes the household profile in a way that matters for tutoring. These are families who committed to a long lease or a mortgage, who expect to keep their children in the same school for years, and who therefore ask questions about a two-year Diploma rather than about a six-week rescue.

The community has a British-curriculum school of its own in Royal Grammar School Guildford Dubai. Many children walk or take a short buggy ride to it. Many others do not: siblings already settled at GEMS Metropole in Motor City, at Victory Heights Primary School, at Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, at Ranches Primary School, or at the IB schools further up Hessa Street in Al Barsha South. One street in Tilal Al Ghaf will have children sitting Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the IB Middle Years Programme and the IB Diploma in the same academic year, with four different coursework calendars.

That spread is the single most useful fact about tutoring here. A neighbour's recommendation is close to worthless, because the neighbour's child is on a different syllabus with a different internal deadline and a different set of command terms. A tutor who was excellent for a Year 11 student sitting Cambridge Biology 0610 is not automatically the right person for a DP1 student taking Biology at Higher Level, and the gap between those two jobs is larger than most parents are told.

The second fact is school size. Tilal Al Ghaf sits in a belt of schools that have opened recently and are still filling their upper year groups. A school in its fourth or fifth year of operation may have a strong primary phase and a very thin Year 12 and 13. Thin year groups create a specific academic problem that older Dubai schools do not have: option blocks with fewer columns, Higher Level groups that run with a handful of students or do not run at all, and teachers covering two subjects because the timetable cannot justify a specialist. None of that shows up in a prospectus.

This page is written around that problem. It sets out who lives in Tilal Al Ghaf and what each kind of household tends to ask for, then explains what a small upper school means for subject choice, which subjects are hardest to staff, what the Dubai market charges for one-to-one help, and which entry deadlines bind a small cohort more tightly than a large one. Every lesson described here happens online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and the comparison table further down explains why that works in your favour here.

dubai/tilal-al-ghaf.programmesIntro: Tilal Al Ghaf children sit three programme families between the ages of eleven and eighteen. The notes below are about what each one demands of a student in a small school, not about what the programme promises in a brochure.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and each described by a published strand. A student can work hard for a term and move nothing, because effort went into criterion A knowledge while the task was weighted towards criterion C communication. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project, which is supervised rather than taught, and with eAssessment in schools that enter for it.
programmes.countryNote: In the Hessa Street belt the MYP is offered mainly by the IB continuum schools in Al Barsha South and Dubai Investments Park rather than inside Tilal Al Ghaf. Families who choose that route commute. A Tilal Al Ghaf MYP student therefore loses roughly an hour a day to the car, which is the hour most tutoring timetables need, and online delivery is what puts it back.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two boards, two sets of papers, two sets of command terms. Cambridge codes subjects as four digits, so Physics is 0625 and Maths is 0580, with a Core and Extended split that fixes the grade ceiling. Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1 and offers modular entry on some subjects. Students lose marks in both for the same reason: answering the question they expected rather than the one printed.
programmes.countryNote: The British-curriculum schools around Tilal Al Ghaf use both boards, sometimes within one department. Checking which code appears on your child's exam entry slip takes a minute and changes which past papers are worth practising. Families who skip that step buy a term of tuition against the wrong mark scheme, which is the most common waste of money we see in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level carries extra teaching hours and an extra paper in most sciences. The internal assessment in each subject is marked against criteria named by letter, and the Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words. The workload is front-loaded into the second term of DP1, which is when most Tilal Al Ghaf enquiries arrive.
programmes.countryNote: A student living in Tilal Al Ghaf who wants the Diploma commutes to an IB school, most often in Al Barsha South, Al Khail or Dubai Investments Park. Those schools have larger IB cohorts than the new British schools nearby, but they still cannot run every Higher Level subject every year. The availability table on this page is about exactly that constraint.

dubai/tilal-al-ghaf.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Tilal Al Ghaf households request most, with the specific thing that costs marks in each. A tutor who cannot name that thing in the first session is guessing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof, calculus and complex-number content separates this course from Applications. Marks go on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers: a correct result with no reasoning earns a fraction of the method marks available. HL students also sit Paper 3, a long problem-solving paper that rewards persistence over recall.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work. Students who chose this course to avoid proof often underestimate the graphical calculator skill required, and lose marks presenting a regression or a chi-squared test without stating the hypothesis or the conclusion in context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the sharpest drop in both programmes. At IGCSE the issue is usually circuit reasoning under changed conditions; at Diploma level it is the shift from recall to derivation. Practical and data-analysis questions reward uncertainty handling, which almost nobody practises deliberately.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and mole calculations carry most of the lost marks. Higher Level adds depth in energetics and kinetics that cannot be revised the week before. The internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to measure, which is where a supervising tutor earns their fee without touching the student's writing.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The content volume misleads students into reading instead of answering. Examiners reward precise command-term responses, so a question asking students to explain earns nothing for a description. Statistical treatment of data in the internal assessment is where Higher Level marks are most often left on the table.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides grades. An unlabelled axis or a missing shift arrow removes marks that the written analysis cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a heavier paper three. The commentaries require real published articles and a disciplined word count.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper one is an unseen guided analysis, and students who revise content rather than technique arrive unprepared for it. The individual oral requires a global issue and two texts, prepared months in advance. Higher Level adds the essay, which rewards an argument rather than a summary.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is the whole game: a student who recalls a framework but cannot apply it to the stimulus case loses most of the available analysis marks. The internal assessment depends on usable real-world data, and choosing an organisation that will not supply figures is a common first mistake.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions differ between boards, and students who learned Python at school write answers that examiners cannot award. The IB solution requirement needs a real client and documented success criteria, both of which have to be arranged early in DP1.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools run Arabic for every pupil regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Non-Arab students starting late need vocabulary and script fluency work that the school timetable cannot provide at the pace required.

dubai/tilal-al-ghaf.regionsIntro: Tilal Al Ghaf sits inside a belt of Dubailand and Sports City communities whose children share schools and school buses. The notes below describe the practical difference between them for a tutoring timetable.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Two minutes along Hessa Street and the nearest source of primary places for Tilal Al Ghaf families. Afternoon traffic around the stadium and academies pushes realistic lesson starts past 17:00 for children doing club sport.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: GEMS Metropole draws a large number of Tilal Al Ghaf siblings. The internal road loop clears quickly, so Motor City children are often home earlier than the Sports City cohort, which makes a 16:30 slot workable.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills
regions.note: Jebel Ali School sits here and takes a substantial Tilal Al Ghaf intake. The bus route back along Umm Suqeim Street adds time, and families on that route usually settle on two weekday evenings plus a Saturday morning.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: The established villa communities next door, with older schools and larger year groups. Tilal Al Ghaf parents comparing option blocks often look at Ranches schools first because their upper school has been running longer.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: A short run up Al Khail Road and the nearest cluster of IB provision for families who want the Diploma rather than A Levels. The commute is tolerable in the morning and poor at 15:30.

regions.name: Mudon and Town Square
regions.note: Further into Dubailand, with their own schools and a longer run to the Hessa Street corridor. Households that moved from these communities into Tilal Al Ghaf often keep the old school for a year, which creates the longest school runs in this area.

regions.name: Dubai Studio City and Dubai Production City
regions.note: Immediately west of Tilal Al Ghaf. Few family villas, but the free-zone offices here mean a number of Tilal Al Ghaf parents work five minutes from home, which is why mid-afternoon supervision is more achievable here than in Marina households.

schoolClusters.city: Tilal Al Ghaf and the Sports City corridor
schoolClusters.note: The schools a Tilal Al Ghaf child can reach in under fifteen minutes outside peak. British curriculum dominates, with IGCSE at sixteen and A Levels or the Diploma after. Upper year groups in the newer schools here are still filling, which is the constraint this page is built around.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South and the Hessa Street schools
schoolClusters.note: Where Tilal Al Ghaf families go for IB continuum provision and for established upper schools. The run up Hessa Street is quick before 07:30 and slow after 15:00, which is why these households tend to book later evening slots than their neighbours.

dubai/tilal-al-ghaf.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Tilal Al Ghaf request. All of them are delivered online over live video, and the right one depends on how far through a course your child already is.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one by subject
modes.description: One tutor, one subject, the same slot each week, following the school's own scheme of work and internal deadlines. This is the format for a student who is coping but slipping, and the one that suits a two-year Diploma plan. Progress is measured against marked work rather than against a feeling that lessons are going well.

sections.heading: Who actually lives in Tilal Al Ghaf, and what each household asks for first
paragraphs: Four household types account for nearly every enquiry from this community, and they want different things. The largest group is a family with primary-age children at the school inside the community or at Victory Heights, asking about reading, times tables and whether a report with no grades on it is a cause for concern. Their need is diagnostic rather than remedial, and often the honest answer is to wait a term and watch.

The second group has a child in Year 10 or 11 at a British-curriculum school in the Sports City corridor, three terms from a Cambridge or Pearson paper. These enquiries are specific, late and fixable. The third group has a DP1 student commuting to an IB school up Hessa Street, and the question is almost always about Higher Level mathematics or a science, arriving in January or February when the internal assessment and the first real mock land in the same fortnight.

The fourth group is the one this area produces more of than older districts: a family whose child is strong, whose school is new, and whose subject is thinly staffed. Nothing is wrong with the student. The problem is supply. That household does not need encouragement or study skills, it needs a subject specialist for two terms, and recognising which of the four groups you are in saves a term of paying for the wrong thing.

One more distinction is worth drawing before you spend anything. Two of these four households have a problem a tutor can close inside a term, and two have a problem that is structural and needs a longer plan. A slipping IGCSE grade with three terms left is fixable. A thinly staffed Higher Level group in a sixth form of forty students is not fixable at all, only compensated for, and compensating for it properly takes two terms of specialist teaching rather than six weeks of revision. Knowing which of those you are buying changes the budget and the timetable, and it is the first thing a diagnostic session establishes.

sections.heading: Why a young school's option block quietly decides your child's subjects
paragraphs: A school timetable is built from option blocks: columns of subjects taught at the same time, from which a student picks one. The number of columns a school can run depends on how many students are in the year group and how many specialist teachers it employs. A Year 12 cohort of two hundred supports five or six columns with real choice inside each. A cohort of forty supports three, and the subjects inside them are chosen by the school to cover the most common combinations rather than yours.

The practical effect in the Hessa Street belt is that a student who wants a particular pairing may be told it clashes. Higher Level Physics against Higher Level Economics is a frequent example, as is a third science alongside two mathematics-heavy subjects. Parents hear the word clash and assume it is administrative stubbornness. It is arithmetic. The school cannot staff a group of four students in a subject already running once.

What a family can do about it is narrower than they hope but not nothing. Ask for the option blocks in writing before the choice form goes in, not after. Ask how many students were in last year's Higher Level group for the subject your child wants, because a group of five is at risk of not running at all. Ask whether the subject will be taught by a specialist or covered. And then plan the year around the answer, which is where private tuition shifts from being a comfort purchase to a structural one.

sections.heading: When the school cannot offer the Higher Level your child needs
paragraphs: Some subjects are harder to staff than others everywhere in Dubai, and the shortage is sharper in schools whose sixth form is still small. The pattern is consistent: the subjects that require a specialist degree and have few teachers in the local market are the ones that disappear from a small option block first. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics, Computer Science and the less common second languages are the ones Tilal Al Ghaf parents ask about most.

There are three normal responses from a school. It may run the subject with a very small group, which is academically fine and timetabled awkwardly. It may ask a teacher from a related department to cover it, which works for the first term of content and shows up later on the harder papers. Or it may not offer it, and suggest an alternative. All three are reasonable school decisions, and all three leave work for the student to do outside lessons.

A specialist tutor is the obvious answer to the second and third cases, and online delivery is what makes it available. A Higher Level Physics specialist who can teach the full programme does not need to live within a twenty-minute drive of Tilal Al Ghaf. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes at all, so the pool your child draws from is defined by subject and level rather than by postcode, which is the whole point of the arrangement here.

sections.heading: What one-to-one tuition costs around Tilal Al Ghaf, in dirhams
paragraphs: The Dubai tutoring market publishes very little about price, and three of the six agency pages ranking for these searches quote no figure at all. The bands below are market rates collected from providers who do publish, in October 2026, with the source named in each row. They are not IB Gram's price list. What they do is tell you whether a quote you have been given sits inside the market or outside it.

Two patterns are worth knowing before you call anyone. The first is that in-home delivery costs more than online for the same tutor quality, because travel time is inside the rate whether or not it appears as a line item. Bestimate's Dubai figures put home visits in a higher band than online lessons across every level. The second is that rates rise towards the examination session, so a specialist booked in January is cheaper and more available than the same specialist booked in March.

Set the figures against the fees you already pay. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package worth AED 1.5 billion. For a Tilal Al Ghaf household that means the tuition budget is the variable part of the education bill this year, which is an argument for spending it deliberately on one subject rather than thinly across three.

One practical warning about quotes. Ask whether a published rate is per sixty-minute hour or per lesson, because a ninety-minute session quoted at an hourly figure is a different number, and ask what is included: marked homework, a written note after each session, and access to the tutor between lessons are either inside the rate or they are not. Several providers in this market quote a headline figure and add a registration charge, a materials charge or a minimum block of sessions. Get the total for a term in writing before the first lesson rather than after the third.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor on the Hessa Street extension against a specialist on screen
paragraphs: This is the comparison most Tilal Al Ghaf parents are actually making, so here it is with the local detail in it. A tutor driving to a Tilal Al Ghaf villa for a 17:00 lesson leaves their own area around 16:15 and gets home after 19:00. That is three hours of their working day for one paid hour, and it has three consequences: the rate carries the travel, the tutor can take fewer students, and your choice narrows to people who live within reach of the Hessa Street extension.

The second consequence is the expensive one. Subject depth is not evenly distributed across Dubai, and the pool of people who can teach Higher Level Physics or the quantitative half of Higher Level Economics is small. Filtering that pool by driving distance from a Dubailand community removes most of it. A parent who insists on a tutor in the room is, in practice, choosing availability over specialism, and in an examination year that is the wrong way round.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the trade is not available to us to sell. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on live video with a shared whiteboard and the student's own marked script on screen. For internal assessment supervision that is better rather than merely equivalent: the draft, the criteria and the data are all visible to both people at once, which is awkward across a dining table and simple on a screen.

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA inspection report when the school is still new
paragraphs: KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Parents in Tilal Al Ghaf use those bands to choose schools, which is reasonable, and then use them to predict their own child's result, which is not. The band is a judgement about a whole school across all phases, and a new school's overall rating is dominated by the phase with the most students, which in this belt is usually primary.

Read the report rather than the headline. The published report breaks performance down by phase and by subject, and a school rated Good overall may have a secondary phase rated Acceptable and a specific subject flagged for attainment. If your child is in Year 12 taking that subject, the phase and subject lines matter and the overall band does not. The reverse is also true: a strong overall band does not mean the Higher Level group your child sits in is well staffed.

Look for the lines about teaching for effective learning and about assessment in the relevant phase. Those two indicators predict what your child will actually experience in a classroom better than the overall judgement does. And check the year of publication, because a school in its fourth year may have been inspected before its sixth form existed. None of this is an argument against a new school. It is an argument for asking narrower questions than the band answers.

One last caution about using bands to choose at all. A school rated Outstanding with a sixth form of three hundred students and a school rated Good with a sixth form of fifty may offer the same quality of teaching in the subject your child cares about, and the smaller one may offer more attention and fewer option columns at the same time. The band answers a question about the whole institution. You are asking a question about one child, one year group and three or four subjects, and that question has to be asked directly of the school.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops on internally assessed work
paragraphs: Every programme a Tilal Al Ghaf child might sit includes work that must be the student's own: the MYP Personal Project, internal assessments in each Diploma subject, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, IGCSE coursework components where a school enters for them. The IB requires the supervisor to authenticate that work, and a student whose submission is not their own faces a malpractice finding rather than a poor mark. The consequences fall on the child, not on whoever was paid.

This matters commercially because the Dubai market contains people selling the other thing. One operator found in the research for these pages advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price. Buying one is not a shortcut, it is an academic-integrity breach with the student's diploma attached to it. No reputable tutor will go near it, and a tutor who offers to is telling you something useful about everything else they sell.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They can teach the underlying content, explain the assessment criteria strand by strand, interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to measure, show how a similar published investigation was structured, read a draft the student wrote and respond with questions, and check the word count and presentation requirements against the current subject guide. What they may not do is write, rewrite, edit to completion, or supply anything the student could submit. IB Gram tutors work to that line, and will say so to the student in the first session.

sections.heading: The entry deadlines that bind a small cohort more tightly
paragraphs: Examination entries are made by the school, months before the papers. In a large school the process is routine and invisible. In a small or new one it is a point of risk, because a subject with four candidates may be entered late, entered with the wrong tier, or entered for the wrong series. Parents in this belt should know the published dates, because the school's internal deadline sits well before the board's.

Cambridge runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The March series is instructive for how far ahead entries close. For March 2027, Cambridge publishes an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Entries close more than two months before the first paper.

Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a separate timetable for each. Its own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026. For the IB, confirm every session and results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, because those dates are not something this page will state.

sections.heading: Getting started from Tilal Al Ghaf, including what we will not promise
paragraphs: The useful first step is not booking a tutor. It is sending the last piece of marked work, the name of the school, the exact syllabus code from the exam entry slip or the subject guide, and the date of the next assessment. Those four items let a tutor arrive at the first session with a view rather than a questionnaire, and they take ten minutes to gather. A first session that begins with the student explaining their own timetable has wasted the hour you paid for.

After that, expect a diagnostic session rather than teaching. Its purpose is to find out whether the problem is content, technique, timing or confidence, because those four need different work and look identical on a report card. We then propose a weekly slot and a subject, and tell you if we think a second subject should wait. Most Tilal Al Ghaf households start with one subject and add a second only after a mock.

Three honest limits. We do not promise a grade, and anyone in this market who does is selling something they cannot deliver. We do not place tutors in UAE homes; every lesson is one-to-one online, and if that is not what you want we are the wrong provider. And where a very scarce specialism is involved, the match can take longer than a week, or the only available specialist may sit in a different time zone and offer early-morning or late-evening slots. We will tell you that before you pay rather than after.

process.title: Send four things
process.description: The school, the exact syllabus code, the most recent marked piece of work and the date of the next assessment. For a Diploma student add the internal assessment deadline the school has set, which is almost always earlier than anything the board publishes.

process.title: Diagnostic session
process.description: One hour, online, spent finding out which of four problems you have: missing content, weak technique, poor timing under pressure, or lost confidence. The tutor works through the marked script with the student rather than lecturing, and you receive a written summary afterwards.

process.title: Match to a specialist, not a generalist
process.description: We match on subject, level and board. A Cambridge 0580 tutor and a Pearson 4MA1 tutor are different people with different mark schemes in their heads. Where the specialism is scarce we say how long the match will take before you commit to anything.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot and hold it
process.description: The same hour every week, agreed around the school run rather than against it. Tilal Al Ghaf households usually land on a 16:30 slot for primary children and a 19:00 or 20:00 slot for Diploma students who commute up Hessa Street.

process.title: Review against marked work
process.description: Every four to six weeks, progress is checked against something a teacher marked rather than against how lessons felt. If the marks have not moved, we change the tutor, the format or the diagnosis rather than selling you more hours of the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Your child's subject, not your postcode
whyPoints.description: Because every lesson is online, the tutor is chosen for the syllabus and level your child actually sits. A Tilal Al Ghaf family gets a Higher Level Physics specialist rather than whoever was willing to drive out along the Hessa Street extension at five in the afternoon.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: The rate tables on this page name who published each figure and when. You can verify them, compare any quote you have received, and see where a number sits in the Dubai market before you spend anything.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, held through the term
whyPoints.description: The same person each week, following your child's scheme of work and the school's own deadlines. Continuity is what makes the fourth session more valuable than the first, and rotating tutors is why many agency arrangements stall after a month.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated in advance
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain to the student in session one what they will and will not do with an internal assessment or Extended Essay. That conversation protects the child from a malpractice finding and protects the work from being worth nothing.

whyPoints.title: Limits disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: If a specialism is scarce, if the match will take ten days, or if the only available tutor works in a time zone that suits early mornings, you hear it before you pay. No grade promises, no fabricated success rates, no office in Dubai we do not occupy.

faqs.question: Is tuition for Tilal Al Ghaf villas delivered in person or online?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For a community off the Hessa Street extension this works in your favour: a visiting tutor would need to be someone who lives within driving distance and is free at five in the afternoon, which removes most of the subject specialists from your choices. Online, the tutor is selected for the syllabus and level your child sits, not for where they live.

faqs.question: My child is at the school inside Tilal Al Ghaf. Does that change what tutoring is needed?
faqs.answer: It changes the logistics more than the academics. Children who walk or ride to school are home earlier, so a 16:00 or 16:30 slot is realistic where a commuting family needs 19:00. Academically, the questions to ask are about the year group rather than the community: how many students are in the relevant option group, whether the subject is taught by a specialist, and which board the department enters for. Those three answers shape a tutoring plan far more than the address does.

faqs.question: What does it mean if my child's school says a subject combination clashes?
faqs.answer: It means the two subjects sit in the same option block, which is a timetable column taught at one time. A school can only run as many columns as its year-group size and specialist staffing allow, so a smaller sixth form offers less choice inside each column. Ask for the blocks in writing before the option form is submitted, ask how many students took that Higher Level group last year, and plan around the answer. A group of four or five students is at genuine risk of not running at all.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's school actually enters for?
faqs.answer: Ask the subject teacher or the examinations officer for the syllabus code on the entry, and get it in writing. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics; Pearson Edexcel uses forms such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Schools in this belt use both, sometimes within one department. The code decides which past papers and mark schemes are worth practising, and buying a term of tuition against the wrong board is the most common waste of money we see locally.

faqs.question: Is a new school with a small sixth form a problem for a strong student?
faqs.answer: Not inherently, but it creates a supply problem rather than a teaching problem. Small cohorts mean fewer option columns, Higher Level groups that may run with a handful of students, and occasionally a teacher covering a subject outside their specialism. A strong student in that position does not need motivation or study skills; they need a subject specialist for a couple of terms. Recognising that early is what stops a capable child drifting into a grade that does not reflect them.

faqs.question: What do private tutors charge per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 for an IB or IGCSE specialist. A premium named tutor has been advertised at AED 650. Those figures come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED rather than from IB Gram, and they are useful mainly for checking whether a quote you have been given is normal.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a licence to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the application under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Extended Essay without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria strand by strand, challenge the research question until it is answerable in four thousand words, show how comparable published work was structured, read a draft your daughter has written and respond with questions, and check formatting and word-count requirements against the current subject guide. A tutor cannot write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply text or data. The IB requires the supervisor to authenticate the work as the student's own, so the line protects your daughter rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to get help with locally?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics, the quantitative half of Higher Level Economics, Computer Science and second languages beyond French and Spanish are the ones Tilal Al Ghaf families ask about most and the ones with the thinnest local supply. These are also the subjects a small school finds hardest to staff, so the shortage appears twice in the same household. Online delivery is the practical answer, because it removes driving distance from the selection and leaves subject and level as the only filters that matter.

faqs.question: When does a DP1 student usually need to start?
faqs.answer: The second term of DP1 is when most enquiries from this community arrive, and it is not too early. That is when the first internal assessment proposals are due, the first serious mocks land, and Higher Level content moves past what a strong IGCSE student can absorb by reading. Starting in that window gives eighteen months of weekly work rather than a rescue attempt in DP2. Starting later still helps, but the plan shifts from building understanding to protecting marks, which is a narrower job.

faqs.question: Should I read the KHDA band or the full inspection report?
faqs.answer: The full report. KHDA publishes an overall band from Outstanding to Very Weak, but the report breaks performance down by phase and subject, and a new school's overall judgement is usually dominated by its largest phase, which in this belt is primary. If your child is in Year 12 studying a particular subject, the secondary-phase lines and that subject's attainment line tell you what they will actually experience. Check the publication year too, because an early inspection may predate the sixth form entirely.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two of my children in different year groups?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually a mistake. A tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics well is not automatically the right person for a Diploma student taking Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, because the mark schemes, the command terms and the assessment structure differ. Where the subjects and levels genuinely align, the same tutor in consecutive slots works and saves scheduling effort. Where they do not, two specialists in two slots produces better marks than one generalist stretched across both.

faqs.question: Do lessons stop during Ramadan and the long Dubai summer?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. During Ramadan school hours shorten and most families shift sessions to after Iftar, which suits Diploma students revising at night and suits younger children less. Through the summer, families who travel often keep a reduced schedule online from wherever they are, which is one practical advantage of video delivery. The weeks worth protecting are the ones immediately before mocks and before an examination series, and those are agreed in advance rather than cancelled at short notice.

faqs.question: What happens in the first four weeks after we start?
faqs.answer: Week one is diagnostic: the tutor works through recent marked work with the student and reports what the real problem is. Weeks two and three are teaching against the gaps found, with homework set to the school's next assessment rather than a generic worksheet. Week four is usually a short piece of timed work so progress is measured against something marked. You receive a written note after each session. If nothing has moved by the first review, we change the tutor or the diagnosis rather than selling more hours.

faqs.question: What will IB Gram not do for a Tilal Al Ghaf family?
faqs.answer: We will not promise a grade or a points total, because no tutor can honestly offer that. We will not send anyone to your villa, since UAE delivery is online only. We will not supply, write or edit to completion any internal assessment, Extended Essay or coursework, and we will say so to the student directly. We hold no accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and will not imply one. Where a specialist is unavailable in the slot you want, we will tell you before you pay.

dubai/tilal-al-ghaf.closingHeading: Start with the marked work, not the booking form
dubai/tilal-al-ghaf.closingBody: If your child is at a school in the Sports City corridor or commuting up Hessa Street to an IB school, the fastest useful step is to send the last marked assessment, the syllabus code and the date of the next test. One diagnostic hour online will tell you whether this is a content gap, a technique problem or a supply problem created by a small option block, and those three need different work. If the honest answer is to wait a term and watch, we will say that. If it is a specialist for two terms, we will tell you how long the match takes and what the market charges before you commit to anything.

dubai/town-square.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma and IGCSE subjects in evening slots that suit a Dubailand bus timetable. Each works in Gulf Standard Time and holds the slot across a whole term, because a moving session time is the fastest way to lose a student's momentum.

intro.heading: The hour between the bell and the lesson decides everything
paragraphs: Town Square was built as a dense townhouse and apartment community on Al Qudra Road with a park at its centre and nurseries inside it, but no secondary school. That single planning fact shapes the academic life of every family here with a child over eleven. The school run leaves early and arrives back late, and the window in which a tired fourteen-year-old can usefully learn something is narrower than in almost any inner community in Dubai.

Parents discover this when they try to book tutoring. A provider offers a 16:00 slot because that is when the school day ends. The bus pulls into Town Square at 16:20 on a good day and closer to 17:00 when Hessa Street or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road is slow. The child needs food, twenty minutes of nothing, and a working space. A session that starts before all three of those have happened is a session the parent paid for and the child did not attend in any meaningful sense.

The honest answer for most Town Square households is 17:30 for primary-age children and 18:00 to 18:30 for Years 10 to 13. That is late, and it has a consequence: the number of useful weekday slots per child is roughly two, not four. Which means the choice of what to tutor matters more here than it does in a community five minutes from its school. A family cannot cover four weak subjects with weekly sessions; it has to pick the two where the marks actually move and deal with the rest through supervised independent practice.

There is a second clock running underneath the daily one. The UAE academic year is interrupted in ways a British or Indian parent will not have planned for: Ramadan shortens school days and shifts the whole household onto a post-Iftar rhythm, the winter and spring breaks fall at different points from the UK calendar, and the Cambridge and Pearson entry deadlines sit months before the papers. A tutoring plan that ignores those four things gets five productive weeks out of ten. The fix is not more sessions but a term map drawn before the first lesson, with the breaks, the mock season and the entry deadlines already marked on it, so that the weeks which are genuinely available are used at full intensity and the weeks which are not are left alone.

IB Gram is a matching platform, not a centre, and there is no IB Gram building in Dubai. For UAE families every lesson runs one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. We do not send a tutor to any UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a Town Square family that is the point rather than a compromise, because the bottleneck here is time, and a tutor who does not have to drive to Al Qudra Road is a tutor who can start the moment the child is ready.

dubai/town-square.programmesIntro: Which programme a Town Square child sits depends almost entirely on which bus their parents chose at Year 7, because the community feeds several different school systems at once. Here is what each route demands of an evening.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11 on short, highly patterned papers. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade at C; Pearson structures its papers differently and uses its own codes. The decisive activity is timed past-paper work with honest marking, which is exactly the activity that needs an uninterrupted evening hour.
programmes.countryNote: This is the dominant route among Town Square families, because the British-curriculum schools in Motor City, Dubai Sports City and Jumeirah Park are the ones the community's buses serve. The scheduling consequence is sharp: Year 11 needs two to three timed-paper sessions a week in the run-up to the series, and in Town Square those have to come out of weekend mornings rather than weekday evenings.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internal assessment written over months and worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade. The workload is not evenly distributed: November and February are brutal, and the weeks after a mock series are comparatively empty.
programmes.countryNote: Town Square's Diploma students travel mainly to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City or Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches. Because those are long runs, DP families here tend to buy fewer, longer sessions: one ninety-minute block midweek and one at the weekend works better than three short weekday slots that keep colliding with CAS commitments.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked 0 to 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There is no external paper before the optional MYP 5 eAssessment, so progress is judged on teacher assessment of criterion-referenced tasks. Students who write fluently but do not read the criteria lose marks they could see coming.
programmes.countryNote: MYP families in Town Square ask about session length more than about content, because a twelve-year-old off a long bus cannot sustain ninety minutes. Two thirty-five to forty-five minute sessions placed early in the evening beat one long block, and the criteria language is best taught in short doses against a task the school has already set.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units with descriptive rather than numerical reporting, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. The absence of grades means a parent cannot easily tell whether reading fluency or number fact recall is where it should be, which is the most common reason for a first enquiry at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: Primary children in Town Square are the ones the timetable hurts most, because they ride the same long route as their older siblings but run out of concentration earlier. The workable pattern is two twenty-five to thirty-minute sessions a week at 17:00 or 17:15, before dinner rather than after, with nothing scheduled on the day of a late club.

dubai/town-square.subjectsIntro: The subject list below is weighted to what Town Square families actually book, which skews towards the subjects where a single focused evening hour produces visible movement within a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and financial mathematics with calculator access throughout. The trap is interpretation: students produce correct output and then fail to say what it means in context, which is where the marks sit. HL statistics is substantially harder than its reputation suggests.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released statement for the examination. Marks go to candidates who apply tools to the specific organisation rather than describing the tool. HL adds a far heavier quantitative component than most students expect when they choose it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be recalled with enough precision to support an argument, including method and findings. The common failure is a vague narrative about a famous experiment. Essay structure under time is the skill that separates grades here, and it is coachable in six sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is decided by diagram accuracy: labelled axes, a marked new equilibrium and shaded welfare areas. HL Paper 3 adds quantitative work where the arithmetic is simple and the interpretation is not. Real-world examples need to be specific and current to earn evaluation marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms dominate lost marks. The data booklet is allowed but only helps students who have practised with it. HL mechanisms require arrows drawn to a standard the mark scheme recognises, which is a precision skill.

subjects.name: French B and Spanish B
subjects.description: Productive skills are where grades are made: the written task and the individual oral. Students who have read widely still lose marks for register and for failing to address the full prompt. Short, frequent speaking practice outperforms long grammar sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio and Arabic B
subjects.description: Script fluency and the gap between Modern Standard Arabic and spoken dialect cause most of the difficulty for non-Arab students. Because Dubai schools also run mandatory Arabic alongside the Diploma, families often need both streams and should say so when they enquire.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The final third of each paper combines topics, typically geometry inside algebra. Students abandon questions instead of harvesting the method marks available for a correct opening line, which is a decision habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Literature
subjects.description: Textual detail is the currency. Students who have read the set text and not annotated it write general essays that cap in the middle bands. Timed essay practice against the actual assessment criteria is the fastest available improvement.

subjects.name: IGCSE Economics
subjects.description: Definitions earn one mark and application earns the rest. Diagram questions are as unforgiving as at Diploma level. The data-response paper rewards students who quote the extract rather than writing from memory.

subjects.name: IGCSE Information and Communication Technology
subjects.description: The practical papers are marked against precise outcomes, so a spreadsheet that works but does not match the specified formatting loses marks. This is a subject where supervised practice on the exact task types is worth more than conceptual teaching.

subjects.name: IGCSE Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Breadth across three disciplines with less depth in each, which suits some students and leaves others with three sets of half-secured content. Knowing which award your child is entered for matters, because the paper structures differ.

dubai/town-square.regionsIntro: Town Square sits in the same Dubailand belt as a group of communities that share its school routes. The practical differences between them are mostly measured in minutes.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: A short hop west along Al Qudra Road and on several of the same bus routes. Mudon families face a similar evening squeeze but with a younger average cohort, so primary-stage requests dominate and sessions start slightly earlier.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills and DAMAC Hills 2
regions.note: DAMAC Hills has Jebel Ali School inside it, which shortens the run considerably for its own residents. DAMAC Hills 2 sits further out and shares Town Square's long-commute problem, often with a later arrival still.

regions.name: Remraam

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Served by Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches and Ranches Primary School. A Town Square child bussed here is on one of the longer routes, and arrival after 16:45 is common in term time.

regions.name: Motor City

regions.note: Greenfield International School and Durham School Dubai draw Diploma and IGCSE students from Town Square. The run is long but counter-flow in parts, so it is sometimes faster than the shorter northern routes.

regions.name: The Sustainable City
regions.note: Fairgreen International School makes this a genuine IB continuum option within reach. Town Square families choosing it accept a longer morning in exchange for not changing schools at sixteen.

schoolClusters.city: The northern corridor: Motor City, Dubai Sports City and Arabian Ranches
schoolClusters.note: The busiest route out of Town Square and the one most affected by afternoon congestion on Hessa Street. Most of the community's Year 10 and Year 11 cohort travels this way, which is why IGCSE sessions here cluster at 18:00 and later rather than straight after school.

schoolClusters.note: Longer in distance but often steadier in flow, this is the route for families who have chosen an IB continuum or a Dubailand school. Diploma students on this corridor tend to prefer one long midweek block and a weekend session over several short slots.

sections.heading: What the Town Square school run does to a tutoring timetable
paragraphs: The practical question behind a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Town Square is not who is good. It is what time a lesson can start and still be a lesson. Town Square has nurseries but no secondary school, so every child above primary age leaves the community in the morning and comes back on a bus that has collected several other stops first. The return leg is the part nobody quotes when they sell a tutoring package.

Three routes account for almost all of it. North to Motor City and Dubai Sports City, which is short in distance and slow at pickup because of Hessa Street. North-west to Arabian Ranches, which is longer and shares the same congestion. South to Dubai Investments Park and The Sustainable City, which is longest on the map and sometimes fastest in practice because it runs against the main flow. A family's usable evening depends on which of the three their school sits on.

Add the non-negotiables once the child is home: food, a short recovery, and getting to a desk with the right books. In practice that is forty minutes. A 16:00 session is therefore unavailable to almost every secondary student in this community, a 17:00 session works for primary children on the northern routes only, and 18:00 to 18:30 is the realistic window for Years 10 to 13.
