sections.heading: Two usable slots a week, so choose the subjects properly
paragraphs: A Town Square family with a child in Year 11 has roughly two protected weekday evening slots and one weekend morning. That is the real budget, and it is smaller than the four or five subjects a struggling student is usually worried about. Spreading those slots thinly across everything produces a term of light contact with no measurable movement anywhere, which is the most common way money is wasted in this market.

The better approach is to rank subjects by how much a tutored hour moves the grade. Subjects with a high procedural content and a published mark scheme respond fastest: IGCSE Mathematics, the separate sciences, Economics diagrams, ICT practical tasks. A single hour a week on mole calculations or on genetic-cross layout produces visible change inside a month because the skill is narrow and drillable.

Subjects that respond slowly are the essay-based ones where the limiting factor is reading the student has not done. IGCSE English Literature cannot be fixed by tutoring if the set text has not been read properly, and no amount of weekly contact substitutes for that reading. For those subjects the honest advice is often to use the tutor for structure and timed practice only, and to put the recovered hours into reading.

The third category is subjects where the problem is not the subject. A student losing marks across four papers for the same reason, usually command terms or thin working, has one problem, not four. Diagnosing that first can collapse a four-subject tutoring request into one subject plus a technique block, which fits inside a Town Square week.

sections.heading: Ramadan, term breaks and the UAE calendar a tutoring plan has to respect
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written against a British school calendar will lose weeks in the UAE. The academic year here is punctuated differently, and two of the interruptions are substantial enough to need planning rather than accommodating. Families who build them in get ten productive weeks out of ten; families who do not get five and conclude that tutoring does not work.

Ramadan is the big one. School days shorten, the household eats and sleeps on a different schedule, and the useful learning window moves to after Iftar. For Town Square families this is sometimes an improvement rather than a problem: a post-Iftar session at 21:00 has no bus in front of it and no homework deadline immediately behind it, and students are often sharper then than at 18:00 on a normal Tuesday. It needs agreeing in advance with the tutor, not negotiating on the night.

The term breaks are the second. The UAE winter and spring breaks do not align with the UK pattern, and they fall at points that matter: one of them sits close to the mock season and another sits close to the entry deadlines. A break used for a short intensive block is worth more than six scattered weeks of term-time sessions, particularly for a Year 11 student who needs volume of timed practice rather than new teaching.

The third timing issue is the examination calendar itself, which runs on its own logic. Entry deadlines sit months before papers. Cambridge publishes final entries for its March 2027 series as due 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. IB session dates are not confirmable from here, because the IB's site blocks automated checking: UAE schools sit the May session, and the exact window should come from the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org.

sections.heading: Two children, one evening: how sibling scheduling actually works
paragraphs: Town Square has a high proportion of households with two or three school-age children, and the evening arithmetic gets difficult fast. Two children needing two sessions each is four appointments in a window that holds perhaps six usable hours across a week, assuming nobody has a football commitment, which somebody always does.

The pattern that works is staggered rather than simultaneous. The younger child takes the early slot at 17:00 or 17:15 while the older one eats and decompresses; the older child takes 18:30 when the younger is finished. Both sessions are online, so there is no second tutor arriving and no overlap problem beyond bandwidth and a quiet room each. Running both at once is tempting and tends to fail, because one child ends up in a shared space being distracted by the other's lesson.

Where two children study the same subject at different levels, the same tutor can often take both consecutively, which saves the parent one relationship to manage and lets the tutor use one plan with two branches. That is practical for IGCSE siblings a year apart; it is rarely practical across an IGCSE and a Diploma student, because the assessment demands are too different to hold in one plan.

The scheduling rule worth writing down is that a protected slot beats an optimal slot. A session at 18:30 that happens every week for twelve weeks outperforms a session at 17:30 that is moved four times. Movement breaks the between-session homework cycle, and the homework is where most of the learning happens.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition with Town Square travel priced in
paragraphs: The comparison most pages make is abstract. In Town Square it is concrete, because the travel component has a measurable size. An in-home tutor coming to this community from anywhere central is pricing a round trip of well over an hour into the fee, and is drawn from the subset of tutors willing to make that trip on a weekday evening. That subset is selected by geography, not by subject.

Market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, make the premium visible. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour. An in-home one-to-one visit including travel runs AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Group tuition is cheaper per student and has a specific weakness for this community: a group runs at a fixed time, and a fixed time does not survive a variable bus. One missed session in a group is a topic missed permanently, because the group moves on. For a student whose arrival time swings by thirty minutes, one-to-one is not a luxury but the only format with a realistic attendance rate.

Those figures are the market, published by the providers named and read in the month stated. They are not an IB Gram price list, and a free trial session is the sensible way to establish value before committing to any of them. The trial's length and conditions are stated when it is booked.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is not unregulated, and it is worth knowing the rule before paying anyone. Individuals offering private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone telling you it costs money, or that it is optional, is wrong on a point of fact.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. The published list includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

There is a restriction that matters more than the permit itself. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported by Gulf News, prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but no family should be pursuing their child's own classroom teacher for paid lessons.

Those providing private tuition without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which means any specific amount quoted to you, including figures circulating online, is unverified. A separate and much larger requirement applies to anyone running a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai, which needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram has no Dubai premises and holds no such permit; it is a matching platform delivering online lessons.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, said plainly
paragraphs: One provider found in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. Families should know that buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, that the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller, and that the student is the person who signs the authenticity declaration. The boundary is not a matter of taste, so it is worth stating in concrete terms.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. Teaching research method. Interrogating a research question until it is answerable in the word count available. Explaining what each assessment criterion is actually looking for, in the criterion's own language. Reading a draft the student has produced and identifying which criterion is underserved and why. Teaching the statistics, the referencing convention or the lab technique the task depends on. Asking the question that makes the student notice the hole in their own argument.

What a tutor cannot do is supply any part of the submitted piece. No sentences for inclusion. No restructuring by rewriting. No data the student did not gather. The test is simple: feedback describes the problem and leaves the solving to the student, while authorship solves it for them. A tutor who hands back a document with their own prose in it has crossed the line regardless of how it is labelled.

A related rule covers materials. Boards hold copyright in their syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables. A tutor should reference and link them, not distribute them. If a provider is circulating board PDFs as downloads, that is a copyright problem, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well.

sections.heading: Which regulator applies if you move emirate mid-course
paragraphs: Town Square's population is mobile, and a move to Abu Dhabi or Sharjah mid-course changes which authority sets the rules for your child's school. Parents assume Dubai's framework applies nationally. It does not, and the differences are large enough to affect a tutoring plan and a fee conversation.

Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The powers are not identical. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. Underneath all of it is a federal baseline: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

What survives a move is the examination board. A child entered for Cambridge 0580 in Dubai sits the same specification in Sharjah, and the tutoring continues unchanged because it is delivered online. What changes is the school's inspection framework, the fee regime and the mandatory-subject implementation detail, all of which are worth asking the receiving school about directly rather than assuming.

sections.heading: Getting started from Town Square, and what we will not promise
paragraphs: The first message should contain five things: the school, the year group, the board and syllabus code if you have it, the two or three topics where marks are being lost, and the time the bus actually gets home. The last of those is the one nobody sends and the one that determines whether the arrangement holds for a term.

The first session is diagnostic. The student works an unseen paper or brings a marked school assessment, and the tutor marks it against the official criteria and reports which problem is in play: content never secured, content not retrievable under time, command terms misread, or working shown too thinly to collect method marks. Those four need different plans, and the plan a parent arrives with is frequently not the one that survives the hour.

What follows is a term map built backwards from the entry deadline and the examination window, interleaved with the school's own assessment dates, with Ramadan and the UAE breaks already placed on it. Content work front-loads and timed practice takes over in the final eight to ten weeks. Every six to eight weeks the question is whether marks on comparable tasks have moved; if they have not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan or the tutor changes.

There are things we will not promise. No grade is guaranteed, by us or by anyone honest, and a provider promising a specific score is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. We will not claim regulatory approval we do not hold. We will not place a generalist in a Higher Level slot because the specialist is busy; we will say the specialist is busy and give you the options. And we will not pretend that a tutor can arrive at a Town Square address, because for UAE families the lessons are online and that is what makes the subject matching possible at all.

process.title: Send the bus time with the subject
process.description: Include the school, year group, board, syllabus code if known, the topics where marks are going, and the time your child actually gets back into Town Square. That last detail is what makes a slot stick. A request with it is scheduled once; a request without it gets rearranged twice in the first fortnight.

process.title: One diagnostic hour on real work
process.description: Before any teaching, the tutor marks an unseen paper or a recent school assessment against the official criteria and reports which of four failure modes applies. This usually narrows a request covering four subjects down to one subject plus a technique block, which is the only version that fits a Town Square week.

process.title: Fix two protected slots, not four hopeful ones
process.description: Agree one or two weekday evenings and one weekend morning, and then defend them. A slot at 18:30 that runs for twelve consecutive weeks produces more than a 17:30 slot moved four times, because the between-session work is where most of the learning actually happens.

process.title: Map the term around the UAE calendar
process.description: The plan is written backwards from the entry deadline and the exam window, with Ramadan, Eid and the UAE winter and spring breaks placed on it in advance. Post-Iftar slots are agreed before Ramadan starts rather than negotiated during it, and break weeks are used for short intensive blocks.

process.title: Review against marks, every six to eight weeks
process.description: The only honest measure is whether marks on comparable tasks have moved. If they have not, something in the diagnosis or the match is wrong and it changes. A free trial session is available before any commitment, with the length and conditions stated at booking.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around arrival, not around the bell
whyPoints.description: Slots are set from when your child is actually home in Town Square, which on the northern corridor can be forty minutes after school ends. Starting late and finishing the session is better than starting on time and teaching a child who is still in the car.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, said plainly
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson runs one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. IB Gram does not operate home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. Nobody books expecting a car, and no evening is spent waiting for one.

whyPoints.title: Slot scarcity treated as the real constraint
whyPoints.description: With two usable weekday evenings, the question is which subjects repay an hour fastest. We will tell you when a subject is a poor use of a scarce slot, including when the real gap is reading the student has not done rather than teaching they have not had.

whyPoints.title: The UAE calendar built into the plan
whyPoints.description: Ramadan timing, Eid pauses and the UAE winter and spring breaks are placed on the term map before the first session, alongside the Cambridge and Pearson entry deadlines. Plans written against a UK calendar lose weeks here.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED, attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The market figures on this page name the provider that publishes them and the month they were read. Several pages competing for this search publish no price at all. A Town Square parent setting a budget deserves numbers in dirhams with a source attached.

whyPoints.title: Legality explained, not glossed over
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit, its two-year free validity, its eligible categories and the restriction on teaching your own school's students are all set out here. It is reasonable to ask any tutor whether they hold the permit, and reasonable to expect a straight answer.

faqs.question: What time can tutoring realistically start for a Town Square secondary student?
faqs.answer: Between 18:00 and 18:30 on weekdays for Years 10 to 13. Town Square has no secondary school inside it, so children bus out to Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Arabian Ranches, Dubai Investments Park or The Sustainable City and arrive back between 16:20 and 17:15 depending on the corridor. Allow forty minutes for food and a short recovery and the first workable slot is 18:00. Primary children on the shorter northern routes can start at 17:00 or 17:15. Because lessons are online, the session begins when the child is at a desk rather than when a tutor finishes driving.

faqs.question: Does Town Square have its own school, or does every child commute?
faqs.answer: Town Square was built with nurseries but no secondary school, so every child above primary age travels out of the community each morning. Three corridors carry almost all of it: north to Motor City and Dubai Sports City, north-west to Arabian Ranches, and south to Dubai Investments Park, The Sustainable City and inner Dubailand. The southern route is longest on a map and sometimes fastest in practice because it runs counter to the main flow. Which corridor a family is on is the single biggest determinant of what their evenings can hold.

faqs.question: How many tutoring sessions a week fit into a Town Square evening?
faqs.answer: Two protected weekday slots and one weekend morning is the realistic budget for one child, and it shrinks when clubs or a sibling are involved. That is fewer than the four or five subjects a worried parent usually wants covered, which makes subject selection a genuine decision rather than a formality. Procedural subjects with public mark schemes repay an hour fastest. Essay subjects where the gap is unread text repay it slowest. Diagnosing a cross-cutting problem such as command terms can collapse a four-subject request into one subject plus a technique block.

faqs.question: Can a Town Square family keep sessions running through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Town Square families it often works better than a normal term-time slot. School days shorten, the household rhythm shifts, and a post-Iftar session around 21:00 has no bus in front of it and no immediate homework deadline behind it. Students are frequently sharper then than at 18:00 on an ordinary Tuesday. The practical requirement is to agree the timing with the tutor before Ramadan begins rather than renegotiating it nightly, and to reduce session frequency slightly while keeping continuity rather than pausing altogether.

faqs.question: How do we schedule two children in the same Town Square household?
faqs.answer: Stagger them rather than running sessions in parallel. The younger child takes 17:00 or 17:15 while the older eats and decompresses; the older takes 18:30 once the younger has finished. Each needs a quiet space, not a shared table, because a child in earshot of their sibling's lesson is not working. Where two siblings study the same subject a year apart, one tutor can often take both consecutively and run one plan with two branches. Across an IGCSE and a Diploma student that rarely works, because the assessment demands differ too much.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for a Town Square child?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, yes, with one weakness that matters here specifically. A group runs at a fixed time and moves on regardless of who attended. For a child whose bus arrival swings by thirty minutes, missed sessions are likely, and each missed session is a topic permanently skipped rather than deferred. One-to-one is the format with a realistic attendance rate from this community. Groups suit students with reliable arrival times and steady attainment who need pace rather than diagnosis, and for them the saving is real.

faqs.question: What does in-home tutoring cost in this part of Dubailand compared with online?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 180 to AED 350. Specialists in IB or IGCSE are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. The gap is mostly travel: a tutor driving to Town Square from central Dubai is pricing in a round trip of over an hour. Those are market figures from the providers named, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: They need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone providing private tuition without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Can we hire a teacher from our child's own school privately?
faqs.answer: It should not be pursued. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported by Gulf News, prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before relying on the detail, but the direction is clear. A better route is to ask the school what internal support it offers, then use an outside specialist for anything the school cannot supervise.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to schedule from a community like Town Square?
faqs.answer: Thin-pool Higher Level subjects, because availability and a narrow evening window multiply against each other. Higher Level Physics, Economics, Psychology, Business Management, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and second languages at Higher Level have small specialist pools everywhere. When the only free specialist cannot take 18:30, the options are a weekend slot, a different weekday, or a wait with a stated date. Online delivery is what makes any of it possible, since the pool is not limited to tutors willing to drive out to Al Qudra Road on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: If we move from Dubai to Sharjah or Abu Dhabi, does the tutoring have to change?
faqs.answer: The tutoring continues unchanged because it is delivered online, and the examination board travels with the student: a child entered for Cambridge 0580 sits the same specification in any emirate. What changes is the regulator. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah also approve fees, curricula and assessment methods, so ask the receiving school directly.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child finish an internal assessment before the school deadline?
faqs.answer: A tutor will teach the method, narrow the research question, explain each criterion in its own language, read the draft your child has produced and say which criterion is underserved and why. That is genuine help and it is what a school coordinator expects to see. A tutor will not supply sentences, rewrite the draft, provide data your child did not gather, or produce any part of the submission. Your child signs the authenticity declaration, so our role has to be compatible with that signature. Any provider offering a finished assessment is creating an expulsion risk.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see marks move?
faqs.answer: Six to eight weeks for a procedural problem, longer for anything that depends on reading the student has not done. A narrow drillable skill such as mole arithmetic, genetic-cross layout or economics diagram accuracy changes visibly within a month of weekly work. Retrieval under time takes six to eight weeks of timed practice. Essay technique in a literature subject is slower, because the limiting factor is often the text rather than the technique. No grade can be promised by any tutor, and a provider offering one is describing their marketing rather than your child.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutor in the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which board and syllabus code do you teach for this subject, and have you taught that exact specification? What will you do in the first session, and will you mark something of my child's against the official criteria? Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit? What is your position on internal assessment work? And can you hold a fixed slot at the time our bus actually gets home? A tutor who answers all five plainly is a different proposition from one who talks about passion.

faqs.question: Is there a trial session before we commit to a term?
faqs.answer: Yes. A free trial session is available, with its length and conditions stated at the time of booking rather than discovered afterwards. The useful way to spend it is diagnostically: have the tutor mark a real piece of your child's work against the official criteria and explain what they found. That tells you whether the tutor knows the specification and whether your child will work with them, which are the only two things a trial can genuinely establish. Scheduling fit is worth testing in the same session, at the real time.

dubai/town-square.closingHeading: Send us the arrival time, not just the subject
dubai/town-square.closingBody: Most tutoring arrangements in this community fail on scheduling rather than on teaching. So start there. Tell us the school, the year group, the board and syllabus code if you have it, the topics where marks are going, and the time your child actually walks back into Town Square. We will match a specialist who teaches that exact specification, hold a slot that fits after the bus, and run a diagnostic session over live video before anyone commits to a term. If the right specialist cannot take your window, we will say so and give you the alternatives rather than filling it with someone who can.

intro.heading: What a predicted grade is, and what a family can still do about it
paragraphs: Umm Al Sheif is a villa district on the inland side of the Jumeirah coast, bounded by Al Wasl Road, Sheikh Zayed Road and the Umm Suqeim and Al Safa streets either side. The housing is mostly large plots with established families, many of them long-settled in Dubai rather than newly arrived. The children are spread across British-curriculum schools heading into A Levels and IB continuum schools heading into the Diploma, with several of Dubai's most oversubscribed secondary schools within a short drive.

Because the households here are settled and the schools are academically selective in practice, the tutoring question that arrives is rarely 'my child is failing'. It is 'the school has predicted a 5 and the offer needs a 6'. That is a different problem with a different solution, and it has a calendar attached to it. Predicted grades in the Diploma are issued in the autumn of the final year and feed university applications; in the British system, predictions feed UCAS on a similar timetable. In both cases a prediction made in October constrains choices made in January.

The useful thing to understand is where a prediction comes from. It is a professional judgement built from internal assessment marks, mock paper performance, classwork and the subject teacher's read of trajectory. Some of those inputs are fixed by October and some are not. A student can still change mock performance, the quality of an internally assessed draft, and the evidence of trajectory. A student cannot change the first year of coursework marks that are already banked.

That distinction is what a sensible autumn plan is built on. Spend the hours on the inputs that are still live, in the order of how much weight they carry, and stop spending them on the ones that are closed. It sounds obvious and it is routinely got wrong, usually by reteaching the whole syllabus in a panic when the actual problem is that a Paper 2 essay has no evaluation in it.

Dubai's IB sector is growing, which matters for this neighbourhood. KHDA reported that Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7% of Dubai's private-school enrolment in 2024-25, out of 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula.

One limit stated up front. IB session and results dates are not published anywhere on this site, because they could not be confirmed against the IB's own pages — automated access to ibo.org is blocked, and an unverified date repeated across thousands of pages is thousands of errors. Take every IB date from your school's Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates in this page are taken from the boards' own published pages and are attributed where used.

dubai/umm-al-sheif.programmesIntro: Umm Al Sheif children sit mostly on the British route into A Levels and the IB continuum into the Diploma, with IGCSE as the common sixteen-year-old waypoint. Each note below is about what the programme means in a final-year autumn rather than in general.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component with published criteria. Final grades come from external papers sat in a single window combined with internal marks submitted and moderated beforehand. The total sits out of 45, with the core contributing additional points, and university offers are usually expressed as a total with minimum grades named in specific Higher Level subjects.
programmes.countryNote: The autumn of the second year is the pressure point for every Diploma family in Umm Al Sheif. Predicted grades, the Extended Essay final deadline, internal assessment deadlines in several subjects and university application dates land inside the same eight weeks. The households that handle it well are the ones that put all four calendars on one sheet in September. The ones that struggle are usually doing each component in the order its deadline arrives.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined externally, with Cambridge codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics, and Pearson International GCSE codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, which caps or opens the grade range before papers are sat. Results at sixteen determine sixth-form entry in Dubai's selective schools, which is why Year 11 in this area is treated with more seriousness than the qualification alone would suggest.
programmes.countryNote: In Umm Al Sheif the IGCSE grades matter twice: once for the certificate and once as the entry gate to a specific sixth form, since several nearby schools set subject-specific minimums for A Level or Diploma entry. Families are often working to a published entry requirement rather than to a general improvement goal, which makes the planning precise. Ask the receiving school for its subject prerequisites in writing before deciding where the tutoring hours go.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria labelled A to D with levels out of eight, task-specific rubrics and precise command terms. The Personal Project in the final year is an extended independent piece with its own criteria. Reports give criterion levels rather than percentages, which is more informative than parents assume once the letters are understood, and almost useless until they are.
programmes.countryNote: The step from MYP criterion levels into Diploma marks catches strong students in this area regularly. A student who has consistently scored 7s and 8s on criteria arrives in the Diploma and meets raw mark schemes and timed papers for the first time. The useful preparation in Year 11 is not more content; it is sitting timed questions and being marked against a real mark scheme so the change of currency is not a surprise in October.

programmes.name: A Levels after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, assessed almost entirely by external papers, with coursework in a minority of subjects. Offers are expressed as grades in named subjects, and the narrower load means a weak subject cannot be offset by breadth as it can in the Diploma. Students who prefer depth and dislike the Diploma core often do better here, and students who need breadth to stay motivated usually do not.
programmes.countryNote: Several Umm Al Sheif families are deciding between the Diploma and A Levels during Year 11, sometimes with siblings on each route. The decision is better made on evidence than on reputation: a student who writes well under time pressure and wants depth suits A Levels, and one who manages long independent projects well suits the Diploma. We will say which the marked scripts suggest, and we will say when the evidence is genuinely balanced.

dubai/umm-al-sheif.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Umm Al Sheif households ask about in a prediction-driven autumn. The descriptions name the component where the grade is usually won or lost rather than summarising the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level carries a third paper on an optional topic and is where predictions most often sit a grade below a student's self-assessment. The marks are in method lines and in the exploration. A student predicted a 5 who writes correct answers without working is often a 6 once the working habit is installed, which is weeks of work rather than months.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and calculator technique, with interpretation in context carrying real marks. Predictions here are often depressed by written explanation rather than by mathematics. Teaching the sentence that explains what a model implies is one of the fastest grade movements available in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Fields, waves, mechanics and, at Higher Level, quantum and nuclear topics. Predictions are usually limited by Paper 2 extended answers and by experimental-design questions rather than by the multiple-choice paper. The internally assessed investigation rewards a narrow question with controllable variables.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium, organic mechanisms and quantitative work. Mole arithmetic under time pressure is the commonest cap on a prediction. Mechanism questions want arrows and intermediates, not descriptions, and that distinction alone can move a Paper 2 mark noticeably within a few sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Physiology, genetics, ecology and the data-analysis strand. The command-term load is the heaviest of the sciences and the usual reason a prediction sits lower than a student's knowledge. Structured answer practice against mark schemes is the highest-yield intervention in the subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Essays, data response and the internal assessment commentaries. Predictions are usually set by the evaluation sentence at the end of long answers and by diagram accuracy. Both are teachable quickly. Higher Level quantitative work needs regular short practice rather than long sessions.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB Language A HL and SL · IGCSE First Language
subjects.description: Textual analysis, comparative essays, the individual oral and the higher level essay. The prediction is nearly always limited by the move from describing what a text says to analysing how it works. Students who read widely and write descriptively are the commonest case in this neighbourhood.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers rewarding application to the business in the stem. Predictions are limited by generic answers that could fit any company. The internally assessed research project needs an organisation that will actually supply information, which is worth checking before the question is fixed.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies, ethics and research methods, with answers that must name and use specific research. Predictions are usually limited by vague references to studies rather than precise ones. The internal assessment is a replication with strict conventions, and its marks are among the most recoverable in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, contributing to the overall points total alongside the Extended Essay. Rarely revised and frequently underestimated. A weak Theory of Knowledge grade costs points that a strong subject grade then has to make up, which is a poor trade for the hours involved.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. In a prediction-focused autumn it is the subject most often ignored and the one most likely to appear as a weak line on the school report.

dubai/umm-al-sheif.regionsIntro: Umm Al Sheif sits in the middle of the Jumeirah coastal belt, sharing schools and roads with the communities below. The notes describe what each neighbourhood changes for a household planning a final-year autumn.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Immediately to the west, with several of the area's selective secondary schools. Umm Al Sheif and Umm Suqeim families compete for the same sixth-form places, which is why subject-specific entry requirements are a live topic in Year 11 here.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Inland along Al Wasl Road, with long-established British-curriculum schools. The Al Safa run is short in distance and slow at the end of the school day, so an Umm Al Sheif family can usually plan a five o'clock weekday slot with confidence.

regions.name: Al Manara
regions.note: A smaller villa district on the other side of Sheikh Zayed Road, sharing both school routes and bus contractors. Households here face the same autumn calendar collision and often the same schools.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Coastal villas towards the sea, feeding the same primary and secondary schools. The practical overlap with Umm Al Sheif is the school bus timetable, which sets the earliest workable lesson slot in both communities.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The corridor along Al Wasl Road, dense with primary schools and after-school activity centres. Umm Al Sheif students often have an activity commitment here that decides which evenings can carry a 90-minute session.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: West along the coast, home to some of Dubai's most academically selective schools. Relevant to Umm Al Sheif families as a sixth-form destination and as a comparison point for entry requirements.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Offshore apartments and villas with a short connection to the coastal schools. Shares the Diploma autumn pressure and the same shortage of weekday evening tutoring slots in January.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Inland across Sheikh Zayed Road, with a dense school cluster across three curricula. The Al Barsha run is the longer option from Umm Al Sheif and pushes a weekday lesson start towards half past five.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: Newer coastal development with a growing family population. Households here are typically earlier in the school journey, so the requests are primary and lower secondary rather than prediction-driven.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1 and 2
regions.note: The older coastal villa streets closer to the city. Shares the Umm Al Sheif school map almost entirely, so the entry-requirement and prediction questions on this page apply there with little change.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Al Sheif and the Sheikh Zayed Road edge
schoolClusters.note: The schools reached most directly from these streets, covering the IB continuum and selective British routes. Several set subject-specific entry requirements for sixth form, which is why Year 11 planning in this neighbourhood is usually driven by a published prerequisite rather than by a general target.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa and the Jumeirah coast
schoolClusters.note: The inland and coastal runs, taking in long-established British-curriculum schools and the primary feeders that most of this neighbourhood's children pass through. The mix explains why one Umm Al Sheif household can be deciding between A Levels and the Diploma for two different children.

dubai/umm-al-sheif.modesIntro: Three formats that match the way a final-year autumn actually runs, all delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. None of them involves a tutor arriving at an address in the UAE.

modes.title: Component-targeted weekly sessions
modes.description: A fixed weekly slot aimed at one named component rather than at a subject in general: Paper 2 extended answers, the data-analysis strand, the evaluation sentence in long essays. Ninety minutes suits a Higher Level subject because it holds a timed question and the marking of it. The target is written down at the start and reviewed against evidence at six weeks.

modes.title: Internally assessed component supervision
modes.description: Short, well-timed support on an internally assessed piece: testing whether a research question is narrow enough, teaching the criteria letter by letter, and reading drafts the student has produced. Bought at the start of the task it saves weeks. Bought the week before the deadline it mostly salvages. The limits are set out in writing before the first session.

modes.description: A short concentrated block after mock results, built from the marked scripts rather than from a syllabus. The first session is diagnostic: read the scripts, classify the losses, rank them by recoverable marks. The block then works top to bottom through that list, which is usually technique first and content second.

sections.heading: Who lives in Umm Al Sheif, and what each household is actually buying
paragraphs: This is a settled villa neighbourhood rather than a transient one, and the tutoring requests reflect that. Households are generally several years into the same school and know the system; what they lack is not information about the Diploma or A Levels but a way to act on a specific piece of bad news. The bad news is almost always a number: a predicted grade, a mock percentage, or a sixth-form entry requirement that the current trajectory does not meet.

The four recurring cases are distinct enough to need different plans. The final-year Diploma household has eight crowded weeks and needs triage. The Year 11 household is working to a published entry requirement for a specific sixth form. The younger secondary household is trying to keep options open before the Year 9 or Year 11 fork. And the primary household, often in the same house as one of the others, needs short frequent sessions and no exam language at all.

What unites them is an unusually tight evening. Umm Al Sheif children have short commutes by Dubai standards but heavy extracurricular commitments, often sport or music several evenings a week at clubs along Al Wasl Road or on the coast. The practical consequence is that this neighbourhood has fewer usable weekday slots than its geography suggests, and the weekend slot is the one that carries the serious work.

Find your row in the table, then read the two sections that follow it. The order of this page is deliberate: predictions and the autumn calendar first, because those are what the October and January enquiries are about, and everything else afterwards.

sections.heading: The final-year autumn, when school deadlines and university applications collide
paragraphs: Put four calendars on one page in September and the autumn becomes manageable. The four are the school's internal deadlines for assessed components, the school's own timetable for mocks and predicted grades, the university application deadlines for the countries the student is applying to, and the family's own commitments. Each of them is reasonable alone. Together, in an eight-week window, they are what produces the October collapse that Diploma coordinators see every year.

The sequencing insight is simple. Anything that feeds a predicted grade has to be good before the prediction is made, not afterwards. That makes the autumn mocks and the internally assessed drafts the highest-value work in the year, far above general revision. A student who improves in February has improved after the number that went on their application was fixed.

The second insight is about what to drop. Nobody can do everything in those eight weeks, so decide in advance what is being done to a lower standard, consciously, rather than letting the last deadline win by default. Theory of Knowledge is usually the component that gets sacrificed, which is a mistake, because its points are cheap to earn relative to lifting a Higher Level subject by a grade.

For Cambridge and Pearson candidates the equivalent calendar is published and can be relied on. Cambridge's March series key dates put final entries on 27 November 2026 and the exam period on 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. For the IB Diploma we publish no dates: take them from your school's coordinator, because the IB's own pages could not be verified directly.

sections.heading: Predicted grades: how they are made and what can still move
paragraphs: A predicted grade is a professional judgement, not an arithmetic output, and it is made from a mixture of inputs with different degrees of finality. Internal assessment marks already submitted are fixed. Marks from the first year are fixed. Mock performance in the autumn is live. The quality of a draft not yet finished is live. The teacher's read of trajectory is live, and it is influenced by what has happened in the last six weeks more than by what happened a year ago.

That is the whole strategy. Spend the autumn hours on the live inputs, in the order of how much they weigh, and accept the fixed ones. It is also why the conversation with the subject teacher matters: a teacher who can see a student's improved timed work in October has evidence to revise a judgement, and a teacher shown only effort has nothing to revise it with.

Parents sometimes ask whether a prediction can be challenged. In most schools it can be discussed, with evidence, and in some it can be reviewed. What moves it is a marked script that is better than the one the judgement was based on. What does not move it is a parental assessment of potential. Collect the scripts, get them marked honestly against the mark scheme, and present the better ones.

The uncomfortable part is that a prediction can be accurate and still unwelcome. Where the evidence says a Higher Level 7 is not reachable in the time available, the better use of the autumn may be securing the other five subjects and the core points rather than spending every hour on the one that will not move. We will say that where the scripts say it, because the alternative is a family spending a term on the lowest-return hour in the week.

sections.heading: What a university offer actually asks for, and what that changes
paragraphs: Offers are rarely a single number. A typical conditional offer for a Diploma student names a total points figure and then adds minimum grades in specified Higher Level subjects, which means a student can hit the total and still miss the offer. For A Level applicants the structure is simpler but less forgiving: named grades in named subjects, with no breadth to absorb a weak result.

Read the offer letter as a specification and plan against it literally. If the offer requires a 6 in Higher Level Chemistry and a total, then Chemistry is a different kind of priority from a subject contributing only to the total. Hours should follow that hierarchy rather than following which subject feels worst. Families frequently discover in April that they spent the autumn on a subject that was never the binding constraint.

For students staying in the UAE for university there is a second process to plan for. Recognition of a secondary certificate generally runs through the Ministry of Education's equivalency route, which has published criteria. On the British track those are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. On the American track, English proficiency requires 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

We do not publish an IB points figure for equivalency, because no such figure could be verified against a Ministry source and a wrong number repeated at scale is worse than no number. Equivalency is also not something we perform or guarantee; it is a process run by the authority, and families should take the requirements from the Ministry's own channels. Nor is tutoring a requirement for it — any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about an administrative process.

sections.heading: The supervised hour, and what a villa household can actually control
paragraphs: In a large house with a busy family, the hardest thing to produce is not tutoring; it is a reliably quiet, reliably supervised hour of independent work. The Diploma assumes a substantial amount of it and schools cannot provide it. Parents in this neighbourhood often have the resources to buy teaching and no mechanism at all for the unsupervised half of the week, which is where most grades are actually decided.

Three things make that hour work, and none of them costs anything. The first is a fixed place: the same desk, the same room, every time, so the student stops deciding where to work. The second is a fixed start, which removes the negotiation. The third is a defined output — not 'revise biology' but 'this past-paper section, timed, marked against the scheme, with the losses listed'. Vague intentions produce the appearance of study and very little else.

Supervision does not mean sitting with a teenager. It means the output being looked at by someone afterwards. A tutor who starts each weekly session by reviewing what was produced in the independent hours changes the economics of those hours entirely, because they stop being optional. This is the single most useful thing a weekly slot does, and it is rarely what is advertised.

Household staff, siblings and the general traffic of a large villa in the early evening all work against the quiet hour. Choosing a time deliberately — before the household fills up, or late enough that it has settled — matters more than the room. Families who treat the independent hour as a scheduled appointment rather than as leftover time get noticeably more from the same number of paid lessons.
bullets: Fixed place, fixed time, defined output - all free, all effective

sections.heading: What tutoring costs on this stretch of the coast
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai span a wide range, and most of the best-ranking pages for these searches quote no figure at all. The table sets out the market's own numbers with the provider that published each. They describe the market and are not an IB Gram price list; ask us for the trial and the consultation if you want our figures and what sits inside the hour.

Households in Umm Al Sheif usually buy at the specialist end, which is reasonable in a final-year autumn and wasteful earlier. A Year 9 student who needs working-shown habits installed does not need an examiner-experienced specialist at the top of the range; a Diploma student whose offer turns on a Higher Level grade may. Matching the band to the job is where most of the available saving is.

There is a context figure worth holding alongside the rates. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Against flat fees, a household can plan a full-year tutoring spend rather than a reactive term, and spreading the same hours across a year almost always buys more improvement than concentrating them in a panic.

Ask what is inside the rate before comparing numbers: whether marking of work set between sessions is included, whether the rate is per hour or per session, and whether it changes in the exam term. Those three answers vary more between providers than the headline figures do.

sections.heading: The reference, the personal statement and what a tutor may not touch
paragraphs: A final-year autumn generates documents beyond coursework, and the rules around them are less widely understood than the academic-honesty rules for an internally assessed component. A personal statement, an application essay and a reference are each owned by someone, and getting that ownership wrong is a misrepresentation to a university rather than a school matter.

The reference belongs to the school and nobody outside it should be drafting any part of it. The personal statement or application essay belongs to the student, and universities ask applicants to confirm it is their own work; some run similarity checking across submissions. A tutor can teach structure, can explain what admissions readers are assessing, and can read a draft the student has produced and comment on it. A tutor cannot supply sentences, provide a template to be lightly adapted, or produce the piece for the student to submit.

The same ownership logic runs through the academic components. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria letter by letter, test whether a research question is narrow enough to generate usable data, read a draft the student has produced and give feedback on reasoning and structure, and teach the needed skills on a different example. A tutor may not author any part of a submission, build the student's data set, or hand over a model answer to the student's own question.

Where a school's rules are tighter than the board's, the school's rules apply; some Dubai schools limit external feedback on an assessed draft to a single round. Ask about that at the start of a task rather than at the end. And treat any provider offering finished work with real suspicion: at least one operation in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, and what is being sold is a declaration of authenticity the student has to sign.

sections.heading: An online lesson from an Umm Al Sheif villa, practically
paragraphs: The question most parents here ask about format is not price but whether a screen can carry serious analytical work. For written subjects and quantitative subjects it carries it better than a table does, for one specific reason: the script is shared, annotated live and kept by both sides. A page marked at a kitchen table goes into a bag and is not available next week when the same error recurs.

The practical setup takes ten minutes. A laptop rather than a phone, headphones, a flat surface, and a way to get a handwritten page onto the screen — a phone photograph into a shared folder is enough. For mathematics and the sciences a cheap writing tablet is worth having, though a photographed page works. Test all of it in the trial rather than in week four of a paid arrangement.

IB Gram delivers tutoring to Umm Al Sheif as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. That is said plainly because this market has a habit of implying a visit and clarifying later, which wastes a family's time and sometimes a deposit.

The honest comparison is in the table. A tutor in the room wins on physical presence and on young children. Online wins on who you can reach, on whether the full session happens, and on whether the marked work still exists next week. For a prediction-driven autumn in this neighbourhood, those three things are usually what decide the outcome.

sections.heading: Starting in October, which is late but not too late
paragraphs: A family that gets in touch in October has less room than one that started in June, and it is still a workable position. What makes it workable is accepting that triage, not coverage, is the task. Six subjects and three core components cannot all be improved in eight weeks. Two can, and the right two are the ones that carry the most recoverable marks relative to the offer.

The first conversation is short and evidence-led. We want the predicted grades, the offer conditions where they exist, the most recent marked scripts, the school's own deadline schedule for assessed components, and the two slots that genuinely exist in the week. From that we produce a ranked list of where the hours should go and, just as importantly, what is being deliberately left alone.

The trial session is taught rather than sold, with a short diagnostic and a written note afterwards naming the gaps found. Where the evidence says a target is not reachable in the time, we say so. A family spending every remaining hour on a Higher Level grade that will not move, while five other subjects and the core drift, is the commonest expensive mistake of a final-year autumn.

On availability: the weekday window between half past four and six is the most requested in Dubai, and in January, after mocks, it is effectively full. If the slot is not there we say so and offer the real alternatives rather than the nearest substitute. For a few niche Higher Level subjects the specialist may be based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening; we tell you where a tutor is based whenever you ask.

process.title: Send the prediction and the offer
process.description: A predicted grade on its own is half the picture. The offer conditions tell us which subject is the binding constraint, and that is what hours should follow. Families frequently spend an autumn on the subject that feels worst rather than the one the offer turns on.

process.title: Send the marked scripts
process.description: Percentages say how much was lost; scripts say where. Twenty minutes with a marked mock separates technique losses from timing losses from genuine content gaps, and those three problems need three different plans and three different kinds of tutor.

process.title: Put four calendars on one sheet
process.description: School assessed-component deadlines, the mock and prediction timetable, university application dates, and the family's own commitments. Each is reasonable alone; together they are the eight weeks that go wrong. Seeing them together is most of the fix.

process.title: Rank by recoverable marks
process.description: We produce a ranked list of where hours would buy the most, and we name what is being left alone on purpose. Deciding that deliberately is better than letting the nearest deadline decide it for you in week three.

process.title: Protect the independent hour
process.description: Fixed place, fixed time, defined output, reviewed in the next session. The unsupervised half of the week is where Diploma grades are decided, and making it non-optional costs nothing and changes more than an extra paid hour does.

process.title: Review against evidence at six weeks
process.description: A repeat timed paper, marked the same way, compared with the first. If the marks have not moved we change the tutor, the method, or the subject receiving the hours, and we say when the honest answer is that the target needs revising.

whyPoints.title: Built around the prediction, not the syllabus
whyPoints.description: The enquiries from this neighbourhood arrive in October and January because a number came back. We start from that number, work out which inputs to it are still live, and spend the hours there. Reteaching a syllabus in week two of November is the expensive alternative.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts before any teaching
whyPoints.description: A marked mock tells you whether marks went to missing working, command-term mismatch, timing or real content gaps. Those four have different fixes and different costs. We read the scripts first and tell you which case you are in before suggesting a plan.

whyPoints.title: The ownership line written down
whyPoints.description: References belong to the school, statements and assessed work belong to the student. We teach criteria, test research questions and give feedback on drafts the student produced. No sentence in any submission originates with the tutor, and we say so before the first session.

whyPoints.title: Honest when a target will not move
whyPoints.description: Where the evidence says a Higher Level grade is not reachable in the weeks available, the better plan is usually securing the other subjects and the core points. We will say that, even though recommending a term of lessons would be easier.

whyPoints.title: Prices described, never disguised
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market rate with the publisher named, and none of them is ours. We will tell you what sits inside our hour, including whether marking between sessions is part of it, before anything is booked.

whyPoints.title: No unverified dates, no borrowed authority
whyPoints.description: IB session dates are absent from this page because they could not be verified against the IB's own pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates are attributed. KHDA inspects schools and MoHRE issues the tutoring permit; IB Gram holds no accreditation from either.

faqs.question: My child's predicted grade is below the offer. Is there anything we can actually do in October?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only on the inputs that are still live. Internal assessment marks already submitted and first-year results are fixed. Autumn mock performance, unfinished drafts and the teacher's read of recent trajectory are not. So the hours should go to timed papers marked against mark schemes and to finishing an assessed draft properly, which is exactly where most families do not spend them. If a school allows a prediction to be discussed, what moves it is a better marked script, not an assessment of potential.

faqs.question: How is a predicted grade actually decided?
faqs.answer: It is a professional judgement by the subject teacher, built from internal assessment marks, mock paper performance, classwork and a read of trajectory. The weighting varies by school and by teacher, and no formula is published. What matters practically is that some inputs are closed by October and some are open, and that recent evidence tends to carry disproportionate weight in a judgement made in November. A student who produces visibly better timed work across six weeks gives a teacher something to revise the judgement with.

faqs.question: Which schools do Umm Al Sheif families usually apply to for sixth form?
faqs.answer: Households on these streets look mainly at the selective British-curriculum schools and the IB continuum schools within a short drive, across Umm Al Sheif, Al Safa, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh. The practical point is that several set subject-specific entry requirements rather than a general grade average, so a Year 11 plan should be built against a written prerequisite from the receiving school. Ask for it in writing early; families regularly discover in March that a specific subject grade was the gate.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to the house in Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers tutoring in the UAE as one-to-one lessons online, over live video, and does not send anyone to a residential address anywhere in the Emirates. Visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Local agencies and independent tutors do offer visits, with published market rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel. What we offer instead is a tutor matched to the specific component your child is losing marks in, and a shared annotated script that still exists the following week.

faqs.question: Is a 90-minute session too long for a Diploma student after school?
faqs.answer: For most Higher Level work it is the right length, but the slot matters. Ninety minutes is what a timed paper section plus line-by-line marking actually needs, and that exercise is the highest-value thing a tutor does with a final-year student. On a weekday evening after school and an activity, a tired student gets less from it. The pattern that works in this neighbourhood is a shorter weekday session for one technique and a 90-minute weekend slot for timed practice and marking.

faqs.question: Should we spend the autumn on the weakest subject or the one the offer names?
faqs.answer: The one the offer names, almost always. A conditional offer typically combines a total with minimum grades in specific Higher Level subjects, which means a student can reach the total and still miss the offer. Hours should follow the binding condition rather than the subject that feels worst, and those are frequently different subjects. Read the offer letter as a specification and plan against it literally. Families who do not often discover in April that they optimised the wrong variable.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a personal statement or application essay?
faqs.answer: Within limits that are stricter than most people assume. The statement belongs to the student and universities ask applicants to confirm it is their own work, with some running similarity checks across submissions. A tutor can teach structure, explain what admissions readers assess, and read a draft the student has produced and comment on it. A tutor cannot supply sentences, hand over a template to be lightly adapted, or produce the piece for submission. The school's reference is the school's alone and nobody outside should touch it.

faqs.question: How much does tutoring cost for a Higher Level subject in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above per hour, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450+, and premium or examiner-experienced tutors from AED 500-650+, where BartyED publishes AED 650. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors listing AED 200 for IB. Those are the market's figures with their sources, not ours. Ask any provider whether marking between sessions is inside the rate before comparing numbers.

faqs.question: What should a student be doing in the independent hours that nobody supervises?
faqs.answer: Something with an output. Not 'revise chemistry' but 'this past-paper section, timed, marked against the scheme, with the losses listed'. Fixed place, fixed start time and a defined product are what turn an intention into an hour of work, and none of them costs anything. The mechanism that makes it stick is review: a tutor who opens each weekly session with what was produced in those hours changes their status from optional to expected, which is most of the benefit of a weekly slot.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give IB exam and results dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and publishing an unverified date across thousands of pages would multiply a single error thousands of times. Treat the May session as the one UAE schools sit and take exact dates from your school's Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates used on this page come from those boards' own published pages and are attributed where they appear.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge worth spending tutoring hours on?
faqs.answer: More than most families think. It contributes to the overall points total alongside the Extended Essay, and its marks are usually cheaper to earn than lifting a Higher Level subject by a grade, because the skills are specific and teachable: reading a prescribed title precisely, structuring an argument around knowledge claims, using examples that do work rather than decorating the essay. It is also the component most often sacrificed in a crowded autumn, which means a few well-timed sessions can recover points that nobody else is competing for.

faqs.question: My daughter is choosing between A Levels and the Diploma. How do we decide?
faqs.answer: On evidence rather than on reputation. Sit a timed essay or problem paper in her two strongest subjects and have it marked honestly. A student who writes well under pressure, wants depth and dislikes long independent projects usually does better on three or four A Levels. A student who manages extended independent work well and needs breadth to stay engaged usually does better on the Diploma. Where the evidence is genuinely balanced we say so, and the deciding factor is then the school and the teaching rather than the qualification.

faqs.question: What are the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements for a British-track student?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. On the American track, English proficiency needs 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics needs at least 450 in SAT Math. Verify current rules with the Ministry directly; equivalency is not something we perform.

faqs.question: We only want help for the last stretch before the written papers. Is that sensible?
faqs.answer: It can be, provided the target is the right one. A short block in the final weeks works well for timing, paper technique and the two or three topics a marked script identifies as genuinely weak. It does not work for building content that was never learned, and it cannot change a prediction that has already gone on an application. If the goal is the final grade rather than the prediction, a late block is a reasonable purchase. If the goal is the prediction, the work had to happen in the autumn.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we want has no slot left in January?
faqs.answer: We tell you and give you the real options: a different time with the same tutor, a different tutor with the same component experience, or waiting. January after mocks is the busiest period in the Dubai market and the half past four to six weekday window fills first. For a few niche Higher Level subjects the person who knows the paper may be based outside the UAE and teaching into a UAE evening, and we say where a tutor is based whenever you ask. We do not invent availability to hold an enquiry.

dubai/umm-al-sheif.closingHeading: Start from the number that worried you
dubai/umm-al-sheif.closingBody: Send us the predicted grades, the offer conditions if there are any, the most recent marked scripts and the school's own deadline schedule. We will tell you which inputs are still live, rank where the remaining hours would buy the most, and name what we would deliberately leave alone. Where the evidence says a target needs revising rather than chasing, we will say that too. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, and the first one is taught rather than sold.

dubai/umm-suqeim.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below cover the Diploma, the Middle Years Programme, both IGCSE boards and the mandatory UAE subjects. For a multi-child household, ask about consecutive slots on the same evening rather than matching each child separately.

intro.heading: Who lives in Umm Suqeim, and what each kind of household needs
paragraphs: Umm Suqeim is three districts rather than one. Umm Suqeim 1 runs inland from Kite Beach towards Al Wasl Road and holds older villa plots and a growing number of low-rise apartment buildings. Umm Suqeim 2 is quieter, almost entirely residential, and sits between Al Manara and the beach. Umm Suqeim 3 reaches down past Madinat Jumeirah towards Al Sufouh, with large compounds and a mix of long-settled families and newer short-lease tenants. Those three profiles produce three different tuition requests, and treating them as one neighbourhood is why most area pages are useless.

The long-settled villa household typically has two or three children spread across primary and secondary, often at two different schools because the sibling policy ran out or because one child moved for a particular sixth form. Their problem is logistics before it is academic: one evening, two homework loads, one parent driving. The academic pressure point arrives when the eldest hits Year 10 or the first Diploma year and the household discovers that the coursework load does not fit around the younger children's bedtime.

The apartment household in Umm Suqeim 1 looks different. More often a single child or two close in age, a shorter lease, a higher chance of having arrived mid-year from another system entirely. Their pressure point is transition: a child who was two years ahead in a national curriculum landing in a Year 9 set that assesses completely differently, or a Year 11 arrival who has never sat a tiered paper. Those students need diagnosis before they need teaching.

The third group is the household that is bilingual at home but not in Arabic, which in Umm Suqeim is most of them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. That lesson is on the timetable every week, it carries real marks, and it is the subject families most often leave until it becomes a problem on a report.

IB Gram matches tutors to all of that online, one-to-one, over live video. There is no centre in Dubai to visit and no tutor is sent to an Umm Suqeim address; home visits are an India-only service. For a household running consecutive sessions on a Tuesday evening, that turns out to be the easier arrangement anyway: two children, two specialists, two syllabuses, one room, no second car journey. It also changes who you are choosing from. A tutor who drives to this district at five o'clock is selected from the people able to be in this district at five o'clock, which is a large group for Year 8 mathematics and a very small one for Chemistry at Higher Level under the current guide.

The rest of this page is written for those four household shapes rather than for a generic parent. It sets out the school routes from each of the three Umm Suqeim districts, what KHDA actually requires for Arabic and Islamic Education and how that changes the support a non-Arab child needs, how two siblings on two different examination boards end up with two incompatible revision plans, what a term of tuition costs once the hours are multiplied out, and the regulator map that matters the moment a family relocates to another emirate. Every figure is attributed to the source that published it.
