faqs.question: Which schools do Villanova children usually attend?
faqs.answer: The short-run group includes GEMS FirstPoint School in neighbouring The Villa, GEMS Wellington Academy Silicon Oasis, The Aquila School, Dubai English Speaking College, Repton School Dubai and Kent College Dubai. Families wanting an IB continuum or a bilingual diploma route tend to look towards GEMS Modern Academy, Uptown International School, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Greenfield International School, Fairgreen International School or Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. These names are local context only, to help you identify your child's curriculum and entries. IB Gram has no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Should my child sit First Language English or English as a Second Language?
faqs.answer: It depends on marked evidence rather than on nationality or household language. Cambridge 0500 assesses reading and writing at strong first-language level, with evidence selection and timed planning deciding grades. Cambridge 0510 and 0511 assess functional competence across four skills, are more procedural, and improve faster with targeted work. The risk is a student placed in the second-language entry who could manage the first-language paper with two terms of support, because the safer administrative choice is nobody's responsibility to revisit. Test it with a timed 0500-style response marked against the criteria in Year 9.

faqs.question: Can my child take our home language as an IGCSE or Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is frequently unclaimed. Cambridge offers Arabic as a First Language, syllabus 0508, among other first-language entries, and where a school offers the entry it converts an existing strength into a certificated subject. At Diploma level a home language may be available as a Language A, and where the school does not teach it, a school-supported self-taught Language A route at Standard Level may be possible. Ask the Diploma coordinator or the examinations officer directly rather than assuming it is unavailable, because it will not be offered unprompted.

faqs.question: What is a bilingual diploma and does my child qualify?
faqs.answer: It is awarded where a Diploma student completes two Language A subjects, or a Language A plus a subject studied in that language. A meaningful number of multilingual Villanova students either qualify or could qualify with modest adjustment to their course selection, and very few are told it exists. It is a real distinction worth having, and the time to ask is before Diploma subject choices are finalised rather than after. Raise it with the Diploma coordinator specifically, by name, because a general question about languages will not surface it.

faqs.question: Which Arabic stream is my child in, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters, because the streams teach different content. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is primary for Social Studies for Arab students; the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Ask the school which stream applies and why.

faqs.question: Can a tutor use material other than the school's for Arabic or Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: No, and this is a specific KHDA constraint rather than a preference. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support therefore means working through the school's own material: comprehension, written structure, script fluency and systematic vocabulary built on what the school has set. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a reasonable thing to ask your school about.

faqs.question: Why would a confident Arabic speaker in Villanova still lose marks in the Arabic exam?
faqs.answer: Almost always the distance between spoken dialect and Modern Standard Arabic, which is the examined register. A student can hold a fluent conversation and be unable to write to the standard the assessment expects, because the two use different vocabulary, different syntax and in effect different registers. This is predictable rather than a deficiency, and it is coachable: script fluency under time, systematic vocabulary in the standard register, and written structure. It responds better to three short sessions a week than to one long one, which Villanova's short school runs make practical.

faqs.question: Is Language B or ab initio the right Diploma choice for a near-beginner?
faqs.answer: Ab initio is designed for near-beginners with little or no prior study, has prescribed themes and tightly defined assessment, and is unusually coachable as a result. Language B is for competent second-language users and is assessed on receptive, productive and interactive skills. The error that recurs in both directions: a student already past the ab initio ceiling placed there for timetable convenience and left under-credited, or a student put into Language B whose register is considerably weaker than their vocabulary suggests. A short spoken and written assessment settles it.

faqs.question: Where do students actually lose marks in a language paper?
faqs.answer: Rarely on vocabulary. Four places account for most of it. Register: every productive task names an audience and a text type, and those marks are allocated whether or not the student noticed. Incomplete prompt coverage: prompts carry two or three elements and students answer the interesting one. Timed planning, which has to be practised under time rather than understood in principle. And description instead of analysis in unseen papers, where a student says what a text means rather than how it produces its effect. All four are teachable in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Can my child draft in one language and translate into the examined language?
faqs.answer: Not for work that is assessed. Submitted work has to represent the student's own competence in the language being assessed, and in a language paper a translation engine substitutes for precisely the thing being measured. A dictionary, and a bilingual glossary where the school permits one, are tools. A tutor is bound by the same principle: teaching register, modelling text types, explaining criteria and giving feedback on the student's own draft are permitted, while translating the work, supplying sentences or producing any part of the submission is not.

faqs.question: What does a specialist language tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel and budget platforms from AED 33 to AED 65. Scarce courses such as Cambridge 0508, Diploma Arabic B at Higher Level or ab initio sit at the specialist end, and that premium reflects pool depth rather than quality. Those are market figures from published provider pages and Bestimate's 2026 table, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why is an online tutor better for a scarce language course?
faqs.answer: Because the limiting factor becomes course experience rather than geography. The number of tutors who have actually taught Cambridge 0508, Diploma Arabic B at Higher Level or a particular ab initio course is small in absolute terms, and restricting that set to people willing to drive to Dubailand on a weekday evening reduces it to almost nothing. Fluency in a language is not the same as experience of its examined course criteria, and the difference appears in the first marked piece. Online delivery is how you get the second rather than the first.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities near Academic City care which Diploma maths course my child takes?
faqs.answer: Some degree programmes specify one rather than the other, particularly in engineering, economics and the physical sciences, and the Diploma offers Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches alongside Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. The only reliable source is the admissions page of the specific institution and programme, checked in the application year, because requirements change and vary between universities. Proximity to Dubai Academic City makes it easy to ask the admissions office directly. No tutoring page, including this one, is a source for a particular university's requirement.

faqs.question: What does MoE equivalency require for a student with English as a second language?
faqs.answer: On the American track the sourced requirements are English proficiency via IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, plus at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. On the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold appears in that guidance, so verify any IB figure on moe.gov.ae directly.

faqs.question: How early can sessions start for a Villanova family?
faqs.answer: Earlier than in most of Dubailand, which is a genuine advantage here. With GEMS FirstPoint School in neighbouring The Villa and a short, reliable run through the Silicon Oasis corridor, many Villanova children are home well before families in the Al Qudra communities, whose secondary buses take forty to seventy minutes. A 17:00 start is realistic, and that is what makes three short language sessions a week schedulable rather than theoretical. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time and hold the same slot each week.

dubai/villanova.closingBody: If one thing on this page is worth acting on, it is checking which English entry, Arabic stream and Diploma language courses your child is on, and whether anyone examined those choices with evidence. Send us the school, the year group and those three answers, along with a piece of recent written work, and we will match a tutor who has taught that exact course rather than one who simply speaks the language. Where the course is a scarce one and nobody is free for your slot, we will say so and give you the alternatives.

dubai/weekend-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects into Gulf Standard Time weekends. A weekend tutor is chosen for a different skill from a weekday one: marking accurately to the current markscheme and writing feedback a student can act on without the tutor present.

intro.heading: Why the weekend is the only slot where a Diploma student can sit a real paper
paragraphs: The arithmetic of a Dubai school night is unforgiving. The bus returns between about 15:15 and 16:30, there is homework for six subjects, an activity on two or three evenings, and a household that would like to eat together. Into that a family drops a 60-minute tutoring session, usually between 18:00 and 20:00, which is the busiest window in the emirate. Something useful can happen in that hour, but one thing definitely cannot: the student cannot sit a two-hour Paper 2 under timed conditions and then go through it while the decisions are still fresh.

The weekend changes that. Since the UAE moved to a Monday-to-Friday working week with a half-day Friday in January 2022, Saturday and Sunday have been the protected days for most Dubai families, and private schools run Monday to Friday. A Saturday morning block starting at 09:00 or 10:00 gives a Diploma student a clear two hours with a working brain. The paper gets sat properly, the clock gets respected, and the marking conversation happens immediately rather than being deferred to a Tuesday when the student has forgotten why they chose that method.

That is the practical case. The editorial case, and the reason this page is organised the way it is, is evidence. Tutoring in Dubai is frequently sold on reassurance: a nice tutor, an engaged student, a parent who feels better. None of that is evidence. The things that count as evidence are a marked script with a total on it, a criterion-by-criterion note on an internal assessment draft, a list of the specific question types the student is still losing marks on, and the same measurements repeated six weeks later.

Weekend sessions produce that evidence more reliably than weekday ones because the format allows it. There is room for a full paper and the marking. There is room to read an internal assessment draft properly rather than skimming it. And because a weekend slot is usually the only tutoring session of the week, the work between sessions is clearly attributable: whatever changed, changed because of the practice the student did and the feedback they acted on, not because three different adults touched the subject on three different evenings.

The sections below set out what a weekend block should contain, what the internal assessment criteria actually reward, what grade movement is realistic over a term and how to see it in the numbers, how Ramadan and the UAE academic calendar reshape the weekend, and what weekend market rates look like in AED. One section covers the opposite case honestly: the situations where a weekend tutor is the wrong purchase and a different intervention is the right one. Read that one first if you are deciding whether to buy anything at all, because it is the section most likely to save you a term's fees.

dubai/weekend-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: A weekend block is used differently at each stage of the IB continuum. These are the programmes Dubai families book weekend sessions for, and what the time is actually spent on in each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. External papers carry most of each subject grade and the internal assessment carries the rest. A weekend block in Year 13 is normally a timed paper plus marking; in Year 12 it is more often internal assessment planning and content consolidation.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts are small and their internal deadlines are set by the school rather than the IB, so two students in the same emirate can have internal assessment deadlines eight weeks apart. A weekend plan built from your school's own calendar is therefore different from a generic one, and the first question in a diagnostic session is which deadline is next.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The exhibition requires three objects and a commentary of around 1,600 words; the prescribed-title essay is also about 1,600 words; the Extended Essay is 4,000 words with a school-appointed supervisor. Up to three bonus points sit on the 45-point total. These are the components most suited to a weekend slot, because reading and discussing 4,000 words takes longer than an hour.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay supervisor is appointed by the Dubai school and signs the reflection sessions. A weekend tutor works beside that process: testing whether the research question is answerable within the word limit, whether sources are reachable, and whether each section does what the assessment criteria ask. The student writes every word themselves.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four lettered criteria each, marked 1-8 per criterion and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Weekend blocks here are usually spent learning to read the criteria: what separates a 5-6 band response from a 7-8 one in the same task, and why a detailed answer can still sit in the middle band.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 is the highest-value year for weekend work in Dubai, because it is the last chance to build timed-writing stamina before Year 12 demands it. Students arriving in the Diploma from a criterion-based, redraft-friendly MYP often meet their first genuinely timed paper in October of Year 12, which is a poor moment to discover the gap.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into Diploma Year 12
programmes.ageRange: Ages 15-16 · The summer and first term
programmes.description: The bridge most often booked as a weekend block: the step up in abstraction in Mathematics, the jump from structured science questions to extended explanation, and the first encounter with command terms that carry fixed expectations. Six to eight weekend sessions across the summer and early autumn is the common shape.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students arrive in Year 12 from several different Year 11 experiences: Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel, MYP and an American high-school track. Each leaves a different gap. A weekend diagnostic that marks one piece of recent work tells you which of those gaps you are actually dealing with before any money is spent on a term plan.

dubai/weekend-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects most often booked into a weekend block, with what a two-hour weekend session does for each that a weekday hour cannot.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A weekend block fits a complete paper plus marking, which matters here more than in any other subject because method marks are only visible in a full script. The recurring finding is that students lose more marks to unshown working and calculator choice than to not knowing the mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Heavily contextual, so questions are long and reading them accurately takes practice under a clock. Weekend sessions are usually spent on modelling questions and the statistics content, where a correct calculation attached to the wrong interpretation scores a fraction of the available marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The internal assessment is the main weekend workload: a two-hour block is long enough to read a draft against the criteria and work through the evaluation section properly. Paper work concentrates on energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, with significant figures and state symbols as the recurring avoidable losses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Extended-response explanation is the skill that needs unhurried practice: a causal chain written out in full, then marked against the markscheme line by line. Uncertainty propagation in the internal assessment is the other weekend job, because it cannot be rushed and is where a whole criterion band is usually lost.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-analysis questions carry a large share of the paper marks and are the part students practise least. A weekend block allows a set of unseen data questions to be sat, marked and repeated. Terminology precision is marked strictly, so the marking conversation matters as much as the attempt.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries of 800 words each, spread across the two years, which makes this the subject where weekend deadlines bite most predictably. Diagram accuracy is assessed, not decorative, and a weekend session is where a student can redraw a diagram set until the axes and shifts are automatic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under time pressure, which is the definition of a task that needs a clear two hours to rehearse. Weekend blocks are also where the individual oral gets rehearsed properly, because a ten-minute delivery plus feedback does not fit inside a weekday hour.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source papers reward provenance analysis and cross-referencing rather than knowledge, and that is a markscheme habit best built on full papers rather than extracts. The HL regional option needs a bank of dated specifics, which weekend sessions can test systematically rather than incidentally.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level pre-released case study rewards months of structured preparation, which fits a weekly weekend slot better than anything else in the Diploma. Weekend work is mostly applying tools to the stimulus rather than learning them, because unapplied theory scores almost nothing.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay are both long-form and both benefit from an uninterrupted conversation. A weekend block can test whether an argument actually answers the prescribed title, which is the single most common structural failure and the hardest thing to diagnose in a rushed weekday hour.

dubai/weekend-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Weekend availability varies across Dubai less by distance than by what else is in the diary. These are the communities where weekend blocks are most requested and the practical pattern in each.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Apartment living with a heavy Saturday activity schedule: swimming, football and music often fill the morning. The 08:30 and 09:00 starts are the ones that survive a whole term here, and families who start later usually find the slot competing with something by week five.

regions.name: Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Similar rhythm to the Marina with more travel at weekends, so Sunday afternoon blocks are more reliable than Saturday ones. Families often book a fortnightly two-hour block rather than a weekly one, with marked work exchanged in between.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Villa and apartment mix with a high proportion of students at schools across the Marina and Al Sufouh corridors. Saturday late-morning blocks work well, and the internal assessment season in Year 12 is when weekend demand here peaks sharply.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large villas, long school runs out towards Al Barsha and Sheikh Zayed Road, and families who frequently travel at weekends. A fixed Sunday slot survives better than a Saturday one, and sessions are often rescheduled in blocks around travel rather than cancelled singly.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Quieter community with fewer competing Saturday commitments, which makes it one of the easier places in Dubai to hold a 10:00 Saturday block for a full term. Two-hour paper-and-marking sessions are the standard booking here.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Family-heavy villa community where sibling schedules collide at weekends. Consecutive slots for two children on the same morning are common, which online delivery handles without the travel gap an in-home tutor would need between them.

regions.name: Tilal Al Ghaf
regions.note: Newer community with longer commutes to the established school corridors, so weekday evening sessions start late and weekend blocks carry more of the work. Holiday weeks are used heavily here for internal assessment drafting.

sections.heading: What a weekend IB session should leave behind, every single week
paragraphs: A weekend session that produces no artefact has not been measured, and an unmeasured session is indistinguishable from a pleasant conversation. Three things should exist at the end of every weekend block: a piece of the student's work with marks on it, a short written note naming what to practise before the next session, and a running list of the recurring losses that have not yet closed. All three belong to the student rather than to the tutor's records.

The running list is the part families usually skip and the part that does most work. It is not a list of weak topics; it is a list of repeated behaviours. Does not state assumptions in a mechanics question. Drops units in the final line. Writes a narrative when the command term says compare. Starts an essay before deciding what the answer is. Those are the items that recur across papers and subjects, and watching one of them disappear from the list is the most honest progress signal available to a parent.

Marks on a script need context to be readable, which is why the note should also say what the total means. A 31 out of 50 is meaningless alone; a 31 out of 50 on a paper the school's own cohort averaged in the low twenties, or against the same student's 24 four weeks earlier, is information. The table below sets out the week-by-week rhythm a weekend block should follow across a first term, and what a parent should be able to see at each point.

sections.heading: The internal assessment is where a weekend block earns its money
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated by the IB, and it is typically worth around a fifth of the subject grade. It is also the only component with no clock on it, which is precisely why students under-perform on it relative to their papers. A piece of work with no forcing function gets written in the last available week, and the criteria that reward thinking rather than output are the ones that end up thin.

Weekend blocks suit this work because reading a draft properly takes time. A tutor who skims three pages in a weekday hour can comment on expression; a tutor who has read the whole draft against each criterion before the session can say which band each section currently sits in and what specifically is missing from the one above. That is a different kind of feedback, and it is the kind that moves a mark. The student then makes every change themselves, which is both the rule and the only version that teaches anything.

The weighting table below is indicative and should be confirmed against the current subject guide, because the IB revises guides on a subject-by-subject cycle and your school's coordinator holds the version your child is assessed under. What does not change is the pattern: the criteria rewarding evaluation, reflection and personal engagement are where marks are lost, because they are the ones a student cannot write quickly the night before a deadline.

sections.heading: Sitting a timed paper properly: what two hours on a Saturday actually allows
paragraphs: Timed practice is the most under-used revision method in the Diploma because it is the only one that cannot be done badly without the student noticing. Reading notes feels productive at any speed. A paper sat against a clock produces a number, and the number is either acceptable or it is not. The weekend is the only slot in a Dubai school week where this fits: a Paper 2 plus the marking conversation is two hours minimum, and nobody should be attempting that at 19:30 on a Wednesday.

The discipline matters as much as the length. The paper is sat with the real time allowance including any reading time, with the calculator the exam allows and nothing else, in one sitting, without pausing to check a formula. Most students have never done this outside a mock, which is why mock results surprise them. The first weekend paper of a term is usually worse than the student's school marks suggest, and that gap is the single most useful piece of information the term produces.

Marking immediately afterwards is what turns the exercise into teaching. While the student still remembers why they chose a method, the tutor can ask the question that matters: what did you think that question was asking. A paper marked three days later gets a correction; a paper marked in the same block gets a diagnosis. The schedule below is the shape of a standard two-hour weekend block, and it is deliberately ordinary, because the value is in doing it twelve times rather than in designing it cleverly.

sections.heading: What grade movement is realistic in a term, and how to see it in the numbers
paragraphs: Honest answer: it depends almost entirely on what the missing marks are made of. A student losing marks to presentation, question reading and command terms can move a grade band inside a term, because those are habits and habits respond quickly to marked feedback. A student missing a year of content moves more slowly, because content has to be taught before it can be practised, and a weekly weekend block delivers perhaps thirty hours across a year against the school's two hundred.

The way to see movement is to compare like with like. Same subject, same paper type, same conditions, four to six weeks apart. Anything else is noise: a different paper, a kinder markscheme, a topic the student happened to revise. This is why the first weekend block of a term should produce a baseline score that is written down, even when it is uncomfortable, and why the week-six review exists. Without the baseline there is nothing to compare against, and the conversation defaults to whether everyone likes the tutor.

No tutor can promise a grade, and a page that offers one should be read as a warning rather than an offer. What a tutor can promise is the measurement: a baseline, a repeat under the same conditions, and an honest reading of the difference. If there is no movement by week six, the plan should change or the tutor should. Asking for a different tutor needs no explanation, and it is a far better response than waiting another term to see whether things improve on their own.
bullets: Habit losses move fastest; missing content moves slowest
Compare the same paper type under the same conditions, four to six weeks apart
Write the baseline down in week one, however uncomfortable it is

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and what happens to the weekend
paragraphs: The UAE academic year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with a winter break in December, a spring break usually around late March or early April, and shorter half-term breaks in between. Dubai private schools publish their own calendars within that frame, which means two schools can have spring break a week apart. Any weekend plan built across a term has to be laid against the school's own published dates rather than a generic UAE calendar.

Ramadan is the bigger reshaping. School days shorten, the useful study window moves to after Iftar, and weekend mornings become either the best slot in the week or an impossible one depending on the household. The two patterns that work are a late-morning weekend block for families who keep daytime hours, and a post-Iftar evening block for those who do not. Both are easier to hold if the change is booked a fortnight ahead, because the post-Iftar window is the most contested slot in the Dubai calendar.

Eid and the spring break then land immediately before the May examination series, which makes them the most valuable weeks of the year for Diploma candidates and the most commonly wasted. A student with a clear morning can sit two papers in a week with proper marking between them, which is more timed practice than a whole term of weekday hours delivers. Families who plan that fortnight in February get it; families who decide in April find the slots gone.

sections.heading: What weekend tutoring costs in Dubai, and whether the day changes the rate
paragraphs: In the online market, the day usually does not change the rate, and the length of the block does. A two-hour weekend block is billed as two hours at the same rate as one, so the question for a family is not whether weekends cost more but whether two hours once a fortnight beats one hour every week. For a student whose problem is paper technique, it generally does. For a student missing content, weekly contact matters more and the long block is better kept monthly.

The in-home market behaves differently, and this is where weekend pricing diverges. A tutor travelling across Dubai on a Saturday morning is giving up a weekend day for one or two sessions, and the published in-home bands reflect that: AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel built in, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Monthly in-home packages have been published at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

Those figures come from published 2026 rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey. They are the market's numbers, not IB Gram's price list, and they are reproduced because most pages ranking for this search publish no price at all. Set them against the KHDA confirmation in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's economic incentives package, which is the context in which most families are planning this spend.

sections.heading: When a weekend tutor is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: Three situations come up often enough to name. The first is a student who is not sleeping. A Diploma student going to bed at one in the morning is not short of teaching; they are short of recovery, and a Saturday session added to that week makes the problem slightly worse. The honest advice there is to fix the week before buying anything, and a tutor who takes the booking without saying so is selling rather than helping.

The second is a subject that is wrong rather than hard. A student who chose Chemistry Higher Level for a medicine application they no longer want, or who is sitting Mathematics Analysis and Approaches when Applications and Interpretation would serve their degree plan better, has a timetable problem. That conversation belongs with the school's Diploma coordinator, and in Year 12 there is usually still a window to change. Tutoring can hold a wrong subject together for a while, expensively.

The third is a crisis two weeks before a deadline or a paper. Sometimes a short intensive block genuinely helps: a paper format rehearsed, a markscheme habit corrected, a draft read against the criteria. Sometimes the arithmetic simply does not work, and the right answer is to say so and suggest the student spend those two weeks on the three subjects where marks are still reachable. We would rather decline a booking than take money for a plan that cannot produce anything, and the arithmetic is easy to show you on the call.

sections.heading: How weekend delivery works, and why it is online
paragraphs: Sessions run online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. On a weekend page that is worth stating early, because the weekend is exactly when the in-home model is most expensive and least reliable: a tutor crossing the emirate on a Saturday morning is making a bigger sacrifice than one driving ten minutes on a Tuesday, and the rate and the cancellation risk both reflect it.

The online format also fits what weekend work actually is. A timed paper is sat on paper and photographed or scanned, or typed, and marked on a shared screen where the student can see every annotation as it is made. An internal assessment draft is read in advance and annotated in the document. None of that is improved by the tutor being in the room, and the thing that is improved by online delivery is the choice of tutor: a Higher Level specialist in the subject rather than whoever is available locally at 09:00 on a Saturday.

Coverage is stated before anything is booked. Common Diploma subjects at both levels are matched quickly, including weekend slots; Higher Level option topics and second language A subjects take longer because the specialist pool is small. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so rather than implying a local presence. Changing tutor needs no explanation and does not restart anything already paid for.

process.title: Name the next deadline
process.description: Not the exam in May: the next thing with a date on it. An internal assessment draft due in three weeks, a mock in January, a school test on Friday. Weekend plans built against a real deadline produce evidence; plans built against a general ambition produce sessions. The school's calendar is the source.

process.title: Free 45-minute diagnostic lesson
process.description: One session, no card details taken and no obligation to continue. The tutor marks work your child has already done rather than teaching a topic, and returns three specific recurring losses in writing. That list is the baseline for everything afterwards and the thing to judge the tutor on.

process.title: Choose the block, not just the hour
process.description: Decide between a fortnightly two-hour block, a weekly hour, or a weekly hour plus one long block a month. Paper technique needs the long block; missing content needs weekly contact. Then fix the time against the Saturday activity schedule, because a slot that competes with football will not survive to week six.

process.title: Sit a full paper by week four
process.description: A baseline score under real conditions, written down, with a mark breakdown. This is the number everything later is compared against, and getting it early is worth more than getting a comfortable one. Most students score below their school marks on a first properly timed paper, and that gap is the useful finding.

process.title: Review at week six on the same task
process.description: Compare the week-one script and the week-four paper on the same question types. Either the named losses are closing or they are not. If they are not, the plan changes or the tutor changes, and asking for a different tutor needs no explanation and costs nothing already paid for.

whyPoints.title: The block is long enough to measure something
whyPoints.description: Two hours fits a timed paper, live marking and a diagnosis. A weekday hour does not, which is why weekday tutoring so often produces an impression of progress rather than a number. The weekend is the only slot in a Dubai school week where measurement is practical.

whyPoints.title: Marked work the student keeps
whyPoints.description: Every block returns a script with marks on it, a written note and a running list of recurring losses. Those artefacts belong to the student, which means a parent can read the evidence directly rather than relying on a monthly summary written by the person being paid.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment feedback by criterion
whyPoints.description: Drafts are read in full before the session and returned with a note against each published criterion naming the band and the gap. The student makes every change and writes every sentence. The school supervisor remains the official process and signs the declarations.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: AED bands on this page come from published 2026 rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, with the format each applies to. They are market figures rather than ours. Most pages ranking for this query publish no price, which leaves parents comparing quotes against nothing.

whyPoints.title: A calendar that includes Ramadan and the spring break
whyPoints.description: Weekend plans are laid against your school's own published dates, with timing changes for Ramadan booked a fortnight ahead and the pre-series fortnight planned in February rather than April. That single piece of scheduling is worth more timed practice than a whole term of contested evening hours.

whyPoints.title: We say when tutoring is the wrong answer
whyPoints.description: A sleep deficit, a wrong subject choice or a two-week crisis with no reachable marks are not tutoring problems. We will say so and decline the booking rather than sell a plan that cannot produce a change. That is a cheaper conversation than discovering it in week five.

faqs.question: Why book a weekend IB session instead of a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Because of what fits. A Dubai school bus returns between about 15:15 and 16:30, homework runs across six subjects and activities fill two or three evenings, so a weekday session is realistically one hour between 18:00 and 20:00. That hour cannot contain a two-hour Paper 2 sat under timed conditions plus the marking conversation afterwards. A Saturday morning block can. If your child's problem is paper technique rather than missing content, the weekend is where the useful work actually fits.

faqs.question: Which days count as the weekend for Dubai tutoring?
faqs.answer: Saturday and Sunday. The UAE moved to a Monday-to-Friday working week with a half-day Friday in January 2022, and Dubai private schools run Monday to Friday, so the protected days for most families are Saturday and Sunday. Friday remains a working morning for many parents and carries midday prayers, which is why Friday sessions are less commonly requested than Saturday ones. Saturday mornings from 08:30 to 11:00 are the most contested slots in the week and the ones worth fixing early in the term.

faqs.question: What should my child bring to a weekend session?
faqs.answer: Two things for the first session: the last two pieces of work the school marked, and the next deadline with its date. For later sessions, the practice set from the previous week and anything the school has returned since. Bringing marked work matters more than bringing a topic request, because the diagnosis lives in the script. A session that starts with what shall we do today has already lost twenty minutes of a block you are paying for.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether weekend tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: Compare like with like. The same paper type, under the same timed conditions, four to six weeks apart, with both scores written down. If the first paper is sat in week four and the comparison in week eight, the difference is readable. Alongside that, watch the list of recurring losses: items should leave it. What is not evidence is a cheerful session report, a student who likes the tutor, or a school grade that moved for reasons nobody has isolated.

faqs.question: Can a two-hour block really hold a teenager's attention?
faqs.answer: A two-hour block is not two hours of teaching. In the standard shape it is five minutes of set-up, 60 to 75 minutes of the student working alone under exam conditions, 20 to 25 minutes of live marking and ten to fifteen of diagnosis. The attention demand is the same as the exam the student will sit, which is the point: a student who cannot concentrate for 75 minutes on a Saturday morning will not manage it in the examination hall either, and discovering that in October is useful.

faqs.question: How much of the internal assessment can a tutor be involved in?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the content the investigation needs, explain what each published criterion asks for, read a draft in full and return written notes naming which band each section currently sits in. A tutor cannot supply sentences, insert sources, or rework a section into its final state. Your child makes every change and writes every word. The school-appointed supervisor remains the official process and signs the declarations. Any provider offering to produce the work itself is creating a malpractice risk that falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Do weekend sessions cost more than weekday ones in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In the online market, generally not: published 2026 rates put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour and a specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, regardless of the day. In-home sessions are where the weekend premium shows, because a tutor giving up a Saturday to cross the emirate commands more, and published in-home bands run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. Monthly published figures: AED 799 for eight online sessions, AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

faqs.question: Is a fortnightly two-hour block better than a weekly hour?
faqs.answer: For paper technique, usually yes, because the measurement only fits in the long block. For missing content, no: content needs frequent contact and small steps, and a fortnight is long enough for a half-learned method to decay. Many Dubai families settle on a hybrid, with a weekly hour for content and one long block a month as the measurement point. The decision should follow the diagnostic rather than the diary, and it is worth revisiting at the week-six review.

faqs.question: What happens to weekend sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: They move, and it is worth booking the change a fortnight in advance. The two patterns that work are a late-morning weekend block for households keeping daytime hours and a post-Iftar evening block for those that do not. School days shorten, so weekday afternoons are quieter and some families temporarily move the long block to a weekday. Timed-paper work is harder during fasting hours, so Ramadan is usually better spent on internal assessment drafting and content consolidation than on full papers.

faqs.question: Is the spring break worth booking tutoring in?
faqs.answer: It is the highest-value fortnight of the Diploma year, and it is the one most often wasted. A student with clear mornings can sit two full papers in a week with proper marking between them, which is more timed practice than a whole term of contested evening hours delivers. It also sits immediately before the May series, so what is practised is still fresh. Slots fill from about February, so the families who get that fortnight are the ones who booked it before the January mocks.

faqs.question: Can one weekend tutor cover two of my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being careful about. A Mathematics and Physics pairing is common and works well because the overlap is real. A Chemistry and English pairing is not a specialism, it is a generalist, and Diploma marks are lost in subject-specific technique that a generalist cannot diagnose. Two shorter blocks with two specialists usually beats one long block with someone covering both. Where you have two subjects and one weekend morning, consecutive slots with different tutors are straightforward online.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 13 with mocks done. Is a weekend block still worth starting?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the plan narrows. After mocks there is no case for content teaching except where a mock exposed a specific untaught topic. The weekend block becomes paper work only: sit, mark, diagnose, repeat, with the subject list cut to the two or three where marks are most reachable. Spreading a final term of tutoring across five subjects is how families spend a lot and move nothing. The honest conversation in session one is about which subjects to drop from the plan.

faqs.question: What if there is no movement after six weeks?
faqs.answer: Then the plan changes or the tutor does. Six weeks of marked evidence is enough to tell whether the named losses are closing, and if they are not, something in the diagnosis was wrong: the wrong losses identified, content gaps mistaken for habit gaps, or a tutor and student who are not working. Asking for a different tutor needs no explanation and does not restart anything you have already paid for. Waiting another term to see is the expensive option.

faqs.question: Are weekend slots actually available, or is the calendar already full?
faqs.answer: Saturday mornings between 08:30 and 11:00 are the most contested slots in the Dubai week and they go first, particularly in January and in the final term. Sunday afternoons are easier. For common Diploma subjects a weekend slot is usually available within a few days; for Higher Level option topics and second language A subjects it takes longer, because the specialist pool is small before any timing constraint is applied. Where the tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

faqs.question: Where do the lessons take place?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. That matters most at weekends, because the in-home model is at its most expensive and least reliable on a Saturday morning. Online delivery means the tutor is chosen for being a Higher Level specialist in the subject rather than for being available locally at 09:00.

dubai/weekend-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Book the diagnostic, then ask for the baseline paper
dubai/weekend-ib-tutor.closingBody: Start with the free 45-minute diagnostic, which takes no card details and carries no obligation: the tutor marks work your child has already done and returns three specific recurring losses in writing. Then fix a weekend block and ask for a full timed paper by week four, with the score written down. Those two artefacts, the loss list and the baseline, are what every later session gets measured against. If the losses are not closing by week six, say so and change the plan or the tutor. That is the whole method, and it is deliberately dull.

dubai/weekend-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE into Gulf Standard Time weekends. A weekend tutor is picked for a specific skill: marking a full paper accurately against the current markscheme and writing feedback a student can use without the tutor present.

intro.heading: Count the Saturdays first, then decide what they are for
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic rather than the ambition. Between the first week of September in Year 11 and the start of the summer series, a Dubai family has somewhere around thirty usable Saturdays once the winter break, the January mock fortnight, the spring break and travel are taken out. A student sitting nine or ten IGCSE subjects has, across that whole period, perhaps three Saturdays per subject if the slot is shared evenly. Shared evenly, it achieves nothing in any of them.

So the first decision is not which tutor, it is which two subjects. The criterion is not which subject the student finds hardest or which teacher they dislike. It is where the reachable marks are: the subject sitting one grade below target because of a habit rather than a knowledge gap, the subject where a sixth-form place depends on a 6 rather than a 5, the subject whose paper format has never been practised under a clock. Those are retrievable. A subject three grades adrift in November usually is not, and saying so early is kinder than discovering it in June.

The second decision is what the slot produces. A weekend block is long enough to sit a full paper, mark it against the published markscheme and diagnose what went wrong, which is the one thing a weekday hour between 18:00 and 20:00 cannot hold. That makes the weekend the only reliable measurement point in a Dubai school week, and measurement is the whole argument of this page. A school report gives you a grade; a marked paper gives you the question numbers.

The third thing to settle is the board, because it decides what the papers even look like. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award an International GCSE and Dubai schools use both, sometimes in different departments of the same school. Cambridge Mathematics now sets non-calculator papers in both tiers, while Pearson Mathematics A allows a calculator in both of its papers. Preparing for the wrong one is a term wasted, and the only reliable identifier is the syllabus code on the school's entry.

What follows is the detail: how to triage nine subjects down to two, what command words actually require, how to read a marked script against a school report, how to use the fortnight either side of the January mocks, the November retake route with its published dates, and what a Year 11 of weekend blocks costs at current Dubai market rates. Figures carry their source and their date, because a rate or a deadline without either cannot be planned around. Nothing here depends on a figure we cannot attribute, and where a board has not published something, the page says so instead of estimating it.
bullets: Around thirty usable Saturdays in Year 11; two subjects is the honest capacity

dubai/weekend-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Weekend blocks get booked across four stages of the British track in Dubai, and the work is different in each. These are the stages and what a Saturday morning is actually spent on.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, first year
programmes.description: Content delivery year, usually at a pace that assumes everything lands first time. Weekend work in Year 10 is cheap in the sense that it is preventative: securing algebraic manipulation, the mole concept and written structure while there is still a year to use them. Syllabus codes identify the course exactly, such as 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Year 10 tier decision is often already made, sometimes from Checkpoint data at the end of Year 9. Families whose target needs an Extended entry are far better off using Year 10 weekends to build the evidence a department would need to move a set than appealing the decision later, because the set determines which papers the student is taught from all year.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exam year
programmes.description: The year the papers arrive. Weekend blocks shift from content to timed papers and markscheme work, usually from January onwards. Pearson codes are 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language A; Cambridge uses four-digit codes. The paper set differs between the boards even where the subject name matches.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai school mock windows cluster in January but fall on different weeks school by school, and coursework deadlines move independently. The weekend plan is therefore built from your school's calendar rather than a generic one. Ask the exams officer for three dates in writing: the entry deadline, the mock window and the first paper of the series.

programmes.name: The November series and the retake route
programmes.description: Both boards run a November series alongside the summer one, which turns a disappointing August result into a question with options rather than a verdict. Entries are made through a school or an exam centre that accepts private candidates, and the decision has to be taken early because entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's November 2026 final written timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable each. A Dubai family planning a retake should get both the series dates and the zone from the centre, in writing.

programmes.name: IGCSE into A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade is a gate rather than a summary: A Level entry in a subject normally requires a 6, 7 or A in the same or a related subject, and Diploma Higher Level choices are made on the same evidence. That is why one grade in one subject sometimes matters more than the overall profile, and why triage should follow the post-16 plan.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is unusual in offering both routes widely, often inside the same school, so Year 11 students face a genuine choice rather than a default. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E.

dubai/weekend-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often given the weekend slot in Dubai, with what a full-paper block does for each. The question in every case is whether the lost marks are habit or content, because the two need different plans.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge · 4MA1 Pearson)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject where a full paper under a clock is most diagnostic, because method marks only become visible in a complete script. Cambridge now examines without a calculator in part of the paper set; Pearson Mathematics A does not. A student fluent with a calculator and shaky without one has a very specific, very fixable problem.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge · 4PH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Circuit reasoning and waves are the standing weaknesses, and both reward repeated short practice rather than long explanation. A weekend block is where the practical-skills questions get done properly: variables, repeatability, scale reading, lines of best fit and gradients with units.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge · 4CH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Moles, ionic equations and qualitative analysis. The recurring avoidable losses are units, significant figures and half-equations written unbalanced. Observation questions reward memorised specifics, a precipitate colour or a gas test result, which a Saturday block can drill to automaticity in a way a tired Tuesday hour cannot.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge · 4BI1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Volume plus strict terminology, which makes it the subject where marking matters most. Markschemes written for one word will not accept a near-synonym, so the student needs to see their own near-misses marked as wrong once or twice before the habit changes.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 Cambridge · 4EA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Marks follow form and register rather than vocabulary. Directed writing in the wrong form caps low regardless of quality, and reading questions reward precise selection from the passage. A full paper plus marking is the only way to show a student that their best writing scored in the middle band.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Large Dubai cohort, frequently under-prepared because fluency is mistaken for readiness. The marks sit in exercise technique: note-making under the given headings, summary inside the word limit, and a speaking component assessed against published criteria rather than on confidence.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive with little scaffolding, and the step is in abstraction rather than difficulty. A fortnightly weekend block through Year 11 is the usual shape, because the content needs time to settle between sessions.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Both reward application to the stimulus on the paper and give almost nothing for generic theory. Data-response questions are failed at the reading stage rather than the writing stage, which only becomes visible when a whole paper is marked and the pattern of lost marks lines up with the question type.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode written to the published convention and trace tables completed row by row, both of which are scoring conventions rather than understanding. Students who can program well in a real language still lose marks here, and a weekend block fixes it faster than any amount of coding practice.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Dubai students often sit Arabic A while also taking the school's mandatory Arabic provision, with different expectations in each. Dialect speakers read fluently and write below their level in Standard Arabic, which is a written-register problem and responds well to marked weekend practice.

dubai/weekend-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Weekend availability in Dubai is decided by the Saturday diary rather than by distance. These are the communities where weekend IGCSE blocks are most requested, and the pattern that holds in each.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: Established family community with a short run to the Al Barsha and Ranches school corridors. Saturday 09:00 and 10:00 blocks hold well through the autumn term, and demand here spikes sharply in the three weeks before the January mocks.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Villa community with schools within a few minutes, so weekday evenings are workable and the weekend block is usually reserved for full papers rather than content. Two-subject households typically take one long Saturday block and one weekday hour.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Quieter community with fewer competing Saturday commitments, which makes a fixed morning block easier to keep for a whole term. Families here often start weekend work in Year 10 rather than Year 11, which is the cheaper version of the same plan.

regions.name: The Views and The Greens

sections.heading: Counting the Saturdays: what a Year 11 weekend budget actually looks like
paragraphs: Treat the weekend as a budget with a fixed balance. From the start of September to the beginning of the summer series there are around thirty-five Saturdays in a Dubai academic year, and realistically about thirty are usable once the winter break, travel, family commitments and the odd illness are subtracted. That is the total. Everything a family decides about weekend tutoring is a decision about how to divide thirty blocks, and most families make that decision implicitly by booking whatever is available.

Dividing thirty blocks across nine subjects gives each one three sessions in a year, which is below the threshold at which anything changes. Dividing them across two subjects gives fifteen each, which is enough to sit six or seven full papers per subject with marking, and that is enough to move a grade where the gap is technique. The arithmetic is the argument. It is also why the most valuable conversation in a first session is often about which subjects to leave out.

The budget is not evenly distributed through the year either. September to November is the only period with slack in it, January is consumed by mocks, and the final six weeks are fully committed. The table below sets out the phases as they actually fall in Dubai, with what each one is for. Families who plan the spring-break fortnight in February get it; the ones who decide in April find those slots taken, which is the single most common scheduling regret in this market.

sections.heading: Choosing the two subjects: triage by reachable marks
paragraphs: The instinct is to spend the slot on the subject with the lowest grade. That is usually wrong. A subject three grades below target in November is rarely retrievable with one fortnightly block, because the deficit is content and content takes classroom hours the weekend does not have. A subject one grade below target because the student writes narrative where the command word says explain is retrievable in six weeks, because that is a habit and habits respond fast to marked feedback.

The second filter is consequence. One grade in one subject sometimes matters far more than the overall profile: a 6 rather than a 5 in Mathematics may be the condition on a sixth-form place, and five subjects at grade E or 3 or above, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, is the Ministry of Education's published British-track count. A subject that is comfortably at target and a subject that is irrelevant to the post-16 plan should both lose the argument for the slot, however much the student likes or dislikes them.

The third filter is evidence quality. Triage needs marked papers, not school reports, which is why the diagnostic block comes before the plan rather than after it. Reports compress a term into one letter and hide where the marks went. A marked past paper with a question-by-question breakdown tells you whether the student is losing marks in the first ten minutes, on one topic, or on one question type across the whole paper, and those three findings point to three different plans.

sections.heading: What a marked script tells you that a school report cannot
paragraphs: A school report is a compression. One letter per subject, a comment written for thirty families, and a predicted grade that carries institutional caution in both directions. It is useful for noticing that something is wrong and almost useless for deciding what to do about it. Dubai parents often arrive at tutoring with three terms of reports and no idea which question types their child cannot answer, which is not a criticism of the school; reports are not built for that job.

A marked past paper is built for exactly that job. It produces a total, a breakdown by question, and a pattern: marks lost in the first fifteen minutes suggests a start-of-paper panic; marks lost on one topic across both papers suggests a content gap; marks lost on every six-mark question regardless of topic suggests the student does not know what an extended answer requires. Those three patterns look identical in a report and need completely different responses.

This is why the first weekend block should produce a baseline score, written down, even when it is lower than the school's predictions. Most students score below their report grade on a first properly timed paper, because the school's assessments are usually shorter, more recently taught and more generously conditioned. That gap is not bad news; it is the measurement everything else is compared against. Without it, the conversation at week six is about whether everyone likes the tutor. Ask for the total and the breakdown in writing, and keep both; by March you will have four of them and the trend will be unarguable in either direction.

sections.heading: Command words: the cheapest marks in the IGCSE paper set
paragraphs: Both boards publish the command words used in their question papers, and both mark against a fixed expectation for each one. State wants a fact with no reasoning. Describe wants what happens without why. Explain wants the because. Suggest wants a plausible answer the student has not been taught. Compare wants both items in the same sentence. Evaluate wants a judgement with support on both sides. Calculate wants working and units.

Students lose marks here in a very specific way: they answer the question they expected rather than the one printed. A six-mark explain question answered with an excellent description scores in the lowest band. The content was right, the knowledge was there, and the marks went anyway. This is the largest single pool of recoverable marks in most IGCSE papers and it is almost entirely absent from the way revision is usually done, because revision guides organise content by topic rather than by question type.

Fixing it is mechanical and fast. The student takes a marked paper, lists every question by command word, and works through five of the same command word in a row across different topics. After three weekend blocks the pattern of answers changes, which shows up as a jump on the next full paper without any new content being learned. Families frequently mistake this for a sudden improvement in understanding; it is a sudden improvement in reading. It also transfers across subjects, which is why one block spent on command words in Biology often shows up in the next Geography paper as well.

sections.heading: The January mock fortnight, and the two weekends either side of it
paragraphs: Dubai schools cluster their Year 11 mocks in January, and the fortnight itself is the wrong time to buy tutoring. The student is sitting papers, the evenings are consumed by cramming for tomorrow's subject, and nothing a tutor adds in that week survives contact with the timetable. The valuable weekends are the one before and, more importantly, the two after, which is the opposite of how most families book.

The weekend before is for format rather than content. One paper per chosen subject, sat under the real conditions, so the student has done it once before the room does it to them. Nothing new is taught. The aim is that the mock produces a score consistent with the evidence rather than a shock, because a shock in January tends to produce three weeks of panic revision that is poorly aimed and exhausting.

The weekends after are where the mock pays for itself. The student brings the marked mock scripts, and the block is spent reading them as data: which questions, which command words, how many marks were lost to timing, and whether the pattern matches the loss list from the autumn. That exercise usually rewrites the plan for the spring term, and it frequently narrows the subject list, because mock evidence makes the triage argument far better than any prediction does. A student who can see that nine marks went to timing in one paper and twelve to command words in another will argue for the plan themselves, which is worth more than being told.

sections.heading: Saturday mathematics: the non-calculator paper and the board difference
paragraphs: Mathematics gets the weekend slot more often than any other subject in Dubai, and the reason is worth naming: it is the subject where a full paper is most diagnostic, because method marks only exist in a complete script. A student can look competent across a textbook exercise and lose a third of a paper to unshown working, misread questions and arithmetic without a calculator. None of that is visible in homework.

The board difference matters here more than anywhere else in the specification. Cambridge Mathematics now sets non-calculator assessment within its paper set across both tiers, while Pearson Mathematics A allows a calculator in both of its papers. A student who has been practising with a calculator in hand all year and then meets a non-calculator paper has a mechanical problem, not a mathematical one, and the fix is weeks of short arithmetic and manipulation practice rather than more topics. Confirm which paper set applies with the school's exams officer rather than assuming.

The other weekend job in Mathematics is the tier. In a tiered entry the grade ceiling is set by the papers sat, not by the marking, so a Core or Foundation entry caps the outcome regardless of effort. If the post-16 plan needs a 6 or better and the entry is capped below it, the useful action is a conversation with the department about what evidence would move the set, and by when. Tutoring can raise a grade inside a tier and build the content the next stage needs; it cannot lift a ceiling.

sections.heading: The November retake route, with the dates in it
paragraphs: An August result is a decision point rather than a verdict, and the November series is the thing that makes it one. Both boards run a November series in addition to the summer one, so a student who missed a sixth-form condition by one grade can sit the subject again within a term rather than waiting a year. Very few pages in this market mention it at all, which is why families often discover the option after the entry deadline has passed.

The published dates show why early is everything. Pearson's November 2026 final written timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs June and November series and publishes a separate timetable for each of its six administrative zones, warning that the correct version must be used because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss a paper after the wrong zone timetable was used. For its March 2027 series, final entries fell on 27 November 2026 for papers sat from 3 February 2027.

The practical sequence for a Dubai family is short. In the week results arrive, ask the school whether it will enter retake candidates and by what date, and if it will not, find an exam centre that accepts private candidates. Get the series, the zone and the entry deadline in writing. Then decide whether the retake is worth it: one subject with a near miss and a clear reason usually is, three subjects after a difficult year usually are not, and a whole-cohort retake plan is almost never the right answer.

sections.heading: What a Year 11 of weekend blocks costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Published market rates in 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 to 150, and in-home visits in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 with travel built into the rate. Those bands come from published 2026 rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey; they are the market's figures rather than IB Gram's price list, and they are reproduced here because most pages ranking for this search publish nothing at all.

The useful question is not the hourly rate but the annual shape. Two subjects on alternating weekends through Year 11 is around thirty hours of tutoring. The same money spread across five subjects is six hours each, which changes nothing in any of them, and families regularly spend more in total that way while getting less. The table below models the year by phase so the commitment can be seen before it is made rather than discovered in March.

One piece of context worth holding alongside the numbers: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For most families the tutoring decision therefore sits against a flat school-fee bill rather than a rising one, which makes it a genuine choice about where a fixed education budget does the most work.

process.title: Ask the exams officer for three dates and the codes
process.description: Board and syllabus code per subject, the tier where one applies, the entry deadline, the mock window and the first paper of the series. Five lines in an email. Everything in a weekend plan hangs off those, and assuming them is how a term gets spent on the wrong paper format.

process.title: Free 45-minute diagnostic block
process.description: One session, no card details taken, no obligation to continue. The tutor marks a past-paper answer or a recent script against the markscheme for the correct code and returns a written loss list naming the question types, not the topics. That list is the baseline and the thing to judge the tutor on.

process.title: Triage down to two subjects
process.description: Use the loss lists and the post-16 plan rather than the lowest grade. Reachable marks first, consequential grades second, and anything at target or irrelevant to the plan left out. Expect this conversation to feel uncomfortable; a plan covering five subjects with one slot is the comfortable version and it does not work.

process.title: Sit a full paper per subject by November
process.description: Baseline scores under real conditions, with totals written down and breakdowns by question type. Most students score below their report grade here, and that gap is the useful finding rather than a problem. It is also the number the January mock gets compared against.

process.title: Rewrite the plan on the mock evidence
process.description: In the two weekends after the mocks, read the marked scripts as data: which questions, which command words, how many marks went to timing. That almost always narrows the subject list and reorders the spring term, and it is a far better triage tool than any prediction.

whyPoints.title: The weekend budget is counted, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Around thirty usable Saturdays in Year 11, which is fifteen blocks each for two subjects or three each for nine. Stating the arithmetic before the plan is made is what stops a family spending more and getting less, and it is the conversation this market usually avoids.

whyPoints.title: Triage on reachable marks
whyPoints.description: The subject with the lowest grade is often the worst use of the slot. One grade below target on a habit gap moves in six weeks; three grades below on a content gap does not. We say which is which after marking a paper rather than guessing from a report.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the board and the paper set
whyPoints.description: Cambridge Mathematics now examines without a calculator in part of its paper set; Pearson Mathematics A does not. The tutor is matched to the syllabus code the school entered, so a term is not spent rehearsing the wrong paper format.

whyPoints.title: Command-word practice as a mark source
whyPoints.description: The largest pool of recoverable marks in most IGCSE papers sits in answering the printed command word rather than the expected one. It is mechanical to fix, it shows up on the next full paper, and almost no revision plan addresses it because guides are organised by topic.

whyPoints.title: The November route stated with its dates
whyPoints.description: Pearson's November 2026 written timetable runs to 19 November 2026 and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Knowing the retake exists before the entry deadline is the difference between a decision and a regret, and most pages in this market never mention it.
