faqs.question: How many subjects can one weekend slot realistically cover?
faqs.answer: Two, and one is often better. A Year 11 in Dubai has roughly thirty usable Saturdays between September and the summer series. Split across two subjects that is fifteen blocks each, enough for six or seven marked full papers per subject. Split across five subjects it is six blocks each, which is below the point at which anything measurable changes. Families who spread the slot thinly usually spend more across the year and move less, which is why the first session should include a triage conversation rather than a timetable.

faqs.question: Which subject should get the weekend block?
faqs.answer: Not automatically the weakest one. Prioritise where the marks are reachable: a subject one grade below target because the student answers the wrong command word is retrievable in about six weeks, while a subject three grades adrift in November is usually a content deficit that one fortnightly block cannot close. Then weigh consequence: a 6 rather than a 5 in Mathematics may be the condition on a sixth-form place. A subject already at target, or irrelevant to the post-16 plan, should lose the argument however strongly your child feels about it.

faqs.question: Why sit a full past paper rather than work through topics?
faqs.answer: Because a full paper produces a pattern and topic work does not. Marks lost in the first fifteen minutes point to a start-of-paper problem. Marks lost on one topic across both papers point to a content gap. Marks lost on every six-mark question regardless of topic point to a student who does not know what an extended answer requires. Those three findings look identical in a school report and need three completely different plans, so the paper comes before the plan.

faqs.question: My child's report says grade 6 but the first past paper scored a 4. Why?
faqs.answer: Because school assessments are usually shorter, more recently taught and more generously conditioned than a full past paper sat cold. Most students score below their report grade on a first properly timed paper, and the gap is normal rather than alarming. What matters is that the number is written down, because it becomes the baseline the January mock and the spring papers are compared against. A plan without a baseline cannot be evaluated, and the discussion at week six defaults to whether everyone likes the tutor.

faqs.question: What are command words and why do they cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: They are the instruction verbs both boards publish and mark against: state, describe, explain, suggest, compare, calculate, evaluate. Each sets a fixed expectation. A six-mark explain question answered with an excellent description scores in the lowest band, because the content was right and the instruction was not followed. This is the largest pool of recoverable marks in most IGCSE papers and the one most revision misses, since revision guides are organised by topic rather than by question type. Fixing it takes about three focused blocks.

faqs.question: Should we book tutoring during the January mock weeks?
faqs.answer: No. During the mock fortnight the student is sitting papers and cramming for tomorrow's subject, and nothing added in that week survives the timetable. Book the weekend before for one paper per chosen subject under real conditions, with nothing new taught, so the mock produces a consistent score rather than a shock. Then book the two weekends after, which is where the mock pays for itself: the marked scripts get read as data and the spring plan gets rewritten on real evidence.

faqs.question: Does the exam board change how we should prepare for Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the subject where it matters most. Cambridge Mathematics now sets non-calculator assessment within its paper set across both tiers, while Pearson Mathematics A allows a calculator in both papers. A student who has practised all year with a calculator and then meets a non-calculator paper has a mechanical problem rather than a mathematical one, and the fix is weeks of short arithmetic and manipulation work. Confirm the paper set with the school's exams officer rather than assuming from the subject name.

faqs.question: Can my child retake an IGCSE in November in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Both boards run a November series alongside the summer one, with entries made through a school or an exam centre that accepts private candidates. Pearson's November 2026 final written timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Ask the school in the week results arrive whether it will enter retake candidates and by what date. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, so the decision is made early or not at all.

faqs.question: Is a November retake worth doing?
faqs.answer: One subject with a near miss and an identifiable cause, usually yes, particularly where a sixth-form offer turns on it. Three subjects after a difficult year, usually not: the same weeks spread across three retakes tends to produce three more near misses. A whole-cohort retake plan is almost never the right answer. The honest test is whether you can name, in one sentence, what went wrong and what will be different this time. If you cannot, the retake is a hope rather than a plan.

faqs.question: What does a year of weekend IGCSE tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At published 2026 rates, two subjects on alternating fortnightly blocks across Year 11 is around thirty hours, which at AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online tutor comes to roughly AED 4,500 to 9,000 for the year. A specialist at AED 200 to 450 an hour costs more per hour and is usually reserved for the final two terms. In-home equivalents run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. Those are market bands from published rate cards and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, not our price list.

faqs.question: Can the tutor mark my child's papers to the real markschemes?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the core of the block. The student sits the paper under timed conditions, the tutor marks it against the published markscheme for the correct syllabus code, and the session covers the marks that were available rather than the topic in general. Official papers, markschemes and grade-boundary tables are referenced on the board's own site and worked through there; they are not redistributed as downloads, because reproducing board material is a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, worse.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write or finish my child's coursework?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so should be read as a warning about the rest of that provider's page. A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain what the published criteria ask for and question whether a draft answers the task. The student makes every change and writes every sentence. The school remains the official process and signs any declaration of authenticity the board requires. The consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the candidate, not on the person who was paid.

faqs.question: Do weekend slots run through Ramadan and the spring break?
faqs.answer: Yes, with timings changed. During Ramadan the useful window moves to late morning or after Iftar, and the shift is easier to hold if it is booked a fortnight ahead because the post-Iftar slot is the most contested in the Dubai calendar. The spring break is the highest-value fortnight of the year: with clear mornings a student can sit two full papers a week with proper marking between them, which is more timed practice than a whole term of contested evening hours delivers.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same house take consecutive weekend blocks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery is what makes it practical. Two blocks back to back cost two blocks, with no second travel charge and no dead half hour while someone drives across the emirate. Where the subjects differ, two tutors can be booked in sequence in the same morning. Each child gets a separate marked script and a separate loss list, which matters because siblings in Years 10 and 11 are usually at different points of the same specification.

faqs.question: Where do weekend lessons actually happen?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. The weekend is where that distinction matters most, because an in-home tutor giving up a Saturday morning is both the most expensive and the least reliable option in the market. Online means the tutor is chosen for knowing your child's syllabus code rather than for living nearby.

dubai/weekend-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Count the Saturdays, then pick two subjects
dubai/weekend-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Email the exams officer for the codes, the tier, the entry deadline and the mock window. Count the Saturdays left on your school's calendar. Then take the free 45-minute diagnostic block, which takes no card details and carries no obligation: the tutor marks a real paper to the right markscheme and returns a loss list by question type. With that list and the Saturday count in front of you, the triage decision usually makes itself, and it is almost always a shorter subject list than the one you started with.

intro.heading: The system a Pearson Edexcel entry has to pass through in the UAE
paragraphs: An Edexcel IGCSE home tutor in the UAE is a tutor who teaches the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specification, one student at a time, in the hours a UAE school day leaves free. IB Gram delivers that as one-to-one tuition over live video rather than by sending anyone to a villa or an apartment; home visits are a service we run in India only. The reason for keeping it on screen is not cost. It is that a Pearson code is narrow. A tutor who has taught 4PH1 Paper 1 for six series is not interchangeable with a tutor who has taught Cambridge 0625, and in a country where the nearest specialist may be two emirates away, the screen is what makes the match possible at all.

The board matters more than most families are told. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE qualifications are graded 9 to 1, sat in a May or June series and again in a November series, and built from papers whose codes begin with a 4: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics is 4PH1, Chemistry is 4CH1, Biology is 4BI1, English Language A is 4EA1. Those codes are printed on the statement of entry the school issues. A parent who knows the code can tell a tutor exactly what to prepare. A parent who only knows the word IGCSE is relying on a guess, and across two years of teaching, a wrong guess is expensive.

The second thing shaping an Edexcel plan here is not the board at all. It is which authority holds your child's school file. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah those bodies approve curricula, courses and assessment methods as well as fees, so the regulator is not only an inspector.

Two federal rules then sit on top of the Pearson timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, so an Edexcel child is carrying those alongside nine or ten subject entries. And at the far end, the Ministry of Education's equivalency route for the British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competitor page ranking for this query tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects. The Ministry's own July 2026 clarification, as reported by Gulf Today, says five.

What IB Gram does inside that system is narrow and worth stating plainly. We teach, we review the student's own work and we give feedback on it. We do not write an Edexcel coursework folder, we do not supply Pearson mark schemes or past papers as downloads, and we hold no approval, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or Pearson, because no such thing exists for a tutoring platform. What we can do is name the code, name the permit position, teach on your time zone, and tell you honestly when no specialist is free for the subject and tier you need.

edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: A Pearson Edexcel plan rarely starts and ends in Year 11. UAE families who stay on the British track move through four stages, and each one has a different relationship with the emirate regulator and with the Ministry's equivalency file. The notes below describe what each stage is and what it means specifically for a child schooled in the Emirates.

programmes.name: Pearson International Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before the International GCSE course begins. Schools use this stage to set the maths route, decide who will be entered for separate sciences rather than a double award, and build the written English that Paper 1 of 4EA1 later rewards. No external grade is reported to a university, which is exactly why the stage is quietly decisive: the tier a child is placed in for Year 10 is usually decided on Year 9 evidence.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates this stage is also where the mandatory UAE subjects become real work. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. A Year 8 child is therefore carrying an Arabic stream, an Islamic Education stream and a social studies stream on top of the British curriculum. Families who leave Arabic until Year 10 usually find it competing with 4MA1 revision.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9-1)
programmes.description: The two-year course that ends in the Pearson papers. Most UAE schools enter eight to ten subjects, built from a compulsory core of maths, English and science plus options. Grades are reported on the 9 to 1 scale rather than A* to G. Some subjects are tiered, with a Foundation entry carrying a lower grade ceiling than a Higher one, and the tier is fixed by the entry the school submits rather than by anything the student does in the exam hall.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where an Edexcel IGCSE home tutor in the UAE is usually hired, and where the regulator becomes visible to parents. Your school's inspection report names its licensed curriculum and its attainment judgements subject by subject, and it is published by KHDA, ADEK or SPEA depending on the emirate. Entries are made by the school as an examination centre registered with Pearson, not by the family, so the practical move at this stage is a conversation with the exams officer rather than with the board.

programmes.name: Pearson International AS Level
programmes.description: The first half of the International A Level, taken as a qualification in its own right or as a staging post. Subject choice narrows to three or four, and the gap between a grade 7 at International GCSE and an AS grade A is wider than most students expect, because the command verbs change: describe and explain give way to analyse, evaluate and derive. The step is steepest in maths and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: The UAE connection here is the equivalency file. The Ministry's British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, on top of the five IGCSE subjects. A family planning a federal university application should know which of those two shapes their child's timetable actually produces, and should confirm the current requirement on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on any tutoring page, including this one.

programmes.name: Pearson International A Level
programmes.description: The full two-year A Level, assessed in units. Students who struggled with the jump from International GCSE often did so because nobody rebuilt the foundations the new papers assume: algebraic fluency for the maths and physics routes, quantitative chemistry for 4CH1 successors, and the discipline of writing to a mark allocation rather than to a word count.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit these in the same May or June and November windows as the International GCSE papers, which means a household with a Year 11 and a Year 13 can face two sets of entry deadlines, two sets of results dates and one very crowded April. Planning tuition hours around that overlap is a scheduling problem, not an academic one, and it is easier to solve when both students are taught over video on the same evening grid.

edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Pearson codes are the useful unit here, because two subjects with the same name can be different qualifications. The list below gives the codes UAE schools most often enter, what each specification actually rewards, and where marks go missing. Confirm every code against your child's statement of entry before booking hours against it.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two written papers of equal weight, calculator permitted on both. The Higher tier opens the top of the grade scale; a Foundation entry caps it. Marks leave in the same three places every series: algebraic manipulation done in the head, geometry questions where no diagram is annotated, and multi-step problems where the method mark is lost because no working is written down.

subjects.name: Mathematics B (4MB1)
subjects.description: A different specification from Mathematics A, not a tier of it. It leans harder on pure technique and is entered by a smaller set of UAE schools, often those pointing students at International A Level Mathematics. A tutor prepared on 4MA1 past papers is not automatically prepared on this. Ask which of the two is on the entry before the first session.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside Mathematics A by students heading for engineering or economics routes. It covers material most IGCSE students never meet, including calculus and series, and it is where a strong mathematician in a UAE school finally gets stretched. The common failure is not difficulty but pace: schools often timetable it in fewer lessons than the content needs.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, with Paper 1 carrying the larger share of the marks. The practical skills are assessed in writing rather than in a lab, which makes them teachable over video: students lose marks on variable control, on reading a graph gradient as a physical quantity, and on unit conversion inside a multi-step calculation. Confirm current durations and weightings on the live specification.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: The specification that most often brings a UAE family to a tutor, because quantitative chemistry is unforgiving. Moles, concentration and gas-volume calculations carry several marks each and are routinely lost to a rounding error or a missed mole ratio. Organic mechanisms and the tests for ions are memory work that a weekly recall routine fixes faster than any amount of re-teaching.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Deceptive, because the content reads as readable prose and the marks are allocated against precise terminology. A student who writes that a substance moves through the membrane when the mark scheme wants diffusion down a concentration gradient gets nothing. Tutoring work here is mostly command-term discipline and the practical-skills questions on enzymes, osmosis and transpiration.

subjects.name: Science (Double Award) (4SD0)
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics condensed into a two-grade award rather than three separate entries. UAE schools use it to keep the option block open, and it suits students whose strength is elsewhere. It compresses content rather than simplifying it, so the tutoring problem is coverage and triage: deciding which topics are worth the remaining weeks.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with an optional coursework route
subjects.description: Non-fiction reading and transactional writing on one paper, literary texts and imaginative writing on the other, with a coursework alternative available in place of the second written paper. The reading questions are where UAE students lose most: they summarise the passage instead of analysing the writer's method, and they ignore the mark allocation that tells them how many points to make.

subjects.name: English Literature (4ET1)
subjects.description: Closed-text and set-text questions on poetry, prose and drama. The marks follow argument and quotation, not plot retelling. Students in the Emirates often arrive with strong content knowledge and no essay structure, so the work is usually building a thesis-led paragraph pattern and a bank of short quotations that can be deployed under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the grade. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram carries marks that no amount of written explanation can recover, and UAE students who have learnt the theory verbally usually cannot draw it under pressure. Data-response questions reward reading the figures given rather than importing remembered examples.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Applied rather than theoretical: the marks sit in applying a concept to the case material in front of the student, and in evaluation that reaches a judgement. Generic answers about marketing or motivation score the knowledge mark and stop there. Tutoring focuses on the evaluate command and on the arithmetic of ratios and break-even.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (4IT1)
subjects.description: Assessed in part on practical competence with documents, spreadsheets and databases, which translates well to a shared screen. Students who use software daily still lose marks because they cannot describe what they did in the specification's vocabulary, and because they skip the evaluation section at the end of a practical task.

edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Who regulates your child's school changes what you can look up, who answers a complaint and where the inspection report lives. It does not change the Pearson specification, and because lessons run over live video it does not change who can teach your child either. The notes below are the practical differences, emirate by emirate.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA territory: 227 private schools in 2024-25 serving 387,441 enrolments across 17 curricula, with the UK track the largest at 37%. The deepest pool of Edexcel-entering schools in the country, and the emirate where inspection reports are easiest to find and read.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools here. Abu Dhabi families often find Edexcel option subjects taught in smaller cohorts than in Dubai, which makes a one-to-one specialist on video the practical answer for a minority subject such as 4PM1 or 4EC1.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK, not a separate authority, which surprises parents who assume the regulator follows the city. Fewer British-curriculum schools than the coast, so subject availability rather than teaching quality is usually the constraint. Evening video sessions sidestep the drive entirely.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, so a Sharjah school's assessment calendar is an approved document rather than an internal choice.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Families in Al Nuaimiya and Al Rashidiya often commute towards Sharjah or Dubai for a British-curriculum place, which makes a 5pm or 6pm video slot more realistic than any travelling arrangement.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest British-curriculum population in the country, and the clearest case for online delivery: the chance that a 4CH1 specialist happens to live within driving distance of Al Salamah is close to nil, and on video it is irrelevant.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the emirate's own Department of Knowledge, which like SPEA approves curricula, courses and assessment methods as well as fees. Families in Al Nakheel and Al Hamra typically have one or two Edexcel-entering schools within reach, so option blocks are tight and tier decisions are made early.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision, on the east coast, where a two-hour round trip to a Dubai tutor would consume more time than the lesson. Students in Fujairah city, Dibba and Khor Fakkan book exactly the same Pearson specialists as a family in Dubai Marina, on the same evening grid.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai, UK-curriculum cluster
schoolClusters.note: The densest concentration of Pearson and Cambridge entries in the country, spread across Al Barsha, Jumeirah, Nad Al Sheba and Dubai Hills. Option blocks here are wide enough that a student can usually sit three separate sciences, which is why Dubai families more often need depth in one subject than coverage across many.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: ADEK-regulated British-curriculum schools concentrated on the island, in Khalifa City and along the Al Ain road. Cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, so a minority option such as Further Pure Mathematics or Economics may run with a single teacher and no second opinion available inside the school.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry elsewhere. Families here frequently choose between a nearer school with a narrow option block and a longer commute to a wider one, and that trade-off is the single most common reason a northern-emirates parent starts looking for an Edexcel tutor.

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is actually asking for with this search
paragraphs: A parent typing edexcel igcse home tutor in the uae into Google is asking for a tutor who knows the Pearson specification and who is available in the hours between the school run and bedtime. The phrase home tutor is doing two jobs in that search: it means one-to-one rather than a group class, and it means at a time and place that fits the household. IB Gram answers the first job exactly and the second one differently. Lessons are one-to-one, and they happen over live video rather than in the living room.

That is worth being direct about, because the alternative is to let a family discover it after booking. A tutor travelling across Dubai in the 5pm direction can serve perhaps two households an evening, and the candidates are whoever lives within reach. On video the constraint disappears, and the question changes from who is nearby to who has taught 4PH1 Paper 2 repeatedly and can explain why a student keeps losing the gradient marks. For a minority code such as 4PM1 or 4EC1, the second question is the only one with a useful answer in most emirates.

The rest of this page is built around the part of the problem nobody else writing for this search seems to address: the system the entry sits inside. Which authority holds the school file, what the Pearson grade scale means against the Ministry's equivalency floor, who sets the tier, when the entry closes, which credential a UAE tutor is actually required to hold, and where the line sits on coursework. Those are the things that change what a family should buy, and in what order.

sections.heading: Five authorities, one British curriculum: who signed off on your child's entry
paragraphs: There is no single national regulator for UAE private schools, and a family that assumes KHDA covers the whole country will look for documents that do not exist for them. Dubai has KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK. Sharjah has SPEA. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. That is the complete map, and it determines where the inspection report is published and who a parent escalates to.

The remit is not identical across the five. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is curriculum and assessment approval, not inspection alone, so a Sharjah school's internal assessment calendar sits inside an approved framework rather than being set freely by the head of department. Underneath all five sits the federal baseline: private schools are not obliged to follow any particular curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

None of these five bodies approves individual tutors, and none of them issues a credential a tutoring platform can hold. A permit for a training institute with premises in Dubai is a specific KHDA instrument with its own application sequence, initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. It is not a tutor licence, and any provider describing its individual tutors as approved by a UAE regulator is describing something that does not exist. What the regulator genuinely gives a parent is the school's published inspection judgements, and that is more useful than a badge.

sections.heading: The grade scale on a Pearson certificate, read against the Ministry's floor
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE qualifications report on a 9 to 1 scale. Grade 9 is the top; grade 1 is the bottom. Parents who sat O Levels or lettered GCSEs read that scale wrongly in a predictable direction, assuming 9 to 1 maps onto A* to G one step at a time. It does not: the numbered scale has more points at the top of the range, so the distance between a 7 and a 9 is a real academic distance rather than a relabelling.

Where the scale becomes a UAE question is the equivalency file. The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement, as set out in its July 2026 clarification, is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that sits one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states six subjects. The Ministry's clarification says five.

The practical consequence reorders a family's spending. If a child is sitting nine Pearson subjects and three of them are already comfortably above the floor, the equivalency risk lives in the weakest two, not in the strong seven. Hours bought for a subject already at grade 6 buy university competitiveness; hours bought for a subject sitting at grade 2 buy the file itself. Those are different purchases with different urgency, and no tutoring page can tell you which you need without seeing the mock results. Confirm the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before acting on any figure here.

sections.heading: Higher or Foundation: the entry form sets the ceiling before any teaching starts
paragraphs: Some Pearson International GCSE subjects are tiered and some are not, and families routinely assume the wrong one. Mathematics A is tiered: a Foundation entry and a Higher entry sit different papers and reach different parts of the grade scale, with the Foundation route capped below the top grades. Most of the sciences and most of the humanities on the Pearson International GCSE list are single-tier, so every candidate sits the same papers and the whole scale is in reach.

The decision is made by the school, on the entry it submits, and it is usually made on Year 10 evidence. That timing is the problem. A student who was a borderline case in the spring of Year 10 and has since worked hard can be sitting a Foundation paper in Year 11 with a ceiling they no longer deserve, simply because nobody revisited the decision. The window to change it is the school's own entry amendment window, which closes well before the papers, and the conversation has to be opened by the parent.

This is where a short diagnostic is worth more than a term of teaching. Put the student in front of Higher-tier questions from a past series, mark them honestly, and the answer is usually obvious within an hour. If the Higher paper is reachable with support, that is a case to take to the exams officer in writing before the amendment window shuts. If it is not, Foundation is the right entry and the hours should go into securing the top of that tier rather than fighting the ceiling. Always confirm the tier and the code printed on the statement of entry before booking anything.

sections.heading: Two Pearson series a year, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year. Having two series is the single most useful fact in a UAE family's planning, and it is the fact competitor pages for this query leave out entirely. It means a disappointing summer result has a route in the following winter, and it means a student who joined a UAE school late can sometimes split their entries across two sittings rather than facing ten papers in one month.

Working backwards from published dates makes the shape obvious. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October through to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November resit decided in late August produces a certificate in the following January, not the following summer. For a Year 11 student applying to a sixth form, that difference decides whether the grade arrives in time to matter.

Two cautions. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for International GCSE November 2027, and dates can be revised, so the official timetable page is the only safe source for your own series. And entries are made by the school as a registered centre, which means the deadline that actually binds your household is the internal one your exams officer sets, usually weeks before Pearson's. Ask for it in writing in September and put it in the calendar; it is the cheapest piece of exam planning available.

sections.heading: Is the tutor permitted to charge? What the permit does and does not certify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is not unregulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is the credential the state actually issues to an individual tutor. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

The application route is public. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee listed. A tutor who has not obtained one when it costs nothing and takes two working days has made a choice, and a parent is entitled to ask about it before the first paid session.

What the permit does not do is the part that matters for an Edexcel entry. It does not assess subject knowledge, it does not mention a board, and it says nothing about whether the holder has ever taught 4CH1. It is a right-to-work document, not a teaching qualification. Two further conditions sit beside it: the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the holder's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Those press-reported rules should be checked against the current ADEK policy document before anyone relies on their exact wording.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies beside an Edexcel timetable
paragraphs: Every UAE private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines set this out for Dubai and required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position is the same in substance: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The organisation rules are specific enough to matter to a tutor. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval.

Two things follow for a family buying tuition. First, these subjects are marked by the school, not by Pearson, and they do not appear among the five subjects the Ministry counts for British-track equivalency, where Arabic and Islamic education are explicitly excluded. They still sit on the report card and still consume timetable hours. Second, the content is constrained: KHDA states that using any different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited. A tutor working on these subjects should be working from the school's own issued material, and any provider offering a better Arabic syllabus is offering something the rules do not allow.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for Edexcel teaching, and who published each figure
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for UAE tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family pays school fees in. So here are the AED bands, each attributed to whoever published it, read in October 2026. These are market figures and not IB Gram prices; our own position is a free trial lesson and a conversation about what the specific subject and tier actually needs, because quoting an hourly rate before seeing a mock script is guesswork dressed as transparency.

The bands are wide for a reason worth understanding. At the bottom of the market the tutor is often a university student with no board specialism stated and no permit position published. In the middle sits a qualified subject tutor who may or may not have taught the Pearson code your child is entered for. At the top, the premium is usually attached to a claim about examiner experience, and examiner status should never be taken on assertion, nor read as access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

Useful context for any of these numbers: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are the household's fixed education cost and they are flat this year. Tutoring is the variable one, which is why deciding how many hours to buy, and against which subject, is a decision worth making with a marked script in front of you rather than a price list.

sections.heading: A tutor in the living room against a subject specialist on screen
paragraphs: This is the comparison a family searching for a home tutor deserves to see made properly rather than avoided. Both arrangements are one-to-one. Both can be good. They differ on four things: who is in the candidate pool, what fraction of the paid hour is teaching, what evidence you can check before committing, and what happens in the weeks when the schedule breaks.

The candidate pool is the decisive one. A tutor travelling to a Khalifa City villa is drawn from whoever will make that drive on a weekday evening. For 4MA1 that pool is probably adequate. For 4PM1, 4EC1 or English Literature at the top of the scale it frequently is not, and in Umm Al Quwain or Fujairah it is close to empty. On video the pool is every specialist available on Gulf Standard Time, which is why edexcel igcse online tuition in dubai and the same tuition in Dibba are the same product with the same teacher list.

The second difference is arithmetic. A travelling tutor crossing Dubai in the 5pm direction is pricing the journey into the rate, whether or not the invoice says so, and a Bestimate in-home band of AED 180 to 350 against an online band of AED 150 to 300 is roughly that gap. The honest counterweight is that a tutor in the room can read a distracted eleven-year-old better than a camera can, and some students genuinely focus better with someone physically present. For an exam-year student working on timed Pearson papers and marked scripts, the shared screen is the stronger tool: the script is on it, annotated, and the session can be recorded for revision.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor must not cross on a Pearson entry
paragraphs: Where a Pearson International GCSE includes work produced outside an exam hall, a tutor's role narrows sharply and should be stated in advance. English Language A offers a coursework route in place of one written component. Information and Communication Technology assesses practical competence. In the sciences the practical skills are examined through written questions rather than through assessed lab work, which changes the shape of the help but not the principle.

The principle is simple and it is the whole of our position. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the assessment criteria, model the technique on a different question, ask the questions that make a student see a weakness in their own draft, and give written feedback on work the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write, redraft to completion, or supply text for a coursework folder. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is a malpractice trigger for the student and it is not a service we will provide at any price.

The same line applies to materials. We do not reproduce or distribute Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We cite them and link to the official pages on qualifications.pearson.com so a parent can read the primary source, which is also the only place a current paper structure or weighting can be confirmed. And no tutor, however many series they have taught, can tell you what the grade boundaries will be or guarantee the grade your child will finish with. Anyone who offers either is selling something they do not have.

sections.heading: What an inspection report tells you about a 4CH1 grade, and what it does not
paragraphs: Inspection reports are the most useful free document in UAE education and the most commonly misread. A band such as Outstanding or Good is a judgement about a school, built from attainment and progress evidence across phases and subjects, published by KHDA, ADEK or SPEA depending on the emirate. It is not a prediction about one child in one subject, and a strong overall band is entirely compatible with a weak cohort in one science in one year group.

Read it the way a tutor would. Go past the headline band to the subject-level and phase-level judgements, because that is where a parent learns whether secondary science attainment was judged weaker than secondary maths, and whether progress was judged weaker than attainment. Attainment against progress is the distinction that matters most: a school where attainment is high but progress is only acceptable is a school where able children are coasting, and that is a different tutoring problem from a school where both are low.

Then weigh it against the evidence you already own and nobody else has: your child's marked mock script. The report describes a school in the year it was inspected. The script describes your child this term, question by question, with the lost marks visible. When the two disagree, the script wins for the purpose of deciding what to buy. The report is how you judge the school; the script is how you judge where the next ten hours should go, and starting from it is the difference between tuition that moves a grade and tuition that reassures a parent.

process.title: Send the codes, not the subject names
process.description: Start by sending the statement of entry or the subject list with the Pearson codes on it. 4MA1 Higher is a different brief from 4MB1, and a double award is a different brief from three separate sciences. This single step removes most of the mismatch risk before anyone is matched.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it is worth more than any description of the problem. It shows which question types are failing and whether the issue is content, technique or timing. Where no script exists, the trial lesson produces one from a past-paper section.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson with the proposed tutor, at no cost and before any payment is taken. Use it to ask which Pearson codes they have taught and in which series, how they would approach the weakness the script shows, and what their private tuition work permit position is. All three are fair questions.

process.title: Set the weekly slot on your clock
process.description: Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, around the school run, prayer times and the household's evening. Ramadan slots move after Iftar. The slot matters more than families expect: a session scheduled when a student is already exhausted produces attendance rather than learning.

process.title: Review against the school's own reports
process.description: Each term, read the school's assessment report beside the tutor's written feedback. If the two disagree, that is the conversation to have. If neither shows movement after a term of consistent attendance, change the tutor or change the plan rather than buying more of the same hours.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the paper code
whyPoints.description: Tutors are proposed against the Pearson code on the entry rather than against the word IGCSE. A teacher who has taken students through 4CH1 repeatedly knows which quantitative chemistry questions recur and where the method marks sit. That specificity is the main thing a video lesson buys a family outside central Dubai.

whyPoints.title: The permit position stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Each tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit position is stated before you book. The permit is free and takes two working days, so there is no reason to be vague about it. We also say plainly what it does not certify: it is a right-to-work document, not evidence of subject depth.

whyPoints.title: No approval we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or Pearson, and we do not imply one. No UAE authority approves individual tutors. We name the regulators because understanding them helps you, not because any of them endorses us.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line published in advance
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews the student's own work and gives feedback on it. We will not write or finish coursework on a student's behalf, supply mark schemes as downloads, predict grade boundaries, or promise the grade a student will end up with. Publishing that before you ask is more useful than a promise, because it tells you what to expect in week ten.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated honestly
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for the code and tier you need, we say so and offer a waiting position rather than a generalist. For minority codes in the northern emirates that is a real possibility, and a family deserves to hear it before a term of hours is committed to the wrong teacher.

whyPoints.title: One evening grid for the whole country
whyPoints.description: A family in Khor Fakkan books the same Pearson specialists on the same timetable as a family in Jumeirah, because the lesson runs over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Geography stops being a constraint on teacher quality, which is the entire argument for delivering it this way.

faqs.question: Our school enters Pearson Edexcel papers. Which UAE authority actually signed off on that?
faqs.answer: Your emirate's regulator licenses the school and its curriculum, not Pearson's specification. In Dubai that is KHDA; in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, ADEK; in Sharjah, SPEA; in Ras Al Khaimah, the Department of Knowledge; and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves curricula, courses and assessment methods as well as fees, so the choice of board sits inside an approved framework there. Pearson's own involvement is as the awarding organisation and the school's examination centre registration. The practical answer to who chose Edexcel is the school's leadership, inside the licence its regulator granted.

faqs.question: Pearson grades International GCSE from 9 down to 1. Which of those grades clears the Ministry's floor?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement, as reported from its July 2026 clarification, is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3. On the numbered scale that puts grade 3 at the stated floor, so grades 3 and above count and grades 2 and 1 do not. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five subjects. Clearing the floor is not the same as being competitive for a course, though: a grade 4 in maths counts towards the five but rarely supports that subject at A Level. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: Who decides whether my son sits the Higher or the Foundation tier of 4MA1?
faqs.answer: The school does, on the entry it submits to Pearson, usually on evidence from Year 10. The family is not asked to sign anything. That is why the decision is worth revisiting: a student who was borderline in spring and has since worked hard can be sitting a Foundation paper with a grade ceiling they no longer deserve. The route back is the centre's own entry amendment window, which closes well before the papers. Put the request in writing to the exams officer, with evidence, and bring Higher-tier past-paper work to the conversation. An hour of honest diagnostic marking usually settles which tier is the right one.

faqs.question: What would a tutor have to show us to prove they teach the Edexcel specification rather than the Cambridge one?
faqs.answer: Ask three concrete questions. First, which Pearson codes they have taught and in which series: 4CH1 and 0620 are different specifications with different paper structures. Second, how the practical skills are assessed on the Pearson science papers, since a Cambridge-trained tutor may expect a different arrangement. Third, what changes in their teaching between Mathematics A and Mathematics B. A tutor who has genuinely taught the board answers all three without hesitation. There is no Pearson certificate for tutors that would settle this on paper, so the trial lesson is where the question gets answered. Use it for exactly that.

faqs.question: Our daughter is at school in Ras Al Khaimah. Does KHDA guidance apply to her Edexcel timetable at all?
faqs.answer: Not directly. KHDA regulates private education in Dubai. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The federal baseline still applies to her: Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies are required of private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed to teach. So the mandatory subjects are on her timetable, but the document setting out how they are organised is her own emirate's, not Dubai's. The Pearson specification is identical either way, which is why her tutor can be the same one a Dubai student uses.

faqs.question: The school has offered the November series instead of June. What does that change about the next six months?
faqs.answer: It moves every date, including the one that matters most. Pearson runs International GCSE papers in May or June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Results follow the series, not the school year: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, where June 2026 results reached them on 20 August 2026. So a November entry means teaching peaks in September and October rather than April, and the certificate arrives in January. Check your own series on the official Pearson timetable page, since provisional timetables can be revised before they are confirmed.

faqs.question: Is a Science Double Award entry counted as one subject or two for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: The Pearson Science Double Award produces two grades rather than one, which is why it is called a double award. How the Ministry's attestation process counts it towards the five accredited subjects on the British track is a question for the Ministry or your emirate's attestation authority, and we will not publish an answer we have not read on moe.gov.ae. What we can say is that it is worth settling before Year 11, not after results. If the count matters to a federal university plan, ask the school's university counsellor to confirm it in writing with the authority rather than relying on any tutoring provider's interpretation.

faqs.question: We live in Khalifa City and every Edexcel Chemistry tutor we found advertises in Dubai. What are the options?
faqs.answer: This is the exact problem online delivery solves. A tutor travelling to Khalifa City is drawn from whoever will make that drive on a weekday evening, and for 4CH1 at the top of the grade scale that pool is thin. Over live video the pool is every Pearson chemistry specialist free on Gulf Standard Time, and the drive disappears from both the schedule and the rate. IB Gram does not send anyone to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run in India only. The session happens on a shared screen, with your daughter's marked script open and annotated as it is discussed.

faqs.question: How far ahead of a Pearson paper does the entry actually close?
faqs.answer: Months, and the deadline that binds your household is earlier than Pearson's. Final entries go to Pearson from the school as a registered examination centre, and the school sets its own internal cut-off weeks before that so it can collate and check the data. The comparison that makes this vivid is Cambridge's published March 2027 series, where final entries were due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period starting 3 February 2027. Pearson's pattern is similar in shape. Ask your exams officer in September for the internal deadline in writing, and put it in the family calendar alongside the paper dates.

faqs.question: My son takes the coursework route in English Language A. Where exactly does a tutor's help have to stop?
faqs.answer: At the point where words stop being his. A tutor may teach the skill, explain how the assessment criteria allocate marks, model the technique on a different text, ask the questions that make him see a weakness in his own draft, and give written feedback on what he has written. A tutor may not write a section, redraft it to completion, or supply text to be used. That line is not ours; it is what keeps the submission his own work and keeps him clear of a malpractice finding. Any provider offering to finish the folder is offering to put his qualification at risk.

faqs.question: The private tuition permit is free and takes two working days. Does that make it worth checking?
faqs.answer: It makes it more worth checking, not less. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services under the service name Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. A tutor who has not obtained a free document that takes two days has made a choice worth asking about. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted with scepticism.

faqs.question: Our school moved from Cambridge to Pearson between Year 10 and Year 11. What has to be re-taught?
faqs.answer: Less content than you fear and more technique than you expect. The underlying subject knowledge largely transfers, but the paper structures, the mark allocations and the command verbs differ, and students lose marks on the shape of the answer rather than on the facts. The first job is to get the statement of entry with the new codes on it and map each one to its current paper structure on qualifications.pearson.com. The second is timed practice on the new papers, marked against the published criteria. A term of that usually closes the gap; a year of re-teaching content is mostly wasted money.

faqs.question: Should my daughter take Arabic as a Pearson International GCSE, or is the school's Arabic lesson a separate requirement?
faqs.answer: They are separate things. The Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons on her timetable are mandatory UAE subjects required of private schools whatever curriculum they are licensed to teach, marked by the school, and excluded from the five subjects the Ministry counts on the British track. A Pearson International GCSE in Arabic would be an additional external qualification with its own entry and grade. Whether to add it depends on her level and her timetable space, not on the mandatory requirement, which she is already meeting. Ask the school which Arabic stream she is in, since classes are organised separately by first language.

faqs.question: The inspection report praised teaching, but our son's 4CH1 mocks sit at grade 4. Which of the two should we believe?
faqs.answer: Both, for different purposes. The inspection judgement describes the school in the year it was inspected, built from attainment and progress evidence across phases and subjects. The mock script describes your son this term, question by question, with the lost marks visible. A well-judged school can still have a weak cohort in one science in one year group, and a strong overall band tells you nothing about quantitative chemistry. Use the report to judge the school and the script to decide where the next ten hours go. When they disagree about your child specifically, the script is the better evidence.

faqs.question: Our plan is a federal university here in the Emirates. Does an Edexcel International GCSE on its own get her there?
faqs.answer: No, and the Ministry's own requirement explains why. The British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. So the International GCSE is one half of the file and a post-16 qualification is the other. Nothing about tutoring is required for any of it, and we do not perform equivalency or attestation ourselves. Confirm the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority before building a plan on it.

faqs.question: If an August result is one grade short, what is the Pearson route and how long does it take?
faqs.answer: Two routes, on different clocks. A review of marking is requested through the school within the board's published window after results, and it can only correct a marking error, not a performance. A resit in the next series is the other route: Pearson runs International GCSE papers in May or June and again in November, so a result received on 20 August 2026 could in principle be followed by a November entry. Judging by the November 2025 series, whose results reached students on 22 January 2026, the new grade lands in January. Decide quickly, because the entry deadline sits weeks after results.

If nobody is free for the code and tier you need, we will say so.

edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications rather than a general school subject. Each works from the current specification and the published assessment weightings, marks timed papers against the real criteria, and plans around the series date on your child's statement of entry.

intro.heading: Start from the series, not from the syllabus
paragraphs: Most families looking for an Edexcel IGCSE online tutor in the UAE start the search in the wrong order. They begin with a subject, then a price, then availability, and only afterwards discover that the tutor has been teaching the Cambridge syllabus for a child entered with Pearson, or revising topics that sit in a paper the child has already sat. The order that works is the reverse. Find the series, find the codes, then find the teacher. A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE candidate in Sharjah and a Cambridge candidate in the same classroom can be revising the same topic for papers with different lengths, different mark totals and different calculator rules.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, which means that as this page is reviewed, one series is live and the next entry window is already close. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and the previous November series reached students on 22 January 2026. Those four dates are the skeleton of the whole school year, and almost nothing a UAE tutoring provider publishes mentions any of them.

The practical effect of that calendar is that the useful question is never "how long will this take". It is "how many teaching weeks are left, and which papers do they belong to". A child in Year 11 in Dubai who starts in September has roughly thirty teaching weeks before a May/June series, minus the mock fortnight, minus Eid, minus the half-term weeks the school takes, minus the fortnight before the papers when nothing new can be learned. Written out honestly, thirty becomes about twenty-two. A plan built on twenty-two weeks looks nothing like a plan built on a vague "nine months".

This page covers the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE across all seven emirates, because the exam calendar is federal in a way that school regulation is not. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. None of them sets the date your child walks into the exam hall. Pearson does, and the centre's exams officer holds the entry deadline that comes months earlier.

Lessons here are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. For an Edexcel International GCSE that is less of a compromise than it sounds, because the scarce thing in this market is not a person who can drive to Mirdif at six o'clock. It is someone who has marked four hundred scripts of 4PH1 Paper 2 and knows which six marks the astrophysics questions give away. Online delivery is what makes that person reachable from Fujairah as easily as from Jumeirah.

edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Pearson's school qualifications form a ladder, and each rung has its own entry deadlines and its own relationship to the series calendar. These are the four stages UAE families most often ask about when they are planning an Edexcel International GCSE route.

programmes.name: International Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Pearson's Lower Secondary curriculum is the preparation stage, with no external series and no entry deadline. The work that matters here is algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and extended writing stamina, because those are the three things a weak Year 9 brings into a Year 10 specification and the three things that cost the most teaching weeks to repair later.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this stage is where curriculum transfers cluster. Families arriving from CBSE, American or MoE-curriculum schools usually enter at Year 7 to Year 9, and the gap that shows up first is not content but question style: UK-curriculum papers ask students to explain and evaluate rather than to recall, and that is a habit built over terms.

programmes.name: International GCSE (9-1)
programmes.description: The main event. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is graded 9 to 1, assessed linearly at the end of the course rather than in units, and sat in a May/June or November series. Most UAE candidates take eight to ten subjects, with Mathematics A, English Language A and three separate sciences the common spine.
programmes.countryNote: Which board a UAE school enters is a departmental decision, and large schools split: a maths department may use Pearson while the sciences use Cambridge. The statement of entry your child receives from the exams officer is the only reliable record, and it lists the specification codes, the tier and the component numbers that a tutor actually needs.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The step after International GCSE, and structurally different: International AS and A Level work in units, so a student can bank unit results across series and resit a single unit. That unitised structure is what people mean by modular, and it does not apply to International GCSE, where a resit means sitting the whole subject again.
programmes.countryNote: The distinction matters for UAE equivalency. The Ministry of Education's British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the International GCSE requirement, so the AS year is not merely a stepping stone on paper.

programmes.name: Resit and private-candidate route
programmes.description: A November series sits roughly five months after June results and about six months before the next June papers, which makes it the natural repair window for one or two subjects that did not land. A resit at International GCSE means sitting every component of that subject again; no marks carry across from the earlier attempt.
programmes.countryNote: A candidate no longer at school sits as a private candidate, which means finding a UAE examination centre that accepts external entries and applying through it, not directly to Pearson. Centres cap external numbers and close early, so the search for a centre belongs in the same week as the decision to resit.

edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications UAE families request most, with their codes. Ask a prospective tutor which of these codes they have taught and when; a tutor who recognises 4MA1 but not 4MB1 is telling you something useful about their experience.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of two hours and 100 marks each, weighted 50% apiece, with a calculator permitted in both. The Higher tier reaches grade 9 and the Foundation tier stops at grade 5, which makes the tier decision one of the few genuinely irreversible choices in the whole International GCSE. Marks go missing on multi-step problem questions and on unshown working.

subjects.name: Mathematics B (4MB1)
subjects.description: A different specification rather than a harder version of the same one: two papers of unequal length, a single untiered entry, and a content range that leans further into algebra, trigonometry and calculus-adjacent work. Schools that enter Mathematics B often do so to feed International A Level Mathematics, so a tutor needs to know which specification is on the statement of entry.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, taken alongside Maths A or B
subjects.description: An additional qualification taken by students heading for engineering or mathematics, examined in two papers. It introduces calculus, series, matrices and vectors a year early. The usual problem is not ability but sequencing: students meet differentiation here before their main maths course reaches it, so the tutoring job is ordering the topics sensibly.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Paper 1 runs two hours for 110 marks and carries two thirds of the grade; Paper 2 runs an hour and fifteen minutes for 70 marks and carries the remaining third. There is no separate practical examination, so experimental skills are tested inside the written papers. Electricity, moments and the astrophysics content at the end of Paper 2 are where marks drain away.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: The same two-paper shape as Physics, with Paper 1 taking the principles, inorganic and physical content and Paper 2 taking organic chemistry and the later topics. Moles calculations and the required practical write-ups generate the predictable losses, and students who have never been asked to describe a test for a gas in exam language lose easy marks.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Again two papers in a roughly two-to-one weighting. Biology punishes imprecise language more than any other science at this level: a correct idea written loosely scores nothing against a mark scheme that wants named structures and directional statements. Transport in plants, genetics crosses and the practical-skills questions are the standard repair list.

subjects.name: Science (Double Award) (4SD0)
subjects.levels: Single tier, awarded as two grades
subjects.description: Three written papers, one per science, producing two International GCSE grades rather than three. It is a sensible choice for a student carrying nine or ten subjects, but it is not a lighter syllabus per paper. Families should check it against university or school-progression requirements before assuming it substitutes for separate sciences.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with a coursework route option
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers non-fiction reading and transactional writing across two hours and fifteen minutes; the second component covers anthology poetry and prose plus imaginative writing, and a school may enter candidates for a coursework route in its place. Which route a school chose changes what a tutor can legitimately do, so this needs establishing in the first session.

subjects.name: English Literature (4ET1)
subjects.description: Set texts, unseen poetry and extended comparative response. The recurring problem for UAE candidates is quotation under timed conditions: students who know a text well still underperform because they have not drilled a bank of short, flexible quotations they can deploy without the book in front of them.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1) and Business (4BS1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, two written papers each
subjects.description: Both reward structure over content. Marks sit in the chain of reasoning and in the evaluation sentences at the end of a long answer, not in the definition at the start. Students at UAE schools often have strong real-world examples from the local economy and no framework for turning them into a diagram-plus-consequence answer.

subjects.name: Geography (4GE1) and History (4HI1)
subjects.description: Both are two-paper specifications with heavy source and case-study demands. Geography assesses fieldwork understanding inside the written papers rather than through separate coursework, and History lives or dies on whether a student can turn knowledge into an argument that answers the question asked rather than the question revised.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0)
subjects.description: Theory plus practical programming assessed by written examination. Students who have learned to code in a classroom still lose marks on trace tables, on writing pseudocode to a specification's conventions, and on the written questions about data representation and networks, which look nothing like the programming they enjoy.

edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE across the seven emirates
edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: The exam calendar is the same in every emirate; the regulator, the school supply and the realistic session time are not. Online delivery is what lets a family in Umm Al Quwain book the same specialist as a family in Jumeirah, which is the point of the format rather than a consolation for it.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education here, across 227 private schools in 2024-25 teaching 17 curricula. The UK curriculum is the largest single share of enrolment, so Pearson and Cambridge departments sit side by side in the same school, and board confusion is commonest in Dubai precisely because both are everywhere.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school. For an Edexcel International GCSE plan that matters: the obvious tutor, your child's own subject teacher, is the one you should not be arranging privately.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller pool of UK-curriculum secondary departments than the island. Families here feel specification scarcity first: a 4PM1 or 4CP0 specialist within driving distance may simply not exist, which is the clearest case in the country for an online match.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families send children to Dubai schools, so the realistic session start is after the evening commute rather than at four o'clock.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The practical consequence for exam planning is a shorter list of local examination centres, which is the first thing to check if a resit or a private-candidate entry is likely.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees. Northern-emirate families are almost invisible in competitor tutoring content, which is why availability here is worth asking about explicitly rather than assuming.

regions.name: Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Both sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Between them they appear in essentially none of the published UAE tutoring content we reviewed. A live-video lesson removes the only real barrier here, which was never the quality of local teaching but the size of the local specialist pool.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai UK-curriculum secondaries
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend schools across this group. We do not publish which board each department enters, because it changes between departments and between years; your child's statement of entry is the record that matters.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: ADEK-regulated schools, where the ethics rules on staff tutoring their own students shape how families arrange support. Specification scarcity is sharper here than in Dubai, particularly in Further Pure Mathematics and Computer Science.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Regulated by SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Session times here are set by the commute, not by the school bell.

edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of support cover almost every Edexcel International GCSE request we see, and which one fits is decided by the distance to the series rather than by budget. All three run one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Two-year weekly one-to-one, Years 10 and 11
modes.description: A single weekly slot per subject held for the whole course, moving in step with the school's scheme of work and stopping for the mock fortnight. This is the only shape that can fix foundations rather than patch symptoms, because it has the teaching weeks to go back to algebra in October and still cover the Paper 2 content by February.
