Specification checked against the school's scheme of work in session one
A timed past paper every half-term, marked against the published criteria
Pauses for the mock fortnight and for Eid rather than pretending they are not there

modes.title: The six-week block before a live series
modes.description: Short, intense and deliberately narrow. Six weeks is enough to repair four topics per paper and to drill exam technique; it is not enough to teach a year. The first session is a diagnostic paper, and the plan that follows is built from what that paper showed rather than from the student's own account of what is difficult.
bullets: Starts with one full timed paper under exam conditions
A maximum of four target topics per paper, chosen from the script
Two sessions a week in the final three weeks, then one
Nothing new introduced in the last ten days

modes.title: A resit block between November and May/June
modes.description: The gap between a January results release and a spring entry deadline is short, and the resit decision has to be made inside it. A resit block treats the previous script as data: which paper lost the marks, in which topics, and whether the honest answer is more content or more timed practice. An International GCSE resit covers every component again.

Confirms the entry deadline with the centre before any teaching is planned

sections.heading: What an Edexcel IGCSE online tutor in the UAE actually has to get right
paragraphs: An Edexcel IGCSE online tutor in the UAE teaches a named Pearson specification to a named series date. In practice that means three things: working from the specification code on the statement of entry, marking to the published criteria rather than to a general impression, and sequencing the content so that the Paper 1 material is secure before the Paper 2 material is started. Everything else is secondary to those three.

The reason this needs saying is that the commonest failure in UAE tutoring is not weak teaching. It is a board mismatch. A tutor who learned the Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 syllabus will drill a non-calculator paper that a Pearson Mathematics A candidate will never sit, because both 4MA1 papers permit a calculator. A tutor who learned Cambridge Physics 0625 will prepare for a practical or alternative-to-practical paper that 4PH1 does not have. The teaching is fine. The target is wrong.

There is a second, quieter mismatch: timing. A tutor who starts in week one with the first topic in the specification is building towards a finish line that may be nine months away or may be four weeks away. The calendar question comes first. What is the series, how many teaching weeks remain once the school's own interruptions are subtracted, and which papers can realistically be made safe in that time? A plan that answers those three questions before the first lesson is worth more than a plan that is merely thorough.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The honest case for the online format on an Edexcel International GCSE is specificity. A family in Ajman is not choosing between a 4CH1 specialist and a worse 4CH1 specialist. Most of the time they are choosing between a 4CH1 specialist on a screen and a capable generalist in the room.

sections.heading: Which board is your child actually sitting? How to check in five minutes
paragraphs: The statement of entry is the document that settles this. It is issued by the school's exams officer ahead of each series and lists, per subject, the awarding organisation, the specification code, the tier where one applies, the component numbers and the candidate number. A parent who has that sheet in hand can brief a tutor in two minutes. A parent who has only the subject names is guessing, and so is the tutor.

If the statement of entry has not arrived yet, the textbook spine and the school's own curriculum booklet are the next best evidence. A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE book carries the specification code on the cover; Cambridge books carry a four-digit syllabus number such as 0580 or 0625. Codes beginning with a 4 and ending in a 1 or 0, such as 4MA1, 4PH1 or 4CP0, are Pearson International GCSE. Where a department has switched boards between cohorts, the booklet for your child's year group is the one to trust.

It is normal for a single UAE school to use both boards. A maths department may enter Pearson while the sciences enter Cambridge, and some schools split English Language from English Literature across boards. That is a departmental decision, not an error, and it is one reason why asking a tutoring provider "do you cover IGCSE" produces a useless answer. The question that produces a useful answer is "have you taught 4MA1 Higher tier, and in which series".

sections.heading: The November 2026 series, counted backwards
paragraphs: This is the part of an exam year that almost no UAE tutoring page addresses, and it is the reason for this page's shape. The November 2026 International GCSE series ran from late October to 19 November 2026 on Pearson's final timetable. Work backwards from that and the whole year acquires structure: entries closed months earlier with the centre, internally assessed work went in before the written papers, and the mock sat in September. Results follow the series by roughly two months, and the next entry deadline arrives within weeks of them.

The single most expensive mistake in this sequence is treating the entry deadline as administrative. It is not. The tier on a 4MA1 entry, the coursework route on a 4EA1 entry and the decision to enter at all are all fixed at that point, and a late change costs a fee or is simply refused. A family that starts tutoring in September has already lost the ability to influence the two decisions that most affect the grade ceiling, which is why the entry deadline belongs on a parent's calendar rather than only on the exams officer's.

The second mistake is leaving the results decision until results arrive. The window between a November-series result and the next entry deadline is short. The previous November series released results to students on 22 January 2026; a spring entry deadline for the following May/June series falls not long after. A family that has already agreed what each outcome means, as in resit, enquire or accept, acts inside the window. A family that starts deliberating on results day often discovers the decision has been made for them.

sections.heading: A May/June International GCSE year, month by month
paragraphs: The May/June series is the one most UAE candidates sit, and it maps onto the local academic year awkwardly. The school year starts in late August or early September and the papers fall in May and June, which looks like nine months of runway. It is not. Subtract the National Day break, the winter holiday, the mock fortnight, the spring half-term, Ramadan's shortened days, Eid and the fortnight before the papers when nothing new can be absorbed, and the honest figure is closer to twenty-two teaching weeks.

Those twenty-two weeks have to carry two different jobs, and they are not interchangeable. The first job is content: closing the gaps that the specification exposes. The second is technique: command words, working, timing, and the particular habits each paper rewards. Technique work is nearly worthless in September, because there is not enough content to apply it to, and content work is nearly worthless in May, because there is no time to consolidate it. The calendar decides which job a session does.

Ramadan sits inside this window, and it moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which in recent years has pushed it into the mock and pre-exam season. The practical response is not to pretend the schedule is unchanged. Sessions move to after Iftar, duration drops from ninety minutes to sixty, and the work shifts to review and timed questions rather than new content. Families who plan that in January keep their momentum; families who plan it in week one of Ramadan lose a month.

sections.heading: Edexcel International GCSE components: duration, marks and weighting
paragraphs: Weighting is the most actionable number in an exam year and the least known. A student revising Edexcel Physics equally across both papers is misallocating effort, because Paper 1 carries about two thirds of the grade and Paper 2 about one third. A student revising Edexcel Mathematics A unequally is also misallocating, because the two papers are worth 50% each. Neither student is lazy. Both have been given no information.

The pattern across Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences is consistent and worth memorising: a long first paper of two hours and 110 marks carrying roughly two thirds, and a shorter second paper of about an hour and fifteen minutes and 70 marks carrying roughly one third. Mathematics A is the symmetrical exception at two hours and 100 marks per paper. English Language A splits roughly sixty to forty between its two components, with a coursework route available in place of the second.

Two practical consequences follow. First, in the final fortnight the hours should be split in proportion to the weightings, not in proportion to how much a student dislikes a topic. Second, the content that sits only in the lighter paper, such as organic chemistry in 4CH1 or astrophysics in 4PH1, is the content most often abandoned, which is exactly why it is a reliable source of recoverable marks for a student who has not abandoned it.

Component structures are revised between specification versions. The table below reflects the current shape at the time of writing and should be confirmed against the specification PDF for your child's cohort on qualifications.pearson.com before it drives a revision plan.

sections.heading: Tiering: the one Edexcel decision that cannot be undone later
paragraphs: Most Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are single tier, graded 9 to 1, with every candidate sitting the same papers. Mathematics A is the exception that UAE families meet, and it is tiered: a Higher tier entry reaches the top of the scale, and a Foundation tier entry has a ceiling several grades below it. That makes the tier decision different in kind from every other choice in the year, because it is fixed at the entry deadline and sets a maximum before any teaching happens.

The decision is usually taken by the maths department on the evidence of internal assessment, and it is usually right. Where it goes wrong is at the margins, in both directions. A student placed on Higher tier who cannot access the harder half of the paper spends the year demoralised and finishes with a grade the Foundation tier would have delivered more comfortably. A student placed on Foundation tier who is capable of more finishes with a grade that closes doors at sixth form, having never been shown the content that would have opened them.

What a tutor can usefully contribute here is evidence rather than opinion. A full timed paper at each tier, marked against the published criteria, produces two numbers and a pattern. If a student scores comfortably at the top of the Foundation tier paper and lands within reach of a pass on the Higher tier paper, that is an argument a head of department will listen to. A parental request without a marked script is not an argument, and school-entry decisions made against evidence are the only ones that get revisited.

The timing is unforgiving. This conversation has to happen before the entry deadline, which means early in Year 11 and in some schools at the end of Year 10. Families who raise it in February are asking for something that is no longer available. Families who raise it in October, with a marked script, are asking for something routine. The difference is the calendar, not the argument.

sections.heading: Where Edexcel International GCSE marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Marks are rarely lost because a student does not know the content. They are lost in predictable, diagnosable places, and almost all of them are habits rather than knowledge. The first is command words. Describe, explain, compare and evaluate ask for structurally different answers, and a mark scheme written for explain will not credit an accurate description. A student who answers every question in the same register loses marks across the whole paper, which is why command-word work pays better than any single topic.

The second is unshown working. In both 4MA1 papers, method marks exist independently of the final answer, so a wrong answer with visible correct method scores and a right answer with no method risks nothing at all when a transcription error creeps in. In the sciences the equivalent is the calculation question where the substitution, the rearrangement and the unit each carry credit. Students trained on multiple-choice-style practice have often never been required to show any of this.

The third is the family of precision errors: units omitted, significant figures ignored, graph points plotted outside tolerance, axes unlabelled, and biological or chemical terms used loosely where the mark scheme wants a named structure or a specified reagent. Each costs one or two marks, which sounds trivial until the audit across a full paper reaches double figures. A student who fixes only this, and learns nothing new, typically moves a visible distance up the scale.

The fourth is timing, and it concentrates in the shorter second papers. An hour and fifteen minutes for 70 marks leaves no recovery room, so a student who overruns on an early extended response arrives at the final questions with minutes to spare. The fix is mechanical: a target time per mark, a watch on the desk, and a rehearsed decision to abandon a stuck question and return to it. None of this is teaching content, and all of it is recoverable marks.
bullets: Command words: describe, explain, compare and evaluate are different tasks with different mark schemes

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in the UAE market, and what changes near a series
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are easy to find and rarely explained. The figures below are market rates collected from providers' own published pages in October 2026; they are not IB Gram's price list. They are here because three of the six most visible UAE tutoring pages publish no price at all, and two of the remaining ones quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family actually pays in. A parent comparing offers deserves the AED bands in front of them.

What the bands hide is that the number is only half the information. The other half is what moves as a series approaches. Availability goes first, and it goes from the top of the market downwards: the specification specialists are committed for the final weeks long before the generalists are. Then session length inflates, because a provider with one slot left would rather sell two hours than one. Then the monthly package stops making sense, because a six-week plan does not fit a rolling monthly commitment.

KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. Tutoring costs sit on top of fees and are not covered by that freeze, so it is worth putting the two numbers side by side before committing to a two-year weekly slot. Two subjects at one session a week for a full academic year is a four-figure annual commitment in AED at any tier in the table.

IB Gram's own model is a free trial lesson and then a conversation about the plan, rather than a rate card on a landing page. That is deliberate: the honest price for a 4PM1 specialist for six weeks before a live series is a different number from the honest price for weekly 4EA1 support across two years, and a single headline figure would misrepresent one of them.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what an Edexcel transcript has to show
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a foreign school certificate, and it matters because it sits between an International GCSE transcript and a university place in the Emirates. It is also, in the published UAE tutoring content we reviewed, almost entirely absent. Families find out about it late, discover a subject requirement they could have met two years earlier, and have no good options left.

On the British track, which is the track an Edexcel International GCSE candidate is on, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and, at post-16, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects, which is a detail worth knowing before a subject-choice conversation in Year 9.

That detail is also where a visible competitor gets it wrong. One UAE tutoring page currently tells parents that candidates here must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five. Most UAE students take eight to ten anyway, so the count is rarely the binding constraint, but the exclusion of Arabic and Islamic education from the five can be, particularly for a student carrying a light subject load.

Two cautions. The first is that no equivalency figure for the IB Diploma appears on any ministry page we were able to read, so no points threshold for that route is published here; families on the IB track should ask the school's IB coordinator and the ministry directly. The second is that equivalency is a process families complete through the official channel. IB Gram does not perform it, cannot expedite it, and nothing about tutoring is a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and the mandatory UAE subjects running alongside
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools in the UAE, and knowing which one covers your child's school changes what you can ask for and from whom. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, both approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

None of them sets an exam date, and none of them accredits a tutor. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated separately, by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own channels with a stated two working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

Two consequences follow for a UAE family. The first is that you can ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit, and a legitimate tutor will answer plainly. The second is a boundary: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct to similar effect. The convenient arrangement with your child's own subject teacher is the one to decline.

Alongside an Edexcel timetable, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed to teach, with those requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and for these subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the ministry is prohibited, which limits what any tutor may legitimately introduce.

sections.heading: Coursework, academic honesty and what a tutor may legitimately do
paragraphs: Most Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are assessed entirely by written examination, which removes a category of risk that exists at other levels. Where an internally assessed route does exist, as with the coursework option in English Language A, the boundary has to be explicit, because the consequences of crossing it fall on the student rather than on the tutor. A piece of internally assessed work must be the student's own, produced under the conditions the specification sets and declared as such by the school.

What a tutor may do inside that boundary is substantial and often misunderstood as less useful than it is. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, explain the criteria in plain language, model a technique on a different text or question, read a draft and say which criterion is not yet met and why, ask the questions that make a student see a weak paragraph for themselves, and set a schedule that stops the whole thing happening the night before. All of that moves marks.

What a tutor may not do is supply text. Not a sentence, not a corrected paragraph, not a restructured draft, not a model answer close enough to the task to be copied. Where a provider in this market offers finished assessed work for a fee, that is not a service with a different ethical position from ours. It is the thing that gets a student's entry invalidated, and the student carries that outcome for years. A tutor who edits a student's folder to completion has done the same thing more quietly.

The same logic applies to past papers and mark schemes. We reference the official specification and assessment materials and link to them on qualifications.pearson.com rather than reproducing or supplying them, because those documents belong to Pearson. A tutor who hands over a folder of copied material is a copyright problem; a tutor who teaches a student to navigate the official documents has given them something that lasts into sixth form.

sections.heading: Resits, enquiries about results, and sitting as a private candidate
paragraphs: At International GCSE a resit is a fresh sit of the whole subject. No component marks carry forward from an earlier attempt, which is the single biggest structural difference from the unitised International AS and A Level that follows it. A student retaking 4CH1 sits both papers again, and the new grade is a new grade rather than an improvement on the old one. That changes the arithmetic of whether a resit is worth the term it costs.

The decision has a calendar, and the calendar is tight. June results reached students on 20 August 2026 and the previous November-series results reached students on 22 January 2026. The next available series sits roughly three months after a summer result and about four months after a January one, and the entry deadline falls weeks before that. A family deciding in the first week after results has options. A family deciding a month later usually has one fewer.

Before a resit, there is an enquiry about results. If a grade sits just under a boundary, the centre, not the parent, can request a review or a copy of the script within a short published window after results. The sequence that works is to request the script copy first, have the subject teacher read it, and then decide; a review requested without seeing the script is a guess, and a mark can move in either direction. Schools handle this routinely and will do it when asked promptly.

A candidate who has left school sits as a private candidate, which means finding a UAE examination centre that accepts external entries, meeting its own earlier internal deadline, and paying its entry and administration fees. Centres limit external numbers and some decline them for particular subjects, so the centre search belongs in the same week as the resit decision rather than after it. A tutor cannot enter a candidate; only a centre can.

process.title: Send the statement of entry, not the subject names
process.description: The first thing we ask for is the sheet from the school's exams officer. It carries the awarding organisation, the specification codes, the tier where one applies and the component numbers. With that in hand the match is to a specification, not to a subject label, and nobody spends week one discovering the child sits Cambridge.

process.title: One timed paper, marked against the real criteria
process.description: Before any plan, the student sits a full past paper under timed conditions and a specialist marks it against the published criteria. That produces a list of lost marks sorted by cause: content, technique, precision or timing. Those four causes need different sessions, and guessing between them wastes the first fortnight.

process.title: Count the teaching weeks backwards from the series
process.description: We take the series date, subtract the mock fortnight, the school holidays, Eid, Ramadan's shortened sessions and the final fortnight when nothing new lands, and write down the real number. That number decides whether the plan can rebuild foundations or only repair four topics per paper. Both are legitimate; pretending is not.

process.title: Hold one weekly slot, in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time that works around school hours, the commute and prayer times, and that moves to after Iftar during Ramadan. A fixed slot survives a busy term; a flexible one quietly becomes fortnightly, then monthly, then a conversation in April about why nothing changed.

process.title: Agree the results decision before results day
process.description: Ahead of the release we write down what each outcome means: accept, ask the centre for a script copy and an enquiry, or enter the next series. The window between results and the next entry deadline is weeks, not months, so the decision rule is agreed while there is still time to act on it.

whyPoints.title: Matched by specification code
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed for 4MA1 Higher tier or 4PH1, not for maths or physics. That one habit removes the board mismatch that costs UAE families whole terms, and it is why we ask for the statement of entry before anything else happens.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts at the series date
whyPoints.description: Every plan is written backwards from the Pearson series your child is entered for, with the school's own interruptions subtracted. A parent sees the real number of teaching weeks in the first conversation rather than discovering it in April.

whyPoints.title: Online, which is why the pool is national
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so a family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain chooses from the same specialists as a family in Dubai. Delivery is online everywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India, and we say so rather than burying it.

whyPoints.title: Permit questions answered plainly
whyPoints.description: Tutors hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is free for two years and checkable. We hold no regulator accreditation and claim none: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the ministry regulate schools, not tutoring platforms.

whyPoints.title: Feedback on the student's own work only
whyPoints.description: Where a coursework route exists, a tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and comments on the student's own drafting. Nobody here supplies text or finished assessed work, which is a real boundary in a market where finished coursework is openly sold.

whyPoints.title: A free trial lesson, then a conversation
whyPoints.description: One free trial lesson is booked before any paid block, so the match is tested against the actual specification rather than against a profile. The plan and the cost are discussed after that lesson, because a six-week sprint and a two-year weekly slot are not the same commitment.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the statement of entry. It lists each subject with its awarding organisation, specification code, tier where one applies and component numbers, and it is the only record that settles the question. If it has not been issued yet, check the textbook spine and the year group's curriculum booklet: Pearson International GCSE codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1 or 4CP0, while Cambridge syllabuses are four digits such as 0580 or 0625. One UAE school commonly uses both boards across different departments, so the answer can be Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for maths in the same timetable.

faqs.question: The November series has already started. Is there any point starting a tutor now?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which papers are left. If Paper 1 has been sat and Paper 2 is ten days away, a focused block on the content that sits only in Paper 2, such as organic chemistry in 4CH1 or astrophysics in 4PH1, is a reasonable use of the time, because that content is the most commonly abandoned and the paper is the shorter one. If both papers fall this week, the honest answer is that revision technique and sleep matter more than new teaching, and the better conversation is about the next series and the entry deadline that follows results.

faqs.question: When do Pearson International GCSE entries actually close for a May/June series?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, and the exact date sits with your child's centre rather than with you. Schools lodge entries with Pearson and set their own earlier internal deadline so they can collect decisions, which means the tier for 4MA1 and any coursework route are fixed well before the exam year feels urgent. Pearson publishes key dates and provisional timetables, and those are revised, so the exams officer's deadline is the one to diarise. Late changes attract a fee or are refused outright, which is why the entry window belongs on a parent's calendar.

faqs.question: My son is entered for Foundation tier in 4MA1 and wants a grade 7. Can the tier be changed?
faqs.answer: Only before the entry deadline, and only with the maths department's agreement. Foundation tier in Mathematics A caps the attainable grade several grades below the top of the scale, so the ceiling is set at entry rather than in the exam hall. What moves the conversation is evidence: a full timed Higher tier paper and a full timed Foundation tier paper, both marked against the published criteria, produce two scores and a pattern a head of department will engage with. Raise it early in the autumn term; by February the entry is usually lodged and the question is closed.

faqs.question: Are Edexcel International GCSE sciences tiered the way Cambridge Core and Extended are?
faqs.answer: No. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics, Chemistry and Biology are single tier, graded 9 to 1, with every candidate sitting the same two written papers. Cambridge enters candidates for Core or Extended and adds a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, which Edexcel does not have: experimental skills are assessed inside the written papers instead. Among the subjects UAE families commonly take, Mathematics A is the tiered exception at Edexcel. This is one of the clearest reasons to establish the board before revision starts, because the two structures reward quite different preparation.

faqs.question: Does Edexcel International GCSE still involve coursework, and what may a tutor do with it?
faqs.answer: Most subjects are assessed entirely by written examination, which is a real simplification. Where an internally assessed route exists, such as the coursework option in English Language A, the work must be the student's own and the school declares it as such. A tutor may teach the skill being assessed, explain the criteria in plain language, model a technique on a different text, read a draft and say which criterion is not yet met, and set a schedule. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a paragraph or hand over work close enough to copy.

faqs.question: When will November 2026 International GCSE results reach my child?
faqs.answer: Roughly two months after the papers, going by the pattern of previous series, but confirm the exact date with your centre rather than relying on a pattern. For reference, the previous November series released results to students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Results reach candidates through the school, which is also how any enquiry about results has to be submitted. The useful preparation is agreeing in advance what each possible outcome will mean, because the next entry deadline follows within weeks.

faqs.question: A grade came back one mark under a boundary. Who can ask Pearson to look at it again?
faqs.answer: The centre, not the parent. Schools can request a copy of the script or a review of marking within a published window after results, and they do this routinely when asked promptly. The sequence that works is to request the script copy first, have the subject teacher read it against the mark scheme, and then decide whether a review is worth submitting. A mark can move down as well as up on review, so a request made without seeing the script is a gamble rather than a correction. Act in the first days after results.

faqs.question: Can my daughter resit one Edexcel International GCSE paper, or does she sit the whole subject again?
faqs.answer: The whole subject. At International GCSE no component marks carry forward, so a resit of 4BI1 means both papers again and the new grade replaces nothing automatically; it stands alongside the earlier one on her record. That is different from International AS and A Level, which is unitised and does allow single units to be retaken and banked. The practical effect is that a resit costs a full preparation cycle for the subject, so it is worth the term only where the lost marks were concentrated and diagnosable rather than spread thinly across both papers.

faqs.question: We are moving from a CBSE school into Year 10 Edexcel. What has to be caught up first?
faqs.answer: Question style before content, in most cases. Students arriving from CBSE are frequently ahead on mathematical technique and behind on extended written explanation, because the papers they have sat rewarded recall and accuracy rather than describing, explaining and evaluating. The first repair list is therefore command words, showing method for its own marks, and writing to a mark scheme rather than to a correct answer. Content gaps do exist, most often in the practical-skills questions and in the English anthology work, and a diagnostic paper in each subject sorts the real gaps from the assumed ones within a fortnight.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does one Edexcel International GCSE subject need in the final term?
faqs.answer: One well-used session a week per subject, plus the student's own timed practice, is the pattern that works for most candidates in the final term. Two sessions a week makes sense in the last three weeks for a subject where the diagnostic found content gaps rather than technique gaps, and it stops making sense in the final ten days, when nothing new can be absorbed and the value is in timed rotation. More than that usually means hours are substituting for a plan, and the student is too tired to use them.

faqs.question: Ramadan falls in the middle of our mock season. How should the schedule change?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, and in January rather than in the first week of Ramadan. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which has been pushing it into the mock and pre-exam window. The changes that hold are moving sessions to after Iftar, shortening them from ninety minutes to sixty, and switching the work from new content to review and timed questions, which are less demanding to sustain while fasting. Families who plan this in advance keep their momentum through the month; families who improvise usually lose three or four weeks of the twenty-two they had.

faqs.question: Does an Edexcel International GCSE transcript satisfy UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no lower than grade E or grade 3, and at post-16 one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Most UAE candidates take eight to ten International GCSE subjects, so the count is rarely the obstacle. Equivalency is completed by the family through the official ministry channel; verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae, because a tutoring provider has no role in the process and cannot speed it up.

faqs.question: Do the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons our school runs count towards the Ministry's five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published equivalency rule states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects on the British track, which surprises families who assumed the school's mandatory lessons would count towards the total. They are still required: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed to teach. The point is simply that a student needs five other accredited subjects at the stated grade, so a very light International GCSE subject load deserves checking against the rule in Year 9.

faqs.question: Our school in Fujairah has no Edexcel Further Pure Maths specialist. What are the options?
faqs.answer: This is the clearest case for an online match in the country. Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain sit under the federal Ministry of Education and have the smallest pool of UK-curriculum secondary departments, so a 4PM1 or 4CP0 specialist within driving distance may genuinely not exist. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video, which means the choice is the same list a Dubai family sees rather than whoever is local. Where no specialist in a niche specification is free at the time you ask, we say so and give a realistic date rather than substituting a generalist quietly.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own channels with a stated two working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include school and government or private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold it; it is the one credential a parent can actually verify.

faqs.question: Can my child sit Edexcel International GCSE as a private candidate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an examination centre that accepts external entries, rather than directly with Pearson. The centre lodges the entry, sets its own earlier internal deadline and charges entry and administration fees of its own. Centres cap external numbers and some decline them for particular subjects, especially where practical or internally assessed components are involved, so the search for a centre should start in the same week as the decision to sit. A tutor can prepare a candidate and cannot enter one; only a registered examination centre can do that.

Then one free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video, with a tutor who has taught those codes rather than the subject in general. Lessons run in Gulf Standard Time across all seven emirates, from Dubai and Abu Dhabi to Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain. If no specialist in a niche specification is free when you ask, we will say so and give you a date.

Each profile names the codes they teach, the tier they are strongest on and the hours they hold in Gulf Standard Time, so you can compare on substance before you compare on price.

intro.heading: Why two quotes for the same Edexcel subject can differ by AED 400 an hour
paragraphs: A parent in Mirdif and a parent in Khalifa City can ask for exactly the same thing - one hour a week of Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry for a Year 11 student - and be quoted AED 90 by one provider and AED 480 by another. Neither number is a mistake. They are pricing two different products. The first is supervision: a graduate who worked through the same papers a few years ago, sitting with your child while they attempt questions. The second is instruction: a teacher who has marked against the Pearson mark scheme, knows which command words carry which marks, and arrives with the next six weeks already planned.

Most UAE tutoring pages will not tell you this, because most of them publish no figure at all. Of the six provider pages that rank hardest for International GCSE tuition searches in this market, three show no hourly rate anywhere, and of the remaining three, two quote in US dollars - a currency no family in the Emirates pays a school fee in. The practical consequence is that parents here negotiate blind, and the usual result is paying a specialist rate for supervision, or paying a supervision rate and wondering in May why nothing moved.

This page exists to end the guessing for one specific qualification. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is not interchangeable with Cambridge. The codes are different, the paper counts are different, the tiering decisions are different, and several Edexcel subjects carry a coursework or on-screen component that changes what an hour of tuition is even for. A quote that does not reference your child's code - 4MA1, 4PH1, 4EA1, 4CP0 - is a quote for something generic, and generic is the single most expensive thing you can buy in this market.

The honest answer on value is that tuition is worth funding when there is a diagnosable gap, enough weeks left to close it, and a tutor who can name both. It is poor value when it is bought as reassurance in the last fortnight, when it duplicates something the school already does well, or when it is spread so thin across five subjects that no single weakness gets eight consecutive weeks of attention. Those three failures account for most of the money wasted on tutoring in the Emirates, and none of them are fixed by paying more per hour.

What follows is the arithmetic rather than the argument: a market rate table with its sources and its date, the seven things that genuinely move a quote, a cost view of every major Edexcel code, the calendar counted backwards in both hours and money, and the costs that sit outside a tutor invoice entirely - private candidate entry, a review of marking, Ministry of Education equivalency. Figures on this page were reviewed in October 2026 and carry the source that published them.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Pearson Edexcel runs a connected set of international qualifications, and the stage your child is at decides both the shape of the teaching and the size of the bill. These are the four routes UAE families most often ask about on this page.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before International GCSE begins, assessed internally by the school with optional Pearson tests at the end of Year 9. English, mathematics and science carry progression tests that many UAE schools use to set Year 10 groups, which means a Year 9 result often decides whether a child is put on the Foundation or Higher route for 4MA1.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest place in the whole sequence to buy help, and the least popular. An hour a week in Year 9 at the lower end of the market band does the work that forty hours of Year 11 repair tries to do later. UAE families typically start spending two years after the gap opens, which is the single most expensive habit on this page.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9-1)
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1 rather than A* to G, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers, with a coursework route available in a handful of subjects such as English Language A. Candidates sit either a May/June or a November series. Most subjects run two papers; Science Double Award runs three and awards two grades.
programmes.countryNote: This is where nearly all UAE tutoring money goes, and where it is most often mistimed. Final entries are submitted by the school months before the paper, so the decisions worth paying a tutor to inform - tier, subject count, whether to move a candidate from Core-style supervision to full Higher teaching - have to happen in the autumn term, not after the February mocks.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International A Level
programmes.description: The unitised route after International GCSE: subjects break into units that can be sat across several series rather than in one terminal block, which is the main structural difference families notice when they move up from the linear International GCSE. Grades run A* to E and feed directly into Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track.
programmes.countryNote: Unitisation changes the economics of tuition. Because a unit can be re-sat in a later series, families in the Emirates often fund short, intense blocks aimed at one unit rather than a year-long weekly hour. That is usually better value, provided the re-sit entry deadline is known before the block is booked rather than after.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme (the alternative sixth-form route)
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma that many UAE students move into after Edexcel International GCSEs, with six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessments are marked by the school and moderated by the IB, which is a different assessment culture from a terminal Pearson paper.
programmes.countryNote: The transition cost is real and predictable. A strong grade 8 in 4MA1 Higher does not automatically carry into Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, because proof, modelling and the toolkit of mathematical investigation are taught differently. Families who budget six to ten hours across the first Diploma term spend less overall than those who wait for the first internal assessment to go wrong.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Edexcel prices by specification, not by subject name. The code tells a tutor the paper count, the weighting split, the tier decision and where the marks leak. These are the codes UAE families most often ask about, with the part of each that actually consumes paid hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of two hours, 100 marks each, fifty per cent apiece. Foundation covers grades 5 to 1 and Higher covers 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. The tier decision matters more than any topic: a Foundation candidate never meets several Higher-only topics, so tuition aimed at a grade 7 is wasted if the entry says Foundation.

subjects.name: Mathematics B (4MB1)
subjects.description: Two papers with the longer one carrying the larger share of the marks, and no tier to fall back on. Algebraic manipulation and structured proof are heavier than in Mathematics A. Schools usually enter their strongest sets. Hours go on fluency and on writing an argument that earns method marks rather than circling an answer.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.levels: Untiered, sat alongside a main maths entry
subjects.description: Two papers of two hours at fifty per cent each, covering calculus, series, matrices and coordinate geometry well beyond the standard International GCSE. Most UAE timetables do not teach it in full, so it is the most common reason a family funds a second weekly hour. Scarcity pushes the rate above the normal band.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Paper 1 runs two hours for 110 marks, roughly sixty-one per cent of the grade; Paper 2 runs an hour and a quarter for 70 marks. There is no separate practical exam, so experimental method is examined in writing. Marks leak on equation recall, unit conversion and the six-mark questions that ask for a method rather than a result.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: The same two-paper split as Physics, with Paper 2 concentrating the organic chemistry and the quantitative work. Moles arithmetic is where a mid-grade candidate loses most, followed by electrolysis and rates. A tutor who sets a timed mole-calculation drill every week does more for the grade than one who re-explains the periodic table.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Two papers on the same weighting pattern as the other sciences. The content is learnable, which is exactly why marks go missing: extended-answer questions reward precise command-word responses, and vague answers to explain or describe score zero. Paid hours are best spent marking written answers against the mark scheme, not re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Science (Double Award) (4SD0)
subjects.description: One paper per science, awarded as two International GCSE grades. It is the quiet budget trap on this page: three syllabuses sit behind one timetable slot, so a family funding one hour a week is funding twenty minutes per science. Families who get value from it pick the weakest of the three and work only on that for a term.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.levels: Written papers, or a coursework route
subjects.description: Paper 1 handles non-fiction reading and transactional writing; the second component covers poetry and prose with an alternative coursework route the school chooses, not the parent. Marking time is what makes this subject expensive to tutor properly: every piece has to be read before it can be taught, so an hour of lesson implies real work outside it.

subjects.name: English Literature (4ET1)
subjects.levels: Anthology, unseen poetry, prose and drama
subjects.description: Quotation recall under closed-book conditions plus comparative structure, which is a skill rather than a body of knowledge. Hours spent summarising plot are hours wasted. The productive use of paid time is building four or five transferable argument frames and then testing them against unseen poetry under a clock.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0)
subjects.levels: Written principles plus an on-screen paper
subjects.description: Paper 1 is written theory; the second component is a long on-screen programming paper sat at a computer. That single fact changes the tutor market: the person teaching it has to be able to code fluently in the school's chosen language as well as teach, and that combination is thin on the ground in the Emirates, so the rate sits above the band.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: Microeconomics and business economics in one paper, macroeconomics and the global economy in the other. Diagram accuracy and evaluation marks decide the grade, and neither is revisable from a textbook. Paid hours earn their keep on labelled diagrams drawn under time pressure and on the structure of an evaluative paragraph.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with application marks that require the candidate to use the business in front of them rather than a memorised example. UAE students who have grown up around family businesses often reason well and still score poorly, because they answer from experience instead of from the stimulus material. That is a teachable fix inside a term.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: What the same Edexcel hour costs across the seven emirates
edexcel-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Rates in this market are partly a function of geography: how many subject teachers live within driving distance, and how long that drive takes at five in the afternoon. Delivering over video removes the second variable entirely, which is why the bands below converge once travel comes out of the fee.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest British-curriculum pool in the country - 227 private schools in 2024-25 with 37 per cent of enrolments on a UK curriculum. Depth is why Dubai quotes span the whole AED 45 to 650 range, and why a Foundation-tier maths hour and a 4PM1 hour are priced nothing like each other here.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Schools licensed by ADEK, with the British-curriculum cluster spread between the Corniche, Al Bateen, Khalifa City and Al Raha. A visiting tutor crossing from the islands to Khalifa City at 5pm is charging for roughly ninety minutes of road, which is most of the gap between the online and in-home bands.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a far smaller resident pool of International GCSE subject specialists. Families here feel the scarcity premium first on sciences and Further Pure Mathematics. Over video the Al Ain rate is the Dubai rate, because the only thing distance was ever pricing was petrol and traffic.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves fees, curricula and assessment methods in the emirate. Many Sharjah families work in Dubai, so evening slots are tight; the practical saving is a 7pm video session that needs no return trip across the Al Ittihad corridor.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The resident specialist pool is thin enough that in-home quotes often include a surcharge for the drive up from Dubai. Removing the drive is the whole argument for video in the northern emirates, and it is a cost argument before it is an education one.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education, and the emirate where a parent is least likely to find a resident Edexcel Chemistry teacher at all. Families here are typically choosing between a generalist who can attend and a specialist who cannot. Video makes that a false choice.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the emirate Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees and curricula. The school pool is small and concentrated, so a single subject gap can go unmet for a whole term locally. Scheduling around the longer school run matters more here than the hourly rate does.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and the clearest illustration of why travel dominates in-home pricing: a tutor driving from Dubai is committing four hours to the road around a one-hour lesson. That is the top of the AED 180-500 band before a word has been taught.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai - British-curriculum schools entering Pearson papers
schoolClusters.note: Schools in this group commonly split their entries between Pearson Edexcel and Cambridge by department, so a single student can sit 4MA1 for maths and a Cambridge code for a science. Ask the exams officer for the statement of entry rather than assuming the school is a one-board school, because the code decides the tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from taking paid private tuition with students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct to the same effect. That rules out the cheapest-looking option in this cluster, which is your child's own classroom teacher.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Fewer schools means fewer teaching sets per subject, so a child who needs Higher-tier mathematics in a school that runs one Higher set has no internal alternative if the fit is wrong. This is the cluster where families most often fund a weekly hour as a substitute for a second set rather than as remediation.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the UAE Edexcel ecosystem and because families recognise them; no affiliation, endorsement or relationship with any school or school group is implied.
edexcel-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families in the Emirates buy Edexcel help, priced differently because they do different jobs. All of them are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: The weekly hour against one specification code
modes.description: One subject, one code, one hour a week through the academic year, with the topic order taken from the Pearson specification rather than from the school's sequence. This is the lowest-cost route to a grade change because it spreads the work across enough weeks for practice to compound, and because weekly marking catches a misconception before it becomes a habit.
bullets: Priced per hour, no block commitment before the trial lesson
Written work marked against the published mark scheme between sessions
Topic order follows the specification, so school gaps surface early
Best value from September of Year 10 or Year 11 onwards

modes.title: The paper sprint in the final ten to twelve weeks
modes.description: A short, dense block aimed at technique rather than content: timed sections, command-word discipline, and the two or three topics a mock showed were recoverable. It costs more per week than the weekly hour and less in total, and it is the right purchase once final entries are locked and the tier can no longer change.
bullets: Two sessions a week, each built around a timed paper section
Explicit work on the command words Pearson uses in each subject
A deliberately short topic list - everything else is triaged out
Scheduled around the mock window, not around convenience

modes.title: Coursework and practical-skills clinic
modes.description: For the Edexcel components that are not a conventional written paper: the English Language A coursework route, the on-screen programming component in Computer Science, and the experimental-method questions that stand in for a practical exam in the sciences. The tutor teaches the skill the task assesses and gives feedback on work the student has already done.
bullets: Teaching and feedback only - submitted words must be the student's own
Experimental method taught through method design and data questions
Programming taught by live screen-share in the school's language
School deadlines drive the sessions, not the other way round

modes.title: Holiday and post-results blocks
modes.description: The UAE academic calendar leaves three usable windows - the winter break, the long summer, and the fortnight after results arrive. Hours bought in these windows are cheaper in opportunity cost because nothing competes with them, and they are the only time a full syllabus repair is realistic rather than aspirational.
bullets: Four to six consecutive days rather than scattered single hours
Winter break used for the mock, summer for the next year's foundations
Post-results sessions begin with the decision, not with teaching
Sessions time-shifted to post-Iftar hours through Ramadan

sections.heading: What an Edexcel IGCSE tutor costs in the UAE, with the sources attached
paragraphs: An Edexcel IGCSE tutor in the UAE is quoted between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour as of October 2026. A qualified subject teacher working one-to-one over video sits at AED 150 to AED 300. A visiting in-home tutor sits at AED 180 to AED 500, because travel time is paid time. A former examiner or premium brand sits above AED 500. Those four sentences are more pricing information than most provider pages in this market publish at all.

The bands come from two places: provider rate cards published openly and surveyed in October 2026, and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, which is the only independent compilation of UAE tutoring rates we could verify. They are market figures. They are not an IB Gram price list, and nobody should read a range as a quote - the point of publishing them is so that you can tell whether the number you have been given is normal, high or implausibly low for what is being promised.

Monthly packages behave differently from hourly rates and are worth understanding separately. Packages seen in this market run at about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. On a per-hour basis the online package is competitive and the in-home package is not, which is almost entirely the cost of a car. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

One warning about the bottom of the range. A tutor charging AED 45 an hour is not necessarily bad, but they are almost certainly not reading your child's work between sessions, because nobody can mark a 110-mark Physics paper against a mark scheme for that money. If marking matters to you - and for 4BI1 and 4EA1 it is the single highest-yield activity available - then the rate you are comparing has to include it explicitly, or you are comparing two different products again.

sections.heading: The seven things that actually move an Edexcel quote
paragraphs: Price in this market is not a mystery, it is a sum. Seven variables account for almost every quote you will be given, and six of them are things you control or at least know in advance. Ask a provider which of the seven they are pricing and the conversation stops being about brand and starts being about the work.

Tier sits at the top because it changes the content, not just the target. A Foundation-tier entry for Mathematics A caps the grade at 5, so an hour aimed at a 7 for a Foundation candidate is an hour spent on topics they will not be asked about. Scarcity sits second: Further Pure Mathematics and the on-screen Computer Science component have a thin regional teaching pool, and thin pools price up regardless of where you look.

Time is the variable parents underestimate most. Eight weeks before a paper, the cheap slots and the strong tutors are already committed, so late demand buys from a smaller, pricier pool - and buys fewer usable weeks with it. The fourth and fifth variables, format and marking, are where the biggest hidden differences live: travel inside a fee can be a third of the price, and whether somebody reads a timed paper between sessions can double the real work behind a stated hour.

The last two are mundane and still worth asking about. Time of day concentrates almost all UAE demand between 5pm and 8pm on school nights, which is exactly why weekend-morning and holiday hours are easier to book and often cheaper. And session count per subject matters: two subjects at one hour each is a different purchase from one subject at two hours, and the second usually produces a grade change sooner.
bullets: Ask which tier the entry actually is before agreeing a target grade
Ask whether written work is marked between sessions, and by whom
Ask what the travel component of an in-home quote is worth per hour
Ask whether a weekend or holiday slot changes the rate

sections.heading: Priced by specification code, not by subject name
paragraphs: Pearson publishes its International GCSEs as coded specifications, and the code is the most useful four characters in this entire conversation. It tells a tutor the paper count, the weighting split, whether a tier decision exists, and whether a component is written, coursework or on-screen. A provider who quotes for International GCSE Physics without asking whether it is 4PH1 or a double-award component is quoting for a subject they have not yet identified.

The practical test is simple. Before you pay anything, get the statement of entry from the school's exams officer, or at minimum the subject code list. Then ask the prospective tutor what Paper 2 of that code contains and how it is weighted. A specialist answers in one sentence. Somebody who has worked from generic British GCSE material will answer in generalities, and generalities are what you are trying not to buy at AED 300 an hour.

Codes also explain price differences that otherwise look arbitrary. The sciences at 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 share a two-paper structure where the first paper carries around sixty-one per cent of the marks over two hours and the second around thirty-nine per cent in an hour and a quarter. No separate practical exam exists, so experimental method is examined in writing - which is teachable over video in a way a laboratory is not, and which is one of the few places where the online format is straightforwardly better value rather than merely equivalent.

Two codes deserve a specific warning. Science Double Award, 4SD0, puts three sciences behind one entry and awards two grades, so an hour a week is twenty minutes per science and almost always the wrong shape of purchase. And Computer Science, 4CP0, carries a long on-screen programming component, which means the tutor must code fluently in the school's language as well as teach - a combination scarce enough in the Emirates that the rate sits above the standard band. Always confirm the current structure of any code on qualifications.pearson.com before planning hours around it.

sections.heading: Mathematics A, Mathematics B or Further Pure: the route choice that moves the bill most
paragraphs: Of every decision on this page, the maths route changes the budget most and gets the least attention. Pearson offers three distinct maths qualifications at International GCSE level, they are not ranked versions of each other, and the one a child is entered for determines both the grade ceiling and the kind of teaching an hour can usefully contain.

Mathematics A, 4MA1, is the common route and the only tiered one. Foundation covers grades 5 down to 1; Higher covers 9 down to 4 with an allowed 3. That cap is the single most expensive misunderstanding in UAE tutoring, because a family can spend a full year funding work towards a grade 7 that the entry makes impossible. The tier is a school decision, it is reviewable in the autumn term, and it is the first thing a tutor should ask about rather than the last.

Mathematics B, 4MB1, is untiered, so the whole 9 to 1 range sits on one route with no safety net below. It leans harder on algebraic manipulation and on structured proof, and schools generally reserve it for stronger sets. Hours here are spent differently from 4MA1: less topic repair, more fluency and more attention to writing an argument a marker can follow and award method marks to.

Further Pure Mathematics, 4PM1, sits alongside a main maths entry rather than replacing it, and covers calculus, series, matrices and coordinate geometry. Most UAE schools cannot timetable it fully, which is why it is the most common reason a family funds a second weekly hour and why its rate sits above the ordinary band. For a student heading towards engineering or mathematics at university it is usually money well spent; for a student who still loses marks on 4MA1 algebra it is money spent in the wrong order.

sections.heading: What a single paid hour should actually produce
paragraphs: Value in tutoring is measurable, and the unit is not satisfaction. By the end of a first paid hour on an Edexcel subject you should be able to see four things: a named list of the topics that are costing marks, the specification code and tier confirmed out loud, a piece of the student's own written work annotated against the mark scheme, and a plan for the next three sessions with the order explained. If an hour produces only the feeling that it went well, you bought reassurance.

By the end of a month - four hours, somewhere between AED 600 and AED 1,200 at the mid-market band - the test changes. There should be at least one timed section attempted under exam conditions and marked, a visible change in how the student answers a command word such as explain or calculate, and a shorter list of weak topics than the one you started with. A list that has not shortened after four hours is information: either the diagnosis was wrong or the match is wrong, and both are worth acting on quickly.

The cost-per-mark view is more useful than cost-per-hour, even though nobody advertises it. Twelve hours spread across one term on one subject, at AED 200 an hour, is AED 2,400 aimed at a specific band of recoverable marks. The same AED 2,400 spread over four subjects in the last fortnight buys three hours each, which is not enough to change how anyone answers anything. The arithmetic is unglamorous and it is the whole argument for concentration over coverage.

There is a point at which the right decision is to stop paying. If two consecutive marked papers show no movement on the topics the plan named, if sessions are being filled with content the school has already taught well, or if the student cannot say what the last session was about, the hours are not working. A provider worth using will raise that before you do, and will say plainly when a weekly hour has done its job and a short sprint nearer the paper is the better remaining purchase.
bullets: After one hour: a named topic list, the code and tier confirmed, work annotated

sections.heading: The Pearson calendar counted backwards in hours and money
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a date copied from a page like this one.

What this means financially is that the value of an hour decays, and not smoothly. Three decisions stop being available at different moments: the tier stops being changeable once the school submits final entries, the subject count stops being changeable at the same moment, and after that only technique and topic triage remain. Money spent before those gates can change what is sat; money spent after can only change how it is answered. Both are worth spending - but confusing the two is how families end up disappointed by a tutor who was never able to affect the thing they cared about.

The second timing fact worth planning around is the gap between the last paper and results day, which for the June 2026 series was roughly eleven weeks. That gap is dead time for tuition and live time for decisions, and the fortnight after results is the single most productive block in the whole year: a review of marking has a deadline, a November entry has a deadline, and both are better decided with two or three paid hours of analysis than with a family argument.

Ramadan deserves explicit planning rather than improvisation, because in recent years it has sat across the UAE mock window. Schools shorten the day, energy drops in the afternoon, and the honest answer is that the usual 5pm slot does not work. Families who move sessions to post-Iftar hours for the month keep their momentum; families who simply cancel four weeks lose a tenth of a year's tuition at precisely the point when a mock result is meant to be driving the plan.

sections.heading: Online, visiting, group or centre: the four formats compared on cost
paragraphs: This is the comparison UAE parents search for most and get answered least honestly, usually because the page answering it sells only one of the four. The useful version prices each format against the thing it is actually good at, and states plainly what it gives up.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address. That is a limit and it is also the argument: a family in Al Zahia or Fujairah gets the specialist who teaches 4CP0 or 4PM1 rather than whichever generalist can reach the gate by five o'clock. On the cost side, no travel is being paid for, and a 5pm session starts at 5pm whether the student is in Jumeirah or Umm Al Quwain.

A visiting tutor buys presence in the room, which genuinely helps some students - the ones who need a book physically taken off them and a page pointed at. It costs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour in this market with travel inside the fee, the tutor pool shrinks to whoever can reach your address, and in practice cancellations cluster on the days the roads do not cooperate. Small groups and centre classes cut the per-hour price and hand the pace to the group, which works for coverage and fails for a specific weakness.

There is no format that is best for everyone, and anyone who says otherwise is describing their own inventory. The question worth asking is narrower: for this code, this tier and this number of remaining weeks, which format puts the right teacher in front of the student for the most hours per dirham? For scarce Edexcel codes in the northern emirates, that answer is almost always video. For a Year 10 student who needs supervision more than instruction, a group class may be the honest recommendation even though it is not what we sell.

sections.heading: The Edexcel costs that sit outside a tutor's invoice
paragraphs: Tuition is rarely the only line item, and the ones families miss are the ones with deadlines attached. Four sit around a Pearson entry: the entry itself if the candidate is private rather than school-registered, a review of marking after results, a re-sit entry in a later series, and Ministry of Education equivalency for the certificate once it exists.

Private candidate entry is the first surprise. A student not entered through their own school has to find a centre that accepts external candidates, and those centres set their own administrative charges on top of the Pearson entry fee. There is no central published figure for the UAE, so the only reliable step is to ask the centre for its fee list in writing, along with its own internal deadline, which always sits before Pearson's. Centres also fill up, and in this market a late private entry can fail on capacity rather than on money.

A review of marking carries an administrative fee set by the board and is requested through the centre, not by the family directly, with a deadline measured in weeks after results rather than months. That is the real cost of the post-results fortnight: not the fee, but the fact that a decision has to be made quickly and well. Two or three paid hours spent reading the paper and the grade against the mark scheme is a rational purchase at that moment, and it is cheaper than a re-sit entered in panic.

Equivalency is the one families discover latest. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects at International GCSE or GCSE with grades of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade - and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competing provider page states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. Equivalency is a process the family completes with the Ministry, not something a tutoring provider performs, and no tutoring is required for it.
