sections.heading: What money cannot buy: the honesty line on Edexcel components
paragraphs: Some Edexcel subjects carry components that are not a terminal written paper: the coursework route in English Language A, the on-screen programming paper in Computer Science, and the experimental-method questions that stand in for a practical exam in the sciences. Those are exactly the components where a market in finished work exists, and where parents are occasionally offered something that would end their child's entry rather than improve it.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, model an equivalent example that is not the task itself, question a draft the student has already made, and give feedback the student then acts on alone. A tutor may not supply sentences, paragraphs, code or data for submission. Submitted material has to be the student's own, and board malpractice rules treat the student as responsible for it regardless of who was paid.

The test we apply is whether a session could be described out loud to the school's exams officer without anyone becoming uncomfortable. Teaching paragraph structure before a coursework piece passes. Reading a draft and saying which paragraph does not answer the question passes. Dictating a replacement paragraph does not, and neither does debugging a student's on-screen programming submission to the point where the work is no longer theirs. Any provider in this market offering a finished piece of assessed work for a fee is selling an entry cancellation with a lesson attached.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because it is the clearest difference between providers in this SERP. One operation found during research sells completed internal assessments outright. Pages that quietly imply the same thing use phrases such as help with your submission and done-for-you. A provider that writes the boundary down, as this paragraph does, is a provider you can hold to it - and that is worth more than any claim about quality that nobody can check.

sections.heading: Regulators, mandatory UAE subjects and what each does to a tutoring budget
paragraphs: Which authority oversees your child's school changes what you can ask for, what is public, and occasionally who is allowed to teach your child privately. In Dubai that is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

The budget consequence runs through inspection reports, which are published and which almost nobody reads before buying tuition. A school rated strongly in mathematics and weakly in a science is telling you where a paid hour will and will not add value. Buying a weekly hour in the department your school does best is the most common avoidable expense in this market, and the report is free.

There is also a rule that removes the cheapest-looking option from the table. ADEK professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 carries a code of conduct to the same effect. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor you pay directly whether they hold it.

Finally, the subjects your Edexcel fees do not cover. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools need prior Ministry permission to use different or additional content. That last rule is why honest tutoring in these subjects follows the school's own materials rather than importing a syllabus of its own.

process.title: Send two documents before anything is quoted
process.description: The statement of entry or subject code list, and the most recent marked paper or report. Those two documents turn a generic enquiry into a specific one: they confirm the Edexcel code, the tier, the series and the current standard, which between them determine the kind of tutor needed and the honest number of hours.

process.title: A trial lesson that produces a diagnosis
process.description: One session, used as a diagnostic rather than a sales call. The student attempts questions from their own specification while the tutor identifies what is actually costing marks. You should finish it holding a named topic list and a view on the tier, which is the first thing worth paying for and the first thing most providers skip.

process.title: A written plan with hours and cost attached
process.description: Before any block is agreed: topic order, number of hours, what is marked between sessions, and the total. Written plans make tutoring comparable and arguable, which is the point. If a provider will not put an hour count against a target, the target is decoration rather than a plan.

process.title: Weekly teaching with work marked between sessions
process.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's written work annotated against the published mark scheme between them. Marking is where most of the real value sits, and it is the first thing cut by a rate too low to pay for the reading it requires.

process.title: Two scheduled reviews, pinned to real dates
process.description: One after the mock window, one before the school submits final entries, because those are the two moments when the plan can still change what is sat rather than only how it is answered. Each review ends with a decision: continue, concentrate on fewer topics, change the format, or stop.

whyPoints.title: The market rate is published here, with its date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the source that published it and the month it was surveyed, because three of the six provider pages ranking for this search publish no rate at all. You can tell from this page whether a quote you have been given is normal for the Emirates, which is the minimum a parent needs.

whyPoints.title: Teaching from the code, not from a generic syllabus
whyPoints.description: 4MA1 is not 4MB1, and Science Double Award is not three single sciences. Tutors work from the Pearson specification the student is entered for, which is why the first question is always about the statement of entry rather than about a year group or a target grade.

whyPoints.title: Online because the specialist matters more than the postcode
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video. Home visits are offered only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For scarce codes such as Further Pure Mathematics or the on-screen Computer Science paper, that is the difference between the right teacher and the nearest available one.

whyPoints.title: The academic honesty boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and feedback on work the student has already done. No supplied sentences, paragraphs, code or data for submission. The line is stated on the page so it can be held to, which is more useful than an unverifiable claim about quality.

whyPoints.title: What happens when nobody is free is stated too
whyPoints.description: If no specialist covers a code and tier at the hour you want, you are told that rather than offered a generalist at a specialist price. Where the best available match sits outside the UAE, that is disclosed before the first session, with the time zone written into the schedule.

whyPoints.title: Nothing here is a guarantee, and no statistic is invented
whyPoints.description: No promised grade, no claimed pass rate, no self-published star rating, and no claim of approval or partnership with any board or authority. The figures are market rates with sources, and the regulatory facts carry the government page they came from.

faqs.question: What is the going hourly rate for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE tuition in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: Surveyed in October 2026, quotes in this market run from AED 45 to AED 650 an hour. A qualified subject teacher working one-to-one over video sits at AED 150 to AED 300. A visiting in-home tutor sits at AED 180 to AED 500, because travel time is inside the fee. Former examiners and premium brands sit above AED 500. Those bands come from published provider rate cards and from the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list, and the right use of them is to judge whether a quote you have been given is normal for what it promises.

faqs.question: Why does a Physics specialist for 4PH1 quote more than one for English Language 4EA1?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, mostly. The regional pool of teachers who can handle the full Physics specification, including the experimental-method questions that replace a practical exam, is smaller than the pool who can teach English Language, so the hour is bid up. The counter-point is marking load: a 4EA1 hour implies real reading time outside the session, because every piece of writing has to be read before it can be taught. A rate that looks lower per hour is not automatically cheaper per mark once you ask which quote includes work annotated against the mark scheme between sessions.

faqs.question: Is Mathematics Specification A cheaper to tutor than Specification B?
faqs.answer: Usually, and for a structural reason rather than a quality one. Mathematics A is the common route and is tiered, so most tutors in the market know it and the supply is deep. Mathematics B is untiered, carries heavier algebraic manipulation and structured proof, and is typically entered by stronger sets, so fewer tutors offer it confidently. Expect Specification B quotes nearer the upper half of the band. The more important question is which one your child is actually entered for, because planning hours for the wrong specification wastes every dirham spent regardless of the rate.

faqs.question: Our school mentioned units rather than papers. Does that change what we should budget?
faqs.answer: It usually means your child has moved up to International A Level, which is unitised: subjects break into units that can be sat across more than one series rather than in a single terminal block. That changes the shape of sensible spending. Instead of a year-long weekly hour, families often fund a short intense block aimed at one unit, then stop. It is generally better value, with one condition: find out the entry deadline for the next available series before booking the block, not after, because a block timed for a series the school has not entered is money spent on nothing.

faqs.question: Pearson runs a November series as well as May and June. Which is cheaper to prepare for?
faqs.answer: Preparation for the November series is often cheaper in practice, because demand is thinner and the strong tutors are less fully committed than they are in the spring rush. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The trade-off is teaching time: a November candidate has the summer in the middle of their run-up, which suits a disciplined student and undoes a disorganised one. Check the live timetable on the Pearson support pages before planning anything around either series.

faqs.question: We can fund two subjects, not five. Which Edexcel codes repay the hours fastest?
faqs.answer: Pick by recoverable marks, not by weakest grade. Mathematics A rewards concentrated work quickly because its topics are discrete and testable, so a term of focused hours usually shows on a paper. The sciences respond well where the loss is traceable to one mechanism, such as moles arithmetic in 4CH1. The slowest returns come from English Literature, where the gain is a skill built over months. Two subjects with eight consecutive weeks each beats five subjects with three hours each, every time, and that is the whole argument for choosing rather than spreading.

faqs.question: What does the on-screen programming paper in Computer Science 4CP0 do to the cost of tuition?
faqs.answer: It raises it, because the component demands a tutor who can write working code fluently in the school's chosen language as well as teach a syllabus. That combination is thin on the ground in the Emirates, so quotes sit above the ordinary band and availability is tighter than for other subjects. It is also the clearest case for live video rather than a visiting tutor: screen-sharing an editor while a student writes and debugs their own program is a better teaching tool than sitting beside one laptop, and it costs no travel.

faqs.question: Our son is entered for Foundation tier in maths. Is that a reason to spend less?
faqs.answer: It is a reason to spend differently. Foundation tier in Mathematics A caps the award at grade 5, so hours aimed at a 7 are hours spent on topics he will not be asked about. Two sensible options exist. Fund a smaller number of hours squarely inside the Foundation content and target the top of that range, or raise the tier with the school in the autumn term, while entries can still change, and then fund the Higher content properly. What makes no sense is paying specialist rates for Higher teaching against an entry that caps the result.

faqs.question: We were quoted a monthly figure rather than an hourly one. What should the invoice itemise?
faqs.answer: Four things: the number of sessions, the length of each, whether written work is marked between them, and what happens to an unused session. Monthly packages in this market run at about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, so the per-hour maths is easy once the session count is explicit. Ask whether the figure includes VAT as quoted, and get the answer in writing. A package that does not state its session length is not a price, it is a deposit.

faqs.question: What will the exam itself cost if our daughter sits Edexcel papers as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: More than the board fee, and it is not published centrally for the UAE. A candidate not entered through her own school needs a centre that accepts external candidates, and those centres set their own administrative charges on top of the Pearson entry fee. Ask the centre for its fee list in writing, together with its internal deadline, which always falls before the board deadline. Capacity matters as much as cost here: popular centres fill, and a late private entry can fail on space rather than on money. Start the conversation a full series ahead.

faqs.question: A grade came back one mark under a boundary. What can be done and how fast?
faqs.answer: A review of marking is requested through the centre rather than by the family, carries an administrative fee set by the board, and runs on a deadline measured in weeks after results day rather than months. So the sequence is: get the paper and the mark breakdown, read them against the mark scheme, and decide quickly. Two or three paid hours of analysis at that moment is a rational purchase, because it tells you whether a review is plausible or whether an entry in the next series is the better use of the same money.

faqs.question: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 came up when we asked about permits. What does it mean for us?
faqs.answer: It introduced the UAE private tuition work permit, issued by MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible holders include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals providing private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. For a parent paying an individual directly, the practical step is simply to ask whether they hold it. The permit is permission to charge, not a teaching qualification, and the two should not be confused.

faqs.question: Our son's English coursework folder is due next week. What are we allowed to pay a tutor to do with it?
faqs.answer: Teach the skill it assesses, model an equivalent example that is not his task, question the draft he has already made, and give feedback he then acts on alone. Not supply sentences, paragraphs or structure for submission. The useful test is whether the session could be described out loud to the school's exams officer without discomfort. Reading a draft and saying which paragraph fails to answer the question passes that test. Dictating a replacement paragraph does not, and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student under board malpractice rules, whoever was paid.

faqs.question: We asked for a tutor to come to our villa in Dubai. What are we actually buying instead?
faqs.answer: One-to-one tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram offers home visits only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. The cost case for that is straightforward: an in-home hour in this market runs AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the fee, and the pool shrinks to whoever can reach your gate by five o'clock. Over video the same money buys the specialist who teaches your child's exact Edexcel code, and a 5pm session starts at 5pm rather than whenever Sheikh Zayed Road allows.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education add to our tutoring bill if the Ministry does not count them?
faqs.answer: They are separate questions. For British-track equivalency, the Ministry of Education counts five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not among the five. They are still mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, so they affect the school report and the timetable. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects and sets instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools need prior Ministry permission to use different content, so honest support follows the school's own materials.

faqs.question: Nobody covers Accounting at the hour we want. What happens then?
faqs.answer: You are told, before any money changes hands. Scarce codes in this market include Accounting, Further Pure Mathematics and the on-screen Computer Science component, and the honest answer when no specialist holds your slot is a choice: wait for an opening, shift the session to a weekend morning where availability is better, or accept a match based outside the UAE with the time zone written into the schedule. What should not happen is a generalist being presented at a specialist rate, which is how most disappointing tutoring in the Emirates starts.

faqs.question: How do we know after a month whether the money is working?
faqs.answer: Check three things rather than asking how it is going. First, has at least one timed section been attempted under exam conditions and marked against the mark scheme? Second, has the list of weak topics got shorter, with a reason for each removal? Third, can your child say what the last session was about without prompting? Four hours at the mid-market band is AED 600 to AED 1,200. If none of those three has moved, the diagnosis or the match is wrong, and the right response is to change one of them rather than to buy more hours.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change what we pay for in a month?
faqs.answer: It changes when sessions happen, not what they cost. Ramadan has recently fallen across the UAE mock window, schools shorten the day, and the usual 5pm slot stops working for most families. Moving sessions to post-Iftar hours keeps the plan intact for the month; cancelling four weeks removes roughly a tenth of a year's tuition at exactly the point where a mock result is meant to be driving decisions. Agree the shifted timetable before the month begins rather than renegotiating it weekly, and keep the marking cycle running even if the lesson count drops.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code and the number of weeks, not with a price
edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Two pieces of information decide almost everything on this page: the Pearson Edexcel specification code your child is entered for, and how many weeks remain before the paper. With those, an honest hour count and an honest cost follow in one conversation. Send the statement of entry and the most recent marked paper, take a trial lesson used as a diagnosis rather than a sales call, and read the written plan before agreeing to a block. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The figures on this page were reviewed in October 2026 and each carries the source that published it.

evening-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the Diploma subjects UAE families book most often into an evening slot: both mathematics routes, the three sciences on the guides first examined in 2025, Economics and English A. Each teaches one subject at one level on live video, and each holds a slot that belongs to the student for the term rather than moving week to week.

intro.heading: The evening slot is the real constraint, not the subject
paragraphs: Parents rarely look for an evening IB tutor in the UAE because evenings are convenient. They look because the evening is the only time left. School here ends in the early afternoon, the bus adds another thirty or forty minutes, and by the time a bag is open on the kitchen table it is past four. What remains is a window of roughly two and a half hours before dinner, homework and a bedtime that still has to leave eight hours of sleep ahead of a seven o'clock start. One subject fits inside that window. Occasionally two halves of two subjects fit. Nothing else does, and pretending otherwise is how families end up paying for hours that are taught to a tired child.

That window is also the only part of the week a family controls. The school owns the day. The IB coordinator owns the internal deadlines. The board owns the exam dates. The evening belongs to you, and there are five of them in a UAE school week, because most private schools in the Emirates run Monday to Friday, which makes Sunday through Thursday the school nights. Multiply five by the thirty-odd teaching weeks between September and a May session and the number stops feeling infinite. Subtract mocks, Ramadan, Eid al-Fitr, two term breaks and the fortnight when no one concentrates on anything, and the usable total for one subject at one evening a week lands closer to twenty-six.

This page is therefore built as a countdown rather than a pitch. Every section answers a timing question: what genuinely fits inside one evening, how many evenings are left, which ones the school has already claimed, where Ramadan moves them, what an evening hour costs in this market, and what a tutor is allowed to say on the evening before an Internal Assessment is uploaded. Subject detail is here too, including component weightings and the places Higher Level marks go missing. It is organised by when to fix a thing rather than by what the thing is, because a Diploma parent in February needs a different answer from the same parent in September.

All of it happens on live video, one-to-one. IB Gram does not send anyone to an address in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah or anywhere else in the Emirates; visiting tuition is a service the platform runs only in India. On a school-night evening slot that turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise. A visiting tutor costs the family thirty to sixty minutes of someone else's drive time, priced inside the hour, and narrows the choice of teacher to whoever can reach your district by six o'clock. Online, an IB Higher Level specialist is chosen for the subject and the level, not for a postcode and a parking space.

One note on dates before the countdown starts. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so this page prints no May session date and no results date; those come from your child's coordinator or from ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson publish theirs, so where a real calendar date is useful, it is one of theirs with the source named. Everything else here is counted in weeks before your child's first paper, which is the number that decides what an evening is for and the one a coordinator can confirm in a single email.

evening-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run in UAE schools, and each makes a different claim on an evening. A Primary Years evening is short and early. A Middle Years evening is usually about criterion letters nobody has explained to the family. A Diploma evening in the second year is a timed-paper evening. The core, meanwhile, has deadlines that all arrive before the examinations do.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme has no external examinations, which means an evening session is diagnostic rather than remedial. Forty to forty-five minutes is the ceiling for a child of eight or nine after a full school day; past that, attention is gone and the money is wasted. A productive PYP evening does one thing: a single reading strategy, a single number operation, or one stage of the Exhibition inquiry, modelled by the tutor and then practised by the child while the tutor watches and says very little.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates the PYP sits alongside Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, which KHDA requires in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. That matters to an evening plan because those lessons carry homework of their own. Families who book a 4.30pm slot for English or mathematics often find the Arabic worksheet is the thing actually causing tears, and the honest answer is to move the hour.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years reporting runs on four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and the conversion from those thirty-two marks to the 1-7 grade on a report card is set by grade boundaries the school applies. Most families booking an MYP evening session have been told a child is at 4 in Criterion C and have no idea what Criterion C assesses. One evening spent reading the criterion descriptors with the student is worth three spent on content, because it tells you which half of the problem is knowledge and which half is presentation.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 in a UAE school is also the year the Diploma choice gets made, and the two mathematics routes diverge there. A student heading for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level needs algebraic fluency built in Years 9 and 10, not in the first term of DP1. Evening hours spent in MYP 4 and 5 are cheaper than the same hours bought in a panic eighteen months later, and the slot is easier to get.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, plus the core. In DP1 an evening is for building syllabus content and establishing a working method. In DP2 an evening is for timed questions and the feedback that follows them, because by then the content exists in a file somewhere and the lost marks come from timing, command terms and working that an examiner cannot follow. A DP2 evening that does not involve a pen moving under time pressure is usually a comfortable hour that changes nothing.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, which is why the countdown table on this page is built around it. A small number of UAE candidates sit November, usually retakes or students who joined the system late, and their calendar is shifted by roughly six months with the same internal deadlines in the same order. Your coordinator confirms which session a cohort is entered for; it is worth asking in writing in DP1 rather than assuming.

programmes.name: Diploma Core: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · Running across both Diploma years
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three bonus points, and a failing grade in either can cost the Diploma outright regardless of subject scores. The core is also where internal deadlines bite hardest, because the school sets them and the school moves them. An evening spent on the Extended Essay is spent on the research question, the argument structure and the reflections, with the tutor asking questions and the student answering them in their own words on their own screen.
programmes.countryNote: Creativity, Activity, Service is the part UAE families underestimate. Many Emirates-based students build CAS around sport and volunteering that stops during Ramadan and the summer, which leaves a gap in the portfolio at exactly the point DP2 deadlines land. CAS needs no tutoring, but it does need a calendar, and the evening you spend mapping it in DP1 saves three in DP2.

evening-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Component weightings below follow the subject guides currently in use. Confirm with your child's coordinator which version their cohort sits, because the three sciences changed with first examinations in 2025 and the weightings moved with them. Each entry names where marks actually go missing, since that is what decides which evening is worth spending on it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20 per cent; Higher Level splits 30, 30, 20 across three papers with the same exploration weight. Paper 1 allows no technology, which is where marks vanish: students who have learned the graphing display calculator as a crutch cannot sketch a derivative by hand. One evening a week on non-calculator algebra from DP1 onward prevents the whole problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Both papers permit technology throughout, which fools students into thinking the course is easier. The marks go on modelling and interpretation: choosing the right statistical test, justifying a model, and writing a conclusion in the context of the question rather than in the language of the calculator output. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a two-question investigation worth 20 per cent, which rewards stamina and punishes a student who has never written mathematics in prose.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: On the guide first examined in 2025, Paper 1 carries 36 per cent, Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and the scientific investigation 20 per cent. Paper 2 is where the Higher Level grade is decided, and the common losses are not conceptual: unit errors, significant figures, and extended-response answers that describe a phenomenon without ever reaching the equation. An evening of marked past-paper responses with the mark scheme open changes more than an evening of re-teaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same structure as Physics at 36, 44 and 20 per cent. Organic chemistry and energetics generate the most evening bookings in the Emirates, usually from students who can name a mechanism but cannot explain why a step happens. The other recurring loss is data-based questions, where a student calculates correctly and then fails to comment on uncertainty. Both are fixable in a handful of evenings because both are habits rather than gaps.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Weighted 36, 44 and 20 per cent on the current guide. Biology punishes imprecise language more than any other science: an answer that says a substance moves rather than diffuses down a concentration gradient loses the mark it has earned. Higher Level students also underestimate the volume of named examples required. Evening sessions work best when the student writes the answer first and the tutor marks it live, line by line, against command-term expectations.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level runs Paper 1 at 30 per cent, Paper 2 at 40 and the portfolio of three commentaries at 30; Higher Level adds Paper 3 and reweights to 20, 30, 30 and 20. Diagrams are the fastest marks available and the most frequently botched, usually through unlabelled axes or a shifted curve with no explanation. The commentaries are the other pressure point, because each is capped at 800 words and students overwrite by half.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study released ahead of Paper 1 tempts students into memorising the company rather than the tools. Marks come from applying a named concept to the stimulus and evaluating it, in that order. The internal assessment is capped at 1,500 words at Standard Level and 1,800 at Higher Level, and the most common error is a research question so broad that no evidence can answer it. One evening spent narrowing that question saves ten later.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 is comparative essay, and Higher Level adds an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words on a studied text. Marks are lost in Paper 1 when students summarise rather than analyse, and in the individual oral when the global issue is asserted rather than demonstrated through the extracts. Evening work here is reading aloud, annotating together and timing the first ten minutes of Paper 1.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.levels: HL, SL and ab initio SL
subjects.description: Arabic B assesses productive writing, listening and reading, and an individual oral, and the marks a UAE student leaves behind are usually in the oral, where fluency is scored alongside accuracy. Arabic ab initio suits a genuine beginner and cannot be taken by a student with prior schooling in the language. Families here often need this alongside the mandatory Arabic the school already runs, which is a separate requirement with separate homework.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Standard Level weights Paper 1 at 35 per cent, Paper 2 at 40 and the fieldwork at 25; Higher Level adds the global change paper and reweights. Case-study recall is the differentiator, and most students carry too many examples at too shallow a depth. An evening spent reducing six half-remembered case studies to three fully evidenced ones, each with figures and dates, typically moves a grade more than new content does.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision
subjects.description: The Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at 1,600 words and the exhibition commentary at 950, and both are marked against criteria most students never read. Supervision in an evening slot means questioning the knowledge claim, testing whether an example genuinely supports it, and checking the reflections exist. The tutor does not supply text, sentences or structure; the student writes it, and the evening is spent making them defend what they have written.

evening-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: The evening slot in each emirate
evening-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Which emirate you live in changes two things about an evening: the authority your child's school answers to, and how much of the slot a commute would have eaten if anyone had to drive to you. Both matter when a session is booked for six o'clock on a Tuesday and the plan has twenty-six evenings in it.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate, which in 2024-25 meant 227 private schools and 387,441 students across seventeen curricula. Evening IB tuition in Dubai competes with the worst of the traffic between four and seven, which is precisely why an online slot that starts on time is worth more here than in any other emirate.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the capital, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Families on the island whose children attend mainland schools lose the most time to the commute, so the 6pm and 7pm slots fill first.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain also sits under ADEK but has far fewer IB World Schools than the capital, which thins the local tutor pool for Higher Level sciences and both mathematics routes. This is the clearest case in the country for an online IB Diploma tutor on Gulf Standard Time rather than whoever happens to live within a short drive.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai for work, which pushes the realistic start of an MYP evening session back to 6pm or later on weekdays.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Commuting households often cannot be home before seven, so a late evening slot for UAE families on that pattern is the only workable one, and it needs to be booked as a late slot rather than fought for weekly.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The emirate has very few international-curriculum options, so students frequently attend school in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah and travel daily. The evening plan has to assume a tired student and should run shorter, more frequent sessions rather than one long block.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Distance from Dubai makes visiting specialist tuition impractical at any sensible price, which is why the countdown plan here is built entirely around online slots.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education. The mountain road between the east coast and the Dubai-Sharjah corridor rules out a visiting specialist for a weekday evening, and students in Khor Fakkan or Dibba are among the most reliant on a fixed video slot that starts the moment it is supposed to.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai and Sharjah
schoolClusters.note: This corridor holds the densest concentration of IB World Schools in the country, and the evening demand pattern follows it: Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches book out first, Economics and English A fill the later slots. Students we support attend schools including those below, and the schools set their own internal Internal Assessment deadlines, which is why the countdown has to be built per school rather than per city.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: The capital has a solid group of IB World Schools and Al Ain has markedly fewer, which is the single biggest driver of online bookings from the Western Region and the Al Ain road. Students we support attend schools including those below. Verify any school's current programme authorisation and inspection record on ADEK's own site before it influences a decision.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

evening-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Four shapes of session cover almost every UAE family's week. The difference between them is not teaching style; it is which slot on which day, and how many unbroken minutes the student can actually give. Pick the shape first and the subject plan second, because a plan that needs a slot the family does not have is not a plan.

modes.title: The 60-minute school-night evening
modes.description: One subject, one fixed evening between Sunday and Thursday, same time every week for the term. This is the default and it works because it is boring: the student stops negotiating about whether tonight is a tuition night. Sixty minutes is enough for one syllabus sub-topic taught and tested, or one past-paper section written and marked live, and it ends early enough that homework still happens.
bullets: Earliest realistic start 5pm for MYP, 6pm for Diploma students
Same tutor, same slot, held for the term rather than rebooked weekly
Ends by 8.30pm so the evening still contains homework and sleep
One subject only; two subjects in one hour teaches neither

modes.title: The 90-minute Saturday block
modes.description: Internal Assessment work, Extended Essay supervision and full timed papers need more than an hour and should not be attempted on a school night. A Saturday morning block gives ninety unbroken minutes when the student is rested, which is the only condition under which a three-hour Paper 2 can be rehearsed honestly. Most DP2 families run one school-night evening plus one weekend block in the final term.
bullets: Used for timed papers, IA stages and Extended Essay checkpoints
Scheduled Saturday or Sunday morning, never after a full school day
Marked live, with the student rewriting the weakest answer before the block ends

modes.title: The post-Iftar Ramadan slot
modes.description: During Ramadan the school day shortens and the useful part of the evening moves after Iftar. A post-Iftar IB session during Ramadan typically runs from around 9pm, is shorter than the usual hour, and is used for consolidation and marked feedback rather than new Higher Level content. It is agreed in writing before Ramadan starts, not negotiated on the night, because every family in the slot queue is moving at the same time.
bullets: Session moves rather than stops; the slot is reserved at the new time
Shorter blocks, often two 45-minute halves across the week
No new Higher Level content introduced during the fasting weeks
Eid week is written off in the plan from the start

modes.title: The late slot for split-timezone households
modes.description: Some UAE families run on two clocks: a parent working European hours, a student who travels during school holidays, or a tutor based west of the Gulf. A late evening slot for UAE families on that pattern starts at 8pm or 8.30pm Gulf Standard Time and is agreed as a permanent arrangement. It suits DP2 students who revise late anyway and is a poor fit for anyone under fourteen.
bullets: Starts 8pm to 8.30pm GST, finishing by 10pm at the latest
Suitable for DP1 and DP2 only, not for MYP or Primary Years

sections.heading: What a search for an evening IB tutor is actually asking
paragraphs: A parent typing evening IB tutor in the UAE into Google is asking one question: can somebody competent teach my child between roughly five and nine o'clock on a school night, reliably, every week, until the examinations. Everything else, including price and credentials, is secondary to the slot existing. The answer is yes, it is a standard arrangement, and in the Emirates it is almost always delivered on live video because that is the only way the slot starts on time.

There is a second, quieter question underneath it, which is whether the evening is already too late in the year to matter. That depends entirely on how many weeks sit between today and the first paper, and on which parts of the course are still unexamined. Nine months out, an evening a week comfortably covers a Higher Level subject from a weak base. Nine weeks out, the same evening can still move a grade, but only if it is spent on timed questions and marked feedback rather than on re-teaching a syllabus that cannot be re-learned in that time.

The third question nobody types but everybody means is whether this will cost the family the evening as well as the money. A badly planned hour does: it starts late because the tutor is stuck on Sheikh Zayed Road, it overruns because nobody set an end time, and it leaves a child doing homework at ten. A well planned hour protects the rest of the evening. It starts at the minute agreed, ends at the minute agreed, and sends a two-line note about what was covered so the parent does not have to interrogate a teenager at bedtime.

That is the standard this page is written to. The sections that follow count the evenings available, name what each one can hold, and say plainly where the limits are, including the evenings on which a tutor should decline to work at all.

sections.heading: Five school-night evenings, and what genuinely fits inside one
paragraphs: The usable week is Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evening, because most UAE private schools run a Monday-to-Friday week and the night before a school day is the night that has to be protected. Friday and Saturday evenings exist, but a session on a Friday night competes with the entire family's weekend and is abandoned by the third week. The weekend's useful slot is Saturday morning, not Saturday night.

Inside one school-night evening, the limiting factor is not the syllabus; it is the student's remaining attention. A child of nine has perhaps forty-five minutes of real concentration after a full school day. A sixteen-year-old has sixty to seventy-five. A seventeen-year-old in the final term, running on adrenaline and coffee, can hold ninety but will pay for it the next morning. Booking beyond those ceilings buys time, not learning, and the second half of an over-long session is where a tutor ends up talking while a student nods.

Start times matter as much as length. KHDA calculates school teaching time in forty-minute lesson units and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes, which is a useful reminder that a productive teaching block does not have to be an hour. Two forty-minute evenings a week often beat one eighty-minute evening, particularly for mathematics, where the gap between sessions is when consolidation happens. For Internal Assessment work the opposite holds: ninety unbroken minutes on a weekend morning beats three fragmented evenings.
The table below is the shape of an evening by age band. It is a planning tool, not a rule; the number that overrides all of it is the time your child's bus actually arrives.

sections.heading: Counting the evenings backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Most tuition plans are written forwards. A family starts in October, books an evening a week, and discovers in March that three topics were never covered and no complete paper was ever sat under timing. Counting backwards fixes that, because it forces the plan to answer a harder question: of the evenings that remain, which ones are already spoken for, and what has to be finished before each block closes.

The arithmetic is blunt. Between the start of September and a May session there are roughly thirty-five weeks, which is about 175 school-night evenings in total across all subjects. A single subject at one evening a week gets around thirty of them on paper and about twenty-six in practice, once term breaks, Ramadan, Eid, mock weeks and the exam block itself are removed. Two subjects at one evening each halves nothing, but it does mean two of the five evenings are committed before homework is considered, which is usually the real ceiling on how much tuition a family can absorb.

An IB exam countdown plan built this way has one rule: nothing new is introduced inside the final four weeks. By then the content either exists or it does not, and the evenings are worth more spent on command terms, timing and the particular mistakes that student makes under pressure. The blocks before that each have a closing condition, and if a block closes with its condition unmet the plan is rewritten rather than the deadline quietly moved.

Dates in the table below are relative, counted back from your child's own first paper, with one exception. Cambridge publishes its March 2027 series dates, and they are included because they show how far ahead entry deadlines sit: the final entry date of 27 November 2026 falls more than two months before the exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. IB session dates are not printed here, because the IB's site cannot be checked automatically and a guessed date in a plan is worse than no date at all.

sections.heading: The evenings your child's school has already claimed
paragraphs: A family planning evenings often forgets that the school has first claim on several of them. Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay reflection sessions, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, mock weeks and CAS deadlines all land on dates the school chooses, and they are rarely spread evenly. In most UAE IB schools the heaviest cluster falls between late November and early February, which is also when Ramadan can arrive and when mocks are scheduled. Three competing claims on the same fortnight is the normal state of DP2.

Those evenings need a different kind of session, and a strict one. Internal Assessment feedback is the single most misunderstood service in this market. A tutor may read a draft, ask what the research question is actually asking, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and explain a criterion the student has not read. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the piece on the student's behalf, or hand back a marked-up version with the fixes written in. Everything that appears in the submitted work has to be the student's own, and the IB treats the alternative as malpractice with consequences that fall on the student, not the tutor.

The practical test is simple: after the session, could the student explain every change and reproduce the reasoning unprompted? If not, the line has been crossed. Providers that offer to produce finished coursework exist in this SERP, and one of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is a different and dangerous transaction, and a student caught using it can lose the Diploma.

Word limits are the other thing a tutor can usefully police, because they are published, absolute and routinely ignored until the week before submission. The table below collects them in one place, with what a tutor may legitimately do on an evening devoted to each.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the evenings that move
paragraphs: Ramadan is the single largest disruption to an evening tuition plan in the Emirates, and it is also the most predictable, which means there is no excuse for handling it badly. School days shorten, the useful part of the evening moves after Iftar, concentration in the late afternoon drops sharply, and the week of Eid al-Fitr disappears entirely. Four or five weeks of a twenty-six evening plan are affected. A plan that does not account for it is short by roughly a fifth before it starts.

In 2027 Ramadan is expected to open in the second week of February, subject to moon sighting, which puts it directly on top of two things: DP2 mock season in most UAE schools, and Cambridge's March series, whose exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 with forecast grades due on 27 February. A household with one child sitting IGCSE in the March series and another in DP2 is therefore managing fasting, mocks and live external examinations in the same four weeks. That situation needs a written timetable agreed in January, not a weekly conversation in February.

The workable pattern is to move the slot rather than cancel it. A post-Iftar session starting around 9pm, running forty-five to sixty minutes, with no new Higher Level content, keeps continuity without asking a fasting student to absorb new material at four in the afternoon. Some families prefer a short early-afternoon slot straight after the shortened school day instead, which works well for Primary Years and MYP and badly for Diploma students who need to be sharp.

Eid week should be written off in the plan from the outset. Trying to hold sessions through it produces cancellations, and cancellations produce the sense that the whole arrangement has lapsed. Booking one catch-up evening in the week after Eid recovers more than fighting for sessions during it ever does.

sections.heading: What an evening hour costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The figures below are market rates in dirhams, each attributed to the provider or survey that published it, gathered in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's price list. What they are good for is judging whether a quote you have been given sits inside the market or outside it.

Time of evening affects the number more than most parents expect. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is the one every family wants and the one specialists fill first, so a Higher Level science tutor with a free 6pm slot is either new, unusually good at scheduling, or charging a premium for it. Slots from 8pm carry more availability and often a lower rate, which is a genuine saving for a DP2 student who revises late anyway and a false economy for a fourteen-year-old.

Two other variables move the figure. Level is one: Higher Level and Diploma-core supervision command more than MYP or Primary Years, because the pool of people who can teach them is smaller. Travel is the other, and it is the biggest single component in a visiting tutor's rate. Market rates for a visiting one-to-one tutor in a UAE city run from around AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online, and most of that gap is a car.

On price honesty: no UAE authority sets or caps a tutoring rate, so a quote is only as meaningful as what it includes. Ask whether the rate covers marking between sessions, whether a cancellation inside twenty-four hours is charged, and whether the figure includes VAT. A provider who will not answer those three questions in writing is telling you something.

sections.heading: The six o'clock Tuesday test: online against a visiting tutor
paragraphs: This is the comparison most parents are really making, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales one. A visiting tutor has one real advantage: a physically present adult is harder for a thirteen-year-old to ignore than a face on a screen. For younger students with attention difficulties, that advantage is genuine and should be weighed honestly. Everything else in the comparison runs the other way, and on a six o'clock Tuesday in the Emirates it runs strongly the other way.

Start with the arithmetic of a ninety-minute window. A visiting tutor who arrives at 6pm has usually left home at 5.15pm and will leave yours at 7pm to reach somebody else by 7.45pm. Inside your ninety-minute window, perhaps fifty-five minutes are taught, because arrival, settling, the search for the right exercise book and the goodbye all consume real time. An online session in the same window teaches eighty-five. At a market rate of AED 300 an hour, thirty lost minutes is AED 150 of nothing.

The second difference is the pool. A visiting arrangement limits the choice of teacher to people who can reach your district by six, which in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain may mean nobody at all for Chemistry at Higher Level. On video, the question becomes who is free at that Gulf Standard Time slot, which is a far larger group. This is why IB Gram delivers UAE tuition online: it is not a limitation we are explaining away, it is the reason a family in Khor Fakkan can book the same specialist as a family in Emirates Hills. Visiting tuition is a service the platform runs in India only, and nobody is sent to an address in the Emirates.

The third difference shows up in February. When a school bus runs forty minutes late, an online slot shifts by ten minutes and proceeds. A visiting tutor is already on the road and the hour is either lost or paid for twice. Over a twenty-six evening plan, that reliability is worth more than any single lesson.

sections.heading: Where Higher Level marks go missing, and which evening fixes them
paragraphs: Marks are rarely lost where families think they are. A parent reports that a child does not understand electricity, and the past papers show something narrower: the student understands potential difference perfectly and loses four marks a paper writing answers that never reach an equation. That is a two-evening problem, not a term-long one, and diagnosing it correctly is the difference between a plan that works inside twenty-six evenings and one that does not.

Across the Diploma subjects UAE families book most, four failure modes recur. Command terms are the first: students answer describe when the paper asked explain, or evaluate with a list rather than a judgement, and the mark scheme has no route to award credit. Timing is the second, and it is almost always structural rather than a matter of speed; a student who spends twenty-two minutes on a six-mark opener has not run out of time, they have mismanaged it. Working that an examiner cannot follow is the third, which costs method marks even when the final answer is right. Unit and significant-figure discipline is the fourth, and it is pure arithmetic of lost marks.

Each of those has an evening shape. Command terms respond to a session where the student writes short answers to one command verb at a time and the tutor marks them against the published descriptors on screen. Timing responds to a stopwatch and nothing else. Working responds to the student being made to narrate their method aloud while writing it. Units respond to a single rule, applied relentlessly for three weeks, until it stops being a decision.

The one failure mode that does not respond to evenings is a genuine content gap in the last month. A DP2 student who has never met a topic in April will not meet it properly before the paper, and an honest tutor says so and spends the evening maximising what is securable instead. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who offers to is selling something other than teaching.
bullets: Command-term confusion: answering describe when the paper asked explain
Structural mistiming: twenty-two minutes spent on a six-mark opener

Unit and significant-figure slips, worth several marks a paper by themselves

sections.heading: Permits, school ethics and who may legally teach in the evening
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The route is a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published, so any figure you see quoted for it should be treated as unverified. What a parent can reasonably do is ask to see the permit before booking a block of exam-term hours, and check that the name on it matches the person who will actually teach.

One restriction catches UAE families out every year, and it is specifically an evening problem. A teacher at your child's own school offering paid lessons after hours is the arrangement most likely to be prohibited: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also addresses serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before acting on it, but treat the offer with caution rather than gratitude.

A final point on what nobody can claim. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which is a specific licence for a specific kind of business. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform; it is not approved, licensed, endorsed or accredited by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the federal Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here should be read as suggesting otherwise. A provider describing its individual tutors as authority-approved is describing something that does not exist.

sections.heading: Equivalency, university deadlines and the dates you can trust
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the step UAE families discover late, usually when a university asks for an attested certificate. For the British track the published requirements are concrete: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor ranking for these searches publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published here, because none has been read on an official Ministry source. Confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate rather than trusting any tutoring site, including this one, on that specific number.

Equivalency is also not something a tutoring platform performs, arranges or guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. What tutoring can affect is narrow and worth knowing: the grades in the subjects that have to be counted. If a student is sitting on a grade 3 borderline in one of five required IGCSE subjects, that subject is where an evening belongs, ahead of a subject where the difference is between a 6 and a 7 that nothing depends on.

Which brings the page back to dates. Cambridge publishes a full key-dates document per series, and its March 2027 series is the clearest illustration available: entries closing 27 November 2026, exams 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades 27 February, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable, so the version your school uses is the only one that matters. Pearson publishes its own series timetables and provisional ones ahead of time. The IB's site blocks automated checking, which is why no IB session or results date appears on this page: a date that cannot be sourced should not be planned against, and your coordinator can give you the real one.
bullets: Five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at E or grade 3 minimum, Arabic and Islamic education excluded
Plus one A Level at E, or two AS Levels at E, for the British track
American track: IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 reading and writing, and SAT Math 450
