sections.heading: If no specialist is free at the evening slot you need
paragraphs: Every tutoring site implies infinite availability and none of them has it. The honest position is that a specific combination of subject, level and Gulf Standard Time slot sometimes has nobody free, and the 5pm to 7pm window for Higher Level sciences in the weeks before a session is the hardest combination in the UAE market. Saying so is more useful than matching a family with a generalist and letting them discover the problem in week three.

When that happens there are three options and they are offered in this order. The first is a different slot with the right specialist: an 8pm Gulf Standard Time session with a Chemistry Higher Level teacher beats a 6pm session with somebody who last taught the subject at IGCSE. The second is a waiting list with a named date, which suits families more than six weeks out from a deadline. The third, where the subject is genuinely rare and the timing is tight, is a tutor outside the UAE teaching on your clock, which is stated upfront rather than concealed behind a local-looking phone number.

Two competitors in this market route UAE parents to numbers in another country without mentioning it, and one shows a Dubai address on a page about Abu Dhabi. Both are the same failure: concealing where delivery actually comes from. An online IB Diploma tutor on Gulf Standard Time may be sitting in Dubai, Mumbai or Manchester, and the only things that matter to the evening are that they teach your child's subject at your child's level, they are available in your slot every week, and you were told plainly which it is.

The practical first step is small. Send the student's timetable, the subject, the level, the school, and the two evenings that could realistically work. The reply says who is free, at what time, and from which week. If nothing fits, that is the answer you get, and it arrives before any money has changed hands.

process.title: Send the timetable, not just the subject
process.description: Start with the practical facts: which school, which programme year, which subjects and levels, what time the bus actually arrives, and the two evenings that could work. A request that says Chemistry HL, DP2, bus at 4.10pm, Tuesday or Wednesday after 6pm can be answered properly. A request that says maths help cannot.

process.title: A trial lesson in the slot you actually want
process.description: The first lesson is a trial at no charge, one per student, and it is deliberately booked into the slot being considered rather than whenever a tutor is free. That is the only way to find out whether your child can still concentrate at that hour. No payment is taken before it, and you watch the first ten minutes if you want to.

process.title: Lock the slot, then write the countdown
process.description: Once the slot is agreed it is held for the term rather than rebooked weekly. The plan is then written backwards from the first paper using the block structure on this page, with a closing condition for each block. A plan that cannot state what will be finished by mid-December is not finished itself.

process.title: A written note after every evening
process.description: Each session ends with two or three lines: what was covered, what was marked, what the student is to do before the next evening. It goes to the parent, not through the student. This is also how a tutoring arrangement that has quietly stopped working becomes visible in week three rather than in March.

process.title: Reset the plan when the mock marks arrive
process.description: Mock results are the one genuinely diagnostic data point in the Diploma year, and they usually land fifteen to nineteen weeks before the first paper. That is the moment to redistribute evenings between subjects, add or drop an hour, and decide whether the plan still fits the time left. Plans that are never reset are plans nobody is reading.

whyPoints.title: The slot is the product
whyPoints.description: A fixed weekly evening at a time the student can genuinely use is worth more than a nominally better tutor at an hour that does not work. Slots are held for the term, start on the minute and end on the minute, because a session that routinely overruns into homework time gets cancelled by the family within a month.

whyPoints.title: The plan runs backwards
whyPoints.description: Every plan is written from the first paper back to today, with a closing condition on each block, rather than forwards from the first available evening. That is what stops a family reaching March having never sat a complete paper under timing, which is the most common way a year of weekly tuition produces nothing much.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down before the first draft
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may do with an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is stated at the start: question, teach, explain criteria, give feedback. Not supply sentences, not restructure on the student's behalf, not hand back a fixed version. The student writes every word, and that is a feature of the service rather than a limitation of it.

whyPoints.title: The specialist pool is not a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are on live video, the question is who teaches Chemistry at Higher Level and is free at your Gulf Standard Time slot, not who can reach Al Ain or Fujairah by six o'clock. For the less common subject and level combinations, that is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

whyPoints.title: What is not claimed here
whyPoints.description: No authority approval, no accreditation, no school partnership, no UAE office, no promised grade and no invented statistic. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and says so. Every AED figure on this page is a market rate attributed to the provider or survey that published it, dated October 2026, and none of it is a quote from us.

whyPoints.title: Dates that cannot be sourced are not printed
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson publish their series dates, so those appear here with the source named. The IB's site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date is printed on this page at all. A guessed exam date inside a countdown plan is worse than no date, and your coordinator has the real one.

faqs.question: What time can an evening IB session realistically start on a UAE school night?
faqs.answer: Work from the bus, not from the school bell. Most UAE private schools finish in the early afternoon, but a bus route can add thirty to forty minutes, so the usable start is rarely before 4.30pm for a primary child and rarely before 5.30pm or 6pm for a Diploma student who needs to eat first. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is the one every family wants and the one that fills first. If that window is impossible, an 8pm slot with the right specialist is a better trade than a 6pm slot with the wrong one.

faqs.question: How many school-night evenings are actually left between September and a May session?
faqs.answer: About 175 across all subjects, and roughly twenty-six per subject if you book one evening a week. The arithmetic is five school-night evenings a week, Sunday through Thursday, across roughly thirty-five teaching weeks, minus two term breaks, mock weeks, the four or five weeks Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr affect, and the exam block itself. Writing that number down at the start changes how families behave: twenty-six evenings is enough to move a Higher Level subject substantially, and not enough to cover two subjects properly from a weak base.

faqs.question: Is one evening a week enough for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: From a reasonable base, yes, provided the work between sessions actually happens. One evening a week gives about twenty-six teaching hours a year, which covers a Higher Level syllabus if the student arrives having attempted the set work. From a weak base in DP2 it is not enough, and the honest options are two evenings a week, one evening plus a weekend block for timed papers, or narrowing the goal to the parts of the course that are still securable. Doubling the hours in the final month rarely helps; doubling them in October usually does.

faqs.question: Is a 60-minute evening or a 90-minute one the better use of a school night for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes if it is a timed-paper evening, sixty otherwise. A DP2 past-paper section needs around seventy unbroken minutes to be worth sitting, plus time to mark it, so a sixty-minute slot forces the marking into the following week when the memory of the attempt has gone. For content teaching, sixty minutes is better: the last thirty minutes of a ninety-minute content session on a school night is usually the tutor talking. Many families run one sixty-minute school-night evening plus a ninety-minute Saturday morning block in the final term.

faqs.question: Which evening of the week is the worst one to book?
faqs.answer: Thursday, because it is the last school night of the UAE week and everything that was postponed lands on it. By Thursday evening a student has the week's accumulated fatigue and the weekend in sight, and cancellation rates are highest. Sunday evening is the strongest slot, since the student is rested and the week's work has not yet piled up. Monday and Tuesday are close behind. If Thursday is the only possible evening, keep the session shorter and use it for marked feedback on work already done rather than new content.

faqs.question: We can only take the last slot of the night. What does that change?
faqs.answer: It widens the choice of tutor and narrows the choice of student. Slots from 8pm Gulf Standard Time carry far more availability than the 5pm to 7pm window, often at the lower end of the market rate, because fewer families want them. That makes a late evening slot a genuine saving for a DP1 or DP2 student who revises late anyway. It is a poor arrangement for anyone under fourteen, where the session competes directly with sleep and the next school day pays for it.

faqs.question: Ramadan lands on top of our revision block. How should the evening plan change week by week?
faqs.answer: Move the slot rather than cancel it, and agree the move in January. The usual pattern is a post-Iftar session from around 9pm, forty-five to sixty minutes, used for consolidation and marked feedback rather than new Higher Level content, with the week of Eid al-Fitr written off in the plan from the start. Primary and Middle Years students often do better in a short slot straight after the shortened school day instead. Book one catch-up evening the week after Eid; that recovers more than fighting for sessions during it.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to say about an Internal Assessment draft the night before it is uploaded?
faqs.answer: Plenty, as long as nothing the tutor says ends up as text in the document. A tutor can point out that the conclusion does not follow from the data, that a criterion has not been addressed, that the word count is being spent on background rather than analysis, or that a graph is unlabelled. A tutor cannot supply sentences, rewrite sections, or hand back a version with the fixes written in. The test afterwards is whether the student can explain every change unprompted. If not, the line has been crossed and the risk falls on them.

faqs.question: Does the private tuition permit cover someone who tutors only after 7pm as a second job?
faqs.answer: Yes, that is substantially what it exists for. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and its eligible categories explicitly include employees in the government and private sectors as well as registered school teachers. Evening-only tutoring alongside other employment is therefore a normal permitted arrangement. Working without the permit exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any figure you see quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Why will you not print the May IB exam dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB directly. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so every IB session and results date in circulation on tutoring sites is second-hand, and a guessed date inside a countdown plan is worse than no date at all. Cambridge and Pearson publish theirs openly, which is why their dates appear here with the source named. For the IB, your child's coordinator can confirm the session, the window and the results date in one email, and that is the version worth planning against.

faqs.question: Cambridge's March series sits inside Ramadan in 2027. What does that do to an evening plan?
faqs.answer: It creates the hardest four weeks in the UAE academic year for a household with children on both boards. Cambridge's March 2027 exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February, and Ramadan in 2027 is expected to open in the second week of February subject to moon sighting. That means live external examinations, fasting and DP2 mock season in the same month. The plan has to be written in January: fewer, shorter post-Iftar sessions, nothing new introduced, and the IGCSE candidate's evenings prioritised while their papers are actually running.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start evening tuition before the first paper?
faqs.answer: Four weeks is the point where the nature of the work changes rather than the point where it stops being worthwhile. Inside four weeks nothing new should be introduced, and the evenings are worth spending on command terms, paper timing and the specific errors that student repeats. Nine to twelve weeks out is still ample for a meaningful shift in one subject. Two weeks out, an honest tutor will tell you which marks are securable and which are not, and will decline to sell a programme that implies otherwise.

faqs.question: An evening visit from a tutor sounds simpler. Why is this delivered over video instead?
faqs.answer: Because of what the visit costs the evening. A visiting tutor arriving at 6pm has left home around 5.15pm and must leave by 7pm for the next family, so of a ninety-minute window roughly fifty-five minutes are taught once arrival and settling are counted. Online, around eighty-five are. The drive is also inside the rate: market figures for visiting one-to-one tuition in UAE cities run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 online. IB Gram runs visiting tuition in India only; UAE lessons are on live video.

faqs.question: The tutor is three and a half hours behind Gulf Standard Time. Can an evening slot still work?
faqs.answer: It works well in one direction and badly in the other. Gulf Standard Time is UTC+4, so a tutor in the United Kingdom is three or four hours behind depending on the season, which makes your 7pm a comfortable mid-afternoon for them. A tutor in India is ninety minutes ahead, so your 8pm is their 9.30pm, which is workable but should be agreed as a permanent arrangement rather than assumed. What matters is that the slot is stated in Gulf Standard Time in writing and that you were told where the tutor is.

faqs.question: What should an evening session never be spent on?
faqs.answer: Four things. Re-teaching a whole topic in the final fortnight, when the time is better spent securing what exists. Supplying text, structure or corrections for assessed work, which is malpractice and falls on the student. Covering two subjects in one hour, which teaches neither properly. And the evening immediately before a paper, which belongs to sleep: a student who revises until eleven and sits a three-hour paper at nine the next morning loses more to fatigue than the session could ever have added.

faqs.question: If we can fund two evenings a week for one year only, which Diploma year should get them?
faqs.answer: DP1, in almost every case, and most families choose the opposite. DP1 is where the syllabus is built, where working habits are set and where the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay groundwork gets done cheaply. Two evenings a week in DP1 usually means one is enough in DP2. Two evenings a week in DP2 against a weak DP1 is remedial work running against a fixed deadline, and it is the more expensive way to buy a smaller result. If DP1 has already gone, prioritise the subject where the student is closest to a boundary.

faqs.question: Which part of the Ministry of Education equivalency file can tutoring actually affect?
faqs.answer: Only the grades, and only in the subjects that have to be counted. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. If a student sits on a borderline in one of those five, that subject is where an evening belongs. Equivalency itself is handled by the Ministry and the attestation authority in your emirate, not by any tutoring provider, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

evening-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Book the evening you have, then count backwards
evening-ib-tutor.closingBody: Start with the slot rather than the subject. Send the school, the programme year, the subjects and levels, the time the bus actually arrives, and the two evenings that could realistically work every week until the examinations. The reply names who is free, at what Gulf Standard Time, and from which week, and says plainly if nothing fits. The first lesson is a trial at no charge, one per student, booked into the slot you are considering rather than whenever somebody happens to be available, because the only useful test is whether your child can still think at that hour. After that the plan is written backwards from the first paper, and every evening in it has a job.

experienced-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are tutors currently teaching IB subjects for UAE families. Read the line that says which syllabus and which level they last taught, and which session that cohort sat. That line, rather than a number of years, is what tells you whether the experience matches the paper your child is sitting.

intro.heading: Experience, measured against the system your child studies inside
paragraphs: Parents who search for an experienced IB tutor in the UAE are usually trying to filter out one specific risk: paying for somebody who knows the subject but not the examination. Those are different jobs. A graduate chemist can explain redox clearly. Only somebody who has taught the Diploma version of redox to several cohorts knows that the marks sit in the state symbols and the balanced half-equations, and that a student who explains it fluently out loud can still lose four marks in writing. Experience, in this market, means experience of where marks are awarded.

In the UAE a second layer sits above that. Your child's school is licensed and inspected by a body that depends on the emirate. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does the same in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah those authorities approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so they reach further than an inspection grade. A tutor who has worked here knows which body holds your school's file, and therefore which documents you can reasonably ask the school to show you.

A third layer surprises families who have moved from Europe or South Asia. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and the federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever else they offer. Those lessons take up real timetable minutes beside Higher Level maths and the Extended Essay. An experienced tutor plans the week around them rather than discovering them in March.

The supply problem behind this search is arithmetical. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of the roll, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. The Diploma is a minority programme inside a very large market, and Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are a minority inside that minority. Seven new private schools open in Dubai for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Places are being added faster than experienced Diploma teachers are.

That is why IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video rather than sending anybody to an address in the Emirates. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Online delivery is not a compromise on the promise in this page's title; it is the only way a family in Mirdif or Mirfa reaches the person who has taught their exact paper, instead of the best-qualified adult inside a twenty-minute drive. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run and prayer times, and move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan.

The rest of this page is written to be used rather than admired. It sets out how to count a tutor's experience, what the emirate regulators control, which kinds of experience evidence what, how diagnosis differs from more practice papers, what the market charges and who published those numbers, and where the line sits between teaching a student's coursework and producing it.

experienced-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: An experienced tutor treats the four IB programmes as four different jobs, because the assessment model changes at each stage. A Primary Years student needs the habits that survive the move into subject teaching. A Diploma student needs marks in named components by a dated deadline. The notes below say what each programme asks of a UAE family in particular.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three usually at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries internally assessed work marked by the teacher and moderated externally, and externally marked papers that decide most of the grade. Experience here means knowing how a component weighting converts into a revision plan: time spent on a paper worth 35% is not interchangeable with time spent on one worth 20%.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and a smaller number of candidates sit November. Registration and internal coursework deadlines are set months before either window, by the school rather than by the tutor. A tutor who has run two-year plans here already knows that the heaviest coursework weeks collide with mock season and, in some years, with Ramadan.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria, with a Personal Project in the final year. Marks come in criterion bands rather than percentages, which is why a parent can see 6 out of 8 on one criterion and 3 out of 8 on another in the same report and have no idea which to worry about. Experienced teaching here is largely translation: turning criterion language into a specific thing the student does differently next week.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools run the MYP only to Year 10 or 11 and then move students into the Diploma, which makes the Year 11 to DP1 summer the single most useful tutoring window in the whole programme. Families who move between emirates mid-programme often find criterion reporting styles differ between schools even under the same authority.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units with no external examination, which makes a weak maths or literacy foundation easy to miss until secondary school. Useful support at this stage is quiet and specific: number facts, place value, sentence structure, reading stamina. There is no syllabus code to teach to, so experience shows in whether the tutor can name the gap in one sentence and give the parent something measurable to watch over four weeks.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons begin in the primary years, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Non-Arab families often meet Arabic as an additional language here for the first time and need to know which stream their child sits in.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by relatively few schools in the region, so tutors with genuine experience of it are rarer than tutors with experience of the Diploma. If a school offers it, ask who in the tutoring market has supported the reflective project before, because its requirements are not the Extended Essay's.
programmes.countryNote: Because the route is uncommon locally, a UAE family choosing it should check how the certificate will be presented for Ministry of Education equivalency and for the universities on their list, and verify that with the attestation authority rather than with a tutoring company.

experienced-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Experience is subject-shaped, not general. The notes below say what each course actually assesses and where UAE students most often lose marks, so you can judge whether a tutor's stated experience lines up with the paper your child is sitting rather than with the subject's name.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy route, and the one most competitive university courses expect. Higher Level adds a third paper built on extended problems rather than recall. Marks go missing in method communication: a correct answer with no visible working scores less than a wrong answer with a clear method. Experienced teaching here spends time on how an answer is written, not only on whether it is right.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work, with heavy graphical calculator use. Students who chose it to avoid proof often underestimate the data handling at Higher Level. The usual failure is treating a modelling question as arithmetic and never interpreting the result in context, which is where the marks sit. Route choice between AA and AI should be checked against the entry requirements of the actual universities on the list.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward precise definitions; the data-based questions reward reading a graph rather than remembering an equation. Higher Level depth is where Standard Level habits break. The scientific investigation is marked against published criteria, and students lose marks for a weak research question long before anything goes wrong with the data. Online sessions use shared screens for working, which suits physics well.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry the most marks and the most confusion. Papers punish loose notation: missing state symbols, unbalanced half-equations and answers given to the wrong number of significant figures. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, so a student who is secure at Standard Level can still be a long way from a Higher Level grade without targeted work on the extra content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Students who revise by rereading notes do well in class tests and badly in papers, because the questions ask for application to unfamiliar contexts and for command terms answered exactly. Experienced teaching trains the difference between describing a process and explaining it, and keeps the internally assessed investigation moving while the syllabus is still being taught.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks that prose cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative work that surprises students who chose the subject as an essay subject. The internally assessed commentaries need current articles and genuine theory applied to them, not a summary of the news. UAE students often write strong evaluation and still lose marks for an unlabelled axis or a missing definition.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with tools that must be applied rather than described. The common pattern is a student who can define every acronym and cannot use one on an unseen company. Higher Level questions demand sustained evaluation with a judgement actually made. Marks are also lost to answers that ignore the command term and write everything the student knows about the topic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis under time pressure, plus oral and written components built on the student's own chosen texts. The usual gap is technique spotting without argument: a list of devices with no claim about meaning. Experienced teaching here works on the thesis sentence and on how an oral is structured, because the student is assessed on a performance that cannot be redrafted.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course that many UAE students take alongside English-medium schooling, which makes level choice genuinely difficult. Receptive skills are tested on authentic texts, and productive skills on text types with conventions that must be obeyed. Marks go missing when a student writes a good essay in the wrong text type, or ignores audience and purpose in the task instruction.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: Ab initio, B SL and B HL
subjects.description: The subject most often sat alongside the mandatory school Arabic lesson, and the one families least expect to need support with. Progress depends on script fluency and on vocabulary built for the assessed text types. In Dubai, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, so knowing which stream a child is in matters before any support is planned.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory assessed on paper, plus a solution developed by the student. Students who code confidently still lose marks on paper questions about algorithms, data structures and systems design, because the written answer has conventions of its own. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study that has to be read early rather than skimmed in the final term.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition, both assessed against published criteria and both capable of moving the final points total through the core. Students treat it as an opinion piece; it is an argument with examples that have to do work. Support here is strictly discussion and feedback on the student's own drafts, which is also what the honesty rules require.

experienced-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: This is a federal market with seven different school-system experiences inside it. The notes below say what changes about finding experienced Diploma support depending on where a family lives, because the regulator, the number of IB schools and the realistic session time are not the same in Dubai as in Fujairah.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest IB market in the country and the one with the most published data: 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the IB at 7% of the roll. Depth of market does not mean depth in your subject, because three of the seven schools opening for 2026-27 are IB and recruit from the same teacher pool.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation here, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That single rule removes the most obvious local option for many families, which is why experienced support is usually found outside the school rather than inside it.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, but with far fewer IB schools than the island, so Higher Level cohorts can be very small. A student may be one of three or four taking a Higher Level science, which limits how much in-class differentiation is possible and makes one-to-one work on paper technique more valuable than more content coverage.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many families commute to schools in Dubai, so the realistic start time for a weekday session is later than a Dubai-resident family's, and two shorter sessions often work better than one long one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, so the inspection vocabulary a parent reads differs from Dubai's. IB provision is thin locally and several families travel to Sharjah or Dubai, which makes evening scheduling the binding constraint on any tutoring plan.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai school belt is the practical issue: a visiting specialist in a niche Higher Level subject is close to unobtainable, while a live video session with one costs the same here as anywhere else in the country.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under federal Ministry of Education supervision, on the east coast and separated from the main school corridor by the mountains. Cohorts are small, subject choice at Higher Level is limited by what the school can staff, and travel time makes in-person arrangements with a subject specialist impractical rather than merely expensive.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the federation, also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Families here tend to be choosing between a local school and a commute, and the tutoring question is usually about covering a subject the nearest school cannot staff rather than about topping up a subject it teaches well.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend IB schools across the emirate, from Emirates Hills and Al Barsha to Dubai Festival City and Mirdif. The practical difference between them, for a tutoring plan, is which Higher Level subjects each actually runs in a given year and when internal coursework deadlines fall, both of which the school publishes to parents.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: ADEK's school file and its staff ethics rules shape the options here more than anything else. Families typically want a specialist outside the school for a Higher Level subject, scheduled after a long school run, and want it to survive a move between Khalifa City, the island and Al Ain without changing tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Three different regulators cover this stretch: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Smaller IB cohorts are the norm, so the gap a tutor is asked to fill is more often subject coverage than exam polish.

experienced-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of working cover almost every request a UAE family makes of an experienced tutor. All three run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The difference between them is how much of the year they occupy and what the tutor is being asked to carry.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the year
modes.description: One or two sessions a week in the same subject with the same tutor, following the school's sequence and arriving at the exam with the content already consolidated. This is the pattern in which a tutor's experience compounds, because they see the same student's errors repeat and can name the cause rather than the symptom. It also absorbs the school's internal deadlines without a scramble.

It is the wrong purchase when a whole unit is missing, because no amount of paper practice will teach content that was never covered.

sections.heading: Experience in the Diploma is counted in cohorts, not calendar years
paragraphs: Ask a tutoring company how experienced its tutors are and you will usually be told a number of years. That number is nearly useless on its own, because the Diploma runs on a two-year cycle and the unit of experience is the completed cohort: a group taken from subject choice through the internal assessment and the mocks to the papers and the results. Two years of teaching can mean one DP1 group and one DP2 group who were never the same students, which is not the same as having followed one set of students all the way through.

The second thing to count is sessions sat. UAE schools sit the May session, and a smaller number of candidates sit November. A tutor who has taught for five years has seen four or five May sessions if the teaching was continuous and in the same programme, and possibly none at all if those years were spent on IGCSE or on a national curriculum. Years spent teaching a subject at a different level are real experience of the subject and no experience at all of the assessment your child faces.

The third is variation. Ten years in one school means ten years under one coordinator's internal deadlines, one reporting style and one exam centre's arrangements. That is deep experience of a single setting. A tutor who has worked across schools and emirates has seen different internal deadlines, different inspection vocabularies and the practical fact that two students sitting the same qualification can be on different timetables because their centres sit in different administrative zones. Both kinds of experience are useful; they answer different questions, and it is worth knowing which one you are buying.

sections.heading: A growing school sector does not grow experienced Diploma teachers at the same rate
paragraphs: The published numbers for Dubai explain why experienced Diploma teaching is scarce even in a market this large. In 2024-25 the emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula. The UK curriculum accounted for 37% of the roll, Indian for 26%, American for 14% and the International Baccalaureate for 7%. Most private-school teachers in the emirate therefore work in a system that is not the Diploma, and a parent who assumes that a large school market implies a deep Diploma bench is reasoning from the wrong number.

Growth makes it tighter rather than looser. Seven new private schools open in Dubai for 2026-27, four following the UK curriculum and three the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Three new IB schools have to staff Diploma classes from the same pool everybody else recruits from, and experienced teachers move between schools when they do. For a family, that shows up as a change of subject teacher in DP2, which is the worst year in which to have one.

There is one number moving the other way. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package the emirate valued at AED 1.5 billion. A fixed school bill is the one part of an education budget a family can plan around, which makes it a sensible anchor for deciding what, if anything, to spend on tutoring and when to spend it.

sections.heading: Experience of one emirate is not experience of all seven
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not regulated by a single body, and the differences are substantive rather than administrative. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and both of those bodies approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

That last point is worth sitting with. In two emirates the regulator signs off the assessment methods a school uses, not only the quality of its teaching. A parent in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah can therefore ask the school which methods have been approved for their child's year group, and a tutor who has worked in those emirates will know that this is a reasonable question rather than an awkward one. In Abu Dhabi, the relevant local knowledge is different again: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

This matters for the search you are running because it determines what good advice sounds like. A tutor whose whole career was in Dubai may describe inspection in KHDA's vocabulary to a family whose school is supervised federally, where that vocabulary does not apply. The useful test is simple: ask which authority holds your school's file and what that authority controls. An experienced tutor will name the body, say what it approves, and point you at the authority's own published material rather than paraphrasing it.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of these bodies, and no tutoring company that is not a licensed training institute with premises should imply otherwise. What we do is name the right regulator and explain what it governs.

sections.heading: Teaching, assessing and tutoring are three different kinds of experience
paragraphs: The word experience is doing at least four jobs in this market, and separating them is most of the work of choosing well. Classroom experience is experience of pacing a syllabus for thirty students and meeting a coordinator's deadlines. Assessment experience is experience of how a criterion is applied rather than how it reads. Tutoring experience is experience of diagnosing one student quickly and teaching to their gaps. Experience of the UAE system is experience of regulators, mandatory subjects, zones and equivalency. A tutor can have a great deal of one and almost none of another.

We do not describe tutors as examiners for a board, because current examining status is something a provider would have to be able to evidence and most of the market cannot. There is also a boundary that matters more than the label: assessment experience tells you how marks are awarded, and it gives nobody access to unreleased papers, mark schemes or grade boundaries. Any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation. The honest version of the claim is narrow and still valuable: somebody who has applied a criterion repeatedly can tell your child what the criterion actually requires in writing.

The practical move is to ask questions whose answers cannot be improvised. Which topic did your last cohort lose the most marks on, and why? What do you do in the first forty minutes with a new student? What does a strong criterion-B response contain that a middling one does not? How would the plan change if my child dropped from Higher to Standard Level? Vague answers to those questions are not a sign of modesty.

sections.heading: Experience shows up as topic-level diagnosis, not as more past papers
paragraphs: The clearest difference between an experienced tutor and a capable graduate appears in the first session with a real script in front of them. A capable graduate sees a wrong answer and reteaches the topic. An experienced teacher sees a pattern and asks a diagnostic question, because the same wrong answer has several different causes and each one needs a different fix. Rounding errors, a calculator left in radians, a misread command term and a genuinely missing concept all look identical in a mark total.

This is where more past papers stop helping. Papers are a measuring instrument. Doing another one tells you that the student is still losing marks; it does not tell you why, and a student who does five papers a week without analysis simply rehearses the same errors with increasing confidence. The useful sequence is narrow and repetitive: find the cause, teach the specific thing, then test the same question type cold a week later to see whether the fix held.

Diagnosis is also what makes an honest conversation about timing possible. If a student is losing marks on command terms, six weeks is plenty of time to change the outcome, because command-term discipline can be taught quickly and rehearsed. If a whole unit was never covered, six weeks is a different proposition and a family deserves to be told so before they pay for it. An experienced tutor will tell you which of those two situations you are in after reading the work, not after ten sessions.

sections.heading: The subjects an experienced tutor already knows are on the timetable
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in Dubai private schools, and the federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever curriculum they otherwise follow. KHDA's requirements on these subjects were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 as the equivalent point for schools whose year begins in April. A tutor who has worked here does not need to be told that these lessons exist.

The rules around them are specific, and they limit what any outside tutor can properly do. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language is used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two further details change how a week can be planned. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run for at least 25 minutes. For these subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited. The honest consequence is that an outside tutor supports a student's understanding and their work for the school's own course; they do not substitute a syllabus of their own.

For a Diploma family the practical point is time. These lessons occupy timetable minutes that a revision plan has to work around, and a tutor who ignores them will propose a week that does not exist. Ask which Arabic stream your child is in before anything is scheduled.

sections.heading: The questions an experienced tutor asks in DP1 because the equivalency office will ask them later
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the step that decides whether a school-leaving certificate is recognised for use in the UAE, and it is routinely discovered late. An experienced tutor working with a UAE family raises it in the first year, not the last term, because the documents come from different bodies on different timetables and because some of the requirements can only be satisfied by sitting a test that has to be booked in advance.

The British-track requirements were set out publicly in July 2026: a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause is where a competitor page has gone wrong by telling UAE candidates they need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, excluding those two.

For the American track the same reporting set out English proficiency as a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB Diploma we publish no points threshold at all, because we have not read one on an official Ministry page and an unsourced number in this position is worse than no number. Verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority, and treat any tutoring company that quotes one without a source with suspicion. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: The boundary an experienced tutor has already been asked to cross
paragraphs: Every tutor who has worked in this market for any length of time has been asked, politely and usually late at night, to do slightly more than teach. The internal assessment is due on Sunday, the student is struggling, and the parent would like the tutor to tidy it up. The answer has to be the same every time, and knowing how to give that answer without losing the family is itself a form of experience. The reason is not squeamishness. Work that must be the student's own is declared as the student's own by the student and their school, and a breach is an academic-honesty matter that can cost a diploma.

There is a market for the other thing. A page found in this research sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is a service we will not provide at any price, and the practical risk to a family is not the money. Submitted work that is not the student's own exposes the student to a malpractice finding at the point where the qualification is being awarded, which is the worst possible moment for it to surface.

What a tutor may properly do is substantial, and families often underestimate it. A tutor can explain what each criterion asks for and how many marks hang on it. They can interrogate a research question until it is answerable with the data a school can actually collect. They can read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is weak and why. They can teach the statistics, the lab technique or the referencing convention. They can ask the questions a supervisor asks, and they can tell a student that a section is not yet good enough without rewriting it for them.

The distinction holds for papers too. We reference official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes and point to where a board publishes them; we do not reproduce or supply those materials. Both halves of that position come from the same place: the student's work and the board's material belong to the student and the board, not to the tutor.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for experience, and what each band actually buys
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The figures below are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026, with the provider named. They are the market, not our price list. We publish them because a parent cannot judge whether an hourly rate is reasonable without knowing the bands, and because the relationship between price and experience in this market is real but loose.

Budget online tuition runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between about AED 150 and 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A visiting tutor at a UAE address runs higher, between roughly AED 180 and 500, with Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table putting in-home work at AED 180 to 350 and some home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work sits around AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly packages appear too: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

The useful question is what moves a rate inside those bands. Level does, because Higher Level in a scarce subject has fewer people able to teach it. Scarcity of the subject itself does, which is why a Higher Level Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specialist is harder to book than an English one. Format does, because travel is paid for whether or not it appears as a line on the invoice. Time of year does, because demand rises as a session approaches. Years of experience correlate with price less tightly than any of those, which is precisely why the number of years is a poor thing to buy on.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page. What we do publish is the market, the fact that the first lesson is a free trial with no payment taken beforehand and no obligation to continue, and a quoted figure in AED in writing before anything is booked.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live online, when experience is the scarce thing
paragraphs: Searches for an experienced IB tutor in the UAE are often really searches for somebody who will arrive at the door. That is a reasonable thing to want and a real market: the published in-home band runs from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour visits appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. The honest answer is that IB Gram does not provide it anywhere in the Emirates. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and no page of ours will tell a UAE family otherwise.

The case for online delivery here is not about convenience. It is about what a distance filter does to a pool that is already thin. Requiring a tutor to be physically present at a given address at 5pm on a Tuesday selects for adults who live nearby and are free then. Requiring that they have taught Higher Level Physics through several cohorts selects for a much smaller group, scattered across the country and beyond it. You can satisfy one condition or the other. For common subjects the two groups overlap enough that it hardly matters; for Higher Level sciences, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Economics at Higher Level or a less-taught language, they barely overlap at all.

The arithmetic of time favours online too, in a way that shows up in the plan rather than the invoice. A visiting arrangement bundles travel into the evening at both ends, which pushes families towards one long weekly session. Live video makes two shorter sessions a week practical, and for consolidation work two thirty-minute contacts usually beat one ninety-minute block. Rescheduling behaves differently as well: a missed slot can move within the same week rather than waiting for the tutor's route to come round again.

Where in-person genuinely wins is with a young child who needs an adult in the room, or a student who cannot work independently on a screen. We say so rather than arguing against it. The table sets out what changes between the two arrangements when the thing you are buying is experience.

sections.heading: When nobody with that experience is free, and what we say instead
paragraphs: No provider in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, which is a strange silence in a market where niche Higher Level subjects plainly outnumber the people able to teach them. Our position is to say it plainly. Some requests cannot be matched immediately, and the common ones are predictable: Higher Level Physics and Chemistry in exam term, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, a less widely taught language, Computer Science at Higher Level, and any request for a specific weekday slot between four and six in the afternoon Gulf Standard Time, which is when most of the country wants a lesson.

When that happens there are four honest options and we will tell you which apply. A different slot with the right specialist, often earlier or later in the same week. A short wait, with a date rather than a vague assurance. A generalist who can hold the content while the specialist slot opens, described as exactly that and not dressed up as a specialist. Or nothing from us, with the reason stated, which is better than an unsuitable match billed at a specialist rate.

What we will not do is put a tutor in front of your child on the basis that they are free. A mismatch costs more than the fee: it costs the weeks during which the real problem went undiagnosed, and in DP2 those weeks are not recoverable. This is also why the first lesson is a trial, with no payment taken before it and no obligation afterwards. The trial exists so that the diagnosis arrives before the commitment, and so that a family who was told their child's problem is command terms can hear whether the tutor reaches the same conclusion from the same script.

If the match turns out to be wrong after a few sessions, say so and we will change it. Judging a tutor on one session is unfair to both sides; judging them on a term is expensive. Three or four sessions is usually enough to see whether the diagnosis was right and whether the student is doing something differently as a result.

process.title: Tell us the school, the subject and the component
process.description: The school tells us which authority holds its file and which internal deadlines apply. The subject and level tell us who could teach it. The component tells us what the work is: a Higher Level paper, an internal assessment criterion, a command-term problem. Those three facts are what turn a request into a match rather than a referral to whoever is free.

process.title: Send recent work rather than a description of it
process.description: A marked script, a report or a draft is worth more than a summary of how things are going. Experienced tutors read scripts for patterns: rounding, units, command terms, blank final parts, criterion losses. The diagnosis that comes out of twenty minutes with real work is what the trial lesson is then built around, so the first session starts at the problem.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before paying anything
process.description: The first lesson is a trial, with no payment taken beforehand and no obligation to continue. Watch for one thing: does the tutor name the cause of the lost marks and give your child something specific to do differently? A pleasant hour of revision is not a diagnosis. You will have a figure in AED in writing before any paid session is booked.

process.title: Agree a plan with dates attached to it
process.description: A plan should name the component, the sessions per week, what the first four weeks will cover and which of your school's deadlines it is built around. Ramadan slots, mock weeks and the exam block go in at this point rather than being absorbed later. If the time available is too short to change the outcome, this is where you should be told.

process.title: Review after three or four sessions, and change the match if it is wrong
process.description: Three or four sessions is long enough to see whether the diagnosis held and whether the student is working differently. We would rather change the tutor at that point than let a mismatch run to the end of term. Tell us what is not working and the next match is made on that information rather than on availability.

whyPoints.title: Experience quoted in cohorts and sessions
whyPoints.description: You will be told which syllabus and level a tutor last taught, and which session that cohort sat, instead of a round number of years. That is the information that tells you whether the experience matches your child's paper, and it is specific enough to be wrong, which is why most of this market avoids giving it.

whyPoints.title: The regulator named correctly for your emirate
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry govern different schools and different things. We name the one that holds your school's file and say what it controls. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them and says so, which is more than several pages in this search can claim.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The rates on this page are other providers' published numbers, read in October 2026, with the provider named. We do not present them as ours and we do not invent a median. Three of the six competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in a currency UAE families do not pay in.

whyPoints.title: A coursework line that does not move
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, interrogate research questions and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. Nobody supplies text or finished coursework, at any price. There is a market in this region doing the opposite, and the risk of buying it lands on the student at the moment their qualification is awarded.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated once, plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for working and notes kept afterwards. Nobody is sent to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying this clearly is how a family avoids discovering it after a payment has been made.

whyPoints.title: Unavailability disclosed, not disguised
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for the subject, level and slot you need, you will be told that, with the options and a date. A mismatch costs more than the fee because it costs the weeks in which the real problem went undiagnosed, and in the second Diploma year those weeks do not come back.

faqs.question: How many Diploma cohorts does ten years of IB teaching actually cover?
faqs.answer: Four or five, if the teaching was continuous and in the same programme. The Diploma runs on a two-year cycle, so a complete cohort means taking a group from subject choice through the internal assessment and mocks to the papers and results. Ten years of continuous Diploma teaching also means nine or ten May sessions seen. The figure drops sharply if some of those years were spent on another curriculum, at a different level, or in a non-teaching role. Ask for cohorts and sessions rather than years, and ask which subject and level each one was in.

faqs.question: Does teaching experience from another country transfer to a UAE IB classroom?
faqs.answer: The subject and assessment part transfers almost entirely. A Higher Level Chemistry teacher from Singapore or the UK knows the same syllabus, the same criteria and the same places marks are lost. What does not transfer is the system around it: which authority licenses your school, that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit on the timetable beside the Diploma, how Ministry of Education equivalency works, and that exam centres are allocated to administrative zones. Those take a year or two of working here to learn, and they are the part a family notices when planning a week or a document file.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who taught IGCSE for years automatically experienced with the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common mismatch in the market. The subject content overlaps, so the tutor will be comfortable explaining the material. The assessment does not overlap. Internal assessment criteria and their mark allocations, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, Higher Level paper 3 and the points structure are all specific to the Diploma, and a strong IGCSE teacher may never have taught any of them. If your child is in DP1 or DP2, ask which Diploma cohorts the tutor has taught and which components they have marked work against.

faqs.question: What should an experienced tutor already know about our school before the first session?
faqs.answer: Which authority holds its file, so advice is given in the right vocabulary. Which board it uses for IGCSE if a younger child is involved, since Cambridge and Pearson set different papers and different dates. Which Higher Level subjects it actually runs this year, because the published list and the staffed list are not always the same. When its internal coursework deadlines fall, which the school sets rather than the IB. And which Arabic stream your child sits in. A tutor who asks those questions at the start is working from the system your child is actually inside.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects have the thinnest supply of experienced teachers in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics and Chemistry, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science at Higher Level and the less widely taught languages. The reason is structural: the IB accounts for roughly 7% of Dubai's private-school roll, so Diploma teachers are a minority of a large teaching market, and Higher Level specialists in those subjects are a minority of that minority. Expect a shorter list of candidates, less flexibility on the afternoon slot everybody wants, and a genuine wait at exam time. That scarcity is also the strongest argument for delivering lessons online.

faqs.question: Our child's school opened this year. Does that change the experience we should look for?
faqs.answer: It changes what the school can give you and therefore what you need from outside it. Dubai added six private schools in 2025-26 and opens seven more for 2026-27, three of them IB. A new school is staffing Diploma classes from the same pool as everybody else, and in the first cohort there is no local history of what the internal deadlines look like in practice or how a mock compares with the real thing. A tutor who has taken several cohorts through, anywhere, supplies exactly that missing pattern.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a tutor knows which authority inspects our school?
faqs.answer: It matters for the advice you get. KHDA oversees private education in Dubai, ADEK handles licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA regulates Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, while the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A tutor who names the wrong body is describing a school system your child does not attend.

faqs.question: What does experience with the Internal Assessment look like in a session?
faqs.answer: It looks like criterion letters and numbers rather than general encouragement. An experienced tutor can say which criterion a draft is losing marks under, how many marks that criterion carries, and what a stronger response to it contains in writing. Before data collection they interrogate the research question until it is answerable with what a school lab can actually produce, which is where most of the eventual damage is done or avoided. They read what the student has written and feed back on it. They do not supply text, and the work submitted is the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: Can an experienced tutor predict the grade our child will finish with?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so is a reason for caution rather than confidence. What experience does buy is a realistic read of distance: which components are costing marks, whether the cause is content, technique or timing, and whether the weeks remaining are enough to change it. That read is useful precisely because it is honest about the cases where it is not enough. No tutor should promise a score, a points total or a grade improvement, and no provider should publish a success statistic without saying how many students it covers and when it was measured.

faqs.question: How much more does the UAE market charge for an experienced subject specialist?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online tuition at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, and IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. A visiting tutor at a UAE address sits at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 table at AED 180 to 350. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. Level, subject scarcity, format and time of year move a rate more than years of experience do.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's experience change the permit they need to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. The requirement is the same whatever the experience. Private tuition work permits were introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and it covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own channels, where the service is listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the permit's code of conduct also restricts tutoring students from the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: Does experience of Arabic and Islamic Education matter if our child only needs maths help?
faqs.answer: It matters for the plan, not for the maths. Those lessons are mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools and they occupy real timetable minutes, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A tutor who does not know they are there will propose a week that does not fit. It also matters if you later want support in them: schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in three of those subjects, teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need the appropriate KHDA approval, and using different or additional content needs prior Ministry permission.

faqs.question: Has an experienced tutor seen the Ministry of Education equivalency paperwork before?
faqs.answer: Somebody who has taken UAE cohorts through to results will have watched families go through it, which is why the question gets raised in DP1 rather than after results day. The British track, as reported in July 2026, asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the IB Diploma we publish no points figure, because none has been read on an official Ministry page. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What experience of the November session should we ask about?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether the tutor has taught a November cohort, because most UAE candidates sit May and a tutor's experience often follows that pattern. The practical differences are in the calendar rather than the content: internal deadlines, mock timing and the revision block all sit in different months, and a student retaking after May has a compressed run at it. Cambridge and Pearson also run their own November series for IGCSE, with dates published on their sites. We do not publish IB session dates here, because they should be confirmed with your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: If the right specialist lives outside our emirate, how does the lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: Over live video, one-to-one, in a Gulf Standard Time slot agreed with you. The tutor and student share a screen and work on the same page, so a maths solution or a chemistry mechanism is written out and annotated rather than described. Work can be photographed and marked up in the session, and the notes stay available afterwards. Nothing about the arrangement depends on which emirate anyone is in, which is the point: it is how a family in Fujairah or Ras Al Khaimah reaches a Higher Level specialist at the same rate as a family in Dubai.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we watch before judging whether the experience is real?
faqs.answer: Three or four. One is too few to be fair, and a term is an expensive way to find out. In the trial lesson, which is free and taken before any payment, look for a named cause rather than a general diagnosis: command terms, units, timing per mark, a specific criterion. By the third or fourth session the student should be doing something identifiably different, and you should be able to say what it is. If you cannot, tell us and the match changes.

faqs.question: What happens when no tutor with that experience is free in the week we need?
faqs.answer: We say so. The predictable shortages are Higher Level Physics and Chemistry in exam term, Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Computer Science, the less widely taught languages, and the weekday slot between four and six in the afternoon. The options are a different slot with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date, a generalist described honestly as a holding measure, or nothing from us with the reason given. Putting a free tutor in front of your child is how families lose the weeks during which the real problem goes undiagnosed.

experienced-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start by making the experience specific
experienced-ib-tutor.closingBody: Tell us the school, the subject, the level and the component that is costing marks, and send a recent marked script or draft. We will name the authority that holds your school's file, say who could teach that component and which cohorts they have taken through, and arrange a free trial lesson with no payment taken beforehand. If the time left is too short to change the outcome, or if nobody with the right experience is free in the slot you need, you will hear that instead of a sales pitch. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we run only in India.

experienced-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at the tiers UAE centres actually enter. Each profile names the syllabuses taught through to a final series, so a match can be made on the code printed on your child's statement of entry rather than on a subject label alone.

intro.heading: Experience in IGCSE is counted in series, not in years
paragraphs: Ten years in a classroom and ten IGCSE series are not the same quantity. Most UAE centres enter their main cohort for one series a year, usually June, so a school teacher's decade covers roughly ten sets of entries, ten mock windows and ten results days. A tutor who also prepares November candidates and private candidates for the March series sees the calendar from more angles in less time. When a family asks for an experienced IGCSE tutor in the UAE, the useful question is not how long someone has taught. It is how many times they have stood at each of the dates that cannot be moved.

Those dates are public and they are not negotiable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series as well, and it allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May or June and again in November. For the Cambridge March 2027 series the board published a final entry deadline of 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, and the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. The entry closes before the exam period even begins.

That geometry is what separates a tutor who has run the year from one who has not. An inexperienced plan works through the syllabus in the order the textbook prints it and arrives at paper technique in April. An experienced plan reads the statement of entry first, notes which components carry the coursework and practical marks and when the school wants them, and schedules the irreversible things first. The tier decision, the coursework deadline and the entry itself all have owners who are not the tutor and not the parent, and every one of them closes earlier than families expect.

Delivery matters less than people think and more than providers admit. Every lesson IB Gram arranges for a family in the Emirates is one-to-one and delivered over live video. Home visits are part of what we do in India, not here, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address. The reason is not cost. A family in Fujairah looking for someone who has taken Chemistry 0620 candidates through four series is choosing from a national pool rather than from whoever is within a half-hour drive, and in the final term the hour that would have gone to the drive goes to a timed paper instead.

What follows is the IGCSE year laid out backwards, from the last paper to the first conversation in Year 10, with the market rates UAE providers publish, the permit a tutor must hold, the five windows that open around results day, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that reaches back into subject choices made two years earlier. Every figure is attributed to whoever published it and dated. Where the source is a board, the official timetable is the thing to read before acting, because provisional dates get revised and ours are not a substitute for your centre's.
