sections.heading: Permit, qualification, examiner: three claims, and the one we will not make
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school pupils aged 15 to 18 and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount should be quoted to you.

A permit is not a qualification, and neither is a company permit. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit says a centre may operate. It says nothing about whether the person in front of your child has taught Higher Level Economics.

The third claim is the one this page declines. IB Gram does not describe its tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for an individual, and because examiner status is routinely used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content that no examiner has. What we will tell you is the subject, the level and the teaching history, and the ADEK position worth knowing: its professional-ethics rules, as reported in the press, prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and which band buys a specialist
paragraphs: These are market rates, published by other providers, not IB Gram's price list. Reading them matters because the spread is enormous and the labels are unregulated: the same hour is advertised at AED 45 and at AED 650, and nothing in either advert explains the difference. Figures below are drawn from competitor pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, as read in October 2026.

Monthly patterns in the same market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set that against school fees that KHDA confirmed in May 2026 will not increase for private schools in Dubai for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

The useful question is not which band is cheapest but which band buys a subject specialist at the level your child is taking. Below roughly AED 150 an hour the market is largely university students and generalists, which can be the right purchase for Standard Level consolidation and is a poor one for Higher Level content. IB Gram does not publish an hourly list on this page; the first lesson is free, with no card required, and the rate is quoted for the actual subject and level after that.

sections.heading: A tutor at a UAE address against live one-to-one online
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market here and the question deserves a straight answer. A visiting tutor in Dubai or Abu Dhabi charges between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour, often with a two-hour minimum, and the pool a family can actually draw from is whoever is willing to drive to that address in the evening traffic. For a Standard Level maths top-up that pool is usually adequate. For Chemistry Higher Level, or Computer Science, or Economics Higher Level in Fujairah, it frequently contains nobody.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online IB tuition over live video. Tutors are not sent to a UAE address; home visits are part of the service only in India. The case for the online format here is not that it is a cheaper substitute. It is that the constraint which decides the outcome is subject match at the right level, and geography is what breaks subject match. An Al Ain family gets the Higher Level specialist rather than the nearest available adult.

There is a second, duller advantage. A shared screen is better than a shared table for the specific work that moves IB grades: putting a mark scheme and a student's script side by side, annotating in two colours, and saving the result so the student can re-read it the night before. Session recordings and notes survive; a kitchen-table conversation does not. A student who can re-read last week's annotated script before this week's lesson arrives already halfway through it.

sections.heading: Three bodies set the dates, and one gives your centre a zone
paragraphs: UAE families often sit two awarding bodies across one school career, and the calendars behave differently. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that the correct version of the timetable for your zone is used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used.

The Cambridge March 2027 series shows why entry deadlines sit so far ahead of the papers: the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official PDF is what a plan should be built on.

For the IB, this page deliberately stops short. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is the right anchor for a two-year plan, but ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. So no IB date is published here. Ask the school's IB coordinator, or read ibo.org directly, and treat any tutoring website that prints precise IB dates without a source as having guessed.

sections.heading: The equivalency file: five subjects, grade E, and two exclusions
paragraphs: A UAE secondary certificate needs federal equivalency before universities here treat it as one, and the requirements are published per curriculum track. On the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five.

That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely, because at least one page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. On the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the IB there is a gap, and this page leaves it a gap. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so no IB equivalency figure is published here and none should be taken from a tutoring site. Open the file with the Ministry or your emirate's attestation authority in the first year of the Diploma rather than after results day, and let the official channel tell you what the certificate needs. IB Gram describes this process; it does not perform it, submit it or guarantee its outcome, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the test a tutoring provider cannot half-pass
paragraphs: Internally assessed work is the student's own, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice with consequences that fall on the candidate rather than on the provider who caused it. That asymmetry is the whole reason to be strict about it. A provider in this market advertises finished internal assessments at AED 3,750; buying one risks a diploma for the price of a few tutoring hours, and there is no version of that trade that favours the family.

The permitted boundary is narrower than most advertising implies, and it is also genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, help a student narrow a research question to something the mark scheme can reward, discuss a plan before data is collected, and give feedback as questions on a draft the student produced. A tutor may not supply sentences for submission, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, hand over a finished piece of coursework, or take a Personal Project off a student's hands.

Two practical habits keep a family on the right side of it. Keep the student's own drafts dated, so authorship is demonstrable if a coordinator asks. And declare outside support honestly when the school asks about it; the question exists precisely so that legitimate tutoring can be acknowledged. Schools are also not permitted to receive reproduced syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables from a tutor; those are cited and linked from the official sites, not handed over as downloads.

process.title: Tell us the school, not just the subject
process.description: The first message should name the school, the emirate, the year group, the subject and the level. That tells us which authority inspects the school, which awarding body is likely in play, and how much of the week the mandatory Ministry subjects already hold. It takes a parent two minutes and removes a fortnight of guessing.

process.title: A free first lesson with a marked diagnostic
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing and requires no card. It is not a sales call: the tutor sets real past-paper questions, marks them against the published criteria, and says where the marks are going. If the diagnostic shows the problem is scheduling or coursework sequencing rather than content, we say so.

process.title: Read the school's calendar before the plan is written
process.description: We ask for the school's own internal deadline list, the mock window and the examination series the student is entered for. Internal deadlines are set by the school, not the IB, and they are what a revision plan collides with. The plan is then built backwards from those dates.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives March
process.description: A weekly slot is chosen against the commute, the after-school timetable and Ramadan hours rather than against the tutor's convenience. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan without a change in rate. A slot that only works in October is not a slot.

process.title: Review against marks, and change the tutor if needed
process.description: Progress is reviewed on marked work and on the criteria that are still costing bands, not on how the lessons felt. If the match is wrong, a different specialist takes over and the diagnostic carries across so the new tutor does not start from nothing.

whyPoints.title: The authority above your school is named, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts by identifying which of the five bodies holds the school's file and what its published report says about the relevant subject. IB Gram holds no permit, approval or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and does not claim any.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, not on distance
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to the course and the level, so an Al Ain or Fujairah family reaches the same Higher Level specialist a Dubai family does. Where no specialist is free for a subject and level, we say that plainly rather than putting a generalist in the slot and hoping.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory subjects are treated as real
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit on the timetable because the school's licence requires them, and support for them runs on the school's own set material. For these subjects KHDA prohibits different or additional content without prior MoE permission, so no substitute scheme is offered.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than as our price. No satisfaction percentage, star rating or score statistic appears here, because none could be produced with its sample size and method.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support stops where honesty does
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is supplied for submission, and we would rather lose the booking than put a diploma at risk. Dates we cannot source, including IB session dates, are left off the page rather than guessed.

faqs.question: What does expertise in the UAE school system actually consist of?
faqs.answer: Four things, in practice. Knowing which of the five authorities inspects your child's school and what its report said. Knowing what the mandatory Ministry subjects take out of the week, and that their content cannot be substituted. Knowing which awarding body and series the student is entered for, and that Cambridge allocates centres to one of six timetable zones. And knowing that an IB or IGCSE certificate needs federal equivalency before a UAE university treats it as a secondary qualification. A tutor can be excellent at Chemistry Higher Level and know none of this, which is how plans collide with coursework deadlines in February.

faqs.question: Is there a public register where I can look up an IB tutor's credentials?
faqs.answer: No single register exists. There are three separate things to check and none of them is one list. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is the legal permission to tutor privately; ask the tutor to show it. A teaching qualification is a document the tutor holds and can send you. IB course experience is not registered anywhere, so it is established by asking how many cohorts they have taught at that level and by a marked diagnostic in the first lesson. Treat any claim you cannot test as unproven, including examiner claims.

faqs.question: Does the authority that inspects my child's school also sign off its assessment methods?
faqs.answer: In two emirates, yes. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so assessment arrangements are not the school's alone to change. KHDA in Dubai oversees the quality of private education and sets mandatory-subject requirements including instructional time. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly. That is why a tutor proposing to replace the school's scheme of work is often proposing something the school cannot accept.

faqs.question: Dubai is adding 16,846 private school places. Does that make a Diploma specialist easier to find?
faqs.answer: Not immediately. Seven private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, and six opened the year before while enrolment rose 6%. More school places create more Diploma candidates faster than they create experienced Diploma teachers, and the IB accounts for about 7% of Dubai's private-school enrolment, so the specialist pool for one Higher Level subject stays thin. Expansion helps with fees, choice and commute times. It does not solve the problem of finding someone who has taught Computer Science Higher Level through a full second year.

faqs.question: Our school's Diploma cohort is its first. Who holds the past papers and the mark archive?
faqs.answer: Nobody at the school yet, and that is the honest answer worth planning around. A new IB school has no shelf of previously marked internal assessments to show a student what a top band reads like, no history of how its predicted grades have tracked against final results, and often no teacher on site who has taken a cohort through the second year there. Ask the coordinator how many of the teaching team have. Outside support in a first cohort is largely supplying that missing institutional memory: exemplar standards, realistic timelines and criterion-level feedback.

faqs.question: Does a 40-minute school lesson mean a tutoring session should be 40 minutes too?
faqs.answer: No. The 40-minute unit is a regulatory measure, not a pedagogical one: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs under 25 minutes. For one-to-one work, 60 minutes suits weekly consolidation and 90 suits exam-technique or coursework sessions where a full paper has to be marked and reworked. During Ramadan, shorter post-Iftar sessions usually work better than long ones.

faqs.question: Is Islamic Education taught in English for a non-Arab child, and does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: For non-Arab pupils, KHDA requires Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies to be taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language, which in most IB schools means English. Arab pupils receive Islamic Education and Arabic as a first language in Standard Arabic, and the two groups must be taught in separate classes; combined classes are strictly prohibited. It changes tutoring in one specific way: support should match the stream and language the school has placed the child in, and work from that stream's set material rather than a translation of the other one.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not describe any of its tutors as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for an individual, and an unevidenced claim is worth nothing to you. The claim is also often used to imply privileged access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, which no examiner appointment provides. What we will tell you instead is checkable: the subject, the level, how many cohorts the tutor has taught, and a marked diagnostic in the free first lesson. If another provider makes the examiner claim, ask what evidence exists for the named subject and component.

faqs.question: A tutor says they hold a KHDA permit. What is that permit actually for?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly for a centre rather than a person. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit says premises may operate. It says nothing about the individual teaching your child. The permit that covers an individual giving private lessons is the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Ask which of the two is being referred to, and ask to see it.

faqs.question: What should a tutoring quote show me in writing before we pay anything?
faqs.answer: Six things. The named subject and level, not just the board. The session length and the rate per session, with whether VAT is included and a TRN if one is held. The tutor's permit position. Who teaches if that tutor becomes unavailable. The cancellation terms, including who absorbs a late cancellation. And the conditions attached to any free trial, stated on the same page as the word free. If a quote arrives without the subject level on it, the provider has not yet matched anyone to your child.

faqs.question: Which price band buys a subject specialist rather than a general tutor?
faqs.answer: In the UAE market, specialist IB and IGCSE support is advertised around AED 200 to AED 450 or more an hour, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at 200 to 450+. Qualified but curriculum-general teachers sit roughly AED 150 to AED 300 online, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Below about AED 150 the market is mostly university students, which can suit Standard Level consolidation and rarely suits Higher Level content. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Are these lessons online, and why does IB Gram not offer visits in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: All UAE teaching is one-to-one online IB tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of the service only in India. The reason is not cost: it is that subject match at the right level is what changes marks, and geography is the thing that breaks subject match. A family in Al Ain or Fujairah reaches the same Higher Level specialist a family in Dubai does. A shared screen also beats one printed copy of a mark scheme between two people, and the annotated version survives the session.

faqs.question: How do I tell an exam date that is sourced from one that is guesswork?
faqs.answer: Check whether the page names the awarding body's own document. Cambridge publishes key dates per series: for March 2027 the examination period is 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027 and results on Direct 13 May. Pearson publishes final and provisional timetables, with the November 2026 International GCSE timetable running to 19 November 2026. For the IB, ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB date appears on this page at all. A site printing precise IB dates without citing ibo.org has guessed.

faqs.question: Should we handle the Ministry of Education equivalency file ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the official channel, and start it in the first Diploma year rather than after results. The requirements are published per track: the British route needs five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E. No IB points threshold has been read on moe.gov.ae, so do not accept one from a tutoring website. IB Gram describes the process and does not submit, perform or guarantee it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: A tutor offered to take my son's Extended Essay from first draft to finish. Should we accept?
faqs.answer: No. Internally assessed work must be the student's own, and the consequences of malpractice fall on the candidate rather than on whoever offered the shortcut. One provider in this market advertises finished internal assessments at AED 3,750; that risks a whole diploma. What a tutor may legitimately do is teach the content, explain what each criterion is asking for, help narrow a research question, discuss a plan before data is collected, and return feedback as questions on a draft your son produced. Keep his dated drafts, and declare outside support when the coordinator asks.

faqs.question: Our child's school is inspected by the Ministry rather than KHDA. Does that limit anything?
faqs.answer: It changes where you read the inspection report and who you write to, not what your child can achieve. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, so inspection and curriculum questions go federal rather than to an emirate authority. What does differ is local supply: these emirates have the smallest IB cohorts in the country, so a Higher Level specialist is genuinely hard to arrange locally twice a week. Online delivery removes that constraint, which is why it matters more here than in Dubai.

expert-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the school, then the subject
expert-ib-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an expert IB tutor in the UAE, the useful first message names the school and the emirate as well as the subject and the level. That tells us which authority inspects the school, which awarding body and series are in play, and how much of the week is already committed to the mandatory Ministry subjects. The first lesson is free, with no card required: a real diagnostic on past-paper questions, marked against the published criteria, and an honest answer about whether the problem is content, technique or the calendar. Lessons then run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the slot chosen to survive March.

female-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The specialists below cover IB Diploma and MYP subjects for UAE families. Where a family asks for a female IB tutor, we say plainly whether one is free for that subject and level this term, which Gulf Standard Time slots are open, and what the alternative is if nobody is. Availability is a fact, not a sales line.

intro.heading: The two things a UAE parent is really checking
paragraphs: Parents in the UAE ask for a female IB tutor for reasons that are rarely the same twice. A Grade 11 girl at a Dubai IB school may simply find it easier to admit she has not understood binomial expansion to a woman. A family following a more conservative household practice may want a female tutor for one-to-one work with a daughter as a matter of course. An Arabic-speaking household may be looking for a woman who can teach Islamic Education and Arabic as a first language, because those two subjects are compulsory in every private school in Dubai whatever curriculum the school is licensed to teach. All three requests are reasonable, and none of them is a judgement about teaching quality.

What those requests run into is a supply problem that no page competing for this search describes honestly. A gender preference narrows an already narrow pool. There are not many people in this country who can teach Physics at Higher Level to the standard a 7 demands, and asking that the same person also be female, free at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, and not employed by your own daughter's school cuts the list again at every step. An agency promising an instant match in any subject with any preference is promising something the arithmetic will not support.

The second question is legal, and almost nobody in this market touches it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the federal portal at u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 can all apply. A parent who knows that can ask one question which separates a serious tutor from an opportunist.

Then there is the school system itself. Your child's school is not overseen by a single national body. Dubai answers to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Those bodies set different reporting rhythms, consider fee changes on different terms, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah approve curricula and assessment methods outright. A tutoring plan that ignores which authority your school reports to will keep missing deadlines that the school does not control.

So this page is built around the regulatory and school-system context a UAE family cannot opt out of. It covers who may lawfully tutor and how you verify it, what the compulsory UAE subjects do to a Diploma week, what the market charges in AED and why a preference moves waiting time rather than price, where the line sits on an Internal Assessment, and what the Ministry of Education wants to see before a certificate is recognised inside the country. Lessons are one-to-one, delivered live online, and scheduled to Gulf Standard Time.

female-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three IB programmes UAE schools run most, plus the Career-related Programme where a school licenses it. The note under each programme is about this country specifically: which authority reports on the school, where the mandatory UAE subjects sit in the week, and at which point a request for a female tutor is most commonly made.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP sets no external examinations. Learning is organised into transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and progress is reported against conceptual understanding and learner-profile attributes rather than subject marks. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the written and spoken English a unit of inquiry quietly assumes. A parent who cannot find a grade on a PYP report is not missing anything: the programme does not produce one, which is also why a problem can sit unnoticed for two years.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai PYP school still has to deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies under KHDA rules, and KHDA calculates the required instructional time in 40-minute lesson units. For many families this is where a female tutor is first requested, usually for Arabic reading with a younger daughter who started the language two years behind her classmates and has been quietly behind ever since.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by subject-specific boundaries. There is no past-paper bank to drill, which is exactly what unsettles families arriving from a CBSE or British background. The Personal Project in the final year is the first piece of work that must demonstrably be the student's own, supervised rather than taught, and it is the first time a UAE student meets a formal academic-honesty declaration.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 11 is the pressure point in the UAE, because one year carries the Personal Project, the subject choices that lock in Higher Level options, and in Dubai the mandatory subject load KHDA requires. Families wanting a female tutor for a daughter often start here, and ask for someone who can hold a student through the Personal Project process without touching the writing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject and is marked by the teacher against published criteria before external moderation. The May session is the one UAE schools sit. Most of the grade is settled by work done between October and March of the final year, not by revision in April, which is why a January start and an April start are different purchases.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma students carry the mandatory UAE subjects on top of six IB courses in most private schools, which is why a Diploma week here is heavier than the same week in London. Scheduling matters as much as total hours: a session set at 5pm or 6pm Gulf Standard Time, after the school run and before the evening goes, gets used. One pushed to 9pm in the week an IA draft is due does not.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, and a core of personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. A smaller number of UAE schools license it, usually alongside the Diploma. Support concentrates on the Diploma courses the student has taken and on the reflective project, which is supervised work and must remain the student's own from research question to final draft.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP enrolment in the UAE is small, a gender-specific request is harder to fill here than at Diploma level, and we say so at the point of asking rather than after a deposit. Where no female specialist covers the Diploma course a CP student is taking, the honest options are a male specialist, a stated wait, or a different session time.

female-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects UAE families request most. Each line says what the subject actually assesses and where marks go missing, because that is what tells a parent whether one hour a week will move anything. Where a family wants a female IB Diploma tutor, availability for that specific subject and level is confirmed at the enquiry rather than assumed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, two at Standard, plus a 20-mark Exploration. Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving paper and the one that separates a 6 from a 7. Marks go missing in proof, in complex numbers, and in criterion E of the Exploration, where students do mathematics below the level of their own course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Most UAE students who move from Analysis to Applications do it in the first term of DP1, usually a term later than they should. The Exploration carries the same 20 marks, and the same trap: a correlation coefficient and a bar chart will not reach the top band.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A concept-led syllabus organised around unity and diversity and form and function. Paper 1 pairs multiple choice with the data-based section; Paper 2 rewards precise reading of command terms. The Scientific Investigation is the internal assessment, and the marks nobody sees coming are in evaluation, where students describe limitations instead of weighing their effect on the conclusion.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most lost marks at Higher Level. The syllabus is structured around structure and reactivity, and questions increasingly ask a student to apply both inside one answer. Higher Level content is examined in the same papers as the core, so a topic skipped in DP1 returns in May with interest.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The gap between a 5 and a 7 is almost always algebra under time pressure rather than conceptual confusion. Fields, circular motion and the Higher Level extensions carry the heaviest mark loss. The internal assessment rewards a tightly controlled question; broad investigations run out of usable data long before they reach a defensible conclusion.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied texts, with the Individual Oral assessed internally and an HL Essay added at Higher Level. Students in UAE schools often read well and write generically. Marks come back for the quality of an argument about the text rather than a summary of it.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: For students who use English confidently but not as a first language. Receptive skills, writing and the individual oral are assessed separately, and the oral is where fluent speakers still lose marks by describing the stimulus instead of arguing from it. Range of vocabulary is marked, and rehearsed phrasing is visible to an examiner immediately.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Two different courses for two different students: ab initio for near-beginners, Arabic B for those with real prior exposure. UAE families often discover in DP1 that a child placed in Arabic B after years in an international school is sitting the harder of the two. This is the subject where a female tutor is requested most often.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and definition precision carry more marks than essay length. Higher Level adds the quantitative paper, which punishes students who learned the diagrams but never the calculations behind them. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, each to a strict word limit and each marked against its own criteria.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-release case study for Paper 1 rewards months of preparation and is routinely left until April. Higher Level Paper 2 includes quantitative work. The Higher Level internal assessment is a research project on a real organisation, which means a research question narrow enough to answer with evidence the student can actually obtain.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Compulsory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students under KHDA rules. Content is set by the Ministry of Education, and schools may not use different or additional material without prior permission. Support here is about the set content and the language of instruction, not enrichment.

female-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Which authority regulates your child's school
female-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: There is no single national schools regulator in the UAE. Five bodies divide the seven emirates between them, and they do not all do the same job. The notes below say who governs what, taken from the federal portal at u.ae, and what each one changes about the way tutoring should be planned.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA also publishes the mandatory-subject requirements every Dubai private school must implement, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by none of the competing tutoring pages examined for this project. Its professional ethics rules are the reason a teacher cannot take payment to tutor a student from their own school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Covered by ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi city, with a smaller Diploma cohort and a much longer travel radius. For families here the online format removes the only genuine constraint on specialist choice, which is how far a tutor is willing to drive on a weekday evening.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit extends to approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is broader than inspection, and worth knowing before assuming a Dubai school's calendar applies here.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, together with Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here often commute into Dubai or Sharjah schools, which pushes a realistic session start past 5.30pm Gulf Standard Time on a normal school day.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah returned no mentions at all across the competitor pages examined for this project, which tells you how thinly this emirate is served.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Private schools come under the federal Ministry of Education. The IB cohort is small and a specialist for a Higher Level science is unlikely to live within driving distance, which makes online delivery a practical answer here rather than a marketing preference.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Families here are the clearest case for the online format: a Chemistry Higher Level specialist, or a female Arabic first-language teacher, is matched on subject and availability rather than on postcode.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of that enrolment. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, creating 16,846 new places. Students we support attend schools including these.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: ADEK territory, and a different rhythm from Dubai: longer distances between communities, a smaller Diploma cohort per school, and ethics rules barring school staff from paid tutoring of their own students. Students we support attend schools including these.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Northern Emirates
schoolClusters.note: Sharjah's authority approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same. Subject specialists are thin on the ground outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi, which is the real reason online matching works here. Students we support attend schools including these.

female-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three or four session patterns cover almost every UAE request. All of them are one-to-one and delivered live online over video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own school material on screen. Group classes are not offered, because the point of a one-to-one hour is that it follows one student's errors.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: One sixty-minute session a week with the same specialist, timed to Gulf Standard Time and set around the school run. This is the pattern that moves a grade, because it tracks the school's own sequence of topics rather than running a parallel syllabus beside it. The tutor reads the last piece of marked work before each session and plans from that, not from a generic scheme.

It is not a substitute for a year of teaching and we say so: a block can repair exam technique and timing, but it cannot install a missing topic list.

sections.heading: What a request for a female IB tutor actually changes
paragraphs: Nothing in the syllabus. Paper weightings, command terms and assessment criteria are identical whoever teaches them, and an examiner cannot tell from a script who sat opposite the student in September. What a preference changes is the arithmetic of the match. The number of people in this country who can teach Physics at Higher Level to the standard a 7 demands is small to begin with. Ask that the same person be female, free at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, and not employed by your daughter's own school, and the list shortens at every step.

That is worth saying plainly because the pages competing for this search do not say it. Three of the six strongest pages in this market publish no price at all, and none of them publishes a coverage limit of any kind. A platform promising any subject with any preference matched immediately is describing a wish rather than a roster. Families asking for female IB tutors in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Sharjah are usually told yes and then handed whoever happens to be free. The result is a trial lesson with the wrong person and a parent who concludes that tutoring does not work.

The reasons behind the request vary, and interrogating them is not our business. Some are about a teenage girl's willingness to admit confusion out loud. Some are about household practice. Some are specific to a subject: a female Arabic as a first language tutor, or a female Islamic Education tutor in Dubai, is requested far more often than a female Economics tutor, because of who teaches those subjects in schools here. We treat the preference as a filter on the match and answer the only question that decides anything, which is whether somebody suitable is free.

So the order of this page is deliberate. Availability first, legality second, cost third. What follows sets out who may lawfully tutor in the UAE and how a parent verifies it, which of five regulators governs your child's school, how the compulsory UAE subjects reshape a Diploma week, what this market charges in AED, and where the line sits on work that must be the student's own.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to tutor your child in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring here is a licensed activity. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits, and the federal portal at u.ae lists them among the permits issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two working day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

u.ae also states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published anywhere official, and a figure circulating online could not be matched to a ministry source, so this page quotes none. What a parent needs from the rule is not an amount but a question: does this person hold the permit, and when does it expire? Anybody who holds it answers in one sentence and without changing the subject.

The second half of the rule is about who a tutor may teach. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi the ADEK professional ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours need the permit in any case. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy document, but the practical effect is the same in every emirate: do not buy your child's own teacher.

A tutoring business is a separate legal animal from an individual tutor. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which begins with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and is renewed annually with the request made at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram runs no premises in the UAE and holds no such permit, which is one reason every lesson for a UAE family is delivered online.

sections.heading: Five regulators, seven emirates, one school report to read
paragraphs: Parents arriving from the UK or India often assume a single national schools inspectorate. The UAE divides that job five ways. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools, covering Al Ain as well as the capital. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Those bodies do not all do identical work. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a far wider remit than inspection. KHDA publishes the mandatory subject requirements every Dubai private school must implement, and confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. ADEK, the regulator of the capital, is named by none of the competing tutoring pages examined for this project.

For a tutoring plan this is not trivia. The authority governing your school influences when reports land, when fee changes are considered, and in two emirates which assessment methods a school may use at all. A plan built around a Dubai school's reporting cycle will be out of step in Sharjah, and a parent who quotes KHDA guidance to an Ajman school is quoting the wrong body. Underneath all of it sits one federal rule: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That rule is why the next section exists.

sections.heading: The compulsory UAE subjects that sit alongside the IB
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. A Diploma student at a Dubai IB school is therefore carrying six IB courses, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, plus the mandatory UAE subjects in the same week. Any tutoring plan treating a UAE Diploma week as equivalent to a London one has already mis-budgeted the student's available hours.

The KHDA mandatory subjects guidelines are specific about organisation, and worth reading before you ask a school a question. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and for non-Arabs Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies are delivered in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details shape what support can honestly look like. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time in 40-minute lesson units, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. Tutoring in this stream therefore follows the set material at the school's pace, and schools must separately ensure their own teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them.

sections.heading: What this market charges, and what a preference does to the number
paragraphs: Nobody competing for these searches publishes a rate table, so here is one, built from what competitors publish on their own pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 figures, read in October 2026. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. The spread is wide for a real reason: an hour with a university student revising IGCSE Maths and an hour with a Diploma specialist dismantling a Physics Higher Level Paper 3 are different products that happen to be sold by the same unit of time. That is what IB tutoring rates in AED look like across this market.

Monthly figures seen in the same market run to roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions with a tutor travelling to the family. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Read those against the school fee they sit beside: KHDA confirmed no fee increase for Dubai private schools in 2026-27, so a tutoring decision this year is not competing with a fee rise.

A gender preference appears in none of these bands, and it should not. What it moves is waiting time. At the qualified-online tier the pool is broad enough that a female IB tutor is usually available within days. At the specialist end, where a subject may have only a handful of people in the country teaching it at Higher Level, a preference can add a week or change the slot you are offered. The same holds for a female IGCSE tutor in the UAE, where the pool is wider because more teachers work to IGCSE level than to Higher Level. IB Gram's own figure comes from a consultation after the free first lesson rather than from a chart, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many sessions are genuinely needed.

sections.heading: A tutor who travels to you, or one-to-one live online
paragraphs: The phrase most UAE parents type is some version of a home tutor, and the request behind it is reasonable. Somebody who travels to the family removes the problem of a teenager who will not settle in front of a screen, and with a younger child it keeps an adult in the room. It also costs more. Market rates for a tutor travelling to a UAE address run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and the difference is mostly the journey rather than the teaching.

Then there is the clock. A 5pm start in a Dubai Marina tower or a Khalifa City villa depends on Sheikh Zayed Road behaving itself, and a tutor who has committed to four families in one evening has to leave each one on time whether or not the student has finished the question. The deeper problem is the pool. A family hiring locally chooses from whoever is willing to drive to their community, which in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Al Ain may be nobody holding a Higher Level science. The same family choosing online chooses from everybody free at that hour.

IB Gram's position is plain and it is the same on all 48 country pages on this site. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and delivered live online over video, on a shared screen with the student's own school material open beside the working. IB Gram does not arrange for anybody to travel to a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. We would rather lose an enquiry that wants a doorbell than take a deposit for something we do not sell. The table sets the two options against each other on the dimensions that actually decide it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: The IB's academic-honesty rules make assessed work the student's own, and the consequences of breaching them land on the student rather than the tutor. That is precisely why this section belongs on a page selling tutoring. Internal assessment carries real weight in every Diploma subject and is marked by the school against published criteria before external moderation, so it is also the part of the course where a parent is most tempted to buy help rather than teaching. At least one page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is a malpractice trigger, and it is not a service we compete to provide.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. A tutor can press on a research question until it is narrow enough to answer with evidence the student can actually obtain. A tutor can explain which criterion the marks hang on, read one draft against those criteria, and say where an argument is unsupported or a limitation has been described rather than weighed. In Mathematics, the twenty marks of the Exploration are divided across five criteria, and criterion E alone, use of mathematics, carries six of them. A student who knows that spends their final fortnight differently.

What a tutor cannot do is write, restructure, rewrite or supply the work, choose the topic, or hand over material a student then presents as their own. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes: we cite the official page and link to it, because reproducing them is a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, something worse. Feedback is given in writing so a school can see exactly what was said and when. If a service offers to produce assessed work for your child, the risk it creates sits with your child's diploma.

sections.heading: The school year, Ramadan and when the work actually happens
paragraphs: The May session is the one UAE Diploma schools sit, and most of a grade is settled between October and March of the final year rather than in April. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay all come due inside that window, which is also when school mock examinations land. These pages publish no IB session or results dates: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and plan backwards from the school's internal deadlines rather than from the examinations.

For IGCSE and A-Level the dates are published, and they are the clearest worked example of how early entries close. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The March 2027 series is examined between 3 February and 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May or June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of a series, so always open the live official timetable rather than trusting a date restated on a tutoring page. Around all of this sits Ramadan: school days shorten, and a Ramadan tutoring schedule normally means an early afternoon slot after a shortened school day, or a post-Iftar session in the evening. Online delivery is what makes either workable, because nobody has to drive.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the number we will not publish
paragraphs: Equivalency is how the Ministry of Education recognises a school certificate for use inside the UAE, and it is the step families discover late. For the British track, the requirements clarified in July 2026 are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at the Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises most families who had assumed the opposite.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. At least one page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The figure reported in July 2026 is five. Publishing the correct number is not a small matter when a family is choosing Year 9 subjects on the strength of it.

The IB row in the table is deliberately unfilled. The source we read states no IB points threshold, and an invented threshold on a page like this would do real damage to a family's planning, so the honest entry is to verify. Check MoE equivalency for IB students on moe.gov.ae, or with the attestation authority in your own emirate, and get the answer in writing before you build subject choices around it. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not a requirement for any of it.
