sections.heading: What happens when no female specialist is free
paragraphs: No page competing in this market discloses a coverage limit, which means every one of them implies full coverage of every subject at every level in every emirate. That is not true of anybody, and it is not true of us. A UAE-based specialist for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, free at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, who is female and not employed by your daughter's school, is a genuinely narrow set. Pretending otherwise produces the familiar sequence: a confident yes, a mismatched first lesson, and a family that gives up on tutoring altogether.

So the answer arrives before the invoice. Within a working day you are told whether a specialist matching your request is free, which Gulf Standard Time slots are open, and where that person is based. If the honest answer is a four-day wait, you get the four days. If the only person covering Chemistry at Higher Level in your slot is male, you are told so and can decide whether the preference or the specialism matters more for that one subject. Keeping the preference for English and Arabic while taking the available Chemistry specialist is a common and perfectly sensible outcome.

Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject at the level required, the lesson is delivered online by an IB specialist based in India, teaching at your Gulf Standard Time slot. We say so before the first lesson rather than letting a family work it out from an accent. That disclosure is the whole point: a family that knows what it is buying can judge it fairly. Online IB tuition in the UAE works because the format makes a tutor's location irrelevant to everything except the clock, and the clock is the part we manage.

sections.heading: Safeguarding, session conduct and the data we hold
paragraphs: A one-to-one lesson with a minor needs rules a parent can check rather than assurances they have to accept. Sessions run on the family's own device, in a shared room if the family prefers, and a parent is welcome to sit in. After every session a written note says what was covered, what was set and what comes next, which gives a parent visibility without turning the hour into a performance. With a Year 12 or 13 student that note is usually more useful than attendance, because a teenager who knows a parent is listening admits to less confusion, not more.

The permit's code of conduct and, in Abu Dhabi, the ADEK professional ethics rules already bar a tutor from serving students enrolled at their own school. We ask that question at the match stage rather than leaving a parent to discover it at a parents' evening. A tutor is also asked which board and level they are currently teaching, because somebody who last taught the Diploma four syllabus revisions ago is a different proposition from somebody marking Higher Level work this term. Neither question is adversarial; both are the kind a school would ask.

Data is the part most tutoring sites skip. Lead forms in this market routinely ask for a child's school, grades and a photograph with no stated purpose at all. Ours asks for the subject, the level, the year group, the board and a parent contact, which is what a match genuinely needs. We hold it under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection, use it to match a specialist and attach session notes to the right student, and delete it on request, session notes included. The privacy link sits on every page of this site.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level, the board and the preference
process.description: One message with the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the year group, the school and the emirate, plus any preference such as a female IB tutor. The emirate matters because it tells us which authority your school reports to and roughly when a session can realistically start on a school day.

process.title: We answer availability before anything else
process.description: Within a working day you learn whether a specialist matching your request is free, at which Gulf Standard Time slots, and from where. If the honest answer is a wait, you get the wait in days. If no UAE-based specialist covers the subject, we say that the tutor would be an IB specialist based in India teaching online.

process.title: A free first lesson of one hour, no card needed
process.description: The specialist works through your child's most recent marked assignment, finds the point where the method breaks down, and says what a term of weekly sessions could realistically change. You get a written plan afterwards whether or not you continue. The condition is simply that this is one lesson, not a trial week.

process.title: A weekly slot and a written note each time
process.description: Sessions run at the same hour each week, planned from the school's own topic sequence rather than a parallel syllabus. After each one a note records what was covered, what was set and what the next session will do. Those notes are what a parent takes into a school meeting instead of an impression.

process.title: Review against the school's own reports
process.description: At the end of each reporting cycle we read the school report with you and decide whether to keep the slot, change the focus, or stop. Stopping is a legitimate outcome. A student who has caught up does not need a standing weekly hour, and we will say when that point has arrived.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, not discovered
whyPoints.description: A gender preference narrows a pool, and narrow pools mean waiting. You get the wait, the slot options and the tutor's location before you pay anything. No page competing for these searches publishes a coverage limit of any kind, which is how families end up with a first lesson that was never going to work.

whyPoints.title: The permit question gets asked for you
whyPoints.description: Every tutor working with UAE families is asked where they stand on the MoHRE private tuition work permit and whether your child is enrolled at their own school. In Abu Dhabi the ADEK professional ethics rules make that second question a live one rather than a formality.

whyPoints.title: Built for five regulators, not one
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education run private education on different terms. A plan assuming a Dubai reporting cycle applies in Sharjah will miss deadlines the school itself does not control.

whyPoints.title: The compulsory UAE subjects are in the plan
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are not optional extras in a Dubai private school; they sit in the same week as six IB courses. We budget a student's hours around that load instead of pretending a Diploma week here looks like a Diploma week in London.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions a research question, reads one draft against the published criteria, and gives feedback in writing a school can see. A tutor does not write, restructure or supply assessed work. That boundary is on this page because at least one page ranking for these searches offers the opposite.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure carries a source and a date
whyPoints.description: The rates here belong to the market, attributed to the page or table that published them in October 2026. Our own number comes out of a consultation after the free first lesson rather than from a chart, because it depends on the subject, the level and how many sessions are actually needed.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a female IB tutor for my daughter in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and say so in the first message rather than after a trial lesson. A gender preference is treated as a filter on the match, not as an awkward special request. What we will not do is pretend the pool is larger than it is. For a widely taught subject such as Biology at Standard Level or English A, a female specialist is usually free within a few days. For a narrow combination, say Physics at Higher Level at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, it can take longer, and you are told the likely wait before committing to anything.

faqs.question: Does a female tutor in the UAE need her own MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: The permit rule does not depend on gender. Any individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The federal portal at u.ae states the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that people tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time. Ask any tutor, male or female, where their permit stands and when it expires.

faqs.question: Is the KHDA separate-classes rule about boys and girls?
faqs.answer: No, and the confusion is common. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups. Combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. That rule is about first-language background, not gender. Any separation of boys and girls at a particular school comes from that school's own model or the curriculum it is licensed to teach, so the question belongs to the school rather than to the regulator.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school if we live in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education. It supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Dubai answers to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge. This matters for tutoring because the emirate authority, not a national one, shapes inspection and fee approval, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah approves curricula and assessment methods as well. If you commute into a Dubai or Sharjah school from Ajman, it is the school's emirate that governs it.

faqs.question: Can my daughter's own schoolteacher tutor her privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Not for payment. The ADEK professional ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours need the permit in any case. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but the direction is clear enough that no serious platform should be offering you your own child's teacher privately.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is permitted to teach privately here?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions and listen to how quickly they come back. First, do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and when does it expire? Second, which school or employer are you with, and is my child enrolled there? Third, are you teaching my child's board and level this academic year? Somebody who holds the permit answers the first question in a sentence. A tuition business with premises in Dubai is a different case: that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which has a number and an expiry date you can ask to see.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on an online one-to-one lesson?
faqs.answer: You are welcome to, and plenty of families do for the first few sessions with a younger child. Our sessions are built to be observable: they happen on the family's device, on a shared screen, and the written note afterwards says what was covered and what was set. With a Year 12 or 13 student, sitting in usually reduces how much they are willing to admit they have not understood, which is the opposite of what the hour is for. Read the note instead, and ask about the one topic it flags.

faqs.question: Does a female tutor cost more in the UAE than a male tutor?
faqs.answer: Not in the rates published across this market. The figures track level, subject scarcity and format instead. Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist sits nearer AED 200 to 450 and above, and a tutor travelling to a UAE address carries AED 180 to 500 because the journey is priced into the hour. Those are market figures from competitor pages and Bestimate's 2026 cost table, not IB Gram's price list. A preference changes waiting time, not the hourly number.

faqs.question: Can a female tutor cover Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Yes, and these are the two subjects where UAE families request a female tutor most often. Both are compulsory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, both are taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students. Schools must ensure their own teachers of these subjects hold appropriate KHDA approval. Support follows the set Ministry of Education material, because schools may not use different or additional content without prior permission.

faqs.question: What if no female specialist is free for IB Chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: You are told before paying anything, and given three real options. You can wait for the next opening, with an estimate of how long that is likely to be. You can take a male specialist for that one subject and keep the preference for the others. Or you can move the slot, because availability at 4pm Gulf Standard Time is not the same as availability at 7pm. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject at the level needed, the lesson is delivered online by an IB specialist based in India at your slot, and we say so in advance.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change our weekly session time?
faqs.answer: School days shorten during Ramadan and the useful hours move, so a Ramadan tutoring schedule normally means either an early afternoon session straight after a shortened school day, or a post-Iftar slot in the evening. Both work online because nobody is driving anywhere. Families who fast usually find the post-Iftar slot more productive for anything analytical, and keep lighter review work for the afternoon. Tell us before the month begins and we move the recurring slot, rather than cancelling three weeks and trying to catch up in April.

faqs.question: How much of the Mathematics Exploration is a tutor allowed to see?
faqs.answer: A tutor may question the topic, press on whether the mathematics matches the level of the course, and read one draft against the published criteria. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six of the twenty marks and is where Higher Level students most often sit below their own course, so that is the useful conversation to have early. What a tutor may not do is choose the topic, supply the mathematics, or write or rewrite passages. The school requires the work to be the student's own, and feedback given in writing is feedback the school can read.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSEs be enough for UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the requirement reported in July 2026 is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. At least one page ranking for these searches states that six subjects are needed. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae, or with the attestation authority in your emirate, in writing, before planning subject choices around it.

faqs.question: Does the IB Diploma need Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Equivalency and attestation are how the Ministry of Education recognises a school certificate for use inside the country, including for university applications. The British and American track requirements have been reported publicly and are set out on this page. We will not publish an IB points threshold, because the source we read states none, and an unsourced number here would be worse than no number at all. Check MoE equivalency for IB students on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of that process, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: What do you keep about my child, and how do I have it deleted?
faqs.answer: The enquiry form asks for the subject, the level, the year group, the school board and a parent contact. It does not ask for a photograph, a report card or a predicted grade, and you should be wary of any tutoring form that does. We hold what you send so a specialist can be matched and so session notes attach to the right student, under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. Ask us to delete it and we delete it, session notes included. The privacy link sits on every page.

faqs.question: Is the first lesson genuinely free, and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: One hour, once, with the specialist matched to your request, and no card details are needed to book it. The condition is that it is a single lesson rather than a trial week, and that it ends with a written plan whether or not you continue. The hour is used for diagnosis: the tutor works through the most recent piece of marked school work, finds where the method breaks down, and says what a term of weekly sessions could realistically change. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than the plan.

female-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the availability answer, not a deposit
female-ib-tutor.closingBody: If you want a female IB tutor for a student in the UAE, the first thing worth knowing is whether one is actually free for that subject, at that level, in your slot. Send the subject, the year group, the school and the emirate, and you will have that answer inside a working day, along with the market context for what this costs in AED and a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live online to Gulf Standard Time. Home visiting is a service we offer only in India, and we would rather say that here than after you have paid.

female-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are women who teach IGCSE subjects to UAE timetables: graduates and qualified teachers who work to Cambridge and Pearson specifications, know how Year 10 and Year 11 are sequenced in British-curriculum schools here, and teach from the student's own scheme of work rather than a generic course.

intro.heading: The gender request, and the school system it has to fit inside
paragraphs: A request for a woman tutor is one of the most common things UAE parents say first and explain least. Some families make it for religious or cultural reasons. Some make it because a daughter in Year 11 has stopped asking questions in a mixed classroom and the household wants that pattern broken before the series. Some make it because the child asked. None of those reasons needs defending, and none of them should cost a family the subject specialist they actually need.

The problem is arithmetic rather than principle. A family hiring locally in Al Barsha or Khalifa City is choosing from the people who can reach the villa on a school night. Add a subject constraint — Physics Extended, not general science — and that pool thins. Add a gender preference on top and, for several IGCSE subjects, it can empty out entirely. What usually happens next is the compromise nobody admits to: the household keeps the preference and gives up the specialism, so a Year 11 girl sitting Cambridge Physics 0625 is taught by someone whose own degree was in biology.

Live one-to-one online lessons break that trade-off, because the constraint that was geographic stops being geographic. The question changes from which qualified women live within a 25-minute drive of this community to which qualified women are free at 17:30 Gulf Standard Time on a Tuesday. IB Gram works that way across the UAE: one-to-one, over video, with the subject and the preference both treated as requirements rather than one being traded against the other. Home visits are part of what we offer in India, and this page does not pretend otherwise.

This page is built around the context a UAE family has to work inside, because that context is where the useful detail lives and it is the part the tutoring market here almost never writes down. The country has five separate school regulators, not one. It has a federal rule requiring Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside whichever international curriculum a school is licensed to teach — and, in Dubai, a KHDA requirement that some of those classes be organised separately for Arab and non-Arab students. It has a private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 that is free of charge for two years and open to categories of people most families never think of as tutors. And it has professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi that stop a teacher taking paid lessons with a student from her own school.

Each of those facts changes who can teach your daughter, when, and on what terms. Read in order, they explain why the female tutor your neighbour recommended may not legally be able to take your child, why the Arabic teacher at her school is held to a credential check that her maths tutor is not, and why a two-year IGCSE plan should be drawn backwards from an examination series rather than forwards from the week the first grade disappointed you.
bullets: Five regulators: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah
The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years and covers teachers, employed residents, unemployed residents and university students
KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies
ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school
Market rates published across the UAE run from roughly AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor to AED 650 for a premium named tutor
A gender preference does not change an hourly rate; it changes how many specialists remain in the pool you are choosing from

female-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: An IGCSE page in the UAE has to cover more than two years. British-curriculum schools here run Lower Secondary before it and International AS and A Level after it, and the subject choices made in Year 9 decide what is still available in Year 12. These are the stages a woman subject specialist is most often asked for.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed internally and, in many UAE schools, with Cambridge Checkpoint tests taken in March, May or October. Mathematics, English and Science are the three strands that matter most for what follows, because the Year 9 report is usually what a school uses to place a student into Core or Extended tiers. Work here is about closing specific gaps — negative indices, rearranging formulae, writing a method a marker can follow — rather than exam technique.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this stage is also where the mandatory Ministry subjects settle into the timetable, so a Year 8 girl may be carrying Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside her licensed curriculum. Families who want a woman tutor often start here rather than in Year 11, which is the easier conversation: there is no series pressure, and a weekly slot after the school run is simple to protect.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series available in some regions. Most subjects are tiered: Core caps the grade at C or grade 5, Extended opens the full range to A* or grade 9. Papers are sat per subject rather than as one qualification, so a student can be Extended in Mathematics 0580 and Core in a second language in the same year. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the exam window.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable for each, and it states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper because the wrong zone timetable was used. UAE families should take dates from the school's exams officer, not from a timetable found online. Tutoring plans in this country are therefore built around the school's own entry and forecast-grade deadlines.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board widely taught in UAE British-curriculum schools, with exams available in a May/June series and a November series each year. Subject codes run differently — 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology — and the assessment pattern is not interchangeable with Cambridge. Mathematics is tiered as Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and some subjects offer a modular route with assessment spread across sittings.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson published a November 2026 International GCSE timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and it issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027. Dates can be revised, so a UAE family should work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date. A tutor who teaches 4PH1 to the Cambridge 0625 sequence will drill the wrong paper structure, which is the single most common board mismatch we are asked to correct.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The two years after IGCSE in most UAE British-curriculum schools. Cambridge and Pearson both run AS and A Level in June and November series. Subject choice is narrow — usually three or four — and the prerequisite grades are decided by IGCSE results, so a girl who finishes IGCSE Mathematics on a grade 6 will find Mathematics at A Level closed in several schools here regardless of how the rest of her certificate reads.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, in addition to five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. That makes the A Level stage part of a UAE university file rather than an optional extension, and it is a reason to protect the IGCSE grades that open it.

female-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Requests for a woman specialist cluster in a predictable set of subjects, and the pattern is worth knowing before you start calling around. The sciences and upper Mathematics are where local supply is thinnest; the languages and humanities are where it is deepest. Syllabus codes are given because a tutor who cannot name yours is teaching from memory.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject most often tutored and the one where tier placement does the most damage. Marks go on method lines left unwritten, on algebraic fractions, and on the Extended-only topics a Core-tiered class never met. Work is diagnostic first: a past paper marked question by question, then the three topics that are actually costing grades.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical-skills paper are where UAE students lose most. Circuit questions reward a student who can redraw a diagram before calculating; the alternative-to-practical paper rewards one who has read real method sections. This is the hardest subject in which to find a woman specialist locally, and the most common reason a family ends up online.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways account for a large share of lost marks. The fix is rarely more content: it is a worked habit for setting out mole calculations with units at every line, and recall of the specific observation words a mark scheme accepts for a colour change.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Deceptively content-heavy, and the subject where able students plateau at grade 6 because answers describe instead of explain. Command terms do the work here. A tutor's job is to show the difference between stating that a plant wilted and explaining the water potential gradient that made it wilt.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Taken by students who need science but not three separate certificates, and widely offered in UAE schools. The challenge is breadth across three disciplines with one tutor. Sessions are usually split across a fortnight so that each discipline gets real time rather than fifteen minutes each.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading passages are where marks move fastest. Students who read widely still lose marks for ignoring the audience and form the question specified. Timed practice with feedback on structure, not vocabulary, is what shifts a grade 6 to a grade 8.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A large entry in UAE schools, with speaking assessed separately. The written papers reward precision over fluency: one tense held consistently across a paragraph scores better than ambitious vocabulary wrongly used. Speaking preparation is the part most often neglected until the last fortnight.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508) and Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Two different qualifications for two different students, and UAE families frequently find their child entered for the wrong one. First Language assumes schooling in Arabic; Foreign Language does not. In Dubai, the KHDA requirement for separate classes by group means the school stream and the examined syllabus do not always align.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries more marks than students expect. A correctly labelled diagram with axes, shifts and a new equilibrium marked earns credit that no amount of surrounding prose recovers. Data-response questions reward reading the table before the question.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the named case business is the whole game. Generic answers about motivation theory score low; the same answer anchored to the stated firm, its market and its numbers scores well. Evaluation paragraphs need a judgement, not a summary of both sides.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory — binary, data representation, networks and security — is where most marks are lost, not the programming paper. Pseudocode conventions matter because a marker reads for them. Another subject where a woman specialist is hard to source locally in most emirates.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics, and the best single predictor of coping in Year 12. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive with little scaffolding. Students who manage it comfortably are usually the ones who already write fluent algebra, which is where support should start.

female-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where you are, and which authority governs the school
female-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The regulator over your daughter's school is not a trivia question. It decides who inspects it, who approves its fees and curriculum, and which authority's rules apply to the teachers inside it. Lessons from IB Gram reach every emirate the same way — live, one-to-one, over video — so the difference below is about the school system around the child, not about coverage.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees would not rise for 2026-27, and seven new private schools are opening for the 2026-27 intake.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK also sets professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, including a prohibition on paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school — the rule that most often surprises families here.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Sharjah has a higher share of single-sex schooling than Dubai, so a gender preference raised here is frequently about matching what the school already does.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. RAK is named by none of the tutoring providers surveyed for this page, which tells you how much local specialist supply a family here should expect to find.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a central role in overseeing private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here often commute into Sharjah or Dubai for schooling, which makes an evening in-person session on a school night genuinely difficult and a video slot straightforward.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country, with a correspondingly thin pool of subject specialists of any gender. A Year 11 girl sitting Extended Chemistry here is unlikely to find a local match on subject and preference at the same time.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education, and on the Gulf of Oman coast rather than the Arabian Gulf side, which puts it outside the commuting range of the Dubai and Sharjah tutoring markets altogether. Online delivery is not a convenience here so much as the only way a subject specialist is available.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under ADEK, alongside Abu Dhabi city. The British-curriculum cohort is smaller and more dispersed, and school-run distances are longer, so sessions are usually scheduled later in the evening than a Dubai family would choose. The ADEK own-school tutoring rule applies here in full.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai British-curriculum schools
schoolClusters.note: Dubai carries the largest IGCSE cohort in the country, with the UK curriculum accounting for the biggest single share of private-school enrolment. Students from these schools sit Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel depending on the school's choice, and families should confirm which before booking any tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain British-curriculum schools
schoolClusters.note: A smaller and more spread-out cohort than Dubai's, under ADEK rather than KHDA. The practical effect for tutoring is the ethics rule: staff at these schools are barred from taking paid private lessons with their own enrolled students, so the familiar teacher is not an option.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Under SPEA in Sharjah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Single-sex schooling is more common here, which is why a gender preference raised by a Sharjah family is often a continuation of the school day rather than a departure from it.

female-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Every format below is delivered live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. The choice is about how a family's week is shaped and how close the examination series is, not about where anyone travels.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with a woman subject specialist
modes.description: One fixed hour a week in one subject, with the same tutor each time. This is the format that suits a Year 10 girl whose grade has drifted rather than collapsed, and it is the one where a stable relationship matters most. The slot is held in the calendar for the term so it survives the weeks when nobody feels like it, and work follows her school's own scheme rather than a parallel course.
bullets: Same tutor every week, named before the first lesson
Taught from the student's own scheme of work and past assessments
Written note after each session on what was covered and what to practise

modes.title: Two subjects split across a fortnight
modes.description: Common for students carrying two weak sciences, or Mathematics plus one other. Rather than two half-hours a week, which achieves very little in either, each subject gets a full hour on alternating weeks with practice set in between. It costs the same as one weekly hour and is far more effective than splitting a single session down the middle.
bullets: One full hour per subject, alternating weeks
Separate specialists where the subjects do not share a tutor
Set work between sessions so the off week is not idle

modes.title: Series block before a June or November sitting
modes.description: A denser run of sessions in the eight to ten weeks before papers, built around the school's own entry and mock dates. The content phase is over by then, so the work is timed papers, mark-scheme reading and the three or four topics a diagnostic says are still costing grades. Families usually run two sessions a week in this phase and stop entirely during the exam fortnight.

modes.title: Coursework and practical-skills review
modes.description: For subjects with an assessed component or an alternative-to-practical paper. A tutor reads what the student has written, asks the questions a marker would ask, and sends her back to improve it herself. She does not take the file away and hand back a finished version. That boundary is what keeps the work hers, and it is stated here because the market around this page does not always respect it.

sections.heading: What a family is actually asking for when they search for a female IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: The search phrase is short and the request behind it is not. In practice the families who type it fall into four groups, and they want different things. The first group has a religious or cultural preference about who spends unsupervised time with a teenage daughter, and that preference is settled before any conversation about grades begins. The second has a daughter who has gone quiet — a girl who stopped putting her hand up in a mixed science set somewhere in Year 9 and has been coasting ever since. The third is following the child's own stated preference, which is usually the easiest version because nobody is negotiating. The fourth is a parent of a son, and that request is far more common here than the market admits.

None of these groups is asking for a lower standard, and that is the thing providers get wrong. The preference is treated as a filter applied after the subject question, as though a family would accept a weaker Physics teacher to satisfy it. What families want is both requirements met at once: a woman who has actually taught Cambridge 0625 Extended, knows what the alternative-to-practical paper asks for, and can explain why a terminal velocity answer earned two marks out of four.

The honest answer is that meeting both at once is a sourcing problem, not a teaching problem. There is no shortage of excellent women teaching IGCSE subjects in this region. There is a severe shortage of them within driving distance of any particular villa on a Tuesday evening. That is why this page spends more time on who is permitted to tutor in the UAE and where the supply actually sits than on reassurance about quality. Quality is the easy part once the pool is big enough to choose from.

One thing worth saying plainly before the detail: a tutor's gender is a legitimate preference and not a proxy for anything else. It is not a safeguarding policy, it does not replace checking a permit, and it tells you nothing about subject knowledge. The later sections treat those as separate questions with separate answers, because conflating them is how families end up reassured and badly taught at the same time.

sections.heading: Where the UAE school system already separates classes, and where it does not
paragraphs: Families sometimes assume the gender question is theirs alone to raise. It is not. The UAE school system already streams certain classes, and understanding which ones explains a great deal about what your daughter's week looks like and who is standing in front of her.

Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why a British-curriculum school in Dubai teaching Cambridge IGCSE still runs Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside it. In Dubai, KHDA requires these subjects in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

KHDA goes further on how those classes are organised. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also sets the language of instruction: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson be at least twenty-five minutes.

The separation that exists in UAE schools, then, is by language group and curriculum expectation rather than by gender — except in the single-sex schools, which are more common in Sharjah and parts of Abu Dhabi than in Dubai. What this means for tutoring is simple and rarely said: the school is not going to solve the gender question for you in a mixed school, and the mandatory subjects carry a teacher-approval requirement that your maths tutor does not. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. No equivalent requirement exists for a private tutor in Physics.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to give paid lessons in the UAE, and why so many of them are women
paragraphs: Private tutoring in this country is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone. MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The eligibility list is the part that explains the shape of this market. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Read that list against the UAE's resident population and the picture resolves: a large share of the people who can lawfully give paid lessons here on a weekday afternoon are qualified women who are not currently in salaried employment — teachers and graduates who came on a spouse's or parent's sponsorship and are not in a classroom this year. That is the single biggest reason the supply of excellent female tutors in this country is real while the supply within any one neighbourhood is not.

It also explains the quality spread. The same permit covers a chemistry graduate with eight years in a Cambridge school and a first-year undergraduate taking her first paid lesson. The permit is a legal requirement, not a teaching credential, and a family that treats it as a quality signal has misread what it is. Ask for the permit because the law requires it. Ask separately about the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the last cohort she took through a series, because that is the question the permit does not answer.

One category deserves a warning rather than an explanation. A school student aged fifteen to eighteen can hold this permit. There are good reasons for that rule, and a bright Year 13 student can be genuinely useful for Lower Secondary support. She is not the person to prepare your daughter for Extended Physics, and an advertised rate near the bottom of the published market band is often what that category looks like from the outside.

sections.heading: The rule that stops your daughter's own teacher taking her on privately
paragraphs: The first instinct of most families is the obvious one: the woman who teaches her Chemistry at school already knows her, knows the scheme of work and knows the mock results. Ask her. It is a reasonable instinct and in Abu Dhabi it runs straight into a rule.

ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This has been reported in the regional press rather than read by us from the current policy document, so a family relying on it should verify the present wording with the school or with ADEK directly. The principle behind it is not obscure: a teacher who sets and marks a student's school assessments and is also paid privately by that student's family is in a conflict that no amount of good faith resolves.

The practical consequence is worth stating because it reframes the whole gender question. The woman a family most wants is usually the one they cannot have. What is available instead is a different woman with the same subject and tier experience — and once you accept that she is not going to be the school's own staff member, there is no longer any reason for her to live nearby either. The constraint that made a local search feel natural has already been removed by the rule itself.

Two related things to avoid. Do not ask a teacher to tutor a student from her own school as a favour or off the books; it exposes her professionally and does the child no good if it comes apart mid-year. And treat any provider that markets your child's own teacher privately as a provider that has not read the rules it is operating under. The correct version of that offer is a teacher from a comparable school teaching the same board and tier, with no assessment relationship to your daughter at all.

sections.heading: What this market charges, and whether asking for a woman changes the number
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars — a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below are what each provider named publishes for itself, read in October 2026. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list.

The short answer to the question in the heading is no. Nothing in the published rate structure of this market prices a gender preference, and any provider that quotes you more for one is charging for scarcity it created by searching a single neighbourhood. What the preference changes is the size of the pool at a given rate. Hiring locally, it can cut the number of qualified subject specialists available to you sharply, and the compromise that follows is a specialism traded away rather than a higher bill. Online, the pool is national rather than local, and the preference costs nothing because it is one filter on a long list rather than the last filter on a short one.

Two figures are worth keeping beside the hourly rate. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. And Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set against school fees — which KHDA confirmed in May 2026 would not rise for 2026-27 in Dubai — a weekly hour is a small line in the household budget, which is exactly why it should buy the right specialist rather than the nearest one.

For IB Gram's own position: start with the free trial lesson and the matching conversation rather than a published rate card. The trial is one lesson, one per family, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue, and a quote follows once the subject, board, tier and the number of sessions a week are known.

sections.heading: Why a gender preference shrinks a local pool and not a national one
paragraphs: This is the section that does the arguing, and it does it with arithmetic rather than adjectives. Consider a family in a Dubai or Abu Dhabi community looking for Extended Physics for a Year 11 girl, with a stated preference for a woman tutor.

Hiring locally, the candidate list is filtered four times before anyone is interviewed. It is filtered by who lives within a realistic school-night drive. Then by who teaches Physics rather than general science. Then by who has taught the Extended tier for the right board. Then by the gender preference. Each filter is reasonable on its own and the four together frequently leave nobody. What happens next is the compromise described earlier: the family holds the preference, drops the tier specialism, and a girl sitting 0625 Extended is taught by someone whose subject is biology. Nobody decided that. The filters decided it.

Live one-to-one online removes the first filter entirely, and removing it changes the order of everything after. The question becomes which women with Extended Physics experience are free at 17:30 Gulf Standard Time, across the whole country and the wider region on the same clock. The preference survives because it is no longer competing with geography for the last place on a short list. The same logic applies with more force in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain and Ras Al Khaimah, where the local specialist pool for several IGCSE subjects is thin for any gender.

There are honest costs to video delivery and they belong in the comparison. A tutor cannot set up apparatus on the student's desk, so practical work is taught through method, variables and the alternative-to-practical paper rather than through handling equipment. A twelve-year-old who will not sit still needs a parent in the house for the first fortnight. And a poor connection ruins a lesson in a way a poor drive does not. Those are the trade-offs. They are smaller than the trade-off a four-filter local search quietly forces.

sections.heading: The IGCSE subjects where a woman specialist is hardest to source locally
paragraphs: Scarcity is not evenly spread, and knowing where it bites saves a family weeks of calling around. The pattern across this market is consistent: the languages and humanities have deep local supply, the physical sciences and upper mathematics do not, and the gap widens as you move north from Dubai.

The reason is structural rather than cultural. The pool of lawful tutors described earlier is dominated by residents whose teaching careers paused when they moved here, and that pool mirrors the subject distribution of the schools they taught in. English, Arabic, Biology and the humanities are well covered. Physics, Computer Science and Additional Mathematics are specialist posts even inside a large school, so a single community is unlikely to contain one of each who is also free on a weekday evening.

What families settle for in that situation follows a predictable sequence, and each step costs something measurable. A general science tutor instead of a physicist means the electricity questions never get fixed, because explaining current in a series circuit well is a different skill from reciting that it is the same everywhere. A maths tutor covering Additional Mathematics 0606 from memory will teach the calculus but not the trigonometric identities that carry the harder marks. A tutor who teaches 4PH1 to the Cambridge 0625 sequence drills the wrong paper structure for an entire year, and that one is invisible until a mock comes back.

The row to hold out for is in the final column below. In every one of these subjects the right answer is a specialist who can name the syllabus code, the tier and the paper pattern before the first lesson — and the only reliable way to insist on that while also holding a gender preference is to stop requiring that she live nearby.

sections.heading: Safeguarding the online room: what to settle before the first lesson
paragraphs: A gender preference is frequently a safeguarding instinct expressed in the only vocabulary a parent has to hand. It is worth separating the two, because the preference does a small amount of the work and the arrangements below do most of it.

The practical rules are simple and a family should state them rather than hope for them. Lessons happen in a shared room of the house, not behind a closed bedroom door. The laptop camera is on for both parties. The session runs on a scheduled link a parent can also open. Communication about scheduling goes through the parent rather than directly to a fourteen-year-old's phone. Any recording happens only with the family's agreement and with a stated purpose, and a parent may sit in on any lesson without notice — most do for the first one and then stop, which is the right pattern.

Data is the part families rarely ask about and should. Collecting information about a minor carries obligations under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. Before a trial, the useful minimum is the subject, the board, the year group, the tier and a recent mock paper or report. A child's photograph, full school timetable or home address is not needed to teach her Chemistry over video, and a provider that asks for it should be asked why. Every page on this site carries a privacy link, and a request to delete what has been collected should be answered rather than negotiated.

Two further checks, in order. Ask for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, because the law requires it. Then ask the subject questions — which board, which code, which tier, which cohort she last took through a series — because the permit is a legal clearance and not a statement about teaching. A family that does both in that order has covered the ground that a gender preference on its own does not.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the shape of a Year 11 girl's week
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the UAE calendar fails in the second month. School hours shift during Ramadan, the working day compresses, evenings reorganise around Iftar, and the weeks after Eid collide with mock season in several schools. None of that is a reason to pause support; all of it is a reason to timetable it differently.

During Ramadan the workable pattern for most families is a post-Iftar slot — later than the usual 17:00 or 18:00 session, shorter, and focused on practice rather than new content. Concentration before Iftar is poor and pretending otherwise wastes an hour. Families who keep a slot through this period and move it rather than cancelling it are the ones who come out the other side without a four-week gap in a Year 11 year that does not have four weeks to spare.

The rest of the year has its own shape. The autumn term is the content term and the one where a drifting grade should be caught. The winter break is when a transition problem gets fixed, which matters for a girl who moved from a different curriculum into Year 10 and has a specific gap rather than a general weakness. Mock season is diagnostic: the marked paper, not the grade on the front, is the most useful document a tutor will see all year. The eight to ten weeks before a series are for timed papers. The exam fortnight itself is for stopping — new material introduced during papers lowers confidence and gains nothing.

Daily timing matters as much as the annual pattern. Sessions between 16:30 and 20:30 Gulf Standard Time cover almost every UAE family's requirement, and a slot can be set after Maghrib where that suits the household. Longer school runs in Al Ain, the northern emirates and the outer Dubai communities push sessions later, which is one more thing a video lesson absorbs without complaint.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: This market contains providers selling finished assessed work. One of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Any family shopping for a tutor in this region will meet that offer, and it is worth being direct about what it is: an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's qualification at risk, not a shortcut.

The boundary is not complicated. A tutor explains what the criteria reward. She reads a draft the student has written and asks the questions a marker would ask — what was the control variable, why that range, how does this conclusion follow from this graph. She points to the paragraph where the method is unclear. Then she gives it back for the student to improve. What she does not do is produce text that goes into an assessed submission, edit a piece to completion on the student's behalf, or supply a finished file. Where the student's own words are the thing being marked, they have to be the student's own words.

For IGCSE specifically, most of this lands on practical assessment and on the alternative-to-practical papers in the sciences. A student taught entirely over video has not stood at a bench, and that gap is real. It is closed by teaching method rather than by pretending otherwise: reading published method sections, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, spotting the deliberate flaw an examiner has built into a described procedure, and knowing the observation vocabulary a mark scheme accepts. That is what the paper actually tests.

On materials, the position is equally plain. Past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them and link to the official source; we do not host or redistribute them. A provider that hands over a bundle of other people's documents is telling you something about its standards before you have had a single lesson.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what her IGCSE certificate has to show
paragraphs: For a girl who intends to study at a UAE university, the IGCSE certificate is not only a school record. It feeds an equivalency file, and the subject count in that file catches families out every year.

On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. The detail that matters most for a UAE student is what does not count: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A girl carrying both as mandatory school subjects is therefore sitting them for her school and her own learning, not for the equivalency count, and families who assume otherwise discover they are a subject short at the point of application. One provider ranking for these queries publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

On the American track the requirements are different in kind: English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one — the source we have read does not state one, and anything circulating unsourced should be checked on moe.gov.ae or with the relevant attestation authority before a family plans around it.

Two cautions belong with this. Equivalency and attestation are processes a family completes with the authority, not services a tutoring platform performs or guarantees; describe them, verify them at source, and use the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling urgency rather than teaching.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the board and the preference together
process.description: The brief we need is short: subject, Cambridge or Pearson, the syllabus code if you have it, the tier, the year group, and the preference for a woman tutor stated up front rather than raised later. One recent marked paper or report is worth more than a paragraph of description, because it shows where marks are actually going.

process.title: We name the tutor before you commit anything
process.description: You are told who she is, what she read at university, which board and tier she has taught, and how long she has been teaching the current syllabus. No anonymous profile and no placeholder. If we do not have a match on both the subject and the preference, we say so and give you a date rather than substituting someone who fits only one of the two.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the conditions stated
process.description: One trial lesson, one per family, no card details taken and no obligation to continue. It is a real lesson rather than a sales call: the tutor works through a paper the student has already sat and sends a short written note afterwards on what she found. If the match is wrong, say so and we try again.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: The session is booked into the calendar for the term, between 16:30 and 20:30 GST for most families, or post-Iftar during Ramadan. A fixed time survives the weeks when motivation dips, which a flexible arrangement does not. Scheduling runs through the parent, and a written note follows every lesson.

process.title: Review at lesson six against the first diagnostic
process.description: At the sixth session we look back at the topics the first lesson identified and ask whether they have moved. Where they have not, the plan changes or the tutor does. A replacement carries the same subject brief and the same preference, so continuity is about the work rather than about starting the conversation again.

process.title: Build the series block backwards from the school's dates
process.description: Once the school confirms its entry dates, mock window and paper dates, the final phase is drawn backwards from them: content finished, then timed papers, then a planned stop for the exam fortnight. Cambridge zone timetables differ, so the dates come from the school's exams officer rather than from anything we hold.

whyPoints.title: The preference and the specialism are both requirements
whyPoints.description: A request for a woman tutor is treated as a matching requirement alongside the subject, the board and the tier, not as a filter applied after the specialist has been chosen. Where we cannot meet both, we say so and give a date rather than quietly satisfying one and hoping the other goes unnoticed.

whyPoints.title: A national pool rather than a neighbourhood one
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run live over video, the people available to your daughter are not limited to those who can reach your community on a school night. That matters most in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain and Ras Al Khaimah, and for Physics, Computer Science and Additional Mathematics anywhere in the country.

whyPoints.title: Named tutors, named credentials, before anything is paid
whyPoints.description: You know her name, her degree, the boards she has taught and the tiers she has covered before the trial. We do not publish a self-assessed rating or a review count we cannot evidence, because figures of that kind are the least reliable thing on a tutoring page and several in this market contradict themselves.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, not invented
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate on this page is published by the provider named and was read in October 2026. Every regulatory statement comes from u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or named press reporting, and where a date or a threshold could not be verified at source, the page says so rather than filling the gap.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and questions. She does not hand back a finished assessed submission, and she does not redistribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB documents. This is said plainly because the alternative is openly sold in this market, and a student caught using it loses more than the piece of work.

whyPoints.title: Delivery described honestly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one and online. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are part of what IB Gram offers in India. Saying that clearly costs us some enquiries and saves every family who reads it from a wasted conversation.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a female IGCSE tutor for my daughter in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most common requests we take. State it at the matching stage, in the same message as the subject, board and tier, so it is treated as a requirement rather than a late preference. Because lessons run live online, the request is one filter on a national pool rather than the final filter on a short local list, which is why it does not force a compromise on the subject specialism. If a woman specialist is not free for your subject and time, we tell you that and give you a date, instead of offering someone who matches the preference but not the syllabus.

faqs.question: Does asking for a woman tutor change the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: It should not, and nothing in the published rate structure of this market prices it. Rates across the UAE are set by level, format, session length and the tutor's experience: budget online platforms advertise from around AED 45 an hour, qualified subject tutors from about AED 150 to 300, specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits higher again because travel sits inside the band. A provider quoting more for a gender preference is charging for scarcity created by searching one neighbourhood. What the preference genuinely changes is the number of specialists left in the pool, not the price of an hour.

faqs.question: Are the female IGCSE tutors in this market qualified teachers or graduates at home?
faqs.answer: Both, and the spread is wide. The UAE private tuition work permit is open to teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. A large part of the strongest supply is former classroom teachers and subject graduates who are resident here without a current school post, which is why the quality available nationally is high while the quality within any one community is unpredictable. The permit is a legal clearance, not a teaching credential, so ask separately about the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the last cohort she took through a series.

faqs.question: Does a woman tutoring my daughter privately in the UAE need her own permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit, introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified. Ask to see the permit, then ask the subject questions separately, because one does not answer the other.

faqs.question: Can my daughter's own teacher at her Dubai school take her on privately?
faqs.answer: It is the first thing most families think of and it is the wrong route. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That reporting should be checked against the current policy wording, but the conflict it addresses is real: the same person should not set and mark her school assessments and be paid privately by the family. What works instead is a teacher from a comparable school, same board and tier, with no assessment relationship to your child.

faqs.question: Who is allowed to teach Arabic and Islamic Education to girls in a UAE private school?
faqs.answer: Inside a Dubai school, KHDA requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and that classes be organised separately for Arab and non-Arab students, with combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Islamic Education and Arabic as a first language are taught in Standard Arabic for Arab students, and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. No equivalent approval requirement applies to a private tutor in Mathematics or Physics, which is worth knowing when you compare credentials.

faqs.question: Will the same female tutor stay with my daughter across both IGCSE years?
faqs.answer: That is the intention and it is what we plan for, because continuity across Years 10 and 11 is worth more than any single lesson. A tutor who taught the Year 10 content knows which topics were shaky in October and does not spend the series block rediscovering them. Things do change: a tutor's own availability shifts, a family moves time zone, or the review at lesson six says the match is not working. When a replacement is needed, she receives the same subject brief, the same tier and the same preference, plus the notes from every previous session, so the handover is about the work rather than about starting again.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find a woman specialist for IGCSE Physics 0625?
faqs.answer: Physics is the hardest IGCSE subject in which to source a woman specialist, because it is a specialist post even inside a large school and few communities contain one who is also free on a weekday evening. Searching locally, families often wait weeks and then settle for a general science tutor, which leaves the electricity questions unfixed. Searching nationally over video, the wait is usually days rather than weeks, and the match is someone who has taught the Extended tier and the alternative-to-practical paper. If we cannot fill it, we give you a date rather than substituting a biology graduate and calling it science.

faqs.question: Can a female tutor teach my daughter after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families that is the only slot that works during the month. School hours shift, the working day compresses and concentration before Iftar is poor, so a shorter post-Iftar session focused on practice rather than new content is the pattern we recommend. Keep the slot and move it instead of cancelling the term: a Year 11 year does not have a spare four weeks, and families who pause in Ramadan usually restart in a worse position than they stopped. Timing can also be set after Maghrib where that suits the household better, and the slot returns to its usual hour after Eid.

faqs.question: My son has asked for a female tutor. Is that an unusual request here?
faqs.answer: Not at all, and it is more common in this market than the advertising suggests. Boys who have gone quiet in a subject sometimes find it easier to admit confusion to someone who is not standing in the same classroom dynamic they have learned to perform in. The reasoning does not need explaining to us. The request is handled the same way as any other: stated at matching, alongside the subject, board and tier, and treated as a requirement rather than a footnote. The subject specialism is never traded away to satisfy it, which is the whole reason this works better over video than locally.

faqs.question: Can I sit in the room while my daughter has her online lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, at any time and without notice. Most parents join the first lesson, watch for ten minutes and then stop, which is the right pattern — enough to see how the tutor works, not enough to make a teenager self-conscious every week. The arrangements we ask for from the family's side are the same ones that make this straightforward: lessons in a shared room rather than behind a closed door, cameras on for both parties, a scheduled link a parent can also open, and scheduling messages to the parent rather than to the student's phone. Recording happens only with your agreement and a stated purpose.

faqs.question: Does a girls' school in Sharjah follow Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the school, and it is the single most important thing to confirm before booking any tutor. Both boards are widely taught in UAE British-curriculum schools, and they are not interchangeable: Cambridge codes Mathematics as 0580 with Core and Extended tiers, while Pearson codes it 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher, and the paper patterns differ across the sciences. SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah and approves curricula and assessment methods, but the board choice sits with the school. Ask the exams officer, in writing, for the board and the subject codes your daughter has been entered for.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my daughter need for a UAE university file?
faqs.answer: On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. The detail families miss is that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A girl carrying both as mandatory school subjects is sitting them for her school rather than for the count. One provider ranking for these searches publishes a six-subject figure; the sourced requirement is five, and it should be verified on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can a female tutor help with coursework and the practical papers?
faqs.answer: With coursework, she explains what the criteria reward, reads a draft the student has written, asks the questions a marker would ask about method and variables, and gives it back for the student to improve. She does not produce text for an assessed submission or hand over a finished file. Some providers in this market openly sell completed assessed work; that is an integrity breach that risks the qualification, not a shortcut. For the alternative-to-practical papers, the work is reading published method sections, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, spotting a deliberate flaw in a described procedure, and learning the observation vocabulary a mark scheme accepts.

faqs.question: What do you collect about my daughter before a trial lesson, and how is it deleted?
faqs.answer: The useful minimum is the subject, the board, the year group, the tier and one recent marked paper or school report. That is enough for a tutor to find where the marks are going. We do not need a photograph, a full school timetable or a home address to teach Chemistry over video, and a provider asking for those should be asked why. Collecting data about a minor carries obligations under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection, so there is a privacy link on every page and a deletion request is answered rather than negotiated. Ask and it is removed.

faqs.question: Which authority inspects my daughter's school, and does it vet private tutors?
faqs.answer: Five separate bodies regulate UAE private schools. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. None of them vets your private tutor: that sits with MoHRE through the private tuition work permit, which is a separate and much narrower check.

female-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the subject and the preference in the same sentence
female-igcse-tutor.closingBody: The useful first message is short: the subject, Cambridge or Pearson, the syllabus code if you have it, the tier, the year group, your daughter's or son's year of entry, and that you would like a woman specialist. Attach one recent marked paper if you have it. We come back with a named tutor, her degree, the boards and tiers she has taught, and a trial slot in Gulf Standard Time — one lesson, one per family, no card details and no obligation. Lessons are live, one-to-one and online across every emirate. If we cannot match the subject and the preference together, we will say so and give you a date.
