fujairah.tutorsIntro: These are tutors open to Fujairah families this term, filtered to the IB Diploma and to Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE. Each card shows the syllabus a tutor has actually taught, the components they have marked, and their availability in Gulf Standard Time. If the specialist your child needs is not shown, name the subject and we will say plainly what the wait looks like.

intro.heading: Start with who inspects the school, not with who lives nearby
paragraphs: Fujairah is the only emirate whose coastline faces the Gulf of Oman, and the Hajar mountains stand between it and the rest of the country. That geography shapes tuition here more than anything else does. The private-school set in the emirate is small, the cohort for any single IB subject is smaller again, and a student taking Chemistry HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL may be one of three or four in the whole year group. There is frequently no local specialist in that subject at all. Not because the east coast lacks good teachers, but because the arithmetic of a small cohort never produces one.

Private schools in Fujairah are inspected by the federal Ministry of Education. Not by KHDA, which parents in Dubai quote at each other, and not by ADEK, which does the same job in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. Sharjah has its own authority, SPEA. On the east coast the inspecting body is the ministry itself, applying the national inspection framework with the same six judgement bands used across the country. The report it produces is the most useful free document a Fujairah parent holds, because it separates attainment from progress and judges both subject by subject and phase by phase. Read properly, it names the two subjects worth spending money on.

The report will not do your thinking for you. A judgement of Acceptable in secondary mathematics does not mean your child is fine. It means a cohort met the minimum standard the framework defines, across a year group holding thirty students with very different starting points, and a weaker student can sit a long way below that line without anyone writing it down. The framework judges a school. You are deciding about one student sitting one paper in one series. Those are different questions, and the distance between them is exactly where one-to-one teaching earns its fee.

Every lesson IB Gram arranges for a family here runs online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. We say that in the first hundred words because the alternative on this coast is not really an alternative. Driving a Chemistry HL specialist from Sharjah over the Wadi Ham road twice a week is either not going to happen or is going to be paid for in travel time dressed up as teaching. Online one-to-one tuition in Fujairah buys the specialist instead of the commute.

So this page is built around the inspection question, because in Fujairah that question decides everything downstream: what the school can realistically cover, which subjects are carried by one teacher rather than three, and whether the gap in front of you is a whole-cohort pattern or personal to your child. Below you will find the six bands and what each one implies for a parent, the regulator map of the east coast, market rates in AED with every figure attributed, the May session counted backwards month by month, assessment weightings by paper, the Internal Assessment criteria letter by letter, the academic-honesty line a tutor does not cross, and the Ministry of Education equivalency route into UAE universities.
bullets: Fujairah's private schools answer to the Ministry of Education; Khor Fakkan and Kalba, minutes up the same coast road, are Sharjah and fall under SPEA.
Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor in the UAE run roughly AED 150-300 an hour; visiting tuition runs AED 180-500 once travel is inside the fee.
IB results for the May session are published on 6 July; registration for that session closes with your school in mid-November of the year before.
A Maths exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, A to E; the science investigation is marked out of 24 across four.
Arabic, Islamic Studies and UAE Social Studies are ministry requirements sitting alongside the IB or IGCSE timetable rather than inside it.

fujairah.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every Fujairah student who asks us for help: the IB Middle Years Programme, the IB Diploma, Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The transitions between them are where marks disappear, because each one assesses differently and the east coast rarely has two teachers in a subject to smooth the handover.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade using published boundaries. There are no papers in the IGCSE sense until the optional eAssessment in MYP 5. The habit it builds is extended, criterion-referenced writing: a student is rewarded for method, communication and reflection, not only for the right answer. Students who are strong here tend to be the ones who later write a clean Internal Assessment, because the criteria vocabulary is already familiar.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Fujairah usually hit their first real wall at the move into DP mathematics, where a criterion-marked investigation is replaced by a timed Paper 1 with no calculator. Because year groups on the east coast are small, the MYP 5 class and the DP 1 class are often taught by the same person, so a gap in algebraic fluency can travel intact from one to the other. We diagnose from MYP criterion A and C scores before assuming the problem is the new course.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject is graded 1-7, and TOK with the Extended Essay together contribute up to three bonus points, for a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the Diploma pass threshold, subject to the IB's conditions on failing conditions and minimum grades. Most of the grade is external: written papers sat in the session, with the internally assessed component worth 20-30% depending on the subject.
programmes.countryNote: The practical problem for a Fujairah DP student is subject-level isolation. Full Diploma provision is concentrated in Dubai, Sharjah and Abu Dhabi, so east-coast families are either commuting across the mountains, boarding, or studying in a small cohort where one HL subject has a single teacher and no second opinion. An IB Diploma tutor on the UAE east coast is therefore usually the student's only source of component-specific feedback: the second reader on an exploration, and the person who has marked Paper 3 before.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed by syllabus code, with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects. Mathematics 0580 splits into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended, which reaches A*. Sciences run as separate 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, or as Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. Most science syllabuses now assess practical skills through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a live examined practical, which matters for any student preparing outside a school laboratory.
programmes.countryNote: Tier entry is the decision that catches Fujairah families, and it is made by the school in late February for the June series. A student entered for 0580 Core cannot be awarded above a C however well the paper goes, and the entry is not easily reversed afterwards. A Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tutor who has taught both tiers can tell you by November whether Extended is realistic, which is early enough to matter. We ask for the mock script, not the mock grade, to make that call.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs the same two-year span with different codes and a different rhythm: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. There is a January series as well as the summer one, which gives a student a second sitting inside the same school year. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher, with papers of equal weight rather than one calculator-free paper carrying a disproportionate share.
programmes.countryNote: Mixed-board timetables are common on the east coast, because small schools pick whichever syllabus suits the staff they have. A Fujairah student can easily sit Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics in the same summer, with two different formula booklets and two different grade scales. An IGCSE tutor in Fujairah needs to know which board owns which subject before the first session, so we take the exact codes from the school's entry list rather than guessing from the textbook.

fujairah.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma subjects Fujairah families ask about most, and each description names what the component actually assesses rather than restating the subject title. Where a subject is commonly taught by a single teacher in a small east-coast cohort, a second specialist reading the same work is worth more than extra hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under time pressure, with HL carrying proof by induction, complex numbers and a separate Paper 3 of long structured investigations. A Maths Analysis and Approaches HL tutor spends most of the first month on Paper 1 technique, because the no-calculator paper is where a capable student most often loses marks they already know how to earn.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the graphic display calculator central rather than incidental. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference. The common failure is treating AI as the easier route: the content differs from AA rather than sitting below it, and several engineering and mathematics degrees still expect AA.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44% of the grade. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where east-coast students most often stall. An IB Chemistry HL tutor works from the student's own marked scripts, because the recurring loss is command-term precision rather than missing content.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward careful algebra; the data-based questions in Paper 1B reward reading a graph properly. HL extends into rigid-body mechanics, induction and quantum phenomena. Students who arrive from MYP science without strong equation manipulation tend to lose marks in rearrangement and unit work rather than in physics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of terminology plus a demanding scientific investigation. The syllabus is organised around unifying themes, so a question can cross topics a student revised separately. Marks go missing in explain and outline questions where an answer lists facts without connecting them to the stated context.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries of up to 800 words each, worth 20% at HL and 30% at SL, plus the HL-only Paper 3 at 30% with its quantitative and policy-evaluation questions. The commentary is where most of the recoverable marks sit, because it is graded on the application of a single key concept, not on the quality of the news article chosen.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with Paper 1 built on a pre-released case and Paper 2 on unseen stimulus and quantitative tools. The Internal Assessment differs by level: HL writes a research project on a real organisation, SL a commentary on supporting documents. Evaluation, not description, is the examiner's demand in the higher mark bands.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, 2h15 at HL and 1h15 at SL. Paper 2 is a comparative essay on studied works. HL adds the 1,200-1,500 word HL Essay. Students in the UAE often have stronger literary than non-literary reading, so Paper 1 is usually the priority.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A treats Arabic as a language of literature and textual analysis; Arabic B is acquisition, assessed through listening, reading, writing and an individual oral. Choosing between them affects both the DP grade and the ministry's expectations, and the choice is harder to reverse than families assume.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers system fundamentals and computational thinking; HL adds abstract data structures and a case study published annually. The solution development component rewards a documented design process. Self-taught coders routinely lose marks on documentation and testing rather than on code.

fujairah.igcseSubjectsIntro: Fujairah's private schools lean towards IGCSE at Years 10 and 11, often with a mixed board list. These are the syllabuses we are asked for most, with the codes to check against your school's entry sheet before anything else is agreed.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decision dominates everything. 0580 Core is capped at grade C; Extended reaches A*. Edexcel 4MA1 splits Foundation and Higher across two equally weighted papers. Most lost marks in the Extended paper are in algebraic fractions, transformation of graphs and multi-step problems where working is not shown.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: A bridge course for students heading to A-level or DP mathematics, covering calculus, trigonometric identities, vectors and series. It is taught in very few east-coast schools, so students often sit it with minimal timetabled support, which makes it one of the most common online requests we receive.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are the reliable difficulty, followed by the alternative-to-practical paper, which asks students to design and critique an experiment in writing. Working through past alternative-to-practical papers transfers directly, because the question types repeat across series.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade more than any other topic, and a student who cannot do mole calculations confidently will cap out regardless of how much organic chemistry is memorised. Qualitative analysis tables and ionic equations are the other reliable mark sources.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions have to be exact, and extended-response questions reward structured answers over long ones. Students lose marks on genetic crosses, transport in plants and the data-interpretation questions that ask them to describe a trend before explaining it.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
igcseSubjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double award, usually chosen so a student can keep a broad subject list. The compression is the problem: topic coverage per hour is high and there is little classroom time to revisit anything. Revision has to be timetabled against the syllabus, not against the textbook chapters.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510)
igcseSubjects.description: 0500 assesses reading passages and directed writing; 0510 assesses listening, reading, writing and speaking for second-language users. Placing a student in the wrong one is common in schools with mixed intakes, and it is a decision worth checking against a timed piece of writing rather than a teacher's impression.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation and a worked diagram. In Economics the diagram is the answer, not decoration, and an unlabelled axis costs marks every time. Business Studies questions carrying eight or more marks need an applied judgement tied to the case, not a general advantage-and-disadvantage list.

fujairah.regionsTitle: Fujairah, the east coast and the places the regulator map changes
fujairah.regionsIntro: Fujairah emirate runs along the Gulf of Oman from Dibba in the north to the Omani border in the south, with inland pockets reached through the mountain passes. Several places on this coast are not in Fujairah at all, which changes who inspects the school and which term dates apply.

regions.name: Fujairah city, Faseel and Sakamkam
regions.note: The emirate's centre of gravity: the corniche, the port and most of its private schools. Nearly every private-school option within a short drive is here, which means one disappointing option in a subject leaves very little to switch to.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The northern end of the coast, where a single town is split three ways between Fujairah, Sharjah and Oman. Dibba Al-Fujairah tuition requests usually come from families with a 40-minute school run each way and no appetite for a second one in the evening.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Coastal villages between Fujairah city and the Sharjah exclaves, served mainly by ministry schools. Families here are the clearest case for online tuition: the specialist does not exist within reach, and the coast road is the only way in or out.

regions.name: Al Aqah and Sharm
regions.note: The northern hotel strip, with a working population on shift patterns. Scheduling matters more than subject choice for these families, and a fixed evening slot that survives a parent's rota is worth more than a nominally cheaper hour.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: A mountain village on the road to Ras Al Khaimah, split between the two emirates. Either side is inspected by the federal ministry, so the emirate boundary changes the address and the term calendar more than it changes the inspection framework.

regions.name: Bithnah and Wadi Ham
regions.note: The inland route through the Hajar mountains towards Sharjah, and the road any visiting tutor would have to drive. In practice it is the reason a twice-weekly visit from a Sharjah specialist prices itself out before teaching starts.

regions.name: Al Hayl and the inland valleys
regions.note: Small settlements behind Fujairah city, where school choice narrows to whatever is reachable in the morning. Connectivity is good enough for live video, which is the only part of the equation that has improved in the last few years.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan and Kalba
regions.note: Both are Sharjah exclaves on the east coast, 20 to 40 minutes from Fujairah city, and both are inspected by SPEA rather than the ministry. A parent comparing two schools across that line is comparing reports written under different authorities.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the east coast
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private-school list is short and mostly British or Indian curriculum through to IGCSE. That is the whole point of this page: a short list means a small cohort, a small cohort means one teacher per subject, and one teacher per subject means no second opinion on an HL script.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: The nearest alternatives across the mountains, and the schools east-coast families most often transfer into when a subject list runs out. Note that these sit under SPEA in Sharjah and under the federal ministry in Ras Al Khaimah, so the reports read differently even where the framework is shared.
schools: Scholars Indian School, Ras Al Khaimah

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Where full Diploma provision is actually concentrated, and where a Fujairah family relocating or boarding for Years 12 and 13 usually ends up looking. A student who stays on the east coast and studies online is competing with these cohorts in the same session, which is the honest reason component-level teaching matters.

sections.heading: Who inspects your child's school in Fujairah, and what the band actually tells you
paragraphs: Fujairah's private schools are inspected by the federal Ministry of Education, which applies the national school inspection framework used across the country. The framework issues a single overall judgement on a six-point scale: Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak. Acceptable is defined as the minimum standard, not as a middling result, and that single word is the one most often misread by parents on the east coast.

The reason it is misread is that the judgement describes a school, averaged over a cohort. Your decision concerns one student sitting one paper in one series. A school judged Good can hold a mathematics department that has lost two teachers in a year, and a school judged Acceptable can have a strong single teacher in the subject your child is weakest at. The overall band is where to start reading, not where to stop.

What to do with it is practical. Find the overall band, then find the subject-level attainment and progress judgements for your child's phase, then compare the two. Where the subject judgement sits below the school's overall band, the school knows it has a problem and is probably working on it. Where attainment is acceptable but progress is weak, the cohort is coasting. Where progress is strong and attainment is low, the teaching is working and the starting point was simply behind. Those three patterns call for three different tutoring plans, and only the last one is mostly about time.
bullets: Read the overall band first, then the subject and phase judgements underneath it.
Acceptable means the minimum standard was met, which is a floor rather than reassurance.
Attainment and progress are judged separately; the combination is what tells you something.
A subject judged below the school's overall band is the one to spend on first.

sections.heading: Reading a Ministry of Education inspection report as a tutoring brief
paragraphs: The framework judges six performance standards. Most parents read the first and skim the rest, which wastes the useful half of the document. The standards cover students' achievement; their personal and social development and innovation skills; teaching and assessment; the curriculum; the protection, care, guidance and support of students; and leadership and management. Each one has a practical consequence for a family deciding whether to buy tuition and what to buy.

Standard one is where the subject gets named. Standard three tells you whether marking is specific enough for your child to know why a mark was lost, which is the single most common reason a capable student plateaus. Standard four explains option blocks, and it is the standard that answers the question Fujairah parents ask most often: why is the subject my child wants not on the list? A narrow curriculum judgement in a small school is usually a staffing arithmetic problem rather than a policy choice.

Standard six matters more here than it would in Dubai. In a school with one teacher per IB subject, leadership and staffing judgements translate directly into continuity. A departure mid-year in a cohort of four HL students is not a gap the school can cover internally. That is the scenario where an outside specialist stops being an enhancement and becomes the only continuous reader of the student's work across the two years of the Diploma.

One more habit worth forming: read the report your school received two cycles ago alongside the current one. Inspection reports list recommendations, and the useful question is not what the school was told to improve but whether the same recommendation appears twice. A repeated recommendation in the subject your child is weakest at tells you the gap is structural and is unlikely to close inside the two years you have. A recommendation that has disappeared tells you the department has capacity and that your money is better spent elsewhere.

sections.heading: The regulator map of the east coast: the Ministry, SPEA and the Omani border
paragraphs: Nowhere else in the country is the question who regulates this school harder to answer than on this coast. Fujairah emirate is inspected by the federal Ministry of Education. Khor Fakkan and Kalba, both well inside the east coast and both a short drive from Fujairah city, are Sharjah exclaves and fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Dibba is divided between Fujairah, Sharjah's Dibba Al-Hisn and Oman's Dibba Al-Baya, which puts three education systems inside one town.

This is not pedantry. The regulator sets the inspection cycle, publishes the report in its own format, governs fee increases and issues the circulars that decide term dates and Ramadan timings. Two families living ten minutes apart can be working to different calendars and reading differently structured reports about schools they are directly comparing. A parent who assumes Dubai's rules apply because Dubai's rules are what the internet discusses will get the details wrong.

For tuition the practical consequences are smaller but real. Lesson scheduling has to follow the school's actual calendar rather than a national average, which is why we ask which authority publishes your school's term dates before fixing a weekly slot. Certificate attestation and equivalency, by contrast, are federal: the Ministry of Education handles those for every emirate, so a Khor Fakkan family and a Fujairah city family follow the same route there even though their schools answer to different inspectors.

The map also explains a pattern we see in enquiries. Families in Qidfa and Mirbah often have schools in two emirates within the same half-hour drive, and they compare an inspection report written by SPEA with one written by the ministry as though the two documents were interchangeable. They are not, in format or in publication cycle, even where the underlying standards are shared. If you are weighing two schools across that line, compare the subject-level attainment and progress judgements rather than the headline band, because those are the parts that mean the same thing in both reports.

paragraphs: Most competitor pages for this query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not a currency any UAE family transacts in. Below are the AED bands we can attribute, taken from what providers publish and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. They are market rates, not ours. IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list, because the right answer depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain before the session.

Two things distort these bands on the east coast. The first is travel. Any figure for a visiting tutor already has a drive priced into it, and from Fujairah that drive is longer than the lesson for most specialists. The second is scarcity: in a thin market the rate for a rare subject is set by availability rather than by qualification, which is how a generalist ends up charging specialist money for Chemistry HL. Monthly packages circulate too, commonly around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

What to do with the table is simple. Decide which band the teaching your child needs actually sits in, then check that what you are quoted matches that band rather than the band above it. A homework supervisor at AED 60 an hour is good value for homework supervision and poor value for an exploration that needs criterion-level feedback. Ask what the tutor has marked, not how many years they have taught.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room versus one-to-one online, measured from the east coast
paragraphs: Parents searching for a home tutor in Fujairah are asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a straight answer before anything is sold. Visiting tuition works where the specialist lives nearby. In Fujairah the specialist for a less common IB subject usually does not. Dubai and Sharjah are roughly 130 to 150 kilometres away by road, through either the Wadi Ham pass or the coast and Masafi routes, and a round trip of two to three hours sits around a 60-minute lesson.

That arithmetic produces one of two outcomes. Either the family pays for the drive, which is why visiting rates run to AED 500 an hour, or the family settles for whoever is local, which usually means a generalist covering three sciences. Neither is a good trade for an HL student. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a family here is delivered online, one to one, over live video.

The honest case for working this way is not that online is universally better. It is that the choice on this coast is between a specialist on a screen and a generalist in the room, and for a single named component the specialist wins. There are real losses: a tutor on video cannot read body language as well, and a student who will not engage without someone physically present is a poor fit. We would rather say that than pretend the format is costless.

sections.heading: The May 2027 session, counted backwards month by month
paragraphs: No competitor page for this query names a single exam session, registration deadline or results date. That is strange, because the calendar is the one part of the year that cannot be renegotiated. A Fujairah family starting tuition in October 2026 has a fixed set of dates ahead of it, and the useful planning direction is backwards from the papers rather than forwards from today.

Three deadlines do real damage when missed. IB registration closes with the school in mid-November for the following May, and that is when HL and SL levels are locked. Cambridge entries for the June series close around late February, which is when the 0580 Core or Extended decision becomes final. The IB enquiry upon results window closes in mid-September, which is the only route to a remark if a grade looks wrong against every piece of evidence you hold.

Dates below follow the usual pattern rather than a published calendar for your specific school, and schools set internal deadlines four to six weeks earlier than the board's. Confirm every one of them with your exams officer. Ramadan is expected across February and March 2027, overlapping the mock-results window, and that overlap is the single most predictable scheduling problem on this coast.

Counting backwards also reframes what tuition is for at each point in the year. From October to December the work is content and technique, because there is time to rebuild a topic chain properly. From January to February it is timed practice against published grade boundaries. From March the useful work narrows to recovering marks the student almost earns already, and from April it is markscheme reading and exam-day discipline. A family that starts in March can still move a grade; a family that starts in March expecting the October programme cannot.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go missing, paper by paper
paragraphs: A grade is not a general level of ability. It is a total of marks awarded against a published scheme on named components, and almost every student who is stuck is stuck on one or two of them. The weightings below are the reason: a Fujairah student losing a third of Paper 1 in Maths AA SL is losing more than a student who never writes the exploration, even though the exploration feels like the bigger piece of work.

The recurring losses are specific and diagnosable. In Maths AA HL it is Paper 3, where candidates abandon the later parts of a long structured investigation rather than attempting them for method marks. In the sciences it is Paper 1B, the data-based section, which rewards careful graph reading over recall and which most revision programmes barely touch. In Economics HL it is Paper 3, where quantitative questions and the final policy evaluation sit together. In English A it is the unseen non-literary text in Paper 1.

This is also why a tutor should ask for the marked script before quoting a programme of work. A grade 4 can be a content problem, a timing problem or a command-term problem, and the three need different work. We read the script against the markscheme and the published grade boundaries, then say which component is worth the first eight weeks. If the honest answer is that the gap is small and the school is handling it, that is also a legitimate answer.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment criterion by criterion, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The internally assessed component is worth 20% of most DP subjects and 30% in a few, and it is marked against published criteria with named letters and fixed mark allocations. No competitor page for this query names a single criterion. That is a gap worth closing, because the criteria are the specification: a student who knows that criterion B in a mathematical exploration carries four marks for communication writes a different document from one who thinks it is a project about a topic they like.

A mathematical exploration is marked out of 20: criterion A presentation carries four marks, B mathematical communication four, C personal engagement three, D reflection three and E use of mathematics six. The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, within a 3,000-word limit. Economics requires three commentaries of up to 800 words each. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria within 4,000 words, and the TOK essay answers a prescribed title in 1,600 words.

Here is the boundary, stated plainly because one competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments and that is an academic-integrity breach as well as a malpractice trigger for the student. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion rewards, question a research question until it is answerable, point at a weak section and say why it is weak, and comment on structure and referencing. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite, edit or supply any part of assessed work, provide a topic to be adopted wholesale, or produce data. The student authors it. We keep a record of each review session so a school supervisor can see exactly where support began and ended.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, attestation and the route into UAE universities
paragraphs: Equivalency is federal, so it works identically for a family in Fujairah city, in Khor Fakkan and in Dubai even though three different bodies inspect those schools. The Ministry of Education issues the equivalency certificate that converts an international school-leaving qualification into something a UAE university or employer can act on, and it is the step families discover late, usually in Year 13 when an application asks for it. Nobody else writing about tuition for this query mentions it at all.

The shape of the requirement is worth knowing early, because it changes subject choices. The IB route expects the full Diploma rather than a handful of course certificates, and the Diploma's own pass threshold is 24 points with conditions on minimum grades. The British route expects a set of IGCSE or GCSE passes alongside Year 13 study at A-level and AS level, with no subject counted twice at two levels. Arabic, Islamic Studies and UAE Social Studies are required study for the students the rules cover, and they are recorded by the school, but they are not part of the counted academic subject total.

Attestation is the separate, procedural half: the certificate itself has to be verified through the issuing route and then processed through the UAE channels before the ministry will act on it. Start it before results day rather than after, because the queue lengthens every August. The published requirements do change, so treat the table below as a map of the questions to ask and confirm the current detail on the ministry's own portal before relying on any of it. MoE equivalency for IGCSE students is also the reason a student should not quietly drop to four subjects in Year 11.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the east-coast school day, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: School days shorten during Ramadan across the UAE, and the ministry publishes the timings private schools in Fujairah follow. Ramadan is expected to fall across February and March in 2027, which lands it directly on top of the mock-results window and the start of the final revision run. That collision is predictable a year ahead, and it is the main reason we ask families to book the exam-term block in November rather than in March.

What works in practice is moving the slot rather than cancelling it. A session that sat at 5pm shifts to after Iftar, often somewhere between 8.30pm and 10pm, and a 60-minute slot works better than 90 minutes for a fasting student. Because the tutor is online and may be in a different time zone, that shift is a scheduling change rather than a logistical problem, and it can go back to the original time after Eid without renegotiating anything.

The last thing to be honest about is availability. Fujairah families ask for genuinely rare combinations: Computer Science HL, Arabic A literature, Additional Mathematics 0606, Economics HL in the weeks before Paper 3. Sometimes no specialist in that exact component is free at the hour your child can work. When that happens we say so, give an honest estimate of the wait, and offer the nearest real alternative rather than a generalist described as a specialist. A fortnight's wait for the right tutor beats eight weeks with the wrong one, and a family that is told the truth once will believe the next thing we say.

process.description: Not the grades, the scripts. A marked paper plus the school's most recent inspection report tells us whether the gap is personal to your child or a pattern across the cohort, and those two cases need different plans. If you do not have a script to hand, the last report card and a photograph of a recent test will do to start.

We work out which paper, criterion or syllabus section is costing the most marks per hour of work, and say whether tuition is the right answer at all. Sometimes it is not, and sometimes the honest recommendation is six weeks rather than two terms.

process.description: The trial runs with the tutor proposed for the slot, not with a coordinator. Your child works on real material and you get the tutor's written read of where the marks are. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist with it.

Sessions are delivered online over live video. After each lesson the student keeps the annotated script and the notes, so progress is auditable rather than remembered.

process.description: Every few weeks the plan is checked against the registration deadlines, mock dates and session dates that actually apply to your child. From February onwards the work shifts to timed papers and markscheme reading, and new content is only introduced if a syllabus audit shows a genuine gap.

whyPoints.title: We read the Ministry of Education report with you
whyPoints.description: Fujairah's private schools are inspected by the federal ministry, and the report is the best free diagnostic a parent has. We read the subject and phase judgements with you before recommending anything, because the subject lagging the school's overall band is usually the subject worth paying for first.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by driving distance
whyPoints.description: The east coast's tutor pool is thin, so matching by proximity means matching by chance. We match on the component your child is actually assessed on: 0580 Extended, 0625, Maths AA HL Paper 3, Economics HL Paper 3. The tutor's claim to the subject is what they have taught and marked.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, one student, every session
whyPoints.description: No group classes and no rotating tutors. The same person reads every script for the full programme, which is what makes a diagnosis stick instead of being redone each month. In a cohort where one teacher covers an HL subject alone, that continuity is often the only second reading a student's work gets.

whyPoints.title: Explicit about the academic-honesty line

A tutor does not write, draft, edit or supply assessed work. We log each coursework review so a school supervisor can see where help began and ended, which protects the student's own authorship.

faqs.question: Which authority inspects private schools in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education. Dubai's private schools are inspected by KHDA, Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's by ADEK, and Sharjah's by SPEA, but Fujairah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain sit with the ministry directly. It applies the same national inspection framework and the same six judgement bands, from Outstanding down to Very Weak, so the vocabulary in the report will look familiar to anyone who has read a Dubai one. The practical differences are where the report is published, who issues the circulars that set term dates and Ramadan timings, and which body handles a complaint about the school.

faqs.question: What does an Acceptable inspection judgement actually mean for my child's maths?
faqs.answer: It means the school's performance met the minimum standard the framework defines, averaged across a cohort. It is a floor, not reassurance. A year group judged Acceptable in secondary mathematics can contain students working two grades apart, and a weaker student can sit well below the line without it appearing anywhere. Read the subject-level attainment and progress judgements for your child's phase, then compare them with the overall band. If attainment is acceptable but progress is weak, the cohort is coasting and the work is pace. If progress is strong and attainment low, teaching is working and the starting point was simply behind.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors charge around Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE run roughly AED 45-150 an hour for a budget or university-student tutor, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180-500 for visiting tuition once travel is inside the fee, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner end. Those are other providers' figures and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, not ours. IB Gram does not publish an hourly list; the first step is a free trial and a short call.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to get a subject specialist to drive to Fujairah twice a week?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the arithmetic is the reason rather than any policy. Dubai and Sharjah are roughly 130 to 150 kilometres away over the Hajar mountains, so a round trip runs two to three hours around a 60-minute lesson. Either that drive is priced into the fee, which is how visiting rates reach AED 500 an hour, or the tutor is local and usually a generalist covering several sciences. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Fujairah families are delivered online, one to one, over live video.

faqs.question: Does a school in Dibba Al-Fujairah fall under the Ministry of Education or under Sharjah's SPEA?
faqs.answer: It depends which Dibba. The town is split three ways: Dibba Al-Fujairah is in Fujairah and inspected by the federal ministry, Dibba Al-Hisn is a Sharjah exclave inspected by SPEA, and Dibba Al-Baya is in Oman's Musandam governorate under Omani authorities. Khor Fakkan and Kalba, further south on the same coast, are also Sharjah and also SPEA. So two families living minutes apart can be reading differently structured reports and working to different term calendars. Check which authority publishes your school's term dates before you fix a weekly tuition slot around them.

faqs.question: My daughter is one of three students taking Chemistry HL. Can tuition fix being in such a small cohort?
faqs.answer: It cannot change the cohort, but it addresses the actual consequence of it. A class of three usually means one teacher, no second opinion on a script, and no moderating comparison with a larger group. What an outside specialist adds is a second reader: someone who has marked Paper 2 extended responses before, who can tell your daughter whether an answer meets the command term, and who reads the scientific investigation against criteria A to D rather than against a general impression. That second reading is the part a small cohort structurally cannot provide, and it matters most in the exploration and in Paper 1B data questions.

faqs.question: When does registration close for the IB May session?
faqs.answer: Registration closes with your school in mid-November of the previous year, with a late window running to mid-January and additional fees attached. That November deadline is when HL and SL levels and any subject change are effectively locked, so a decision about dropping an HL has to be made in the autumn rather than after the mocks. Results for the May session are published on 6 July, and the enquiry upon results window, which is how a remark is requested, closes in mid-September. Schools set their own internal deadlines four to six weeks ahead of the board's, so confirm the exact dates with your exams officer.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if my child is tutored online?
faqs.answer: In most current Cambridge and Edexcel science syllabuses the practical skills are assessed through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a live examined practical, so what a student needs is the ability to design an experiment, identify variables, read apparatus correctly and criticise a method in writing. That work transfers to a screen without loss, and past alternative-to-practical papers are the most efficient preparation there is because the question types repeat across series. Laboratory work for coursework or school assessment stays with the school. Check the exact syllabus code on your school's entry sheet, because the assessment pattern differs between boards and between subjects.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Maths exploration without breaking the IB's honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the mathematics, explain what each criterion rewards, press on whether the research question is answerable, point at an undefined variable or an unlabelled axis and explain the cost, and comment on structure and referencing. A tutor cannot write, draft, rewrite, edit or supply any part of the exploration, hand over a topic to be adopted whole, or produce the data. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is an integrity breach and a malpractice risk carried by the student, not the seller. We log each review session so a supervisor can see where help began and ended.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education want for equivalency if my son sits IGCSEs and then A-levels?
faqs.answer: The British route expects a set of IGCSE or GCSE passes at grade C or 4 and above, with Year 13 study at A-level and AS level above them, and no subject counted twice at two different levels. IGCSE on its own is treated as the Grade 10 or 11 stage rather than a school-leaving qualification, which is why dropping to four subjects in Year 11 can create a problem two years later. The certificate also has to be attested through the issuing route and the UAE channels before the ministry acts on it. Requirements are published and do change, so confirm the current list on the ministry's portal.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Studies counted in the equivalency subject total?
faqs.answer: No. They are required study for the students the ministry's rules cover, and the school records that study, but they are not part of the counted academic subject total used for equivalency. That catches families out in both directions: some assume Arabic will fill a subject slot and find it does not, and others treat it as optional and discover the school is obliged to timetable it. UAE Social Studies sits in the same category. Plan the counted subjects separately from the required ones, and ask your school in writing which of your child's subjects it expects to submit for equivalency.

faqs.question: How does the shortened Ramadan school day change our weekly tuition slot?
faqs.answer: School days shorten during Ramadan under timings the ministry publishes for Fujairah's schools, so an afternoon slot that worked in January usually stops working. Most families here move the session to after Iftar, commonly between 8.30pm and 10pm, and cut it from 90 minutes to 60 for a fasting student. Because the tutor is working online rather than driving over the mountains, that is a calendar change and nothing more, and the slot returns to its original time after Eid. Ramadan is expected across February and March in 2027, directly over the mock-results window, so book the exam-term block in November.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Fujairah need a permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through MoHRE, which issues a private tutor permit, and every regulatory source we checked states that the permit itself is issued free of charge. The requirement is federal, so it applies on the east coast exactly as it does in Dubai. An employed applicant may need their employer's agreement, and tutoring at a scale that becomes a business is treated differently from individual tutoring. Penalties for tutoring without a permit have been reported without published figures, so treat any specific fine amount circulating online with caution and check the current terms on the MoHRE portal.

faqs.question: How late in Year 11 can we start IGCSE tuition and still change the grade?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents fear, with one hard constraint: the tier entry. A student entered for Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Core cannot be awarded above a C however good the paper is, and entries for the June series close around late February. Inside the right tier, a focused run from February is often enough to move a grade, because the work is recovering marks already nearly earned rather than learning new content. We start from the mock script, list what the markscheme awarded and what it refused, and order the work by marks recoverable per hour. What rarely works is new content from April onwards.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers the exact subject we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, give an honest estimate of the wait, and offer the nearest real alternative rather than a generalist relabelled as a specialist. Fujairah families ask for genuinely rare combinations: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science HL, Arabic A literature, Economics HL in the final weeks before Paper 3. For a component as specific as Paper 3 that can mean a fortnight's wait for the right person. A fortnight's wait beats eight weeks with the wrong tutor, and it is also the only answer that survives the second conversation.

faqs.question: Should my child take Maths Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Start from the degree, not from the perceived difficulty. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with a calculator-free Paper 1 and, at HL, a separate Paper 3 of long investigations. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with the calculator central throughout. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many computer science courses, in the UAE and abroad, still expect Analysis and Approaches, often at HL, while economics, business and life-science routes commonly accept either. Check the stated entry requirements of three target universities before the November registration deadline, because changing route after that point is difficult.

fujairah.closingHeading: Start with the report, then the script, then the slot
fujairah.closingBody: If your child is in a Fujairah school, you already hold the two documents that matter: the ministry's inspection report and the last marked paper. Send both. We will read the subject and phase judgements against the script, say which component is costing the most marks, and tell you whether tuition is the right answer or whether the school is already handling it. If it is the right answer, the next step is a free trial with the specialist who would actually teach the slot, delivered online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. If the specialist is not free, we will say that too.

intro.heading: In Al Faseel the constraint is the calendar, not the commute
paragraphs: Al Faseel sits on the Fujairah City coastline near the corniche and the port, close to the emirate's private-school cluster. A child living here is usually at school within fifteen minutes, which removes the problem that defines tutoring further up the coast. What replaces it is a scheduling problem. The afternoon between the final bell and dinner is the most contested block of time in a Fujairah City household, and it rarely has an empty hour in it by accident.

Look at a typical week honestly. Two afternoons go to sport or swimming at the corniche clubs. One goes to Arabic or Islamic Education homework, which in a UAE private school is real homework with real assessments attached rather than a token subject. Maghrib shifts the usable evening depending on the time of year. A sibling's schedule takes another slot. By the time a parent sits down to book a weekly tutoring session, the week has one or perhaps two viable windows, and they are not at the hour most tutors prefer.

That is why delivery format decides whether a plan survives. IB Gram teaches UAE students online, one to one, over live video, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. For an Al Faseel family the gain is not distance saved but flexibility: a 6.15pm slot can become a 8.45pm post-Iftar slot during Ramadan without renegotiating with someone who has to drive, and a cancelled football session can be converted into a lesson at short notice rather than lost.

The second thing an Al Faseel plan has to respect is the mandatory UAE curriculum running alongside the international one. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects are timetabled, examined and reported on, and they compete for exactly the same evening hours as IGCSE Chemistry revision. A study plan that pretends they do not exist fails in week three.

There is a third fact that shapes an Al Faseel plan, and it is the one families discover late. Fujairah's private-school cohorts are small, so option blocks are narrower than in Dubai and a student may end up with a subject combination chosen by the timetable rather than by interest. The same scarcity applies to Diploma classes: a student taking a less common Higher Level subject may be one of a handful in the whole emirate, which makes a matched specialist harder to find locally and makes the tutor, rather than a classmate, the only other person who reads a draft.

What follows is written around those facts. It maps the Fujairah City week, sets out how the mandatory subjects are organised and taught, explains the Core and Extended tier decision that quietly caps an IGCSE grade, reads the Pearson Edexcel session calendar in order, compares what a tuition centre and an online specialist actually deliver, and puts tutoring cost next to the other numbers in a UAE family's education budget.
bullets: Al Faseel is minutes from the Fujairah City school cluster, so distance is not the issue
Afternoons are taken by sport, Arabic and Islamic Education work, and prayer times
Lessons are delivered online one to one, which makes the slot movable
Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are examined subjects competing for the same hours
Tier and syllabus code, not subject name, decide which specialist is the right match

fujairah/al-faseel.programmesIntro: Three routes account for nearly every Al Faseel enquiry: IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, the IB Diploma in Years 12 and 13, and the Middle Years Programme before either. Each carries a different kind of deadline pressure, so each needs a different session rhythm.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11. Cambridge identifies syllabuses by four-digit code, such as 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, and splits several of them into Core and Extended tiers. Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1 and takes a different approach to tiering and to practical assessment, which changes how a paper should be practised.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Faseel student carries Arabic and Islamic Education on top of this load, and in a British-curriculum school those lessons are timetabled against the same week as IGCSE options. The practical effect is that revision time is scarcer than the subject count suggests, so a tutoring plan has to pick one or two subjects and work on them properly rather than spreading an hour across four.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments are marked against published criteria and submitted months before the written papers, which means the heaviest weeks of the Diploma are coursework weeks rather than exam weeks. Most families misjudge that and book help too late.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah runs very few Diploma cohorts, so an Al Faseel student may be among a small number in the emirate taking a particular Higher Level subject. Sessions therefore carry a load they would not elsewhere: the tutor is often the only person other than the class teacher who reads a draft. That argues for starting coursework support early in the cycle rather than near the deadline.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four published criteria and reported as criterion levels rather than percentages. The programme rewards investigation and reflection, which means a student can hold strong subject knowledge and still sit at a middling criterion level because the explanation of method is thin. That pattern transfers straight into Diploma internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP in the UAE still sits under the federal requirement for Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, so an Al Faseel student is managing criterion-based assessment in eight groups plus mandatory subjects with their own assessments. Session time is best spent on the criteria the reports show as weakest rather than on general subject revision.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 route most British-curriculum schools on this coast offer. Three or four subjects in depth with externally examined papers, and a noticeable jump in abstraction from IGCSE, sharpest in mathematics and physics. Cambridge and Pearson structure the qualification differently, and the modular pattern changes when a student can bank a result.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, in addition to five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects. An Al Faseel family planning a UAE university application should read the current requirement on the Ministry's own pages before fixing subject choices.

fujairah/al-faseel.subjectsIntro: This list reflects what Fujairah City families actually ask for, which includes the mandatory UAE subjects as often as it includes IGCSE sciences. Each line names what the assessment rewards, because that is what a session can change.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Reading comprehension of unseen classical and modern texts, grammar, and extended writing in Standard Arabic. UAE private schools organise this as a separate stream from Arabic as an additional language, and the two are not interchangeable. Marks are usually lost on grammatical accuracy in extended writing rather than on comprehension.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Functional reading, listening, controlled writing and speaking for students who did not begin in Arabic. Progress is fastest with short frequent practice rather than long weekly sessions, because vocabulary retention drives the grade. Students often plateau when they rely on transliteration instead of reading the script fluently.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: A timetabled, assessed subject in UAE private schools, taught in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arab students. Content is set and schools may not substitute material without prior Ministry permission, so support work means teaching the prescribed content properly rather than finding alternatives.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: UAE history, geography, civics and values, assessed in school and reported on. Delivered in Arabic for Arab students and in the licensed curriculum language for others. Students who treat it as a soft subject lose marks on structured extended answers, which respond quickly to the same paragraph-planning work that helps humanities essays.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry and statistics across two papers. The tier decides the grade ceiling, so confirming which tier a school entered is the first question. Marks go missing on rounding instructions, bearings and multi-stage percentage problems where a student answers the first stage and stops.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics content compressed into one or two award structures. Students frequently revise it as three subjects and run out of time, when the examined content is narrower than the separate sciences. Knowing exactly which sub-topics are excluded is worth several grades of revision efficiency.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, in some variants, an assessed speaking component. The writing marks reward register and task fulfilment as much as accuracy, so a student who writes a fluent but off-register letter loses marks they could have kept. Practice under timed conditions with marked feedback moves this quickly.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Ownership structures, marketing, operations, human resources and finance, assessed largely through case studies. Answers that explain a concept without applying it to the stimulus business score in the lower bands. The evaluation marks at the end of longer questions are the most commonly abandoned marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases and organic chemistry, with Higher Level adding orbital and electrochemical depth. The Internal Assessment is where Diploma marks are most recoverable, because evaluation and uncertainty analysis are taught skills and most students write description where the criteria ask for argument.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof, with a non-calculator paper and, at Higher Level, the long Paper 3 problem-solving paper. Method marks left unwritten are the single largest avoidable loss, followed by radian and degree errors and explorations that calculate without justifying the model chosen.

regions.note: Where the private-school cluster, tuition centres and most after-school activities sit. Convenient for everything and therefore the reason the diary fills, since each added commitment is easy to say yes to.

regions.name: Merashid

fujairah/al-faseel.modesIntro: Format should follow the gap in the diary rather than a standard package. All three options below are taught online over live video, which is what makes them movable when the week changes.

modes.title: One fixed evening a week
modes.description: A single weekly slot with the same specialist, usually sixty minutes at IGCSE and seventy-five to ninety minutes for Higher Level Diploma work. It is the format that fits an Al Faseel week because it only asks for one evening and can be placed after Maghrib. The tutor tracks the school's own scheme of work so the session reinforces that week's teaching.
bullets: One evening committed, not three
Placeable after Maghrib or after Iftar in Ramadan
Follows the school's current unit rather than a parallel syllabus
Worked solutions and a short note sent after each session

modes.title: Split sessions across two short slots
modes.description: Two thirty or forty-minute sessions instead of one long one. This suits Arabic as an additional language and vocabulary-heavy subjects, where retention responds to frequency rather than duration, and it suits a student whose afternoons are broken up by sport. It also survives a cancelled activity better, because a gap of forty minutes is usable.
bullets: Two short slots instead of one long evening block
Better retention for language and vocabulary work
Fits into gaps left by cancelled activities
Easier to sustain through a heavy sports term

modes.title: Coursework block around a school deadline
modes.description: A short run of sessions timed to the school's internal draft deadlines for an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The tutor teaches the criteria, questions the method and responds to the student's own draft. The student produces every word. The block ends at submission rather than running on, which keeps the cost tied to the deadline.
bullets: Timed to the school's own draft deadlines
Criteria explained by letter with mark allocations

sections.heading: What a short school run changes about tutoring in Al Faseel
paragraphs: An Al Faseel family searching for IB and IGCSE tutors is rarely asking who can reach them. The schools are close, the drive is short, and a tutor living in Fujairah City could be at the door in ten minutes. The question that actually needs answering is which hour of the week is free, and whether the person teaching in that hour knows the specific paper the child is sitting.

Those two requirements pull in opposite directions in a small emirate. The hours that are free in an Al Faseel week tend to be late, after sport and after prayers, and often after Iftar for a third of the year. The pool of people who teach Diploma Chemistry Higher Level in Fujairah is small, and the subset of that pool free at 8.45pm and willing to drive is smaller again. Choosing on availability means accepting a generalist.

Teaching online separates the two. The specialist is chosen for the syllabus, and the slot is chosen for the household, because no journey has to be priced into either. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; lessons are delivered live online, one to one, with the first one free. For a family whose constraint is the diary rather than the distance, that is the part that matters.

The rest of this page deals with the things that fill an Al Faseel week and the decisions that quietly set a grade ceiling: the mandatory UAE subjects and how they are organised, the Core and Extended tier choice, the Edexcel session calendar, what a tuition centre delivers compared with a matched online specialist, and where tutoring sits against the other costs of a UAE education.
bullets: The binding constraint in Al Faseel is the free hour, not the distance
Choosing a tutor by availability usually means choosing a generalist
Online delivery lets the subject pick the tutor and the household pick the time
The first lesson is free and ends with a written diagnosis

sections.heading: Mapping the Al Faseel week before booking a slot
paragraphs: Booking a tutoring slot without mapping the week is how a weekly session turns into a fortnightly one. The exercise takes ten minutes: write out the five school days, mark what is genuinely fixed, and see what is left. Most Fujairah City households discover they have one strong window and one fragile one, and that the fragile one is the slot they were about to book.

Three things do the filling. Sport and swimming at the corniche clubs take two or three afternoons. Arabic and Islamic Education homework is substantial and has its own assessments, so it cannot be displaced to make room for Chemistry. Prayer times move the usable evening through the year, and in Ramadan the whole structure inverts, with post-Iftar hours becoming the productive ones and afternoons becoming unusable.

The pattern that holds best over a full term is one fixed evening at a time chosen for the worst week rather than the best one. If Tuesday works in October but collapses once the football season starts, Tuesday was never the slot. Families who choose the awkward but reliable hour keep their session; families who choose the convenient one spend the term rescheduling.

One more variable deserves a line of its own: siblings. An Al Faseel household running two or three school timetables has a diary where the free hours of one child are the busy hours of another, and a shared car couples them together. Where two children both need support, booking them into adjacent slots on the same evening works better than spreading sessions across the week, because it protects the remaining evenings rather than nibbling at all of them.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the international curriculum
paragraphs: No competing tutoring page in this market treats these subjects as real. They are. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement sits on that foundation, and in Dubai the KHDA guidelines spell out the operational detail in a way that is useful everywhere as a reference point.

Those guidelines set out how the subjects are organised. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students and the licensed curriculum language used for non-Arabs.

Two further details affect how tutoring can honestly be offered. Teaching time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the advice is that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. More importantly, for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. Support work therefore means teaching the prescribed content well, not supplying an alternative course.

For an Al Faseel student the practical consequence is capacity. These are examined subjects with homework and reports, taught in a language that may not be the student's strongest, sitting on top of a full IGCSE or Diploma load. Any study plan that allocates every spare hour to the international curriculum is overbooked before it starts.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the IGCSE tier decision that sets a ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge splits several IGCSE subjects into a Core tier and an Extended tier, and the tier a school enters a student for caps the grade available. A student on the Core tier cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, which is why this decision deserves more attention than it usually gets in Year 10. Parents in Al Faseel often discover the tier only when a mock result does not match the effort behind it.

The tier is chosen on evidence rather than ambition. A student with secure algebra, confident trigonometry and the stamina for a longer paper belongs on Extended. A student still rebuilding number work benefits from a Core entry that lets them secure a solid pass rather than scatter marks across questions they cannot reach. Moving up a tier mid-course is possible in principle but depends on entry deadlines, which sit months before the exam.

This is where tutoring hours have the clearest return. Six to ten weeks of focused algebra and trigonometry work in Year 10 can make an Extended entry realistic that would otherwise have been ruled out, and that single decision affects the grade ceiling more than anything done in the final revision term. Starting the same work in February of Year 11 changes far less, because the entry has already been made.

Pearson Edexcel takes a different approach in several subjects, and the differences matter when comparing offers or moving school. Ask the exams officer which board, which code and which tier applies, and check the position before the entry deadline rather than after a disappointing mock.

sections.heading: The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE calendar in order
paragraphs: Al Faseel families whose school uses Pearson Edexcel are working to a different calendar from their Cambridge neighbours, and the two are easy to confuse. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which puts the autumn series much earlier in the academic year than most parents expect.

Results arrive on fixed dates rather than approximate ones. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January date is the one worth noting for anyone using a November entry as a retake or an early sitting, because it determines whether a result is available in time for a given application deadline.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for future November sittings. Provisional means revisable, so a tutoring plan built on a date read from a summary page rather than from the live official timetable can be wrong by a week. The exams officer at your child's school holds the version that counts, and it should be the only source used for planning a revision block.

Reading the series in order rather than backwards helps for this board, because the November window arrives so early. A student entered for November has their peak workload in October, which collides with the start-of-year settling period rather than with the usual spring revision season.

sections.heading: Tuition centre, group class or matched online specialist
paragraphs: Fujairah City has tuition centres, and for some purposes they are the right answer. A centre running a broad IGCSE revision course for a student who has fallen behind across several subjects offers structure and a fixed timetable at a lower cost per hour than one-to-one teaching. What a centre cannot easily do is work on one student's specific weakness in one paper of one syllabus, because the class is built around the median student in the room.

The cost picture, read from rates published by UAE providers and rate trackers in October 2026, runs from roughly AED 33 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, around AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, about AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and AED 500 and above for named or examiner-level specialists. Monthly packages advertised in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices.

A centre also adds a journey back into a week that has no room for one, and it fixes the timing to the centre's timetable rather than the household's. For an Al Faseel family whose constraint is the evening window, that is the deciding factor more often than the hourly rate. An operation with premises and staff also needs its own educational services permit, which is a different thing from an individual tutor's permit and worth asking about.

sections.heading: Where tutoring sits in a UAE family's education budget
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually assessed in isolation, which makes the hourly rate look either large or small depending on mood. It reads more clearly next to the other numbers. School fees are the dominant line, and in Dubai the regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. Fujairah fees are approved federally rather than by an emirate authority, but the direction of travel is the useful context.

Against that, a weekly one-hour session at market mid-range rates is a modest fraction of annual education spend and a large fraction of the discretionary part of it. Rate trackers put monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market estimates read in October 2026.

The decision that actually controls the total is duration, not rate. Two subjects supported for two years costs several times what one subject supported for a term does, and the second pattern is more often the one that was needed. A diagnosis that says four sessions and then a review is cheaper and usually more effective than an open-ended booking that nobody revisits until the exams are over.
