sections.heading: Week one to week four: what a good match looks like early
paragraphs: In the first session, most of the hour should be teaching. A tutor reading a marked script, asking the student to attempt a question, and then explaining why two marks went missing is doing the job; one spending forty minutes on rapport and ten on a sales pitch for a package is not. By the end of the first hour you should have a named weakness - a topic, a question type, a criterion - rather than a general impression of ability.

By week two, the test is whether the session set work and whether the work came back. Teaching produces learning through what the student does afterwards, so a tutor who sets nothing has removed the mechanism. By week three the student should be able to explain, in their own words, what they are working on and why. That is a parent-administered test, it costs nothing, and it catches a poor match faster than any progress report.

By week four there should be a fresh marked piece and a comparison. Not necessarily a better grade - four weeks is short, and claiming otherwise would be a promise nobody can keep - but visible movement in the specific thing being targeted: working set out properly, a conclusion that evaluates, a data question attempted rather than abandoned. If none of that is visible and the tutor cannot say why, the conversation to have is about changing the approach or the tutor.
bullets: Week one: most of the hour is teaching; it ends with a named weakness
Week two: work was set and the student did it
Week three: the student can explain what they are working on
Week four: a fresh marked piece shows movement in the targeted skill

sections.heading: The first term: what should be different by the end of it
paragraphs: A term is long enough to judge properly, and the things to judge are not all academic. Did the slot hold through the weeks when school assessments, a school trip and a public holiday all landed? Did the notes arrive? Did the tutor know, without being told, what the school's internal deadline was and when the next assessment fell? Reliability over twelve weeks is the strongest predictor of what the second year of a Diploma will look like.

Academically, a term should have narrowed the problem rather than widened it. Good diagnosis shrinks the work: a student who arrived failing at chemistry should by now be working on calculation layout and explanation questions, not on chemistry. If the description of the problem at week twelve is as broad as it was at week one, the sessions have been teaching the subject rather than fixing the weakness.

The third thing to look for is independence. The student should be doing something differently without being prompted - marking their own answer against criteria, writing a plan before a long task, attempting the data question first. A tutor whose student becomes more dependent across a term is producing a result that will not survive the examination hall, where nobody is available to prompt. That is the quiet failure mode in this market, and it looks like a good relationship from the outside. A simple check at the end of a term is to ask the student to work through a question with the tutor listening rather than teaching. If the student stalls and waits to be rescued, the dependence is real and it needs addressing now rather than in the examination term, when there is no time left to unwind it.
bullets: Did the slot hold through a difficult term?
Has the problem narrowed rather than broadened?
Does the tutor track the school's own calendar unprompted?
Is the student doing anything differently without being told?

sections.heading: The exam term, when best means something narrower
paragraphs: Close to the papers, the definition of a good tutor changes. Breadth stops mattering and triage starts. The work is to read the mock scripts question by question, rank the topics by marks lost against the study time each would need, and then spend the remaining weeks on that ranking, keeping the final fortnight for timed papers rather than new content. A tutor who is still teaching the syllabus in order at this stage has misread the calendar.

A second change is honesty about what remains possible. Six to eight weeks can change examination technique, timing and performance on two or three high-yield topics in one subject, and that can be worth a grade. It cannot rebuild two years across six subjects, and it cannot touch an internal assessment mark already submitted. A provider who agrees to everything at this point is selling reassurance, and reassurance is the most expensive thing in this market per unit of benefit.

The third is scheduling discipline. Exam-term sessions have to hold against school revision programmes, Ramadan in some years, and a household under strain, and on this coast they have to hold without depending on anyone crossing the mountains. Where a family is choosing between a locally available generalist and an online specialist at this stage, the deciding question is simple: which of them will still be teaching your child in the last week before the first paper. The fourth change is in what a session should contain. New explanation shrinks and marked work grows, until the final weeks are mostly the student writing and the tutor showing them where the marks went. A family paying for teaching at that stage and receiving conversation should say so, because the weeks do not come back.

sections.heading: What the price actually signals
paragraphs: Published market rates in this country sort roughly into five bands, and the bands correlate with what the tutor brings rather than with how good they are. Budget online tutoring advertises from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, often university students or generalists. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted from AED 150 to 300. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 once travel is included. IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted from AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and a premium named or examiner-led tier reaches AED 650. Monthly packages seen in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours.

Those figures come from provider pricing pages and a published 2026 Dubai rate survey. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and the useful reading of them is directional. Paying budget rates for a Higher Level Diploma subject usually buys a generalist, which is a poor trade for a narrow problem. Paying the premium tier does not buy a different syllabus, and the research found the highest-priced claims in this market are also the least evidenced. The in-home band is the clearest case of paying for something other than teaching, since a large part of it is travel.

The honest guide is to pay the qualified specialist band for the one subject that is costing the most, and to buy fewer hours of it rather than more hours of something cheaper. A single well-targeted session a week that sets work the student then does will beat three sessions that replace the student's own practice time. That is also why a provider quoting a monthly package before asking what the problem is has the sequence backwards.

sections.heading: The claims that are a reason to stop the conversation
paragraphs: Some claims are not merely overcooked; they signal a provider who will create problems. A promise of a particular grade is the obvious one, because nobody controls a student's performance in an examination hall and a refund tied to an outcome is a promise with no mechanism behind it. Regulator approval is the second: there is no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or federal ministry accreditation for a tutoring platform, so the phrase is either a misunderstanding or a fabrication.

The third is an offer to supply assessed work. Services in this search cluster sell completed internal assessments; the research found one advertising them at AED 3,750. For the student that is a malpractice trigger with the Diploma at risk, and no mark is worth that. A provider who markets coursework completion has told you what they are, and the correct response is to leave rather than negotiate the boundary.

The fourth is misdirection about where the teaching happens or who is responsible. A UAE address that is not occupied, a phone number in another country presented as a local line, a school listed as a partner without a relationship, or a statistic with no n, date or method attached. Each is a small thing; together they describe a provider whose published claims cannot be relied on, which is the single worst property a two-year academic relationship can have. None of this requires a judgement about teaching quality, which is the useful part. A parent can read a provider's own published pages, count the claims that could be checked, and see how many of them have a source, a date or a method attached. On the evidence of the pages ranking for these searches, that count is usually zero, and a provider who scores even four or five is operating differently from the market around it.

sections.heading: Fujairah: what best means on a small coast
paragraphs: Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman with the Hajar mountains separating it from the western emirates, and its private-school set is small. The practical result is generous access to teachers and limited depth in any one subject at the top level. A Higher Level Chemistry student may be one of four, taught by someone also carrying Standard Level and a lower-school course. That is arithmetic, not a failing, and it determines what outside help is for here.

It also means the best available tutor for a Fujairah family is frequently not on this coast, and pretending otherwise is the main way families get badly matched. A visiting tutor spends close to three hours on a one-hour lesson, which is why published in-home rates reach AED 500 and why the distant slot is the first casualty of a busy week. Across thirty teaching weeks, four lost sessions removes more than a month of teaching, usually from the term that mattered.

The honest position is therefore narrow and checkable. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time; a slot is chosen so it survives the whole year rather than the first month; and where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject at a workable hour, a family is told that and offered either a tutor elsewhere teaching into this time zone or an honest wait. None of that makes anyone the finest tutor on the east coast. It does make the claim checkable, which is the most any page in this search can offer.

process.title: Ask the school first, before anyone else
process.description: Which criterion or topic is weakest, for how long, and what the school is already doing about it. That conversation is free, it is better informed than any provider, and it occasionally ends the matter. Bring its answer to every tutoring conversation afterwards as the brief rather than as a question.

process.title: Send the specifics, then judge the reply
process.description: The programme, the subject, the exact level, the school and the point in the term. A reply that asks what has already been submitted internally and when the next assessment falls is doing the job. A reply that quotes a monthly package without asking anything has answered a different question.

process.title: Use the free trial as an audition
process.description: Send a marked script in advance and listen for teaching rather than selling. By the end of the hour you want a named weakness, a view on how many weeks it needs, and a short written note. One lesson, no card details, and no obligation to continue afterwards.

process.title: Buy four weeks, not a term
process.description: Four weekly sessions with the same tutor is long enough to see movement on the targeted skill and short enough that a wrong decision costs little. Ask for a fresh marked piece at the end of it and compare. Only then commit to a term, and only for the subject where the evidence supports it.

process.title: Say it quickly if it is not working
process.description: Two poor sessions is enough. The subject gets rematched to a different tutor without a new fee, because an unsuitable pairing left in place out of politeness costs a family a term they cannot recover, particularly in DP2 or the spring of Year 11.

whyPoints.title: Claims that can be checked, not ranked
whyPoints.description: Every substantive claim on this page is either sourced to a named authority or testable in a single message: the permit, the market band, the delivery format, the exit terms. There is no rating, no review count and no student total, because we cannot show you the method behind one.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes before the package
whyPoints.description: The first output is a written note naming the topic, question type or criterion where marks are going, with a realistic number of weeks attached. Sometimes it says the school already has it covered, which is a legitimate outcome of an honest first session.

whyPoints.title: Specialists rather than proximity
whyPoints.description: On this coast the required specialist frequently lives elsewhere. Online matching draws on everyone who teaches the subject at the level and can make a Gulf Standard Time slot, which is a larger pool than any twenty-minute radius around Fujairah City contains.

whyPoints.title: A stated coverage limit
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based tutor covers a narrow subject at a workable hour, you are told before paying and offered a specialist elsewhere teaching into this time zone, or an honest wait. The competitor research found no ranking page in this cluster that discloses a limit at all.

whyPoints.title: Coursework boundaries in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria, questions a research design and responds to the student's own drafts. No text, no sections, no editing to completion, and no redistribution of board papers or mark schemes. That protects the candidate, which is the only protection that matters.

whyPoints.title: Rematch rather than persuasion
whyPoints.description: If two sessions show the pairing is wrong, the subject moves to a different tutor without a new fee. No provider matches perfectly every time, and the useful question is what happens next rather than whether the first attempt was flawless.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as a best IB tutor, or only a best match?
faqs.answer: Only a match, because no UAE authority rates or ranks tutoring providers and nothing would make a ranking checkable. What exists instead is fit: a tutor who has taught your child's subject at the exact level, who can mark a script against the published criteria, who holds the MoHRE private tuition permit, and whose slot suits your household. Those four things are verifiable in a couple of messages. A provider who answers them precisely has told you more than any superlative, and the pattern of what they avoid answering is informative too.

faqs.question: How should I read a tutoring site's star rating and review count?
faqs.answer: With scepticism, and preferably by ignoring it. The competitor research behind this site found one page displaying two different ratings with two different review counts, and another claiming a perfect score from twenty reviews alongside a four-figure claim for students taught. Self-asserted review markup breaches Google's structured-data policy and is unverifiable by design. A more useful request is to ask the tutor directly whether two current families would speak to you, and to judge the trial session you can observe yourself.

faqs.question: What qualifications actually predict good IB teaching?
faqs.answer: Subject depth at the level being taught, plus experience of the assessment. A degree in the subject matters more than a general teaching award, and having taught the specific course for several cohorts matters more than either. Ask how many years they have taught the Higher Level course, which papers students struggle with, and what a particular answer lost two marks on. Vague answers about passion for learning are not qualifications. The strongest single test is watching them mark your child's work and explain each lost mark.

faqs.question: How much weight should I give a tutor's claim to have marked IB papers?
faqs.answer: Treat it as neutral unless it is evidenced, and never as a route to inside knowledge. Examiner status is widely claimed and rarely demonstrable, and it should not be presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, which it is not. We do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status. What correlates with results is whether the tutor marks your child's script against published criteria and teaches the gap. Ask them to do that in the trial, and judge the demonstration rather than the label.

faqs.question: How long should it take to be matched for a Fujairah student's subject?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects at the usual levels, a day or two. For narrow requests - Higher Level Computer Science, Additional Mathematics, a minority language - it can take longer or prove impossible at a workable hour, and that is the answer a family should get rather than a substitute. Ask the question directly: who exactly is available, at what times, with what history in this syllabus. A provider who promises a match before checking availability is making a commitment on someone else's behalf.

faqs.question: What should be visibly different four weeks into a good match?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily a better grade, because four weeks is short and anyone promising one is promising what they cannot control. What should be visible is movement in the specific thing being targeted: working set out so a mark scheme can follow it, a conclusion that evaluates rather than describes, a data question attempted instead of abandoned. The student should also be able to explain what they are working on and why. If neither is true and the tutor cannot say why, change the approach or the tutor.

faqs.question: How do I compare two tutors who both sound convincing on a call?
faqs.answer: Stop talking and watch them teach. Give each a copy of the same marked script in advance, and compare what they do with it in the trial: whether they name specific lost marks, whether they ask the student to attempt something, whether they set work at the end. Two trials is an hour each and it settles the question better than any amount of discussion. Also compare the written note afterwards, because the tutor who writes a clear one is usually the one who has an actual plan.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean better teaching?
faqs.answer: Up to a point, then no. Published market bands run from roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors online, AED 200 to 450 and beyond for IB and IGCSE specialists, and up to AED 650 at a premium named tier. Moving from the budget band to the specialist band buys genuine subject depth for a narrow problem. Moving to the premium tier buys reputation, and the research found those claims the least evidenced in this market. The in-home band largely buys travel.

faqs.question: Why will nobody quote me a price in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Because a vague price lets the quote adjust to the enquiry, which is why the figures on this page are published as market bands with their source stated instead. One competitor's own frequently-asked-questions section asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. The questions to insist on are the hourly figure, the smallest unit you can buy, whether written notes are included, and whether the rate changes closer to the examination session. A provider unwilling to put those four in writing has given you an answer.

faqs.question: Is a Dubai agency better than an online match for an east-coast family?
faqs.answer: For teaching, it depends entirely on the individual tutor; for logistics, the arithmetic is against it. A tutor crossing the Hajar mountains spends close to three hours on a one-hour lesson, which is why published in-home rates reach AED 500 and why the far slot is the first one cancelled in a difficult week. Over thirty teaching weeks, four lost sessions is more than a month of teaching gone. Ask any agency quoting for travel what happens when the road is slow, and get the answer before the exam term.

faqs.question: What does a UAE address with an overseas contact number tell me?
faqs.answer: That the published claims are not reliable, which matters more than the detail itself. The competitor research found UAE pages routing parents to numbers in other countries and one showing a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. A provider should be able to say plainly where lessons are delivered from and where the tutor is based. We state it: lessons are delivered online, we hold no UAE office or centre, and home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to try is a warning rather than a convenience. Higher Level Chemistry, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and English A are three different specialisms with three different assessment structures, and the tutor who claims all of them usually teaches none at depth. One subject properly supported, chosen because it is costing the most marks, outperforms three covered thinly. If a family needs two subjects, that is two matches, and a provider should say so rather than stretching one person across both.

faqs.question: How much of a first session should be teaching rather than selling?
faqs.answer: Most of it. A free trial is useful only if it functions as a lesson: the tutor reads a marked piece of work, teaches, asks the student to attempt something, and ends by naming the weakness and roughly how long it will take to address. Forty minutes of rapport-building followed by a package recommendation is a sales call with a lesson attached. Send the marked work in advance so there is no excuse for the hour to be spent on introductions, and judge what actually happened in it.

faqs.question: What should I do if the school says outside tutoring is unnecessary?
faqs.answer: Take it seriously and ask for the specifics behind it. A teacher who says a child is secure and simply needs to complete the set work is often right, and that answer saves a family money. Ask which assessment evidence supports it and what the next piece of marked work should show. If the evidence arrives and matches, do nothing. If the same weakness appears again in the next marked piece, you now have a documented pattern, which is a far better brief for a tutor than a general worry.

faqs.question: Who should hold the plan: the parent, the student or the tutor?
faqs.answer: The student, with the parent holding the evidence and the tutor holding the teaching. A plan that lives only in the tutor's head produces a student who performs well in sessions and poorly in an examination hall where nobody prompts them. By the end of a term the student should be able to say what they are working on, why, and how they will know it has worked. That is the quiet test of whether the money was well spent, and it costs nothing to run at any point.

fujairah/best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Replace the ranking question with a checklist
fujairah/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: There is no league table of tutors in the UAE, so the useful work is verification rather than comparison. Ask the school what is weakest and for how long. Ask the provider for the permit, the exact level history, the hourly figure and the exit terms. Then use the free trial as an audition: send a marked script in advance and judge whether the hour produced a named weakness or a sales pitch. Four weeks of evidence after that is enough to commit or to change course. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, from Fujairah City to Dibba Al-Fujairah.

intro.heading: What "best" has to mean on the east coast
paragraphs: A parent in Fujairah typing "best IGCSE tutor" is not asking for a slogan. They are asking a narrower question: who can actually teach Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended, or Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 Higher tier, to a Year 11 student in this emirate, starting this month. The honest answer is that the local pool of people who can do that is thin. Fujairah has a small private-school sector compared with Dubai or Sharjah, and the number of adults living within half an hour of Fujairah city who have taught a specific IGCSE syllabus to examination standard is smaller still.

That scarcity is the single fact that should shape the decision. In Dubai a family can treat geography as a filter and still have a choice of subject specialists. In Fujairah, filtering by geography first usually means accepting a generalist: a tutor who is comfortable with school maths but has never seen the mark scheme for a 4MA1 Paper 2 question, or who teaches biology from a textbook rather than from the 0610 syllabus statements the examiner is working from.

The Hajar mountains make this concrete. The road from Dubai or Sharjah to Fujairah runs through Masafi or down the Kalba road, and a tutor crossing it for a one-hour lesson is committing two to three hours of travel on either side. Nobody absorbs that for long. Either the rate rises to pay for the car, or the lesson is scheduled at the tutor's convenience instead of the student's, or it quietly stops. All three outcomes are common on the east coast and none of them is good for a student eight months from a June series.

IB Gram does not solve this by sending somebody over the mountains. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; home visits are a service offered only in India. What that buys a Fujairah family is a different kind of choice. The subject specialist does not need to live in Fujairah, in Sharjah, or in the UAE at all, so the shortlist is built from people who know the exact syllabus and tier your child sits, and the 4.30pm slot stays at 4.30pm because nobody is driving to it.

So the rest of this page replaces the word "best" with things a parent can check: which board and syllabus code the tutor teaches, whether they mark against the published scheme, whether they hold the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit required of anyone giving paid private lessons in the UAE, what the market charges in AED, and how the Cambridge calendar for your child's zone actually runs. A tutor who answers those five questions clearly is a better bet than one described as the best by their own website.

fujairah/best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Fujairah families reach IGCSE by several routes: a British-curriculum school running Years 7-11, an Indian-curriculum school switching a child to Cambridge for Year 10, or a move into the emirate mid-key-stage. The programme notes below describe what each stage assesses and what it means for a student studying from this emirate.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary (pre-IGCSE)
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE decide how much ground has to be made up later. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October and give a first external read on English, mathematics and science. Work here is about securing algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and extended writing, because IGCSE assumes all three from the first week of Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: In Fujairah the practical issue at this stage is subject staffing. A small school may have one specialist covering all three sciences across Years 7-11, which is workable but leaves little room for a child who needs a second explanation. Online one-to-one support at Year 8 or 9 is usually cheaper and shorter than the rescue work the same gap needs in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined in a June series and a November series, with syllabus codes that matter: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511, First Language English 0500 or 0990. Most subjects tier into Core and Extended, and the tier caps the grade available, so the entry decision is an academic decision rather than an administrative one.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah centres are allocated to a Cambridge administrative zone like every other centre, and Cambridge is explicit that a candidate who follows the wrong zone's timetable may miss an exam. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it sits in and work from that version of the timetable, not from a PDF found by searching.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSEs use their own codes - Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1 - and some are available in a modular route where units are banked across sessions. Papers are sat in May/June and November. The assessment style differs from Cambridge enough that past-paper practice has to match the board your child is actually entered for.
programmes.countryNote: East-coast schools do not all use the same board, and a child who moves from a Cambridge school in Sharjah to a Pearson school in Fujairah can arrive mid-course with the wrong practice papers. The first job of a tutor in that situation is a board audit: codes, tiers, papers and the calculator policy for each.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside IGCSE
programmes.description: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must follow the Ministry's general regulations. These subjects run alongside IGCSE rather than instead of it, and they carry their own reporting, their own language of instruction rules and their own timetable pressure in Years 10 and 11.
programmes.countryNote: Because Fujairah's private schools answer to the federal Ministry of Education, families should take the Ministry's general regulations as the baseline and ask the school directly how Arabic and Islamic Education are timetabled against IGCSE options. Arabic and Islamic Education are also excluded from the five-subject count used in the British-track equivalency rule.

fujairah/best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Fujairah families ask for most often, with what each one actually assesses and the point at which marks start leaking. Entries list both Cambridge and Pearson codes where a school in the emirate might use either.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers in most routes, with the tier fixing the grade ceiling. Marks go missing in the same four places every series: unsimplified surds and indices, algebraic fractions, the difference between a bearing and an angle, and method marks lost because working was not shown. A tutor's first task is to find which of those four is costing the most.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves, thermal physics, magnetism and atomic physics. Electricity is where most Extended candidates lose grades: series and parallel reasoning collapses under time pressure, and units get dropped in the final line. Practical and data-handling questions reward a student who can read a graph gradient properly, which is coachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, rates, equilibrium, electrolysis, organic families and qualitative analysis. The mole calculation chain is the most common single failure point, closely followed by ionic equations written without charges balanced. Organic nomenclature is pure recall and the cheapest marks on the paper to recover, so it is usually where a late-starting student should begin.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where the examiner rewards precise terminology rather than general understanding. Students who revise by reading lose marks on transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance diagrams. Working from the syllabus statements one at a time, with recall tested aloud, moves grades faster than re-reading a textbook chapter.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, in 0511, a speaking endorsement. The writing papers are marked on task fulfilment, organisation and language accuracy, and many students write fluent answers that ignore the register the task asked for. Teaching the question wording itself is usually worth more than vocabulary drilling.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 / 0990 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. Marks concentrate in the reading paper, where students summarise instead of analysing the writer's choices. The reliable fix is sentence-level work on explicit comment: naming the technique, quoting short, and explaining effect in one clause rather than three sentences.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics / Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A-Level or IB Diploma mathematics. Calculus, trigonometric identities and proof arrive earlier than in the main syllabus, and the gap between a strong 0580 candidate and a comfortable Additional Mathematics candidate is algebraic stamina. Sessions here are best used on timed question sets rather than on new content.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study papers where command terms carry the marks: analyse, evaluate, justify. Students who know the content still cap at a middle grade because they describe rather than weigh. Marking two case studies against the published scheme usually shows a student exactly where their answers stop.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Theory papers on data representation, networks and algorithms, plus practical or pre-release material depending on the board and series. Pseudocode conventions differ between boards, and a student practising with the wrong convention writes correct logic in a form the mark scheme does not credit.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the school's international curriculum under the Ministry's general regulations, with their own language-of-instruction rules. Support here is about the school's own scheme of work, because the Ministry restricts the use of different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission.

fujairah/best-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in Fujairah students are studying
fujairah/best-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Fujairah is a long coastal emirate with an enclave at Dibba and inland pockets reached through the mountains. Travel time between these places is the reason a session that works for one family is impossible for another, so each note below is about the practical shape of a school night.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: The emirate's administrative and school centre, and where most private-school families live. Afternoon traffic is light by UAE standards, so a student is typically home soon after the school run and a 4.30pm or 5pm online session is realistic on a weeknight.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: A residential district north of the city centre, close enough that school transport arrives early. Families here often run two children through back-to-back online sessions on the same evening, which is only workable because no tutor travel is involved.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Inland of the corniche and quieter, with a mix of villa and apartment housing. Internet provision is ordinary household broadband, which is enough for one-to-one video with screen sharing; the limiting factor is usually a shared living room rather than bandwidth.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal and close to the port and corniche. Parents working shift patterns at the port or airport often want a later slot, and the 8pm to 9pm window after dinner is the one most frequently requested from this area.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: South along the coast road towards Kalba, with a longer run to the city's schools. Students arriving home after 4pm from a Fujairah city or Sharjah-side school need an evening slot rather than an afternoon one.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The northern enclave, an hour or more from Fujairah city by road and effectively a separate catchment. In-home tutoring from the city is impractical from here; online one-to-one is the only format that reliably holds a weekly slot.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Small coastal communities between the city and Dibba. Families here usually accept a longer school commute, which pushes tutoring to 7pm or later and makes a fixed weekly online slot more valuable than a flexible one.

regions.name: Masafi and the mountain road
regions.note: The crossing point between Fujairah and the Dubai-Sharjah side. Its relevance to tutoring is the travel cost it imposes on any in-person arrangement, which is why east-coast rates for home visits sit above the national range.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and Sakamkam
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private-school provision is concentrated here, with British and Indian curriculum options and a smaller cohort per year group than a comparable Dubai school. Students sitting less common IGCSE subjects frequently have no local specialist teaching them, which is the gap online tuition fills.

sections.heading: Replacing "best" with five things a parent can verify
paragraphs: There is no ranking authority for IGCSE tutors in the UAE, so "best" is a word a parent has to define for themselves. The useful definition is narrow: the tutor who can teach the exact syllabus your child is entered for, at the tier they are entered at, in a slot that survives a school week, and who shows their marking. Everything else is decoration.

Five checks cover it. First, the board and syllabus code - not "IGCSE maths" but 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher, because the papers, the formula provision and the calculator rules differ. Second, mark-scheme literacy: ask how the tutor marks a six-mark question and listen for whether they talk about method marks and error carried forward. Third, the permit position, since paid private tutoring in the UAE runs through a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.

Fourth, what happens between sessions. A tutor who sets nothing and marks nothing is running a conversation, not a course. Fifth, what happens if the match is wrong - a clear change process matters more on the east coast than in Dubai, because the local alternative pool is small and a family cannot afford to lose a month discovering a mismatch.

Nobody can promise a grade, and a tutor who does should be treated as a warning rather than a find. What a good arrangement can promise is specificity: a named weakness, a method for attacking it, marked evidence each fortnight, and an honest view of what is achievable in the time remaining before the series.

sections.heading: Who regulates Fujairah's schools, and why it changes the answer
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages written for UAE parents assume Dubai. They name KHDA, quote Dubai inspection bands and describe a market of hundreds of private schools. None of that is the system a Fujairah family is inside. According to the UAE government's own private-schools page, the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge.

The practical consequences are real. The published inspection reports a Dubai parent can read before choosing a school are a Dubai product. Fee approval in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah sits with the emirate authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. In Fujairah the reference point is the federal Ministry and the school itself, which means more of the information a parent needs has to be asked for rather than looked up.

It also means a tutor who talks fluently about KHDA ratings is telling you about somebody else's emirate. What matters for a Fujairah student is the school's own scheme of work, the board it enters candidates with, and the Ministry's general regulations, including the requirement for Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum.

One more distinction is worth holding. Regulators license schools and, in some emirates, tuition centres with premises. No regulator approves individual online tutors, and IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation of any kind. Any page claiming a tutor is approved by a UAE education authority is describing something that does not exist in that form.

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar counted backwards, and the zone trap
paragraphs: The most useful thing a tutor does in the first week is build the calendar backwards from the series your child is entered for. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and a student who discovers the date late loses the planning that makes the difference.

The March series key dates published by Cambridge show the shape clearly: the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results are released on Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates follow in late June. The exact numbers differ by series, but the pattern - entries first, exams, then a long wait for results - is constant, and it is the reason a Year 11 plan that starts in January is already behind.

There is a trap specific to centres outside the United Kingdom. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. A Fujairah family should get the zone from the school's exams officer and work only from that timetable.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs run in May/June and November each year. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning against.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs on the east coast, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six tutoring pages ranking for UAE queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Here are the market bands in the currency families actually transact in. These are market rates compiled from competitors' own published figures and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, not IB Gram's price list.

A budget online tutor, often a university student, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. A named IGCSE, IB or A-Level specialist is AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium examiner-marketed tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Fujairah distorts two of those bands. The in-home figure is a Dubai figure, and the mountain crossing has to be paid for by somebody, so east-coast quotes for a visiting tutor sit at or above the top of the range and often come with a minimum booking of two hours. Meanwhile the specialist band is where the emirate's thin local pool matters most: a family wanting a 0620 Chemistry Extended specialist may find nobody locally at any price, which makes the online rate the only real rate.

Monthly packages advertised in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson and a consultation first, so a family sees the match before any money moves.

sections.heading: Online, or a tutor who drives over the Hajar
paragraphs: This is the decision most Fujairah parents are actually weighing, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. A tutor sitting in your living room has advantages: a teenager is harder to distract, materials are physically shared, and some children simply focus better with an adult beside them. Those are real and worth something.

What they cost in this emirate is the subject nobody writes about. A tutor who lives in Fujairah city can reach most of the city in fifteen minutes, so for a Fujairah City or Sakamkam family an in-home arrangement with a local generalist is genuinely practical. For Dibba, Al Gurfa, Qidfa or anywhere past Masafi, the same arrangement means an hour or more of driving each way, which is paid for either in the rate or in the reliability of the slot. The first cancelled session in exam term is usually a travel cancellation.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. UAE tutoring is one-to-one over live video, and the reason to prefer it here is not price but supply. A Fujairah student entered for Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended gets a physics specialist rather than whoever is willing to drive. The same applies to Additional Mathematics, Business Studies, Computer Science and the second-language English papers, where a small emirate may have no local teacher of that syllabus at all.

The honest comparison is in the table below. Where an in-home option genuinely wins - a younger child needing supervision, a student who will not engage with a screen - a parent should take it, and there are local tutors in Fujairah city who do that work. Where the need is a specific syllabus at a specific tier with marked papers coming back each week, geography is the wrong filter to apply first.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally allowed to charge for lessons?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is the question Fujairah parents ask least and should ask first. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 regarding the introduction of private tuition work permits, administered through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Two details matter to a parent. The permit costs nothing, so a tutor who says the paperwork is too expensive is telling you they have not done it. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the Ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted; figures circulating online are not verifiable.

The official route is the Ministry's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time. A parent can simply ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit and under what category. The answer is quick for anyone who has one.

A separate rule applies to teachers. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than quoted policy, verify it against the current document, and do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by their own class teacher. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different matter again: that needs an educational services permit from the relevant authority, and IB Gram holds no such permit and runs no UAE centre.

No fine amount has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule, and the mistake a ranking site makes
paragraphs: An IGCSE student in Fujairah who may later apply to a UAE university needs to understand equivalency, because it is a documentation process with subject-count rules, and it is almost never mentioned on tutoring pages. For the British track, reported requirements are proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, together with a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A child taking five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education does not have five counting subjects. One site currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the five-subject rule says - a useful reminder that a confident page is not necessarily a correct one.

For the American track, reported English requirements are a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that reporting, so any page publishing an IB equivalency score without a Ministry source is guessing.

Equivalency is not something a tutor performs, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. What a tutor can do is make sure the subject choices in Year 10 leave a student with five counting subjects at a usable grade, which is a planning conversation that belongs at the start of Year 10 rather than after results. Verify current requirements with the Ministry of Education or the attestation authority before acting on any version of them, including this one.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market treats Arabic as a chip in a subject list. It is not; it is a timetabled requirement that sits beside the international curriculum and takes up hours a Year 11 student would otherwise spend on IGCSE revision. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

Dubai's requirements are published in detail and are a useful reference even outside Dubai, because they show how seriously these subjects are structured. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with implementation required by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. Separate classes must be organised for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

Language of instruction is specified too: Standard Arabic as the main language for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson is at least 25 minutes.

For a tutor, the binding constraint is content. For these mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which means support has to work from the school's own scheme rather than from imported material. Dubai also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from the authority to teach those subjects, which is a credential question worth asking of any Arabic tutor anywhere in the country.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less internally assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where coursework or a practical endorsement exists, the boundary matters, and it is the boundary one competitor in this market crosses commercially. A page that sells finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price is selling a malpractice finding, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller.

The line is simple to state. A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria, discusses an approach, reads what the student has produced and says where it falls short of the descriptor. The student does every piece of the work that is assessed. A tutor does not supply sentences for a coursework piece, does not restructure a draft for the student, and does not provide material to be submitted as the student's own.

Stated that plainly, it sounds like a limitation. In practice it is where most of the available improvement sits. A student who understands what an examiner means by evaluate, who can see from a mark scheme why their six-mark answer earned three, and who has corrected their own work twice, has gained something that transfers to every paper. A student handed a finished piece has gained nothing and risks everything.

The same applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor should reference them and point you to the official source rather than hand over copies, and no tutor has access to unreleased papers, live mark schemes or boundaries. Anyone implying otherwise is making a claim that cannot be true.
bullets: A tutor teaches, explains criteria, reviews and gives feedback
The student produces every word of any assessed piece
Nobody has access to unreleased papers, boundaries or live mark schemes
Official syllabus material is referenced and linked, not redistributed
A seller of completed coursework is selling the student a malpractice risk

process.title: Tell us the board, the code and the deadline
process.description: The first message should carry four things: the subject, the board, the syllabus code and tier if you know them, and the series your child is entered for. For a Fujairah family it helps to add the school, because the Cambridge administrative zone and the school's scheme of work both follow from it.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: The trial is with the tutor who would actually teach, not a sales call. It is a working session: a diagnostic question set, a short piece of marking, and a view on where the marks are currently going. You see the match before any commitment, and if it is wrong you say so.

process.title: A written plan counted back from the series
process.description: After the trial the tutor sets out the weeks available before the entry deadline and the exam window for your centre's zone, what will be covered in each block, and what is set between sessions. For a Year 11 starting late, this is also where an honest view of what is reachable appears.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work coming back
process.description: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, delivered one-to-one over live video. Each session ends with a short set task; the task comes back marked against the published scheme, with the specific marks lost identified rather than a grade written at the top.

process.title: Review at six weeks, and change if it is not working
process.description: At six weeks there is enough marked evidence to judge whether the arrangement is moving anything. If it is not, the right response is a different tutor or a different plan, decided then rather than after results. A request for a change is handled as a normal part of the service.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not whoever is within driving distance
whyPoints.description: The constraint on the east coast is supply. Delivering lessons online removes geography from the match, so a Fujairah student is taught by somebody who knows the syllabus and tier they are sitting rather than by the nearest available adult with a maths degree.

whyPoints.title: Marking you can actually read
whyPoints.description: Work set between sessions comes back marked against the published scheme, with the lost marks named. A parent without a teaching background can see from the script where the problem is, which is more useful than a percentage and a comment.

whyPoints.title: The calendar built backwards from your centre's zone
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines sit months before papers, and Cambridge timetables vary by administrative zone. Planning starts from your school's zone and series rather than from a generic exam date, because a candidate working from the wrong timetable can miss a paper outright.

whyPoints.title: Prices discussed in AED, with the market shown
whyPoints.description: Market bands are published on this page in dirhams with their sources, so a quote can be judged against something. IB Gram's own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a price list dropped on a parent cold.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on what a tutor will touch
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation, review and feedback - and the student does every assessed word themselves. That boundary is stated up front because the alternative, widely sold in this market, puts the student's qualification at risk.

whyPoints.title: A slot that survives a school term
whyPoints.description: Nothing travels, so nothing cancels for traffic, weather or a closed mountain road. The 5pm Tuesday slot stays 5pm Tuesday through October and through the final six weeks before the series, which is when consistency matters most.

faqs.question: How do I judge which IGCSE tutor in Fujairah is actually the best fit for my child?
faqs.answer: Replace the word best with five checks. Ask for the syllabus code your child is entered for, not just the subject. Ask how the tutor marks a six-mark structured question, and listen for method marks and error carried forward. Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Ask what is set and marked between sessions, and to see a recent marked script. Ask how a tutor change is handled. Any tutor who answers those five clearly is a better bet than one described as the best by their own advertising, and nobody can honestly promise a grade.

faqs.question: Why are there so few IGCSE subject specialists living in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Fujairah has a small private-school sector compared with Dubai or Sharjah, so the number of adults in the emirate who have taught a specific IGCSE syllabus to examination standard is small. A school may run one science specialist across Years 7 to 11. That is workable for teaching but leaves almost no local pool for a student who needs a second explanation in Chemistry 0620 Extended or Additional Mathematics. Delivering lessons online is how that gap is closed: the tutor is matched on the syllabus and tier rather than on whether they can reach Fujairah city on a weeknight.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our house in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. There is no IB Gram office or centre in the UAE. If an in-home tutor is what your family needs, there are independent tutors in Fujairah city who do that work, and this page sets out what the market charges for it so you can judge a quote. For a specific syllabus at a specific tier with marked papers each week, the online format gives access to a far wider pool of specialists.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's Fujairah school use, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: East-coast schools do not all use the same board, and some use both across different subjects. The exams officer can confirm it, and your child's entry paperwork carries the syllabus codes: Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580, 0625 and 0620, while Pearson uses codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. This matters more than it sounds. Paper structures, formula provision and calculator rules differ between boards, so a student practising with the wrong board's past papers is rehearsing for an examination they are not sitting.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge mean by administrative zones, and why should a Fujairah parent care?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, then work only from that timetable. A timetable found through a general search may belong to another zone, and a planning calendar built on the wrong dates is worse than no calendar at all.

faqs.question: How far before the exams do IGCSE entries have to be submitted?
faqs.answer: Months before. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 for an examination period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The dates differ by series but the shape does not. The practical consequence is that tier decisions for tiered subjects are locked in well before the exam, so a conversation about Core versus Extended belongs early in the year, not in the term the papers are sat.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay per hour for IGCSE tuition on the east coast?
faqs.answer: Market rates, compiled from providers' own published figures and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for a named IGCSE or A-Level specialist. Fujairah shifts the in-home figure upward, because a tutor travelling from the Dubai side absorbs a mountain crossing. Those are market numbers rather than IB Gram's, and our arrangement begins with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is my tutor legally permitted to charge for private lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: They need a private tutor work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so any figure you see quoted online is unverified. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold it.

faqs.question: Can my child be tutored privately by their own teacher at school?
faqs.answer: It is better not to arrange that. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported to prohibit serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Those reports should be verified against the current policy documents, but the direction is clear enough to avoid the arrangement. An independent tutor also gives a second professional view of where marks are going, which a child's own teacher cannot easily provide.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Fujairah students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the three separate sciences account for most requests, followed by First Language English and the second-language English papers. Within those, the recurring pressure points are the mole calculation chain in Chemistry, series and parallel reasoning in Physics electricity, precise terminology in Biology, and in Mathematics the loss of method marks because working was not shown. Business Studies and Economics appear less often but produce a particular problem: students who know the content cap at a middle grade because they describe rather than evaluate in case-study answers.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with the series a few months away. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: It is late but not useless, and what changes is the method rather than the subject. With a short runway the work shifts from covering content to recovering marks: timed papers under conditions, marked to the published scheme, with an error log kept so patterns surface across papers. Cheap recall marks come first, because topics like organic nomenclature or biological terminology return marks quickly. What no tutor can do is promise a particular grade from a short block of sessions, and an honest plan says what is realistically reachable in the weeks left.

faqs.question: Do we need five or six IGCSE subjects for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Reported requirements for the British track are a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One site ranking for UAE queries states six subjects are required, which does not match the five-subject rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutor performs, and current requirements should be confirmed with the Ministry of Education or the attestation authority before you act on them.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around an IGCSE timetable?
faqs.answer: They run alongside it. Private schools in the UAE must provide Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for, and must follow the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai these subjects also carry rules on separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and on the language of instruction. For tutoring the binding point is content: the use of different or additional material for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so any support has to work from the school's own scheme of work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework or a practical endorsement without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor explains the assessment criteria, teaches the underlying skill, discusses an approach, reads what the student has produced and says where it falls short of the descriptor. The student produces every assessed word themselves. What a tutor must never do is supply content to be submitted as the student's own work, and one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is a malpractice risk carried by the student, not by the seller, and it is the clearest reason to ask a tutor where their line sits.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session, and how quickly do we see anything change?
faqs.answer: The first session is diagnostic: a short question set across the syllabus areas, a piece of written work marked against the scheme, and a view on where marks are currently being lost. You get that in writing. Movement usually shows first in the quality of written answers rather than in a grade, because command-term errors and missing working are the fastest things to fix. Judge the arrangement at about six weeks, when there is enough marked evidence to see a trend, and change tutor or plan then if there is nothing moving.

faqs.question: Can lessons be scheduled around a long school commute or around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this emirate that flexibility matters more than usual. Students travelling in from Dibba, Al Gurfa or the Sharjah-side schools often cannot start before 7pm on a school night, and online sessions hold that slot without anybody driving to it. During Ramadan families commonly move sessions later, after Iftar, and shorten them from ninety to sixty minutes. Because the tutor may sit in another time zone, the slot is set in Gulf Standard Time and stays there, so the weekly rhythm survives a change in the daily one.

fujairah/best-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a trial lesson, not a promise
fujairah/best-igcse-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up IGCSE support in Fujairah, the quickest way to judge it is a working session. Tell us the subject, the board, the syllabus code and the series your child is entered for, and we will put forward a tutor who teaches that specification, for a free trial lesson delivered one-to-one over live video. You will see how they mark, what they notice in the first thirty minutes, and whether your child engages with them. Then decide. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does has told you something useful about themselves; what a good one can give you is a named weakness, a method, and marked evidence every fortnight.
