fujairah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses to east-coast students over live video. A request is matched by code and tier - 0580 Extended, 0620, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences - because the paper structure, not the subject label, determines what the teaching has to cover.

intro.heading: The calendar belongs to Cambridge, not to the tutor
paragraphs: Families on this coast usually start looking for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in the autumn of Year 11, a few weeks after a set of mock results. The instinct is to find someone good and start immediately. The more useful first step costs nothing: find out from the school which series your child is entered for, in which administrative zone, at which tier, and when the entries close. Those four facts decide what the next six months can and cannot change.

Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A parent reading a timetable found online is reading the wrong document unless they know the zone.

The lead times are longer than families expect, and Cambridge's own published key dates for the March 2027 series make the point: the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Whichever series your child sits, the pattern holds - the entry decision is made a full season before the paper, and once it is made, the tier is largely fixed.

That is why this page is built as a timeline rather than as a subject list. Where a student stands relative to the entry deadline determines whether the conversation is about tier choice, about subject count, about technique, or about a retake. A tutor who does not ask the date first is guessing, and in a small school where one teacher handles several year groups, the family is often the only person holding the full picture.

IB Gram teaches Fujairah students online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - so nothing here promises a tutor arriving in Fujairah City before dinner. What online delivery buys on this coast is a specialist in the exact syllabus at the right tier, holding a slot that does not depend on the weather over the Hajar mountains, through to the week of the first paper. The sections that follow take the route in order: the published calendar, the sequence of decisions from Year 9 options to results day, what the syllabus codes commit a candidate to, the Core and Extended question, and the nine weeks before the first paper.
bullets: June and November are the main series; the school decides which one and makes the entry
Centres sit in one of six Cambridge administrative zones, each with its own timetable
Cambridge's March 2027 series closed for final entries on 27 November 2026
Forecast grades are collected by Cambridge before results are issued
Core entries cap the attainable grade; Extended does not
Arabic and Islamic Education do not count towards the five subjects the MoE requires on the British track

fujairah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge sits inside a longer British-curriculum route, and the stage either side of IGCSE changes what a Year 10 or Year 11 decision costs. These are the four stages east-coast families are usually choosing between.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The years before any entry is made, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. Checkpoint is diagnostic rather than certificated, and its value to a parent is as early evidence of whether a child is heading for Core or Extended in Year 10. Schools use it differently, so ask whether your child sat it and what the report said.
programmes.countryNote: In Fujairah, where cohorts are small and setting is broad, Checkpoint data is often the only external reference point a family gets before the IGCSE tier decision. It is worth asking for the subject breakdown rather than the overall judgement.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject certification, each with its own syllabus code and paper structure. Many subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, with the Core route capping the grade available. Entries are made by the school as the registered centre, against a published deadline months ahead of the series, and the tier is part of that entry.
programmes.countryNote: Most private schools on this coast run a British or Indian curriculum, so Cambridge entries make up a large share of external examination traffic in the emirate. The school is the centre, which means the entry conversation is with the school rather than with Cambridge directly.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The usual post-16 continuation, examined in the same June and November series. For the Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency, the published requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, on top of the five IGCSE or GCSE subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 provision in Fujairah is limited, so families compare a local sixth form against schools in the northern emirates or a move west. The IGCSE grade profile is the evidence those conversations use, which gives Year 11 more weight than it feels like at the time.

programmes.name: The IB Diploma alternative after IGCSE
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level plus a core of Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, sat in the May session by UAE schools. Students arriving from Cambridge IGCSE bring strong timed-paper stamina and usually less practice at independent investigation, which is the first thing DP1 internal assessment asks for.
programmes.countryNote: East-coast students choosing between A Levels and the Diploma are often also choosing between two schools in two different emirates. Settle which subjects each option can actually staff at the top level before the IGCSE results arrive, not after.

fujairah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Cambridge subjects are defined by their codes, and the code sets the paper structure a tutor has to teach. These are the ones Fujairah families ask for most, with the assessment shape rather than a sales description.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers in each tier, no coursework, calculator use defined per paper. Extended adds functions, vectors, harder trigonometry and more demanding algebraic manipulation. The tier is part of the entry, so the decision belongs to the autumn of Year 11 at the latest and is best evidenced by mock performance on Extended-style questions rather than by general confidence.

subjects.name: International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A different syllabus from 0580, built around graphic display calculator use and with an investigation element in some routes. Schools choose between them, and a tutor matched to the wrong code will teach the wrong paper structure. Worth confirming which one appears on the option sheet before any teaching starts.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for A Level Mathematics or the Diploma at Higher Level. Calculus, series and more formal algebra appear here first. Cohorts are tiny on this coast, which makes it the clearest case for an online specialist rather than a local generalist.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Written papers plus a practical component: either a laboratory paper or the alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on the route the centre offers. Mole calculations, electrolysis and organic families carry the marks. Students lose them on presentation of multi-step working rather than on chemistry they do not know.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves, thermal physics and atomic physics, with a practical or alternative-to-practical paper. Command terms do real work here: a question asking for an explanation is marked against different criteria from one asking for a description, and students routinely answer the wrong one.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Large content load marked on precise terminology, with transport, homeostasis, inheritance and ecology accounting for most dropped marks. The practical or alternative-to-practical paper rewards planning and variable control rather than laboratory dexterity, which makes it teachable without a bench.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics in one double-award qualification, common where a timetable cannot carry three separate sciences. The content is broad and shallower than the separate syllabuses, and students moving to A Level sciences should check entry requirements against it early rather than in Year 12.

subjects.name: First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing plus composition, with marks for reading response that students assume are for style. Where a school offers English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511 instead, the demand and the mark criteria differ substantially, so the code on the entry matters for how sessions are spent.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study assessment where application marks require the stimulus material to be used. The longer evaluate questions have a published mark allocation that rewards a judgement, and teaching that structure is usually faster than teaching more content.

subjects.name: Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks prose cannot recover, and the Fujairah port and the UAE logistics economy supply usable local examples for application marks. Demand and supply analysis and government intervention are where answers drift into description.

subjects.name: History 0470 and Geography 0460
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study subjects where mark schemes reward structure over volume. Both are commonly taught by one teacher across several year groups in a small school, which is why question technique is often the gap rather than the content itself.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data representation, logic gates and systems account for more of the mark total than programming does. Confident coders lose marks on trace tables and number-base conversion, which are both drillable in a handful of sessions.

fujairah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The useful local variable for a Cambridge candidate is not distance to a tutor but which centre enters them, when their mocks fall, and what time they can work. These notes cover that.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Where most of the emirate's Cambridge entries originate, since the private schools acting as centres are concentrated here. Families should ask their school's examinations officer for the zone and the series in writing; it is a two-minute question that governs the whole revision calendar.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Short journeys, so a Year 11 student can hold an earlier slot and still have the evening for timed practice. Useful in the final term, when the right pattern is one taught session plus two unsupervised papers a week.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland, with transport arriving later. A 6pm start holds through the mock season and the exam term, which matters because a slot that slips in February is the one that disappears in April.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Students here attend several different schools, so two neighbours sitting Chemistry can be entered for different codes, different tiers and even different boards. Any plan has to start from the option sheet rather than from the subject name.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: South along the coast with a long school journey, so concentration in the early evening is genuinely limited. Content review moves better to the weekend here, with weekday sessions kept for marked work and questions.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: At the northern end of the coast, where neighbouring Dibba Al-Hisn falls under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. A family crossing that line changes regulator and school calendar, and sometimes the exam centre as well.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Smaller coastal communities whose candidates travel furthest to school. For them the online slot is often what makes a second weekly session possible at all once the mock season starts.

modes.description: Work in the autumn and spring of Year 10 aimed at the Core or Extended question, using Extended-style questions as the evidence. The output a family needs is not reassurance but a view on whether the Extended tier is realistic, early enough that the school can still enter either way.

modes.description: Twice-weekly work in the target subject from the start of the final year, sequenced so that the mock examinations act as a checkpoint. Topic selection follows marks lost per paper rather than the student's sense of difficulty, which is usually a different list.

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar, and why it starts a season early
paragraphs: Cambridge publishes key dates for each series, and reading one set makes the shape obvious. For the March 2027 series the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released to centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates issued in late June. The entry closed more than two months before the first paper, and the certificate arrives nearly four months after it.

Whichever series your child sits, that pattern is the one to plan against: a decision window, a long quiet stretch, the papers, and then a wait. The March series is administered for particular zones rather than being open everywhere, so the first question for a Fujairah family is which series the school enters candidates for, and in which zone. Pearson Edexcel, used by some schools on this coast, runs its own pattern - the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August.

The practical use of all this is to stop a family buying help at the wrong moment. Before the entry closes, tuition can still change the tier and the subject count, which are the two decisions with the largest effect on the eventual certificate. After it closes, the work is technique and triage inside a fixed entry. Ask the examinations officer for the series, the zone and the entry deadline in a single email, and keep the reply.

sections.heading: Year 9 to results day, in the order the decisions arrive
paragraphs: The decisions that shape an IGCSE certificate are not evenly spread, and three of the four biggest are taken before any revision begins. The first is the subject list, usually in Year 9, which fixes what can be certificated at all. The second is the tier, which caps the grade in tiered subjects. The third is the series, which sets every date that follows. Only the fourth - examination performance - is what most families think of as the thing tuition buys.

That ordering has a direct consequence for a parent on this coast. A conversation with the school in Year 9 or early Year 10 is worth more than three months of tutoring in the spring of Year 11, because it is the only point at which the ceiling can still be raised. Small schools often set the option blocks around staffing, which means a subject may be unavailable rather than inadvisable, and knowing which it is changes what a family should do next.

The table below sets the stages out with the decision each one carries and who actually makes it. Two of the rows belong to the school, one to Cambridge and one to the student. Families who read it in Year 9 generally spend less on tutoring overall than families who meet it in Year 11, which is the opposite of how this market is usually sold. The reason is simple enough: a ceiling raised in Year 9 costs one conversation, and a ceiling discovered in Year 11 costs a resit.

sections.heading: Syllabus codes: the four digits that decide the teaching
paragraphs: A request for a chemistry tutor is not specific enough to match well. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different syllabuses with different paper structures, and within Cambridge, 0580 Mathematics and 0607 International Mathematics are different again, with 0607 built around graphic display calculator work. A tutor who prepares a student for the wrong structure teaches real chemistry or real mathematics and still leaves marks on the table.

The codes also carry the practical component. In the sciences the centre chooses between a laboratory practical paper and the written alternative-to-practical paper, and which one a candidate sits changes what revision should look like. The alternative paper rewards planning, variable control, reading apparatus diagrams and interpreting results, all of which are teachable over video. A candidate sitting the laboratory paper needs bench practice the school provides, and a tutor should be reinforcing technique rather than pretending to replace it.

So the first message to a provider should contain the code, the tier and the series. Those three items are on the option sheet or available from the examinations officer, and they turn a vague request into a specific match. They also let a tutor say honestly whether they have taught that syllabus. On this coast, where small cohorts mean one teacher may cover several codes, the family holding that detail is doing real work. The option sheet is worth photographing and keeping, because the same four digits will be asked for again at sixth-form application and at attestation.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier that caps a grade
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects the Core route covers less content and limits the top grade available, while the Extended route carries the full range. Schools place students on evidence, and the placement is usually provisional through Year 10 before becoming final at entry. The decision is defensible either way: an Extended entry a student cannot access produces a worse outcome than a secure Core entry, and a Core entry for a student who could have managed Extended closes doors at sixth form.

The honest test is performance on Extended-style questions under time, not general classroom confidence or parental ambition. A student who scores steadily in the middle band on Extended papers across a term is an Extended candidate. One who collapses on the second half of every paper is being asked to carry content they have not secured, and the useful intervention is to build that content in Year 10 rather than to argue about the tier in Year 11.

This is the single most valuable conversation a Fujairah family can have before the entry closes, and it has to happen with the school. Bring marked Extended-style work rather than opinions. Where the school holds firm and the evidence genuinely supports it, the right response is to accept the tier and plan the sixth-form route around it, including whether a resit in a later series is worth considering for a subject that matters for a specific course. The decision is reversible in a way the Year 11 timetable is not.
bullets: Core limits the top grade available; Extended does not

sections.heading: Timetable zones, and the document you should not download
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a timetable per zone. Its own guidance to examinations officers is blunt: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong zone timetable was used. That is a warning aimed at centres, and it is a warning parents should inherit.

The practical risk is mundane. A parent searching for a Cambridge timetable finds a PDF, builds a revision plan around it, and the dates are an hour or a day out because the zone differs. In a household with two candidates at two schools, the zones may not even match. The fix is to ask the examinations officer for the final timetable for your centre and your series, and to build the revision calendar from that document only.

There is a second scheduling reality on this coast. The examination period overlaps with Ramadan in some years, which changes school hours, sleep and the time of day a student can concentrate. Online sessions move easily to a post-Iftar slot, and the useful thing is to decide that in advance rather than improvising in the first week. A revision plan written against the real timetable and the real household routine survives; one written against a generic calendar does not. The same applies to the gap days inside a series: candidates often have a free week in the middle of the examination period, and knowing where it falls is worth more than any amount of generic advice about pacing.
bullets: Six administrative zones, six timetables; only one is yours
Ask the examinations officer for the final timetable for your centre
Two children at two schools can sit in two different zones
Decide the Ramadan session pattern before the month starts, not during it

sections.heading: Practicals, the alternative paper and what video can teach
paragraphs: Science candidates sit either a laboratory practical paper or the written alternative to practical, and which one the centre offers is part of the entry. For the written alternative, the assessment is of experimental thinking rather than manual skill: reading a burette diagram, identifying the dependent variable, spotting the control that is missing, explaining an anomalous result. All of that is teachable over a shared screen, and in some respects better, because a tutor can display a diagram and annotate it with the student rather than hovering at a bench.

Where a candidate sits the laboratory paper, the school's practical programme is doing the essential work and outside support should reinforce rather than imitate it. The useful contribution is method discipline: recording results as they are taken, repeating sensibly, and writing an evaluation that criticises something specific. A tutor who claims to replace laboratory time is overselling, and a family paying for that is paying twice for one thing.

The boundary on materials matters here too. Cambridge past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to the board, and we do not reproduce or supply them as downloads. Where a student has legitimate access through the school, a tutor can teach from them and point to the official source. Marking a student's script against the published criteria is legitimate and useful; distributing the board's material is not, and providers who offer paper banks as a selling point are describing a copyright problem.

sections.heading: The last nine weeks before the first paper
paragraphs: Once the entry is fixed and the mocks are marked, the remaining work is narrow and the main risk is spreading it. The sequence that works is to read each mock script question by question, rank topics by marks lost against likely study time, and build the calendar backwards from the first paper in the series, with the final fortnight reserved for timed papers rather than new content. Most students discover their ranking is not the list of topics they dislike.

Two habits carry the weeks. Writing full answers to time, which is a physical skill that fades without practice, and marking those answers against the published criteria, which shows the difference between an answer that is correct and one that collects marks. A tutor who marks a paper and then teaches the three recurring losses is doing the highest-value work available at that stage, and it is measurable the following week.

The other thing to settle is subject triage. A candidate entered for eight or nine subjects cannot work on all of them in nine weeks, and the honest choice is to protect the subjects that matter for the next stage while keeping the rest ticking. For the Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency the published requirement is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five, so the arithmetic of which subjects must land is worth doing on paper rather than in the head.
bullets: Rank topics by marks lost, not by how uncomfortable they feel
Write to time, then mark against the criteria
Keep the final fortnight for papers, not new content
Decide which subjects are protected and which are maintained

sections.heading: After results: equivalency, remarks and the next series
paragraphs: Results reach centres before candidates, and certificates follow weeks later - for the March 2027 series, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Keep the certificates. Attestation and equivalency processes ask for originals, and a family that has moved twice since Year 11 will be glad of a folder. The Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring provider performs or can promise, and the detail should be confirmed on the Ministry's own channel before any decision rests on it. One competitor page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must sit six IGCSE subjects; the published figure is five excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, which is the kind of error worth checking at source rather than inheriting from a tutoring site, this one included.

If a grade is close to a boundary or clearly out of line with the forecast, the centre can request a review within Cambridge's published window, and the school will advise whether the evidence supports it. A retake in the next series is the other route, entered through a centre, and it needs a plan built from the component results rather than a general resit of the syllabus. Both decisions are time-limited, so the week results arrive is the week to ask, not the month after.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the series
process.description: One message with the syllabus codes from the option sheet, the tier in each tiered subject, the series the school enters candidates for and the examination zone if you have it. Those details turn a general request into a specific match and let a tutor say honestly whether they have taught that paper structure.

process.title: Free trial built on a marked paper
process.description: One hour online at a time that fits the school transport. The tutor works from a marked mock or a piece of timed work, teaches for most of the session, then names the recurring losses by question type. Booked without card details, one lesson per student.

process.title: A revision calendar counted back from the series
process.description: You receive a short written plan starting at the first paper and working backwards: what must be secure before the mocks, which topics are ranked by marks lost, and where the final fortnight of timed practice sits. If the school's own programme already covers it, the plan says so.

process.title: Fixed sessions through the mock and exam terms
process.description: The same tutor, a set slot on Gulf Standard Time, following the school's internal assessment calendar and the real zone timetable rather than a generic one. The slot moves permanently for Ramadan hours or a change in transport, because a plan that works only in October is not a plan.

process.title: Checkpoints on marked timed work
process.description: Progress is read from papers written to time and marked against published criteria, at intervals agreed in advance. Two checkpoints without movement means the approach or the tutor changes. In a Year 11 spring there is no spare term to spend being polite about a poor match.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: A 0607 candidate and a 0580 candidate need different teaching, and so do a 0620 practical-paper entry and an alternative-to-practical entry. Matching on the code is the difference between a tutor who teaches chemistry and a tutor who prepares your child for the paper they are actually sitting.

whyPoints.title: The dates are published with their source
whyPoints.description: The entry, forecast-grade and results dates on this page come from Cambridge International's own key dates document for the March 2027 series, and the series pattern from its exams officers guide. Competitor pages in this cluster name no session, no deadline and no results date at all.

whyPoints.title: Tier advice before the entry closes
whyPoints.description: The Core or Extended decision caps or releases the grade, and it is made months before the papers. Sessions in Year 10 aimed at that decision, with marked Extended-style questions as the evidence, are worth more than a term of revision in the spring of Year 11.

whyPoints.title: No board material redistributed
whyPoints.description: Cambridge papers, mark schemes and syllabuses belong to the board, so we teach from the access the student has through school and point to the official source. Marking a student's own script against the published criteria is the legitimate and more useful half of that work.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that holds through the exam term
whyPoints.description: Transport from inland districts arrives late, the examination period can overlap with Ramadan, and a slot that slips in February disappears in April. Sessions are placed to survive the whole run and can be moved permanently rather than once as a favour.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer on small-cohort subjects
whyPoints.description: Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and the less common languages often have no local specialist on this coast at a workable hour. You are told that before paying, and offered either a tutor elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time or an honest wait.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge timetable zone is our school in, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer, because only the centre knows. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, and its guidance states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A timetable found through a search engine may be a different zone's. Build the revision calendar from the final timetable your centre supplies, and check it again if your children attend two different schools.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge March series and can a Fujairah candidate enter it?
faqs.answer: It is an additional series administered for particular zones rather than being open to every centre, so the answer comes from your school. Its published dates are a useful illustration of lead times: for March 2027 the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. Most UAE candidates sit the June or November series instead. Ask the examinations officer which series the centre enters candidates for before planning around any of these dates.

faqs.question: Our school asked for forecast grades. What are they used for?
faqs.answer: Forecast grades are submitted by the centre to Cambridge ahead of results, built from the evidence the school holds: mock examinations, classwork and internal assessments. For the March 2027 series Cambridge set the forecast deadline at 27 February 2027, after the examination period had begun. They support the board's own processes and give the school a documented position, and they are also what a sixth form may ask to see. A tutor cannot influence a forecast directly; what tuition can do is improve the mock evidence before the forecast is compiled.

faqs.question: Can a Core entry be changed to Extended, and up to when?
faqs.answer: In practice until the centre makes its final entry for the series, which for March 2027 was 27 November 2026. Up to that point the tier is a school judgement that a family can ask to have reviewed, and the review should be based on marked Extended-style questions written to time rather than on classroom confidence. After the entry closes, the tier is fixed for that series. If the Extended grade matters for a specific sixth-form course, raise it in Year 10 while the evidence can still be built.

faqs.question: How many Cambridge subjects should a Year 11 student in Fujairah be entered for?
faqs.answer: Enough to cover the next stage with a margin, which is usually seven to nine, and the number matters less than which ones land. The Ministry of Education's published British-track equivalency requirement is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five. Sixth-form courses add their own requirements. Work out on paper which five must land and which are useful extras, because in the final nine weeks a candidate cannot work on nine subjects equally.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a 0580 and a 0607 mathematics entry?
faqs.answer: They are separate syllabuses. 0580 Mathematics is the long-standing route with two written papers per tier and defined calculator use; 0607 International Mathematics is built around graphic display calculator work and includes an investigation element in some routes. The school chooses, and a tutor prepared for the wrong one will teach sound mathematics and the wrong paper structure. Check the code on the option sheet before any teaching starts, and tell the provider which one it is in the first message.

faqs.question: My son got a D in his mock Chemistry 0620. What does the next step look like?
faqs.answer: Start with the script rather than the grade. A D produced by running out of time on paper two is a different problem from one produced by losing every calculation mark, and only the question-by-question breakdown distinguishes them. Rank the topics by marks lost, confirm which practical route he is entered for, and plan two sessions a week in that subject with a timed paper between them. If the tier is Extended and the pattern shows a collapse in the back half of every paper, that evidence belongs in a conversation with the school now, not in April.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge offer a resit in the same academic year?
faqs.answer: There are two main series each year, June and November, plus a March series administered for particular zones, so a candidate can often re-enter in the next available series rather than waiting a full year. The entry is made by a centre, which is the practical question for a student who has left school: which centre will register them. Revision for a resit should be built from the component results rather than from the syllabus, because the diagnosis already exists. Ask the school which window applies and whether it will enter a former candidate.

faqs.question: How does the alternative-to-practical paper differ from a laboratory exam?
faqs.answer: It assesses experimental thinking on paper instead of manual skill at a bench: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying variables and controls, interpreting results and spotting what a method failed to control. That makes it well suited to teaching over a shared screen, where a diagram can be annotated together. Which route your child sits is part of the centre's entry, so confirm it before planning revision. Where the laboratory paper applies, the school's practical programme does the essential work and outside sessions should reinforce method discipline rather than pretend to replace bench time.

faqs.question: What do Cambridge results need to show for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education's published British-track equivalency requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Individual universities set their own, usually higher, entry requirements on top. Equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees, so confirm the current detail on the Ministry's own channel before a decision rests on it.

faqs.question: When do the certificates arrive, and who should keep them?
faqs.answer: Later than the results. For the March 2027 series Cambridge published results to centres on Direct on 13 May with certificates issued in late June, and the June and November series follow the same shape of a gap between the result and the paper document. The centre receives them and passes them on. Keep the originals somewhere a family that may relocate can find them, because attestation and equivalency processes ask for original certificates rather than screenshots, sometimes years after the examination.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark Cambridge answers properly without being an examiner?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the claim to be an examiner is worth treating carefully. What matters is whether the tutor marks a student's script against the published assessment criteria for that syllabus and can explain why a particular answer collected three marks instead of five. We do not describe tutors as Cambridge examiners unless that status can be evidenced, and examiner status should never be used to suggest access to live papers, boundaries or marking. Ask instead which codes they have taught and ask to see a marked script from the trial session.

faqs.question: We arrive at a Fujairah school in Year 11 from another board. What happens to the entries?
faqs.answer: The receiving school becomes the centre and makes the entries, within Cambridge's published deadline for the series, so the first conversation is with its examinations officer about which subjects it can enter and at which tier. Where a subject is not taught at the new school, ask whether the centre will still enter the candidate. Any previous board's coursework does not transfer across boards. For a mid-year arrival, the honest plan usually protects the five subjects needed for equivalency and the sixth-form route and treats the rest as maintenance.

faqs.question: How do the Checkpoint tests in Years 6 and 9 relate to IGCSE?
faqs.answer: They are diagnostic rather than certificated, available in March, May and October, and they are the main external evidence a family gets before the IGCSE tier decision. A Checkpoint report with a weak strand in one subject is an early, cheap signal that Core or Extended will be a live question in Year 10. Ask the school for the subject and strand breakdown rather than the headline, and use it to decide whether a term of work in Year 9 is worth more than a year of worry later.

faqs.question: Is nine weeks before the series enough for two subjects at once?
faqs.answer: It is enough for one subject done properly and a second maintained, and that is the honest shape. Nine weeks will change technique, timing and performance on two or three high-yield topics, which can be worth a grade. It will not rebuild two years of content in two subjects simultaneously, because the limiting factor is the student's independent practice time rather than the number of sessions bought. Pick the subject where the mock script shows the largest recoverable loss, and treat the second as timed practice with light marking.

fujairah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Get the series, zone and tier in writing first
fujairah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingBody: One email to the school's examinations officer answers the questions that govern everything else: which series your child is entered for, which administrative zone the centre sits in, which tier in each tiered subject, and when the final entry closes. Those four facts cost nothing and decide whether the next three months are about tier, subject count or technique. Bring them to a free trial lesson with a marked mock paper, and the plan you get back will count backwards from the first paper in your zone's timetable. Sessions run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, from a Year 10 tier decision through to a retake in the following series.

intro.heading: Why finding a subject tutor in Dibba is a geography problem before it is an academic one
paragraphs: Dibba sits at the northern end of Fujairah's coast, roughly an hour's drive up the coast road from Fujairah City, with the Hajar mountains on one side and the Gulf of Oman on the other. The town runs into Dibba Al-Hisn, which belongs to Sharjah, and into Dibba Al-Baya across the Omani border. For a parent, that layout has one practical consequence: almost nothing academic is within ten minutes. The British-curriculum and IB schools that Fujairah families use cluster in and around Fujairah City, so a Year 11 IGCSE student or a Diploma Programme student from Dibba is often in a car or on a school bus for a long stretch of every weekday.

That commute is what breaks in-home tutoring on this coast. A tutor who lives in Fujairah City and agrees to a 5pm session in Dibba has to leave at 4pm, teach for an hour, and drive back in the dark along a single coastal road. Most tutors price that travel into the rate, and the ones who do not simply stop accepting bookings north of Khor Fakkan after a few weeks. The result is a market where the deciding factor is not whether a tutor knows Chemistry HL assessment criteria but whether they are willing to make the drive.

IB Gram does not solve that by sending someone. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. On this coast that is the stronger option rather than the compromise one: a Dibba student can take Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL from a specialist who teaches that course full time, instead of from whoever is prepared to drive forty-five minutes each way. The drive stops being part of the decision.

It also changes the clock. The honest question for a Dibba family is not what time a tutor is free but what time the student is actually home, fed and able to think. School buses serving Fujairah City schools from the northern coast typically drop back well after the final bell, so a 4pm session that looks fine on paper gets cancelled in practice. Sessions that hold are the ones booked at 5.30pm, 6pm or later, and shorter in exam term where the student is already tired.

What follows is specific to this town rather than to the UAE in general. It covers what the school run does to a timetable, which subjects a small emirate genuinely cannot staff locally, what the market charges in dirhams for online and in-home tuition, the MoHRE permit any private tutor in the UAE needs, the Cambridge exam calendar read backwards from the paper to the entry deadline, who regulates a Fujairah school, and what a tutor is allowed to touch on an Internal Assessment.

fujairah/dibba.programmesIntro: Dibba families are usually sitting one of three things: a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE set in Years 10 and 11, the IB Diploma Programme in Years 12 and 13, or the Middle Years Programme before it. The programme decides what a session has to produce, so it is the first thing a match is built on.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Final grades combine internal assessment marked against published criteria with externally examined papers. The programme is front-loaded with coursework deadlines that sit months before the written exams, which is where most of the pressure on a Dibba student actually lands.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah has very few DP cohorts, so a Dibba student sitting a less common Higher Level subject may be one of a handful in the whole emirate taking it. That makes a local in-home specialist statistically unlikely and makes a matched online specialist the realistic route. It also means fewer classmates to compare notes with, so the tutor often becomes the only second reader of a draft.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, with marks reported as criterion levels rather than percentages. The programme rewards process: investigation, communication, reflection. Students who have only been graded on right answers often lose marks on the criteria that ask them to explain method, and that pattern carries straight into Diploma internal assessment if nobody corrects it.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the moment Fujairah families most often look for help, because criterion marking stops and examined papers start. A Dibba student moving from MYP into a Diploma maths or science course needs the algebraic fluency the MYP never tested directly. Six to ten weeks of targeted work over the summer closes most of that gap before Year 12 begins.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Normally eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11, with Cambridge syllabuses identified by four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE by codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge separates Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, and the tier a school enters a student for caps the achievable grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dibba students need five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. That rule shapes subject choice in Year 9 more than most families realise, so it is worth knowing before options are locked rather than in Year 11.

programmes.name: International A Level and AS Level
programmes.description: The route most British-curriculum schools on this coast offer instead of the Diploma. Three or four subjects studied in depth, assessed by written papers, with Cambridge and Pearson running different modular structures. Grades carry directly into UK and UAE university offers, and the jump in abstraction from IGCSE is steeper in mathematics and physics than in any other pair of subjects.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency a British-track student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, on top of the five IGCSEs. A Dibba student planning on a UAE university should confirm the current requirement on the Ministry's own pages before relying on any summary, including this one.

fujairah/dibba.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Fujairah coast families request most for online one-to-one work. Each line says what the subject actually assesses and where marks go missing, because that is what a session has to fix rather than what a syllabus summary says.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic manipulation, calculus, proof and the non-calculator paper. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a long problem-solving paper that rewards students who can sustain an argument across several parts. Marks are lost on method lines left unwritten, on degrees-versus-radians errors, and on exploration write-ups that describe a calculation instead of justifying a model.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling, financial mathematics and graph theory at Higher Level, with heavy graphical calculator use. The common failure is treating it as the easy maths: the data-handling questions carry long chains of marks and students who skip the interpretation sentence after a calculation lose the final mark in question after question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, organic mechanisms, and at Higher Level the extra depth on orbitals and electrochemistry. The Internal Assessment asks for a genuine personal investigation with an uncertainty analysis. Most lost marks sit in evaluation: students report what happened instead of arguing what the data can and cannot support.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, fields and the quantum topics at Higher Level. Multi-step questions are where grades move: a student who can state a definition but cannot select between energy and momentum approaches stalls at the four-mark questions. Graph-gradient interpretation and unit tracking recover marks quickly in one-to-one work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology, nucleic acids, metabolism, genetics and ecology, with command terms doing more work than in any other science. Students who answer every question with description lose the marks reserved for explanation, comparison and evaluation. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments are the most teachable gap on the whole course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and, at Higher Level, extra quantitative work. Diagrams are assessed, not decorative: an unlabelled axis or a shifted curve without an explanation of the mechanism forfeits marks. Internal assessment commentaries on published news articles need a clearly identified key concept and real diagrammatic analysis.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, comparative essays, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the written essay. Students lose marks for retelling the text rather than analysing how meaning is constructed. Work on the oral tends to pay back fastest, because it is rehearsable and the global issue framing is a skill rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics across two papers. The Extended and Higher tiers carry the algebra and trigonometry that decide an A or A*. Marks go missing on rounding instructions, on bearings, and on multi-stage percentage questions where students answer the first stage correctly and stop.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1)
subjects.description: Particles, stoichiometry, reactivity, acids and bases, organic chemistry and chemical analysis. Alternative-to-practical style questions on apparatus, anomalous readings and improvement suggestions are the most reliably recoverable marks on the paper, because they test experimental reasoning that can be taught directly rather than recalled.

subjects.name: Physics (IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1)
subjects.description: Forces and motion, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, and atomic physics. Electricity is the topic most Fujairah coast students name as the hardest, usually because series and parallel reasoning was never separated from formula recall. Rearranging equations under time pressure is a drill, not a talent, and it moves grades.

subjects.name: Biology (IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1)
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, coordination, inheritance and ecology. The long-answer questions reward structured sequences, and students who write in bullet fragments lose marks that full causal chains would have earned. Graph and table interpretation questions are worth practising with a timer rather than reading about.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Accounting
subjects.description: Business ownership, marketing, operations, finance, and for Accounting the full set of ledgers, control accounts and final statements. Case-study questions require application to the stimulus business rather than a general answer, and the evaluation marks at the end of the paper are the ones most commonly left on the table.

fujairah/dibba.regionsIntro: Dibba sits inside a short string of coastal towns and Fujairah City districts that share the same roads and the same school options. The notes below are about travel and timing, because on this coast those are what decide whether a tutoring plan survives past the second week.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The Fujairah-administered part of the town, at the northern end of the emirate's coastline. Families here are furthest from the Fujairah City school cluster, so bus journeys are long and evening sessions need to start late.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Hisn
regions.note: The adjoining Sharjah enclave. Households straddle the two administrations within the same town, which means some neighbours sit under Sharjah's private education authority while others sit under the federal Ministry of Education.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan
regions.note: The Sharjah-administered port town south of Dibba on the same coast road. It is the usual halfway marker on the drive to Fujairah City and the point beyond which in-home tutors stop travelling north.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Where the emirate's private-school cluster, the port and the corniche sit. Most Dibba students with an IB or IGCSE place are enrolled here, which is why the school run defines their week.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: A coastal district of Fujairah City near the corniche. Relevant to Dibba families mainly as a school-run destination and as the place after-school activities are usually scheduled.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: An inland Fujairah City district on the road out towards the mountains. Another cluster point for schools and tuition centres, and another forty minutes from Dibba in each direction.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: A northern district of Fujairah City, the first part of town a Dibba family reaches on the coast road. Convenient for drop-off, still an hour from home once school finishes.

regions.name: Masafi and the mountain road
regions.note: The inland route over the Hajar mountains towards Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. Families who use it for weekend travel know how quickly a journey here stops being predictable, which is an argument for lessons that do not depend on anyone driving.

schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private schools are concentrated here, running British, Indian and bilingual curricula. fujairah/dibba.modesIntro: Three formats make sense for a Dibba student, and the right one usually changes over the two years rather than being chosen once. All three are delivered online over live video, so the coast road never appears in the scheduling conversation.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: A fixed slot each week with the same specialist, usually sixty minutes for IGCSE and seventy-five to ninety for Higher Level Diploma work. The session follows the school's own scheme of work, so the tutor is reinforcing what was taught that week rather than running a parallel course. This is the format that suits a long school-run day because it only needs one evening.

modes.title: Coursework and internal assessment support
modes.description: Scheduled around the school's own draft deadlines for the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The tutor teaches the criteria, questions the method, and gives feedback on the student's own work; the student produces every word of it. For a Dibba student with no classmate taking the same subject, this is often the only second opinion available before submission.

sections.heading: What a Dibba parent is actually searching for
paragraphs: A search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Dibba is almost never a search for a stranger with a car. It is a search for someone who knows the syllabus a child is sitting, is free at a time that exists in that household's week, and can be relied on past the first fortnight. On this coast the third condition is the one that fails. Tutors who agree to travel north from Fujairah City renegotiate or quietly withdraw once the drive has been made a few times in the dark.

The useful reframe is to separate the two things the query bundles together. One is the subject expertise: a Chemistry HL specialist who has marked the Internal Assessment criteria enough times to see a weak evaluation coming. The other is logistics: being present at 6pm on a Tuesday. In-home tutoring ties those two together and lets geography pick the tutor. Online one-to-one teaching splits them, and lets the subject pick the tutor while the clock stays local.

IB Gram delivers to Dibba as live online one-to-one tuition, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. That is stated plainly rather than buried, because the alternative on this coast is a family discovering it in week three. What a Dibba household gets instead is a specialist in the exact syllabus, a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, a free trial lesson before any commitment, and a replacement tutor if the match is wrong rather than a refund argument.

Everything below is written for that decision. It sets out the timing arithmetic for this town, which subjects a small emirate can and cannot staff, what the wider UAE market charges in dirhams, the permit rules a legitimate private tutor works under, and the exam deadlines that sit months before the papers a family is worrying about.

sections.heading: The Dibba school run, timed properly
paragraphs: Scheduling a tutoring session from Dibba is an arithmetic problem with four numbers in it: when the school day ends, how long the journey home actually takes on a weekday, how long the student needs before they can concentrate, and how long a session can run before it stops being useful. Families who skip the middle two numbers book a 4.30pm slot, miss it twice, and conclude that tutoring does not work for them.

The journey from the Fujairah City school cluster back up the coast to Dibba takes most of an hour in a private car and longer on a school bus making stops. Add a decompression gap and the earliest honest start on a school night is around 5.30pm, with 6pm or 6.30pm more robust. Families who have a sibling on a different bus route usually find that the later of the two arrivals is the one that actually sets the slot.

Session length should then flex with the term. Ninety minutes is productive in September for a Higher Level subject being built from the ground up. In the four weeks before mocks, the same student does better with forty-five minutes of timed paper work four times a week, because fatigue is the constraint rather than content. During Ramadan the whole pattern shifts, and post-Iftar slots are usually calmer and more productive than anything attempted in the afternoon.

sections.heading: Why a small emirate runs short of subject specialists
paragraphs: Fujairah has a small private-school sector compared with Dubai or Abu Dhabi, and the numbers cascade. Fewer schools means fewer Diploma cohorts; fewer cohorts means fewer teachers of any given Higher Level subject; and fewer teachers means almost no pool of experienced local tutors for the less common courses. A Dibba student taking Physics HL will usually find somebody in the emirate who has taught it. A Dibba student taking Economics HL, Computer Science HL or a Group 2 language at Higher Level may genuinely find nobody.

This is the gap that no local tutoring listing admits to. The usual pattern is that a general science graduate accepts a Diploma Chemistry booking, teaches the content competently, and has never read the Internal Assessment criteria closely enough to know how the evaluation marks are awarded. The student gets help and still loses the marks that were available. Honest coverage disclosure is more useful to a parent than a longer list of subject names.

Online matching changes the arithmetic because the pool is no longer bounded by the Hajar mountains. A Dibba family can be matched to a tutor who teaches only Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or only Cambridge 0620 Chemistry, and who has done so across several exam series. Where a specialist genuinely is not free, the right answer is to say so and offer a timeline rather than fill the slot with the nearest available graduate.

sections.heading: Online versus an in-home tutor on the Fujairah coast
paragraphs: Comparing the two formats properly means comparing them on cost, on who you can actually get, and on what happens in week six. Published market rates in the UAE, read in October 2026, put budget online tutoring from around AED 33 to AED 150 per hour, qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, in-home one-to-one visits at about AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and named or examiner-level specialists at AED 500 and above. Those are market figures published by providers and rate trackers, not IB Gram prices.

The travel premium inside those bands is not a rounding error. A tutor pricing a Dibba visit has to cover roughly two hours of driving around a one-hour lesson, and the rate reflects it or the booking does not survive. That is before the quieter cost: a student whose tutor is chosen from the subset of people willing to drive the coast road is choosing from a very small group, and subject match is the first thing sacrificed.

The reliability column is where families on this coast usually end up. A session that depends on nobody breaking down on the coast road, on no weather on the mountain route, and on a tutor still being willing in February is a session with several ways to fail. A live video lesson has one: the connection. That is a solvable problem and a much smaller one.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page for it is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee stated and a completion time of two working days, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the government's words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated with suspicion.

Two further points matter for a Dibba family. First, a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs its own educational services permit from the relevant authority; an individual permit does not cover a centre. Second, the permit carries a code of conduct, and press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules describes teachers being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Asking your child's class teacher to tutor them privately is the one arrangement to avoid.

The table sets out the categories as the regulations describe them. It is a guide for asking the right question, not legal advice, and the position should be confirmed on mohre.gov.ae before any arrangement is signed.

sections.heading: The Cambridge exam calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Most families start worrying about exams about six weeks before the first paper. By then the decisions that mattered have already been made, because entry deadlines, tier decisions and forecast grades all sit months earlier. Reading the calendar backwards is the single most useful hour a Year 11 or Year 13 parent can spend, and it is a view no competing page on this coast publishes.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The March series is a worked example of how far ahead the real deadlines sit: for March 2027 the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

There is a trap in the timetable itself. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A UAE school and a UK school can therefore sit the same paper at different local times. Always work from the version your child's own exams officer issues.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so dates should be read from the live official timetable rather than from any summary.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school in Dibba and Fujairah
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai talk about KHDA inspection bands the way parents elsewhere talk about league tables, and families moving to Fujairah often assume the same framework applies. It does not. Fujairah's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which, in the government's own words, plays a supervisory role over private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. There is no Fujairah-specific equivalent of KHDA or ADEK.

That matters inside a single town. Dibba Al-Fujairah is Fujairah territory and therefore federally supervised, while Dibba Al-Hisn is Sharjah territory and falls under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Two children in the same neighbourhood can be studying under different regulatory regimes, with different fee-approval processes behind their invoices.

The federal baseline applies everywhere: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement, and the reason a British-curriculum school in Fujairah still timetables Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE options.

For a tutoring plan the practical consequence is that a Dibba student is often carrying mandatory UAE subjects on top of a full IGCSE or Diploma load. Those subjects are examined, they appear on reports, and they compete for the same evening hours. Any honest timetable has to account for them rather than treat the international curriculum as the whole week.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that gets students into real trouble, and it is the one the market is least honest about. Some operators in this region advertise completed Internal Assessments for a fixed fee. Under IB academic-honesty rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller: a withdrawn grade or a withdrawn diploma. No part of IB Gram's service goes anywhere near it.

A tutor's legitimate role is large even so. They can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter and explain how marks are distributed between them. They can interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to answer in the word limit. They can challenge a method before data collection rather than after. They can read a draft the student has produced and say where the evaluation is thin, where a claim is unsupported, and which criterion is currently capped. All of that is teaching.

What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure an argument into their own words, or hand back a document the student could not have produced. The line in practice is simple to apply: feedback points at the student's work and names the criterion; a service that produces the work does not. Every school also requires an authenticity declaration, and supervisors are expected to have seen the work develop across drafts.

For a Dibba student the honest value of this is often that there is nobody else to read the draft. If no classmate is taking the same Higher Level subject, the tutor may be the only second reader before submission. That makes keeping the boundary visible more important rather than less, so it is stated at the start of any coursework block and written into the session notes.
bullets: Criteria taught by letter, with their mark allocations explained

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for a Dibba student
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns a foreign school certificate into a document a UAE institution will accept. It is administered by the Ministry of Education, not by any tutoring provider, and IB Gram neither performs it nor guarantees any outcome from it. What a tutoring plan can do is make sure subject choices made in Year 9 do not block it in Year 13.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. On top of that they must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

For the American track the thresholds are test-based: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics via at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold has been confirmed from the Ministry's own pages in the research behind this page, so none is published here. Confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on anything.

The exclusion of Arabic and Islamic Education from the count is the detail that catches families out, because it means a student with exactly five passes including Arabic does not have five countable subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is not what the published guidance says. Check the current rule yourself rather than inheriting either number.

sections.heading: Starting from Dibba, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is short on purpose. You tell us the subject, the board, the level and the school's current grade or criterion marks. We ask which syllabus code the school is entered for, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different structures and a tutor who knows one is not automatically useful for the other. Then we propose a specialist and a slot, and the first lesson is a free trial with no obligation to continue.

The trial is diagnostic rather than a sales meeting. The tutor works through something the student has actually been set, usually a recent assessment or a paper question they got wrong, and reports back on what the gap is. Sometimes that report says the gap is narrower than the parent feared and recommends four sessions rather than a year. That is a better outcome than a long booking that nobody questions in February.

Where things get honest is availability. For a narrow Higher Level subject there may be no specialist free at the slot a Dibba family needs. The answer in that case is a stated timeline and the option of a different slot, not an immediate substitute who nearly fits. If a match turns out to be wrong after two or three sessions, the tutor is changed; nobody learns much from a pairing that is not working, and a replacement is faster than a renegotiation.

After that, the rhythm is simple. Notes and worked solutions after each session, pacing against the school's own assessment calendar, a short review every half term against the grade the student started at, and a deliberate stop at the end of the exam series rather than a booking that rolls on by default.
