sections.heading: The weeks from the mock examinations to the May session
paragraphs: The stretch after the mocks is the only part of the Diploma where almost everything a student does is examination performance, and it is also where effort is most often misallocated. The instinct is to revise the topics that feel uncomfortable. The better plan is to revise where the marks are, which means reading the mock scripts question by question and ranking topics by marks lost per hour of likely study. In most subjects that ranking is not what the student expected.

Two habits do more than any amount of content review in this window. The first is writing full answers to time, which is a physical skill that degrades without practice. The second is marking those answers against the published criteria, because it shows the student the difference between an answer that is right and an answer that collects the marks. A tutor who marks a script and then teaches the three recurring losses is doing the highest-value work available at this point in the calendar.

Dates matter here and we do not publish them. UAE schools sit the May session, registration is handled by the school as the registering centre, and the exact windows for examinations and results come from the IB or the school's coordinator rather than from a tutoring site. Ask for them in writing at the start of DP2 and build the revision calendar backwards from the first paper, leaving the last fortnight for timed practice rather than new learning.
bullets: Rank revision by marks lost, not by discomfort

sections.heading: What two years of support actually costs, in context
paragraphs: Diploma tutoring is bought in hours and experienced as a two-year line in the household budget, so it is worth seeing against the other costs around it. Published market rates in this country put budget and generalist online tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at about AED 150 to 300, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 once travel is included, and IB or IGCSE specialists from AED 200 to 450 and upwards. A published 2026 Dubai survey put monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget help, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and beyond for specialist exam-year support.

Those are market figures with their source stated, not IB Gram prices, and the point of showing them is to make the planning arithmetic visible. One Higher Level subject supported weekly across both Diploma years is a different commitment from an eight-week intensive before the papers, and families routinely discover the difference after committing. School fees are the other half of the context: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, which at least makes the tuition line the variable one.

The sensible sequencing on the east coast is to spend early and narrowly rather than late and broadly. One subject in DP1, chosen because it is the Higher Level the school can least support, costs less across two years than three subjects bought in panic in DP2, and it is the version that actually changes the examination result. sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge, CAS and the quiet failing conditions
paragraphs: The core components are worth up to three points between the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, which sounds minor until a university offer sits at a point above the predicted total. More importantly, the core carries failing conditions: a Diploma can be withheld over an incomplete core requirement even where the subject grades are comfortable. Families who treat Theory of Knowledge as the soft subject on the timetable are reading the point total and ignoring the award rules.

Theory of Knowledge is also genuinely difficult to teach in a small school, because it is nobody's subject specialism. The essay responds to a prescribed title and is marked on the quality of the argument about knowledge rather than on content knowledge, which means a strong science student can write fluently and score poorly. Teaching it is a matter of structure and of using examples that do real work in the argument, and it is one of the few places where a handful of sessions reliably changes the outcome.

CAS is a requirement rather than a graded component, and the usual east-coast difficulty is not finding activities but documenting them. Reflections left to the final weeks are thin, and the coordinator cannot sign off what is not recorded. Fujairah families have good access to coastal and community projects; what they often lack is a habit of writing the reflection at the time. That habit is free to establish in DP1 and expensive to retrofit in DP2.

An incomplete core requirement can block the award regardless of subject grades
Theory of Knowledge is marked on argument about knowledge, not subject content
CAS reflections written at the time are worth more than any amount written later

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma coursework
paragraphs: The IB's academic honesty rules make the student responsible for the work submitted in their name, and the consequences of a malpractice finding fall on the student rather than on whoever helped. That makes the boundary a practical matter rather than a point of principle. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, explain what a command term demands, question whether a research question can be answered in the available length, and respond to a draft the student has written. That is legitimate, documented support and it is what a supervisor does too.

What a tutor must not do is supply the work. Nobody at IB Gram hands over essay text, internal assessment sections, Theory of Knowledge paragraphs or finished analysis, and we do not edit a student's submission into shape sentence by sentence. Services in this search cluster do sell completed internal assessments; that is an integrity breach which puts a candidate's whole Diploma at risk, and it is the clearest line between a tutoring service and an essay mill.

There is a second boundary families run into. Board papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, and we do not reproduce or supply them as downloads. A tutor can teach from them where the student has legitimate access through the school, and can point to the official source. If a student arrives the night before a deadline hoping someone else will carry the work over the line, the honest answer is that a weak mark is survivable and a malpractice finding is not.

sections.heading: Fujairah specifics: thin cohorts and the Higher Level nobody can staff
paragraphs: Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman with the Hajar mountains between it and the western emirates, and its private-school set is small. For the Diploma that produces a particular pattern: generous access to teachers, limited depth in any single Higher Level course, and subject combinations constrained by the timetable rather than by ability. A student may be one of three or four taking a subject, taught by someone who also covers Standard Level and a lower school course.

The honest consequence is that the thing a Fujairah family most often needs is not more teaching but different teaching: one specialist in one Higher Level subject, for two years, who has taught that course repeatedly. That is also the thing a twenty-minute radius cannot supply, and it is the reason a visiting tutor is rarely the answer here. A one-hour lesson costs a tutor crossing the mountains close to three hours, which is why published in-home bands reach AED 500 and why the far slot is the first one cancelled in a busy week.

Online delivery is what makes the specialist available at all, and the honesty rule applies in both directions. Where no UAE-based tutor covers a narrow Higher Level subject at a workable hour, a family is told that and offered a specialist elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time, or told to wait for one. Across thirty teaching weeks, the consistency of a slot that never depends on the weather on the mountain road is worth more than any single session.

process.title: Say where you are on the timeline
process.description: Tell us the Diploma year, the term, the six subjects with their levels, and which internal assessment components have already been submitted internally. That one message determines whether the useful plan targets the prediction, the papers or the core, and it stops a package being sold for the wrong phase.

process.title: Free trial with a marked script or draft
process.description: One hour online at a time that fits the school run. The tutor works from a marked paper or an internal assessment draft, teaches for most of the session, and ends by naming the specific losses. No card details are needed to book it, and it is one lesson per student.

process.title: A plan written backwards from the session
process.description: You get a short written plan that starts at the May session and counts back: what has to be secure by the mocks, what can still be changed after them, and which subject is first. Where the honest answer is that the school's own programme covers it, the plan says so.

process.title: Fixed slots that survive the exam term
process.description: Sessions run at a set time on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor, following the school's internal deadlines rather than a generic Diploma calendar. Slots shift permanently for Ramadan hours or a change in school transport, because a plan that only works in October is not a plan.

process.title: Checkpoints on marked work, not on feel
process.description: Progress is read from timed questions marked against published criteria, at intervals agreed in advance. If two checkpoints show no movement, the approach changes or the tutor changes. In DP2 there is not enough calendar left to spend a term discovering a poor match.

whyPoints.title: The plan is dated, not open-ended
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from the examination session and counts backwards, so a family can see which weeks are still useful and which components are already closed. That is the opposite of an open-ended monthly package, and it occasionally produces the recommendation to buy less rather than more.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level depth a small cohort cannot carry
whyPoints.description: The common Fujairah requirement is one specialist in one Higher Level subject for two years. Online matching draws on everyone who teaches that course and can make a Gulf Standard Time slot, which is a larger pool than the east coast contains for Chemistry, Analysis and Approaches or Computer Science.

whyPoints.title: Core components treated as real work
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge carry up to three points and can block the award if left incomplete. Support is scheduled against the school's internal deadlines rather than squeezed in when a subject session has spare time, because the core is where quiet losses happen.

whyPoints.title: Coursework boundaries stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches criteria, questions research design and responds to the student's own drafts. No text, no sections, no editing to completion, and no reproduction of board papers or mark schemes. That boundary protects the candidate, and it is the difference between this and the essay services ranking alongside it.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown as the market, with the source named
whyPoints.description: The AED bands and monthly figures on this page come from published provider pricing and a 2026 Dubai rate survey, presented as market context rather than as our price list. Most pages ranking for these searches publish no figure at all.

whyPoints.title: Disclosure when nobody is free
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist covers a narrow Higher Level subject at a workable hour, you are told before you pay, and offered either a tutor elsewhere teaching into your time zone or an honest wait. A weak substitute in DP2 costs more than an awkward message does.

faqs.question: My son is in DP1 and predicted 28. What is realistically fixable from here?
faqs.answer: Most of it, because DP1 is the phase where time still exists. With eighteen months to the papers, the two levers are the foundations his Higher Level courses will assume and the design of his internal assessment work, both of which are cheap to fix now and expensive later. Start with the single subject where marks are most recoverable rather than spreading across three. What cannot be recovered later is a component already submitted internally, so ask the school which ones those are before planning anything.

faqs.question: When should a Fujairah Diploma student start subject tuition to make a difference?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and in one subject rather than three. The cheapest useful intervention is in the first or second term of DP1, aimed at the Higher Level the local school can least support, because it changes both the content base and the internal assessment design. The most expensive is a panic purchase in DP2 across several subjects, which divides attention at the point where independent practice time is already short. If you are already in DP2, start with the subject whose mock script shows the largest recoverable loss.

faqs.question: How are predicted grades decided, and can extra tuition change them?
faqs.answer: The school produces them from evidence it holds: internal assessment marks, mock examinations and classwork, usually during DP2 and before university deadlines. A tutor cannot influence a prediction directly and should not try to. What tuition can do is improve the evidence before the prediction is made, which is why the timing question matters so much. Ask the coordinator when predictions are produced and from what. If the window has closed, aim the plan at the final result and adjust the application strategy instead.

faqs.question: What should a tutor be doing differently in DP2 from DP1?
faqs.answer: Almost everything. DP1 work is foundational and design-led: securing content the Higher Level course will assume, settling internal assessment questions, building written volume. DP2 work is triage and technique: timed questions, scripts marked against published criteria, and a ranking of topics by marks lost rather than by difficulty. A tutor still teaching new content in the final term has misjudged the calendar, and a DP1 tutor drilling past papers has done the same thing in the other direction.

faqs.question: How many hours outside school does a Higher Level subject actually need?
faqs.answer: Plan on four to six hours of independent work a week per Higher Level subject, of which a tutored session is one. That ratio is the important part: sessions are useful because they set work the student then does, so buying more sessions at the cost of practice time makes the result worse. In DP2 a second weekly session in the one subject costing the most marks is usually the best available spend, and a third subject added at the same time is usually the worst.

faqs.question: Our school moved an internal assessment deadline. Does that affect the IB submission?
faqs.answer: The school's deadline and the IB's submission schedule are different things, and the first exists to protect the second. Coordinators build internal dates with a margin so marking, moderation and upload can happen in order, so a slipped internal deadline eats that margin rather than the IB's. Get the internal calendar for every subject and component in writing at the start of DP2, and treat a moved date as a warning rather than a reprieve. A student who misses a rebuilt deadline usually has no margin left behind it.

faqs.question: What happens between the mocks and the May session, week by week?
faqs.answer: The mocks produce evidence, and the weeks after them should be spent on what that evidence says. Read the scripts question by question, rank topics by marks lost per likely study hour, and build the calendar backwards from the first paper, keeping the final fortnight for timed practice rather than new learning. Two habits matter more than content review: writing full answers to time, and marking them against the published criteria. Exact session dates come from the school's IB coordinator, not from any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Can we start Diploma tuition six weeks before the papers and still change anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, within limits worth being honest about. Six weeks is enough to change examination technique, timing, and performance on two or three high-yield topics in one subject, and that can be worth a grade. It is not enough to rebuild two years of content across six subjects, and it cannot touch internal assessment marks already submitted. The right shape is narrow: one subject, the specific papers that underperform, marked scripts every week. Anyone selling a broad six-week programme at this stage is selling comfort.

faqs.question: Is a November retake sensible for a student on the east coast?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the logistics need settling before the academic plan. A retake is entered through a school acting as the registering centre, so the first question for a candidate who has left is which centre will enter them, and whether that centre is in the emirate. Where internal assessment marks can be carried forward under the current subject guide, the work is narrow: the specific papers that underperformed, nothing else. Confirm what carries forward with the coordinator rather than assuming, because it varies by subject.

faqs.question: What does a two-year Diploma plan cost in dirhams if we budget from DP1?
faqs.answer: At published market rates, one subject supported weekly sits in the AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-range band, rising towards AED 1,000 to 2,000 and beyond for specialist exam-year support, with in-home visits quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is priced. Those figures are from provider pricing and a published 2026 Dubai survey, and they are the market rather than our price list. The cheaper two-year shape is one subject early rather than three late, and it usually produces the better examination result.

faqs.question: Does Theory of Knowledge really affect the final Diploma score?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three points on top of the subject total, which is often exactly the margin a university offer turns on. More seriously, the core carries failing conditions, so an incomplete requirement can block the award even where subject grades are strong. It is also hard to teach in a small school because it belongs to no subject specialism, which makes it one of the few components where a handful of structured sessions changes the outcome reliably.

faqs.question: My daughter has three Higher Levels and is drowning in September. What comes off first?
faqs.answer: Nothing comes off until the school has been asked, because a level change is a school decision with deadlines attached, and dropping a Higher Level to Standard is usually possible early in DP1 and not later. Before that conversation, separate overload from misplacement: a student failing to keep up in all three has a workload and method problem, while one drowning in a single subject has a placement problem. Fix the method first with one subject supported properly, then revisit the combination with the coordinator using evidence rather than impressions.

faqs.question: How many drafts of the Extended Essay may a supervisor or tutor read?
faqs.answer: The supervisor relationship is defined by the school and the IB, and typically allows a limited number of formal checkpoints with written feedback on one full draft. A tutor works behind that rather than in place of it: teaching the assessment criteria, testing whether the research question is answerable in 4,000 words, and responding to what the student has written. Supplying text, rewriting sections or editing a submission into shape is outside that boundary and puts the candidate at risk. Ask the school for its own supervision schedule in writing.

faqs.question: If we move country mid-Diploma, what carries over and what restarts?
faqs.answer: The registration and the internal assessment position travel with the candidate through the coordinators rather than with the family, so the first call is to both schools. Subjects and levels may not match between timetables, and a Higher Level the new school cannot staff is the usual breaking point. Settle three things before accepting a place: which subjects at which levels the receiving school can actually offer, what internal assessment work it will accept as complete, and who registers the candidate for the session. Online subject support is often what keeps a mismatched subject alive through a move.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects can a small Fujairah school rarely staff at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: In practice, the narrow and the technical: Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science, and minority second languages. These are not criticisms of the schools; a cohort of three or four cannot justify a dedicated specialist, and the teacher is usually carrying several courses. That is exactly where an online match earns its place, because the requirement is narrow and specific rather than general. Where nobody inside the UAE covers it at a workable hour, you should be told that before paying.

fujairah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Fix the date first, then the subject
fujairah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: Before buying anything, get two things from the school in writing: the internal deadline calendar for every subject and core component, and the date predicted grades are produced. Those two facts determine whether the next six weeks should target the prediction, the papers or the core, and they are free. Bring them to a free trial lesson with a marked script or a draft, and the plan you get back will count backwards from the May session with the weeks named. Sessions run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, from DP1 foundations through to a narrow retake plan if one is needed.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched to one Diploma or International GCSE subject at the level your child is registered for. The first session is diagnostic rather than instructional: nobody can sequence fourteen weeks of teaching before reading what the last two marked scripts actually show.

intro.heading: Where your child is now, where they need to be, and the weeks in between
paragraphs: Almost every parent who types this phrase is asking a timing question wearing a logistics costume. The anxiety is not about who stands in the room. It is that a Diploma year is running, a report has come home that nobody can interpret, and there is no clear sense of whether the gap between now and the papers is four weeks of work or four months. That question has an answer, and it can be reached in one diagnostic session rather than guessed at over a term of pleasant weekly meetings.

The honest part first, because the rest of the page depends on it. Visiting tuition exists in Fujairah and families here do buy it. Published market rates for in-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE run AED 180-500 per hour with travel priced inside the fee, and monthly packages of four two-hour visiting sessions have been advertised at AED 1,599-1,799. For a household in Fujairah City with a child in Year 9 who needs supervision and routine, that can be money well spent. IB Gram does not sell it. Visiting tuition is a service offered only in India, and nobody will be sent to a Fujairah address.

What IB Gram arranges is one-to-one teaching delivered live over video, in Gulf Standard Time. On this coast the argument for that is not cost and not convenience; it is reach and continuity. The Hajar mountains put the Dubai school belt two to three hours away by road, so a visiting specialist is paying for the drive twice per lesson. The mountain road closes after heavy rain. Slots stop moving because rescheduling costs somebody a round trip. Over two years that arithmetic decides how many lessons actually happen, and lessons that happen are the only ones that change a mark.

The timeline itself is more predictable than parents expect, because the Diploma has a fixed shape. There is a diagnostic phase, lasting one session. There is a content phase, where identified gaps get rebuilt, which usually runs six to fourteen weeks for one subject. There is a technique phase, where knowledge becomes marks, driven by timed papers and mark schemes. Then there is the final stretch, where new content stops entirely. Cutting across all of it are the school's own internal deadlines for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and each subject's assessed component, which run on dates the school chooses rather than the examination timetable.

The rest of this page walks that sequence in order, says what each phase can and cannot achieve, and gives a table for families starting late with a realistic aim for each remaining window. It also covers the two things that break timelines on the east coast specifically: the shortened Ramadan school day, and assessed components landing in the same fortnight. If your child is in DP2 with one term left, skip to the section on starting late. If you are in DP1 with nothing obviously wrong, the diagnostic section is the one worth reading.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Each programme has its own milestone calendar, and the milestones are what a plan is built around. These are the four that matter on the east coast, described by when the pressure arrives rather than by what the programme contains.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years with the load concentrated unevenly. DP1 looks quiet and is not: subject choices, Higher Level levels, the Extended Essay question and the first assessed drafts are all decided inside it. DP2 is where everything internally assessed falls due, usually before the mock season, which is why a student who leaves the core until DP2 is revising and writing at the same time.
programmes.countryNote: A Fujairah student is more exposed to this than a Dubai one, because a small school coordinates the whole programme through fewer people. There is often no dedicated core team chasing a timetable, so an Extended Essay deadline in DP1 passes without anyone noticing until the draft is already late.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed continuously against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, so there is no single point where everything is decided. The Personal Project in the final year is the first long self-managed piece a student writes, and how it goes is a fair predictor of how the Extended Essay will go two years later.
programmes.countryNote: For east-coast families the useful MYP milestone is the options conversation in Year 9, because what is chosen there determines which Diploma or IGCSE routes a local school can actually staff. That conversation happens earlier than most parents here expect it to.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The milestone that catches families out is the entry deadline rather than the exam. Cambridge published final entries for its March 2027 series as due 27 November 2026, with the exam period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results to centres on 13 May. Tier and subject are fixed at entry, months before anybody sits a paper.
programmes.countryNote: Because east-coast schools sit as Cambridge centres allocated to an administrative zone, the correct timetable version depends on that zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in before planning the final weeks.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Examined in a May or June window and again in November, which creates a second attempt inside the same academic year. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: The November window matters on this coast because repeating a year is rarely practical when school choice is limited. A student who underperforms in June can re-sit in November without changing school, and the planning question becomes which subjects are worth the second attempt rather than whether to move.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects east-coast families ask about, described by when in the course the difficulty usually arrives. Knowing the month a subject tends to bite is what turns a vague worry into a dated plan.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Bites in the second term of DP1, when the algebra stops being revision of IGCSE and starts assuming fluency. Students who were comfortable to that point often slip quietly. The exploration lands in DP1 or early DP2 and competes directly with content revision for the same hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Difficulty arrives later, usually in the statistics and modelling units, and shows up as interpretation rather than calculation. A plan here is often shorter than for Analysis and Approaches: six to eight weeks to establish the habit of writing what a result means.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two pressure points: moles and stoichiometry early in DP1, organic mechanisms in DP2. The scientific investigation is normally due in DP2 before mocks, so a student with an unresolved content gap is writing it while still behind, which is the worst sequence available.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circuits are where east-coast students most often stall, generally in the middle of DP1. Uncertainty treatment surfaces late, in the investigation, and is a fast fix once identified. The ten-week window after the DP1 mock is the most productive one in this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Rarely produces a dramatic failure and often produces a disappointing grade, because the revision method is the problem rather than the content. Gains come in a short block converting recall into extended-response structure, not in a year of weekly content coverage.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the analysis marks before the evaluation is read, and the Higher Level third paper arrives late in DP2 with quantitative questions students have never systematically practised. Budget specific weeks for Paper 3 rather than assuming it falls out of general revision.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The assessed research project is the timeline risk. A topic too broad to answer in the word limit is chosen in a busy week and the problem is baked in before the first draft. Fixing it after the data has been collected is expensive in weeks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is the component families forget to plan for, because it has no written deadline attached in most schools' minds. It needs a global issue argued rather than announced, and that argument takes weeks of practice rather than one rehearsal.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive skills under timed conditions improve steadily rather than suddenly, so this is one of the few subjects where a long, low-intensity arrangement genuinely beats a short block. Start early and keep sessions short.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: The tier decision in Year 10 is the real deadline, because it sets a ceiling on the grade and is fixed at entry. A borderline student has a genuine window in the first term of Year 10 and a much narrower job once entries have gone.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: Required study alongside the licensed curriculum
subjects.description: Runs in parallel all year with first-language and additional-language streams taught separately. The timeline issue is that it is never the subject a family plans for, so it absorbs hours in the exam term that were budgeted for something else.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where you live in Fujairah changes what time a session can start and how reliably it holds, which is a timeline question rather than a geography one. These are the districts enquiries come from and the practical constraint in each.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Shortest school run in the emirate, so a four o'clock start is realistic for most households. The timeline risk here is the opposite of distance: families delay starting because everything feels accessible, then begin in DP2.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Corniche sports and club commitments run late, pushing a sustainable weekday slot past five. Two shorter sessions a week usually survive the term better here than one long evening that collides with fixtures.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: A mixed-curriculum intake where school reports rarely identify the component at fault, so the diagnostic session earns its place more clearly than elsewhere. Early-evening slots hold well once activities end.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Residential and close to the city schools. Households here often have children in two different year groups, which makes back-to-back slots the practical arrangement and a single visiting appointment awkward to price.

regions.name: Madhab and Al Gurfa
regions.note: A steady turnover of posted families means mid-year arrivals are common. A student joining a Diploma cohort in DP1 mid-term needs a compressed version of the whole sequence, starting with what the new school has already taught.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: An hour up the coast with minimal school choice in range. School buses arrive late, so a realistic first slot is after five, and any plan depending on a weekly drive from the city has a continuity problem built in.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Long gaps between settlements on the northern coast road. Timeline reliability here comes from the arrangement not requiring travel at all, which is the whole reason video sessions dominate this stretch.

regions.name: Masafi and the inland route
regions.note: On the road west, split between Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah. After heavy rain the route closes, which turns a visiting lesson into a lost week at the point in the year when weeks stop being recoverable.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah City and the coastal districts
schoolClusters.note: The schools within a normal school run of the city, covering British and Indian curricula. Internal deadlines differ between them even for students sitting the same session, which is why a plan starts from the school's own dates rather than a generic calendar.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Khor Fakkan corridor
schoolClusters.note: Minutes down the same coast and under the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than the Ministry of Education, with different term dates. Families who move between the two mid-course meet two calendars in one academic year.

schoolClusters.city: Campuses families consider for sixth form
schoolClusters.note: Where a Higher Level combination is not available locally, these are the realistic alternatives, usually on a weekly-boarding or relocation basis. Named as context for a decision, not as a daily commute over the mountain road.

sections.heading: What a home tutor in Fujairah actually involves, and what happens here instead
paragraphs: Take the question literally for a moment, because it deserves a straight answer. Hiring someone to teach your child at a Fujairah address means hiring from the people who live within a sensible drive of it. In Fujairah City that is a real if small pool for general academic support. In Dibba, Qidfa or Mirbah it is a very short list, and for a Higher Level Diploma subject it is frequently empty. The hourly rate reflects the travel: published market figures for visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE run AED 180-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and advertised monthly packages of four two-hour visiting sessions have sat at AED 1,599-1,799.

There is a legal dimension worth knowing before anybody is invited round. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated: individuals giving private lessons need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. MoHRE states that anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted online should be treated as unverified. Ask to see the permit. It costs the tutor nothing to hold.

IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Fujairah, and no tutor will be sent to a Fujairah address; visiting tuition is offered only in India. The teaching here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The case for that on this coast is specific and it is about the calendar rather than the technology: a plan that depends on somebody driving the mountain road loses lessons to weather, traffic and the ordinary friction of rescheduling, and lost lessons in February are not recoverable in April. The table sets the two arrangements against each other on the terms that decide a timeline.

sections.heading: Step one: establishing where your child actually is
paragraphs: Everything downstream depends on this and almost nobody does it first. The usual sequence is that a report arrives, a grade looks wrong, and a weekly session is booked in that subject. Three months later the grade has not moved, because the session was aimed at the syllabus when the problem was two paper sections. One diagnostic hour, worked from the last two marked scripts, replaces that guess with a target.

What a diagnosis actually reads is the pattern of lost marks rather than the total. Method marks gone on questions where the final answer is right point at working and presentation. Marks draining through the last third of a paper point at pacing, which is a different fix entirely. Answers that are factually correct and still score below band point at command terms: describe answered as explain, deduce answered as state. Whole questions untouched, or working that fails at the same step every time, point at genuine content gaps. Those four diagnoses lead to four different plans of four different lengths.

The second document to put on the table is the school's internal deadline list for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and each subject's assessed component. These dates are set by the school rather than by the examination timetable, and they differ between schools sitting the same session. On the east coast, where a small staff coordinates the whole programme, they are also the dates most likely to arrive unannounced. A plan built without them will aim a term of sessions at content revision while an assessed draft quietly goes late, and that is the single most common way tutoring money is wasted in a Diploma year.
bullets: Bring the last two marked scripts, not the report card
Four diagnoses, four plan lengths: method, pacing, command terms, content
Ask the school for its internal deadline list in writing
Expect a written plan naming components after the first session

sections.heading: The first six weeks: rebuilding what is actually missing
paragraphs: Content gaps are the slowest thing to fix and the most satisfying to watch close. The work is unglamorous: find the earliest point in the topic chain where understanding failed, rebuild from there, and resist the temptation to start at the point where the school currently is. A student who cannot rearrange an equation reliably will not be rescued by more practice on the topic that exposed it, and in a Diploma subject the exposed topic is usually three steps downstream of the actual break.

Six weeks is the realistic floor for one substantial gap in one subject, assuming a weekly session and work done between them. That is worth saying plainly because the market tends not to. A family starting in week one of a block should expect the first two sessions to look like going backwards, the middle two to feel slow, and the change to appear in the school's own assessment rather than in how the sessions feel. Judging progress by whether a lesson went well is the least reliable instrument available.

Two practical notes for this phase on the east coast. First, follow the school's teaching order rather than the textbook's, because a student who is behind cannot afford to be learning two sequences at once; that means the tutor needs to know what was covered in class last week. Second, protect the phase from the core. If an Extended Essay draft or an assessed component falls inside these six weeks, the content work has to be shortened rather than squeezed alongside, because a student doing both badly in the same fortnight is the position this whole exercise exists to avoid.

sections.heading: Weeks seven to fourteen: turning what they know into marks
paragraphs: This is the phase families skip, and it is where most of the recoverable marks live. A student who understands the material and still scores below expectation is losing marks in the translation: the question is read wrongly, the command term is answered generically, working is not written down, time is allocated badly across a paper. None of that is content, so no amount of further teaching fixes it. The work is timed questions, marked against the published scheme, with the mark scheme read afterwards line by line.

Reading a mark scheme is a skill in itself and it transfers across subjects. Students are usually astonished by how mechanical the marks are: a point scored for naming a variable, a point for a unit, a point for a comparison word. Once a student has seen three mark schemes for the same style of question, they start writing for the marker rather than for themselves, and the score moves without a single new fact being learned. In the sciences, where Paper 2 extended response carries 44 per cent, this is the highest-return work available in the whole Diploma.

Pacing is handled here too, and it needs real papers under real time. A student who scores well on untimed practice and badly in the hall is not short of knowledge; they are short of a plan for the hour. Working out how long each section may take, deciding in advance what to do when a question will not come, and practising the decision to leave something and come back are all trainable. Eight weeks is a comfortable window for this phase. Four weeks will shift one paper. Two weeks will shift one section, which is still worth having if that section is where the marks are.

sections.heading: The final stretch: what stops and what continues
paragraphs: In the last weeks before the papers, new content stops. This is the hardest instruction to follow and the most reliable one. A student learning a new topic in the final fortnight is spending the scarcest hours of the year on the least secure material, and doing it in place of consolidating the eighty per cent they already half know. The exception is narrow: a single identified topic that carries disproportionate weight and is genuinely absent rather than shaky.

What continues is timed practice, mark scheme reading and the mechanical business of exam logistics. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates, confirm which series and which timetable version applies, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable. For Diploma candidates, confirm dates with the school's coordinator. This page publishes no IB session or results date, because the IB's own assessment pages could not be verified for this project and an unverified exam date on a page like this is worse than no date at all.

The other thing that continues is sleep, and it is not a soft point. Students on this coast with long bus journeys are already losing an hour a day to travel, and families regularly add a late-evening session in the final fortnight that costs more in concentration than it returns in content. In the last two weeks the sensible pattern is shorter sessions, earlier, with a hard stop. If a tutor proposes intensifying in the final week, ask what will be dropped to make room, because something always is.

sections.heading: Starting late: what each remaining window can realistically achieve
paragraphs: A large share of enquiries from this coast arrive with the clock already running, and the useful answer is neither reassurance nor refusal. Each remaining window has a realistic aim, and naming it honestly is what lets a family decide whether the spend is worth it. The pattern below is drawn from how these blocks actually run rather than from what sounds encouraging.

Two principles run through all of it. The shorter the window, the narrower the aim: with a term left the target is a component, with six weeks it is a paper, with a fortnight it is a section. And the shorter the window, the more important it is to drop something. A student with four weeks who adds two sessions a week to an unchanged workload will do everything slightly worse. Deciding what comes off the list is part of the plan, not an afterthought, and it is a conversation for the family rather than the tutor to settle.

One more thing is worth saying for DP1 families reading this with nothing obviously wrong. The cheapest intervention in the whole Diploma is a single diagnostic session in the first term of DP1, when the Extended Essay question is still open, the Higher Level levels can still change, and a content gap can be closed before the course assumes it. Nobody searches for a tutor at that point, which is exactly why the phase is worth mentioning here.

sections.heading: Where the timeline breaks on the east coast
paragraphs: Plans fail for predictable reasons here, and all of them can be scheduled around if they are named in advance. The shortened Ramadan school day changes the whole rhythm for several weeks, and it lands in the part of the year where mocks have just been marked and the papers are close. A late-afternoon slot that worked all year stops working; a session after Iftar usually holds. Agreeing that shift before the month begins rather than during it is the difference between an adjusted plan and three missed weeks.

The second break is the collision of assessed components. Schools set their own internal deadlines, and two of them landing in the same fortnight is common rather than unlucky. A student with the scientific investigation and an Extended Essay draft due together will do both badly unless something gives. The adjustment is to pause content teaching for that fortnight and use the sessions for process coaching on whichever piece carries the most marks, which is a decision that needs the school's deadline list in hand.

The third is travel and the fourth is the school calendar itself. Families on this coast travel in the long breaks, often for extended periods, and the honest options are to continue over video from wherever they are, or to stop cleanly and restart with a short re-diagnosis rather than pretending a six-week gap did not happen. School events, fixtures and club commitments produce the slow version of the same problem: a slot that cannot move gets cancelled, and three cancellations become a lapsed arrangement. Building the ability to shift a lesson inside the week into the agreement at the start is worth more over two years than any difference in hourly rate.

sections.heading: What the timeline costs, stage by stage
paragraphs: Spreading the cost over the sequence makes it easier to judge than an hourly rate does, because the pattern changes as the plan progresses. A diagnostic is one hour. A content block is weekly for six to fourteen weeks. A technique block is often twice weekly for a shorter period. The final stretch is short sessions, more often, for two or three weeks. A family that budgets a flat weekly figure for two years is usually over-buying in the quiet terms and under-buying in the one that matters.

The figures in the table are market rates published by named providers in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. They are given so a family can size the commitment before starting rather than discovering it in month four. For what a specific subject, level and session length would cost, the route is a short consultation followed by one trial session per family at no charge, arranged after that conversation. There is no term block to exit and no package that renews unless somebody asks for it.

It is worth putting the number in context rather than in isolation. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees holding steady does not hold tutoring costs steady, but it does mean a family planning an exam year has one fewer variable. Set the tutoring figure against school fees, exam entry costs for any private-candidate subject, and the travel a visiting arrangement would add, and the comparison usually settles itself.

sections.heading: What stays the student's own work, whatever the deadline
paragraphs: The pressure points in a timeline are exactly where the honesty line gets tested, so it belongs on this page rather than in a footnote. A student two days from an internal deadline with an unfinished draft is the moment a family is most likely to be offered something they should refuse. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, read the criteria with the student, discuss the student's own ideas and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it to completion, or hand over a model to adapt.

The consequence of crossing that line falls on the candidate, not the tutor. An academic-honesty finding is a far worse outcome than a late or weak piece of coursework, and it is not a theoretical risk: one site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright. If the deadline really is tomorrow, the useful help is triage. Work out what can be finished honestly, what has to be submitted incomplete, and what the school needs to be told, and then do that rather than buying a problem.

Materials follow the same rule. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and are referenced and linked at source rather than redistributed as a folder of downloads. A tutor who offers everything is convenient in the short run and is distributing somebody else's copyright. Ask the school which documents it has already provided; on the east coast the answer is often more than the family realised.

process.title: Book the diagnostic before anything else
process.description: One session, worked from the last two marked scripts and the school's internal deadline list. The output is a written statement of what is wrong and roughly how many weeks it will take. Families who act on it themselves and buy nothing further have still had the most useful hour available.

process.title: Fix the end date before the start date
process.description: Agree how long the block runs and what the review point is, which should be the school's next assessment rather than a count of weeks. A block with a stated end makes renewing a decision. An open arrangement renews by default and nobody notices the target has drifted.

process.title: Decide what comes off the list
process.description: Adding sessions to an unchanged week makes everything slightly worse. Before the block starts, settle which commitment pauses, which subject stops getting general revision, and what happens in mock weeks. That conversation belongs to the family; the tutor's job is to say what the plan requires.

process.title: Agree the Ramadan and travel adjustments up front
process.description: Sessions after Iftar hold better than late-afternoon ones, and extended travel is easier handled as a clean pause with a re-diagnosis than as a silent lapse. Both decisions are cheap to make in September and expensive to make in March.

process.title: Review on the marks, then change the aim
process.description: At the review point, the only question is whether marks moved in the component the plan targeted. If they did, continue or stop. If they did not, the aim was wrong and the plan changes rather than the hours increasing. Buying more of a plan that is not working is the commonest mistake in this market.

whyPoints.title: A dated plan, not an open weekly habit
whyPoints.description: Every block has a stated length and a review point set at the school's next assessment. Nothing renews by default. The point of an end date is that it forces somebody to look at whether the marks moved, which an open-ended arrangement never does.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes before the teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session reads marked scripts and internal deadlines rather than opening a textbook. Four different patterns of lost marks lead to four different plans of four different lengths, and guessing between them costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Continuity that weather cannot interrupt
whyPoints.description: Nothing in the arrangement depends on the Hajar road being open or on a two-to-three-hour round trip remaining attractive in February. Slots shift inside the same week at no cost, which over two years is worth more lessons than any hourly discount.

whyPoints.title: Visiting-tuition rates published honestly
whyPoints.description: The in-home option is described with its real market cost, AED 180-500 per hour with travel inside the fee, attributed and dated to October 2026. IB Gram does not sell it in the UAE and says so rather than leaving the question open.

whyPoints.title: No exam date published that could not be verified
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from the boards' own published key dates. No IB session or results date appears, because the IB's assessment pages could not be verified for this project. Confirm Diploma dates with your child's coordinator.

whyPoints.title: Independent, and plain about the limits
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform holding no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority. No school named here is a client, and coursework support never includes producing the work.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to our house in Fujairah for the lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide visiting tuition anywhere in the UAE; that service is offered only in India. Teaching arranged here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Fujairah school day. Visiting tutors do exist on this coast and families do hire them, with published market rates running AED 180-500 per hour because the travel is priced into the lesson. If you go that route, ask to see the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years and which any working tutor has no reason not to hold.

faqs.question: What should the first two weeks of tutoring actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written target, not a feeling. The first session should read the last two marked scripts and the school's internal deadline list and come back with a short document naming which papers or criteria the marks are sitting in, which two or three topics come first and in what order, and when the plan will be reviewed. By the end of the second session you should know roughly how many weeks the gap is likely to take to close. If after two weeks you have warm impressions and no named components, the arrangement is not aimed at anything measurable.

faqs.question: How long does it take to close a content gap in a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Six to fourteen weeks for one substantial gap in one subject, assuming a weekly session with work done between them. The variation depends on how far back the break is: a student whose problem is three steps upstream of the exposed topic takes longer than one with a single missing unit. Expect the first two sessions to feel like going backwards, because rebuilding from the earliest failure point is how this works. Judge it on the school's next assessment rather than on how the lessons feel, which is the least reliable instrument available to a parent.

faqs.question: We are six weeks from the papers. What is realistically achievable?
faqs.answer: One paper's technique, done properly. In six weeks a student can learn to read command terms accurately, write for a mark scheme rather than for themselves, and pace an hour sensibly, and those changes move scores without a single new fact being learned. What is not achievable is new content across a syllabus, and a plan that promises it is selling the wrong thing. Pick the paper with the largest recoverable mark total, work twice a week with marked practice in between, and decide what comes off your child's week to make room, because something has to.

faqs.question: My daughter is in DP1 with no obvious problem. Is this too early to start?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest point in the whole Diploma to do something, which is why almost nobody does. In the first term of DP1 the Extended Essay question is still open, Higher Level levels can still be changed, and a content gap can be closed before the course starts assuming it. A single diagnostic session at that stage often produces a plan a family executes themselves with no further sessions bought. The expensive version of the same conversation happens in DP2, when the levels are fixed, the core is late and the only available lever is intensity.

faqs.question: How much notice does a tutor need before the mock season?
faqs.answer: Three to four weeks to be useful, and the more important point is what happens afterwards. Mocks are the best diagnostic a Diploma year produces, so the valuable work sits in the weeks after the scripts come back rather than the fortnight before they are sat. A sensible arrangement pauses or switches to timed papers during mock week itself, then re-diagnoses from the actual script: which section, which command terms, where the pacing failed. Families who intensify before mocks and then stop have usually bought the less useful half of the opportunity.

faqs.question: What happens to the plan during Ramadan in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: It shifts rather than pauses, and the shift should be agreed before the month starts. The shortened school day changes the whole rhythm, late-afternoon slots stop working well, and sessions after Iftar generally hold better. Shorter sessions more often tend to survive the month better than one long evening. The timing matters because Ramadan falls close to the exam term, so three weeks lost here are three weeks that cannot be recovered later. Deciding the adjustment in advance is the difference between an adapted plan and a lapsed one.

faqs.question: We travel for several weeks in the summer. Should lessons stop or continue?
faqs.answer: Either is fine; drifting is not. Continuing over video from wherever you are works, with the slot moved to suit the new time zone, and suits students with an assessed component in progress. Stopping cleanly also works, provided it is a decision with a restart date and a short re-diagnosis when term begins, because six weeks away from a subject changes where a student is. What causes damage is the silent version: two sessions missed, then a vague intention to resume, then September arriving with the plan untouched and the target now out of date.

faqs.question: How do we know the plan is working before the next school report?
faqs.answer: Ask for marked work rather than progress reports. A session that produces an annotated script is evidence; a session that produces a verbal summary is not. Within a block you should be able to see the same style of question attempted twice, several weeks apart, with the second attempt scoring better against the same scheme. That is a smaller and faster signal than a report card and it is the one a tutor should be providing without being asked. If nothing written is coming home, there is nothing to review at the review point.

faqs.question: What does a visiting tutor on the east coast charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE ran AED 180-500 per hour in October 2026, with travel inside the fee, and advertised monthly packages of four two-hour visiting sessions sat at AED 1,599-1,799. Qualified subject tutors working online were published at AED 150-300, specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium or examiner-experienced tutors at AED 500-650 and above. Those are other providers' figures rather than a price list. On this coast the travel component dominates the visiting rate, because the round trip from the Dubai school belt is two to three hours.

faqs.question: Should we book a term in advance to secure a slot?
faqs.answer: Secure the slot, but be careful what else comes with it. A standing weekly time is genuinely worth holding, particularly for an evening slot on this coast where the usable window is narrow. Paying a term's fees up front is a different thing: it removes the main protection a family has, which is the ability to change a decision cheaply when a match turns out to be wrong. A reasonable arrangement holds the slot, has a stated end date for the block, and does not renew unless somebody asks. Ask what happens if you stop after two sessions.

faqs.question: My son has two assessed components due in the same fortnight. What comes first?
faqs.answer: The one carrying more marks, and the other one gets a reduced, honest submission rather than both being done badly. This collision is common rather than unlucky, because internal deadlines are set by the school and nobody coordinates them against each other. The adjustment is to pause content teaching for that fortnight and use the sessions for process coaching: narrowing the question, reading the criteria, feedback on the student's own draft. Content work squeezed alongside two drafts achieves nothing in any of the three. Getting the school's deadline list in September is what lets you see this coming.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor stay with my child across both Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is worth asking for explicitly at the start rather than assuming. Continuity across DP1 and DP2 means the tutor already knows which topic chain was rebuilt in the first year and does not need to rediagnose, which saves real weeks. What breaks it is more often scheduling than availability: a slot that worked in DP1 collides with a DP2 timetable, and the arrangement lapses rather than moving. Agreeing at the outset that the slot can shift inside the week, and reviewing it at the start of each term, is what keeps a two-year arrangement intact.

faqs.question: What do we do if the marks have not moved after a term?
faqs.answer: Change the aim, not the hours. A term of sessions with no movement in the targeted component means the diagnosis was wrong, the plan was aimed at the wrong thing, or the work between sessions was not happening. Those are three different problems with three different fixes, and buying more sessions addresses none of them. Ask for the marked work from the term and look at whether the same questions improved. A tutor who responds to a flat review by proposing additional weekly hours is answering a commercial question rather than an academic one.

faqs.question: Is there a point in the Diploma where starting is genuinely too late?
faqs.answer: Not quite, but there is a point where the aim has to shrink to one section of one paper. With a fortnight left the honest target is the single section with the largest recoverable mark total, worked in two or three short sessions with everything else protected, including sleep. Anyone proposing a broad programme at that stage is not reading the calendar. No tutor can promise a grade at any stage, and a first conversation that opens with one has told you how the rest of the arrangement will go.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one hour and a date
fujairah/ib-home-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step is small: a diagnostic session worked from the last two marked scripts and the school's internal deadline list, which produces a written target and an honest number of weeks. From there a block has a length, a review point and an end date, and renewing it is a decision rather than a default. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video in Gulf Standard Time; nobody is sent to a Fujairah address, and visiting tuition is offered only in India. IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board approval and names no school as a partner. What it offers is a plan with dates in it.

intro.heading: Two boards, four years, and which term each problem belongs to
paragraphs: The households that search for this phrase in Fujairah are rarely looking for one tutor for one problem. They are managing a sequence. A Year 11 student is three terms from an IGCSE series while an older sibling is halfway through the Diploma, or a single student is about to cross from one board to the other and the family has worked out that nobody has explained what that crossing involves. The question underneath the search is not which tutor is nearest. It is which of the next eight terms each worry actually belongs to.

That sequence is unusually visible on the east coast. Fujairah's private-school set is small, and families here frequently split their children across boards or across emirates for sixth form, which means one household can be working to two sets of term dates, two assessment calendars and two sets of academic conventions at the same time. A parent who has only ever dealt with IGCSE meets the Diploma core in October of Year 12 and discovers that an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge course and a service commitment have all started without anybody sending a letter about it.

Before the map, the honest answer to the home-tutoring part of the search. Visiting tuition on this coast is real and it is priced for the drive: published market bands put visiting one-to-one in the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For a two-child household the arithmetic compounds, because two visiting tutors means two sets of travel, two availability windows and usually two different evenings committed. The first table on this page works that through.

IB Gram delivers to UAE families one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so each child's hour sits in a Fujairah evening. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. For a two-board household that limitation turns out to be less costly than it sounds, because the thing such a household most needs is two correctly matched specialists on one evening rather than two people who happen to be available in the same emirate.

The rest of the page is the sequence. The four-year map from Year 10 to Diploma results, with what each window decides. The IGCSE-to-Diploma gap set out subject by subject rather than as a general warning about rigour. What IGCSE attainment actually suggests about Higher Level, with the check worth running before the choice is made. The Diploma core and its internal deadlines. The handover summer, which almost nobody uses. The scheduling and cost of running two children at once. And the honesty boundaries, which differ between the two boards and matter more under the IB.
