intro.heading: Reading an MYP report before buying anything
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IB MYP tutor in Fujairah have usually just read a report they cannot decode. It shows four letters with numbers beside them, a subject grade between one and seven, and comments about conceptual understanding. There is no percentage, no class rank and no past paper to point at. A parent who did O Levels or CBSE has no reference point for a five in criterion B, and the school's explanation at parents evening lasted four minutes.

That opacity is why MYP help gets bought badly. The common mistakes are to treat the programme as early exam preparation and drill questions that do not exist, to buy general homework supervision that touches none of the criteria, or to wait for the Diploma on the theory that the marks start counting then. The third is the most expensive, because the skills the Diploma assesses - independent investigation, evaluation, reflection - are precisely what the MYP criteria have been marking all along.

The useful work is narrower than parents expect. In most cases one criterion is being lost repeatedly across subjects. A student strong on content who scores well in criterion A and poorly in criterion C in sciences has a data-handling problem, not a knowledge problem, and no amount of revision will move it. Finding that pattern takes one session with three marked tasks in front of a tutor who knows what each criterion rewards.

On the east coast there is a second complication. Fujairah's private-school set is small, so MYP cohorts are small, and a student may go three years without being taught by a specialist in their weakest subject group. Design and Arts are often taught by generalists, mathematics sets are broad, and a child who needs stretching in one subject and rebuilding in another gets the average. That is not a criticism of the schools; it is arithmetic.

IB Gram works with Fujairah families online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which is a service we run only in India, so nothing here should be read as a promise that a tutor appears in Sakamkam on a Tuesday. The practical gain is access: a specialist in the exact subject group, working from your child's own unit plan and task sheet, at an hour that fits the school bus. The rest of this page is written for that decision. It explains how criterion marks become a grade, sets the four realistic responses to a weak report against each other with their costs, names the criteria where marks usually go missing in each subject group, and answers the two questions MYP 4 families on this coast keep asking: whether to finish MYP 5 or move to an IGCSE route, and how to handle the Personal Project year without crossing the academic honesty line.

fujairah/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: The MYP sits in the middle of a three-stage continuum, and the stage either side changes what support is worth buying. A student entering MYP 1 from a primary route has different gaps from one leaving MYP 5 for the Diploma.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no subject-by-subject criterion marking and no formal grade. Students arrive in MYP 1 fluent in asking questions and often unpractised at producing a structured written answer under a time limit. The transition gap is almost always in writing stamina and in handling a task sheet with explicit assessment language on it.
programmes.countryNote: Few Fujairah schools run a full PYP, so most local MYP 1 intakes mix students from a national curriculum, an Indian board and a British primary. Three different starting points in one classroom is the normal condition here, and it is why early MYP reports vary so sharply between neighbours.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each, every criterion marked out of eight against published descriptors. Grade boundaries convert the criterion total into a 1-7 subject grade, which is why two students with the same raw total can sit in different bands. Interdisciplinary units and approaches-to-learning skills are assessed too, and the Personal Project arrives in MYP 5.
programmes.countryNote: In a small Fujairah cohort a student can be the only one in a set needing a particular kind of stretch. That shows up as a stable mediocre grade across several terms rather than as a crisis, which is why east-coast families often start looking in MYP 4 rather than earlier.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment is weighty and deadline-driven, and UAE schools sit the May session. The step from MYP 5 to DP1 is mostly about volume and independence rather than new content, and students who were carried by a teacher in MYP feel it in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma places on this coast are limited, so a Fujairah MYP 5 student may be choosing between a local sixth form, weekly boarding in Sharjah and a British A-Level route. The MYP grades are the evidence those conversations use, which gives MYP 4 and 5 a weight parents often discover late.

programmes.name: The IGCSE alternative to MYP 4-5
programmes.description: Some UAE schools run IGCSE in place of the final two MYP years, trading criterion assessment for external papers and a portable certificate. Cambridge tiers subjects into Core and Extended with capped Core grades; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher in maths. The certificate is externally recognised, which matters for the Ministry of Education equivalency route.
programmes.countryNote: The choice between finishing MYP 5 and moving to an IGCSE route is a live question in Fujairah because families relocate and because some local schools offer only one of the two. It deserves a decision rather than a drift, and it is covered in its own section below.

fujairah/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP help is bought by subject group, and each group has its own four criteria with its own names. These are the groups Fujairah parents ask about most, with what the marking actually rewards in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where confident calculators lose marks: the task wants a general rule, tested and justified, not a correct answer. Students who have never been taught to generalise score a four for years without anyone naming the cause.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is the usual gap: processing data, explaining a trend against theory and evaluating a method. A student can know every fact in the unit and still be stuck at four because nobody taught them to interrogate their own results.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Marks go missing in analysing, where students summarise a text instead of examining how the writer builds meaning. The fix is close reading on short extracts rather than more essays, because the skill is noticing and the volume of writing is not the problem.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. The phase matters more than the age: a student in phase 3 being taught alongside phase 5 peers will read as weak when the real issue is placement. Worth confirming which phase the school has entered your child in.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the criterion that separates grades: it wants evaluation of sources and of different perspectives, with judgement. Students who write accurate description reliably land in the middle band, and they rarely know why.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating. The assessment is of the documented process, so a beautiful final product with a thin design folder scores badly. This is the group most often taught by a non-specialist in a small school, and the one where a few sessions on process documentation change the grade fastest.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. As with Design, the process journal carries marks that the finished piece cannot recover. Students who have been praised for talent are often the ones losing marks, because nobody asked them to document how a decision was reached.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on performance. The written and planning criteria surprise families who assumed this subject sits outside academic reporting. A student with a stable five here usually has a reflection problem, not a fitness one.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.levels: Assessed separately in each MYP year
subjects.description: Assessed on evaluating, synthesising and reflecting across two subject groups. Students who do well in both parent subjects can still score poorly because they treat the unit as two pieces of work rather than one argument that needs both lenses. This is the single most-misunderstood piece of MYP assessment.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Marked on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process journal as evidence. It is the first long independent task most students manage and it rewards honest documentation of difficulty. A tutor's role is to teach the criteria and question the plan; the project, the journal and the report remain the student's own work throughout.

fujairah/ib-myp-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a Fujairah family lives changes which schools are realistic, how large the MYP cohort is likely to be, and what time a session can start. These notes are about those three things.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Where most of the emirate's private-school MYP provision sits. Cohorts are modest, and a single subject group may be taught by one teacher across all five MYP years, which makes a weak match in that subject hard to escape without outside help.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Short school runs and an early finish, so MYP students here can realistically hold a 4.30pm or 5pm slot. Useful for the younger years, where a shorter session twice a week works better than a single long one after a full day.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland, with transport that arrives home later than the school day suggests. A 6pm start holds through the year. For MYP 4 and 5 students carrying the Personal Project alongside subject tasks, a later fixed slot protects the evening rather than fragmenting it.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Students here are spread across several schools, so two MYP 3 neighbours can be working to different unit plans and different interdisciplinary pairings. Any support has to follow the school's own task sheet, which is why we ask for it before the first session.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: South along the coast, where the school journey is long enough that fatigue is a genuine variable in the evening. Shorter, more frequent sessions work better here than a ninety-minute block, particularly for MYP 1 and 2.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: At the top of the coast, where neighbouring Dibba Al-Hisn is Sharjah territory and its schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Families comparing MYP provision across that line are comparing two different regulators as well as two schools.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Small coastal communities whose students travel for school. For MYP families the practical question is how much of the evening survives the journey, because MYP tasks are produced at home over several days rather than crammed before a paper.

schoolClusters.note: Private schools inside the emirate are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Curriculum provision on this coast leans British and Indian, so full MYP continuum places are limited and some families run an MYP-style middle school into an IGCSE Year 10 instead.

fujairah/ib-myp-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of working on MYP subjects, each aimed at a different problem. All of them run live online, one-to-one, at a time that fits the east-coast school run.

modes.title: Criterion diagnostic
modes.description: One session with three marked MYP tasks from different subjects in front of the tutor. The purpose is to find the criterion being lost repeatedly rather than to teach content. It ends with a written note naming the criterion, the type of task where it shows, and what practice will move it.

modes.title: Unit-paced support through the term
modes.description: A fortnightly or weekly slot that follows the school's own unit plan, working on the task that is actually due. The tutor teaches the criterion the task is assessed against, questions the student's plan, and responds to drafts the student has produced. Content gaps are filled as they surface rather than pre-taught.

Built around the specific subjects chosen, with the gap between MYP marking and external papers made explicit.

sections.heading: What an MYP report is actually telling you
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of eight against published descriptors. The criterion names differ by subject group, which is where most of the confusion comes from: criterion B in mathematics is investigating patterns, in sciences it is inquiring and designing, and in language and literature it is organising. A parent who learns what B means in one subject and applies it to another will draw the wrong conclusion.

The four criterion levels are added and converted to a subject grade from one to seven using published boundaries. Two consequences follow. First, the grade hides the shape of the performance: a student at seven, seven, three, six has a very different problem from one at six, five, six, six, and both can land on the same number. Second, movement in one weak criterion shifts the grade more than broad improvement does, which makes the diagnosis worth more than extra generic practice.

So the first question to ask the school is not how your child is doing but which criterion has been lowest for the longest, in which subjects. Schools hold that data in the gradebook even when the report does not show it. Three marked tasks with the task sheets attached will usually reveal the same pattern without anyone having to ask. That is the material a first session should work from, and it is more useful than any diagnostic test a tutor could invent. A school that cannot produce the criterion history is telling you something worth knowing as well.

sections.heading: The three alternatives Fujairah parents weigh against MYP tutoring
paragraphs: Almost every family searching for an IB MYP tutor in Fujairah is choosing between four courses of action, and three of them cost nothing to start. The first is to wait for the Diploma, on the theory that MYP grades do not count. The second is to ask the school for intervention, which is free, informed and limited by the staffing the school has. The third is to buy exam-style drilling of the kind that works at IGCSE, which is the most common wasted spend in the programme. The fourth is criterion-led one-to-one work.

Waiting is the costliest of the three free options, and not because the grades matter in themselves. The MYP marks the skills the Diploma then assesses under time pressure: investigation, evaluation, reflection, documentation. A student who reaches DP1 having never been taught to evaluate a method does not have a two-year problem to fix, they have a first-term crisis. School intervention is genuinely worth asking for first, and on a small coast it is sometimes limited to the one teacher who already teaches the subject.

Drilling is the one to be suspicious of. In MYP 1 to 3 there is no external paper to practise for, so question drills deliver a false sense of progress, and in MYP 4 and 5 the internal examinations are still marked against criteria. A tutor who opens with a past paper has misread the programme. The table below sets the four options against what each one actually changes.

sections.heading: Criterion by criterion: where MYP marks go missing
paragraphs: In sciences, the reliable gap is processing and evaluating. Students present data accurately, state what happened, and stop. The descriptors want the trend interpreted against the underlying theory, the method criticised with specific reference to what it could not control, and improvements that are more than a longer repeat. That is a teachable move set, and it is usually three or four sessions of work with the student's own practical reports rather than a term of content revision.

In mathematics, investigating patterns is the equivalent. The task asks for a general rule, justified and tested on a case that was not used to build it. A student who finds the pattern and writes it down without justification is capped by the descriptors whatever their arithmetic is like. In language and literature, the recurring loss is in analysing: summarising what a text says rather than examining how the writer produces an effect, which feels like diligence and marks like a four.

In Individuals and Societies, thinking critically is where grades separate, because evaluation and perspective require a judgement the student is often reluctant to make. In Design and Arts, the marks sit in the documented process, so students with real ability score below their work. The common thread is that none of these is a content weakness, which is exactly why extra content teaching leaves the grade where it was. A parent can test this cheaply: ask the student to explain, in their own words, what the weak criterion is asking for. A student who cannot say it has not been taught it, however much of the syllabus they can recite back.

sections.heading: MYP 4 and 5, or a move to IGCSE: deciding rather than drifting
paragraphs: Some UAE schools run the final two MYP years as published, and some substitute IGCSE in Years 10 and 11 while keeping the MYP framework below. In Fujairah, where provision is limited, a family may have the choice made for them by which school has a place. Where there is a choice, it is worth making it deliberately in MYP 3, because transferring mid-course costs a term of settling in whichever direction it goes.

The arguments are not evenly matched across purposes. IGCSE produces an external certificate that is portable, recognised, and relevant to the Ministry of Education equivalency route: the published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. MYP 5 completion is internally assessed and continuum-facing, and the equivalency position for the IB route should be checked on the Ministry's own channel rather than taken from any tutoring site, including this one.

Against that, the MYP route keeps the student inside the assessment language the Diploma will use, which is a real advantage for a child going on to DP1 at the same school. The decision therefore turns on two things: whether the family expects to stay through sixth form, and whether the local school can staff the subjects the student wants at Higher Level. Both questions belong in a meeting with the school, not in a brochure.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process journal as the evidence base. Students consistently misread it as a product assessment and pour their effort into the artefact while keeping a thin, retrospective journal. Marks follow the documented process, so a modest outcome with an honest, detailed record of decisions and setbacks will outscore an impressive outcome with nothing behind it.

This is also the point where outside help is most easily misused. The IB's academic honesty rules make the student responsible for their own work, and a project that shows an adult's hand is a malpractice risk for the student rather than an advantage. Nobody at IB Gram supplies project text, journal entries or report sections, and we do not edit a student's submission into shape. What a tutor can legitimately do is teach the criteria, question whether the plan is achievable, probe a reflection that has gone shallow, and respond to what the student has already drafted.

In practice the most valuable sessions are early. A plan with a clear goal, a defined set of criteria for success and a realistic timeline makes the rest of the project self-documenting. A supervisor at school holds the formal relationship and sets the internal deadlines, and a tutor should be asking what the supervisor has said rather than competing with it. If a project is already late and the temptation is to have someone else carry it over the line, the honest answer is that the mark for a thin project is survivable and a malpractice finding is not.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units and the skills no timetable owns
paragraphs: Each MYP year includes at least one interdisciplinary unit, assessed on evaluating, synthesising and reflecting across two subject groups. Students who are comfortable in both parent subjects routinely underperform here, because they produce two parallel pieces of work rather than one argument that genuinely needs both disciplines. The criterion rewards the synthesis itself: what the second lens showed that the first could not.

Approaches to learning sit in the same category of unowned skills. Research, self-management, communication and thinking skills are explicitly part of the programme and are reported on in most schools, but they belong to no single teacher's scheme of work. A student who cannot plan a two-week task or take usable notes loses marks across every subject group simultaneously, and the pattern reads as general weakness when it is actually one fixable habit.

These are good targets for outside work precisely because they fall between departments. Note-taking that produces something usable a week later, a planning routine for a multi-stage task, and a method for checking a draft against a task sheet are all teachable in a handful of sessions, and they transfer to the Diploma intact. A small cohort school cannot easily timetable them; an individual session can do nothing else. The test of whether the work has landed is also unusually simple. Ask the student to show you their plan for the next long task before they start it, and ask again a week later whether the plan survived contact with the work. A student who can answer both questions has the self-management the Diploma will assume, and one who cannot will lose marks in DP1 for reasons no subject tutor can diagnose.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: UAE private schools teach the mandatory national subjects whatever international curriculum they are licensed for. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA's published requirements go further: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for the two groups strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Those requirements shape the timetable your MYP child actually sits. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For a student in MYP 4 carrying eight subject groups plus Arabic and Islamic Education, the practical effect is that the week is full before any homework is set, and an evening tuition slot competes with real fatigue.

For tutoring there are two consequences. Arabic support is examination and technique work in Arabic, not conversational practice, and it is streamed by whether the student is a first-language or additional-language learner. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is not allowed, so support means teaching the school's own material better rather than importing a parallel course. Fujairah schools answer to the federal Ministry of Education, so their published requirements are the reference point rather than KHDA's.
bullets: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the MYP by regulation

sections.heading: Building the bridge from a small cohort to DP1
paragraphs: The gap between MYP 5 and DP1 is not mainly about content. It is volume, independence and the fact that internal assessment deadlines arrive while new teaching continues. A student in a cohort of eight has often been carried by proximity: the teacher noticed the unfinished task, the deadline moved, the conversation happened in the corridor. In DP1 the same student meets a schedule that assumes they manage themselves, and the first set of grades can be a shock to a family who saw sixes throughout MYP.

Two pieces of work in the final MYP term reduce that. The first is written volume under time, because MYP tasks are produced over days and Diploma papers are not. The second is a working method for a long task with stages - the thing the Personal Project was supposed to teach, applied to a subject. Where the student is heading for a Higher Level subject the local school cannot staff deeply, the third piece is simply starting with a specialist early enough that DP1 is not the introduction.

This is where distance stops mattering and the subject pool starts to. A Fujairah student who wants Chemistry at Higher Level, or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, needs a tutor who has taught that course rather than one who lives nearby. Online matching makes that available on a Tuesday evening at Gulf Standard Time, and the same tutor can usually continue through DP1 and DP2, which is worth more than any single term of support.

process.title: Send three marked MYP tasks and their task sheets
process.description: Not a report summary: the actual marked work, with the criterion breakdown and the task sheet that came with each piece. Three tasks from different subjects is enough for a pattern to show. Say which year group your child is in and which subjects the school is worried about.

process.title: Free trial session that names a criterion
process.description: One hour online, at a time that fits the school bus. The tutor reads the marked work, teaches against the weakest criterion for most of the session, and finishes by naming it and the kind of task where it shows. Booked without card details, one per student.

process.title: A short written plan with a number of weeks
process.description: You receive a note saying which criterion is being targeted, what practice moves it, and roughly how many weeks to expect before marked work shows the change. Where the honest answer is that the school is already on it, the plan says that and nothing further is spent.

process.title: Fortnightly or weekly slot built around school tasks
process.description: Sessions follow the school's unit plan and the task that is actually due, rather than a parallel syllabus. The same tutor stays with the subject so the criterion work accumulates. Slots move permanently when transport times or Ramadan hours change the evening.

process.title: Reviewed on the school's own marking
process.description: Progress is read from the next marked task, not from how the sessions felt. If two cycles of school marking show no movement, the approach changes or the match changes. Families say so early; a term spent being polite about a poor fit is a term the MYP does not give back.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject group and criterion
whyPoints.description: A request for MYP science help is answered by someone who can teach processing and evaluating specifically, with your child's own practical reports in front of them. In a small Fujairah cohort that specificity is the thing the school finds hardest to supply, whatever the quality of its teaching.

whyPoints.title: Works from the school's task sheet
whyPoints.description: Sessions use the unit plan, the task and the criterion descriptors the school issued, because MYP work is only assessable against those. Importing a generic course produces a student who is busy and a grade that does not move.

whyPoints.title: No exam drilling where there is no exam
whyPoints.description: MYP 1 to 3 has no external paper, and MYP 4 and 5 internal examinations are still criterion-marked. Past-paper drilling is the most common waste of money in this programme, and a tutor who opens with one has misread what is being assessed.

whyPoints.title: Honest boundaries on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: The project, the journal and the report stay the student's own throughout. A tutor teaches the criteria, questions the plan and responds to drafts. That boundary is what makes the help safe to use under the IB's academic honesty rules, and it is a real difference from the essay services in these results.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the east coast
whyPoints.description: Transport from inland and northern districts arrives later than a Dubai timetable assumes, the week is already full of mandatory subjects, and Ramadan moves the evening. Slots are chosen so they hold for the year rather than for October, and they can be moved permanently.

whyPoints.title: The same tutor can continue into DP1
whyPoints.description: A match made in MYP 4 for a subject the student intends to take at Higher Level can carry through the transition and into the Diploma. Continuity is worth more than any single term of support, particularly where the local school has limited depth in that subject.

faqs.question: How is a 1-7 MYP subject grade worked out from criteria marked out of eight?
faqs.answer: Each of the four criteria is marked out of eight against published descriptors, the four levels are added to give a total out of 32, and published grade boundaries convert that total into a subject grade from one to seven. Two students with the same grade can have very different profiles, which is why the grade alone is a poor guide to what needs fixing. Ask the school which criterion has been lowest for the longest. Moving one persistently weak criterion usually shifts the grade more than broad improvement across all four.

faqs.question: What does criterion C in MYP sciences actually measure?
faqs.answer: Processing and evaluating. The descriptors want data presented correctly, the trend interpreted against the underlying science, the method criticised with specific reference to what it failed to control, and improvements that go beyond repeating the experiment more times. Most students stop after describing what happened, which caps them in the middle bands however well they know the content. It is a teachable set of moves, and three or four sessions working through the student's own practical reports normally changes the quality of the write-up visibly.

faqs.question: Is the MYP weaker preparation for external exams than an IGCSE route?
faqs.answer: For timed-paper stamina, yes, and that is a real gap worth planning for. MYP tasks are produced over days against criteria, so students arrive at external examinations with less practice at writing fast under pressure. What the MYP builds instead is investigation, evaluation and reflection, which is precisely what Diploma internal assessment demands. Families who finish MYP 5 and then meet external papers should budget a term for timed work; families who take the IGCSE route should expect to build investigation skills later, in DP1.

faqs.question: Should a Fujairah student stay in MYP 4-5 or transfer to an IGCSE school?
faqs.answer: Decide it in MYP 3, because a mid-course transfer costs a term either way. IGCSE gives an externally examined, portable certificate relevant to the published Ministry of Education British-track equivalency rule of five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Finishing MYP keeps your child inside the assessment language the Diploma uses, which helps if they are staying for sixth form at the same school. The deciding questions are usually whether your posting is secure and whether the local school can staff the Higher Level subjects your child wants.

faqs.question: Our Fujairah school runs MYP without eAssessment. Does that matter later?
faqs.answer: It matters for documentation rather than for learning. Without eAssessment the MYP produces school-reported outcomes rather than an externally examined certificate, so a receiving school or an attestation process has less external evidence to read. For the Ministry of Education equivalency route, check the Ministry's own current guidance for the IB rather than relying on any tutoring provider, including this page: the published figures we can source cover the British and American tracks, not the IB. Ask the school directly what documentation a transfer out would carry.

faqs.question: Who inspects private schools in Fujairah and where is the report published?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Fujairah, along with Ajman and Umm Al Quwain, so you will not find a KHDA report for a Fujairah school. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge. If you are comparing a Fujairah school with one in Khor Fakkan or Dibba Al-Hisn, you are comparing two regulators. Ask each school directly for its most recent published judgement.

faqs.question: My daughter's MYP maths grade fell from six to four in one term. What causes that?
faqs.answer: Most often a shift in which criteria the unit assessed rather than a loss of ability. A unit weighted towards investigating patterns will expose a student who has never been taught to state and justify a general rule, even one whose calculation is reliable. Ask for the criterion breakdown on the two reports and compare them side by side. If criterion B dropped while A held, the problem is generalisation and justification, and that is a narrow fix rather than a rebuild of the year's content.

faqs.question: Can an MYP tutor work from my child's own school unit plans?
faqs.answer: That is the only sensible way to do it. MYP work is assessed against the task sheet and criterion descriptors the school issues, so a session that teaches a parallel syllabus produces a busy student and an unchanged grade. Send the unit plan, the task sheet and the last marked piece before the first session. A tutor should be asking what the teacher's feedback said and what the internal deadline is, then working behind the school rather than alongside it in competition.

faqs.question: Where does a tutor fit alongside the school's Personal Project supervisor?
faqs.answer: Behind them. The supervisor holds the formal relationship, sets the internal checkpoints and signs off the process, and a tutor should be asking what the supervisor has already said. Legitimate outside help means teaching the three criteria, testing whether the goal and success criteria are achievable, and probing reflections that have gone shallow. It does not mean supplying text, journal entries or report sections: the project must be the student's own throughout, and work showing an adult's hand is a malpractice risk for the student.

faqs.question: How much timetable time do the mandatory UAE subjects take from MYP options?
faqs.answer: Enough to notice. UAE private schools teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's published requirements calculate the time in 40-minute lesson units, advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. For an MYP 4 student carrying eight subject groups, the week is effectively full before homework. That is worth remembering when choosing a tuition slot: the later time that always works beats the earlier one that works until the first assessment week.

faqs.question: What is an interdisciplinary unit and why does my child find it harder?
faqs.answer: It is a unit assessed across two subject groups on evaluating, synthesising and reflecting. Students who are strong in both parent subjects often score poorly because they submit two parallel pieces of work instead of a single argument that needed both lenses. The mark rewards the synthesis: what the second discipline revealed that the first could not. It is one of the most teachable things in the programme, and one of the least explained, so it is worth asking the school which units are coming.

faqs.question: How long does work on one MYP criterion take to show in marked work?
faqs.answer: Usually two cycles of school assessment, which on a typical unit calendar is six to ten weeks. That is the honest answer rather than a promise: criterion marks move when the student produces a task differently, and the next task has to arrive before anyone can see it. What should be visible much earlier is the student explaining what the criterion wants in their own words. If that has not happened after three or four sessions, the approach needs changing rather than extending.

faqs.question: Is one-to-one online teaching suitable for an eleven-year-old in MYP 1?
faqs.answer: Yes, with two conditions. Keep the sessions short - forty-five minutes is usually better than an hour at that age - and keep a parent within earshot for the first few, which also tells you whether the tutor is actually teaching. Younger students do well on a shared screen because the work stays visible and can be revisited, and the written note afterwards gives a parent something concrete. What does not work at any age is a long passive session at the end of a long school day.

faqs.question: We may leave Fujairah before DP1. Does MYP work transfer to another school?
faqs.answer: The learning does; the documentation depends on both schools. MYP outcomes are school-reported unless the school offers eAssessment, so a receiving school will usually place your child on its own assessment rather than on the previous report. Ask the current school what records a transfer would carry and ask the receiving school how it places mid-course arrivals. For families whose posting may end, this is the strongest argument for an externally examined route, and it is a decision worth settling before Year 10 choices are locked.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost on the east coast compared with exam-year help?
faqs.answer: The market does not discount by programme, so the same published bands apply: budget and generalist online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online from about AED 150 to 300, and in-home visits from AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in. Those figures come from provider pricing and a published 2026 Dubai rate survey and are market rates, not ours. MYP families usually need fewer hours than exam-year families, because the work is a diagnosis followed by targeted practice rather than a revision programme.

fujairah/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Find the criterion first, then buy the teaching
fujairah/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step costs nothing: pull three marked MYP tasks with their task sheets and ask the school which criterion has been lowest for the longest. Bring that to a free trial lesson and an hour is usually enough to name the pattern and say how many weeks of work it needs. From MYP 1 through the Personal Project year, sessions run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, working from your child's own unit plans. Where a match is made for a subject your child intends to carry into the Diploma, the same tutor can stay with it through the transition.

fujairah/ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Tutors here work in one subject at one level, with a document camera or second device pointed at the student's page so working is visible as it is written. Matching is done on the subject and level your child is registered for rather than on who is closest to the east coast.

intro.heading: The hour itself, and the record it leaves behind
paragraphs: Parents on this coast have usually settled the question of whether to teach remotely before they arrive at a page like this. The Hajar mountains put the Dubai school belt two to three hours away by road, the emirate's Diploma cohorts are small, and a subject specialist is not going to appear in Qidfa because somebody wished for one. What remains unanswered is mechanical. What does the hour actually contain? How does a tutor see a student's algebra? What happens to a practical subject? And how would a parent who is not in the room know whether anything useful happened?

Those questions deserve concrete answers rather than reassurance, because the honest version is more persuasive. A session runs on a shared whiteboard with two video feeds: one on the student's face and one, from a phone on a stand or a second device, pointed at the page they are writing on. The tutor can see working appear, which is better than seeing a finished answer, because almost all diagnosable error in a Diploma subject lives in the middle steps. Files are annotated live and saved. Past papers are photographed, marked against the published scheme, and returned with the scheme alongside the script.

The second half of the question is evidence, and it is where remote teaching has an advantage nobody advertises. A visiting lesson produces a conversation; a video session produces artefacts. An annotated script, a saved whiteboard, a short note naming what was covered and what was set. Over a term those accumulate into something a parent can actually read, which means a review point can be based on marked work rather than on an impression. This page is organised around that: the mechanics first, then the term-by-term evidence a plan should produce across the two Diploma years.

What remote delivery does not do also belongs here, stated plainly. It does not supply motivation to a student who will not work between sessions. It does not substitute for a laboratory where a school's own practical programme is genuinely absent, though it handles the assessed components better than most parents expect. It does not make a weak diagnosis into a good one. And it does not solve the problem of a subject nobody in the UAE teaches at a workable hour, which happens and is disclosed rather than concealed.

One statement of fact to clear the ground. Tuition arranged through IB Gram is one-to-one and delivered live over video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Fujairah address; visiting tuition is offered only in India. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority. Everything below describes how the online format works in practice for a household on the east coast, with the equipment, the timings and the limits set out.

fujairah/ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Each programme makes different demands on a remote session: some need a visible page, some need a document on screen, some need an unscripted spoken exchange. These are the four that matter on the east coast, described by what the format has to support.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most demanding programme to teach remotely and the one it suits best, because the work is written. Papers are marked against published schemes, extended responses are annotated on screen, and the internally assessed components are drafted in documents the student shares. The only component needing special handling is the spoken one, which needs an unscripted exchange rather than a presentation.
programmes.countryNote: For a Fujairah student the format is frequently the only route to a Higher Level specialist, since the emirate's cohorts are small enough that one teacher may cover a whole science faculty. The practical gain is a tutor who has marked that subject's Paper 2 repeatedly rather than a generalist who has read the syllabus.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, with no external papers in most schools. Remote work here is mostly about structure: reading the criteria, planning written tasks, and coaching the Personal Project, which is the first long self-managed piece a student produces. Shorter sessions suit this age group better than a full hour.
programmes.countryNote: East-coast MYP students at a continuum campus often need help bridging into an IGCSE cohort or into the Diploma. Over video that bridging work is straightforward, because it is document-based: comparing what the receiving course assumes against what the student has actually been assessed on.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Handled through past papers almost entirely, which makes it well suited to the format. Papers are photographed, marked against the published scheme and returned annotated. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable, so the correct timetable version is confirmed early rather than assumed.
programmes.countryNote: For the March 2027 series Cambridge published final entries as due 27 November 2026, the exam period as 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades as due 27 February 2027 and results to centres on Direct on 13 May. Ask the school which zone and which series apply before planning the final weeks.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Examined in a May or June window and again in November, which gives a second attempt inside one academic year. Some subjects are modular, which changes how a two-year plan is sequenced. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should work from the board's live timetable rather than a restatement, including this one. On the east coast the November window matters because repeating a year is rarely practical when school choice is limited.

fujairah/ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects east-coast families ask about, described by what the remote format has to handle in each. The mechanics differ more between subjects than parents expect.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The clearest case for a second camera on the page. Diagnosis lives in the middle steps of an algebraic manipulation, not the final answer, so the tutor watches working appear rather than reviewing it afterwards. Paper 3 at Higher Level needs long investigations worked live, with the student writing and the tutor annotating alongside.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-heavy, which suits screen sharing: the student drives the graphing software while the tutor watches and questions the interpretation. The recurring fix is writing a sentence that says what a result means, which is easier to enforce in a shared document than on paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanisms are drawn on the shared whiteboard, which works better than paper because arrows can be moved and redrawn. The scientific investigation is handled through real data sets the student collects at school, with the tutor working on research design, uncertainty treatment and evaluation rather than the laboratory session itself.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Circuits and fields are diagram problems, so both parties draw on the same canvas. Apparatus description for the written practical questions is taught by walking through real set-ups in photographs and schematics, which is how the papers test it in any case rather than through live handling.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Almost entirely a writing subject at assessment, which makes it the easiest to teach remotely and the easiest to teach badly. The productive work is annotating extended responses against the published scheme and practising data-analysis items, not re-explaining content the student has already read twice.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are drawn live and corrected as they are drawn, which is the fastest way to fix a curve shifted in the wrong direction. Higher Level Paper 3 quantitative work needs the second camera on the page, because the marks are in the steps rather than the figure at the end.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Document-based and well suited to the format. The assessed research project is coached in the student's own shared file, with comments left in the margin on a draft the student wrote. The commonest fix is narrowing a research question that cannot be answered inside the word limit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen text analysis works well on a shared screen, with the text annotated jointly in real time. The Individual Oral needs something else entirely: an unscripted spoken exchange, practised with interruption, which is one of the few components where the camera on the face matters more than the one on the page.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive skills improve with frequency rather than intensity, so shorter and more regular sessions beat long ones. Speaking practice is the part the format handles most naturally, because an audio-visual exchange is exactly what the assessment asks for.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Entirely document work: criteria read line by line, a research question narrowed until it can be answered in the word limit, and comments left on a draft the student has written. Nothing is written or completed on the student's behalf, and that limit is stated before the first session.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: Required study alongside the licensed curriculum
subjects.description: Runs in parallel with the international programme, with first-language and additional-language streams taught separately and the language of instruction differing between streams. Remote support focuses on written structure and assessment language rather than supplying alternative material, which is not permitted without ministry approval.

fujairah/ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: What changes between Fujairah's districts, for a remote arrangement, is the household rather than the distance: where a student can sit, how reliable the connection is, and what time the house is quiet. These are the practical notes from each.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Apartment living is common, so the usual question is where a student can sit with a door that closes. A corner with a wall behind the camera and a desk lamp in front of the page solves most of what parents worry about here.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal households with activities running late. The reliable pattern is a slightly later start and a hard stop, rather than an earlier slot that gets abandoned when a fixture overruns twice in a row.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Mixed-curriculum intake and mostly villa households, which usually means a quiet room is available. The constraint is more often shared devices between siblings than bandwidth, which back-to-back slots solve neatly.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Families here frequently have children in two year groups. Consecutive sessions on one device work provided the second student is sitting down before the first finishes, which a visiting arrangement cannot replicate without paying twice for travel.

regions.name: Madhab and Al Gurfa
regions.note: Posted families arriving mid-year, often with a laptop already set up for a previous school's platform. Nothing specialised is needed: a browser, a stable connection and a phone on a stand pointed at the page.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: An hour up the coast with late school-bus arrivals, so the first workable slot is usually after five. The format's value here is simply that the lesson does not depend on anyone making that drive in either direction.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Long gaps between settlements on the northern coast road and no local Diploma specialist in any subject. Connection quality is the only variable worth checking in advance, and a mobile hotspot is a workable fallback.

regions.name: Masafi and the inland route
regions.note: On the road west, where heavy rain closes the route. For a remote arrangement the weather is a non-event, which is the clearest single contrast with a visiting tutor on this coast.

modes.description: The standard hour. Two video feeds, a shared whiteboard both parties can write on, and the subject's own materials open on screen. Working is watched as it is produced rather than reviewed afterwards, which is where the diagnosis in a Diploma subject actually comes from.

sections.heading: A one-to-one online session, minute by minute
paragraphs: The first five minutes are not teaching. They are the student saying what happened in class since the last session and what they could not do in the homework, and the tutor opening the piece of marked work that came in between. This is deliberately unglamorous and it is the part that keeps a plan aimed at something, because the school's teaching order changes and a plan built in September is out of date by November if nobody checks.

The next thirty-five minutes are the work, and what it looks like depends on the subject. In mathematics the student writes while the tutor watches the page through the second camera, interrupting at the step where the error occurs rather than at the end. In a science the shared whiteboard carries the diagram and both parties draw on it. In an essay subject the text sits on screen and is annotated jointly, sentence by sentence. In every case the student is producing and the tutor is reading production, which is the opposite of a lecture and the reason an hour of this is tiring.

The final ten minutes set the work for the week and write it down. One timed section, under real conditions, to be photographed and sent in. The whiteboard is saved and shared. A short note goes out naming what was covered, what was set and what the next session will open with. That note is worth more than it sounds: it is what lets a parent see the shape of a term without sitting in a single lesson, and it is what makes a review point a reading exercise rather than a conversation about impressions.

sections.heading: The kit and the connection a Fujairah household actually needs
paragraphs: Less than families assume, and the list has not changed much in several years. A laptop or desktop with a browser is the primary device, because a full-size screen is needed for a shared document and a tablet keyboard is not adequate for extended writing. A phone on a cheap stand provides the second camera pointed at the page. Headphones with a microphone remove most of the audio problems before they start. That is the whole of it.

Bandwidth is the thing people worry about and it is rarely the binding constraint. Two video streams and a shared canvas run comfortably on a few megabits of upload; what causes trouble is not total speed but contention, which is several people in a household streaming at the same hour. A mobile hotspot is a serviceable fallback and worth testing once in advance rather than discovering during a session. For households in Qidfa, Mirbah or along the northern coast road, that single test is the one preparation genuinely worth doing.

The room matters more than the equipment. A student needs a surface they can write on, a light in front of the page rather than behind the screen, and a door that closes, or failing that a corner facing away from the household. Siblings sharing one device is common in Fujairah households and is handled by scheduling back to back rather than by buying hardware. If something in this list is not available, say so before the first session; it changes how the hour is structured rather than whether it can happen.

sections.heading: Four things people assume remote teaching cannot do
paragraphs: Each of these comes up in nearly every first conversation with a family on this coast, and each has a specific answer rather than a reassurance. They are worth taking seriously because two of them are partly true, and knowing which two is more useful than being told everything works equally well.

The two that are largely solved are handwritten working and past-paper marking. Working is visible through the second camera, in real time, which is actually better than a visiting tutor reading a completed page, because the tutor sees the step where the student hesitated. Marking is stronger remotely than most families expect: a photographed script annotated against the published scheme and returned with the scheme attached is a more durable artefact than verbal feedback delivered across a kitchen table and forgotten by Thursday.

The two that need real handling are practical science and spoken assessment. Practical science has its own section below. Spoken components, such as the Individual Oral in English A or the oral in a language subject, need an unscripted exchange with interruption, and they need the camera on the face rather than the page. Both are achievable, but they need to be planned for rather than assumed, and a family should ask how a tutor handles them rather than taking a general answer about technology.

The fifth objection is the one parents raise last and worry about most, which is attention. A well-run session is harder to drift through than a classroom lesson, because the student is writing and being questioned continuously rather than listening to an explanation. Where attention is genuinely the constraint, the fix is structural: a shorter session, two blocks instead of one, a device with notifications switched off. None of that is a concession about the format. It is the same adjustment a good teacher makes in a room.

sections.heading: Practical science without standing in the laboratory
paragraphs: This objection deserves a straight answer because it is the one with real substance. A remote tutor cannot run a titration with your child. What they can do is the part that carries the marks, and it is worth being precise about where those marks actually sit. In the Diploma's scientific investigation, research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks. None of those is awarded for handling apparatus. They are awarded for a research question that can be answered, variables genuinely controlled rather than merely listed, data processed with uncertainties, and an evaluation naming this method's real weakness rather than generic human error.

The written papers work the same way. Practical skills in Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE sciences, and in the Diploma's Paper 1 data section, are examined in writing: describe the apparatus, identify the variable, read the graph, explain the anomaly. A student who has done the experiment at school and cannot write about it loses those marks, and that gap is a writing problem taught on photographs, schematics and real data sets. The laboratory time comes from the school, which is where it should come from.

The honest limit is this. If a school's own practical programme is thin, remote tuition will not replace it, and no tutor should claim otherwise. What it will do is make sure that whatever practical work the student does get is converted into marks: data recorded properly, uncertainties handled, the investigation designed before the first measurement rather than written up afterwards. On the east coast, where a single teacher may cover three sciences, that conversion is frequently where the recoverable marks are.

sections.heading: Term by term across DP1 and DP2, and the evidence each term should leave
paragraphs: A two-year plan is easier to judge if you know what each term is supposed to produce. The pattern below is how these arrangements actually run rather than an idealised schedule, and the useful column is the third one: what a parent should be able to see without attending a lesson. If a term goes by and nothing in that column has arrived, the arrangement is drifting regardless of how the sessions felt.

Two notes on the calendar itself. The Diploma's internally assessed components and core deadlines are set by the school rather than the board, and they differ between schools sitting the same session, so the term plan starts from the school's own list. And no IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page: the IB's assessment pages could not be verified for this project, so dates must be confirmed with your child's Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates quoted elsewhere here come from the boards' own published key dates and should still be checked against the live timetable.

The last column is deliberately blunt. A red flag is not a reason to end an arrangement on its own, but it is a reason to ask a direct question at the review point. Most arrangements that fail on this coast do not fail dramatically; they drift, the aim goes stale, and a year passes with pleasant sessions and unchanged component scores. The point of writing down what each term should produce is to make that drift visible early enough to correct.

A revised plan written after the mock, naming different targets
The pre-mock plan continuing unchanged after the scripts came back
No new content; one or two components, pacing, mark scheme reading
Short sessions, more often, with a clear statement of what was dropped
New topics being introduced in the last fortnight

sections.heading: Evidence instead of reassurance
paragraphs: The hardest thing for a parent who does not teach the subject is knowing whether the money is doing anything. School reports arrive too infrequently to steer by, and the feel of a session is a poor signal: a warm, organised adult produces a pleasant hour whether or not the component scores are moving. What works instead is a small, boring discipline of artefacts, and the remote format produces them almost automatically.

Three things are enough. An annotated piece of the student's own work after most sessions. A short written note naming what was covered and what was set. And, across a block, the same style of question attempted twice several weeks apart, marked against the same scheme, so improvement is visible as a number rather than as an impression. None of that requires a parent to understand the subject. It requires them to read four short documents a month and ask one question at the review point.

This is also the answer to a question families ask delicately, which is how they would know if a tutor were coasting. A coasting arrangement produces no artefacts. The sessions happen, the student says they were fine, and there is nothing to read. That is not evidence of bad faith, but it is evidence that nothing is being measured, and an unmeasured plan has no mechanism for noticing that it is aimed at the wrong thing. Ask for the artefacts at the start, as a normal part of the arrangement rather than as a challenge.

sections.heading: Fitting a session into the east-coast week
paragraphs: Scheduling is where remote arrangements on this coast succeed or quietly fail. The Fujairah school day ends in the early afternoon, buses from the outlying districts arrive later, clubs and fixtures run on, prayer timings shape the evening, and port shift work means some households need a slot that can move between weeks rather than a fixed hour for two years. Because every tutor here works in Gulf Standard Time regardless of where they live, the tutor's location is not the constraint; the household's week is.

A few patterns hold reliably. Younger students do better with shorter, more frequent sessions than with a single long evening. Siblings share devices more often than bandwidth, so consecutive slots solve more than upgrades do. The shortened Ramadan school day changes the whole rhythm for several weeks, and sessions after Iftar hold better than late-afternoon ones, which is a decision worth making in advance rather than in week one of the month. And the single most valuable term in any agreement is that a slot can shift inside the same week instead of being cancelled.

The table sets out the usable window as it actually looks from Fujairah. It is worth reading with one eye on the exam term, when the window narrows further: revision, mock results and assessed deadlines all compete for the same evenings. Families who set a realistic slot in September keep it; families who set an optimistic one lose three lessons in October and then stop asking.
