sections.heading: What remote teaching does not fix, and where coverage runs out
paragraphs: A page that only lists advantages is not useful to a parent making a decision, so here are the limits. Remote teaching does not supply motivation. A student who will not do the timed section between sessions will not be rescued by the format, and the arrangement will produce a pleasant hour a week and no movement. If that is the actual problem, it is worth naming before buying lessons, because the fix is a conversation at home rather than a tutor.

It does not replace a school's practical programme, as the earlier section sets out, and it does not substitute for a teacher's knowledge of the cohort and the internal deadlines, which is why the school's own support is usually the right first move rather than the last resort. It also does not make a wrong diagnosis right: sessions aimed at a syllabus when the problem was two paper sections will miss whether they happen over video or across a table.

And sometimes there is simply nobody free. Higher Level physics, Further Mathematics where a school offers it, and the smaller Group 3 and Group 6 options regularly have no UAE-based specialist available at the hour a Fujairah family needs. When that happens the options are a specialist in another time zone teaching into a Gulf Standard Time slot, a fortnightly longer session, or a wait. That is said rather than hidden, which distinguishes this page from the competing ones: no provider in this market publishes its coverage limits. On the same principle, coursework support is teaching and feedback on the student's own work, never a draft supplied, and board papers and mark schemes are linked at source rather than redistributed. No tutor can promise a grade.

process.title: Test the setup once, before it matters
process.description: Ten minutes with the laptop, the phone on a stand and the headphones, on the connection you will actually use at the hour you will actually use it. Households on the northern coast road should test the mobile hotspot fallback at the same time. This single test prevents most first-session problems.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the school's deadline list
process.description: Which Diploma or International GCSE subjects, which are at Higher Level or Extended tier, and the school's internal deadlines for the core and assessed components. Those dates are set by the school, differ between schools, and decide what the first term of sessions should be aimed at.

process.title: Agree a slot that survives a full year
process.description: Pick the window that works in a normal week rather than the earliest one that works in a quiet week, and agree explicitly that it can shift inside the same week. On this coast the 17:00 to 18:30 window is the one that tends to hold once clubs and bus times are accounted for.

process.title: Ask for the artefacts from session one
process.description: An annotated piece of work, a short written note of what was covered and set, and the saved whiteboard. Requesting these at the start makes them routine rather than a challenge later, and they are what a review point reads.

process.title: Review on marked work at the school's next assessment
process.description: Compare the same style of question attempted twice, weeks apart, against the same scheme. If it improved, continue or stop. If it did not, change the aim rather than adding hours, because more of a plan that is not working is still a plan that is not working.

whyPoints.title: Working is watched, not reviewed
whyPoints.description: A second camera on the page means the tutor sees the step where a student hesitates rather than a finished answer. In a Diploma subject almost all diagnosable error lives in those middle steps, which is why the format can be more precise than a tutor reading a completed page.

whyPoints.title: Every session leaves something readable behind
whyPoints.description: An annotated script, a saved whiteboard and a short note naming what was covered and set. Four short documents a month is enough for a parent who does not teach the subject to judge whether the arrangement is aimed at anything.

whyPoints.title: The pool is defined by the subject, not the coast
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the subject and level your child is registered for. In an emirate where one teacher may cover a whole science faculty, that is the difference between a specialist who has marked the paper and a generalist who has read the syllabus.

whyPoints.title: Practical components taught where the marks actually are
whyPoints.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation carry six marks each in the Diploma's scientific investigation, and none of them is awarded for handling apparatus. Laboratory time comes from the school; converting it into marks is the work done here.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the east-coast week
whyPoints.description: Slots are set in Gulf Standard Time around bus times, clubs, prayer timings and port shift work, with the Ramadan adjustment agreed before the month begins. Slots shift inside the same week rather than being cancelled.

whyPoints.title: The limits are written down
whyPoints.description: Remote teaching does not supply motivation, replace a school's practical programme or repair a wrong diagnosis, and some subjects have no UAE-based specialist free at a workable hour. Those limits appear on this page because no provider in this market publishes theirs.

faqs.question: What internet speed does a live video lesson actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. Two video streams plus a shared canvas run comfortably on a few megabits of upload, and the usual cause of trouble is not total speed but contention: several people in the household streaming during the same hour. Test the connection once, at the hour the session will run, rather than at a quiet time of day. For households along the northern coast road, test a mobile hotspot as a fallback at the same time. Ten minutes of checking in advance prevents nearly every connection problem that would otherwise appear in week one.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tablet, or will the family laptop do?
faqs.answer: A laptop or desktop is the better primary device, because a full-size screen is needed for a shared document and extended writing on a tablet keyboard is genuinely difficult. The tablet or phone is more useful as the second camera, on a cheap stand, angled down at the page the student is writing on. Add wired headphones with a microphone and the kit list is complete. Nothing specialised is required and nothing needs buying beyond a stand, which matters because the equipment question is often what delays a family from starting.

faqs.question: How does a tutor see my son's working while he writes it?
faqs.answer: Through the second camera pointed at the page, which runs alongside the main video feed. The tutor watches the working appear and interrupts at the step where it goes wrong rather than reading a finished answer afterwards. This is the single most important piece of the setup, particularly in mathematics and in quantitative economics, because a Diploma answer that reaches the wrong result usually broke three lines earlier. A visiting tutor reading a completed page does not see that moment either; watching production is a genuine advantage of the format rather than a workaround.

faqs.question: Can handwritten past papers be marked properly if nobody is in the room?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the artefact is more durable than verbal feedback. The student completes a timed section under real conditions, photographs it square on in good light, and sends it in. It comes back annotated, with the board's published mark scheme attached alongside the script, so the student can see exactly where each mark was awarded or lost. Over a block this builds a visible record of the same question type improving, which is what a review point should be reading. Feedback given across a table is typically forgotten by midweek and leaves nothing to compare.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled when the tutor is not in a laboratory?
faqs.answer: By teaching the parts that carry marks. In the Diploma's scientific investigation, research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks, and none is awarded for handling apparatus. The work is designing the research question before the first measurement, controlling variables rather than listing them, processing data with uncertainties, and writing an evaluation that names this method's real weakness. The written papers test practical skills in writing too: describe the apparatus, identify the variable, explain the anomaly. Laboratory time comes from the school, and remote teaching will not replace a thin practical programme.

faqs.question: Is a recording of the lesson available afterwards?
faqs.answer: The artefacts are, which is usually more useful than video. The saved whiteboard, the annotated work and a short written note of what was covered and set are shared after each session, and those are what a student actually returns to. A full recording tends to go unwatched, and it raises data questions about a minor that are worth avoiding where the same purpose is served by a page of notes. If your child needs to revisit an explanation, ask for it to be written on the shared canvas during the session so it is in the saved file.

faqs.question: Where should my daughter sit for a video lesson in a busy apartment?
faqs.answer: Facing a wall, with a light in front of the page rather than behind the screen, at a surface she can write on. A door that closes is ideal and a corner facing away from the household is a workable substitute. The point is not privacy for its own sake: the session requires her to write and speak continuously, and that does not happen in a room where she is half-attending to something else. In Fujairah City apartments the practical answer is usually a bedroom desk and headphones, which also solves most of the audio problems.

faqs.question: Will my child really concentrate for a full hour on a screen?
faqs.answer: A properly run session is harder to drift through than a classroom lesson, because the student is writing and being questioned the whole time rather than listening. Even so, an hour is not right for everyone. Younger students and MYP-age children usually do better with shorter sessions more often, and some Diploma students concentrate better in two forty-minute blocks than one long one. If attention is the concern, say so before the first session so the hour can be structured for it rather than discovering it halfway through a term.

faqs.question: What time slots are available in Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: Every slot is set in Gulf Standard Time regardless of where the tutor lives, so the constraint is your household's week rather than the tutor's. From the east coast the window that reliably survives a full year is roughly 17:00 to 18:30, after clubs and after the outlying school buses. Earlier slots suit Fujairah City and Merashid; later ones suit older students and shift-working households. Weekend mornings are better used for timed papers and assessed-component work than for weekly teaching, because the available attention span is longer.

faqs.question: Can a session run at the weekend or late in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both have specific uses rather than being simply alternatives. Weekend mornings give a longer attention span, which suits timed papers and work on an assessed component where an hour is not enough to get anywhere. Late evening suits older students and households working port shifts, with the caveat that concentration in the exam term declines noticeably after a long day and a shorter session is usually a better trade. During Ramadan, sessions after Iftar hold better than late-afternoon ones, and that adjustment is best agreed before the month begins.

faqs.question: Who makes up the time if an outage cuts a lesson short?
faqs.answer: The session is picked up on the fallback, usually a mobile hotspot, and if that is not viable the time is made up rather than lost. This is worth settling at the start rather than improvising: agree what happens to a session cut short by an outage, who makes the call, and how the remaining time is rescheduled. Because the slot can move inside the same week at no cost to either side, a dropped session is an inconvenience rather than a lost lesson, which is not true of a visiting arrangement where the alternative was a round trip.

faqs.question: How do I see what was covered without sitting in on the lesson?
faqs.answer: Read the four short documents a month that the arrangement should produce: the annotated work, the written note naming what was covered and what was set, and the saved whiteboard. None of it requires you to understand the subject. What you are checking is whether the same style of question is being attempted more than once and scoring better, and whether the targets named in the plan are the ones being worked on. If nothing written is arriving, there is nothing to review and nothing is being measured.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know what the school taught that week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the first five minutes of every session are spent on exactly that. A student who is behind cannot afford to be learning two sequences at once, so the teaching order follows the school's rather than the textbook's. Schools also change their order mid-year, which means a plan written in September goes stale by November unless somebody checks. Your child reporting what happened in class is usually enough; where a school publishes a scheme of work, sending it once at the start saves several weeks of guessing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor based outside the UAE teach the Diploma properly?
faqs.answer: The Diploma is an international qualification with published subject guides and mark schemes, so subject competence does not depend on country of residence. What does depend on it is scheduling, which is why every slot here is set in Gulf Standard Time, and knowledge of your child's school, which no external tutor has and which is why the school's teaching order and internal deadline list are asked for at the start. The honest point in the other direction is that a tutor outside the UAE will not know the local cohort or the mandatory-subject arrangements, so those stay with the school.

faqs.question: What will online tutoring not fix for my child?
faqs.answer: Three things. It will not supply motivation: a student who does not do the timed section between sessions will produce a pleasant hour a week and no movement in the marks. It will not replace a thin practical programme at school, though it will convert whatever laboratory work happens into marks. And it will not repair a wrong diagnosis, so sessions aimed at a whole syllabus when the problem was two paper sections will miss regardless of format. There is also a fourth limit worth naming: some subjects have no UAE-based specialist free at a workable hour, and that gets said rather than hidden.

fujairah/ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Test the setup, then send the deadline list
fujairah/ib-online-tutor.closingBody: Two short tasks get a plan started. Spend ten minutes checking the laptop, the phone on a stand and the headphones on the connection you will actually use, at the hour you will actually use it. Then send the subjects, the levels and the school's internal deadlines for the core and assessed components. The first session can then be diagnostic rather than introductory, and the plan it produces will be aimed at this term rather than at a generic calendar. Lessons are one-to-one and live, set in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Fujairah address, holds no examination-board or regulator approval, and publishes no IB exam date it could not verify.

fujairah/ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: Tutors below teach single Diploma subjects at Higher or Standard Level rather than covering a phase. The match is made on the subject and level your child is registered for, because a student sitting Chemistry at Higher Level needs the Paper 3 specialist, not a science teacher who covers three subjects in one slot.

intro.heading: A small emirate, a small cohort, and a subject nobody local teaches
paragraphs: Fujairah is the only emirate on the Gulf of Oman coast, cut off from the Dubai school belt by the Hajar mountains. That geography shapes the tutoring question more than anything in the Diploma itself. The private school set here is small. Where a Dubai campus might run two parallel Higher Level chemistry classes, a Fujairah school may run one group of eight, taught by the same person who covers physics and biology. When a student in that group stalls, the school has no second specialist to hand them to, and neither does the neighbourhood.

This is why the search looks different from the equivalent search in Dubai. A Dubai parent is choosing among many people who teach their subject. A Fujairah parent is usually choosing among three things that are not really the same thing: more of the school's own support, a local tutor who is strong generally but has never taught a Diploma paper, and an agency west of the mountains whose tutor would have to make a round trip of two to three hours around a sixty-minute lesson. The fourth option, a specialist reached over live video, exists precisely because the first three run out.

The Diploma itself also resists general tutoring in a way that surprises people. It is not six subjects with exams at the end. Each subject carries internally assessed work with its own criteria and mark allocations, each Higher Level course adds components a Standard Level student never meets, and the whole thing sits on top of the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, which run to school-set internal deadlines rather than to an examination timetable. A tutor who has not worked inside that structure will teach content competently and miss where the marks are going.

What a parent can check, before paying anything, is whether the person in front of them talks in components. A Diploma specialist will name the papers in your child's subject, say what each is worth at Higher and Standard Level, and ask to see the last marked script and the school's internal deadline list. A generalist will talk about confidence and rapport, which matter but are not diagnosable. That distinction is more useful on the east coast than anywhere else in the country, because the cost of a wrong match here includes the weeks it takes to notice.

Delivery is stated plainly so nothing has to be assumed. Tuition arranged through IB Gram is one-to-one and delivered live over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Fujairah school day. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Fujairah address; visiting tuition is offered only in India. The gain for a family here is not convenience, it is reach: the pool stops being people willing to drive the mountain road twice a week and becomes people who teach your child's subject at your child's level for a living.

fujairah/ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Four programmes account for nearly every enquiry from this coast: the Diploma that a student is sitting or about to start, the Middle Years Programme that feeds it, the Primary Years Programme at continuum campuses, and Cambridge IGCSE, which is what most east-coast students actually hold when they reach sixth form.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject has externally examined papers and at least one internally assessed component marked against lettered criteria. Higher Level courses add material a Standard Level student never sees: a third paper in the sciences and in mathematics, extra depth in the options, longer written components in the humanities.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision on the east coast is thin, so a Fujairah student's subject combination is frequently decided by what the school can staff rather than by what the student wants. That is the single most common reason a family here ends up looking for outside teaching: not weakness, but a subject taught by someone covering it as a second specialism.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, reported on a 1-7 scale. The Personal Project in the final year is the first piece of long self-managed work a student produces, and it is a reliable predictor of how the Extended Essay will go two years later. Content is not harder than a national curriculum at the same age; the assessment language is unfamiliar.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving from an MYP campus into a Fujairah IGCSE year group, or the other way, meet a different assessment system rather than a different difficulty level. Where that transfer is on the table, the useful question is which subjects the receiving school would enter them for and at which tier, because that decides whether any gap is content or technique.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with no external examinations, reported against learner-profile attributes and subject strands. Support at this stage is about securing number facts, reading fluency and written structure rather than examination technique, and it is usually short: a defined block to close one identifiable gap, then a stop.
programmes.countryNote: Few east-coast families ask about primary tuition, and most of those who do are moving between systems. The honest answer for a Fujairah parent here is often that nothing is needed yet, which is worth saying because the alternative is a weekly commitment running for years against no measurable target.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, the local feeder
programmes.description: Most students on this coast reach sixth form with IGCSEs rather than the MYP. Each subject has a four-digit code that governs papers, tier and practicals. Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable.
programmes.countryNote: The tier taken at IGCSE decides which Diploma routes stay open. Core-tier mathematics generally closes Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, and on the east coast the fallback is not a different sixth form down the road. That makes the Year 10 tier conversation unusually consequential for a Fujairah family.

fujairah/ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects east-coast families ask about most often, with the component that usually decides the grade named rather than implied. Where a Higher Level course adds a paper, the paper is stated.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and carries 30 per cent at Higher Level and 40 per cent at Standard Level. Higher Level adds Paper 3, worth 20 per cent: two long structured investigations that students abandon rather than attempt for method marks. Algebraic fluency under time pressure is the usual limiting factor.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout and heavier on modelling, statistics and technology use. Marks are lost in interpretation: a correct regression reported without a sentence saying what it means scores the calculation and not the conclusion. Higher Level carries a Paper 3 of its own with extended modelling tasks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 combines multiple choice with a data-based section worth 36 per cent; Paper 2 carries 44 per cent in extended response. Higher Level depth in organic mechanisms and energetics separates the top grades. The scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The commonest east-coast stall is in fields and circuits, where students can quote a relationship but cannot apply it to an unfamiliar arrangement. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, and the data-based questions reward graph reading over recall. Uncertainty treatment is a repeated and avoidable loss in the investigation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most over-revised and under-scored subject in the Diploma. Students reread notes and score the same mark twice. Gains come from converting recall into the structure the extended-response questions want, and from practising the data-analysis items where the marks sit outside the textbook.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds Paper 3, worth 30 per cent, with quantitative questions and policy evaluation at the end. Diagram accuracy decides more marks than essay style: an unlabelled axis or a shifted curve drawn in the wrong direction costs the analysis marks before the evaluation is read.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is where grades separate. Students name a framework and then describe the case rather than applying the framework to it. The internally assessed research project needs a real question and real data, and the commonest problem is a topic too broad to answer in the word limit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, worth 35 per cent, two hours fifteen at Higher Level. Students who read widely still lose marks by summarising the text instead of analysing how it works. The Individual Oral is assessed on a global issue, which has to be argued rather than announced.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Common across the emirate's mixed-language intakes. Productive skills are assessed under timed conditions, and the Higher Level reading texts are longer and denser. The individual oral rewards students who can sustain an unscripted exchange, which is a different skill from writing well.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the licensed international curriculum as required study, in first-language and additional-language streams taught separately. Where it is taken as a Diploma subject, assessment structure rather than vocabulary is usually the gap, particularly in the written tasks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core contributes points to the Diploma total and runs to school-set internal deadlines rather than an exam timetable. Both are self-managed, which is precisely why they slip. Support is process coaching, reading the criteria, and feedback on the student's own drafts.

fujairah/ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Fujairah's districts differ on how long the school run takes and when a weekday session can realistically start. They do not differ on which Diploma subjects are taught locally, which is why the reach of the arrangement matters more here than its distance.

regions.name: Fujairah City and Merashid
regions.note: Where most of the emirate's private school places sit. Families here have the shortest school run and the widest local choice, and are the most likely to try the school's own after-school support before looking outside it.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal and close to the city schools, with corniche sports and club commitments running late into the afternoon. The binding constraint on a weekday slot is the end of those activities rather than the drive home.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland of the city with a mixed-curriculum intake. A practical early session here is usually after five, and a diagnostic first session works better than a content lesson because the local school report rarely identifies the component at fault.

regions.name: Madhab and Al Gurfa
regions.note: Residential districts with a steady turnover of posted families, so mid-year arrivals are common. A student joining a Diploma cohort in DP1 mid-term has a different and more urgent job than one who started with it.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: An hour up the coast from the city, with very little school choice in range. Any arrangement depending on someone driving here twice a week has a continuity problem before term begins, which is the main reason video sessions dominate this stretch.

regions.name: Qidfa, Mirbah and Al Aqah
regions.note: Spread along the northern coast road with long gaps between settlements. Households here are the clearest case for subject matching over proximity: there is no local Diploma specialist to choose from in any subject.

regions.name: Masafi and the mountain road
regions.note: Split between Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah, on the route west. The road closes after heavy rain, which turns a visiting arrangement into a missed week rather than a late lesson.

regions.name: Kalba and Khor Fakkan
regions.note: Sharjah exclaves minutes down the same coast, under the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than the Ministry of Education. Term dates and fee rules differ even though the drive does not.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah City and the east coast
schoolClusters.note: The schools within a normal school run of the city. Between them they cover British and Indian curricula; Diploma provision is limited, which is why sixth-form choices here often involve a move rather than a change of class.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Khor Fakkan corridor
schoolClusters.note: Reachable from the east coast and under a different regulator. Families comparing these campuses with a Fujairah school are comparing two inspection cycles and two term calendars as well as two curricula.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma campuses west of the mountains

sections.heading: What an east-coast parent is actually asking for
paragraphs: The search phrase is about location, but the problem underneath it is almost never location. Families on this coast rarely contact anybody because no adult within reach can help with schoolwork. They contact somebody because one Diploma subject has stopped moving, the school has one teacher in it, and there is no second specialist inside a reasonable radius. Proximity cannot solve that. Only a bigger pool can.

It helps to be precise about what is scarce. General academic help is not scarce in Fujairah; competent, patient adults who can supervise homework and keep a teenager working exist here as everywhere. What is scarce is component-level knowledge of a specific Diploma course at a specific level: someone who has marked Chemistry Paper 2 against the published scheme, who knows what the data section of Paper 1 rewards, who can look at a scientific investigation and say which of the four criteria is costing marks. That person may not exist within an hour's drive in any direction.

So the honest framing of the question is a trade. A tutor physically present brings the things presence brings: a fixed appointment somebody has travelled for, a direct relationship with the household, and a hand on the page. A tutor reached over video brings subject precision and continuity, because nothing about the arrangement depends on the mountain road being open or on a two-hour round trip remaining attractive in February. For a Diploma subject, and particularly a Higher Level one, precision usually wins. For a nine-year-old who needs reading practice, presence probably does. The next sections set that trade out with numbers attached.

sections.heading: Four things about the Diploma a general subject tutor has never had to handle
paragraphs: A strong school teacher from any system can teach Diploma content. What they have usually not had to handle is the Diploma's machinery: the internally assessed components with lettered criteria, the Higher Level extras, the core running on school-set dates, and the academic-honesty rules that govern what anyone outside the school may do with a student's work. Each one is a place where a well-meaning generalist costs marks.

The internally assessed work is the biggest of the four. Every Diploma subject has at least one piece marked against named criteria with published mark allocations, and the marks are not distributed the way students assume. In the scientific investigation, research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks, so a beautifully written conclusion sitting on a vague research question has already lost most of the top band. In the mathematical exploration, presentation and communication carry four marks each and personal engagement carries three, which is why a technically correct exploration with no stated aim scores poorly. A tutor who does not know those numbers cannot direct the student's effort.

The core is the second, and it fails quietly. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS run to internal deadlines the school sets, not to an examination timetable, and nobody chases a student in September about a date in March. By the time a parent notices, the window for choosing a workable Extended Essay question has closed and the student is committed to one that cannot be answered in the word limit. The third issue is the Higher Level extras, which appear in the table below. The fourth is the honesty line, which has a section of its own further down.

sections.heading: The three alternatives, and what each one costs a Fujairah family
paragraphs: Set against each other, the options differ less on price than on reach. The school's own support is the cheapest and the most convenient, and in many cases it is the right first move: a subject teacher giving a Diploma student an extra hour a week knows the cohort, the teaching order and the internal deadlines. Its limit is structural rather than a criticism. If the subject has one teacher and that teacher is the reason the student has stalled, more of the same input will not move it, and in a single-figure cohort there is no colleague to swap to.

A local generalist is the next step most families take, often on a neighbour's recommendation. It works well below sixth form and runs into trouble at Higher Level, for the reasons in the table above. An agency west of the mountains is the third, and the arithmetic is the problem: a round trip from the Dubai school belt to Fujairah City runs two to three hours around a sixty-minute lesson, so either the lesson is long enough to justify the drive or the drive is priced into the hour. Published market rates for visiting tuition in the UAE run AED 180-500 per hour, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online.

The fourth option exists because the first three run out of specialists, not because it is cheaper. It is worth being clear about what it costs and what it does not include. The figures in the table are market rates published by named providers in October 2026, not a price list; a specific subject, level and session length is a short consultation, followed by one trial session per family at no charge. What the table does show is that the premium end of this market reflects scarcity at least as much as skill, which is why the dearest option is not automatically the right one for a Fujairah household.

sections.heading: The mountain road, priced into an hourly rate
paragraphs: The Hajar mountains are the single most under-discussed fact in tutoring on this coast, and they are worth stating as arithmetic rather than scenery. A tutor based in the Dubai school belt who agrees to teach a Fujairah student in person is agreeing to spend two to three hours travelling around one hour of teaching. Nobody sustains that at the online rate. It either appears in the fee, which pushes the hour towards the upper end of the visiting band, or it appears in reliability, as the arrangement quietly becomes fortnightly and then occasional.

The weather makes it worse at exactly the wrong time of year. The mountain road closes after heavy rain, which in a visiting arrangement means a missed week rather than a late start. In February, with mocks marked and a May session approaching, a missed week is not recoverable by doubling up later. This is the practical reason continuity matters more than presence for a Diploma student on the east coast, and it is a reason specific to this emirate rather than a general argument about online teaching.

There is a second-order effect families notice only after a term. When the lesson is a round trip, rescheduling becomes expensive for the tutor, so slots stop moving. School events, mock weeks, CAS commitments and the shortened Ramadan day all push against a fixed slot, and a slot that cannot move is a slot that gets cancelled. A video session can shift inside the same week at no cost to anybody, which over a two-year Diploma is worth more lessons than any difference in hourly rate.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, component by component
paragraphs: Parents are usually shown grades and predicted grades, which are summaries. The useful object is the marked script, because marks go missing in patterns and the patterns are diagnosable. Method marks lost on questions with the right final answer point at working and presentation. Marks lost in the last third of a paper point at pacing. Marks lost where an answer is factually correct but scores below band almost always point at command terms.

That last one is the most common and the most fixable. The Diploma defines its command terms, and they are marked differently: outline wants a brief account, explain wants reasons, deduce wants a conclusion reached from given information, discuss wants a balanced review. A student who answers every one of those as describe is not short of knowledge. They are answering a different question from the one on the paper, and a tutor can correct it in a handful of sessions once somebody has identified it.

The table below sets out the components where east-coast students most often lose ground, with the weightings they carry. Two things are worth noting about it. First, the heaviest components are not the ones students spend the most time on; the data-based sections and the internally assessed work are routinely under-practised relative to their weight. Second, no IB session or results date is published on this page. The IB's own assessment pages could not be verified for this project, so dates must be confirmed with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any third-party restatement.

sections.heading: The core, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Three parts of the Diploma are self-managed, and all three fail the same way. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the internally assessed component in each subject run to dates the school sets rather than to the examination timetable, and nobody rings a bell. A Fujairah student with a supervisor who teaches a different subject, in a school where one person coordinates the whole programme, is more exposed to this than a student in a large Dubai cohort with a dedicated core team.

The most useful intervention is also the earliest and the cheapest: narrow the research question until it can be answered in the word limit, and read the criteria before writing anything. Most weak Extended Essays are not badly written. They are answering a question nobody could answer in four thousand words, chosen in a week when the student was busy, and the problem was baked in before the first draft. The same is true of the mathematical exploration and the scientific investigation: the research question decides the ceiling.

Where the line sits should be stated before anybody pays for anything. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss the student's own ideas with them, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it to completion, or supply a version to adapt. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright; a candidate who submits one is exposed to an academic-honesty finding, and the exposure falls on the student. Board syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked at source rather than redistributed, because they belong to the IB and to Cambridge, not to a tutoring platform.

sections.heading: Who supervises a Fujairah school, and what follows for sixth form
paragraphs: Private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in overseeing private schools in those three emirates. That is different from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education, and from Abu Dhabi, where the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Minutes down the coast at Kalba and Khor Fakkan, the Sharjah Private Education Authority applies instead, and Sharjah's authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

What that means for a parent is practical. There is no emirate-level inspection portal for Fujairah of the kind a Dubai parent is used to, so school-level information comes from the school and from ministry circulars. The federal baseline also applies: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the required subjects running alongside whatever international programme a school is licensed for.

Looking further ahead, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements decide what a leaving certificate is worth for UAE university entry. On the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the Diploma, no points threshold is published here, because the figure could not be verified from the ministry's own source. Equivalency is a ministry process, not something a tutoring platform performs; check the current requirements through the official channel before relying on any restatement.

sections.heading: The east-coast week, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Scheduling is where arrangements on this coast actually break. A Fujairah school day ends in the early afternoon, clubs and sports run on into the late afternoon, prayer timings shape the evening, and families working shifts at the port need a slot that can move between weeks rather than a fixed hour for two years. Add the shortened Ramadan school day, when the whole rhythm changes for several weeks, and a rigid weekly slot looks less like discipline and more like a plan that will lose lessons.

What works in practice is a standing slot that can be moved inside the same week, a shorter session more often rather than one long evening for younger students, and an explicit decision about mock weeks and exam weeks: either pause or switch the content to timed papers, but decide rather than drift. During Ramadan, sessions after Iftar tend to hold better than late-afternoon ones, and it is worth agreeing that change before the month starts rather than during it.

The last thing to say is the one most providers in this market leave out. Some Diploma subjects at Higher Level have no UAE-based specialist free at the hour a Fujairah family needs. It happens most in the smaller Group 3 and Group 6 options, in Higher Level physics and in Further Mathematics where a school offers it. When it happens, the straight answer is to say so and name the alternative: a specialist in another time zone teaching into a Gulf Standard Time slot, a fortnightly longer session, or a wait for a slot to open. No tutor can promise a grade, and a conversation that starts with one has told you how the rest will go. Coverage limits disclosed in advance are the reason this page is longer than the ones it is competing with.

process.title: Name the subject and the level, not the year group
process.description: Start with the Diploma subjects your child takes and whether each is Higher or Standard Level. On the east coast this matters more than anywhere else, because the Higher Level extras are exactly the components a local generalist has never taught and the ones where marks are usually going.

process.title: Send the last two marked scripts and the internal deadlines
process.description: A recent marked paper shows whether marks are lost on method, pacing or command terms. The school's internal deadline list for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the subject's assessed work shows what is genuinely urgent, which is rarely the thing that feels urgent.

process.title: Agree a slot that can move inside the week
process.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around the Fujairah school day, clubs and prayer timings. Build in the ability to shift a lesson rather than cancel it, because over two years that single arrangement decides how many lessons actually happen.

process.title: One trial session, then a plan that names components
process.description: One trial session per family at no charge follows the consultation. Ask for the plan in writing afterwards: it should name papers, components and a sequence. A plan written in terms of confidence and motivation cannot be measured against the next marked script.

process.title: Review at the next school assessment
process.description: Set the review point at the school's next assessment rather than after a number of weeks, and judge it on whether marks moved in the components the plan targeted. If they did not, the aim was wrong and should change. That is a normal event in a two-year programme.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. faqs.question: What does an IB tutor need to know that a strong maths teacher does not?
faqs.answer: The machinery around the content. A capable maths teacher from any system can teach Diploma mathematics, but they may never have taught Paper 3, which exists only at Higher Level and carries 20 per cent of the grade as two long structured investigations. They may not know that the mathematical exploration is marked on presentation, communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics with published mark allocations, so a technically sound piece with no stated aim loses the top band. Command terms are the third gap: deduce, outline and explain are marked differently, and a student answering them all the same way is losing marks they already earned.

faqs.question: My son's school has one teacher per Diploma subject. Is outside teaching the right fix?
faqs.answer: Often, but check the cheaper option first. If the problem is a missed sequence of lessons or confusion about the teaching order, the subject teacher is the fastest and least expensive route and knows the cohort and the internal deadlines. Outside teaching earns its cost when the bottleneck is the input itself: a single-figure cohort with one teacher has no colleague to swap to, and more of the same explanation will not move a student who has already not understood it twice. The test is diagnostic rather than emotional. Ask what the last two marked scripts show, and whether the gap is content, technique or pacing.

faqs.question: Is the school's own after-school support enough to get through DP2?
faqs.answer: For many students, yes. School support has advantages nobody outside can match: it is close to the teaching order, cheap or included, and the person giving it knows the internal deadlines. It runs out in three situations. The subject has one teacher and that teacher is the reason the student has stalled. The need is Higher Level depth the school does not routinely teach, such as a third paper or an option topic. Or the core has slipped and the student needs sustained process coaching the school cannot give to one individual. Outside the first case, more school support is usually the right next step.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is content or examination technique?
faqs.answer: Read the marked script rather than the grade, and look for the pattern. Marks lost where the final answer is correct point at working and presentation, not understanding. Marks lost steadily through the last third of a paper point at pacing. Marks lost on answers that are factually right but score below band almost always point at command terms. Content gaps look different: whole questions untouched, or working that goes wrong at the same step every time. The distinction matters financially, because a technique problem can often be fixed in a short block while a content gap needs sustained weekly teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tutor based in Dubai realistically teach my daughter in Fujairah every week?
faqs.answer: In person, rarely for long. The round trip from the Dubai school belt to Fujairah City runs two to three hours around a sixty-minute lesson, so either the lesson gets long enough to justify the drive or the drive gets priced into the fee, which pushes the hour towards the upper end of the AED 180-500 visiting band. The arrangement then becomes fragile: the mountain road closes after heavy rain, slots stop moving because rescheduling costs the tutor a round trip, and by February the weekly lesson has become occasional. Over video the same specialist teaches the same hour with none of that attached.

faqs.question: What does an hour of Diploma tuition cost a family on this coast?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300 per hour, visiting one-to-one tuition at AED 180-500 with travel inside the fee, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium or examiner-experienced tutors at AED 500-650 and above. Monthly packages seen in this market ran around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, not a price list. For a specific subject, level and session length the honest answer is a short consultation, then one trial session per family at no charge.

faqs.question: How many Higher Level subjects can one student sensibly have support in at once?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two at the outside. The constraint is not money but the student's week. A Diploma year already contains six subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, and adding three weekly sessions to that usually means homework gets done worse rather than better. The productive pattern on this coast is to start with the subject where the marked scripts show the largest recoverable mark total, hold it for a term, and add a second only if the first has moved. A short pre-session block in a third subject is a different thing and can sit alongside.

faqs.question: How many points does the Diploma core contribute to the final score?
faqs.answer: They contribute points on top of the six subject grades, and they are awarded together rather than separately, which is why a weak Extended Essay cannot be fully offset by a strong Theory of Knowledge essay. The more important point for a Fujairah family is that both run to deadlines the school sets rather than to the examination timetable. Confirm the exact point allocation and the current core requirements with your child's Diploma coordinator, because the IB's own published documentation is the authority on it and this page does not restate figures it could not verify from the source.

faqs.question: Does a tutor really need to see my child's school deadline list?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most useful document a parent can send. The Diploma core and every internally assessed component run on dates the school chooses, and those dates differ between schools sitting the same session. Without the list, a tutor works to the examination timetable and discovers an internal deadline after it has passed, which is the commonest way a term of sessions gets aimed at the wrong thing. With it, the plan can put the exploration or the Extended Essay draft ahead of content revision in the weeks where that is genuinely the priority.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to staff from inside the UAE?
faqs.answer: The smaller Group 3 and Group 6 options, Higher Level physics, and Further Mathematics where a school offers it. The pattern is simple: a subject taken by few students nationally is taught by few teachers, and those teachers are already fully committed during the hours a Gulf Standard Time family wants. When that happens the options are a specialist in another time zone teaching into a Gulf Standard Time slot, a fortnightly longer session, or a wait for a slot to open. None of those is hidden behind an enquiry form, and no provider in this market publishes its coverage limits, which is why they are stated here.

faqs.question: We may move west of the mountains next year. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the school and the regulator, and it need not change the teaching at all. A move from Fujairah into Dubai moves your child from federal Ministry of Education supervision to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with a different inspection cycle and term calendar; a move to Sharjah or Kalba puts them under the Sharjah Private Education Authority instead. What usually causes trouble in a mid-course move is coursework in progress, because internal deadlines and supervisor arrangements differ between schools. Settle the Extended Essay question and any assessed component before the transfer rather than after it.

faqs.question: Which authority supervises my child's school in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge. The practical consequence for a Fujairah parent is that there is no emirate-level inspection portal of the kind Dubai families use, so school-level information comes from the school itself and from ministry circulars rather than from a public dashboard.

faqs.question: Is a Diploma student allowed to use a tutor for the exploration at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits, and the limits are the point. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, read the criteria with the student and explain what each one rewards, discuss the student's own ideas, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it to completion, or supply a model to adapt. The work must be the student's own, and the consequence of crossing that line falls on the candidate rather than on the tutor. Any provider offering to supply a finished internal assessment is offering an academic-honesty exposure rather than a grade.

faqs.question: How late in DP2 is it still worth starting with an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, provided the aim narrows as the time shortens. With two terms left, content teaching is still viable in a subject with identifiable gaps. With one term left, the productive work is technique: timed papers, mark scheme reading and command-term precision, aimed at the one or two components carrying the largest recoverable marks. With six weeks left, the honest answer is triage on a single paper rather than a broad programme. What does not work at any stage is starting from chapter one, which is why the first session reads the marked scripts instead of the textbook.

faqs.question: What should the first session with a Diploma specialist actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written plan that names components. Not a reassurance, not a general impression, but a short document saying which papers and criteria the marks are sitting in, which two or three topics come first and in what order, and when the plan will be reviewed against the next school assessment. Ask for it after the trial session and read it for nouns. A plan describing attitude and engagement cannot be measured against anything, and an unmeasurable plan is how two years of weekly sessions pass on the east coast without the component scores moving.

fujairah/ib-tutor.closingHeading: Send the subject, the level and the deadline list
fujairah/ib-tutor.closingBody: The useful first message is short: which Diploma subjects your child takes, which are at Higher Level, the school's internal deadlines for the core and the assessed components, and a weekday window that survives clubs and prayer timings. Attach the last two marked scripts and the consultation can start on a diagnosis instead of an introduction. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Fujairah address, holds no regulator or examination-board approval, and names no school as a partner. What it does is reach past the mountain road to someone who teaches your child's subject at your child's level.

fujairah/ib-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched by Diploma subject and level rather than by location, because on this coast the nearest available adult and the right subject specialist are almost never the same person. Sessions are one-to-one over live video, scheduled around the east-coast school day.

intro.heading: The nearest specialist is further away than the map suggests
paragraphs: Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman, behind the Hajar mountains, which is the single fact that governs this search. The emirate has a small private school set and small subject cohorts inside it. A Higher Level science group may be eight students taught by someone who also covers two other sciences. When a parent types a proximity query, the map answers with a handful of results that are either general tutors or businesses west of the mountains quoting a national service area. Neither is what the query was asking for.

So it is worth being exact about what distance means here rather than trading in impressions. From Fujairah City the Dubai school belt is a two-to-three-hour round trip by road. Khor Fakkan and Kalba are minutes up the same coast but are Sharjah exclaves under a different regulator. Dibba is an hour north with almost no school choice in range. Masafi sits on the inland route west, which closes after heavy rain. None of those numbers is a complaint about the roads; they are the figures that decide whether a weekly appointment survives to February.

The next thing to establish is what proximity would actually buy. For a nine-year-old who needs reading practice and a routine, a nearby adult is genuinely valuable and the right answer. For a Diploma Higher Level subject, proximity buys almost nothing that matters and costs the thing that matters most, which is access to someone who has marked that subject's papers repeatedly. In a cohort of eight, the local pool of people who have done that is frequently zero, and no amount of driving changes it.

There are questions where being near home is decisive, and this page covers them rather than brushing them aside. Where the papers are physically sat, and whether a student can enter as a private candidate for a subject their school does not teach, are both local questions with local answers. So is which authority supervises the school, which changes within a few minutes' drive on this coast. So is the practical business of a school run, a bus timetable and the hour at which a session can start. Those are the parts of the search that proximity really does answer.

The delivery position is stated so nothing is assumed. Tuition arranged through IB Gram is one-to-one and delivered live over video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Fujairah and will not send anyone to a Fujairah address; visiting tuition is offered only in India. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform holding no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority. What follows is the geography, measured, and the decisions that follow from it.

fujairah/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: What is available within reach differs sharply by programme on this coast, and that availability is usually what decides a family's options rather than preference. These four are the ones that actually appear.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level courses add components Standard Level students never meet, including a third paper in mathematics and the sciences. Every subject carries internally assessed work marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision within reach of the east coast is limited, so a Fujairah student's subject combination is often determined by what a school can staff rather than what the student wants. Families weighing a move or weekly boarding west of the mountains are usually weighing it for this reason alone.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, reported on a 1-7 scale. Continuous assessment means there is no single point at which everything is decided, and the Personal Project in the final year is the first long self-managed piece a student writes.
programmes.countryNote: The nearest continuum campuses to the east coast sit in Sharjah and the northern emirates rather than in Fujairah itself, so an MYP family here is frequently already commuting or boarding. Where a student moves between the MYP and an IGCSE cohort, the gap is assessment language rather than content difficulty.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The qualification most east-coast students actually hold. Four-digit syllabus codes govern papers, tier and practical arrangements. Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones; it states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version of the timetable for their zone.
programmes.countryNote: This is where proximity genuinely matters, because the exam centre is a physical place. For the March 2027 series Cambridge published final entries as due 27 November 2026, the exam period as 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results to centres on Direct on 13 May, with certificates in late June.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Available in a May or June window and again in November, with some subjects modular in structure. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: The November window is the practical fallback for east-coast families, because repeating a year is rarely viable where school choice is thin. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series, so plan from the board's live timetable rather than from any restatement of it, including this page.

fujairah/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects east-coast families ask for, listed with an honest note on how easy each is to find within reach. Scarcity rather than difficulty is what usually sends a Fujairah family looking.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Widely taught, so the local pool is better here than anywhere else in the Diploma. The scarcity appears at Higher Level, where Paper 3 and its long structured investigations need somebody who has marked them rather than somebody who has read about them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Newer in most schools' teaching memory, which thins the pool of people confident in the modelling and statistics units. Local generalists frequently teach it as though it were Analysis and Approaches with a calculator, which misses where the marks are.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Commonly offered and commonly under-staffed at Higher Level. On the east coast one teacher frequently covers chemistry, physics and biology, so the organic mechanisms that separate the top grades get less specialist attention than they need.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The hardest Diploma science to find within reach, and consistently the hardest to staff nationally. Fields, circuits and uncertainty treatment are the components where east-coast students lose ground, and they are precisely the ones a generalist handles least well.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The easiest to find locally and the easiest to teach unproductively. Content re-explanation feels like progress and changes nothing; the recoverable marks sit in extended-response structure and in the data-analysis items.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Taught in fewer east-coast schools than the sciences, so the local pool is thin. Higher Level Paper 3, with its quantitative questions and policy evaluation, is the component most often left to general revision rather than practised directly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Popular and reasonably well covered, with the assessed research project as the real gap. A question too broad to answer inside the word limit is the commonest failure, and it is chosen before anybody outside the school sees the work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Generally available locally. The component families struggle to prepare for is the Individual Oral, which needs an unscripted spoken exchange rather than a rehearsed presentation, and which is rarely practised enough in a small cohort.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Well covered across the emirate's mixed-language intakes. Improvement comes from frequency rather than intensity, which makes this one of the few subjects where a long, low-intensity arrangement genuinely beats a short block.

subjects.name: Group 3 and Group 6 options
subjects.description: Psychology, global politics, visual arts, music and the smaller humanities. These are the subjects where a Fujairah student is most likely to be the only candidate in the emirate, and where no local specialist exists at any price.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: Required study alongside the licensed curriculum
subjects.description: Locally well staffed, since every school must provide it. First-language and additional-language streams are taught separately and material may not be substituted without ministry approval, so support is about assessment language and written structure.

fujairah/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: Distance from provision, not distance from the city, is what shapes the options in each district. These notes give the practical position from the places enquiries come from.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: The centre of what provision exists, and the only district where a local pool of general tutors is worth considering at all. Even here the Diploma Higher Level pool is small enough that subject matching beats proximity.

regions.name: Al Faseel and the corniche
regions.note: Minutes from the city schools, so the school run is short and the binding constraint is club and fixture times rather than distance. Proximity is already solved here; subject coverage is what is missing.

regions.note: Inland of the city with a mixed-curriculum intake. Close enough to the schools that a local tutor is practical for younger year groups, and far enough from any Diploma specialist that sixth-form support comes from elsewhere.

regions.name: Merashid and Madhab

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: An hour north with very little school choice in range and no realistic local tutor market for examined subjects. A weekly drive from the city in either direction is the arrangement most likely to lapse by the second term.

sections.heading: What a proximity search actually returns here, and why
paragraphs: Three kinds of result come back from this query on the east coast, and it is worth knowing which is which. The first is general local tutors: real people, often very good with younger children, usually covering a phase rather than a Diploma subject. The second is national agencies declaring a service area that includes Fujairah, which in practice means a tutor would travel from west of the mountains or, more commonly, that the lesson would be delivered remotely without the page saying so. The third is marketplace listings with no local content at all.

None of those is dishonest exactly, but the aggregate effect misleads, because the thing the parent is implicitly asking for is a Diploma subject specialist within a short drive, and that is the one category the results do not contain. The reason is arithmetic. Specialists concentrate where cohorts are large. Fujairah's cohorts are small, so a teacher here covers breadth rather than depth, and the depth a Higher Level student needs sits where the student population is.

The useful reframe is to split the search in two. There are things only proximity can answer: where the papers are sat, which authority supervises the school, what time the bus gets home, whether a local centre will accept a private candidate. And there are things only subject matching can answer: who has marked this paper, who knows what criterion A actually rewards, who can tell a pacing problem from a content gap. Treating one question as if it were the other is the mistake that costs an east-coast family a term.

sections.heading: Drive times from the east coast, measured rather than estimated
paragraphs: Straight-line distance is misleading here because of the mountains, so the figures worth planning against are round trips at the hour a lesson would actually run. A tutor travelling from the Dubai school belt to Fujairah City is committing two to three hours of driving around a sixty-minute lesson. Nobody sustains that at an online rate, which is why published visiting rates in the UAE run AED 180-500 per hour with travel inside the fee, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online.

The second number that matters is reliability rather than duration. The inland route through Masafi closes after heavy rain, which in a visiting arrangement means a missed week rather than a late start. A missed week in February, with mocks marked and the papers approaching, is not recoverable by doubling up in April. And there is a slower failure that families only notice after a term: when a lesson is a round trip, rescheduling is expensive for the tutor, so slots stop moving, and a slot that cannot move is a slot that gets cancelled when a fixture or a school event lands on it.

The table below sets out the practical positions from the districts enquiries come from. It is worth reading alongside one more fact: Kalba and Khor Fakkan are closer to several Fujairah households than Fujairah City is, and they sit in Sharjah. Proximity on this coast does not map onto emirate, regulator or term calendar, which is the kind of thing that only becomes obvious after somebody has made a decision on a map.

sections.heading: The nearest three alternatives, ranked by what they stop short of
paragraphs: Set out in order of distance, the options a Fujairah family can reach are the school's own subject teacher, a local general tutor, the nearest tuition provision in the city, and a provider in the Sharjah exclaves or beyond the mountains. Each covers something real, and each stops at a specific point. Knowing where it stops is more useful than knowing how far away it is.

The school's own teacher is nearest and often best for the first move. They know the cohort, the teaching order and the internal deadlines, and an extra hour from them costs little or nothing. The stopping point is structural rather than a judgement: in a single-figure Higher Level cohort with one teacher, if that teacher's explanation is the thing the student has already not understood twice, more of it will not move the grade and there is no colleague to swap to. A local generalist stops earlier still on a Diploma subject, for the component-level reasons set out across this page.

Provision in the city and in the Sharjah exclaves extends the range without changing the fundamental problem: these are places with small cohorts too, so the pool they draw from has the same shape. The provider beyond the mountains has the specialists and cannot reliably deliver them to an east-coast address week after week. That is the gap the online option fills, and it is worth being precise that it fills a coverage gap rather than a price gap. The table puts the four side by side.

sections.heading: Why scarcity beats proximity in a cohort of eight
paragraphs: A small cohort changes more than the class size. It changes how much a teacher's time is divided across subjects, how many past papers the group has worked through collectively, how much peer comparison a student gets, and how quickly an individual gap is noticed. None of that is a criticism of small schools, several of which get excellent results. It is a description of the conditions under which an individual student can quietly drift for a term.

The most consequential effect is on specialism. Where a school runs one Higher Level science group, the teacher almost certainly also teaches the other sciences and probably the Middle Years Programme below. Their subject knowledge may be strong, but their accumulated experience of this specific paper, this specific mark scheme and this specific internally assessed component is spread across three syllabuses rather than concentrated in one. The gap that produces is not about intelligence or effort. It is about repetitions.

This is why subject matching rather than proximity is the right filter on this coast, and why the argument holds even for a family in Fujairah City with a tuition centre ten minutes away. The question to ask of any prospective tutor is how often they teach your child's subject at your child's level, and what they can tell you about the component where the marks are currently going. A specialist answers in the language of papers and criteria. Somebody covering it as a second subject answers in the language of topics. On the east coast the first answer is almost always further away than the second, and almost always worth the distance that no longer has to be driven.

sections.heading: What proximity genuinely does settle, and where to get it locally
paragraphs: It would be dishonest to spend a page arguing against proximity without listing the things it decides. The first is the exam centre: papers are sat at a physical place, under a centre number, with a timetable determined by Cambridge's administrative zone or Pearson's series. That is entirely local and worth confirming early rather than in the final fortnight. The second is peer study. A student who has two classmates to work through past papers with has something no remote arrangement supplies, and on this coast that is worth organising deliberately rather than leaving to chance.

The third is the school relationship. Internal deadlines, predicted grades, subject changes, access arrangements and any conversation about the Extended Essay supervisor all happen locally, in person, with people who know your child. No outside tutor substitutes for that, and a good one will keep pointing you back to it. The fourth is pastoral: a student under real pressure in DP2 needs adults who can see them, and a video session for one hour a week is not that.

The fifth is simply logistics, and it is why the school run and the bus timetable appear repeatedly on this page. A session has to fit into a real evening in a real household. Dibba's late bus arrivals push the first workable slot past five. Al Faseel's fixtures collide with the four o'clock hour. Port shift patterns mean some households need a slot that moves between weeks. Those are local facts, they decide whether a plan survives, and they are the part of a proximity search that deserves a straight answer rather than an argument.

sections.heading: Sitting the papers near home: centres and private candidates
paragraphs: This is the local question with the most consequences and the one families leave latest. Where a student's school is an exam centre, entries are handled by the school and the only thing to confirm is which series and which timetable version apply. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version of the timetable for their zone, so the zone is worth knowing in writing rather than by assumption.

Where a student wants a subject the school does not teach, the private-candidate route exists and it is genuinely local: the entry has to be made through a centre that accepts private candidates, within that series' deadline, and the student travels to that centre to sit the papers. The deadlines sit months before the exams. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. Pearson examines International GCSE subjects in a May or June window and again in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

For Diploma subjects the position is different and more restrictive, because the programme is delivered by authorised schools rather than entered privately in the way an International GCSE subject can be. That means a Fujairah student whose school cannot staff a Higher Level subject has school-level options rather than exam-entry options: a different subject, a different school, or in some cases a distance-learning arrangement through a provider that is itself an authorised school. A tutor does not solve that problem and should say so. What a tutor can do is make sure the subjects the student is actually entered for are taught to the level of the paper.
